Among the listed chromosomal mutations, inversion is the exam's chosen best answer, though the causal link is weak.

questions.question_text: Which of the following characteristic can show the evolutionary relationships among organisms?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The presence of homologous structures can show evolutionary relationships among organisms, because homologous structures share a common evolutionary origin even if their functions differ, such as the forelimbs of mammals. Analogous structures look similar but arise independently through convergent evolution.

questions.question_text: Which of the following species isolating processes could lead to the evolution of a new species by the mechanisms known as sympatric speciation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A river that change its course for many years

options.label: B
options.option_text: A new mountain range that was created many years

options.label: C
options.option_text: Population of a species having different breeding seasons
options.explanation: Sympatric speciation occurs when populations diverge into new species without geographic separation. A population of a species having different breeding seasons can isolate gene flow over time, eventually producing separate species, whereas rivers, mountains, and land masses cause allopatric speciation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A land mass that separated two water bodies for many years

questions.question_text: What is an apoenzyme?

options.label: A
options.explanation: An apoenzyme is a protein molecule, the protein portion of an enzyme that requires a non-protein cofactor or coenzyme to become catalytically active. The complete enzyme, the apoenzyme plus cofactor, is called a holoenzyme. Apoenzymes alone are inactive.

questions.question_text: For which of the following can divergent evolution be taken as an alternative name?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Divergent evolution can also be called adaptive radiation, a process in which a single ancestral species diversifies into many forms adapted to different environments, as seen in Darwin's finches and marsupial mammals. Allopatric speciation and selection types are related but not alternative names.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the result of the similarity observed between the wings of a bird and a pterodactyl?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The similarity between the wings of a bird and a pterodactyl is the result of convergent evolution, because these flying organisms are not closely related but independently evolved similar wing structures to solve the problem of flight. Their wings are analogous structures.

questions.question_text: Which of the following played an important role in the evolution of human being?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Emergency of wings in addition to limbs

options.label: B
options.option_text: Development of even toes in the forearms

options.label: C
options.option_text: Development of feathers and hallow bones

options.label: D
options.option_text: Development of opposable thumb to grasp
options.explanation: The development of an opposable thumb to grasp played an important role in human evolution, because it allowed early hominids to manipulate tools, use hands for fine tasks, and increase survival and brain development. Wings, even toes, and hollow bones relate to birds, not humans.

questions.question_text: In which one of the following do we use genetically modified bacteria for purpose other than human health?

options.label: C
options.explanation: We use genetically modified bacteria to produce herbicides for a purpose other than human health, because herbicide production serves agriculture. Insulin, antibiotics, and vaccines are all produced for human health purposes, treating or preventing disease.

questions.question_text: which knowledge about cell biology scientists discover after all the others?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The first understanding that all living things are made of cells

options.label: B
options.option_text: Knowledge about how chromosomes behave during mitosis

options.label: C
options.option_text: First understanding about the double helix structure of DNA

options.label: D
options.option_text: First understanding about the DNA sequence in human genome
options.explanation: The first understanding about the DNA sequence in the human genome was discovered after all the others, since the Human Genome Project was completed in 2003. The cell theory, understanding of mitosis and chromosomes, and the double helix model all came much earlier in biology's history.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements can be considered as the better definition of the biological concept of behavior?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The reaction of a person or an animal in response to an external or internal stimulus

options.label: B
options.option_text: The responses or reactions or movements that a living plant makes in any situation

options.label: C
options.option_text: A system of coordinated response by an organism to an external or internal stimulus
options.explanation: The better definition of the biological concept of behavior is a system of coordinated response by an organism to an external or internal stimulus. This emphasizes the organized, integrated nature of responses rather than a simple reaction, movement, or the possession of a receptor alone.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A receptor of some kind of stimulus that an organism has which produces a response

questions.question_text: To which category of behavior does the human behavior that involves the strengthening of existing responses or the formation of new responses to existing stimuli that occur because of practice or repetition belong?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The behavior described, strengthening existing responses or forming new responses due to practice or repetition, belongs to the category of learned behavior. Learning produces lasting changes in behavior through experience, practice, and repetition, in contrast to innate or instinctive behaviors present from birth.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT grouped under genetically pre-programmed pattern of behavior?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Conditioned behavior is not grouped under genetically pre-programmed patterns of behavior, because conditioning requires learning through association between stimuli. Reflex actions, orientation behavior, and instinctive behaviors are genetically pre-programmed, inherited responses that do not require learning.

questions.question_text: Which group of bacteria reduces nitrate to nitrogen gas in th nitrogen cycle?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Denitrifying bacteria reduce nitrate to nitrogen gas in the nitrogen cycle. This denitrification converts nitrate back to atmospheric nitrogen, completing the cycle. Nitrogen-fixing bacteria convert nitrogen gas to ammonia, while ammonium-forming bacteria convert nitrogen into ammonium ions.

questions.question_text: The main factors that determine the types of terrestrial biomes in a certain geographical area are:

options.label: D
options.explanation: The main factors that determine the types of terrestrial biomes in a certain geographical area are precipitation and temperature. Together these climate factors control which plants can grow, and vegetation in turn determines the animal life found there, so soil and succession are secondary influences.

questions.question_text: In which parts of Ethiopian are Lions, Elephants, & Giraffes found more community?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In the afroalpine and subafroalpine zones

options.label: B
options.option_text: In the highland areas of northern Ethiopian

options.label: C
options.option_text: In the grasslands of southwestern Ethiopian
options.explanation: Lions, elephants, and giraffes are found in greater numbers in the grasslands of southwestern Ethiopia, where savannah habitats provide food and space for these large herbivores and predators. Afroalpine and highland areas support different, smaller wildlife communities adapted to cooler conditions.

options.label: D
options.option_text: In central and northern parts of the rift valley

questions.question_text: Which of the following tools is used by a biologist to study the internal anatomy of experimental animals?

options.label: A
options.explanation: A dissecting kit contains scalpels, scissors, and probes used to cut open and examine the internal organs of experimental animals during dissection. This tool allows biologists to study internal anatomy directly, whereas a hand lens, Petri dish, or microscope serves other observation or culture purposes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of an enzyme?

options.label: C
options.option_text: It lowers the energy of activation

options.label: D
options.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts, usually globular proteins, that speed up reactions by lowering activation energy. They are not consumed or converted to products in the reaction; they remain unchanged and can be reused. Therefore the statement that an enzyme is converted to products is NOT a characteristic of enzymes.

questions.question_text: Who was the first person who believed to have seen moving cells under a microscope?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Anton van Leeuwenhoek was the first person to observe living moving cells, such as protozoa and sperm cells, using simple hand-made microscopes in the 1670s. Robert Hooke had earlier seen non-living cork cell walls, while Schwann and Dutrochet contributed to the cell theory later.

questions.question_text: Why do micro-organisms decompose dead organic matters?

options.label: A
options.option_text: To release mineral nutrients for the plants

options.label: C
options.option_text: To drive energy for their own uses
options.explanation: Microorganisms decompose dead organic matter to obtain energy and nutrients for their own metabolism and growth. By breaking down complex organic molecules, they release energy for their own use, and as a beneficial side effect they return mineral nutrients to the soil for plants and keep the ecosystem cycling.

options.label: D
options.option_text: To keep the balance of atmospheric gases

questions.question_text: The practice of modern agriculture that reduces crop biodiversity is:

options.label: C
options.explanation: Monoculture, the practice of growing a single crop species over large areas, directly reduces crop biodiversity by eliminating genetic and species variety. The exam key marks fertilizers, but fertilizers do not inherently reduce biodiversity, so monoculture is the clearest practice reducing crop biodiversity. Flagged: answer overridden from D to C.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the best scientific approach to come to conclusive evidence showing that a given event is caused by a certain factor?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The best scientific approach for conclusive evidence is conducting a controlled experiment, which tests cause and effect under controlled conditions. Strong belief and guessing lack empirical support. The input file incorrectly marks making a good guess as correct and repeats that option twice, so the answer is overridden to conducting an experiment. Flagged.

questions.question_text: Of the following organic molecules which one includes a pentose sugar?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Deoxyribose is a pentose sugar, meaning it contains five carbon atoms, and it is a component of DNA nucleotides. Glucose, fructose, and galactose are all hexose monosaccharides containing six carbon atoms, so they are not pentose sugars.

questions.question_text: What dose an enzyme do to a chemical reaction that allows it to proceed optimally?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It lower the required activation energy.
options.explanation: Enzymes lower the activation energy required for a chemical reaction, allowing the reaction to proceed more quickly at normal body temperatures. They do not increase substrate amount, raise activation energy, or modify pH and temperature; they simply reduce the energy barrier so reactions occur optimally.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It increases the amount of the substrate.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It increases the required activation energy.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It modifies both th Ph and the temperature.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is lacking in prokaryotic cells?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Prokaryotic cells lack cellulose in their cell walls, which instead contain peptidoglycan, while cellulose is a feature of plant cell walls. Prokaryotes do possess cytosol, ribosomes, and a DNA strand in the nucleoid region, so cellulose is the component that is lacking in prokaryotic cells.

questions.question_text: What is the name of a major group of eukaryotic organisms that obtain their nutrition using extracellular digestion?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Fungi are eukaryotic organisms that secrete digestive enzymes outside their cells and absorb the resulting nutrients, a process called extracellular digestion. Viruses and bacteria are not eukaryotic, and algae are photosynthetic autotrophs, so fungi are the group that uses extracellular digestion for nutrition.

questions.question_text: What kind of nutrition do most of the decomposers have in general?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Most decomposers, such as many bacteria and fungi, use saprobiotic nutrition, secreting enzymes to break down dead organic matter and absorbing the released nutrients for energy. This contrasts with autotrophic, chemosynthetic, and endosymbiont nutritional modes, which do not rely on decomposing dead material.

questions.question_text: To which genus of primates are the Neanderthal humans classified?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Neanderthals are classified in the genus Homo, specifically as Homo neanderthalensis. They are closely related to modern humans, Homo sapiens, and share the same genus. Ardipithecus, Australopithecus, and Zinjanthropus are earlier hominid genera that predate the genus Homo.

questions.question_text: In which of the following is there a MISMATCH between the type of innate behavior and the resulting action/response?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Imprinting in birds is a learned behavior in which young birds form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see, so pairing it with instinctive behavior is a mismatch. Nest-building is instinctive, blinking is a reflex, and web-weaving is innate. The exam key marking nest-building is incorrect. Flagged: answer overridden from C to A.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Reflex action- blinking of the eyes in humans

options.label: D
options.option_text: Presentational movement-weaving a web in spiders

questions.question_text: Cells were first seen using the microscope by:

options.label: B
options.explanation: Robert Hooke first observed and described cells in 1665 when he saw the box-like walls of dead cork tissue under his microscope and named them cells. Leeuwenhoek later saw living cells, while Schleiden and Schwann later formulated the cell theory, so Hooke is credited with first seeing cells.

questions.question_text: The ultimate source of genetic variation is:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Mutation is the ultimate source of genetic variation because it creates entirely new alleles, which are the raw material for evolution. Migration, genetic drift, and natural selection redistribute or select existing alleles but do not create new genetic variation; they act upon variation that mutation first produced.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the first step in starting a research process?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Searching sources of information to locate problem.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Identifying or stating the research problem is the first step in the research process, because it defines what the researcher wants to investigate. Only after the problem is identified do researchers search for information sources, review related literature, and seek solutions to address the problem.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Searching for solution to the problem

questions.question_text: For which of the following purpose is GLOBAL positioning system (GPS) used?

options.label: A
options.explanation: GPS, or Global Positioning System, is primarily used to determine exact locations and is used for mapping an area, navigation, and surveying. A theodolite is a separate optical surveying instrument, while microwave and satellite signal refer to technologies used in communication rather than positioning purposes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is INCORRECT with respect to an enzymes ability to catalyze a reaction?

options.label: B
options.option_text: An enzyme birds reaction such that they are positioned correctly and can attain their transition-state configurations.

options.label: C
options.option_text: An enzyme allows the reaction to go through a more stable transition state than would normally be the case.

options.label: A
options.option_text: An enzyme provide a reaction surface and a hydrophilic environment for the reaction to take place.

options.label: D
options.option_text: An enzyme can change the final equilibrium point of the reaction it catalyzes.
options.explanation: Enzymes cannot change the final equilibrium point of a reaction; they only speed up the rate at which equilibrium is reached. Enzymes do stabilize transition states, bind substrates correctly, and provide active-site environments for reactions. The statement about changing equilibrium is the incorrect one, so the exam key is overridden. Flagged: answer overridden from C to D.

questions.question_text: The amount of organic matter present at a given time per unit area is called?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Standing crop is the amount of organic matter or biomass present in a given area at a particular time, while productivity measures the rate of biomass production over time. The term for biomass present per unit area at a given moment is standing crop, so the exam key is overridden. Flagged: answer overridden from D to B.

questions.question_text: In the energy pyramid, which group of organisms has least amount of energy?

options.label: B
options.explanation: In an energy pyramid, energy decreases at each successive trophic level because much is lost as heat. Tertiary producers occupy the top trophic level and therefore possess the least energy. Animals is too vague because herbivores and other animals at lower levels have more energy. Flagged: answer overridden from D to B.

questions.question_text: The sets in which scientists usually conduct two or more sets of the same experiment at the same time is:

options.label: C
options.explanation: Replication is the practice of conducting two or more identical sets of the same experiment at the same time to confirm results and reduce the effect of chance variation. The experimental group is the set receiving the treatment, so the exam key marking it is incorrect. Flagged: answer overridden from A to C.

questions.question_text: Which of the following properties of water makes sweat a good body coolant?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Its low density in the solid state

options.label: C
options.option_text: Its strong adhesion to a surface

options.label: D
options.explanation: Water's high heat of vaporization means a large amount of heat energy is absorbed when sweat evaporates from the skin, effectively cooling the body. Surface tension, low density of ice, and adhesion do not explain why sweating cools the body, making high heat of vaporization the correct property.

questions.question_text: How many molecule of glycerol and fatty acids, respectively, are needed to from 100 molecules of triglyceride fat?

options.label: C
options.explanation: One molecule of glycerol combines with three fatty acids to form one triglyceride molecule through ester bonds. Therefore, forming 100 triglyceride molecules requires 100 glycerol molecules and 300 fatty acid molecules, so the correct ratio is 100 and 300.

questions.question_text: In a metabolic pathway(A->B->C->D) where each step is catalyzed by a separate enzyme which substance in the pathway serves as an allosteric regulator?

options.label: D
options.explanation: In the metabolic pathway A to B to C to D, the end product D typically acts as an allosteric regulator. It inhibits the first enzyme of the pathway by binding to a site other than the active site, a mechanism called feedback inhibition, which prevents wasteful overproduction of the final product when it is already abundant.

questions.question_text: Which of the following organelles settles out last when homogenized cells are centrifuged?

options.label: D
options.explanation: When homogenized cells are centrifuged, heavier organelles sediment first and smaller, less dense organelles sediment last. Ribosomes are the smallest organelles listed, so they settle out last in the pellet, whereas chloroplasts, nuclei, and mitochondria are larger and pellet earlier.

questions.question_text: At which stage is most of the carbon dioxide released during aerobic respiration?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Most carbon dioxide is released during the Krebs or citric acid cycle in aerobic respiration, when acetyl-CoA is oxidized and carbon atoms are removed as carbon dioxide. Glycolysis produces no carbon dioxide, and the electron transport chain and chemiosmosis generate ATP without releasing carbon dioxide.

questions.question_text: One of the following groups of plants carry out light dependent and high independent reactions of photosynthesis in separate cells of the leaf.

options.label: C
options.explanation: C4 plants, such as maize and sugarcane, carry out the light-dependent reactions in mesophyll cells and the light-independent Calvin cycle in bundle sheath cells, separating the two phases into different leaf cells. This spatial separation reduces photorespiration and improves carbon fixation efficiency in hot, sunny conditions.

questions.question_text: What is the nutritional mode of those bacteria which decompose dead organic matter and thus recycle nutrients?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Bacteria that decompose dead organic matter and recycle nutrients use saprobiotic nutrition, secreting enzymes to break down dead material and absorbing the released nutrients for energy. Autotrophic, parasitic, and symbiotic modes do not involve the decomposition of dead organic matter for nutrition.

questions.question_text: In what main way do retroviruses such as HIV differ from other types of RNA viruses?

options.label: A
options.option_text: They require a host cell to reproduce

options.label: B
options.option_text: They reversely copy RNA to DNA
options.explanation: Retroviruses such as HIV differ from other RNA viruses because they contain reverse transcriptase, an enzyme that copies their RNA genome into DNA. This DNA integrates into the host cell genome. Other RNA viruses replicate directly via RNA without the RNA-to-DNA reverse transcription step.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Their genes are resistant to mutation

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT true about the flow of energy in the ecosystem?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Energy in an ecosystem is not recycled; it flows in one direction, entering as sunlight and being lost as heat at each trophic level. Decomposers recycle matter and nutrients, not energy. Therefore, the statement that energy is recycled by decomposers is NOT true about energy flow.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It passes from one trophic level to the next.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It enters the ecosystem in the form of light.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It leaves the ecosystem in the form of heat.

questions.question_text: Through which of the following processes do all living organisms contribute to carbon cycle?

options.label: B
options.explanation: All living organisms carry out cellular respiration, releasing carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, which is how every organism contributes to the carbon cycle. Photosynthesis only occurs in producers, decomposition only in decomposers, and combustion involves human activity, so cellular respiration is the universal process.

questions.question_text: In ecological context which of the following is a population ?

options.label: A
options.option_text: All living organisms in a habitat

options.label: B
options.option_text: All the producers in a habitat

options.label: C
options.option_text: All individuals of same species in a habitat
options.explanation: In ecology, a population is defined as all individuals of the same species living in a particular habitat at the same time and potentially interbreeding. A community includes all living organisms of different species, while producers and consumers describe functional groups within the ecosystem rather than a population.

options.label: D
options.option_text: All the consumers in a habitat

questions.question_text: During meiosis, which processes makes the four chromatids of a homologous pair of chromosomes genetically different from one another?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Crossing over during prophase I of meiosis exchanges segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes, making the four chromatids genetically different from one another. Segregation separates alleles into gametes but does not change the genetic content of chromatids. Flagged: answer overridden from C to B.

questions.question_text: One of the following is NOT true about protein synthesis in eukaryotes.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Translation takes place in the cytoplasm

options.label: B
options.option_text: Transcription takes place in the nucleus

options.label: C
options.option_text: Both Transcription and translation takes place in the cytoplasm
options.explanation: In eukaryotic cells, transcription occurs in the nucleus while translation occurs in the cytoplasm, so the statement that both take place in the cytoplasm is NOT true. Additionally, mRNA is modified after transcription. This spatial separation is a key difference between eukaryotic and prokaryotic protein synthesis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following combinations is known as Neo-Darwinism?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Acquired inheritance and Mendelian law of inheritance

options.label: C
options.option_text: Natural selection and Lamarck's theory of evolution

options.label: D
options.option_text: Natural selection and Mendelian law of inheritance
options.explanation: Neo-Darwinism combines Darwin's natural selection with Mendelian genetics. It explains that genetic variation arises through mutations and recombination in genes, and natural selection acts on this heritable variation, providing the modern synthesis of evolutionary biology. Acquired inheritance and Lamarck's ideas are not part of Neo-Darwinism.

questions.question_text: In the process of allopatric speciation, which of the following is the mechanism that prevents populations from exchanging genes?

options.label: B
options.explanation: In allopatric speciation, a geographic barrier such as a mountain range, river, or ocean physically separates populations, preventing them from exchanging genes. Over time, the isolated populations diverge genetically and reproductively. Seasonal and temporal isolation are mechanisms of sympatric rather than allopatric speciation.

questions.question_text: A boy who had seen a snake crossing his way earlier jumped up violently when grass touched his legs. Which behavior is it?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The boy's violent jump when grass touched his legs after seeing a snake is an example of conditioning, specifically classical conditioning. The snake produced fear, and the previously neutral grass became associated with danger, triggering the same fearful jump response. Habituation and sensitization do not involve this kind of stimulus association.

questions.question_text: What material do microbiologists use to culture bacteria in the laboratory?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Microbiologists culture bacteria using nutrient agar, a solid medium containing nutrients and agar as a solidifying agent. Moist soil contains many competing organisms and is not a controlled growth medium, so the exam key is incorrect. Flagged: answer overridden from A to C.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is usually taken as a signal for the final stage of HIV infection?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Signs of the disease Kaposi's sarcoma
options.explanation: The final stage of HIV infection, AIDS, is signaled by the appearance of opportunistic infections such as Kaposi's sarcoma, a cancer caused by a herpes virus that develops when T-helper cells are severely depleted. Uninfected T-helper cells indicate a healthy immune system, so the exam key is wrong. Flagged: answer overridden from C to A.

options.label: D
options.option_text: No infection by other parasitic diseases

questions.question_text: Though which process can inorganic ions from the soil be absorbed in to the root hairs?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Inorganic ions from the soil are absorbed into root hairs by active transport, which uses energy to move ions against their concentration gradient because soil ion concentrations are often lower than those inside root cells. Osmosis only moves water, not ions, so the exam key is incorrect. Flagged: answer overridden from D to C.

questions.question_text: How are organic molecules distinguished from inorganic molecules? Organic molecules always contain:

options.label: D
options.explanation: Organic molecules always contain carbon and hydrogen, and are typically compounds in which carbon forms the backbone. Inorganic molecules may contain carbon, as in carbon dioxide, or oxygen and hydrogen, but the combination of carbon with hydrogen distinguishes organic compounds such as carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids.

questions.question_text: In which industrial enzyme technology is lactase practical applied to produce lactose-free mile for used by lactose intolerant individuals?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Lactase, an enzyme that breaks down the milk sugar lactose into glucose and galactose, is practically applied in the dairy product manufacturing industry to produce lactose-free milk for lactose-intolerant individuals. This prevents the digestive discomfort these individuals experience when consuming ordinary milk products. Other industries such as chocolate, hormone, or cereal manufacture do not use lactase this way.

questions.question_text: Which kind of enzyme inhibitors bind to enzyme only weakly and the bond that hold them breaks easily releasing the inhibitor to allow the enzyme to become active again?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Reversible inhibitors bind weakly to enzymes and can easily dissociate, releasing the enzyme and allowing it to become active again. This weak, reversible binding contrasts with irreversible inhibitors, which bind strongly and permanently alter enzyme structure so that enzyme activity cannot be restored.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Inhibitors that bind strongly to enzymes

options.label: D
options.option_text: Inhibitors that permanently alter enzyme structure

questions.question_text: Of the following models describing the nature of the cell membrane, which one was proposed before all the others?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The phospholipid bilayer model was proposed first by Gorter and Grendel in 1925, based on the idea that membranes consist of a double layer of phospholipids. It predates the later sandwich model, unit membrane model, and fluid mosaic model proposed by Danielli-Davson, Robertson, and Singer-Nicolson.

questions.question_text: Why is that longer races by athletes must be run slower than shorter than shorter races?

options.label: A
options.option_text: To give time for lactic acid fermentation in muscle cells

options.label: B
options.option_text: To avoid hunger as food is quickly converted to energy

options.label: C
options.option_text: To allow aerobic respiration to produce the required ATP
options.explanation: Longer races must be run slower so that muscles can rely on aerobic respiration, which produces ATP steadily and efficiently using oxygen. Sprinting too fast causes oxygen debt, forcing anaerobic respiration and lactic acid accumulation, leading to fatigue. A sustainable pace allows aerobic respiration to meet the continuous ATP demand of long-distance running.

options.label: D
options.option_text: To adapt to the weather condition at the racing place

questions.question_text: In which organ of the human body are more bacteria found?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The large intestine or colon harbors the greatest number of bacteria in the human body, with trillions of microbes forming the gut microbiota. These bacteria aid digestion, synthesize vitamins, and protect against pathogens. The lungs, stomach, and small intestine have fewer bacteria due to acidic conditions and other defenses.

questions.question_text: From which group of micro-organisms was the first antibiotics produced ?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The first antibiotic, penicillin, was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928 and is produced by the fungus Penicillium. Antibiotics such as penicillin are therefore produced from fungal organisms, not from bacteria or viruses, making fungi the correct group for the origin of the first antibiotics.

questions.question_text: What is the other name for the primary consumers of the ecosystem?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Primary consumers are organisms that feed directly on green plants and other producers, so they are also called herbivores. Carnivores and predators feed on other animals at higher trophic levels, while green plants are producers, so only herbivores correctly name the primary consumers of the ecosystem.

questions.question_text: Of the following activities which one is considered to have an indirect negative effect on biodiversity?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Human and livestock population growth indirectly harms biodiversity by increasing demand for land, food, and resources, which drives direct destructive activities such as logging and deforestation. Charcoal making, deforestation, and monoculture are direct actions that reduce biodiversity, so the exam key is incorrect. Flagged: answer overridden from D to A.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Mono culture farming with improved crop varieties

questions.question_text: If two heterozygous tall pea plants are crossed, how many of the offspring would be phenotypically tall plants?

options.label: D
options.explanation: When two heterozygous tall pea plants, Tt, are crossed, the offspring genotypes are TT, Tt, Tt, and tt. Since tall is dominant, three of the four genotypes appear tall, giving 75 percent phenotypically tall offspring, while only the homozygous recessive tt plant is short.

questions.question_text: How can biotechnology be applied to reduce the use of inorganic fertilizers in agriculture?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By using the golden rice and producing organic fertilizers from betacarotenes

options.label: B
options.option_text: By using thermostable enzyme of genetically engineered bacteria used in washing powders

options.label: C
options.option_text: By selecting and propagating varieties with high growth rates and high productivity.
options.explanation: Biotechnology can reduce inorganic fertilizer use by selecting and propagating crop varieties with high growth rates and productivity, which require fewer nutrient inputs. Among the listed options, this is the only approach directly relevant to reducing fertilizer dependence, so it is the best answer. Golden rice and washing powder enzymes are unrelated applications.

options.label: D
options.option_text: By using enzyme produced by genetically engineered bacteria used in the food industry

questions.question_text: Which of the following feature do analogous structures mostly share?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Analogous structures, such as the wings of birds and insects, perform similar functions but have different evolutionary origins. Therefore, analogous structures mostly share functional similarity rather than phylogenetic, ancestral, or developmental similarity, which are characteristics of homologous structures that share a common evolutionary origin.

questions.question_text: In which of the following ways dose learned behavior differ from innate behavior?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Learned behavior is adaptive in nature.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Learned behavior is modified by new experiences.
options.explanation: Learned behavior differs from innate behavior because it is modified by new experiences and practice. Innate behavior is genetically determined, adaptive, and functional at the first attempt, while learned behavior develops through observation, conditioning, or insight and changes as the animal gains experience.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Learned behavior is functional at the first attempt.

questions.question_text: Current human concerns such as famine, pestilence, and environmental degradation would be solved through the use of:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Current human concerns such as famine, pestilence, and environmental degradation would best be solved through the application of biological principles, including ecology, genetics, and microbiology, which provide the scientific understanding needed for sustainable agriculture, disease control, and conservation. Irrigation, aquaculture, and terracing are specific techniques rather than guiding principles.

questions.question_text: The best way to control HIV/AIDS is:

options.label: D
options.explanation: The best way to control HIV/AIDS is awareness creation, because education about transmission routes and prevention methods enables people to adopt protective behaviors. This is more effective than relying only on condom distribution or antiviral drugs, which may be limited in availability, making prevention through knowledge the most sustainable control strategy.

questions.question_text: Which is the possible effect of the weak hydrogen bond among water molecules?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It helps water to build at low temperature

options.label: B
options.option_text: It results in the crystal shape of ice
options.explanation: The weak hydrogen bonds between water molecules cause water molecules to arrange in a fixed, open lattice when it freezes, producing the characteristic crystal shape of ice. These bonds also contribute to ice floating and other water properties, but the crystal structure of ice directly results from hydrogen bonding.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Plays a significant role in the interaction of a water molecule with hydrophobic surfaces

questions.question_text: Cell organelles that contain hydrolytic enzymes are called:

options.label: B
options.explanation: Lysosomes are cell organelles that contain hydrolytic enzymes capable of digesting macromolecules, worn-out organelles, and engulfed particles. Peroxisomes contain oxidative enzymes, mesosomes are bacterial membranes, and ribosomes synthesize proteins, so lysosomes are the organelles specifically associated with hydrolytic enzymes.

questions.question_text: Which part of the cell makes necessary changes packages and secretes proteins?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, packages, and secretes proteins by processing proteins received from the endoplasmic reticulum and dispatching them in vesicles to their destinations. The endoplasmic reticulum synthesizes proteins and lipids, mitochondria produce ATP, and the cell wall provides support, so the Golgi apparatus carries out packaging and secretion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following takes place under normal conditions as electrons flow down the electron transport chain of the mitochondria?

options.label: A
options.explanation: As electrons flow down the mitochondrial electron transport chain, NADH and FADH2 are oxidized, donating electrons, while protons are pumped to form an electrochemical gradient that drives ATP synthesis. Multiple options describe true events, making the question defective, so the keyed answer is retained as the best choice. Flagged: defective.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The ph of the matrix increases

questions.question_text: In the processes of photosyntheses light is necessary to:

options.label: D
options.option_text: Produce ATP and a reducing substance
options.explanation: Light energy is necessary during photosynthesis to drive the light-dependent reactions, which split water through photolysis, produce ATP, and generate the reducing substance NADPH. These products supply energy and reducing power for the Calvin cycle to fix carbon dioxide into glucose, which does not directly require light.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an industrial use of bacteria?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Recycling minerals through ecosystems is an ecological role of bacteria, performed by decomposers, rather than an industrial use. Bacteria are industrially used in food processing, genetic engineering, and wastewater treatment, where they produce desired products or break down waste materials under controlled industrial conditions.

questions.question_text: Carbon cycle is important in nature because:

options.label: A
options.option_text: The amount of energy before and after a reaction must be the same

options.label: B
options.option_text: It continuously reuse and recycles carbon in the ecosystem.
options.explanation: The carbon cycle is important in nature because it continuously reuses and recycles carbon through the ecosystem, moving carbon between the atmosphere, organisms, and Earth's crust. This recycling maintains carbon availability for photosynthesis and other life processes, ensuring a balanced and sustainable supply of carbon for all organisms.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It consumes oxygen and nitrogen in the atmosphere.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is used in energy capture and recapture.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is essential in order for a virus to replicate?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The capsid must enter the host cell cytoplasm

options.label: B
options.option_text: The host cell must be undergoing mitosis

options.label: C
options.option_text: The host cell must lack cell membrane.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The genome must be released in to the cytoplasm
options.explanation: For a virus to replicate, its genome must be released into the host cell's cytoplasm, where viral enzymes take over the host's machinery to replicate the genome and synthesize viral proteins. The capsid remains outside, and the host cell need not be dividing or undergoing mitosis for viral replication.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following NOT in situ conservation of Biodiversity?

options.label: A
options.explanation: In situ conservation protects species within their natural habitats, using sanctuaries, biosphere reserves, and national parks. A botanical garden is an example of ex situ conservation because plants are maintained outside their natural environment, so it is the option that is NOT in situ conservation.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following represent the population growth curve of a species with limited resources?

options.label: A
options.explanation: A population growing with limited resources follows a logistic growth curve, which is S-shaped: growth is rapid at first, then slows and levels off at the carrying capacity as resources become limiting. Exponential growth occurs only when resources are unlimited, so the exam key is incorrect. Flagged: answer overridden from D to A.

questions.question_text: One goat is heterozygous, long hair(Rr), and its mate carries homozygous short (rr). What is the probability of the offspring having short hair?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Crossing a heterozygous long-haired goat, Rr, with a homozygous short-haired goat, rr, produces offspring genotypes Rr and rr in equal proportions. Since short hair is expressed by the rr genotype, half of the offspring will have short hair, giving a probability of 50 percent.

questions.question_text: The type of enzyme used in recombinant DNA technology to spilt a specific sugar phosphate bond in each strand of a DNA double helix is called:

options.label: B
options.explanation: Restriction enzymes, also called restriction endonucleases, cut DNA at specific recognition sequences, splitting the sugar-phosphate bonds in both strands of the DNA double helix. They are essential tools in recombinant DNA technology for cutting DNA into fragments. Ligase joins DNA fragments, while esterase and lipase act on esters and fats.

questions.question_text: Lamarck's theory of evolution is know as:

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lamarck's theory of evolution is known as the inheritance of acquired characters, proposing that organisms pass on characteristics acquired during their lifetime to their offspring, such as a giraffe lengthening its neck through stretching. This idea contrasts with Darwin's natural selection and the modern mutation theory of evolution.

questions.question_text: Habituation and imprinting illustrate that behaviors are made up of:

options.label: C
options.explanation: Habituation and imprinting illustrate that many behaviors contain both innate and learned components. Habituation involves learning to ignore repeated harmless stimuli, and imprinting combines an innate tendency with learned attachment during a sensitive period, so the exam key is incorrect. Flagged: answer overridden from D to C.

questions.question_text: The evolution of species which is based upon the sum total adaptation changes could be preserved by:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Adaptive changes accumulated in a species are preserved by natural selection, which favors individuals with advantageous traits, increasing their survival and reproduction so beneficial adaptations spread through the population. Speciation, isolation, and human conservation do not preserve the sum of adaptation changes in the same way natural selection does.

questions.question_text: Based on differences in DNA which of the following animals is closer to human beings?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Based on DNA differences, the domestic pig is genetically closest to human beings among the options because both are mammals with more shared DNA sequence similarity. Frogs, zebra fish, and domestic chickens are more distantly related vertebrates, so their DNA differs more substantially from the human genome.

questions.question_text: To which group of sugar can the molecule dihydroxyacetone be classified?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Dihydroxyacetone is a triose sugar because its molecule contains three carbon atoms. It is a ketose triose formed during glycolysis, along with the aldose triose glyceraldehyde. Hexose sugars contain six carbons, pentose sugars contain five, and oligosugars contain a small number of monosaccharide units, so triose is correct.

questions.question_text: Choose the one in which the human digestive enzyme is INCORRECT matched with the substance that it normally catalyzes.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Trypsin is a protease enzyme that digests proteins, not starch, so pairing trypsin with starch is an incorrect match. Lipase digests fat, pepsin digests protein, and pancreatic amylase digests starch, making these pairings correct and leaving trypsin-starch as the INCORRECT enzyme-substrate match.

questions.question_text: The organelle of the cell which is concerned with the synthesis of lipids in addition to being associated with carbohydrate metabolism and detoxification is:

options.label: D
options.explanation: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum synthesizes lipids, participates in carbohydrate metabolism, and detoxifies drugs and poisons. Unlike the rough endoplasmic reticulum, it lacks ribosomes and is abundant in cells that produce lipids and hormones. The Golgi apparatus modifies proteins, while thylakoid membranes are involved in photosynthesis.

questions.question_text: Where is convergence point for the metabolism of the building blocks of carbohydrates lipids and proteins

options.label: B
options.explanation: The Krebs cycle is the convergence point of metabolism because acetyl-CoA, produced from carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins, enters the cycle and is oxidized. Glucose breaks down to pyruvate and then acetyl-CoA, fatty acids are broken to acetyl-CoA, and amino acids are converted to cycle intermediates, all feeding into this central pathway.

questions.question_text: Among the following crops, which one uses a non- C4 photosynthetic pathways?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pineapple uses the CAM photosynthetic pathway, not C4 photosynthesis, so it is the non-C4 crop among the options. C4 photosynthesis is used by maize, sorghum, and sugarcane, which fix carbon in separate mesophyll and bundle sheath cells. Pineapple instead fixes carbon at night through the CAM pathway.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is responsible for rapid evolution in RNA viruses?

options.label: B
options.option_text: High mutation rate of its RNA
options.explanation: RNA viruses evolve rapidly because their RNA polymerases lack proofreading ability, causing a high mutation rate. These frequent mutations quickly generate new variants that can evade immune responses and antiviral drugs, which is why RNA viruses such as HIV and influenza evolve so quickly. Accurate replication would reduce evolution.

questions.question_text: What major consequence dose primary ecological succession involve normally?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Primary ecological succession normally involves a gradual increase in species number and the complexity of food webs, as communities develop from bare rock or lifeless areas toward a mature, stable climax community. Species richness and habitat quality generally improve, making the increase in food web complexity the major consequence.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A biotic factor become less favorable

questions.question_text: How quickly a population would increase or decrease in size is probably least influenced by the presence of:

options.label: B
options.explanation: How quickly a population increases or decreases is least influenced by the presence of disproportionate human races, a concept irrelevant to ecological population dynamics. Population change is mainly influenced by resource availability such as oxygen, competition among species, and predator-prey relationships involving carnivores and herbivores.

questions.question_text: Among the theories about the origin of life which one better agrees with the concept of change in organisms and their genetic composed over generation being caused by meiosis, hybridization, natural selection or mutation?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The biochemical origin theory agrees with the concept of organisms changing genetically over generations through meiosis, hybridization, natural selection, and mutation, because it proposes that life arose and diversified through gradual biochemical and evolutionary processes rather than sudden special creation or spontaneous generation. This theory is compatible with modern evolutionary genetics.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most accepted theory about the origin of life on earth?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The most accepted theory about the origin of life on Earth is the theory of chemical evolution, which proposes that simple inorganic molecules reacted in the primitive reducing atmosphere and oceans, forming organic molecules that eventually assembled into self-replicating life. Miller and Urey's experiment supported this by producing amino acids from such gases.

questions.question_text: What is the possible cause or isolating mechanism for the formation of allopatric species?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The possible cause or isolating mechanism for the formation of allopatric species is geographic isolation, where a physical barrier such as a mountain, river, or ocean separates populations so they cannot interbreed and exchange genes. Over time they diverge into distinct species. Seasonal, temporal, and behavioral isolation operate in sympatric speciation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement about instinctive actions is NOT true?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Instinctive actions are innate, adaptive, and follow a fixed pattern, so they do not require learning. They are genetically programmed behaviors present from birth, such as nest-building or web-weaving. The statement that instinctive actions require learning is therefore NOT true about instinctive behaviors.

questions.question_text: What dose a low value for Simpson's index of diversity normally indicate to the researcher?

options.label: A
options.option_text: An area with high number of endemic species

options.label: B
options.option_text: An area dominated by one or just a few species
options.explanation: A low value for Simpson's index of diversity indicates low species diversity, meaning the area is dominated by one or just a few species. High index values indicate greater diversity with many evenly distributed species. Thus a low value signals a less diverse area dominated by few species.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A biodiversity hotspot with abundant species

options.label: D
options.option_text: An area with plants but no species of animals

questions.question_text: A country with a high youth population but a low old age population and low infant population shows

options.label: A
options.option_text: A population pyramid with bulge in the middle
options.explanation: A country with a high youth population, low old-age population, and low infant population shows a population pyramid with a bulge in the middle. The bulge represents the large youthful working-age cohort, while the low infant population narrows the base and the low elderly population narrows the apex.

options.label: B
options.option_text: A population with wide base and narrow apex

options.label: D
options.option_text: A pyramid assuming a rectangular shape

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the primary contribution of Darwin to biological theory?

options.label: A
options.option_text: An important mechanism of biological evolution is natural selection
options.explanation: Darwin's primary contribution to biological theory was proposing natural selection as the important mechanism of evolution, explaining how organisms change over generations through differential survival and reproduction. The ideas about mutations creating new alleles, gene frequency change, and genes as units of inheritance came later from genetics and the modern synthesis.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Evolution is the change in gene frequencies over time.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Genes are the units of inheritance.

questions.question_text: Retroviruses are able to reverse transcribe RNA to DNA in order to:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Command the host cell in the production of genomes similar to that of the hosts.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Control the formation of viral protein and RNA that can be assembled in to new virus particles.
options.explanation: Retroviruses reverse-transcribe RNA to DNA so they can integrate their viral genome into the host cell's chromosomes, then use the host's machinery to control the formation of viral proteins and RNA that are assembled into new virus particles. This integration allows the virus to hijack the host transcription and reproduction systems.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Control the formation of viral protein and DNA that can be assembled in to new viral particles

questions.question_text: Which of the following nucleotide sequences contains four pyrimidine bases?

options.label: A
options.explanation: In the sequence GATCAATGC, the bases are G, A, T, C, A, A, T, G, C. The pyrimidine bases are thymine and cytosine, which appear four times in this sequence as T, C, T, and C. The other sequences contain only three pyrimidines each, making this the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Significant change in Ph that can affect an enzyme molecule include

options.label: A
options.option_text: Building strong ionic bonds leading to stabilization of enzymes

options.label: B
options.option_text: Altering the charges on some substrates making it difficult to bind to enzyme
options.explanation: A significant change in pH can affect enzyme activity by altering the charges on substrates and on amino acids in the active site, making it difficult for the substrate to bind to the enzyme. This changes enzyme conformation and catalytic activity, which is why enzymes work within an optimal pH range.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Changing the color and palatability of food items

options.label: D
options.option_text: Increasing the boiling temperature of the substrate

questions.question_text: Which of the following two elements are found in all organic molecules?

options.label: C
options.explanation: All organic molecules contain carbon and hydrogen, and the carbon skeleton with hydrogen atoms bonded to it defines organic compounds such as carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids. Oxygen, nitrogen, and phosphorus are present in many but not all organic molecules, while carbon and hydrogen are universally present.

questions.question_text: If two molecule of a six carbon sugar are condensed to form a disaccharide, which of the following is the correct molecular formula of the disaccharide?

options.label: D
options.explanation: When two molecules of a six-carbon sugar, each with the formula C6H12O6, condense to form a disaccharide, a water molecule is eliminated. Summing the atoms gives C12H22O11, which is the correct molecular formula for a disaccharide such as sucrose, maltose, or lactose.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a requirement for a molecule to directly diffuse across the cell membrane?

options.label: C
options.explanation: For a molecule to diffuse directly across the cell membrane, it must be small, non-polar, and lipid-soluble. A large, polar molecule cannot pass through the lipid bilayer by simple diffusion, so large size and polarity is NOT a requirement for direct diffusion and is the incorrect option.

questions.question_text: Which of the following molecules can provide the cell the least amount of energy per molecule?

options.label: D
options.explanation: ATP provides the least energy per molecule among the options because each ATP molecule stores only the energy of one or two high-energy phosphate bonds, roughly 30 kilojoules per mole. Reduced NAD and reduced FAD carry more energy, and glucose stores substantial chemical energy, so ATP releases the least energy per molecule.

questions.question_text: During photosynthesis, which of the following is first step in the transduction of light energy to chemical Energy?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The first step in the transduction of light energy to chemical energy is photolysis of water, in which light energy splits water molecules, releasing electrons, protons, and oxygen. The electrons replace those lost by excited chlorophyll pigments, allowing the light reactions to proceed and eventually produce ATP and reducing power.

questions.question_text: Which of the following terms specifically refers to an ecological succession that starts in an aquatic environment?

options.label: B
options.explanation: A hydrosere is an ecological succession that begins in an aquatic environment such as a pond or lake, progressing from open water through stages of submerged plants, floating plants, and reeds, eventually forming a terrestrial community. Xerose is the term for succession in dry conditions, while primary and secondary succession are general types.

questions.question_text: Suppose the age pyramid of population has a broad base with a narrow top, which of the following is NOT true about the population?

options.label: B
options.explanation: A population pyramid with a broad base and narrow top indicates a fast-growing population dominated by young people with a high birth rate, so all the listed statements are true. Because the question asks for a statement that is NOT true and none qualifies, it is defective. Flagged: defective question, keyed answer retained.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is dominated by young people

options.label: D
options.option_text: It has a high birth rate

questions.question_text: What is the reason that Stanley Miller excluded free oxygen from the Mixture of the gases that he used for his simulation experiment?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Early organic molecules did not contain oxygen

options.label: B
options.option_text: Oxygen cannot react with the rest of the gases

options.label: C
options.explanation: Stanley Miller excluded free oxygen from his gas mixture because the primitive atmosphere was reducing, composed of gases such as methane, ammonia, hydrogen, and water vapor. Free oxygen would have oxidized the early organic molecules before they could form, so its absence allowed the synthesis of organic compounds in his simulation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The primitive atmosphere was full of oxygen

questions.question_text: Which of the following organic molecules is least informative about the evolutionary relationships between species

options.label: A
options.explanation: Carbohydrates are the least informative organic molecules for studying evolutionary relationships because they have simple, similar structures and limited sequence information. Proteins, DNA, and RNA have complex sequences that accumulate changes over time, allowing comparison of relatedness between species, whereas carbohydrate structure varies little among organisms.

questions.question_text: In which of the following ways dose mutation contribute most to evolution?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mutation contributes most to evolution by creating new alleles, which introduce fresh genetic variation into a population. Without new alleles, there would be nothing for natural selection to act upon. Preservation of adaptive genes, gene pool formation, and recombination of existing genes do not generate fundamentally new genetic material.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It forms a new gene poll

questions.question_text: A small girl who had observed her mother making a telephone call one day made a call on her own. Which learning behavior dose this exemplify?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The girl's behavior exemplifies latent learning, in which knowledge is acquired through observation without immediate reinforcement and is later displayed when needed. Having watched her mother use the telephone, she stored the information and demonstrated the skill when she later made a call on her own, without direct reward during observation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a basic SI unit?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Gram is not a basic SI unit; the SI base unit of mass is the kilogram. The seven SI base units are metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela. Candela, mole and second are all fundamental base units, so only gram fails to qualify.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is TRUE?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Ultraviolet light has longer wavelength than visible light.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The energy of radiation decreases as the wavelength decreases.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The frequency of radiation increases as the wavelength decreases.
options.explanation: Frequency and wavelength of electromagnetic radiation are inversely related by c = λν. As wavelength decreases, frequency increases because the speed of light is constant. The energy of radiation increases as wavelength decreases, and wavenumber increases as wavelength decreases, so C alone is true.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Wave number of an electromagnetic radiation increases as wavelength increases.

questions.question_text: Which of the following ionic compounds is formed from the reaction between magnesium and nitrogen?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Magnesium forms Mg2+ ions and nitrogen forms N3- ions. The least common multiple of the charges 2 and 3 is 6, so two Mg2+ ions balance three N3- ions, giving the formula Mg3N2, magnesium nitride. The other formulas MgN2, Mg2N2 and Mg2N3 do not balance charge.

questions.question_text: Which of the following molecules represents a non-polar covalent bond?

options.label: C
options.explanation: A non-polar covalent bond forms between two identical atoms sharing electrons equally. Cl-Cl is a homonuclear diatomic molecule whose atoms have equal electronegativity, so its bond is non-polar. B-Cl and C-Cl are polar covalent because of electronegativity differences, and Mg-Cl is ionic.

questions.question_text: Which of the following groups in the periodic table has paramagnetic atoms?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Paramagnetic atoms contain unpaired electrons. Group IVA elements such as carbon have the configuration s2p2 with two unpaired p electrons, making them paramagnetic. Group zero noble gases, Group IIA and Group IIB elements have all electrons paired and are therefore diamagnetic.

questions.question_text: How many types of cubic unit cells are known?

options.label: B
options.explanation: There are three types of cubic unit cells: simple or primitive cubic with atoms only at the corners, body-centred cubic with an additional atom at the centre, and face-centred cubic with atoms at the centre of each face. Each type contains a different number of atoms per unit cell, so three is correct.

questions.question_text: What is the process that converts liquid vegetable oils to solid fats?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hydrogenation is the process of adding hydrogen across the carbon-carbon double bonds of unsaturated liquid vegetable oils, converting them into saturated solid fats such as margarine. Hydration adds water, hydrolysis splits molecules using water, and saponification is soap-making; none of these solidify liquid oils.

questions.question_text: What would be the solubility of HOCH₂(CH₂)₆CH₂OH compared to CH₃(CH₂)₆CH₂OH?

options.label: B
options.explanation: HOCH2(CH2)6CH2OH is a diol with two hydroxyl groups, while CH3(CH2)6CH2OH has only one. The extra -OH group allows the diol to form more hydrogen bonds with water, making it more soluble in water. The monohydric alcohol is more soluble in non-polar solvents.

options.label: D
options.option_text: More soluble in a non-polar solvent such as dichloroethane.

questions.question_text: Which of the following gases is manufactured using the Haber process?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The Haber process manufactures ammonia, NH3, industrially by combining nitrogen and hydrogen at high pressure and temperature over an iron catalyst. Nitric oxide, nitrogen and nitrogen dioxide are not products of this process; nitric oxide is made by oxidising ammonia and nitrogen dioxide by further oxidation.

questions.question_text: Which one of the mixture of the following pairs will NOT give a buffer solution?

options.label: D
options.explanation: A buffer needs a weak acid or weak base together with its conjugate partner. HCN/NaCN, NH3/NH4Cl and H3PO4/KH2PO4 are all weak acid-conjugate base or weak base-conjugate acid pairs. HNO3 is a strong acid, so mixing HNO3 with NaNO3 will NOT give a buffer solution.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is TRUE for salts formed from strong acids and strong bases?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Produces ions which are proton acceptors.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Depends on the pKa and pKb of the parent acids and bases, respectively.

options.label: A
options.explanation: Salts of strong acids and strong bases, such as NaCl, contain ions that are neither appreciably acidic nor basic, so no hydrolysis takes place and their solutions are neutral. Their ions do not donate or accept protons, and the pH stays near 7 rather than depending on pKa and pKb.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Produces ions that are proton donors.

questions.question_text: Which of the following metals is NOT obtained by commercial electrolytic process?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Silver is obtained commercially by the cyanide process followed by displacement with zinc, not by electrolysis. Aluminium, copper and sodium are all produced industrially by electrolytic methods: aluminium by the Hall-Heroult process, copper by electrorefining, and sodium by electrolysis of molten chloride.

questions.question_text: Which of the following metals has the highest electrical and thermal conductivities?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Silver has the highest electrical and thermal conductivity of all metals, exceeding copper, cobalt and nickel. Its single free s-electron and closely packed structure allow very efficient transport of charge and heat. Copper is the next best conductor, which is why silver is used in specialised electrical contacts.

questions.question_text: Enthalpy is defined as the heat content of the system at constant:

options.label: C
options.explanation: Enthalpy, H, is defined as the heat content of a system measured at constant pressure, expressed as H = E + PV. Under constant-pressure conditions the heat change of a process equals the enthalpy change, ΔH = qp. At constant volume, the heat change equals the internal energy change instead.

questions.question_text: Which of the following elements is the second most abundant element in the earth's crust?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The earth's crust by mass is about 46.6% oxygen and 27.7% silicon. Oxygen is the most abundant element and silicon is the second most abundant. Aluminium is third and iron fourth. Therefore silicon, the basis of silicates and quartz, is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Which of the following plant nutrient will be produced as a result of nitrogen fixation?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Nitrogen fixation converts atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia and nitrate, which are soluble mineral nitrogen compounds. These mineral nitrogen nutrients are absorbed by plant roots and later used to synthesise proteins. Carbohydrate and cellulose contain no nitrogen, and protein is the plant product formed afterwards, not the nutrient directly produced.

questions.question_text: What is the number of significant figures in 0.0030050?

options.label: B
options.explanation: In 0.0030050 the three leading zeros are placeholders and are not significant. The digits 3, 0, 0, 5 and 0 are significant, because the two internal zeros and the trailing zero after the decimal point are counted. Therefore the number has exactly five significant figures.

questions.question_text: Which of the following properties of a substance does NOT represent an intensive physical property?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Intensive properties such as boiling point, colour and density do not depend on the amount of substance present. Volume is an extensive property because it changes with the quantity of material; doubling the amount doubles the volume. Therefore volume is the property that is NOT intensive.

questions.question_text: What is the mass of one molecule of water?

options.label: A
options.explanation: One mole of water has a mass of 18.0 g and contains 6.02×10^23 molecules. Dividing 18.0 g by Avogadro's number gives 18.0/6.02×10^23 = 2.99×10^-23 g per molecule, approximately 3.0×10^-23 g. Options B, C and D give incorrect values.

questions.question_text: Which of the following quantum number (s) is (are) related to the size and energy of an electron in a hydrogen atom?

options.label: A
options.explanation: For a hydrogen atom the principal quantum number n determines both the size and the energy of the orbital. The azimuthal quantum number l fixes the orbital shape, m fixes its orientation, and spin s describes electron spin. Only n relates to size and energy, so A is correct.

questions.question_text: An electron has a spin quantum number, s = +1/2 and a magnetic quantum number, m₁ = +1. In which of the following orbital will it NOT be present?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The magnetic quantum number ml can take all values from -l to +l. An s-orbital has l = 0, so its only possible ml value is 0. An electron with ml = +1 cannot occupy an s-orbital; p, d and f orbitals all permit ml = +1.

questions.question_text: Which of the following molecules has a trigonal bi pyramidal structure?

options.label: A
options.explanation: PCl5 has five bonding electron pairs and no lone pairs on phosphorus, giving sp3d hybridisation and a trigonal bipyramidal shape with 90° and 120° bond angles. IF5 and BrF5 are square pyramidal while ICl4- is square planar, so only PCl5 has the trigonal bipyramidal structure.

questions.question_text: Which of the following represents the general configuration of the transition elements?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Transition elements have the general electron configuration ns(n-1)d1-10, with electrons progressively filling the inner d subshell. Option A describes a noble gas core, C describes f-block elements, and D describes a completed d configuration. A partially filled d subshell defines transition metals.

questions.question_text: The total number of electrons participating in the bond formation of carbonate anion, CO₃²⁻ in the molecule of carbonic acid are:

options.label: C
options.explanation: In the carbonate ion CO3^2- carbon forms three sigma bonds and one pi bond across the resonance structures, giving four shared electron pairs in bonding. Counting the shared electrons gives 4 bond pairs × 2 = 8 bonding electrons. Non-bonding lone pairs are not involved in bond formation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following crystals possess high electrical and thermal conductivities?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Metallic crystals consist of positive ions immersed in a sea of delocalised valence electrons that are free to move, carrying charge and heat efficiently. This mobile electron sea gives metals high electrical and thermal conductivity. Ionic, molecular and covalent network crystals lack such freely moving electrons.

questions.question_text: What is the valid rate expression for the following reaction? 2NO + 2H₂ → N₂ + 2H₂O

options.label: C
options.explanation: For the reaction 2NO + 2H2 → N2 + 2H2O, the rate is defined as -1/2 Δ[NO]/Δt, the reciprocal of the coefficient applied to a reactant concentration with a negative sign. Option D, Δ[N2]/Δt, is numerically equal to the rate, so both C and D are valid expressions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is TRUE about equilibrium reaction?

options.label: A
options.option_text: No more reactants are transformed into products.

options.label: B
options.option_text: There are equal amounts of reactants and products.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The rate constant for the forward reactions equals that of the reverse reaction.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The rate for the forward reactions equals that of the reverse reactions.
options.explanation: At equilibrium the forward and reverse reactions continue at the same rate, so reactant and product concentrations remain constant. Reactants are still being converted to products, reactant and product amounts need not be equal, and the forward and reverse rate constants differ from each other.

questions.question_text: Three gases are in equilibrium in a closed chamber sealed with a piston. The following equilibrium is established: 2NH₃ (g) ⇌ N₂ (g) + 3H₂ (g) What will happen if the piston is pushed into the chamber?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The mole fraction of N₂ increases.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Pushing the piston reduces the volume and raises the pressure. By Le Chatelier's principle the equilibrium shifts toward the side with fewer gas moles: 2NH3 on the left versus N2 + 3H2, four moles, on the right. The shift left decreases the moles and mole fraction of N2.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The mole fraction of N₂ remains the same.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The mole fraction of N₂ increases and then decreases.

questions.question_text: Which of the following reactions will produce an alkyl carboxylic acid?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Heating a methyl ketone with acid and iodine.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Reacting an alkyl halide with hydrogen gas and platinum.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Oxidation of a primary alcohol with hot permanganate or chromate.
options.explanation: Hot acidic potassium permanganate or potassium dichromate oxidises a primary alcohol through the aldehyde stage to a carboxylic acid. Heating a methyl ketone with acid and iodine gives iodoform, alkyl halides are not oxidised by hydrogen and platinum, and ozonolysis of an alcohol is not a standard route.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is NOT TRUE?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Naturally derived soaps consists of a soluble salt of a long chain fatty acid.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Triacylglycerols are esters of glycerol and long chain carboxylic acids.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Long chain carboxylic acids are also known as fatty acids.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The major acidic component of vinegar is formic acid.
options.explanation: The major acidic component of vinegar is acetic acid, not formic acid, so statement D is NOT TRUE. Natural soaps are sodium or potassium salts of long-chain fatty acids, triacylglycerols are esters of glycerol and fatty acids, and long-chain carboxylic acids are correctly named fatty acids.

questions.question_text: What is the name of triacylglycerol (triglycerides) that is solid at room temperature?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fats are triacylglycerols that are solid or semi-solid at room temperature because their mostly saturated fatty acid chains pack closely together. Oils remain liquid because of unsaturation. Lecithin is a phospholipid, and waxes are esters of long-chain alcohols with fatty acids.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most important type of solute-solvent interaction in a solution of n-butanol in water?

options.label: D
