options.explanation: With phase pi/2, at time T/8 the argument is pi/4 + pi/2 = 3pi/4. The position is x = A cos(3pi/4), which is negative, and the velocity is v = -A omega sin(3pi/4), which is also negative. Hence both position and velocity are negative, option C, overriding the pre-marked A.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The position is negative and the velocity is positive.

questions.question_text: If a long rope of uniform linear density is hung from a ceiling and waves are sent up the rope from its lower end, which one of the following is true about the speed of the ascending waves?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The speed decreases as the waves ascend.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The speed increases as the waves ascend.
options.explanation: The speed of a transverse wave on a rope is sqrt(T/mu), where T is the tension. In a rope hanging from the ceiling the tension equals the weight of the rope below a given point, so it is greatest near the top. Hence the wave speed increases as the waves ascend, option B, overriding the pre-marked A.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The waves ascend with a uniform speed.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The speed of the waves is larger around the middle of the rope than around the beginning and end.

questions.question_text: A given minimum point (trough) of a sinusoidal wave is traveling 480 cm along a rope in 12 s. If the oscillator that generates the wave completes 48 vibrations in 30 s, what is the wave length of the wave?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The wave speed is v = 480 cm/12 s = 40 cm/s = 0.40 m/s. The oscillator frequency is f = 48/30 = 1.6 Hz. The wavelength is lambda = v/f = 0.40/1.6 = 0.25 m, matching the pre-marked option C.

questions.question_text: A wave traveling from a medium of index of refraction n₁ toward a medium of index of refraction n₂ undergoes partly transmission and partly reflection. If n₂ is greater than n₁ which one of the following statements is not correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The speed of the wave in the medium with reflective index n₁ is smaller than with n₂
options.explanation: A higher index of refraction means a lower wave speed, so the speed in medium n1 is greater than in n2, not smaller. Hence the statement that the speed in n1 is smaller is NOT correct, matching the pre-marked option A. The other statements about reflection are true.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The incident and the reflected waves are in phase.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The angle of reflection is the same as the angle of incidence.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The reflection angle is less than the incidence angle.

questions.question_text: In Young’s double slit experiment interference pattern which one of the following activities move the successive bright fringes farther apart?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Decreasing the wave length of the light.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Decreasing the distance between the viewing screen and the double slit.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The fringe spacing in Young's experiment is beta = lambda D/d, so the fringes move farther apart when the slit separation d decreases. Decreasing the wavelength or the screen distance brings the fringes closer, and increasing d also narrows them. Hence option D is correct, overriding the pre-marked C.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The electric field strength due to two point charges of equal magnitude and the same sign is zero only at one point on the line joining the two charges.
options.explanation: Two equal like charges produce a field that cancels only at the midpoint on the line joining them, so option A is correct. A charge released in a uniform field accelerates rather than moving uniformly, a dipole field falls as one over the cube of the distance, and a dipole is stable only when aligned with the field, so the others are false.

options.label: B
options.option_text: If a point charge of mass m is released from the rest in uniform electric field, it will move along a line of force with uniform speed.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The variation of the strength of the electric field due to an electric dipole is inversely proportional with the square of the distance from its center of mass.

options.label: D
options.option_text: An electric dipole moment p in a uniform external electric field E is in stable equilibrium if p and E are in opposite directions.

questions.question_text: In a certain region of space, a uniform electric field is directed in the positive x direction. If a particle with negative charge is carried from x = 20 cm to x = 60 cm, what can we conclude about the electric potential and the electric potential energy of the charge-field system?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The electric potential at x = 20 cm is larger than that at x = 60 cm.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The electric potential at x = 20 cm is the same as that at x = 60 cm.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Since the field points in the positive x direction, the potential decreases as x increases, so V at 20 cm exceeds V at 60 cm. For a negative charge the potential energy is U = qV, which increases as the potential decreases. Hence the electric potential energy increases, matching the pre-marked option D.

questions.question_text: A parallel plate capacitor has a capacitance of 10 µF. If the distance between the plates is doubled, keeping all other quantities constant, what is the new capacitance of the capacitor?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is C = epsilon0 A/d. Doubling the plate separation halves the capacitance. Starting from 10 microfarad, the new capacitance is therefore 5 microfarad, matching the pre-marked option B.

questions.question_text: If several resistors are connected in parallel, the equivalent resistance is

options.label: A
options.option_text: greater than any of the resistances in the group.

options.label: B
options.option_text: equal to the average resistances of the group.

options.label: C
options.option_text: less than any of the resistances in the group.
options.explanation: For resistors in parallel the reciprocal of the equivalent resistance is the sum of the reciprocals of the individual resistances, so the equivalent resistance is smaller than every individual resistance. This matches the pre-marked option C. Series connection gives the sum, and the other options are incorrect.

options.label: D
options.option_text: equal to the sum of the resistances in the group.

questions.question_text: In aluminium and copper wires with circular cross sections have equal length and equal resistance, then the ratio of the radius of aluminium to that of copper should be the same as that of the

options.label: A
options.option_text: ratio of the resistivity of aluminium to copper

options.label: B
options.option_text: ratio of the resistivity of copper to aluminium

options.label: C
options.option_text: square root of the ratio of the resistivity of aluminium to copper
options.explanation: For equal lengths and resistances, R = rho L/A gives rho_al/A_al = rho_cu/A_cu, so the areas are in the ratio rho_al/rho_cu. Since the area is proportional to the square of the radius, the radii are in the ratio of the square root of the resistivities of aluminium to copper, option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: square root of the ratio of the resistivity of copper to aluminium

questions.question_text: In the circuit shown below, what is the potential difference between point b and a?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The potential difference between points b and a requires the battery voltages, resistances and branches shown in the circuit figure, which is not present in the transcript. Without the diagram the loop equations cannot be solved. The item is therefore defective and the pre-marked option C is retained.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct about the effect and formation of field?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A magnetic field exerts a nonzero force on a stationary charge object.

options.label: B
options.option_text: A magnetic field exerts a nonzero force on a conducting wire placed in the field.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A uniform magnetic field can be created at all points around a long current carrying wire.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A magnetic field can be created in the space surrounding any charged object that is in motion.
options.explanation: A magnetic field is created in the space surrounding any charged object that is in motion, so option D is a correct statement. A stationary charge experiences no magnetic force, a wire experiences force only when carrying current, and the field around a long wire is not uniform, so the other options are false.

questions.question_text: An electron moving at a speed of 1.5 × 10⁷ m/s enters a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude 2 × 10⁻³ T, direction perpendicular to the field. The path followed by the electron is circular. What is the radius of the circular path?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The radius of the circular path is r = mv/(qB). Substituting m = 9.11 x 10^-31 kg, v = 1.5 x 10^7 m/s, q = 1.6 x 10^-19 C and B = 2 x 10^-3 T gives r = 1.3665 x 10^-23/3.2 x 10^-22 = 0.0427 m = 4.27 cm, about 4.3 cm, matching option B.

questions.question_text: If a wire carrying current in the plane of this paper toward the top of the page experiences a magnetic force toward the right edge of the page, what will be the direction of the magnetic field causing this force?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In the plane of the page and toward the left edge.

options.label: B
options.option_text: In the plane of the page and toward the bottom edge.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Perpendicular and directed out of the plane of the page.
options.explanation: The magnetic force on a wire is F = IL x B. With the current toward the top of the page and the force toward the right, the right-hand rule gives the magnetic field perpendicular to the page and directed out of it, since up crossed with out-of-page yields right. This matches the pre-marked option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Perpendicular and directed into the plane of the page.

questions.question_text: A square flat loop of wire is placed in a uniform magnetic field that is in the y direction. The magnetic flux through the loop is a maximum if the plane of the loop is in the

options.label: B
options.explanation: Magnetic flux is Phi = BA cos theta, maximum when the field is perpendicular to the loop area, meaning the loop's plane is perpendicular to the field. For a field in the y direction the loop must lie in the xz plane, so its normal is along y. This matches the pre-marked option B.

options.label: D
options.option_text: inclined 45° with respect to the xy plane

questions.question_text: Which one of the following actions increases the magnetic energy density in the interior of a very long current carrying solenoid?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Increasing the number of turns per unit length of the solenoid.
options.explanation: The magnetic energy density in a solenoid is u = B^2/(2 mu0) with B = mu0 n I. Increasing the number of turns per unit length increases B and therefore the energy density. Changing the cross-sectional area or the total length does not change B, so option A is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Increasing the cross section area of the solenoid.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Increasing the length of the solenoid keeping the number of turns per unit length fixed.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Decreasing the cross section area of the solenoid.

questions.question_text: Figure below shows a rectangular loop of wire of width L and resistance R. one end of the loop is in a uniform magnetic field of strength B directed perpendicular into the plane of the page, the loop is pulled to the right at a constant speed v. what are the magnitude and direction of the induced current in the loop?

options.label: B
options.explanation: As the loop is pulled out of the field, the magnetic flux through it decreases. The induced emf is emf = BLv, so the induced current is I = BLv/R. The direction opposes the decrease by Lenz's law and is clockwise as pre-marked, giving option B.

questions.question_text: A series RLC circuit has a total impedance of 75.0 Ω. If the resistance is R = 45.0 Ω and the average power delivered to the circuit is P = 352.8 W, what is the root mean square value of the ac voltage source?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The average power is P = V_rms^2 R/Z^2, so the rms voltage is V_rms = sqrt(P Z^2/R). Substituting P = 352.8 W, Z = 75 ohm and R = 45 ohm gives V_rms = sqrt(352.8 x 5625/45) = sqrt(44100) = 210 V, matching the pre-marked option C.

questions.question_text: Which of the following phenomena most clearly demonstrates the wave nature of electrons?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The wave nature of electrons is most clearly demonstrated by diffraction of electrons by crystals, where the periodic atomic lattice acts as a diffraction grating. The photoelectric, blackbody and Compton effects demonstrate the particle nature of light or its energy quantization. Hence option D is correct.

questions.question_text: When the radioactive element ¹⁴⁴Nd₆₀ decays to ¹⁴⁰Ce₅₈, which one of the following particles is emitted?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The decay changes the mass number from 144 to 140, a decrease of 4, and the atomic number from 60 to 58, a decrease of 2. Such a change is characteristic of the emission of an alpha particle. Hence an alpha particle is emitted, matching the pre-marked option B.

questions.question_text: A man is standing on a spring scale in an elevator. When the elevator is at rest, the scale reads 560 N. When the elevator starts to move, the scale reads 600 N. The elevator has

options.label: A
options.explanation: The scale reading equals the normal force on the man. When the reading of 600 N exceeds the rest weight of 560 N, the net force on the man is upward, so the elevator must be accelerating upward. Hence the elevator has an upward acceleration, matching the pre-marked option A.

questions.question_text: What is the necessary and sufficient condition for conservation of linear momentum?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The presence of more linear than non-linear forces in the system.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Net force on the system is zero.
options.explanation: Linear momentum is conserved when the net external force on the system is zero, because the momentum change equals the net external impulse. Internal forces cancel in pairs and cannot change the total momentum. Hence the necessary and sufficient condition is a zero net force, option B.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The presence of only non-linear forces.

questions.question_text: Which statement is wrong about units and dimensions?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Two quantities can have the same units but different dimensions.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Two quantities can have the same dimensions but different units.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is always possible to add two numbers that have the same units.
options.explanation: Quantities with the same dimensions may have different units, and quantities with the same units may have different dimensions, so options A and B are true. However, it is not always physically meaningful to add two numbers with the same units, so option C is the wrong statement, as pre-marked.

options.label: D
options.option_text: There are quantities that have no units and dimension.

questions.question_text: An airplane flies at speed of 720.0 km/hr at 37° North of west direction. How far does the plane travel to the west in 1 hour?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The plane flies at 37 degrees north of west, so the westward component of its velocity is 720 cos37 = 720 x 0.8 = 576 km/hr. In one hour it travels 576 km to the west. This matches the pre-marked option C.

questions.question_text: Abrehet (A), Bekele (B) and Chaltu (C) are pulling a box horizontally with forces F⃗_A, F⃗_B and F⃗_C, respectively as shown below, which statement is correct if the box is in equilibrium?

options.label: B
options.explanation: For the box to be in equilibrium the vector sum of the three forces must be zero, so F_A + F_B + F_C = 0. None of the printed relations involving products or single subtractions represents this correctly. The item is therefore defective and the pre-marked option B is retained.

questions.question_text: Determine the torque in Nm due to a force F = (2î + 4k̂) N acting at point r = (3î + 2ĵ + 3k̂) m about the origin?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The torque is tau = r x F with r = (3,2,3) and F = (2,0,4). The i component is (2)(4) - (3)(0) = 8, the j component is (3)(2) - (3)(4) = -6, and the k component is (3)(0) - (2)(2) = -4. Hence tau = 8i - 6j - 4k, which is not printed; the item is defective and pre-marked C is retained.

questions.question_text: An airplane travelled from Addis Ababa to Mekele, 780 km in 45 minutes. What was its average speed?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Average speed is the total distance divided by the total time. The airplane covers 780 km in 45 minutes, which is 0.75 hours, so the speed is 780/0.75 = 1040 km/hr. This matches the pre-marked option B. The other values come from unit errors.

questions.question_text: An example of a body moving with constant speed but still accelerating is

options.label: A
options.option_text: a body moving on a straight road.

options.label: B
options.option_text: a body moving on a straight railway track

options.label: C
options.option_text: a body moving in a circular path
options.explanation: A body moving in a circular path at constant speed is always accelerating because its direction changes continuously, so the velocity is not constant. This is an example of constant speed with acceleration, matching the pre-marked option C. Motion on straight roads or tracks at constant speed has no acceleration.

options.label: D
options.option_text: a body falling in a viscous fluid.

questions.question_text: A student moves along the boundary of a square field of side 10 m in 40 sec. if he starts from one end of the corners of the square what will be the magnitude of the displacement of the student at the end of 2 minutes and 20 seconds from his initial position?

options.label: B
options.explanation: One lap of the square takes 40 s, so in 140 s the student completes 3.5 laps, ending at the corner diagonally opposite the start. The displacement is the diagonal of the square, which is 10 sqrt2 m. This matches the pre-marked option B.

questions.question_text: The graph below illustrates the position and time for a cat that runs to catch a rat and then returns with it. The cat caught the rat after 2 seconds. What was the cat’s average speed as it returned with it?

options.label: A
options.option_text: its average return speed was 2 m/s.

options.label: B
options.option_text: its average return speed was 4 m/s.

options.label: C
options.option_text: its average return speed was 0.7 m/s.

options.label: D
options.option_text: its average return speed was 0.9 m/s.
options.explanation: The cat's return speed depends on the position-time graph shown in the figure, which is not present in the transcript. Without the graph the return distance and time cannot be read. The item is therefore defective and the pre-marked option D is retained.

questions.question_text: A uniform 6 m long and 600 N beam, rest on two supports as shown. The forces exerted on the beam by the right support B is closest to:

options.label: C
options.explanation: The force exerted by the right support depends on the placement of the supports along the 6 m beam shown in the figure, which is not present in the transcript. Without the diagram the moment balance cannot be computed. The item is therefore defective and the pre-marked option C is retained.

questions.question_text: A rod PQ is attached at P to a vertical wall, as shown in the figure below. The length of the rod is 1.8 m. The weight W of the rod acts at 0.60 m from P. The rod is kept horizontal and in equilibrium by a wire attached to Q and to the wall at R. The wire provides a force F on the rod of 50 N at 30° to the horizontal. By taking moments about P determine the weight W of the rod.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Taking moments about P, the wire force provides a counterclockwise moment of 50 x 1.8 x sin30 = 45 N m. This balances the clockwise moment of the weight, W x 0.60. Hence 0.60 W = 45, giving W = 75 N, which matches the pre-marked option C.

questions.question_text: A large mass (A) and a small mass (B) are pushing one another apart, as shown in the figure below. The small mass moves away at a velocity of 20 m/s to the right. What is the recoil velocity of the large mass?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The recoil velocity of the large mass depends on the masses of A and B shown in the figure, which is not present in the transcript. Without the mass values the momentum conservation equation cannot be evaluated. The item is therefore defective and the pre-marked option D is retained.

questions.question_text: Find the distance of the center of mass of the system shown in the diagram from point A. The rod is mass less

options.label: A
options.explanation: The center of mass distance from point A depends on the masses and positions shown in the diagram, which is not present in the transcript. Without the diagram the weighted-average calculation cannot be performed. The item is therefore defective and the pre-marked option A is retained.

questions.question_text: The area under a force versus distance graph represents

options.label: D
options.explanation: The area under a force versus distance graph gives the work done by the force, because work is the integral of force over displacement. The area under a force-time graph gives impulse, so option D is the correct interpretation.

questions.question_text: A net external non zero force acts on a particle that is moving along a straight line which one of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The velocity, but not the kinetic energy of the particle is changing.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Both the velocity and kinetic energy of the particle are changing.
options.explanation: A net nonzero force produces an acceleration, so the velocity of the particle changes. Since kinetic energy depends on the speed, it also changes as the particle speeds up or slows down along the straight line. Hence both the velocity and kinetic energy change, matching the pre-marked option B.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The kinetic energy but not the velocity of the particle is changing.

questions.question_text: Which statement is correct about conservative and dissipative force?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The work done by conservative forces is path dependent.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The work done along a closed path by non-conservative forces is non zero.
options.explanation: The work done by non-conservative forces depends on the path, so around a closed path the net work is generally nonzero and equal to the mechanical energy lost. Conservative forces do zero work on closed paths, and gravity is conservative while friction is not. Hence option B is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Gravitational force is an example of non-conservative force.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Friction is an example of conservative force.

questions.question_text: The rotational analogue of mass is

options.label: A
options.explanation: In rotational motion the moment of inertia plays the role that mass plays in linear motion, resisting changes in angular velocity. Torque is the analogue of force, and angular momentum and angular acceleration are the rotational counterparts of momentum and acceleration. Hence moment of inertia, option A, is correct.

questions.question_text: A fly wheel is rotating with an angular velocity of 2.0 rad/s acted by an acceleration of 1/π rad/s². How long will it take to complete three revolutions?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Using theta = omega0 t + (1/2)alpha t^2 with theta = 6 pi rad, omega0 = 2 rad/s and alpha = 1/pi rad/s^2, the equation becomes 6 pi = 2t + t^2/(2 pi). Testing t = 2 pi gives 4 pi + 2 pi = 6 pi, so the time is 2 pi seconds, matching the pre-marked option C.

questions.question_text: If the impulse of a rotating disc is non zero what can you conclude?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The change in linear momentum is zero.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The torque acting on object is constant.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Impulse of the disc equals its moment of inertia.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The change in angular momentum is non zero.
options.explanation: Angular impulse is the product of torque and time and equals the change in angular momentum of the body. A nonzero angular impulse therefore implies a nonzero change in angular momentum. This matches the pre-marked option D.

questions.question_text: The number of joules of heat energy required to raise the temperature of a body by 1 K is

options.label: A
options.explanation: Heat capacity is the amount of heat, in joules, required to raise the temperature of a body by one kelvin. Specific heat capacity is the corresponding quantity per unit mass. Since the question refers to the whole body, heat capacity is correct, matching the pre-marked option A.

questions.question_text: A simple pendulum is made using a long thin metal wire. What happens to the period of the pendulum when the temperature drops?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The period of a simple pendulum is T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g). When the temperature drops, the metal wire contracts, so the pendulum length decreases and the period becomes shorter. Hence the period decreases, matching the pre-marked option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: period of oscillation has random dependence on temperature.

questions.question_text: Pressure at the bottom of a liquid column is independent of:

options.label: A
options.explanation: The pressure at the bottom of a liquid column is P = P_atm + rho g h, which depends on the density, depth and gravity but not on the shape of the container. Hence the pressure is independent of the shape of the column, matching the pre-marked option A.

questions.question_text: The definition of Young’s modulus is given by

options.label: C
options.explanation: Young's modulus is defined as the ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain, Y = (F/A)/(Delta L/L), a measure of stiffness. Option A gives stress alone and option B inverts the ratio, while option D ignores the area. Hence option C is the correct definition, overriding the pre-marked A.

questions.question_text: A water pipe has a diameter of 5.0 cm in the inlet side and 1.5 cm in the outlet side. Water flows at 0.50 m³ per minute at the inlet point. What is the speed of the water at the outlet point?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The flow rate is 0.50 m^3/min = 8.333 x 10^-3 m^3/s. The outlet area is pi(0.0075)^2 = 1.767 x 10^-4 m^2. The outlet speed is Q/A = 8.333 x 10^-3/1.767 x 10^-4 = 47.2 m/s, approximately 46.99 m/s, matching the pre-marked option A.

questions.question_text: A metal ball has a diameter that is slightly greater than the diameter of a hole that has been cut into a metal plate. The coefficient of linear expansion for the metal from which the ball is made is greater than that for the metal of the plate. Which one of the following procedures can be used to make the ball pass through the hole?

options.label: A
options.option_text: raise the temperatures of the ball and the plate by the same amount.

options.label: B
options.option_text: heat the ball and cool the plate.

options.label: C
options.option_text: lower the temperatures of the ball and the plate by the same amount.
options.explanation: When both the ball and the plate are cooled, the ball shrinks by more than the hole because its coefficient of expansion is larger. This makes the ball small enough to pass through the hole. Heating or cooling them differently would worsen the fit, so option C is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: there is no way of passing the ball through the hole.

questions.question_text: A billiard ball of radius 4 cm is falling through a liquid of viscosity 0.985 at a velocity of 2.5 m/s the drag force on the ball is

options.label: A
options.explanation: The Stokes drag force on a sphere is F = 6 pi r eta v. With r = 0.04 m, eta = 0.985 and v = 2.5 m/s, this gives F = 6 pi x 0.04 x 0.985 x 2.5 = 0.591 pi N. This matches the pre-marked option A.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Elastic materials retain their shape after deformation.
options.explanation: Elastic materials return to their original shape when the deforming force is removed, so they retain their shape after the deformation is reversed. Plastic materials permanently deform and cannot recover their original shape. Hence option A is the correct statement.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Plastic materials can recover the original size or shape after being distorted.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Plastic materials change their shape by pressure.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Elastic materials cannot recover the original size or shape after being distorted.

questions.question_text: Two bodies that are separately in thermal equilibrium with a third body must be in thermal equilibrium with each other. This statement is statement of

options.label: B
options.explanation: The statement that two bodies each in thermal equilibrium with a third body are in thermal equilibrium with each other is the zeroth law of thermodynamics. It provides the basis for temperature measurement. Hence option B is correct.

questions.question_text: A device for transforming heat energy to mechanical energy is referred to as

options.label: D
options.explanation: An engine is a device that transforms heat energy into mechanical energy by operating in a cycle. A transformer changes voltage, a refrigerant absorbs heat, and a generator converts mechanical to electrical energy. Hence option D is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Three resistors connected in series have individual voltages labelled, Δv₁, Δv₂ and Δv₃ respectively. Which of the following expresses the value of the voltage Δv_T taken over the three resistors together?

options.label: A
options.explanation: For resistors connected in series the same current flows through each, and the total voltage across the combination is the sum of the individual voltage drops. Hence Delta v_T = Delta v1 + Delta v2 + Delta v3, matching the pre-marked option A.

questions.question_text: Which instrument should ideally have zero resistance?

options.label: D
options.explanation: An ammeter is connected in series with the circuit, so to avoid affecting the current it should ideally have zero resistance. A voltmeter, connected in parallel, should ideally have infinite resistance. Hence the instrument that should have zero resistance is the ammeter, option D, overriding the pre-marked C.

questions.question_text: What fundamental frequency can a string vibrate at if it is 30 cm long and the velocity of traveling waves along the string is 120 m/s?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The fundamental frequency of a string fixed at both ends is f = v/(2L). With v = 120 m/s and L = 30 cm = 0.30 m, this gives f = 120/0.60 = 200 Hz, matching the pre-marked option D.

questions.question_text: The hearing curve shown below indicates the vibration of the threshold of hearing with frequency. The ear is most sensitive at the point indicated by

options.label: C
options.explanation: The point where the ear is most sensitive is read from the hearing threshold curve shown in the figure, which is not present in the transcript. Without the graph the most sensitive frequency cannot be identified. The item is therefore defective and the pre-marked option C is retained.

questions.question_text: A wavelength is

options.label: A
options.option_text: A line that represents the direction of propagation of light.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The minimum distance between two points that are in phase.
options.explanation: A wavelength is the minimum distance between two successive points of a wave that are in phase, such as two adjacent crests. A wavefront is the locus of in-phase points, and the number of waves per unit time is the frequency. Hence option B is the correct definition.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The locus of all points of a travelling wave that are in phase.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The number of waves crossing a given plane in a unit time.

questions.question_text: The viewed in white light soap bubbles show color because of

options.label: A
options.explanation: The colors seen on soap bubbles arise from thin-film interference, where light reflecting from the two surfaces of the film interferes constructively for some wavelengths and destructively for others. Dispersion and scattering do not explain the pattern, so option A is correct, overriding the pre-marked B.

questions.question_text: In the sketch below, which best describes the location of the negative charges (electrons) when a negatively charged rod is brought near but not touching the conducting sphere?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The location of the electrons on the conducting sphere when a negatively charged rod is brought near depends on the sketch labels shown in the figure, which is not present in the transcript. Without the diagram the charge distribution cannot be identified. The item is defective and the pre-marked option B is retained.

questions.question_text: What is the potential (V) at a distance of 10 m from a charge of +5.0 C?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The electric potential at distance r from a point charge is V = kQ/r. With k = 9 x 10^9, Q = 5 C and r = 10 m, this gives V = 9 x 10^9 x 5/10 = 4.5 x 10^9 V, approximately 4.45 x 10^9 V, matching the pre-marked option C.

questions.question_text: A positive charge of 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ C is on the negatively charged plate of a parallel plate capacitor as shown below. If the potential (V) on the top plate is +10,000 V and that of the bottom plate is −10,000 V, how much work (w) is required to move the charge from the bottom to the top plate?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The work required to move a charge through a potential difference is W = q Delta V. Moving the charge from the bottom plate at -10000 V to the top plate at +10000 V gives Delta V = 20000 V, so W = 1.0 x 10^-4 x 20000 = 2.0 J, matching the pre-marked option A.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about galvanometer?

options.label: A
options.option_text: it is used to measure small amount of current.

options.label: C
options.option_text: it can be used to measure voltage if shunted with large load in series.
options.explanation: A galvanometer measures small currents and works on the same principle as an electric motor. To measure voltage it must be connected in series with a large resistance, not shunted with a large load, so option C is NOT correct, as pre-marked.

options.label: D
options.option_text: its working principle is the same as that of the electric motor.

questions.question_text: The activity of a radioactive source falls to one sixteenth of its original value in 32 minutes. What is the half-life in minutes of this decay process?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The activity falls to one sixteenth, which equals one half raised to the fourth power, so four half-lives elapse in 32 minutes. The half-life is therefore 32/4 = 8 minutes, which matches option B rather than the pre-marked C.

questions.question_text: Which statements is Not correct about emission from radioactive isotopes?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Alpha particles are positively charged and less penetrating than beta and gamma.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Beta particles are negatively charged and more penetrating than alpha particles.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Alpha emissions are least influenced by magnetic field.
options.explanation: Alpha particles are charged, so they are deflected by magnetic fields, whereas gamma rays are least influenced. Hence the statement that alpha emissions are least influenced by a magnetic field is NOT correct, matching the pre-marked option C. The other statements are true.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the most penetrating emissions are gamma particles.

questions.question_text: The torque experienced by a current carrying loop, in an external, magnetic field is:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Independent of the number of turns of the loop.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Independent of the current in the loop.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Dependent on the orientation of the loop.
options.explanation: The torque on a current-carrying loop is tau = NIAB sin theta, which depends on the number of turns, the current, the field and the orientation angle theta of the loop relative to the field. Hence the torque depends on the orientation, matching the pre-marked option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Dependent on magnetic field generated according to Lenz’s law.

questions.question_text: Two long wires of the same length and cross sectional area carry the same amount of current. Which one of the following statements is correct about the magnetic field and the magnetic forces on the wires?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The magnetic field is zero at the midpoint between the wires when the currents are in the same direction.
options.explanation: At the midpoint between two long parallel wires carrying equal currents in the same direction, the fields from the two wires point in opposite directions and cancel, so the field is zero there. Wires with opposite currents repel, and the fields between the wires reinforce for opposite currents, so option A is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The force is attractive between the wires when they carry current in opposite direction.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The magnetic fields between the wires reinforce each other when the currents are in the same direction.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The magnetic field due to one is proportional to the current through the other wire.

questions.question_text: Self-inductance is a quantity that describes

options.label: A
options.option_text: The number of turns in a circuit.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The induction of an electric field by an AC current in a lone coil.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The induction of a magnetic field by an AC current in alone coil.
options.explanation: Self-inductance is the property of a coil by which a changing current induces an emf in the coil itself through its own magnetic field. Hence it describes the induction of a magnetic field by an alternating current in a single coil, matching the pre-marked option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The steady state current in a coil.

questions.question_text: Which conversion process forms the bases for the function of an electric generator?

options.label: B
options.explanation: An electric generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by rotating a coil in a magnetic field and using electromagnetic induction. A motor does the reverse, and a transformer changes voltage. Hence option B describes the basis of the generator's function.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Low voltage to high voltage or vice versa.

questions.question_text: What is the change in magnetic flux in a coil of area 5 m² as its orientation relative to the perpendicular of uniform 3.0 T magnetic field changes from 45° to 90°?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Magnetic flux is Phi = BA cos theta. Initially, Phi = 3 x 5 x cos45 = 10.6 Wb, and finally at 90 degrees Phi = 0. The change in flux is 0 - 10.6 = -10.6 Wb, about -11 Wb, matching the pre-marked option B.

questions.question_text: A simple transformer is illustrated in the figure below, why is it that the core is laminated?

options.label: A
options.option_text: To increase the induced current in the primary coil.

options.label: B
options.option_text: To increase the induced current in the secondary coil.

options.label: C
options.option_text: To avoid heat exchange between the primary and secondary coils.

options.label: D
options.option_text: To reduce the loss in power in the core due to eddy currents.
options.explanation: The transformer core is laminated to reduce eddy currents induced in the core, which would otherwise heat it and waste power. Dividing the core into thin insulated sheets confines the eddy currents and lowers the power loss. Hence option D is correct, overriding the pre-marked C.

questions.question_text: A common unit of energy in atomic physics is

options.label: B
options.explanation: The electron volt is a convenient unit of energy in atomic and nuclear physics, equal to the energy gained by an electron moving through one volt. Planck's constant, de Broglie wavelength and the uncertainty principle are not units of energy. Hence option B is correct.

questions.question_text: In photoelectric effect, the energy of photoelectrons is proportional to the

options.label: A
options.explanation: In the photoelectric effect the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons is given by KEmax = hf - phi, which is proportional to the frequency of the incident light. The intensity affects the number of electrons, not their energy. Hence option A is correct.

questions.question_text: The range of cannon-ball fired horizontally from a laboratory table is equal to 8/3 times the height of the table. What is the direction of velocity vector of the projectile as it strikes the ground?

options.label: D
options.explanation: For a horizontal launch the horizontal velocity stays equal to the initial speed u while the vertical component grows as gt, and the range equals 8h/3 with time of fall t = sqrt(2h/g). Hence u = (8h/3)/t and tan of the impact angle is gt/u = 3/4, giving 37 degrees, option D.

questions.question_text: Galileo carried out a thought experiment on motion. The line between A and B represents a surface and the center of the ball is placed at A. What would happen in each of the three situations shown in the figure below, without friction when the ball is released?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The ball would never reach point B in all instances.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The ball would reach B in all instances even if point B keeps on receding to infinity in (c).
options.explanation: In Galileo frictionless thought experiment the ball must always rise to the same height from which it was released, so it reaches B in every case. When the surface keeps sloping so B recedes to infinity, the ball never stops but keeps moving forever, so option B describes the outcome correctly.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The ball would reach point B in (a) and (b) and not in (c).

options.label: D
options.option_text: The ball would reach point B only in (a).

questions.question_text: A uranium atom initially at rest has a mass of 2 units and spontaneously disintegrated into two fragments. One of the fragments has a mass of 0.8 units and moves at a speed of 24 m/s as shown in figure below. What is the speed of the second fragments?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The nucleus is initially at rest, so the total momentum before disintegration is zero and the two fragments must carry equal and opposite momenta. The first fragment has momentum 0.8 times 24, which equals 19.2 units, so the second fragment, having mass 1.2 units, moves at 16 m/s, option C.

questions.question_text: A 1 kg object explodes and breaks up into three pieces. One piece has a mass of 400 g and has a velocity of (15î + 10ĵ) m/s. A second piece has a mass of 250 g and has a velocity of (25î + 10ĵ) m/s. What is the velocity of the third piece?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Momentum conservation requires the third piece to balance the x and y momentum of the first two pieces, giving a velocity near minus 35 i minus 18.6 j m/s. Since that vector does not appear among the printed options and the pre-marked option B does not balance momentum either, the item is defective.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Dynamic equilibrium is an equilibrium in which a body is moving at steady velocity without net force or torque acting on it.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Static equilibrium is an equilibrium in which a body is at rest without net force or torque acting on it.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Couples are set of forces with a resultant torque but no net force.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The necessary and sufficient condition for equilibrium of a rigid body is to have the sum of all torques acting on it is zero.
options.explanation: A rigid body is in equilibrium only when both the net force and the net torque on it are zero. Claiming that zero total torque alone is the necessary and sufficient condition ignores the first condition of equilibrium, so statement D is not correct and is the required answer.

questions.question_text: A spring with a spring constant of 300 N/m is stretched 20 cm in 2 seconds. What is the power applied to stretch the spring?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The work done in stretching a spring is half times the spring constant times the square of the extension, which equals half of 300 times 0.04, giving 6 J. Since this work is done in two seconds, the power is 6 divided by 2, which is 3 W, option A.

questions.question_text: A 50 KW machine is used to lift heavy objects to the top of a building under construction. If this machine is replaced with a new machine of 100 KW power, then which of the following statements is not true about the new machine?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The new machine can raise objects with the same mass at twice the speed of the old machine.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The new machine can raise objects with twice as much mass at the same speed as the old machine.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The new machine takes twice as much time to do the same work as the old machine.
options.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work, so a 100 kW machine does the same work in half the time as a 50 kW machine, not twice the time. It can lift the same mass at double speed, double the mass at the same speed, or do double the work in the same time, so option C is not true.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The new machine can do twice as much work in the same time as the old machine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about a work done for dissipative force?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The work done against dissipative forces such as friction depends on the path taken between two points, not only on the initial and final positions. Hence the work is path dependent, which matches option A, whereas the other choices describe energy changes that are not generally equal to the dissipative work.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The same as the loss in kinetic energy.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The same as the gain in potential energy.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The same as the potential energy stored in spring.

questions.question_text: A disk of radius R with uniform distribution of mass M rotates about an axis perpendicular to its plane at the rim with angular speed ω. The moment of inertia of the disc about the axis through the center is ½MR². What is the kinetic energy of the disk?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The axis at the rim is at distance R from the center of mass, so the parallel axis theorem gives I equal to half MR squared plus MR squared, which is three halves MR squared. The rotational kinetic energy is half times this inertia times omega squared, giving three quarters MR squared omega squared, option D.

questions.question_text: A pulley is rotating at a frequency of 20 rev/min. a motor speeds up the wheel so that 30 s later the frequency of the motion is 60 rev/min. How far a point on the pool 0.30 m from its center will has travelled during that period?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The angular acceleration equals the change in angular frequency divided by 30 seconds, giving about 0.14 rad/s squared. The angular displacement during the 30 second interval is then about 125.7 radians, and multiplying by the radius 0.30 m gives 37.7 m travelled by the point, option C.

questions.question_text: A block of mass m₁ = 10 kg placed on a frictionless incline plane connected to mass m₂ = 15 kg using a string of negligible mass passing over a pulley of moment of inertia I = 0.25 kg m² and radius R = 10 cm as shown in the diagram. What is the torque on the pulley?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The torque on the pulley depends on the difference of the two string tensions multiplied by the radius, and the tensions themselves depend on the angle of the incline shown in the missing diagram. Since the incline angle is not given in the transcript, the value cannot be verified, so the item is defective.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct about the first condition of equilibrium?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The net force on an object must be zero.
options.explanation: The first condition of equilibrium states that a body can be in equilibrium only when the vector sum of all forces acting on it is zero. This is a statement about forces rather than torques, so option A is correct, while the other choices refer to the second condition of equilibrium.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The sum of all torques must be zero.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Clockwise moments should balance counter clockwise moments.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The torque produced by a force should be perpendicular to the force.

questions.question_text: A 4 m long uniform board of mass 10 kg hinged on the ground at one end is hanging by a string at the other end. A block of mass 8 kg is placed at 1 m from the hinge on the ground as shown in the diagram below. What is the tension in the string?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Taking torques about the hinge, the string tension at the far end balances the weights. The board of mass 10 kg acts at its center 2 m away, and the 8 kg block acts 1 m from the hinge, so 4 T equals 200 plus 80, giving T equal to 70 N, option C.

questions.question_text: Which of the following refers to the definition of strain as a ratio?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Strain is defined as the ratio of the change in length, namely the extension, to the original length of the object. It is a dimensionless quantity, whereas force per area and the other ratios given are not the definition, so option A is the correct answer.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Force applied to area of the object normal to the force.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the application of Pascal’s law?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pascal law states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally to every part of the fluid and the container walls. The hydraulic brake uses this principle to multiply force, whereas a siphon, submarines and syringes depend on other effects, so option A is the application.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Sucking of liquid into a syringe.

questions.question_text: A large (very large in height and cross-section) water open at the top has a small hole through its side near the bottom. To what height should the water be filled, to double the speed of water that flow out of the hole when it was filled to a height h?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Torricelli law gives the efflux speed as the square root of 2gh, so the speed is proportional to the square root of the filling height. To double the speed the height must be multiplied by four, giving 4h, option D, not the pre-marked 2h.

questions.question_text: If a precision of surveyor measured a distance of 500 meters /between two points in a village/ using a meter that has centimetre division on it, then what is the measurement result?

options.label: C
options.explanation: A meter rule with centimetre divisions allows lengths to be read to one more place, that is, to the nearest tenth of a centimetre or 0.001 m. A measured distance of 500 m should therefore be recorded with three decimal places as 500.00 m, which is option C.

questions.question_text: From the figures given below, which one of them shows precise but not accurate measurements? T represents the true value.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The figures needed to judge which set of measurements is precise but not accurate are not present in the transcript. Without seeing the distribution of readings around the true value T the question cannot be answered, so the item is defective and the pre-marked option A is retained.

questions.question_text: If vector P⃗ is 6 m in the x-direction and vector q⃗ is 8 m in the y-direction. Then what is the value of the vector p⃗ + q⃗?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The two vectors are perpendicular, so the resultant magnitude is the square root of 6 squared plus 8 squared, which is 10 m. The direction is the arctangent of 8 over 6, which is 53 degrees from the x direction, matching option A.

questions.question_text: Given vectors A⃗ = √3 î + ĵ and B⃗ = −√3 î − ĵ. What is the smaller angle between the vectors?

options.label: A
options.explanation: As transcribed, vector B is exactly the negative of vector A, so the angle between them is 180 degrees, which is not among the printed options. The pre-marked 60 degrees presumably corresponds to a different version, so the item is defective and option A is retained.

questions.question_text: If A⃗ = x̂ m/s + 3 m/s ẑ and B⃗ = 2 m/s ŷ + 3 m/s ẑ, then what is the value of |A⃗ × B⃗|?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The cross product of A and B has components given by the determinant of the unit vectors, yielding minus 6 in x, minus 3 in y and 2 in z. The magnitude is the square root of 36 plus 9 plus 4, which equals 7 m/s, so option C is correct.

questions.question_text: A cricketer throws a ball vertically upwards with initial speed of 20 m/s. How long is it in the air before it returns to the cricketer’s hands?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The total time of flight for a projectile thrown vertically is twice the time taken to reach maximum height, which is the initial speed divided by g. Here that is 20 divided by 10, so the upward time is 2 seconds and the total time in the air is 4 seconds, option D.

questions.question_text: Abeba walks to school. She walks 1 km in 15 minutes. She meets her friend Makeda they talk for 5 minutes and then carry on walking to school. They walk 800 m in 10 minutes. Which of the following displacement time graph shows Abeba’s journey to school?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The displacement-time graph for Abeba journey is not included in the transcript. The correct graph should show two increasing segments with a horizontal flat portion where the girls talk for five minutes, but it cannot be selected without seeing the figures, so the item is defective.

questions.question_text: A fun making boy swings a blinking ball tied to the end of a string in a vertical circle. If the radius of the circle is 0.5 m, then what should be the minimum speed of the ball at the bottom of the circle to make a complete circular motion at the top?

options.label: A
options.explanation: At the top of the circle the minimum speed is the square root of gR, which equals the square root of 5 m/s. By energy conservation the square of the speed at the bottom equals that at the top plus 4gR, giving 5 plus 20, so the bottom speed is 5 m/s, option A.

questions.question_text: The activity of radioactive substance reduces from 2000 Bq to 1000 Bq in 10⁶ seconds. What is the decay constant?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The activity falls to half its value in 10 to the sixth seconds, so this interval is the half-life. The decay constant lambda equals the natural logarithm of 2 divided by the half-life, which is 0.693 divided by 10 to the sixth, giving 6.93 times 10 to the minus 7 per second, option B.

questions.question_text: Which of the following phenomena clearly demonstrates the particle nature of light?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The photoelectric effect shows that light transfers energy in discrete packets or photons, each photon carrying energy proportional to its frequency. This behaviour cannot be explained by treating light purely as a wave, so it demonstrates the particle nature of light, making option B correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Diffraction of light by double slit.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Irreversible process is a process that can be reversed through finite change in the system.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Complete conversion of energy from a hot source into work is possible.

options.label: C
options.option_text: There are processes in which there is an overall decrease in entropy.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Entropy is a measure of the amount of disorder.
options.explanation: Entropy is a measure of the disorder or randomness of a system, so option D is a correct statement. Irreversible processes cannot be reversed through finite changes, complete conversion of heat into work is impossible, and entropy never decreases overall in real processes, so the other options are false.

questions.question_text: A certain heat engine draws 500 cal/s from a water bath at 27°C and rejects 400 calories to a reservoir at a lower temperature. What is the efficiency of this engine?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The useful work output of the engine is the heat absorbed minus the heat rejected, which is 500 minus 400, giving 100 cal/s. Efficiency is the work output divided by the heat input, so 100 divided by 500 equals 0.20, or 20 percent, matching option D.

questions.question_text: Three metals are in contact and in thermal equilibrium. The metals have different specific heat capacity. What can be concluded about the temperature of the metals?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Since they have different specific heat capacity, they must have different temperature at thermal equilibrium.

options.label: B
options.option_text: They must have the same temperature at thermal equilibrium.
options.explanation: When two or more bodies are in thermal equilibrium they must have the same temperature, otherwise heat would flow between them until equality is reached. The specific heat capacities do not affect the equilibrium temperature condition, so option B is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: They must have different internal energy.

options.label: D
options.option_text: They must have different kinetic energy.

questions.question_text: Metal A has a coefficient of linear expansion that is three times the coefficient of linear expansion of metal B. How does their coefficient of areal expansion, Y, compare?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The areal expansion coefficient of a material is twice its linear expansion coefficient. Since metal A has three times the linear coefficient of metal B, its areal coefficient is two times three times the linear value of B, which equals three times the areal coefficient of B, so Y A equals 3 Y B, option B.

questions.question_text: On an unknown scale x, the ice point temperature is 50°x and the steam-point temperature is 200°x. If the temperature is 60°C, then what is the reading in °x?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The unknown scale runs linearly between the ice point at 50 degrees and the steam point at 200 degrees. A Celsius temperature of 60 corresponds to 0.6 of the full scale, so the reading is 50 plus 0.6 times 150, which equals 140 degrees on scale x, option B.

questions.question_text: A block of mass 5 kg hanging at the end of spring scale is totally submerged in a beaker of water. The beaker is large enough to avoid overflow of water. If the density of the block is 2.5 × 10³ kg/m³, then what is the reading of the scale?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The block displaces water equal to its volume, which is 5 kg divided by 2500 kg per cubic metre, giving 0.002 cubic metres. The buoyant force equals the weight of this displaced water, about 19.6 N or 2 kg, so the scale reads 5 minus 2, giving 3 kg, option A.

questions.question_text: An electric generator has a coil of 400 turns and cross-sectional area 5 m² rotating at angular frequency 0.524 rad/s in a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T, what is the induced e.m.f produced from the electric generator in each second?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The maximum induced emf of a generator is the product of the number of turns, the magnetic field strength, the area of the coil and the angular frequency. Substituting 400, 0.2 T, 5 square metres and 0.524 rad/s gives 400 times 5 times 0.2 times 0.524, equal to 209.6 V, option A.

questions.question_text: The primary coil of a transformer is connected to a battery, a resistor, and a switch. The secondary coil is connected to an ammeter. What does the ammeter show when the switch is thrown closed?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Zero current as transformer is not working on DC.

options.label: B
options.option_text: A nonzero current for a short instant.
options.explanation: When the switch is closed the primary current grows from zero, so the magnetic flux through the secondary changes during this short interval. This changing flux induces an emf in the secondary and the ammeter shows a brief nonzero current, then zero once the current is steady, so option B is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: emf will be induced but not current.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The direction of induced e.m.f is in such a direction as to reinforce the change produces it.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Self-inductance of a coil is e.m.f divided by a magnitude of rate change of current with time.
options.explanation: Self-inductance is defined as the magnitude of the induced emf divided by the rate of change of current with time. Option B states exactly this relation, whereas the induced emf is proportional rather than inversely proportional to the number of turns, so the other statements are incorrect.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The induced e.m.f in a coil is inversely proportional to its number of turns.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Self-inductance of a coil is inversely proportional to the cross sectional area of the coil.

questions.question_text: The induced electromotive force in a current carrying coil placed in a magnetic field does not depend on which of the following?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The speed at which the coil moves if the relative motion does not result in changing the magnetic flux.
options.explanation: Induced emf depends on the rate at which magnetic flux through the coil changes. If the coil moves but the flux does not change, then no emf is induced regardless of speed, so option A is the quantity on which the induced emf does not depend.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The change of magnetic flux density.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The length of the coil that is moving in a direction perpendicular to that of the magnetic field.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The area of the coil outside the field.

questions.question_text: A positively charged particle of charge q = 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ C is moving parallel to x-axis with speed 1000 m/s in a magnetic field of 0.5 T parallel to y-axis as shown in the diagram below. What is the magnetic force on the charge?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The magnetic force equals q times v times B, since the velocity is perpendicular to the field, giving 3.2 times 10 to the minus 19 times 1000 times 0.5, equal to 1.6 times 10 to the minus 16 newtons. The direction comes from v crossed into B, which points in the positive Z direction, option D.

questions.question_text: A charged particle moves perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. Which statement is correct about the motion of the particle?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Both kinetic energy and linear momentum of the particle change.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The kinetic energy of the particle change but not its linear momentum.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The linear momentum of the particle changes but not its kinetic energy.
options.explanation: A charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field travels in a circle at constant speed. Its kinetic energy therefore stays the same, but the direction of its velocity changes continuously, so the linear momentum changes even though its magnitude is constant, matching option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Both the energy and momentum do not change.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correct about magnetic field?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Magnetic field lines always form closed loops, the field is stronger where the lines are closer, and moving charges produce magnetic fields. Isolated magnetic monopoles do not exist, so the statement claiming they exist is the one that is not correct, option B.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The closer the field lines are, the stronger the magnetic field.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Magnetic field is produced by moving charge.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correct about the circuit shown below?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Voltage across RL is (R_L /(r + R_L)) ε

options.label: B
options.option_text: Current flowing through RL is ε /(r + R_L)

options.label: C
options.option_text: Current flowing through r is (r /(r + R_L)) ε
options.explanation: The current in the circuit is the emf divided by the total resistance r plus R L, and this same current flows through r. The expression giving the current through r as r divided by the total resistance times the emf is dimensionally wrong, so option C is the incorrect statement.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Power drop in RL is (R_L /(r + R_L)²) ε²

questions.question_text: A galvanometer of full-scale deflection 10 mA is to be converted into a 0–10.0 A ammeter. If its coil has a resistance of 100 Ω, then what value of shunt resistance must be fitted?

options.label: A
options.explanation: For an ammeter the shunt is connected in parallel with the galvanometer coil, and at full deflection the voltage across them is equal. Hence the shunt resistance is the galvanometer resistance times the full-scale current divided by the remaining current, giving 100 times 0.01 over 9.99, approximately 0.1 ohm, option A.

questions.question_text: If a cell supplies a current of 0.9 A when connected to a 2 Ω resistor and a current of 0.3 A, then what will be the internal resistance of the cell when connected to a 7 Ω resistor?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Equating the emf in the two situations gives 0.9 times 2 plus r equals 0.3 times 7 plus r. Expanding and solving yields 1.8 plus 0.9r equals 2.1 plus 0.3r, so 0.6r equals 0.3 and the internal resistance r is 0.5 ohm, option D.

questions.question_text: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is 10. If the distance between the plates is halved, keeping all other quantities constant, then what is the new capacitance of the capacitor?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is proportional to the area of the plates and inversely proportional to their separation. Halving the distance between the plates therefore doubles the capacitance, so a capacitor of 10 microfarads becomes 20 microfarads, option D.

questions.question_text: Two positive charges of magnitude 2.4 × 10⁻⁹ C and 1.6 × 10⁻⁹ C are separated in air by a distance of 2.0 cm. How much electrostatic potential is produced by the two charges at midway between them?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The electric potential at a point is the algebraic sum of the contributions from each charge, and each charge is one centimetre from the midpoint. The total potential is 9 times 10 to the ninth times the sum of the charges divided by 0.01, which equals 3600 volts or 3.6 kV, option A.

questions.question_text: A charge of q₁ = −10.0 × 10⁻⁹ C, q₂ = +10.0 × 10⁻⁹ C and q₃ = −2.5 × 10⁻⁸ C are placed on x-y plane as shown in the figure below. What is the electric force on q₃ by q₁ and q₂?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The positions of the three charges on the x-y plane are shown in a figure that is absent from the transcript. Without knowing the separations the forces cannot be computed, so the item is defective and the pre-marked option A is retained.

questions.question_text: In a Young’s experiment, there are two slits, rather than one. What do you think the reason?

options.label: B
options.option_text: One slit is for frequency the other for wavelength.

options.label: C
options.option_text: To create a path length difference.
options.explanation: Two slits illuminated by the same source act as coherent secondary sources whose waves travel different distances to a point on the screen. This path difference produces constructive or destructive interference, which is exactly why Young experiment uses two slits, so option C is the reason.

options.label: D
options.option_text: One slit is for electric fields and the other is for magnetic fields.

questions.question_text: A light of wavelength 590 nm is incident normally on a grating with spacing 1.67 × 10⁻⁶ m. How many orders of diffraction maxima can be obtained (including the zero order)?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The maximum order is the grating spacing divided by the wavelength, since the sine of the diffraction angle cannot exceed one. Dividing 1.67 times 10 to the minus 6 by 590 times 10 to the minus 9 gives 2.8, so orders zero, one and two exist, giving three maxima including the zero order, option C.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Interference is not superposition of waves.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Constructive interference results in decrease in the intensity.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Destructive interference results in an increase in the intensity.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Path difference which is integer multiple of wavelength results in constructive interference.
options.explanation: Constructive interference occurs when the path difference between two waves is an integer multiple of the wavelength, because the waves then arrive in phase and reinforce. Option D states this correctly, whereas interference is superposition of waves and destructive interference decreases the intensity, so the others are false.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not correct about a simple harmonic oscillator?

options.label: B
options.option_text: The acceleration is directly proportional to and opposite in direction to displacement.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The period of small oscillation of a pendulum with string length l, a bob mass m attached to its end is T = 2π√(l/g).

options.label: D
options.option_text: The frequency of an oscillating mass attached to a massless spring is independent of the spring constant.
options.explanation: For a mass on a spring the frequency depends on both the mass and the spring constant through the relation one over two pi times the square root of k over m. Claiming the frequency is independent of the spring constant is therefore incorrect, making option D the statement that is not correct.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following indicates the wavelength of a travelling wave?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The distance between an adjacent trough and a peak.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The distance between a node and antinodes.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The distance between two adjacent points which are in phase.
options.explanation: The wavelength of a travelling wave is the distance between two adjacent points that are in the same phase, such as one crest and the next. The distance between a trough and an adjacent peak is only half a wavelength, so option D gives the correct definition.

questions.question_text: Mutations are the original source of genetic variation in a population. Which of the following statements is true about mutations?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Mutations are always harmful to the organism
options.explanation: Option A is while many mutations are harmful, some are beneficial or neutral.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Mutations can be beneficial, neutral, or harmful
options.explanation: Mutations can have a range of effects.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Mutations only occur in response to environmental changes
options.explanation: Option C is mutations occur randomly, not in response to needs.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Mutations are passed on to all offspring
options.explanation: Option D is only mutations in gametes (germline) are heritable; somatic mutations are not passed on.

questions.question_text: Four vectors are listed below $\vec{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 10 \end{bmatrix}$, $\vec{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -5 \end{bmatrix}$, $\vec{C} = \begin{bmatrix} -6 \\ 15 \end{bmatrix}$, $\vec{D} = \begin{bmatrix} 15 \\ -6 \end{bmatrix}$, Which pair of the vectors is orthogonal?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero. The dot product of A and D is 4 times 15 plus 10 times minus 6, which equals 60 minus 60, giving zero, so A and D are orthogonal, while the other pairs do not give a zero dot product, option A.

questions.question_text: A race car is moving at a constant speed of 35 m/s. A security car was moving at a speed of 5 m/s as the race car passes by it and was accelerating at constant rate of 5 m/s². What was the speed of the security car when it took over the race car?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The race car and the security car travel equal distances when the security car catches up, so 35t equals 5t plus half of 5 times t squared. This gives t equal to 12 seconds, and the security car speed at that moment is 5 plus 5 times 12, which is 65 m/s, option D.

questions.question_text: A car start moving from rest and its motion on a straight line is shown in the figure below. What is the average velocity of the car within the first 6 seconds?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The velocity-time graph of the car is not included in the transcript. The average velocity over the first six seconds must be found from the displacement, that is, the area under the graph, divided by the time, but this cannot be computed without the figure, so the item is defective.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the motion in a plane?

options.label: A
options.option_text: When a body moves in a horizontal circle, its velocity is constant

options.label: B
options.option_text: When a body moves in a vertical circle, its speed is constant

options.label: C
options.option_text: The centripetal force for a body moving in either vertical or horizontal circle is toward the center
options.explanation: For uniform circular motion the centripetal force always points toward the centre of the circle, whether the motion is in a horizontal or a vertical plane. The speed in a vertical circle is not constant, and in projectile motion the horizontal component is uniform, so option C is the correct statement.

options.label: D
options.option_text: In projectile motion the horizontal component of the motion is uniformly accelerated motion.

questions.question_text: A bullet is fired at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. If air resistance is neglected, what should be the bullet’s horizontal acceleration ($\vec{a}_x$) and vertical acceleration ($\vec{a}_y$) when it reaches its maximum height?

options.label: B
options.option_text: $\vec{a}_x$ is 10 m/s² downward, and $\vec{a}_y$ is zero

options.label: D
options.option_text: $\vec{a}_x$ is zero, and $\vec{a}_y$ is 10 m/s² downward.
options.explanation: In projectile motion with negligible air resistance the only acceleration is gravity, which acts vertically downward with magnitude 10 m/s squared. The horizontal acceleration is zero throughout, including at maximum height, so option D correctly gives a x zero and a y 10 m/s squared downward.

questions.question_text: Two students A and B, with masses $m_A$ and $m_B$ respectively, stand on a wheeled trolleys as shown in the figure below. If student A has larger mass and pushes student B, then what can be said about their accelerations?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The acceleration of student B is less than that of student A.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Both boys will be accelerated by the same magnitude but in opposite directions.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The acceleration of student A is less than that of student B.
options.explanation: By Newton third law both students exert equal and opposite forces on each other. Since student A has the larger mass and acceleration equals force divided by mass, the student with the smaller mass receives the larger acceleration, so the acceleration of A is less than that of B, option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: There would be no acceleration because the forces are equal and opposite.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is correct about errors in measurement?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Experimental error is the same as mistake

options.label: B
options.option_text: Errors make measured values same as accepted value

options.label: C
options.option_text: Errors occur in every scientific investigation
options.explanation: Measurements always contain some uncertainty because of instrument limitations, so errors occur in every scientific investigation, option C. Experimental error is not the same as a mistake, errors prevent values from equalling the accepted value, and modern instruments reduce but never completely avoid errors, so the other options are false.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Errors can be avoid by using modern measurement instruments.
