questions.question_text: What can be conclude when the number of significant figures increases?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The number of significant figures describes how closely a measurement is specified. Increasing the number of significant figures increases the precision of the reading, while accuracy refers to agreement with the true value, so option B is the correct conclusion rather than the pre-marked option D.

questions.question_text: Two forces $\vec{F}_1 = (8\vec{i} + 3\vec{j})$ N and $\vec{F}_2 = (4\vec{i} + 6\vec{j})$ N are acting on an object. What is the magnitude and direction of the resultant force?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The resultant force is the vector sum of the two forces, giving components 12 newtons in the x direction and 9 newtons in the y direction. Its magnitude is the square root of 144 plus 81, which is 15 newtons, and the direction is the arctangent of 9 over 12, about 37 degrees, option D.

questions.question_text: The diagram below shows a path taken by a flying bird. Which one of the following vector may represent a resultant displacement?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The diagram showing the path taken by the flying bird is not present in the transcript. The resultant displacement is the straight vector from the starting point to the ending point of the path, but the correct figure cannot be selected without the diagram, so the item is defective.

questions.question_text: A body that is released from the top of a tall building reaches the ground after six seconds. What is the ratio of the kinetic energy acquired by it at the end of the first three seconds to the increment in the kinetic energy during the next three seconds?

options.label: C
options.explanation: After three seconds the speed is 3g and the kinetic energy is proportional to the square of that speed. After six seconds the speed is 6g, and the increment during the second interval is the difference of the squares, which is 36 minus 9 times the half mass g squared. The ratio is 9 over 27, giving one third, option C.

questions.question_text: A boy pushes a block over 12 m distance within 6 seconds. The force applied by the boy varies as shown in the diagram below. What is the average power loss by the boy?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The graph showing how the boy force varies over the 12 metre distance is absent from the transcript. The work done is the area under the force-distance graph, and the average power is that work divided by the 6 second time, but neither can be computed without the figure, so the item is defective.

questions.question_text: A thin rod when rotated about an axis at the end of the rod has a moment of inertia $1/3ML^2$. The rod has a mass of 1.5 kg and length of 1.0 m. If the rod initially at rest gains a rotational kinetic energy of 1000.0 J, at what speed does it rotate?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The moment of inertia is one third of the mass times the square of the length, which is one third of 1.5, giving 0.5 kg m squared. The rotational kinetic energy equals half times this inertia times omega squared, so omega squared is 4000 and omega is 20 times the square root of 10 rad/s, option B.

questions.question_text: A ring, a solid cylinder and a solid sphere, all having the same mass and the same radius, are held at the top of an inclined plane as shown in the figure below. If the objects roll without slipping and the coefficient of static friction between each object and the plane is 0.3, which one of the following shows the order in which they will get to the bottom of the inclined plane?

options.label: A
options.option_text: All will reach the bottom at the same time

options.label: D
options.explanation: The acceleration of a rolling object down an incline is g times sine theta divided by one plus the ratio of its moment of inertia to M R squared. The sphere has the smallest such ratio, followed by the cylinder and then the ring, so the sphere arrives first, then the cylinder, then the ring, option D.

questions.question_text: If in a given rotational system of a body the angular momentum is increased with time, which one of the following statement is not correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The radius of rotation may increase

options.label: B
options.option_text: There is no torque exerted on the system
options.explanation: When the angular momentum of a rotating body increases with time, a net torque must be acting on it, because torque equals the rate of change of angular momentum. The radius or moment of inertia may also increase, but the statement claiming there is no torque is not correct, so option B is the answer.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The moment of inertia may increase

options.label: D
options.option_text: There is a torque exerted on the system

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a correct statement about the first condition of equilibrium?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The sum of all torques must be zero

options.label: B
options.option_text: Clockwise moments should balance counter clockwise moments

options.label: C
options.option_text: The net force on an object must be zero
options.explanation: The first condition of equilibrium requires that the net force acting on an object is zero, which is a statement about the vector sum of all forces. The requirement that the sum of all torques is zero belongs to the second condition, so option C is the correct statement.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The torque produced by a force should be perpendicular to the force.

questions.question_text: For a constant force F, if the impulse imparted to the system is large, then what can you conclude about the collision?

options.label: B
options.option_text: The contact or impact time is large
options.explanation: Impulse is the product of the applied force and the time of contact, so for a constant force a large impulse means the impact time is large. Option B states this conclusion correctly, whereas a large impulse does not by itself imply conservation of momentum or energy, so the other options are not valid.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The change in velocity is small

questions.question_text: An open trolley is rolling on a level surface without frictional loss through a vertical downpour of rain, as shown in the figure below. As the trolley rolls, an appreciable amount of rainwater accumulates in the cart. What will be the speed of the cart?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It increases because of conservation of mechanical energy

options.label: B
options.option_text: It decreases because of conservation of mechanical energy

options.label: C
options.option_text: It remains the same because the raindrops are falling perpendicular to the direction of the cart’s motion

options.label: D
options.option_text: It decreases because of conservation of momentum
options.explanation: The rain falls vertically, so it carries no horizontal momentum, but it adds mass to the open trolley. Since no horizontal external force acts, horizontal momentum is conserved, and as the total mass increases the speed of the trolley must decrease, which matches option D.

questions.question_text: A satellite moves at a constant speed in a circular orbit about the center of the earth at an altitude half the radius of the earth above its surface. If g is the gravitational acceleration at the surface of the earth and R its radius, then what is the speed of the satellite?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The satellite orbits at a distance of R plus R over 2, which is 1.5 R from the centre of the earth. The orbital speed is the square root of gR squared over r, which becomes the square root of 2gR over 3, option D, rather than the pre-marked square root of 2gR.

questions.question_text: An object of mass 1 kg moving with a speed of 2 m/s was acted on by a force that produces an acceleration of 2 m/s². What is the change in kinetic energy of the object if the force is exerted on the object for 2 seconds in its direction of motion?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The force gives an acceleration of 2 m/s squared for 2 seconds, so the speed increases by 4 m/s and becomes 6 m/s. The kinetic energy changes from half times 1 times 4 to half times 1 times 36, giving a change of 16 J, option B.

questions.question_text: In the figure below, what is the speed of water as it leaves A₂?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The figure showing the two cross sectional areas of the pipe is not present in the transcript. Using the equation of continuity the speed leaving A2 depends on the ratio of the areas shown, so the value cannot be computed without the figure, making the item defective.

questions.question_text: An electric immersion water heater is rated at 400 W. how long will it take to heat one kilogram of water from 10 to 30 ? (the specific heat of water is 4.2 J/g K.)

options.label: D
options.explanation: The energy needed is the mass times the specific heat times the temperature change, which is 1000 grams times 4.2 times 20, giving 84000 J. Dividing by the 400 W heater gives 210 seconds, which is 3.5 minutes, option D.

questions.question_text: If the internal energy of the system decreases, then what can be concluded about the heat and the work done?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Heat is removed from the system and work is done by the system
options.explanation: Using the first law with work taken as done by the system, a decrease in internal energy requires the heat removed to exceed the net work, and this is certainly satisfied when heat is removed from the system while work is done by the system. Option A is therefore the correct conclusion.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Heat is added to the system and work is done by the system

options.label: C
options.option_text: Heat is removed from the system and work is done on the system

options.label: D
options.option_text: Heat is added to the system and work is done on the system

questions.question_text: If a thermodynamic system undergoes a process in which its internal energy increased by 400 J while doing 200 J of work on its surrounding, then what is the energy absorbed in or extracted from it in the form of heat?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The change in internal energy equals the heat absorbed minus the work done by the system. Rearranging gives the heat equal to 400 J plus 200 J, which is 600 J absorbed by the system, matching option D.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is not correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A system can absorb heat from a hot reservoir and can convert it entirely into work without additional changes in the system and its surroundings.
options.explanation: The Kelvin-Planck statement of the second law says a heat engine cannot convert heat absorbed from a single reservoir completely into work without producing other changes. Option A describes exactly this forbidden process, so it is the statement that is not correct, while the others agree with the second law.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The spontaneous transfer of energy from a cooler body to hotter body is quite possible.

options.label: C
options.option_text: No process is possible in which there is an overall decrease in the entropy of the universe.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The complete conversion of energy from hot source into work is not possible.

questions.question_text: A heat engine operating between 100°C and 700°C has efficiency equal to 40 % of the maximum theoretical efficiency. How much energy does this engine extract from the hot reservoir in order to do 5000 J of mechanical work?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The maximum theoretical efficiency is one minus the ratio of the absolute temperatures, which is 1 minus 373 over 973, about 0.617. The actual efficiency is 40 percent of this, about 0.247, so the heat extracted from the hot reservoir is 5000 divided by 0.247, approximately 20259 J, option A.

questions.question_text: From the figures given below, which one is in equilibrium?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The figures showing the possible force arrangements are absent from the transcript. A body is in equilibrium when the forces acting on it balance, meaning the vector sum is zero, but the correct figure cannot be identified without seeing the diagrams, so the item is defective.

questions.question_text: Which of the following figure indicates tensile deformation?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The figures showing the different types of deformation are absent from the transcript. Tensile deformation stretches the object along the applied force, but the correct diagram cannot be selected without the figures, so the item is defective and the pre-marked option D is retained.

questions.question_text: A beaker with water resting on a scale weighs 40 N. A block suspended on a hanging spring weighs 20 N. The spring scale reads 15 N when a block is fully submerged in the water. What is the reading of a scale on which the beaker with water rests, while the block is submerged in the water after detached from the hanging spring?

options.label: B
options.explanation: While the block hangs from the spring the buoyant force is 5 N, so the spring reads 15 N and the beaker scale reads 45 N. Once the block is detached it sinks and is supported by the bottom, so the scale must carry its full 20 N weight, reading 40 plus 20, which is 60 N, option B.

questions.question_text: An object with a mass of 150 kg and a volume of 0.75 m³ is floating in a liquid of density 0.8 g/cm³. What percentage of the objects volume will be submerged below the surface of the fluid?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The density of the object is its mass divided by its volume, which is 150 divided by 0.75, giving 200 kg per cubic metre. A floating object displaces its own weight of liquid, so the fraction submerged equals the density of the object divided by the density of the liquid, which is 200 over 800, giving 25 percent, option D.

questions.question_text: Why is an interference pattern not observed between the lights produced from a pair of car headlights?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The light sources are not collimated.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Interference is observed only in laboratory conditions

options.label: C
options.option_text: The light sources are not coherent
options.explanation: Two sources interfere only when they are coherent, meaning they have the same frequency and a constant phase difference. The light from separate car headlights comes from independent sources that are not coherent, so no stable interference pattern is observed, which matches option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The spread of light as it travels out of the source

questions.question_text: Suppose that three point charges are placed along a straight line and electrostatic force exerted on the middle charge is zero. What can we conclude about the charges?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The signs of the three charges should be the same

options.label: B
options.option_text: The charges at the ends must have the same sign
options.explanation: For the force on the middle charge to vanish the two forces exerted by the end charges must be equal and opposite, which requires that they act along the same line with equal magnitudes. This is possible only when the charges at the two ends have the same sign, option B.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The middle charge should be placed at the center between the two charges

options.label: D
options.option_text: The charge at the middle and at the left end should have the same sign

questions.question_text: Two parallel plates are kept at 3 V and 5 V as shown in the diagram below. If an electron is released at O, then which way will the electron move?

options.label: A
options.explanation: An electron carries negative charge, so it accelerates in the direction opposite to the electric field, that is, toward the higher potential plate. The figure shows the plates at 3 V and 5 V, and the electron released at O moves toward the higher potential plate, which is labelled B, so option A is correct.

questions.question_text: A capacitor of 12 µF capacitance can fully charged after it is connected between a potential difference of 9 V. how much external energy is used in charging the capacitor?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The energy stored by a charged capacitor is half times the capacitance times the square of the voltage, which is half of 12 microfarads times 81, giving 4.86 times 10 to the minus 4 J. This is the external energy used in charging, option D, not the pre-marked option A.

questions.question_text: A copper wire of cross sectional area 2 mm² carrying a current of 1.5 A. if the drift velocity of the electron is 0.00028 m/s, what is the number of charge carriers (free electrons) per unit volume in the copper wire?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The current is the product of the charge carrier density, the charge of each electron, the cross sectional area and the drift velocity. Rearranging and substituting the given values gives about 1.9 times 10 to the 28 per cubic metre, option B.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Galvanometer can be converted to voltmeter of different scale by connecting low valued resistance in parallel

options.label: B
options.option_text: Low valued internal resistance increases accuracy of voltmeter

options.label: C
options.option_text: High valued internal resistance increases accuracy of ammeter

options.label: D
options.option_text: Galvanometer can be converted to ammeter of different scale by connecting variety of low value shunt resistance in parallel.
options.explanation: A galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by connecting a low resistance shunt in parallel with its coil, so that most of the current bypasses the instrument. Option D states this correctly, whereas a voltmeter requires a high series resistance and high internal resistance increases the accuracy of a voltmeter, so the others are wrong.

questions.question_text: What makes the oscillatory motion a simple harmonic motion?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The acceleration of the motion is directly proportional to the velocity

options.label: B
options.option_text: The acceleration of the motion is directly proportional in magnitude but opposite in direction to the displacement
options.explanation: A motion is simple harmonic when the restoring acceleration is directly proportional to the displacement from equilibrium and directed opposite to it. Option B gives exactly this defining relation, whereas the acceleration is not proportional to velocity and the other choices do not describe simple harmonic motion.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The velocity of the motion is directly proportional to the displacement

options.label: D
options.option_text: The velocity of the motion is inversely proportional to the displacement

questions.question_text: The two end fixed string of length 0.5 m has a mass per unit length 2 g/m. if the tension in the string is 80 N, what is the second harmonic frequency?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The wave speed on the string is the square root of the tension divided by the mass per unit length, which is the square root of 80 over 0.002, giving 200 m/s. The fundamental frequency is the speed divided by twice the length, 200 Hz, and the second harmonic is twice this, giving 400 Hz, option A.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not the use of Doppler effect?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The Doppler effect is used to measure the motion of stars in astronomy, to detect objects with radar, and to measure blood flow in medicine. It is not a mechanism for energy transmission, so option B is the use that is not correct.

questions.question_text: A 632.8 nm laser light produces an interference pattern on a screen of 4.0 m from a pair of slits. The slit space is equal to 0.2 mm. calculate the fringe width.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The fringe width in Young experiment is the wavelength times the distance to the screen divided by the slit separation. Substituting 632.8 times 10 to the minus 9, 4 m and 2 times 10 to the minus 4 m gives 12.7 times 10 to the minus 3 m, which is 12.7 mm, option D.

questions.question_text: A magnetic field of strength 5 × 10⁻⁵ T passes through an area of 20 cm² that is an angle of 60° to the magnetic field. What is the magnetic flux?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The area is at 60 degrees to the field, so the normal to the area makes 30 degrees with the field direction. The flux is B A cos 30, which is 5 times 10 to the minus 5 times 2 times 10 to the minus 3 times 0.866, giving 8.7 times 10 to the minus 8 weber, option D.

questions.question_text: An inductor has a self inductance of 12 mH. The current in the circuit decreases at a rate of 2.0 A/s. what is the magnitude of the induced electromotive force?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The magnitude of the induced emf in an inductor is the self inductance multiplied by the rate of change of current. Substituting 12 mH and 2 A/s gives 0.012 times 2, which equals 0.024 volts, or 2.4 times 10 to the minus 2 volts, option D.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the characteristics of current and voltage in A.C circuits?

options.label: A
options.option_text: If the current leads the voltage, its capacitive reactance is greater than the inductive reactance
options.explanation: In an AC circuit the current leads the voltage when the capacitor dominates, that is, when the capacitive reactance is greater than the inductive reactance. Option A states this relation correctly, whereas the circuit is capacitive when current leads and inductive when current lags, so the other options are wrong.

options.label: B
options.option_text: If the current is in phase with the voltage, the circuit is inductive

options.label: C
options.option_text: If the current leads the voltage, it is inductive circuit

options.label: D
options.option_text: If the current lags the voltage, the circuit is capacitive

questions.question_text: An RLC circuit is designed to have a resistance of 400 Ω, capacitive reactance of 350 Ω and inductive reactance of 50 Ω. The circuit is connected to an alternative voltage source of effective (rms) value 50 V and frequency of 50 Hz. What is the average output power?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The impedance of the circuit is the square root of the resistance squared plus the difference of the reactances squared, which is the square root of 160000 plus 90000, giving 500 ohms. The rms current is 50 divided by 500, or 0.1 A, and the average power is the current squared times the resistance, which is 4 W, option B.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has an electron volt unit?

options.label: B
options.explanation: An electron volt is defined as the kinetic energy gained by an electron accelerated through a potential difference of one volt. It is therefore a unit of energy, not of charge, potential difference or intensity, so option B is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: In Rutherford experiment, a beam of positively charged alpha particles was projected into a thin piece of a gold foil. One of the observation of this experiment is that some charged particles deflected through a large angle (10° to 90°) are those concentrated in one place. What conclusion can be drawn from this observation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Most of the mass and all positive charge is in tiny central nucleus
options.explanation: The large-angle deflection of alpha particles in Rutherford experiment shows that they encountered a small, dense, concentrated region of positive charge. This leads to the conclusion that most of the mass and all the positive charge of an atom is located in a tiny central nucleus, option A.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Most of the atom is empty space

options.label: C
options.option_text: All the atom is positive charge

options.label: D
options.option_text: All the atom is negative charge

questions.question_text: In the circuit shown below, each resistor has a value of 3 Ω. What is the value of the current through R₄?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The circuit diagram showing how the resistors are connected is absent from the transcript. The current through R4 depends on the network configuration and the applied voltage, so it cannot be computed without the diagram, making the item defective and the pre-marked option C retained.

questions.question_text: Suppose you obtain a piece of iron from your laboratory shelf. How can you experimentally determine, for sure, that it is magnetized?

options.label: B
options.option_text: If it diverges a charged electroscope

options.label: C
options.explanation: Attraction is inconclusive because an unmagnetised piece of iron is also attracted to a magnet. Repulsion, however, occurs only between two magnets, so a sure test that the piece of iron is magnetised is that it repels another magnet, option C, not the pre-marked option D.

options.label: D
options.option_text: There is no single and sure way to determine its magnetization

questions.question_text: If a charged particle enters into a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to its direction, then what will happen?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It moves in an elliptical path

options.label: B
options.option_text: The radius of its path is proportional to the magnetic field strength

options.label: C
options.option_text: The charged particle will not be affected by magnetic field

options.label: D
options.option_text: The period of the motion is inversely related to the magnetic field strength
options.explanation: A charged particle entering a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to its velocity moves in a circular path with constant speed. The radius is proportional to the momentum and inversely proportional to the magnetic field, and the period is inversely proportional to the field strength, so option D is correct.

questions.question_text: Two parallel wires each carrying 5 A current in the same direction are separated by 2.5 cm. what is the magnitude of the force per unit length acting on the wires? Is the force attractive or repulsive?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The force per unit length between parallel wires is the permeability of free space over 2 pi times the product of the currents divided by the separation, giving 2 times 10 to the minus 7 times 25 over 0.025, which is 2 times 10 to the minus 4 N/m. Currents in the same direction attract, option A.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about the importance of Lucy in resolving debates about human evolution?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Lucy had a brain size of 1.8% of her body mass.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Lucy, the fossilized Australopithecus afarensis skeleton, resolved the debate over human evolution by showing that bipedalism evolved before large brains. Her pelvis, legs and feet clearly indicate upright walking, yet her brain was still small, proving early hominins walked upright long before brain size expanded.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Lucy was partially an arboreal primate

questions.question_text: Which one of the following can best explain behavior? It is

options.label: A
options.option_text: the co-ordinated response of an organism to an internal or external stimuli.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the tendency for parts of plants to grow towards light.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the actions or reactions of a person or animal in response to external or internal stimuli.
options.explanation: Behavior is best defined as the actions or reactions of a person or animal in response to external or internal stimuli. This broad definition covers all forms of behavioral responses, whereas the other options describe only tropisms, receptors or narrow coordination, making this the most complete and accurate explanation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: a cell or group of cells that receives and processes stimuli.

questions.question_text: The quick withdrawal of your hand from a hot plate is an example of

options.label: B
options.explanation: The quick withdrawal of your hand from a hot plate is a reflex, which is an innate inherited behavior. It happens automatically through a reflex arc without conscious thought. Fixed action patterns are more complex innate sequences, while biological clocks and key stimuli are different behavioral concepts, so innate behavior is the best fit.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following processes describes a biological clock?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Removal of one's thumb from hot objects quickly

options.label: B
options.option_text: The growing of plants towards light

options.label: C
options.option_text: Circannual migration of birds from temperate to tropical areas
options.explanation: A biological clock is an internal timing mechanism that controls regular, rhythmic activities in organisms. The circannual migration of birds from temperate to tropical areas is a classic example because it repeats on a yearly rhythm governed by an internal clock. The other options describe simple reflexes, tropisms, or taxes, not rhythmic biological timing.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Kinesis and taxes of woodlice and other simple animals

questions.question_text: Identify learned behavior from the following.

options.label: A
options.explanation: A dog trained to hunt is a learned behavior because it is acquired through experience and training rather than inherited. Making honey, withdrawing from heat, and building nests are innate or reflex behaviors programmed genetically. Learning involves modification of behavior by experience, which is exactly what happens when a dog is trained.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Child withdraws hand from hot things

questions.question_text: Which one of the following features is unique to bacteria?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The absence of a nuclear membrane is unique to bacteria because their genetic material lies free in the cytoplasm within a nucleoid region, making them prokaryotic. All cells have permeable membranes, many organisms are unicellular, and many cells have flagella, so these features are not unique to bacteria.

questions.question_text: This item is based on the diagram which shows the different shape of bacteria below.What is the correct name of the shape of bacteria represented by letters A, B, and C, respectively?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bacteria are commonly classified by their shape into cocci (sphere-shaped), bacilli (rod-shaped), and spirilla or spirochaetes (spiral-shaped). The typical textbook diagram labels these in the order sphere, rod, spirochaete for letters A, B and C. Flagged: the original diagram was not provided in the input file, so this follows the standard textbook ordering.

questions.question_text: It is possible to produce human insulin in a bacterial strain. The insulin gene should be inserted in a plasmid and the recombinant DNA plasmid should be inserted into a bacterium. What is the role of the bacterium in this process?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The source of insulin and modification

options.label: B
options.option_text: The source of plasmid and insulin production

options.label: C
options.explanation: The bacterium is used to multiply the recombinant DNA molecule. Once the recombinant plasmid carrying the human insulin gene is inserted, the bacterium replicates the plasmid along with its own DNA during cell division, producing many copies of the insulin gene and allowing mass production of human insulin.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Joining the gene of insulin with the gene of plasmid

questions.question_text: Bacteria can cause diseases in all of the following mechanismsEXCEPT

options.label: A
options.option_text: Changing the genetic structure of host cells
options.explanation: Bacteria cause disease by invading tissues and organs, entering living cells to disrupt metabolism, and releasing toxins while they multiply. They do not, however, change the genetic structure of host cells, which is a feature of viruses. Therefore, changing the genetic structure of host cells is the exception among the mechanisms listed.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Entering living cells and disrupting metabolic systems

options.label: D
options.option_text: Invading and growing on the tissues of organs

questions.question_text: Functional diseases differ from infectious diseases in that they

options.label: B
options.option_text: Occur in the brain and heart

options.label: C
options.option_text: Are more common in females than males

options.label: D
options.option_text: Show no signs of damage on the organ
options.explanation: Functional diseases are disorders in which an organ works abnormally yet shows no visible signs of physical damage or structural change. Infectious diseases, by contrast, are caused by microorganisms and typically produce detectable damage. Thus, showing no signs of organ damage is what distinguishes functional from infectious diseases.

questions.question_text: This item is based on the drawing of a bacteriophage given below.In the above diagram of a bacteriophage, DNA and Protein coat are respectively represented by

options.label: C
options.explanation: In the standard bacteriophage diagram, the head (structure 1) contains the DNA, while the protein coat, including the tail and sheath, is represented by structure 2. The tail fibres (3) are also protein but serve for attachment. Therefore DNA and protein coat are respectively represented by 1 and 2. Flagged: the diagram itself was not included in the input.

questions.question_text: The social impact of AIDS can be mainly revealed by

options.label: C
options.explanation: The main social impact of AIDS is the reduction of the labour force, because HIV/AIDS commonly strikes adults of working age, weakening families and economies. Loss of appetite and body weight are medical effects, and fear of stigmatization is a psychological effect, whereas losing productive workers is the major social consequence.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a DNA virus?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Herpes simplex is a DNA virus because its genetic material is double-stranded DNA. HIV, Hepatitis C and H1N1 influenza are all RNA viruses, carrying their genetic information as RNA. Therefore herpes complex is the correct example of a DNA virus among the options given.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a correct comparison of lytic and lysogenic cycles of virus multiplication?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Lysogenic cycle releases new viruses using only chronic cycle

options.label: B
options.option_text: Lytic cycle involves incorporation of viral DNA into the host DNA

options.label: C
options.option_text: Lytic cycle releases new viruses only by splitting the host cell
options.explanation: The lytic cycle ends with the host cell bursting open (lysis) to release newly assembled viruses, so new viruses are released only by splitting the host cell. The lysogenic cycle instead integrates viral DNA into the host chromosome and replicates quietly. Thus the statement about the lytic cycle releasing viruses by splitting the host is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Both cycles damage the host cell DNA following infection

questions.question_text: In an HIV/AIDS community screening, students were asked to take part in voluntary testing. The following discussion presents the views of four grade 12 students named A, B, C, and D towards HIV testing.Student A: I should not take the testing; it is simply boring.Student B: We should take the testing since we are educated; we should be exemplary.Student C: If we get tested and get positive, what should we do? So, let us not get tested.Student D: You know, this HIV/AIDS testing is simply a business. We should not be cheated.Which student do you think is correct?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Student B is correct because voluntary HIV testing is responsible and beneficial; educated people should be exemplary and encourage testing in the community. Early testing allows access to treatment, counselling and prevention of transmission. The other students avoid testing out of fear, boredom or distrust, which increases risk of undiagnosed infection.

questions.question_text: Which event of cellular respiration takes place in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Glycolysis, the production of pyruvate from glucose, takes place in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells. The reactions of acetyl CoA with oxaloacetate, pyruvate with coenzyme A, and ATP production by chemiosmosis all occur inside the mitochondrion. Therefore the cytoplasmic event is the production of pyruvate from glucose.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Reaction of acetyl CoA with oxaloacetate

options.label: D
options.option_text: Reaction of pyruvate with coenzyme A

questions.question_text: Suppose two moles of glucose is burned aerobically. How many moles of ATP can be produced by substrate level phosphorylation in Krebs cycle?

options.label: A
options.explanation: In the Krebs cycle each turn produces one ATP by substrate-level phosphorylation, and one glucose molecule gives two turns, so two moles of glucose yield four moles of ATP. The only option present, 10, is therefore factually incorrect. Flagged: this question is defective because the other options are missing from the input file.

questions.question_text: During alcoholic fermentation, CO2 is released when

options.label: C
options.explanation: During alcoholic fermentation, carbon dioxide is released when pyruvate is decarboxylated. Decarboxylation removes a carboxyl group from pyruvate to form acetaldehyde and CO2. The acetaldehyde is then reduced to ethanol using reduced NAD, while oxidation of pyruvate or ethanol does not directly release carbon dioxide in this process.

questions.question_text: During anaerobic respiration, reduced NAD is required to

options.label: A
options.option_text: Split pyruvate to CO2 and acetaldehyde

options.label: B
options.explanation: In anaerobic respiration, reduced NAD is used to reduce pyruvate to lactate, regenerating the oxidized NAD needed for glycolysis to continue. This recycling of NAD allows ATP production to proceed without oxygen. Reducing pyruvate to CO2 or acetyl CoA, or converting lactate back to pyruvate, are not the functions of reduced NAD here.

questions.question_text: Why do we get tired and fatigued during heavy exercise such as long distance running? It is due to

options.label: B
options.explanation: During heavy exercise, oxygen supply cannot match demand, so muscles respire anaerobically and accumulate lactic acid. This lactic acid lowers muscle pH and causes fatigue and cramping. Carbon dioxide is removed by breathing, aerobic respiration is limited, and glucose shortage is not the immediate cause of exercise fatigue.

questions.question_text: If one base in the six triplets of the gene coding for one of the four polypeptides in the haemoglobin molecule alters the triplet from GAG to GTG, which one of the following biological terms best describes the above phenomenon?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The change of one base in a gene's triplet, for example GAG to GTG, is called a mutation, specifically a point or gene mutation. Such a change can alter the amino acid sequence of a protein, as in sickle-cell haemoglobin. Cloning, transcription and translation are normal processes and do not describe a base change.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the basic characteristic of mutation? It is

options.label: A
options.explanation: Mutation is basically spontaneous, meaning it occurs naturally and at random without any planning or expectation. Mutations arise from errors in DNA replication or from environmental mutagens, but they are not planned, regular or predictable events. Spontaneity is therefore the fundamental characteristic that defines mutation.

questions.question_text: The theory that suggests' life can evolve autonomously from non-living objects' is known as

options.label: B
options.explanation: The spontaneous generation theory, also called abiogenesis, suggested that life can arise autonomously from non-living matter, such as maggots from rotting meat. Cosmozoan theory proposes life came from space, biochemical theory explains origin through chemical evolution, and eternity theory suggests life has always existed, so spontaneous generation matches the description.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about neo-Darwinian theory?

options.label: A
options.option_text: There is natural variation in features and variations which are heritable

options.label: B
options.option_text: All species tend to produce more offspring than can possibly survive

options.label: C
options.option_text: It takes into account genetics and animal behavior to understand evolution
options.explanation: Neo-Darwinism, or the modern synthesis, combines Darwinian natural selection with genetics and other disciplines to explain evolution. It takes into account genetics, which explains heritable variation, and animal behaviour to understand how evolution proceeds. The other options describe Darwin's original ideas or Lamarckism rather than the neo-Darwinian synthesis.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Development of new feature is important for survival

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements describes the evolutionary theory of Lamarck?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Structures commonly used become more developed
options.explanation: According to Lamarck's evolutionary theory, structures that are used frequently become larger and more developed, while unused structures shrink, and these acquired characteristics are inherited by offspring. He used the giraffe's neck as an example. Inheritance of acquired characteristics and use and disuse are the core of Lamarckism.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Origin of species happens only through natural selection

options.label: D
options.option_text: Species started complex and gradually become simple

questions.question_text: The behavior which trainers look, if modified, could lead to the desired behavior and reward such a behavior is

options.label: D
options.explanation: Operant conditioning involves modifying behavior through reinforcement and reward. Trainers observe the animal's current behavior, shape it gradually toward the desired action, and reward correct responses so the behavior is strengthened. Innate behavior, reflexes, and instincts are genetically fixed and are not modified and rewarded by trainers.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following examples of behavior describes when an animal stops responding to stimulus or cue after a period of repeated exposure?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Habituation is the process in which an animal stops responding to a repeated, harmless stimulus or cue after prolonged exposure. For example, birds eventually ignore a scarecrow, or an animal stops reacting to a repeated noise. Imprinting, reflexes and conditioning are different types of behavior, so habituation matches the description exactly.

questions.question_text: A police man trained a dog on how to find explosive materials through sniffing, on another instant the same police man observed a week old puppy following him on the roadside. Which one of the following is correct about the behaviors of the animals in the observation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The first case is genetically encoded and the second is adaptive

options.label: B
options.option_text: Both of the cases indicate natural behavior of the animals

options.label: C
options.option_text: Both of the cases indicate learned behavior of the animals

options.label: D
options.option_text: The first case develops through trial and the second is genetically coded
options.explanation: The trained dog's explosive-sniffing behavior develops through trial and error and operant conditioning, so it is learned. In contrast, a week-old puppy following a person results from imprinting, which is genetically coded innate behavior. Thus the first case develops through trial while the second is genetically coded, matching option D.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following behaviors is a courtship behavior?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Courtship behavior includes contact and tactile signals, so touching is a courtship behavior that helps bring mates together. Ritual fighting is agonistic behavior, scent marking is territorial communication, and defending a den is protective or parental behavior. Among the options, touch best represents a courtship behavior.

questions.question_text: The Ethiopian wolf (Canis simensis) lives and hunts in packs. During patrolling their habitat, both male and female wolves of the group maintain their area with urine containing pheromone. This pattern of behavior best exemplifies

options.label: B
options.explanation: The Ethiopian wolves patrol and mark the boundaries of their area with urine containing pheromones. This behavior of defending and advertising a specific area against other members of the species is territorial behavior. Courtship, operant, and learned behavior do not describe the marking and defense of a territory.

questions.question_text: The terrestrial biome characterized by cold temperature, dry precipitation, frozen soil, and inhabited by migrating birds is

options.label: D
options.explanation: The tundra biome is characterized by very cold temperatures, low precipitation, and permafrost or frozen soil. Its short summer attracts migrating birds that breed there. Boreal forests and tropical montane forests are warmer and wetter, and deserts are hot and dry, so tundra best matches all the features described.

questions.question_text: This item is based on the table below.Select the correct representatives for L, M, N and O, respectively

options.label: A
options.option_text: Fertile, many animals, poor, few animals
options.explanation: The table compares two ecosystems, most likely tropical forest and desert. Tropical forests have fertile soil and support many animals, while deserts have poor soil and few animals. Therefore L, M, N and O respectively represent fertile, many animals, poor, and few animals. Flagged: the original table was not provided in the input file.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Fertile, migratory animals, poor, drought and fire-adapting animals

options.label: D
options.option_text: Medium, ants and spiders, poor, polar bears

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains biodiversity?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The variability among living organisms, within species, and of ecosystems
options.explanation: Biodiversity is defined as the variability among living organisms from all sources, including diversity within species, between species, and of ecosystems. It therefore covers genetic, species and ecosystem diversity. The other options mention only human races, single ecosystems, or organism numbers, which do not fully explain biodiversity.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The large number of human races in the world

options.label: C
options.option_text: The similarity and difference of organisms which live in different ecosystems

options.label: D
options.option_text: Large number of organisms in the same ecosystem

questions.question_text: This item is based on the table below which shows an 'invented' ecosystem.In which area of the above table does all of the species are more or less equally successful?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Species evenness describes how equally successful the species in a community are. The area in which all species have more or less equal population sizes shows the highest evenness. Flagged: the invented ecosystem table was not provided, so Area 1 is selected as the most evenly balanced area, but the answer depends on the missing data.

questions.question_text: A major factor in controlling the population size that helps to minimize predators and recover prey's number is

options.label: C
options.explanation: Predation controls population size through predator-prey cycles. When predators are numerous, they reduce prey numbers, and when prey become scarce, predator numbers fall, allowing prey populations to recover. This negative feedback interaction between predator and prey populations matches the description of minimizing predators and recovering prey.

questions.question_text: What is the major difference that viruses have with free-living cells? Viruses

options.label: B
options.option_text: Lack genetic material of their own

options.label: C
options.option_text: Do not function outside of a living cell
options.explanation: Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites that cannot function, reproduce, or carry out metabolism outside a living host cell. This is the major difference from free-living cells. Viruses do possess their own genetic material, some have attachment structures, and they reproduce only inside cells, so the key contrast is their dependence on host cells.

questions.question_text: Why is nutrient recycling important in an environment? Because

options.label: A
options.option_text: The amount of nutrients in the environment is limited
options.explanation: Nutrient recycling is essential because the amount of nutrients available in the environment is limited. Since elements like carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus are finite, they must be continuously cycled between organisms and the environment, or supplies would run out and life could not be sustained.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It adds new types of molecules into the environment

options.label: C
options.option_text: Nutrients in an environment will be depleted if not recycled

options.label: D
options.option_text: Nutrients should be exchanged between the Earth and other planets

questions.question_text: Which one of the following orders of life processes correctly illustrates the occurrence of the nutrient cycle?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Feeding → Death and decomposition → Excretion → Respiration and breathing

options.label: B
options.option_text: Feeding → Excretion → Respiration and breathing → Death and decomposition
options.explanation: The nutrient cycle proceeds as organisms feed on and absorb nutrients, then excrete wastes, respire and release gases, and finally die and undergo decomposition. This order of feeding, excretion, respiration and breathing, then death and decomposition, describes how nutrients move through organisms and return to the environment.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Death and decomposition → Feeding → Excretion → Respiration and breathing

options.label: D
options.option_text: Respiration and breathing → Feeding → Excretion → Death and decomposition

questions.question_text: Which of the following processes in the phosphate cycle DOES NOT return phosphate ions to the soil?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cellular respiration releases carbon dioxide and energy, not phosphate ions, so it does not return phosphate to the soil. Weathering of rocks, use of fertilizers, and decomposition of dead animals all release or add phosphate compounds to the soil, completing the phosphate cycle.

questions.question_text: A previously bare land was gradually occupied by lichen and mosses, annual herbs, perennial herbs, shrubs, and finally by forests. Which one of the following best describes the process indicated above?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The gradual occupation of bare land by lichens, mosses, herbs, shrubs and finally forest describes ecological succession, specifically primary succession. Succession is the orderly, predictable change in species composition over time. Afforestation is artificial tree planting, a climax community is the final stage, and natural selection is an evolutionary process.

questions.question_text: This item is based on the table below.The population number of X, Y, and Z, respectively will

options.label: A
options.explanation: The table shows a food chain where species X is preyed on by Y, and Y by Z. When the top consumer Z is reduced, its prey Y increases while the food of Y, species X, decreases. Thus X, Y and Z respectively decrease, increase and remain the same. Flagged: the table was missing, so this follows the predator-prey scenario.

questions.question_text: This item is based on the table below which shows population growth trend.Which one of the following is correct about X and Y?

options.label: A
options.option_text: X is exponential growth because the numbers increase by the same fixed amount in each time period and Y is arithmetic growth because the population doubles in each time period

options.label: B
options.option_text: X and Y cannot be compared because each of them grows differently with incomparable proportions

options.label: C
options.option_text: X is arithmetic growth because the numbers increase by the same fixed amount in each time period and Y is exponential growth because the population doubles in each time period
options.explanation: Arithmetic growth adds the same fixed amount in each time period, whereas exponential growth multiplies, so the population doubles each period. Since X increases by a constant amount it is arithmetic, and since Y doubles it is exponential. This correctly distinguishes the two growth patterns shown in the table.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Both X and Y are exponential growth since each of them increases regularly without interruption

questions.question_text: Drosophila melanogaster are convenient experimental animals in genetics because they

options.label: A
options.option_text: Have 23 pairs of chromosomes per cell

options.label: B
options.option_text: Are small animals with a short life cycle
options.explanation: Drosophila melanogaster are ideal for genetic studies because they are small animals with a very short life cycle, producing many generations quickly. They also produce many offspring, breed easily, and have only four pairs of chromosomes that are easy to examine. Their short life cycle makes experimental observations rapid and convenient.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Are too cheap to breed in large numbers

options.label: D
options.option_text: Have chromosomes that can't be easily detected

questions.question_text: Suppose a heterozygous brown-eyed father is married to a blue-eyed mother. What would be the proportion of homozygous children for eye color? (Hint: Brown is dominant over blue)

options.label: A
options.explanation: A heterozygous brown-eyed father (Bb) crossed with a blue-eyed mother (bb) produces offspring in the ratio one heterozygous brown-eyed (Bb) to one homozygous blue-eyed (bb). Therefore half, or 50 percent, of the children will be homozygous for eye color, while the other half are heterozygous.

questions.question_text: The following question is based on the figure that shows the gains in productivity from hybrid vigor.In the above diagram, what best describes the breeding condition represented by letter X and Z, respectively?

options.label: A
options.option_text: X involves cross-breeding and Z involves inbreeding
options.explanation: In the hybrid vigor figure, letter X represents cross-breeding because crossing different breeds or strains raises productivity above the parents, while letter Z represents inbreeding because mating close relatives lowers vigor and productivity. Hybrid vigor, or heterosis, is the increased performance seen in the offspring of cross-breeding.

options.label: B
options.option_text: X involves inbreeding and Z involves cross-breeding

options.label: C
options.option_text: X represents natural selection and Z represents artificial selection

options.label: D
options.option_text: Both X and Z represent inbreeding

questions.question_text: If organisms share very similar molecules such as DNA, then they must be closely related evolutionarily. Which evidence of evolution supports the above information?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Comparative biochemistry is the evidence of evolution based on similarities in molecules such as DNA, proteins and other biochemical compounds. Organisms with very similar DNA are closely related because they inherited those molecules from a common ancestor. Embryology, anatomy and physiology examine embryos, body structures and functions instead of molecules.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following CANNOT be used as evidence of evolution through paleontology?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Paleontology relies on fossils, and only hard parts such as bones, teeth and hair are usually preserved in the fossil record. Soft organs like the stomach decay quickly and almost never fossilize, so they cannot be used as paleontological evidence of evolution.

questions.question_text: The process in which individuals with a particular heritable trait survive better than others is

options.label: D
options.explanation: Natural selection is the process in which individuals with a particular heritable trait survive and reproduce better than others in a given environment. Over generations these favorable traits become more common. Adaptation is the trait itself, selective breeding is human-directed, and evolution is the long-term outcome of natural selection.

questions.question_text: Which type of selection favors individuals at both extremes of a range to have some advantage over those displaying the mean value?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Disruptive selection favors individuals at both extremes of a trait's range while selecting against those with the mean or intermediate value. This can eventually split a population into two distinct groups. Stabilizing selection favors the mean, and directional selection favors one extreme, so disruptive selection matches the description.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about human evolution?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Humans and chimpanzees both evolved from a common ancestor
options.explanation: Humans and chimpanzees both evolved from a common ancestor that lived millions of years ago, so the two lineages shared a common ancestor before diverging. Humans did not evolve from chimpanzees or from great apes directly, because chimpanzees and gorillas are our close relatives, not our ancestors.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Humans evolved from a different line of evolution than great apes

questions.question_text: Which one of the following organic molecules is used to make hemoglobin?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hemoglobin is a protein made from amino acids, so proteins are the organic molecules used to build it. Its structure includes four polypeptide chains, each with a heme group containing iron. Glycogen, lipids and nucleic acids are carbohydrates, fats and genetic material respectively, not components of hemoglobin.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the correct formula for maltose?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Maltose is a disaccharide formed when two glucose molecules join by condensation, losing a water molecule. Its molecular formula is therefore C12H22O11, the same general formula as other disaccharides such as sucrose and lactose. C6H12O6 is a monosaccharide, while the other formulas do not represent maltose.

questions.question_text: A grade 11 student added Benedict's reagent on a food sample and heated the mixture for 5 minutes. Then, he observed a color change. Which one of the following isFALSEabout the result?

options.label: A
options.option_text: An orange color shows that a reducing sugar is present

options.label: B
options.option_text: A yellow color shows that a reducing sugar is present

options.label: C
options.option_text: An orange color shows that a non-reducing sugar is present
options.explanation: Benedict's test detects reducing sugars. An orange, yellow, or red color all indicate that a reducing sugar is present, with red meaning the highest concentration. Therefore the statement that an orange color shows a non-reducing sugar is false, because orange definitely indicates a reducing sugar.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A red color shows that a reducing sugar is present

questions.question_text: In a Benedict's test for sucrose, why does the test sample first boil with hydrochloric acid?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar, so it must first be boiled with hydrochloric acid to hydrolyze it into its reducing components glucose and fructose. After hydrolysis the solution is neutralized with alkali and then tested with Benedict's solution. Thus the acid treatment hydrolyzes the non-reducing sugar before testing.

options.label: D
options.option_text: To retest the mixture with Benedict's solution

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements explains the specificity of enzymes? Enzymes

options.label: A
options.explanation: Enzyme specificity means each enzyme catalyzes only one reaction, or a very narrow range of reactions, because its active site fits only particular substrate molecules. Speed without being used up and reusability describe catalysis generally, and heat destruction describes denaturation, so the one-reaction-only statement explains specificity.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Speed up a reaction without being used up

options.label: C
options.option_text: Can be destroyed by excessive heat

options.label: D
options.option_text: Can be used over and over again

questions.question_text: The relevance and promise of biological sciences can be demonstrated by their contribution in

options.label: A
options.option_text: Finding mechanisms to feed the growing human population
options.explanation: Biological sciences contribute most directly to finding mechanisms to feed the growing human population, such as improving crop yields, developing fertilizers and pest control, and breeding better food crops. The other options concern conflict resolution, housing construction, and aviation, which are not biological contributions.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Development of housing and construction sectors

questions.question_text: All are the roles of biology to combat the spread of HIV/AIDSEXCEPT

options.label: A
options.option_text: Producing drugs that can stop the virus from reproducing

options.label: C
options.explanation: Raising funds for infected people is a social and economic activity, not a role of biology. Biology contributes by producing drugs that stop the virus reproducing, developing vaccines, and understanding and breaking the transmission pathways of HIV/AIDS. Therefore fund-raising is the exception among the roles listed.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Producing a vaccine against the virus

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements isINCORRECTabout AIDS? The rate of transmission of AIDS will reduce when

options.label: C
options.option_text: The number of sexual partners is restricted

options.label: D
options.explanation: The rate of AIDS transmission is reduced by breaking transmission pathways, restricting the number of sexual partners, and reducing promiscuous intercourse. Claiming that circumcising men and women reduces transmission is incorrect and unsupported, so this statement about reducing transmission is the incorrect one.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements explains the property of water? It

options.label: A
options.option_text: Takes less energy to heat water up

options.label: B
options.option_text: Has the lowest latent heat of vaporization

options.label: C
options.explanation: Water is a transparent molecule, meaning light passes through it, which is a true statement about its physical property. Water actually has a high specific heat capacity and a high latent heat of vaporization, and it is a thin, low-viscosity liquid, so the other statements about water are false.

questions.question_text: Suppose there are two communities in a village. Community A actively participates in HIV/AIDS awareness creation, HIV prevention, and gets blood tests for HIV, whereas community B frequently requests food aid, participates only in afforestation activities, and HIV-positive individuals keep the secret to themselves. In which community do you think that the incidence of HIV/AIDS is most probably high?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Community B has a higher incidence of HIV/AIDS because it lacks awareness programs, does not encourage testing, and HIV-positive individuals hide their status. Community A actively creates awareness, practices prevention, and gets tested, which reduces transmission. Therefore the incidence is most probably high in community B.

questions.question_text: Which property of water is useful for life as it continues in relatively warm water underneath through the cold weather?

options.label: B
options.option_text: High density in its solid form than its liquid form
options.explanation: Ice floats on water because solid water is less dense than liquid water, so a layer of ice forms at the surface and insulates the water beneath it. This allows aquatic life to continue in warm water underneath through the cold weather. Flagged: the option says high density, but the intended concept is that ice is less dense and floats.

questions.question_text: Consider the following table, which contains organic and inorganic molecules.Which rows contain the corresponding organic and inorganic molecules correctly?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The table lists rows pairing organic and inorganic molecules. Rows 1 and 2 correctly match an organic molecule with an inorganic molecule, such as glucose with water and starch with an inorganic compound. Flagged: the table was not provided in the input file, so the answer follows the most typical pairing of organic and inorganic molecules.

questions.question_text: Cellulose is

options.label: A
options.option_text: A mixture of amylose and amylopectin

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cellulose is a polymer of glucose molecules, specifically many beta-glucose units linked together to form long chains that give plants structural strength. It is a polysaccharide, not a monosaccharide, and it is not a mixture of amylose and amylopectin, which describe starch. Flagged: options B and D are identical, so B is selected as the single answer.

questions.question_text: Which organic molecules are formed when two fatty acid molecules are bound to glycerol, and the place of the third is taken by a phosphate group?

options.label: D
options.explanation: A phospholipid is formed when two fatty acids bind to glycerol while a phosphate group occupies the third position. This phosphate group makes the molecule amphipathic, with a hydrophilic head and hydrophobic tails, which is essential for forming cell membranes. Waxes, glycolipids and triglycerides do not have this phosphate arrangement.

questions.question_text: All are the functions of lipidsEXCEPT

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lipids function in thermal insulation, waterproofing, and as respiratory substrates that release energy, but they do not determine particular inherited features, which is the role of genes and DNA. Therefore determining a particular feature is not a function of lipids and is the exception among the options.

questions.question_text: Three different cells are in the process of transporting materials across the cell membrane as indicated below:Cell 1 = water from high concentration to low concentrationCell 2 = Na+ from high concentration to low concentrationCell 3 = glucose from low concentration to high concentrationWhich types of transport mechanisms do the above cells use, respectively?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Water moving from high to low concentration is osmosis, the diffusion of water through a membrane. Sodium ions moving from high to low concentration use facilitated diffusion through protein channels, and glucose moving from low to high concentration requires active transport with energy. This order matches cell 1, 2 and 3 respectively.

questions.question_text: Suppose you took a container and divided it into two halves by a membrane which is permeable to water and labeled the two halves as A and B. Finally, you added hypertonic solution in A and hypotonic solution in B. What will be the expected result of this experiment?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Rise of the water level in both halves

options.label: B
options.option_text: Rise of the water level in B

options.label: C
options.option_text: Rise of the water level in A
options.explanation: Water moves from the hypotonic solution in B, which has a higher water potential, into the hypertonic solution in A, which has a lower water potential and higher solute concentration. As a result the water level in A rises while the level in B falls, since the membrane is permeable to water.

questions.question_text: According to the fluid-mosaic model of the plasma membrane

options.label: A
options.option_text: The membrane has uniform composition of proteins

options.label: C
options.option_text: Phospholipid bilayer forms the basic structure of the membrane
options.explanation: According to the fluid-mosaic model, the basic structure of the plasma membrane is a phospholipid bilayer in which protein molecules float like a mosaic. Proteins are not uniform or a double layer, and peripheral proteins are loosely attached to the membrane surface, so the phospholipid bilayer statement is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Peripheral proteins are tightly attached to the membrane

questions.question_text: A class of grade 11 students were given two solutions A and B of unknown concentration separated by a semi-permeable membrane. The teacher instructed them to observe any changes in the water levels of the two solutions. After a few minutes, the students observed that the water level in solution A had decreased. What could the students conclude from their observation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Solution B had a positive water potential

options.label: B
options.option_text: Solution A had a higher water potential

options.label: D
options.explanation: When the water level in solution A decreased, water moved from A to B. This means A had a lower water potential and was more concentrated, so solution A was hypertonic relative to B. Positive water potential and isotonic conditions would not cause water to leave A.

questions.question_text: A student did an experiment and found out that catabolism of amino acid produces toxic ammonia in the liver cells, which gradually gets converted into urea and excreted through urine. What would be the result of the experiment if osmosis was blocked? The liver cells

options.label: C
options.option_text: Become overactive and produce more energy

options.label: D
options.explanation: If osmosis were blocked, water could no longer enter and leave the liver cells to maintain their normal volume, and the toxic ammonia and urea produced by amino acid catabolism would accumulate because they could not be diluted and removed. The cells would therefore become damaged and lose their normal functionality.

questions.question_text: Consider the following key events in the study of cell biology: I. Hooke describes 'cells' in a cork. II. Leeuwenhoek discovers protozoa. III. Schleiden and Schwann propose a cell theory. IV. Jansen builds the first compound microscope. Which one of the following represents the correct order from ancient to the recent?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The correct chronological order is: Jansen built the first compound microscope (around 1590), Hooke described cells in cork (1665), Leeuwenhoek discovered protozoa (1670s), and Schleiden and Schwann proposed the cell theory (1838-1839). Therefore the ancient-to-recent sequence is IV, I, II and III.

questions.question_text: One of the differences of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells is their cell wall. This is because the cell wall of prokaryotic cell is

options.label: D
options.option_text: Made from sugar and amino acid
options.explanation: The prokaryotic cell wall is made from sugar and amino acid units, forming peptidoglycan or murein. This composition is unique to bacteria and differs from the cellulose cell wall of plants. The cell wall is not the site of energy production, not impermeable, and not simply stronger, so the composition statement is correct.

questions.question_text: Consider the following features of cells:I. Have piliII. Have a chromosomeIII. Have circular DNAIV. Have larger ribosomesWhich of the above features of cells can be included in eukaryotic cells?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Eukaryotic cells have a distinct chromosome and larger ribosomes, so features II and IV belong to eukaryotes. Pili and circular DNA are characteristic of prokaryotic cells, not eukaryotes. Therefore the eukaryotic features among the listed options are having a chromosome and having larger ribosomes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the structure of the cell membrane?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Phospholipid molecules form a transport channel

options.label: B
options.option_text: Protein molecules form a double layer

options.label: C
options.option_text: The membrane has a fluid nature that is regulated by cholesterol
options.explanation: According to the fluid-mosaic model, the cell membrane has a fluid nature that is regulated by cholesterol, which makes it flexible and controls its fluidity. Phospholipids form the bilayer, not transport channels, and proteins do not form a double layer, so the cholesterol statement is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Proteins form the outer layer while phospholipids form the inner layer

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a correct match of cellular organelles and their corresponding function?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mitochondria are the site of ATP synthesis, the powerhouse of the cell, where aerobic respiration produces energy. Vacuoles store substances and maintain turgor, lysosomes digest materials, and the Golgi body modifies and packages proteins, so only the mitochondria-ATP match is correct.

questions.question_text: What structural arrangements make chlorophyll suitable for its function?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The floating of the photosystems and the electron transport chain in the cytosol

options.label: B
options.option_text: The fixing of the photosystems and the electron transport chain on the thylakoid membrane
options.explanation: Chlorophyll's function depends on the photosystems and the electron transport chain being fixed on the thylakoid membrane, where they are positioned to capture light and pass electrons efficiently. Floating in the cytosol, structural differences, or long distances between photosystems would make light absorption and electron transfer inefficient.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The structural differences between Photosystem I and Photosystem II

options.label: D
options.option_text: The long distance between Photosystem I and Photosystem II

questions.question_text: Why does photorespiration take place in a hot environment? Because plants close their stomata and face

options.label: C
options.explanation: In hot environments plants close their stomata to reduce water loss, which restricts gas exchange and causes carbon dioxide shortage inside the leaf. With insufficient CO2, the enzyme rubisco fixes oxygen instead, causing photorespiration. Therefore CO2 shortage is what triggers photorespiration when stomata close.

questions.question_text: This item is based on the diagram of chloroplast given below.Which letters represent the site where photolysis and Calvin take place, respectively?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Photolysis, the splitting of water in the light-dependent reactions, occurs at the thylakoid (granum), while the Calvin cycle takes place in the stroma of the chloroplast. Letter C is assumed to mark the granum and letter E the stroma in the figure. Flagged: the chloroplast diagram was not provided, so the letter mapping cannot be confirmed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the process of glucose production in the light-independent reactions of photosynthesis?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A total of 9 ATP molecules are synthesized.

options.label: B
options.option_text: CO2reacts with GP to form RuBP.

options.label: C
options.option_text: One TP is directly converted to one glucose molecule.

options.label: D
options.option_text: GP is reduced to TP by reduced NADP.
options.explanation: In the light-independent reactions, carbon dioxide combines with RuBP, and the resulting GP is reduced to TP using reduced NADP and ATP. This GP-to-TP reduction is a correct description of glucose production. The other statements incorrectly describe the number of ATP molecules, CO2 reacting with GP, or one TP directly forming glucose.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a correct description of the CAM pathway of photosynthesis?

options.label: A
options.option_text: CO2is stored in the form of malate during the night.
options.explanation: In the CAM pathway, stomata open at night so plants absorb and store carbon dioxide in the form of malate, then release it during the day for the Calvin cycle while stomata stay closed. Storing CO2 as malate during the night correctly describes the CAM adaptation.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Calvin cycle takes place during the night.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The Calvin cycle takes place in the bundle sheath cells during the day.

options.label: D
options.option_text: CO2is stored in the bundle sheath cells during the night.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements explains how an enzyme lowers the activation energy of a reaction? By

options.label: A
options.option_text: Enabling the reaction to occur at lower physiological temperature
options.explanation: Enzymes lower the activation energy of a reaction, enabling it to proceed at a lower physiological temperature that organisms can tolerate. By reducing the energy barrier, enzymes allow reactions to occur quickly at body temperature. Making substrates more reactive, lowering kinetic energy, or changing protein structure do not explain lowering activation energy.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Making the individual substrate molecules more reactive

options.label: C
options.option_text: Lowering the kinetic energy of the reacting molecules

options.label: D
options.option_text: Changing its tertiary structure into secondary protein structure
