questions.question_text: Consider the following chemical reaction below.Based on the above chemical reaction, in which classes of enzymes can enzyme 'E' be grouped?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Enzyme classes are named by the type of reaction they catalyze, such as transferases transferring groups, hydrolases breaking bonds with water, isomerases rearranging molecules, and oxidoreductases carrying out oxidation-reduction. Flagged: the chemical reaction diagram was not provided, so the correct class cannot be determined with certainty; transferases is selected as the most likely intended answer.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following enzymes is used as washing powders?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Lipase is the enzyme used in biological washing powders because it breaks down fatty and oily stains into soluble products. Biological detergents typically contain lipase and protease to remove fat and protein stains. Chymosin, cellulase and pectinase are used in food and beverage processing, not washing powders.

questions.question_text: What happens when the substrate molecule binds to the active site of an enzyme?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The substrate and the enzyme will bond permanently.

options.label: B
options.option_text: They form a stable intermediate substance.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The amino acids in the active site become unreactive.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The chemical bonds of the substrate are distorted.
options.explanation: When a substrate binds to the enzyme's active site, the interaction distorts or strains the chemical bonds of the substrate, weakening them so the reaction can proceed more easily. The enzyme-substrate complex is temporary, not permanent, and the bonds are not stabilized unchanged, so bond distortion best describes the event.

questions.question_text: Which of the following vitamins is used as a component of cofactor?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Riboflavin, or vitamin B2, is used as a component of coenzymes, specifically FAD and FMN, which assist enzyme-catalyzed redox reactions. Many B vitamins form coenzymes, but riboflavin is the standard textbook example of a vitamin serving as a coenzyme component. Flagged: thiamin can also form a coenzyme, making the two options somewhat ambiguous.

questions.question_text: How does crossing over during meiosis bring variation in species?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Increasing the amount of genes in one of the parents during meiosis

options.label: B
options.option_text: Combination of genes in the gametes that are not found in either parent
options.explanation: Crossing over during meiosis exchanges segments between homologous chromosomes, producing gametes with combinations of genes not found in either parent. This recombination creates new genetic combinations in offspring and increases variation in species. It does not increase gene number or create entirely new genes.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Combining sex and somatic cell chromosomes

options.label: D
options.option_text: Creating genes that are not found in both parents due to meiosis

questions.question_text: How does our body synthesize some of the amino acids in our body?

options.label: B
options.option_text: From intermediate molecules of different pathways
options.explanation: The body synthesizes some amino acids from intermediate molecules produced in different metabolic pathways, such as intermediates of glycolysis and the Krebs cycle. These non-essential amino acids are built by transamination from these intermediates. Fatty acids, pre-existing proteins, and cell breakdown are not direct sources for synthesizing amino acids.

options.label: C
options.option_text: From the breakdown of pre-existing proteins

options.label: D
options.option_text: From the biological breakdown of our own cells

questions.question_text: This item is based on the following list of events during cloning of an insulin gene into plasmid. I. Obtaining insulin-producing cells and plasmid from organisms II. Cutting the insulin gene and plasmid III. X IV. Inserting the recombinant plasmid into bacteria V. Production of insulin by bacteria Which one of the following best represents the step listed as 'X'?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Inserting the insulin gene into a bacterium

options.label: B
options.option_text: Inserting the open plasmid into a bacterium

options.label: C
options.option_text: Fusing the insulin and plasmid genes to the cell wall of bacteria

options.label: D
options.option_text: Combining the insulin gene into the opened plasmid
options.explanation: The missing step X is combining or joining the insulin gene into the opened plasmid to form recombinant DNA. After cutting both the insulin gene and the plasmid, they are fused using ligase, and then the recombinant plasmid is inserted into bacteria for insulin production.

questions.question_text: Consider the DNA molecule containing:Strand 1: T A C G T AStrand 2: A T G C A TWhat will be the sequence of the new DNA if the DNA replicates semi-conservatively?

options.label: D
options.explanation: In semi-conservative replication, each new DNA molecule contains one original strand and one new complementary strand. The original molecule with strands TACGTA and ATGCAT produces two identical daughter molecules, each reading TACGTA paired with ATGCAT, so the sequence is TACGTAATGCAT. The options containing the letter U are incorrect because DNA has no uracil.

questions.question_text: During translation, the

options.label: A
options.option_text: tRNA serves as a template of the DNA molecule.

options.label: B
options.option_text: ribosome moves forward over two codons at a time.

options.label: C
options.option_text: mRNA brings amino acids into the ribosomes.

options.label: D
options.option_text: tRNA with complementary anticodon binds on the codon of mRNA.
options.explanation: During translation, a tRNA molecule with a complementary anticodon binds to the matching codon on the mRNA at the ribosome, bringing the correct amino acid. The ribosome moves over one codon at a time, mRNA carries the genetic message rather than amino acids, and mRNA, not tRNA, is the template produced from DNA.

questions.question_text: The step of the scientific method which comesafter analyzing results and drawing a conclusion is

options.label: C
options.option_text: Designing and carrying out an experiment.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The scientific method proceeds from observation and background research, forming a hypothesis, designing and carrying out an experiment, analyzing results, drawing conclusions, and finally accepting or rejecting the hypothesis. Therefore accepting or rejecting the hypothesis is the step that comes after analyzing results and drawing conclusions.

questions.question_text: In a group of individuals in which Group A was a control and Group B was an experimental group, a student gave a placebo to the control group and an unknown drug to the experimental group. At the end, the experimental group got better. Which one of the following is true about the result?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The experimental group received the unknown drug while the control group received a placebo, and at the end the experimental group improved. Since the only difference between the groups was the drug, the result indicates that the drug has an effect. The placebo and experimental procedures appear correct, so a conclusion can be reached.

questions.question_text: A biologist conducted a simple experiment to investigate the effect of pH on salivary amylase. She added 5cm3 amylase solution into 5cm3 starch suspension with a neutral pH in a test tube. After ten minutes, she tested it with iodine reagent and the solution turned into blue-black color. What is the dependent variable of this experiment?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The dependent variable is the variable that is measured as the outcome of the experiment. Here the blue-black color formed when iodine is added is the measured result that indicates how much starch remains, so formation of blue-black color is the dependent variable. pH is the independent variable being tested.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following pairs of biological tools and their functions is FALSE?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Petri dish - used for culturing microorganisms

options.label: C
options.option_text: Quadrate - to separate solids from liquids
options.explanation: A quadrat is a square frame used for sampling organisms in ecology, not for separating solids from liquids, which is done with a filter. Petri dishes culture microorganisms, balances measure mass, and optical microscopes use light beams, so the quadrat-function pair is the false one.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Optical microscope - use beam of light to produce magnified image

questions.question_text: Grade 12 students went to a field and collected plant specimens for identification in the laboratory. They wanted to preserve the plant parts for some time and specimens can be analyzed later. Which one of the following biological tools is used for their activities?

options.label: A
options.explanation: A plant press is used to flatten, dry and preserve plant specimens collected in the field so they can be stored and identified later in the laboratory. Pitfall traps catch ground-dwelling animals, a theodolite measures angles, and a quadrat samples populations, so the plant press matches their activity.

questions.question_text: Some amino acids are synthesized using the transamination process in the cell. This activity more describes the cell's

options.label: D
options.explanation: The synthesis of amino acids by transamination is a building-up process, so it describes anabolism. Anabolism involves constructing larger molecules from smaller ones using energy, while catabolism breaks molecules down, replication copies DNA, and energy production releases energy, none of which describe amino acid synthesis.

questions.question_text: Identify the statement that correctly explains the factors of an enzyme activity.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Excessive heat breaks the ionic bonds that hold the tertiary structure of the enzyme protein.
options.explanation: Excessive heat breaks the ionic bonds and other interactions that hold the enzyme's tertiary structure together, causing denaturation and loss of activity. Hydrogen ion concentration also affects enzymes through pH, but the statement about heat breaking tertiary-structure bonds is the clearest correct factor. Flagged: both A and B are biologically true statements, making the question defective.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Hydrogen ion concentration affects the ionic bonds of an enzyme.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Increasing concentration of substrates does not affect enzyme activity.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Inhibitors increase enzyme activity by increasing their turnover rate.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about allosteric regulation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Enzymes are activated when activators attach to the active site.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Inhibition by competitive inhibitors occurs when they interact at the allosteric site.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Activation by activators occurs when they interact at the allosteric site.
options.explanation: Allosteric regulation occurs when a molecule binds to a site other than the active site. Activators bind to the allosteric site and change the enzyme's shape so it becomes active, while inhibitors bind there and make it less active. Competitive inhibitors, by contrast, bind the active site directly.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Allosteric inhibition occurs when inhibitors attach to the active site.

questions.question_text: If an enzyme from thermophilic bacteria, which catalyzes glucose 6-phosphate into fructose 6-phosphate in the process of glycolysis, is subjected to below the optimum temperature, the rate of the reaction will decrease. This is because

options.label: A
options.option_text: The particles have more kinetic energy.

options.label: C
options.option_text: More collisions between enzyme and glucose 6-phosphate occurred.

options.label: D
options.explanation: At temperatures below the optimum, molecules move more slowly and have less kinetic energy, so fewer collisions occur between the enzyme and its substrate and fewer enzyme-substrate complexes form. The rate therefore decreases. The enzyme is not denatured by cold, and fewer, not more, collisions occur.

questions.question_text: Cyclooxygenase-2 is an enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of arachidonic acid to prostaglandins, which promote pain and fever in our body. The painkiller ibuprofen acts as a non-competitive inhibitor of cyclooxygenase-2, reducing the production of prostaglandins. What would happen if the concentration of ibuprofen increased?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Pain of the body is decreased.
options.explanation: Ibuprofen is a non-competitive inhibitor that binds cyclooxygenase-2 away from the active site and reduces production of prostaglandins. Increasing the inhibitor concentration strengthens this inhibition, so less prostaglandin is made and pain in the body is decreased. Prostaglandin production and arachidonic acid concentration do not increase with more inhibitor.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Concentration of arachidonic acid is decreased.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Substrate affinity of cyclooxygenase-2 is higher.

questions.question_text: Bacterial cell wall is unique due to its

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bacterial cell walls are unique because of their chemical composition, which contains peptidoglycan, a polymer found in no other organisms. This distinctive chemistry provides the wall with rigidity and shape. Selective permeability, free permeability and mechanical support are properties shared with membranes of other cells, not unique to bacteria.

questions.question_text: Which genus of bacteria oxidize hydrogen sulphide to sulphate and make sulphate ions available to be taken by plant roots from the soil?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Thiobacillus bacteria oxidize hydrogen sulphide to sulphate, releasing sulphate ions that plant roots can absorb from the soil. Desulfovibrio carries out the reverse reaction, reducing sulphate to hydrogen sulphide, while Klebsiella and Azotobacter are nitrogen-fixing genera, so they do not perform the sulphide oxidation described.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following diseases is caused by food poisoning bacteria?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Salmonellosis is caused by Salmonella bacteria, which contaminate food and cause food poisoning, with symptoms such as vomiting, abdominal cramps and diarrhoea. Candidiasis is a fungal infection, while tuberculosis and pneumonia are respiratory infections, so none of these matches food poisoning as well as salmonellosis does.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct concerning the reproductive cycles of viruses?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Both lytic and lysogenic life cycles release new viruses without the genetic alteration of the host cell.

options.label: B
options.option_text: In lysogenic life cycle the DNA of the virus integrates with the host cell's DNA.
options.explanation: In the lysogenic cycle, the viral DNA integrates with and becomes part of the host cell's DNA, replicating silently with the host chromosome. The lytic cycle ends with the host cell bursting to release viruses, so both release without genetic alteration and release without killing the host are false statements.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Both lytic and lysogenic life cycles undergo the same life cycle but ending with different results.

options.label: D
options.option_text: In lytic life cycle, viruses are released without killing the host cell.

questions.question_text: Unlike free living cells, viruses are completely

options.label: C
options.explanation: Viruses are completely parasitic because they are obligate intracellular parasites that can reproduce only inside a living host cell, using its machinery. They cannot be mutualistic since they harm the host. Although viruses may be pathogenic and harmful, parasitism most accurately describes their complete dependence on a host cell for reproduction.

questions.question_text: Why are vaccines important? Because they help to

options.label: A
options.explanation: Vaccines are important because they trigger the immune system to produce antibodies and memory cells against a specific pathogen, providing immunity without causing the disease. They do not directly kill pathogens, prevent functional diseases, or heal wounds. Triggering the immune response is therefore the central function of vaccination.

questions.question_text: Assume you wanted to demonstrate compatibility of blood groups. You took four test tubes labeled O, A, B, and AB based on the blood group that each test tube contains. Then you added unknown blood sample into each test tube and no agglutination was observed in each test tube. From this, you can conclude that the unknown blood sample was

options.label: B
options.explanation: Blood group O red cells carry neither A nor B antigens, so they do not agglutinate when mixed with any serum containing anti-A or anti-B antibodies. Blood groups A, B and AB all possess antigens that would clump in at least one tube, so the unknown sample that agglutinates in none must be blood group O.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following diseases increases the likelihood of contracting HIV?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Syphilis is a sexually transmitted infection whose painless genital sores provide an entry point for HIV, increasing the risk of contracting HIV during sexual contact. Tuberculosis is respiratory, and gonorrhoea mainly produces discharge. Chancroid also causes ulcers, making the question somewhat ambiguous, but syphilis is the intended answer.

questions.question_text: Even though pasteurization is a technique used to heat milk, beer and other foods, it cannot kill pathogenic microorganisms because it

options.label: B
options.option_text: reduces the nutritional content of the food.

options.label: C
options.option_text: is conducted in containers that are not properly sealed.

options.label: D
options.option_text: uses mild temperature that kills most but not all bacteria.
options.explanation: Pasteurization uses a mild temperature of about 72 degrees Celsius for a short time, which kills most bacteria but not all, including some heat-resistant pathogens. It therefore reduces the number of harmful microorganisms without completely sterilizing the food. The inability to kill all pathogens results from this mild-heat treatment rather than from nutritional loss or sealing problems.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct about the binomial nomenclature?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The genus name is written in full while the species name is abbreviated.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Both genus and species names are capitalized and italicized when printed.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The first letter of genus name is capitalized while the species name is written in small letters.
options.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the genus name begins with a capital letter while the species name is written entirely in small letters, and both are italicized when printed. The genus is not abbreviated, English and Latin are not mixed in that way, and species names are not capitalized, so option C is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The genus name is written in English while the species name is written in Latin.

questions.question_text: During gas exchange between the alveoli and blood capillaries, oxygen is absorbed by the blood while carbon dioxide is removed. This opposite direction of gas exchange occurs due to

options.label: A
options.option_text: difference in the concentration gradient of oxygen and carbon dioxide.
options.explanation: Oxygen moves from the alveoli into the blood while carbon dioxide moves in the opposite direction because each gas diffuses down its own concentration gradient. Oxygen concentration is higher in the alveolus than in the blood, whereas carbon dioxide is higher in the blood, so the two gases travel in opposite directions by simple diffusion.

options.label: B
options.option_text: difference in the molecular size of oxygen and carbon dioxide.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the small surface area of the alveoli.

questions.question_text: Identify the correct statement about the effect of exercise on breathing rate.

options.label: A
options.option_text: The vital capacity of the lungs decrease during heavy exercise.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The tidal volume of air at rest is greater than the tidal volume of air during exercise.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Fast and deep breathing are the result of demanding less oxygen.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Exercise and getting fit makes the lungs efficient.
options.explanation: Regular exercise and physical fitness make the lungs more efficient by strengthening breathing muscles and improving oxygen exchange, so the statement that exercise makes the lungs efficient is correct. Vital capacity increases rather than decreases with exercise, tidal volume rises during activity, and fast deep breathing occurs when the body demands more oxygen.

questions.question_text: The following is a list of functions of the components of blood:Transport of oxygenFight against diseasesCause blood clottingWhich one of the following is a correct order of blood components responsible for the above functions respectively?

options.label: A
options.option_text: White blood cells, platelets, red blood cells

options.label: B
options.option_text: Platelets, white blood cells, red blood cells

options.label: C
options.option_text: Red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets
options.explanation: Red blood cells transport oxygen, white blood cells fight against diseases by attacking pathogens, and platelets cause blood clotting. Therefore the correct sequence matching the functions transport of oxygen, fight against diseases, and cause blood clotting is red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets respectively.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Red blood cells, platelets, white blood cells

questions.question_text: What is the cause of the back flow of blood into the atria from the ventricles? It could be damage of the

options.label: C
options.explanation: Valves between the atria and ventricles prevent blood from flowing backwards from the ventricles into the atria during ventricular contraction. If these valves are damaged, blood leaks back into the atria. Damage to the aorta, pulmonary artery or pulmonary vein would not directly cause back flow into the atria.

questions.question_text: The capillaries are blood vessels that have thin wall and large surface area since their function is

options.label: B
options.explanation: Capillaries have thin walls and a large surface area precisely because their function is the exchange of substances between blood and tissues. Thin walls allow rapid diffusion of gases, nutrients and wastes, while the large surface area maximises exchange. Transport of blood is the role of arteries and veins, not capillaries.

options.label: C
options.option_text: to return blood to the heart.

questions.question_text: During image formation, light is refracted twice before it is focused on the retina. This phenomenon happens at the

options.label: D
options.explanation: During image formation, light is refracted twice, first at the cornea and then at the lens, before being focused on the retina. The cornea provides the initial refraction and the lens fine-tunes focus. Aqueous humour and vitreous humour do not refract light significantly, so cornea and lens are the correct pair.

questions.question_text: Three students designed the following experimental settings to understand the actual taste of a food.Student 1: Blind folded two students, one of them tightly holding the nose while the other without holding the nose and tasting the food.Student 2: Blind folded one student and the other left with open eyes, both holding their nose tightly while tasting the food.Student 3: None of the participants blind folded and only one of them holding her nose tightly while tasting the food.Student 4: None of the participants blind folded and both of them taste the food without holding the nose.Which student designed the most appropriate experiment?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Student 1 designed the most appropriate experiment because both participants were blindfolded to remove visual influence, while one held the nose tightly and the other did not, allowing smell to be isolated as the variable. This controlled comparison shows how smell contributes to the actual taste of food, making it the best experimental design.

questions.question_text: Short-sightedness is corrected by a concave lens because the problem arises due to a

options.label: A
options.option_text: weak eye lens that converges light slightly.

options.label: B
options.option_text: powerful eye lens that diverges light.

options.label: C
options.option_text: weak eye lens that diverges light.

options.label: D
options.option_text: strong eye lens that converges light too soon.
options.explanation: Short-sightedness, or myopia, occurs because the eye is too long or the lens is too strong, so the lens converges light too soon and focuses the image in front of the retina. A concave lens diverges the rays before they enter the eye, moving the focus back onto the retina, correcting the problem.

questions.question_text: A patient exhibited symptoms of weight loss, sweating, and irritability and the doctor suspected an endocrine malfunction that can be related to the

options.label: C
options.explanation: Weight loss, excessive sweating and irritability are classic symptoms of hyperthyroidism, where the thyroid gland produces too much thyroxine and speeds up metabolism. The pancreas regulates blood sugar, the adrenal glands produce adrenaline and cortisol, and the gonads produce sex hormones, so the thyroid gland best matches these symptoms.

questions.question_text: Secretions of endocrine glands require receptors on cell membrane to be picked by their targets while exocrine secretions do not. This is because

options.label: A
options.option_text: exocrine glands secrete hormone directly to the blood stream.

options.label: B
options.option_text: endocrine glands are controlled by the nervous system.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Endocrine glands are ductless, so they secrete their hormones directly into the bloodstream, where the hormones travel to distant target cells. Because the hormones circulate in the blood, target cells need specific receptors to recognise and respond to them. Exocrine glands instead release their secretions through ducts to specific sites, so no receptors are needed there.

questions.question_text: Which of the following diseases is caused by a DNA virus?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cold sore is caused by the herpes simplex virus, which contains double-stranded DNA and is therefore a DNA virus. AIDS is caused by HIV, swine flu by an influenza A virus, and corona by coronaviruses, all of which are RNA viruses. Thus cold sore is the disease caused by a DNA virus.

questions.question_text: Currently, natural resources are being depleted at increasing rate and waste materials are accumulated and discharged freely into water bodies. What is the best strategy to overcome these problems?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Recycling is the best strategy to solve the dual problems of depleting natural resources and accumulating waste discharged into water bodies. Recycling reuses materials, reducing both the demand for new natural resources and the amount of waste that must be disposed of. Decomposition, succession and fossilization do not address these problems directly.

questions.question_text: Which stage of the nitrogen cycle needs the role of Rhizobium?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria live in root nodules of leguminous plants and fix atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia, a process called nitrogen fixation. Decomposition releases nitrogen compounds from dead organisms, nitrification converts ammonia to nitrates, and denitrification returns nitrogen to the atmosphere, so nitrogen fixation is the stage needing Rhizobium.

questions.question_text: A key aspect in the process of recovery of an ecosystem through succession is that

options.label: A
options.option_text: pioneer species always make the environment better.
options.explanation: A key aspect of succession is that pioneer species, such as lichens and mosses, gradually modify and improve the environment, making it more suitable for later species. Higher organisms do not colonize first, lichens and mosses are pioneers rather than a climax community, and pioneers are lower plants, not lower animals.

options.label: B
options.option_text: higher organisms colonize the environment first.

options.label: C
options.option_text: a climax community of lichens and mosses is established at the end.

options.label: D
options.option_text: pioneer species always tend to be lower animals.

questions.question_text: What are the common plants of the boreal forest?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The boreal forest, also called taiga, is dominated by conifers such as spruce, fir and pine, which are evergreen needle-leaved trees adapted to long cold winters. Deciduous trees dominate temperate forests, mosses are small non-vascular plants, and epiphytes grow on other plants, so conifers are the common plants of the boreal forest.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following may NOT be regulated by a plant hormone?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Seed dispersal is not regulated by plant hormones; it depends on wind, water and animals. In contrast, auxins promote cell elongation, cytokinins promote cell division, and ethylene promotes fruit ripening, all of which are hormonal responses. Therefore seed dispersal is the process that may NOT be regulated by a plant hormone.

questions.question_text: Bushing of a plant results from

options.label: A
options.option_text: cancellation of the positive effect of apical dominance.

options.label: B
options.option_text: removal of the inhibitory effect of auxin.
options.explanation: Bushing, or bushy growth, results when the terminal bud is removed, cancelling apical dominance. The apical bud produces auxin which inhibits the growth of lateral buds. Removing this inhibitory effect of auxin allows side shoots to grow, producing a bushy plant. Increased auxin production by the main shoot would instead maintain dominance.

options.label: C
options.option_text: decreased production of auxin by side shoots.

options.label: D
options.option_text: increased production of auxin by the main shoot.

questions.question_text: Actions such as protection of individual species, reduction of pollution, and biodiversity conservation can collectively be taken as methods of

options.label: B
options.explanation: Protecting individual species, reducing pollution, and conserving biodiversity are all methods of biodiversity conservation, which aims to preserve species, their habitats and genetic diversity. These actions are too specific to be described as agricultural expansion, fighting global warming, or fighting soil erosion, so biodiversity conservation is the correct collective term.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following plants isNOTendemic to Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Mango is not endemic to Ethiopia because it was introduced from other tropical regions. Endemic plants such as Zigba, Noug and Enset occur naturally only in Ethiopia. Enset is the false banana, Noug is an oilseed crop, and Zigba is an indigenous tree, so mango is the one that is not endemic.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following national parks is characterized by the presence of wildlife such as elephant, lion, cheetah and giraffe?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Mago National Park, located in southern Ethiopia, is characterized by wildlife including elephants, lions, cheetahs and giraffes living in its savannah habitats. Bale Mountains and Simien Mountains parks are known for afroalpine species like mountain nyala and walia ibex, while Awash is drier, so Mago best matches the listed animals.

questions.question_text: In kingdom animalia, which phylum poisons its prey by tentacles that contain stinging cells?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Coelenterata, also called Cnidaria, includes jellyfish, sea anemones and corals, which possess tentacles armed with stinging cells called cnidocytes that paralyse and poison their prey. Nematoda are roundworms, Annelida are segmented worms, and Porifera are sponges, none of which use stinging-cell tentacles in this way.

questions.question_text: Mosses are grouped under division bryophyta because they

options.label: A
options.option_text: lack true roots system and vascular tissue.
options.explanation: Mosses are placed in the division Bryophyta because they lack true roots, stems and leaves, and have no vascular tissue for conducting water and nutrients. They instead use simple rhizoids for anchoring and absorb water by diffusion. Having true roots, flat broad leaves, or evergreen photosynthesis are features of vascular plants, not mosses.

options.label: B
options.option_text: have true leaves, stems and roots.

options.label: D
options.option_text: are evergreen and photosynthesize all year round.

questions.question_text: If you are asked to draw a pyramid of biomass of an aquatic habitat that contains zooplanktons, herrings, sea lions and phytoplankton, which organisms should be placed at the top of the pyramid?

options.label: D
options.explanation: In a pyramid of biomass, organisms are arranged from producers at the base to top consumers at the apex. Phytoplankton are the producers, zooplanktons eat them, herrings eat zooplanktons, and sea lions eat herrings. Therefore sea lions, being the top consumer, are placed at the top of the pyramid.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an adaptation to reduce water loss in plants?

options.label: A
options.option_text: a single layered epidermis in leaves

options.label: D
options.explanation: Leaves covered with a waxy cuticle reduce water loss because the cuticle forms a waterproof barrier that limits evaporation from the leaf surface. A single-layered epidermis, thin broad leaves and large wide stomata all increase water loss rather than reduce it, so the waxy cuticle is the correct adaptation.

questions.question_text: Why are arctic animals such as seals, walruses and whales large in body size? To

options.label: A
options.explanation: Large arctic animals such as seals, walruses and whales have a smaller surface area relative to their volume, which reduces heat loss to the cold environment. This follows Bergmann's rule, where larger bodies conserve heat better. Smaller bodies with greater relative surface area would lose heat faster, so large size reduces heat loss.

options.label: B
options.option_text: move in the water bodies easily

questions.question_text: The institute of biodiversity conservation is one of the biological research institutes of Ethiopia attempting to conserve the genetic resources of the country. As such, the institute's major research efforts focus on all of the followingEXCEPT

options.label: C
options.explanation: The Institute of Biodiversity Conservation focuses its research on conserving plant, animal and microorganism genetic resources of Ethiopia. Soil conservation is not part of its biodiversity research mandate, making it the exception. Therefore soil conservation is the correct answer to this EXCEPT question.

questions.question_text: The importance of stains in microscopic investigations is explained by their effect in

options.label: B
options.explanation: Stains are important in microscopic investigations because they create contrast, making transparent cellular structures visible against the background. Stains bind to specific cell components and colour them, improving the distinction of organelles. They do not increase resolution or magnification, nor do they decrease air bubbles, so creating contrast is the correct effect.

questions.question_text: One of the following problems can occur if the liver doesNOTproperly carry out its digestive functions.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The liver produces bile, which emulsifies fats into smaller droplets so that lipase can digest them efficiently. If the liver fails to carry out its digestive functions properly, fats are only partially digested. The liver does not digest polysaccharides or absorb digested foods, and bile is not related to intestinal alkalinity in this context.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the correct order of food substance, enzyme, and breakdown product of the digestive process in the stomach respectively?

options.label: C
options.explanation: In the stomach, the food substance protein is digested by the enzyme pepsin into its breakdown product, amino acids and peptides. Starch is digested by amylase, fats by lipase, but these act in the mouth and small intestine, not the stomach. Therefore protein, pepsin and amino acid is the correct order.

questions.question_text: Assume you are trying to demonstrate breathing movements using artificial lung and you pulled down the rubber sheet. This action of pulling represents which step of the actual breathing process?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Exhalation and contraction of the diaphragm

options.label: B
options.option_text: Inhalation and relaxation of the diaphragm

options.label: C
options.option_text: Inhalation and contraction of the diaphragm
options.explanation: Pulling down the rubber sheet in the artificial lung model increases the volume of the jar, lowering the pressure inside so air enters the balloons, representing inhalation. In real breathing this corresponds to contraction of the diaphragm, which flattens and enlarges the chest cavity, drawing air into the lungs. Hence inhalation with diaphragm contraction is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Exhalation and relaxation of the diaphragm

questions.question_text: When three fatty acid molecules and a glycerol molecule undergo condensation reaction, they form

options.label: B
options.explanation: Three fatty acid molecules and one glycerol molecule combine by condensation reactions, forming ester bonds and producing a triglyceride, or fat. Peptide bonds link amino acids into proteins, glycosidic bonds link sugars into polysaccharides, and phosphate bonds occur in phospholipids, so ester bond and triglyceride is the correct pair.

questions.question_text: In water, phospholipids become organized into a bilayer. In this configuration, which part of the bilayer faces towards the water?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Phospholipids have a phosphate head that is hydrophilic, or water-loving, and fatty acid tails that are hydrophobic, or water-fearing. In water, phospholipids arrange into a bilayer with the phosphate heads facing the water on both surfaces and the fatty acid tails pointing inward away from water. Therefore the phosphate head faces the water.

questions.question_text: Four students wanted to conduct chemical tests on unknown food particles and used the following chemicals and materials.Student A: Test tubes and burnet solutionStudent B: Test tubes, ethanol, water, filter paperStudent C: Test tubes, benedict's solution, water bathStudent D: Test tubes and iodine solutionWhich of the above students planned a test for lipids?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Student B planned a test for lipids using the emulsion test, where ethanol is mixed with the food and shaken, then water is added; a milky white emulsion indicates the presence of fat. Student A tests protein with biuret solution, Student C tests reducing sugar with Benedict's solution, and Student D tests starch with iodine.

questions.question_text: Niacin is used to make the coenzyme

options.label: C
options.explanation: Niacin, also called vitamin B3, is used by the body to make the coenzyme NAD, which acts as an electron carrier in cellular respiration. FAD is made from riboflavin, vitamin B2, while ADP and AMP are forms of adenine nucleotide, not made from niacin. Therefore NAD is the correct coenzyme.

questions.question_text: The following are reaction types catalyzed by different classes of enzymes:1. Transfering hydrogen and oxygen atoms2. Changing of the molecular form of the substrate3. Joining of two molecules by the formation of new bondsWhich classes of enzymes catalyze the above reactions according to their consecutive order?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Transferring hydrogen and oxygen atoms between molecules is catalysed by oxidoreductases, which carry out oxidation and reduction. Changing the molecular form of a substrate without altering its atoms is performed by isomerases, and joining two molecules by forming new bonds is the work of ligases. Thus the correct consecutive order is oxidoreductases, isomerases and ligases.

questions.question_text: The hydrogen ions that used to turn the rotor of ATP synthase come from

options.label: B
options.explanation: The hydrogen ions that turn the rotor of ATP synthase come from the oxidation of NADH and FADH2 in the electron transport chain. As these carriers are oxidized, they release hydrogen ions and electrons, and the ions build up to drive ATP synthesis by chemiosmosis. Phosphorylation, hydrolysis and reduction do not provide the ions.

questions.question_text: What triggers fermentation during exercise?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fermentation is triggered when there is a shortage of oxygen during exercise. Without enough oxygen, cells cannot continue aerobic respiration, so they switch to anaerobic respiration, converting pyruvate to lactate and regenerating NAD. The accumulation of lactate is the consequence of this oxygen shortage, which triggers fermentation.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Production of ATP beyond the cells demand

questions.question_text: Which of the following processes explains lactate production during anaerobic respiration in animal cells?

options.label: D
options.explanation: During anaerobic respiration in animal cells, pyruvate is reduced to lactate using hydrogen from reduced NAD. This reduction regenerates oxidized NAD, allowing glycolysis to continue producing ATP without oxygen. Oxidation, decarboxylation and phosphorylation of pyruvate do not produce lactate in this process.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following descriptions holds true for the link reaction of respiration?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Pyruvate reacts with coenzyme A to form acetyl coenzyme A.
options.explanation: The link reaction of aerobic respiration converts pyruvate, produced by glycolysis, into acetyl coenzyme A. Pyruvate reacts with coenzyme A, releasing carbon dioxide and producing reduced NAD. Converting glucose to pyruvate is glycolysis, and reduced NAD and reduced FAD production occurs in the Krebs cycle, so option A describes the link reaction.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Glucose is converted to pyruvate through a chain of reactions.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Hydrogen ion and ATP are synthesized.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Reduced NAD and reduced FAD are produced.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the neo-Darwinian idea of evolution?

options.label: B
options.option_text: natural selection through genetics and behavior.
options.explanation: Neo-Darwinism combines Darwin's natural selection with modern genetics, explaining evolution through natural selection acting on genetically inherited variation, along with behaviour. Inheriting acquired characteristics and use and disuse of structures are Lamarck's ideas, and competition alone does not capture the genetic basis emphasized by the modern synthesis.

options.label: C
options.option_text: use and disuse of anatomical structures.

questions.question_text: What is the significance of Australopithecus afarensis in the study of human evolution? To confirm

options.label: A
options.option_text: evolution of bipedalism before large brains
options.explanation: Australopithecus afarensis, famously represented by the Lucy skeleton, is significant because it confirms that bipedalism evolved before large brains. Lucy's pelvis, leg and foot bones clearly show upright walking while her brain remained small, proving that our ancestors walked on two legs long before brain size increased.

options.label: C
options.option_text: true common ancestor of chimpanzees and humans

options.label: D
options.option_text: convergent evolution of Homo neanderthalensis and Homo erectus

questions.question_text: Instinctive behavior

options.label: A
options.option_text: is common to all members of a species.
options.explanation: Instinctive behaviour is genetically determined, inherited, and common to all members of a species, so it does not vary from individual to individual. It is fully functional at the first attempt and cannot be modified by new experiences. Behaviours that vary, are modified, or develop through trial and error are learned behaviours.

options.label: C
options.option_text: may be modified by new experiences.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is an example of latent learning?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The random movement of woodlice in response to changes in light intensity and humidity.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Knowledge of a mice about the immediate environment of its burrow may help it escape from predator.
options.explanation: Latent learning is learning that occurs without reinforcement and is not expressed until later when needed. A mouse's knowledge of the immediate environment around its burrow, gained through exploration, is stored and later helps it escape a predator, exemplifying latent learning. The other options describe taxis, communication and courtship behaviour.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Foraging bees returning from successful trip dance on the honey comb to recruit others to harvest a new.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Female baboon turns its buttock toward the dominant male to signify readiness to mate.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about the action of apoenzymes and coenzymes?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Coenzymes bind with cofactors to form an active enzyme.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Apoenzymes bind with enzymes to give catalytic activity.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Both apoenzymes and coenzymes combine with cofactors to form a non-active enzyme.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Coenzymes bind with enzymes to give catalytic activity.
options.explanation: Coenzymes are non-protein organic molecules that bind to enzymes, specifically the apoenzyme protein, to form the active holoenzyme with full catalytic activity. Cofactors are inorganic ions, and neither binds with another cofactor nor forms a non-active enzyme, so option D correctly states that coenzymes bind with enzymes to give catalytic activity.

questions.question_text: Consider the following statements.I. Genetically determined and common to all members of a species.II. The behavior may be modified by new experiences.III. Behavior is fully functional at the first attempt.IV. Generally there is no modification of the behavior.Which numbers describe innate and learned behaviors?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Innate: III, IV and Learned: I, II

options.label: B
options.option_text: Innate: I, II and learned: III, IV

options.label: C
options.option_text: Innate: II, III, IV and Learned: I

options.label: D
options.option_text: Innate: I, III, IV and Learned: II
options.explanation: Innate behaviour is genetically determined, common to all members of a species, fully functional at the first attempt, and generally not modified by experience, matching statements I, III and IV. Learned behaviour may be modified by new experiences, matching statement II. Therefore innate behaviour is described by I, III, IV and learned behaviour by II.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an example of social behavior?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Exaggeration of size by fluffing up of feathers

options.label: B
options.option_text: Singing of frogs on spring nights

options.label: D
options.option_text: Caring for offspring that are not one's own
options.explanation: Social behaviour involves interactions between members of a species, including altruism, where individuals care for offspring that are not their own, such as cooperative breeding in meerkats and birds. Fluffing feathers and marking territory are agonistic or territorial behaviour, while singing frogs is mating behaviour, so caring for others' offspring is the social behaviour.

questions.question_text: Consider the following reaction:Reactant A + Reactant B → Enzyme → Intermediate → Product AB +Enzyme?At which point are the chemical bonds weakened?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The chemical bonds of the reacting molecules are weakened when the reaction reaches the intermediate, or transition state, which is the high-energy stage between reactants and products. At this point the enzyme has bound the substrates and strained their bonds, lowering the activation energy. Thus the bonds are weakened at the intermediate stage.

questions.question_text: How do enzymes bind and act on their substrates? By using the

options.label: A
options.option_text: lock-and-key model and reducing energy of the substrate

options.label: B
options.option_text: induced-fit model and providing extra energy for the substrate

options.label: C
options.option_text: lock-and-key model and changing themselves into products

options.label: D
options.option_text: induced-fit model and putting the substrates under tension
options.explanation: Enzymes act on substrates using the induced-fit model, where the active site changes shape to fit the substrate after binding. The enzyme then puts the substrate under tension, straining and weakening its bonds, which lowers the activation energy needed for the reaction. The lock-and-key model describes rigid fitting, and enzymes do not become products.

questions.question_text: Which of the following external factors influence the turnover rate of enzymes by completely damaging their tertiary structure?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Temperature and pH are external factors that can completely damage an enzyme's tertiary structure by denaturing it, unfolding the three-dimensional shape and destroying the active site so the enzyme stops working. Competitive inhibitors and substrate concentration affect activity but do not permanently destroy the enzyme's tertiary structure, so temperature and pH are correct.

questions.question_text: During baking of injera, the CO2 produced by yeast is used to

options.label: B
options.explanation: During baking of injera, yeast produces carbon dioxide gas by fermentation, and the trapped gas bubbles form the characteristic holes and spongy texture of injera. The CO2 does not kill contaminants, lower the baking temperature, or increase shelf life, so giving injera its typical texture is the correct function.

options.label: D
options.option_text: increase the shelf life of injera.

questions.question_text: The nerve impulse is transmitted from one neuron to another by a neurotransmitter at the

options.label: C
options.explanation: The nerve impulse is transmitted from one neuron to the next by neurotransmitter chemicals released into the synapse, the tiny gap between neurons. The axon conducts impulses along a neuron, the cell body contains the nucleus, and the myelin sheath insulates the axon, so transmission between neurons occurs at the synapse.

questions.question_text: What happens if the axon is stimulated? Formation of

options.label: A
options.option_text: negative charge in both sides of the axon

options.label: C
options.explanation: When the axon is stimulated, sodium channels open and sodium ions rush into the axon, making the inside positively charged relative to the outside. This depolarization reverses the resting negative-inside, positive-outside state. Therefore stimulation of the axon results in formation of positive charge inside the axon.

options.label: D
options.option_text: positive charge outside of the axon

questions.question_text: Assume you wanted to demonstrate a simple reflex action using the knee jerk reflex. You asked a friend to sit with one leg crossed over the other. Which one of the following indicates the correct demonstration?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Pulling down your friend's leg that is followed by downward movement

options.label: B
options.option_text: Hitting your friend on the toes followed by sudden upward movement of the leg

options.label: C
options.option_text: Bending up your friend's leg followed by downward movement of the leg

options.label: D
options.option_text: Hitting your friend below the knee cap followed by a sudden upward movement
options.explanation: The knee jerk reflex is correctly demonstrated by tapping the tendon just below the knee cap, which stretches the muscle and triggers an automatic reflex that produces a sudden upward movement of the lower leg. Pulling or bending the leg, or hitting the toes, do not stimulate the patellar tendon, so option D is correct.

questions.question_text: A finch with an average length beak was not able to obtain insects out of the cracks in the bark of trees as well as one with a longer beak. It was also not able to crush seeds as well as one with a shorter beak. Over time, those with the longer beaks and those with average length beaks decreased in number, while those with shorter beaks increased in number. Which type of selection has been operated in this scenario?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The finch population shifted toward shorter beaks because those birds crushed seeds better, while average and longer beaked birds declined. Since one extreme phenotype became more common over time, the selection is directional, which favors individuals at one end of the trait range. Disruptive selection favors both extremes, and stabilising selection favors the middle.

questions.question_text: What is the name of the human ear part represented by letter 'F' in the above diagram?[IMAGE: img_1.webp]

options.label: D
options.explanation: The human ear contains the semicircular canals, sacculus, utriculus and cochlea in its inner portion, and the cochlea is the snail-shaped hearing organ that converts sound vibrations into nerve impulses. Based on the standard textbook labeling, letter F represents the cochlea. Flagged: the diagram was not included in the input file, so this is a best-guess answer.

questions.question_text: The cell theory states that cells

options.label: A
options.option_text: contain different organelles with no specialization.

options.label: C
options.option_text: come from pre-existing cells by division.
options.explanation: The cell theory states that all living organisms are made of cells, that the cell is the basic unit of life, and that all cells arise from pre-existing cells by cell division. Cells do not arise from non-living objects, and they have basically similar composition with specialized organelles, so option C is correct.

questions.question_text: Which type of chromosome mutation causes leukemia?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Leukemia is a blood cancer classically associated with chromosome mutation, though the standard example, chronic myeloid leukemia, involves a translocation between chromosomes 9 and 22, which is not offered as an option here. Among the available choices, deletion is selected as the closest answer. Flagged: the question is defective because translocation is missing.

questions.question_text: Which theory of the origin of life states that life has no beginning or ending?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The eternity theory, also called the theory of eternal life, states that life has always existed and has no beginning or ending. Cosmozoan theory proposes life came from outer space, special creationism says life was created by a divine being, and biochemical theory explains life arising by chemical evolution, so eternity theory matches the description.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is paleontological evidence of evolution?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The presence of homologous structures in living organisms

options.label: B
options.option_text: Traces of organisms from the remote past
options.explanation: Paleontological evidence of evolution comes from fossils, which are traces of organisms from the remote past preserved in rocks. Homologous structures are anatomical evidence, similar DNA sequences are biochemical evidence, and similar embryos are embryological evidence, so traces of organisms from the remote past are the paleontological evidence.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Similarities in the DNA base sequences of different organisms

options.label: D
options.option_text: Similarities in the development of embryos in different organisms

questions.question_text: In the below diagram of the chloroplast, what are the sites of the light-dependent and light-independent reactions of photosynthesis respectively?[IMAGE: img_2.webp]

options.label: A
options.explanation: The light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis occur in the thylakoid membranes of the grana, where chlorophyll absorbs light, while the light-independent, or Calvin cycle, reactions occur in the stroma, the fluid surrounding the grana. Based on the standard textbook labeling, these sites are structures 3 and 4 respectively. Flagged: the diagram was not included in the input file.

questions.question_text: A colour blind daughter can be born when the

options.label: A
options.option_text: mother is normal and the father is colour blind.

options.label: B
options.option_text: father is colour blind and the mother is normal.

options.label: C
options.option_text: mother is carrier and the father is colour blind.
options.explanation: A colour blind daughter must inherit two X chromosomes carrying the colour blindness allele, one from each parent. Therefore the mother must be a carrier and the father must be colour blind, so the daughter receives the defective allele from both parents. If the mother were normal, the daughter could not be colour blind.

options.label: D
options.option_text: father is normal and the mother is carrier.

questions.question_text: A farmer cut off several regions of a stem near to the buds of a plant. He removed some of the leaves and dipped the cuts end in some hormones rooting powder and planted the cuttings in a compost. He kept the well watered and within a few weeks they developed their own root system and became new independent plants. Which one of the following is correct about this experiment?

options.label: A
options.option_text: phenotypically and genotypically different from the parent plant and from each other

options.label: B
options.option_text: genetically and phenotypically identical to the parent plant and to each other
options.explanation: Growing new plants from stem cuttings is a form of asexual reproduction by vegetative propagation. Since the cuttings develop from somatic cells without fusion of gametes, the new plants are genetically and phenotypically identical to the parent plant and to each other, forming clones. They are not different from the parent in genotype or phenotype.

options.label: C
options.option_text: genotypically identical but phenotypically different from the parent

options.label: D
options.option_text: phenotypically identical but genotypically different from each other.

questions.question_text: During DNA replication

options.label: A
options.option_text: DNA helicase transports nucleotides that are used to build the new DNA.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the base sequence in the new DNA will be slightly changed from the parent DNA.

options.label: C
options.option_text: DNA polymerase assembles new nucleotides into a new strand, the parent DNA will become different from the daughter DNA.
options.explanation: During DNA replication, DNA polymerase assembles new nucleotides into a new complementary strand, and this is the only statement containing correct information. However, the parent DNA is conserved and does not become different from the daughter DNA, so part of option C is incorrect. Flagged: the question is defective because no option is entirely true.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the parent DNA will become different from the daughter DNA.

questions.question_text: With four different bases to work with, there are 64 possible triplet codes, but only 20 amino acids are used to make all the different proteins. This is because the DNA code is

options.label: A
options.explanation: Because 64 triplet codons code for only 20 amino acids, most amino acids are specified by more than one codon, making the genetic code degenerate. Degeneracy explains why there are more codons than amino acids. Non-overlapping, semi-conservative and universal describe other features of the code, not the surplus of codons.

questions.question_text: If mRNA brings the code "UGA" into the ribosome

options.label: A
options.option_text: translation ceases and protein synthesis terminates.
options.explanation: UGA is a stop codon, also called a nonsense codon, which does not code for any amino acid. When mRNA brings UGA into the ribosome, translation ceases and protein synthesis terminates because no tRNA carries an amino acid for it. Therefore the ribosome stops making the protein.

options.label: B
options.option_text: rRNA will bring the amino acid methionine.

questions.question_text: Breakdown of the thick spongy wall of the uterus at the end of the menstrual cycle is associated with the

options.label: C
options.option_text: decrease in progesterone and estrogen concentration.
options.explanation: At the end of the menstrual cycle, the corpus luteum degenerates, causing the concentration of progesterone and estrogen to fall sharply. Without these hormones, the thick spongy uterine lining is no longer maintained and breaks down, resulting in menstruation. Formation of the corpus luteum and rising hormone levels would instead maintain the lining.

options.label: D
options.option_text: increase in estrogen and progesterone concentration.

questions.question_text: The first incubation period of HIV is characterized by a duration of

options.label: A
options.option_text: 20 years before all the symptoms appear in well-nourished people.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The first incubation period of HIV is the time between infection and the production of enough antibodies to be detected, which is typically about two weeks in many cases. The other options describe the later asymptomatic phase or progress to AIDS, so option B is the intended answer. Flagged: the duration figures given in textbooks vary somewhat.

options.label: C
options.option_text: 3-12 weeks when mild symptoms are manifested.

options.label: D
options.option_text: 2-3 years for the progress of infection to AIDS.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a behavioral method of temperature regulation in homoiotherms?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Licking is a behavioral method of temperature regulation in homoiotherms because mammals, such as dogs and cats, lick their fur and the evaporating saliva cools the body surface. Piloerection and vasodilation are physiological methods controlled by the body. Aestivation is also behavioral, making this question ambiguous. Flagged: two behavioral options exist.

questions.question_text: What will happen if the water content of the blood is too high?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The second coiled tubule of the kidney becomes more permeable.

options.label: B
options.explanation: When the water content of the blood is too high, osmoreceptors detect the excess water and the secretion of antidiuretic hormone, ADH, decreases. Less ADH means the kidney tubules become less permeable and reabsorb less water, producing dilute urine. This restores normal blood water levels, so decreased ADH secretion is the correct response.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Osmoreceptors stimulate pituitary gland to release ADH.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The kidney reabsorbs more water back into the blood.

questions.question_text: The movement of water from the roots up to the top leaves of tall trees is carried out by

options.label: A
options.option_text: loss of water by transpiration and its replacement by osmosis.
options.explanation: Water moves from the roots to the top leaves of tall trees mainly by the transpiration pull. Water evaporates from the leaves during transpiration, creating tension that pulls water up the xylem, and the water lost is replaced by osmosis from the roots. Cohesion and adhesion support this column, not low forces or active transport.

options.label: B
options.option_text: active transport in the roots and osmosis in the leaves.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the low cohesive and adhesive forces of water in the xylem.

options.label: D
options.option_text: active transport in both the roots and leaves.

questions.question_text: From the following options, which one contains the steps of writing a scientific report in the correct order?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Title → Prediction → Hypothesis → Procedure → Evaluation → Acknowledgement

options.label: B
options.option_text: Title → Hypothesis → Prediction → Procedure → Results → Conclusion → Evaluation → Acknowledgement
options.explanation: The correct order for writing a scientific report is title, hypothesis, prediction, procedure, results, conclusion, evaluation and acknowledgement. The hypothesis and prediction precede the procedure, results follow the procedure, and the report ends with conclusion, evaluation and acknowledgement, so option B places all steps in the proper sequence.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Title → Hypothesis → Procedure → Conclusion → Acknowledgement → Prediction → Evaluation → Results

options.label: D
options.option_text: Title → Hypothesis → Procedure → Prediction → Results → Conclusion → Evaluation → Acknowledgement

questions.question_text: What type of force is responsible if a stool solution is placed in a centrifuge, spins the tube at high speed and the solid particles are forced to settle down?

options.label: C
options.explanation: When a solution is spun at high speed in a centrifuge, the centrifugal force pushes denser solid particles outward, forcing them to settle at the bottom of the tube. Centrifugal force acts away from the axis of rotation and separates particles by density. Cohesive, adhesive and gravitational forces do not explain this separation.

questions.question_text: Ten percent of attendants of a wedding ceremony were sick just after having lunch at the ceremony. What should a student do first to prove scientifically that the sickness was actually linked to the food eaten at the ceremony?

options.label: A
options.option_text: give drugs to the sick individuals before they contaminate others

options.label: B
options.option_text: take food samples from the laboratory and analyze the presence of toxin.

options.label: C
options.option_text: ask herself why ten percent of the attendants were sick

options.label: D
options.option_text: take stool sample of the sick individuals and analyze the presence of toxins
options.explanation: To prove scientifically that the sickness was linked to the food, the student should first take stool samples from the sick individuals and analyze them for the presence of toxins or pathogens. Positive findings directly link their illness to food poisoning. Giving drugs treats symptoms but proves nothing, and asking questions is not evidence-based investigation.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following importance of water is directly related with its ideal viscosity?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Water's low, ideal viscosity means it flows easily, making it an excellent transport medium in blood, xylem and phloem. The ability to flow freely allows dissolved substances to be carried throughout organisms. Being a habitat, a reactant in photosynthesis, or a reaction medium relates to other properties of water rather than its viscosity.

questions.question_text: Which property of water prevents ponds from drying during the long dry season?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Water's high latent heat of vaporization means a large amount of heat is needed to evaporate it, so water evaporates slowly and ponds do not dry out quickly during the long dry season. Viscosity, transparency and surface tension do not explain the resistance of water to drying up.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is NOT the function of the plasma membrane in eukaryotic cells?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Isolating the cell from the external environment

options.label: B
options.option_text: Transferring chemical energy from carbohydrates to ATP
options.explanation: The plasma membrane isolates the cell, responds to external signals, and exchanges materials and information, but it does not transfer chemical energy from carbohydrates to ATP. That function is carried out by mitochondria during cellular respiration. Therefore transferring chemical energy from carbohydrates to ATP is NOT a function of the plasma membrane.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct with respect to the structural components of the plasma membrane?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Integral proteins are found in the lipid bilayer.
options.explanation: Integral proteins are embedded within the lipid bilayer and span across it, so they are found in the lipid bilayer. Peripheral proteins are located on the membrane surface, channel proteins span the membrane, and glycoproteins are found on the extracellular side, so only the statement about integral proteins is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Peripheral proteins are located outside the lipid bilayer.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Channel proteins cover the outer layer of the cell membrane.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Glycoproteins are found on the cytoplasmic side of the cell membrane.

questions.question_text: The following table compares prokaryotes and eukaryotes.FeatureProkaryotesEukaryotesDNACircularLinearMitochondriaAbsentPresent (80S)RibosomesPresent (70S)Present (80S)Cell membranePresentPresentIn the above table, you can respectively state:

options.label: C
options.explanation: The table compares prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. Reading the eukaryote column for the three listed features gives linear DNA, mitochondria present, and ribosomes present as 80S. Therefore the correct respective statements are Linear, present, present (80S), which is option C.

questions.question_text: Suppose three potato cylinders were kept in 25%, 15% and 5% sucrose solution respectively and a fourth cylinder was placed in distilled water. Which of the cylinders will be more flaccid? The cylinder in

options.label: D
options.explanation: The potato cylinder in the 25% sucrose solution will be the most flaccid because this solution is the most concentrated, with the lowest water potential. Water moves out of the potato cells by osmosis, making them lose turgidity and become flaccid. The 15% and 5% solutions are less concentrated, and distilled water makes cells turgid.

questions.question_text: Consider the following table which shows a result of an experiment where red blood cells were placed in three different solutions X, Y and Z.SolutionsChanges observed on RBCsXShrinkYBurstZNo changeThe three different solutions in which the blood cells were placed in order of X, Y, Z were

options.label: D
options.explanation: Red blood cells shrink when placed in a hypertonic solution because water leaves them, burst in a hypotonic solution because water enters them, and show no change in an isotonic solution where water movement is balanced. Therefore the order for solutions X, Y and Z is hypertonic, hypotonic and isotonic.

questions.question_text: A more comprehensive definition of biodiversity can be given as the

options.label: A
options.option_text: richness, ecological and genetic variability of species.
options.explanation: A comprehensive definition of biodiversity includes the richness of species as well as ecological and genetic variability. Biodiversity encompasses diversity within species, between species, and of ecosystems. Simply counting individuals or naming plants and animals is incomplete, so richness, ecological and genetic variability of species is the most complete definition.

options.label: B
options.option_text: number of individuals of a species in a given area.

options.label: C
options.option_text: diversity of plants and animals in a given area.

options.label: D
options.option_text: number of individuals of a given animal species.

questions.question_text: At which stage of the population growth curve is the rate of natality and the rate of mortality expected to be equal?

options.label: D
options.explanation: At the stationary phase of the population growth curve, the rate of natality equals the rate of mortality, so the population size remains stable. During lag and log phases births exceed deaths, and during the decline phase deaths exceed births, so stationary phase is the stage where natality and mortality are equal.

questions.question_text: Identify the correct statement about intra-specific competition? It is a

options.label: A
options.option_text: competition between individuals with different adaptations

options.label: B
options.explanation: Intraspecific competition occurs between individuals of the same species competing for all the resources they require, such as food, space and mates. Competition between individuals with different adaptations or two species in the same area is interspecific, and competition that causes local extinction applies to interspecific competition, so option B is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: of two species inhabiting the same ecological area

options.label: D
options.option_text: that leads to local extinction of the species

questions.question_text: WhyDrosophila melanogasterare considered ideal for genetic experiments?

options.label: B
options.option_text: have the highest number of chromosomes

options.label: C
options.option_text: breed and keep in large numbers easily
options.explanation: Drosophila melanogaster are ideal for genetic experiments because they are small, inexpensive, breed easily and can be kept in large numbers. They also have a short life cycle and only four pairs of chromosomes. Option D, completing the life cycle within one month, is also true, so this question is defective. Flagged: two options are correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: complete their life cycle within one month

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements best describes the mechanisms by which meiosis brings about variation? Variation in meiosis is because of

options.label: A
options.explanation: Meiosis brings about genetic variation through two key mechanisms: independent assortment, where homologous chromosomes align randomly during metaphase I, and crossing over, where homologous chromosomes exchange segments during prophase I. These recombine parental alleles into new combinations. Mutations are not a specific mechanism of meiosis, so independent assortment and crossing over is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: variations in the content of the cytoplasm between the cells

options.label: D
options.option_text: reduction division that leads to haploid cell formation

questions.question_text: In the tropical regions, where there is higher temperature, which one of the following is most likely to take place in the C3 plant's? Rubisco binds with

options.label: B
options.explanation: In tropical regions with high temperature, C3 plants suffer from photorespiration because the enzyme rubisco binds with oxygen instead of carbon dioxide. This produces GP and phosphoglycolate, wasting energy and reducing photosynthesis. Rubisco binding with CO2 is normal photosynthesis, so binding with O2 to produce GP and phosphoglycolate is what occurs.

questions.question_text: During the light-independent reactions of photosynthesis

options.label: A
options.option_text: glucose is directly produced from GP

options.label: B
options.option_text: RuBP reacts with CO2to directly form TP

options.label: C
options.option_text: some of the GP is used to regenerate RuBP

options.label: D
options.option_text: GP is reduced to TP by reduced NADP
options.explanation: During the light-independent reactions, also called the Calvin cycle, GP is reduced to TP by reduced NADP, which donates hydrogen. This reduction uses ATP and reduced NADP produced by the light-dependent reactions. Glucose is not produced directly from GP, and some TP regenerates RuBP, so option D is the correct statement.

questions.question_text: The suitability of the structural arrangement of a chloroplast in relation to its function can be indicated by the fact that

options.label: A
options.option_text: all pigments of the stroma are floating around the solution

options.label: B
options.option_text: all pigments in the photosystem are linked to the electron transport chain
options.explanation: The structural arrangement of the chloroplast suits its function because all pigments in the photosystems are linked to the electron transport chain, allowing excited electrons to flow efficiently during the light-dependent reactions. Pigments absorb different wavelengths of light, and carotenoids act as accessory pigments, not reaction centres, so option B is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: carotenoids are used as a reaction center from which electrons are excited

options.label: D
options.option_text: the different pigments absorb the same wavelength of light

questions.question_text: Which one of the following events occurs during the day time in the CAM photosynthetic pathway?

options.label: B
options.option_text: The stomata open to allow CO2

options.label: C
options.explanation: In CAM plants, stomata open at night so CO2 is fixed into malate and stored in vacuoles. During the day, the stomata close to prevent water loss, and the stored malate releases CO2, which enters the Calvin cycle. Therefore CO2 entering the Calvin cycle occurs during the daytime.
