questions.question_text: How many turns of the light independent reaction cycle are required to make one molecule of triose phosphate?
Which one of the following sentences is correct about the activities of the heart?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The noise of heartbeat one hears through a stethoscope is the sound of valves.
options.explanation: The lub-dub noise of the heartbeat heard through a stethoscope is produced by the closing of the heart valves. Blood pressure is not uniform in the arteries, diastole is the relaxation phase when the heart fills with blood, and systole is the contraction phase that forces blood out, so only the statement about the valves is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: As the heart beats blood travels through the arteries with a uniform pressure.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Diastole is when the heart muscles contract and force the blood out.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Systole is when the heart muscles relax and it fills with blood.

questions.question_text: During culturing micro-organisms, all of the following activities are importantEXCEPT

options.label: A
options.option_text: tilting the lid of the Petri dish during inoculation.

options.label: B
options.option_text: adding distilled water to a sterilized agar
options.explanation: Sterilizing inoculating loops, transferring target micro-organisms into agar and tilting the Petri dish lid during inoculation are all standard aseptic culturing practices that prevent contamination. Adding distilled water to already sterilized agar is not a routine step in culturing, so it is the activity that is not important.

options.label: D
options.option_text: transferring target micro-organisms into an agar medium.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following diseases can be caused by more than one type of microorganisms?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Gastroenteritis, inflammation of the stomach and intestines, can be caused by many different pathogens, including viruses such as rotavirus, bacteria such as Salmonella and protozoa such as Giardia. Cholera, typhoid and tuberculosis each have a single specific causative organism, so gastroenteritis is the disease caused by more than one type of microorganism.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following diseases is correctly explained with its causes or symptoms?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Syphilis is caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Gonorrhoea has a burning sensation symptom while urinating.
options.explanation: Gonorrhoea is caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae and typically produces a burning sensation during urination together with urethral discharge. Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum, so it is not caused by Neisseria, and gonorrhoea is not caused by Treponema. Option D stating that syphilis causes genital sores is also true, so this question is defective.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Gonorrhoea is caused by Treponema pallidum.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Syphilis has sore ulceration on the genitals as a symptom.

questions.question_text: The names of which two taxa are used in binomial nomenclature?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The two lowest units of classification
options.explanation: Binomial nomenclature uses the genus and species names, which are the two lowest taxa in the classification hierarchy. Every organism is given a unique two-part scientific name consisting of the genus followed by the species name, so the two lowest units of classification are the taxa used in binomial nomenclature.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The two middle units of classification

options.label: C
options.option_text: The highest and the lowest unit of classification

options.label: D
options.option_text: The two highest units of classification

questions.question_text: In a dihybrid self-crossing of a plant with genotype DdCc, 3600 offspring were produced. How many of the offspring will have the ddcc genotype?

options.label: D
options.explanation: In a DdCc dihybrid self-cross, each gene segregates independently, so the probability of dd is one quarter and of cc is one quarter. Multiplying the probabilities gives a ddcc probability of one sixteenth. Out of 3600 offspring, one sixteenth equals 225 offspring with the double recessive genotype.

questions.question_text: Identify the correct statement regarding translation in eukaryotic cells. The

options.label: A
options.option_text: helicase enzyme begins to unwind a section of DNA.

options.label: B
options.option_text: polymerase assembles free RNA nucleotides into a chain.

options.label: C
options.option_text: first two codons of the mRNA enter the ribosome.
options.explanation: Translation is the process in which ribosomes read mRNA to build a polypeptide, beginning when the ribosome binds to the start codon so the first codons of mRNA enter the ribosome. Helicase unwinding DNA, polymerase assembling RNA nucleotides and RNA polymerase moving along the antisense strand all describe transcription, not translation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: RNA polymerase moves along the antisense strand.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sentences explains how crossing over brings variation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In meiosis I, there is splitting up of pairs of homologous chromosomes and line up.

options.label: B
options.option_text: In meiosis I, there is exchange of a section of DNA between chromatids.
options.explanation: Crossing over occurs during prophase I of meiosis when homologous chromosomes pair and non-sister chromatids exchange segments of DNA, creating new combinations of alleles. This exchange of DNA between chromatids generates genetic variation, whereas splitting of homologous pairs, independent alignment and chromatid separation describe other meiotic events.

options.label: C
options.option_text: In meiosis II, homologous chromosomes align themselves independent of other pairs.

options.label: D
options.option_text: In meiosis II, chromatids from each chromosome are separated at random.

questions.question_text: Consider the following model of DNA replication.[IMAGE: img_1.webp]Which one of the following is true about A, B and C?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A and B are identical with each other but not with C.

options.label: B
options.option_text: C is not identical with A and B.

options.label: C
options.option_text: B and C are not identical with each other.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A, B and C are identical with each other.
options.explanation: DNA replication is semiconservative, meaning each new DNA molecule contains one original strand and one newly synthesized strand. The two daughter molecules produced are therefore identical to each other and to the parent molecule. All three DNA molecules, A, B and C, have identical base sequences, so they are identical with each other.

questions.question_text: What is the central role of tRNA in translation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Carrying genetic information from DNA in the nucleus to ribosomes

options.label: B
options.option_text: Recognizing the codon of mRNA and bring the correct amino acid to the ribosomes
options.explanation: Transfer RNA has an anticodon that recognizes the codon on messenger RNA and carries the corresponding amino acid to the ribosome, linking the genetic code to the amino acid sequence. Carrying information from the nucleus is messenger RNA's role, and assembling amino acids is the ribosome's function, so tRNA's central role is codon recognition and amino acid delivery.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Acting as a template for converting a genetic code into amino acid sequence

options.label: D
options.option_text: Assembling the amino acid into a polypeptide chain

questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences explains the traditional use of biotechnology? Production of

options.label: B
options.explanation: Traditional biotechnology includes practices used for centuries without modern laboratory techniques, such as producing dairy products like cheese, yogurt and butter at the household level using microorganisms. Producing insulin with transgenic bacteria, making mycoproteins in laboratories and using industrial fermenters for vinegar are modern applications of biotechnology.

questions.question_text: Consider the following diagram demonstrating the pyramid of energy.[IMAGE: img_2.webp]Which of the following isINCORRECTabout the above pyramid of energy?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The organisms of each trophic level use large proportion of the energy to build their body.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The organisms of the first trophic level convert light energy into chemical energy.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The energy lost as heat to the surrounding in each trophic level is insignificant.
options.explanation: In a pyramid of energy, most energy at each trophic level is lost as heat through respiration, so the energy lost as heat is significant, not insignificant. Energy diminishes with each step up the pyramid, and producers convert light into chemical energy. Option A is also arguably incorrect, making the question defective; C is clearly the intended wrong statement.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The amount of energy transferred through the trophic levels drops with each step up of the pyramid.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences is correct about mitosis? It

options.label: A
options.option_text: is the division of sex cells resulting in identical daughter cells.

options.label: B
options.option_text: produces four different daughter cells from a single cell.

options.label: C
options.option_text: is the division of somatic cells to make identical daughter cells.
options.explanation: Mitosis is the division of somatic or body cells in which one parent cell divides to produce two genetically identical daughter cells with the same chromosome number as the parent. Producing four different cells, reducing chromosome numbers and division of sex cells describe meiosis, so mitosis is the division of somatic cells to make identical daughter cells.

options.label: D
options.option_text: produces half number of chromosomes from the original cell.

questions.question_text: A cross between pea plants having heterozygous genotype (Rr) has been made. Which of the following is correct about the offspring according to the Mendelian inheritance? The genotypic probability of getting

options.label: D
options.explanation: Crossing two heterozygous pea plants with genotype Rr produces offspring in the genotypic ratio of 1 RR to 2 Rr to 1 rr. Therefore the probability of obtaining rr is 25%, while RR is also 25% and Rr is 50%. Option D correctly states that the genotypic probability of getting rr is 25%.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about DNA? It is

options.label: A
options.option_text: smaller molecule and coding for only protein.

options.label: B
options.option_text: made of phosphate, sugar and bases.
options.explanation: DNA is a double-stranded molecule composed of nucleotides, each made of a phosphate group, the sugar deoxyribose and a nitrogenous base. It is a large, stable molecule that codes for proteins and other molecules. Being made of phosphate, sugar and bases correctly describes the structure of DNA.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following phyla is characterized by a flexible cartilaginous rod-like structure, that runs along the dorsal side of the body?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The flexible cartilaginous rod-like structure running along the dorsal side of the body is the notochord, a defining characteristic of the phylum Chordata. All chordates possess a notochord at some stage of development, whereas molluscs, arthropods and annelids lack this structure, so phylum Chordata is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following groups of organisms is correctly matched with its phylum?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Starfish belong to the phylum Echinodermata, characterized by radial symmetry and a water vascular system. Fish belong to Chordata, snails belong to Mollusca, and earthworms belong to Annelida, so the alternative matches are incorrect. Starfish and phylum Echinodermata are therefore correctly matched.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following events happens during carbon cycle? Carbon dioxide is

options.label: A
options.option_text: transferred from plants to animals by their feeding relationship.
options.explanation: In the carbon cycle, carbon is passed from plants to animals when animals consume plant material in feeding relationships, transferring the carbon compounds ultimately derived from carbon dioxide through the trophic levels. Decomposition and respiration release carbon dioxide into the air, while photosynthesis removes it, so the feeding relationship is the correct transfer pathway.

options.label: B
options.option_text: absorbed from air when microbes decompose plants and animals.

options.label: C
options.option_text: removed from the air by animals during respiration.

options.label: D
options.option_text: returned into the air by plants during photosynthesis.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not the function of the liver?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The liver stores glycogen, produces bile and carries out monosaccharide metabolism such as the interconversion of sugars and control of blood sugar levels. Regulating cholesterol levels is not among the primary textbook liver functions listed, making controlling cholesterol the activity that is not a function of the liver.

questions.question_text: A zoologist studied 5 vertebrate species (spA, spB, spC, spD & spE) and described their features as follows.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia, and Pisces.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Pisces, Aves, Reptilia, Mammalia, and Amphibia.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Pisces, Amphibia, Aves, Reptilia, and Mammalia.
options.explanation: The question text describing the features of the five species is missing, so the classification cannot be determined reliably from the provided information. The option placing the vertebrates in the standard sequence, fish first followed by amphibians, is selected as the best estimate, but this question is defective and requires the original species descriptions.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Amphibia, Pisces, Aves, Reptilia, and Mammalia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following plant adaptation mechanisms helps a cactus to adapt in the desert environment?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Spreading its seeds in wider areas

options.label: B
options.option_text: Increasing number of stomata in its leaves

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cacti adapt to the desert environment by storing water in their thick, fleshy stems and tissues, allowing survival through long dry periods. They have reduced or absent leaves, few stomata and extensive shallow roots. Storing water in its tissues is the cactus adaptation mechanism among the options given.

questions.question_text: What is the function of dermis of the skin? It

options.label: A
options.option_text: acts as protection against heat loss.

options.label: B
options.option_text: protects the entry of pathogens into the body.

options.label: C
options.option_text: forms a waterproof around the body tissue.

options.label: D
options.option_text: contains blood vessels and sweat glands.
options.explanation: The dermis is the inner layer of the skin that contains blood vessels, nerve endings, hair follicles, sweat glands and sebaceous glands. Protection against heat loss and pathogen entry is mainly the epidermis' role, while waterproofing involves the keratinized epidermis, so containing blood vessels and sweat glands correctly describes the dermis.

questions.question_text: Children who play by spinning round and round fast, when they stop, they feel dizzy. Why?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The otoliths round in the same direction with the head.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The optic nerves reports that the children are still moving.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The fluid in their semicircular canals keeps on moving after they stop.
options.explanation: The semicircular canals of the inner ear contain fluid that moves when the head rotates. After a child stops spinning, the fluid in the canals continues moving, stimulating the sensory hair cells, which signals that the body is still turning, producing dizziness. Continued movement of fluid in the semicircular canals explains this sensation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The sensory hairs vibrate highly in response to movement of their body.

questions.question_text: When does menstruation start in women with no obvious reproductive health problem? It happens when

options.label: A
options.option_text: the fertilized ovum reaches the uterus and attaches into the thick, spongy lining.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the FSH stimulates the development of a follicle in the ovary and the egg ripens.

options.label: C
options.option_text: pregnancy occurs and the embryo obtains nourishment and oxygen.

options.label: D
options.option_text: thick spongy lining of the uterus detaches in the absence of pregnancy.
options.explanation: Menstruation occurs when no pregnancy occurs, causing the thick spongy lining of the uterus to break down and be shed through the vagina. This detachment happens because hormone levels fall after the corpus luteum degenerates. Menstruation starts when the thick spongy uterine lining detaches in the absence of pregnancy.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences is correctly matched with the function of kidney structures?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Bowman's capsule - acts as a filter to produce urine
options.explanation: The Bowman's capsule, together with the glomerulus, forms the renal corpuscle where ultrafiltration of the blood occurs, producing the filtrate that eventually becomes urine. The cortex does not monitor osmotic pressure, the glomerulus does not concentrate urine, and the Loop of Henle is not involved in ultrafiltration. Bowman's capsule acting as a filter is the closest match.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Cortex - monitors the osmotic pressure of the blood

options.label: C
options.option_text: Glomerulus - concentrates urine and conserves water

options.label: D
options.option_text: Loop of Henle' - involved in ultrafiltration

questions.question_text: Which of the following temperature controlling mechanisms in homeotherms is categorized into behavioral method?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Constriction of capillaries when the temperature falls

options.label: C
options.option_text: Shivering as a result of drop in temperature

options.label: D
options.option_text: Seeking shade when the temperature rises
options.explanation: Seeking shade when the temperature rises is a behavioral method of temperature regulation, because the animal actively changes its surroundings rather than mounting a physiological response. Sweating, constriction of capillaries and shivering are automatic physiological mechanisms of the body, so they are not classified as behavioral methods of temperature control.

questions.question_text: Industries in the medicine sector use glucose oxidase in clinistix strips for

options.label: A
options.option_text: restoring blood supply to area of heart muscle.

options.label: B
options.option_text: detecting toxic metabolites in the blood.

options.label: C
options.option_text: easy diagnosis of diabetes by examining a urine sample.
options.explanation: Glucose oxidase in clinistix strips is used to detect glucose in urine, enabling easy diagnosis of diabetes. When glucose is present, the enzyme catalyses a reaction that produces a colour change on the strip. Detecting toxic metabolites, restoring blood supply and reducing mucus viscosity are unrelated to clinistix strips.

questions.question_text: In the systematic naming of enzymes, assume an enzyme is designated as EC 3.4.11.1. Which of the following correctly describes this enzyme?

options.label: A
options.option_text: 11 - gives a sub-subclass to which the enzyme belongs.
options.explanation: In the Enzyme Commission classification EC 3.4.11.1, the first number 3 indicates the main class, the second number 4 indicates the subclass, the third number 11 indicates the sub-subclass, and the last number is the serial number. Therefore 11 correctly identifies the sub-subclass to which the enzyme belongs.

options.label: C
options.option_text: 4 - shows to which main class the enzyme belongs.

options.label: D
options.option_text: 3 - indicates a subclass to which the enzyme belongs.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences explains the lock-and-key model of enzyme action? The

options.label: A
options.option_text: attached substrate- the enzyme complex enters into a transition state.

options.label: B
options.option_text: model explains enzyme inhibition in a complete manner.

options.label: C
options.option_text: shapes of the substrate is complementary to the active site.
options.explanation: The lock-and-key model states that the shape of the active site is exactly complementary to the shape of the substrate, like a key fitting a lock. This rigid fit allows only the correct substrate to bind. The induced-fit model, not the lock-and-key model, describes conformational changes upon substrate attachment.

options.label: D
options.option_text: attachment of substrate to an enzyme produces a conformational change.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences is correct about apo-enzymes? They are

options.label: A
options.option_text: cofactors that give an enzyme its catalytic activity.

options.label: B
options.option_text: proteins that combine with cofactors to form active enzymes.
options.explanation: Apo-enzymes are the protein components of enzymes, which become catalytically active only when they combine with non-protein cofactors such as coenzymes or metal ions. The complete active enzyme, called a holoenzyme, consists of the apo-enzyme plus its cofactor. Therefore apo-enzymes are proteins that combine with cofactors to form active enzymes.

options.label: C
options.option_text: organic molecules and many are derived from vitamins.

options.label: D
options.option_text: inorganic molecules that bind loosely with the cofactors.

questions.question_text: How does a competitive inhibitor affect an enzyme catalyzed reaction? By

options.label: A
options.option_text: denaturing the active site of the enzyme.

options.label: B
options.option_text: producing conformational change of the enzyme

options.label: C
options.option_text: binding to the allosteric site of the enzyme

options.label: D
options.option_text: blocking the active site of the enzyme
options.explanation: A competitive inhibitor resembles the substrate in shape and competes with it for the active site of the enzyme. By blocking the active site, the inhibitor prevents the substrate from binding and slows the reaction, though increasing substrate concentration can overcome this inhibition. Denaturation and allosteric site binding describe other types of inhibition.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following leaf structures is correctly matched with its function?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Palisade mesophyll - the main photosynthetic tissue of the leaf
options.explanation: The palisade mesophyll consists of closely packed columnar cells containing numerous chloroplasts, making it the main photosynthetic tissue of the leaf. The waxy cuticle prevents water loss, guard cells control stomatal opening, and the spongy mesophyll provides air spaces for gas exchange, so the palisade mesophyll match is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Waxy cuticle - controls the entry of carbon dioxide into the leaf

options.label: C
options.option_text: Guard cells - have lots of air space and gas exchange area of the leaf

options.label: D
options.option_text: Spongy mesophyll - helps to prevent water loss from the leaf

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the movement of materials in plants?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Passive transport can takes place in the phloem.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The transport of organic materials is due to transpiration.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Water is transported in dead tissue.
options.explanation: Water in plants is transported in xylem vessels and tracheids, which are dead, non-living tissues at maturity. Phloem transports organic materials by active loading, and xylem movement is passive due to transpiration pull. The claim that organic transport is due to transpiration is incorrect, so water transported in dead tissue is the correct statement.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Active transport can take place in the xylem.

questions.question_text: What will happen if an agriculture extension worker injects gibberellins into a dwarf plant?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Gibberellins are plant hormones that promote stem elongation by stimulating cell division and enlargement. Injecting gibberellins into a dwarf plant causes the stem to grow longer, restoring the internode elongation that dwarfing genes suppress. Gibberellins do not primarily cause leaf fall, root elongation or rapid side shoot growth.

questions.question_text: A biologist collected two types of seeds (SA and SB) from the field and sowed them in moist soils enriched with nutrients. Then, he recorded his observations as follows:SAThe seedling of this seed emerged from the soil curved while pushing up through the soil.The hypocotyl straightened and carried the cotyledons and plumule above the soil surface.SBThe plumule of the seedling pushed its way out of the soil, while the cotyledon remained underground.Unlike what occurred during the germination of SA, the plumule of this seed did not form a hook.Which one of the following is correct about the observations of the biologist?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Both SA and SB are of monocots.

options.label: B
options.option_text: SA is of a monocot, while SB is of a dicot.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Both SA and SB are of dicots.

options.label: D
options.option_text: SA is of a dicot, while SB is of a monocot.
options.explanation: Seed SA shows epigeal germination, where the hypocotyl elongates, forming a hook, and carries the cotyledons above the soil, a characteristic of dicots. Seed SB shows hypogeal germination, where the cotyledon stays underground and the plumule emerges without a hook, typical of monocots. Therefore SA is a dicot and SB is a monocot.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences correctly describes the properties of water? It

options.label: A
options.option_text: contracts when it freezes and ice acts as an insulator.

options.label: B
options.option_text: takes low energy to change into vapor.

options.label: C
options.option_text: allows all light wavelengths to pass through its various depths.

options.label: D
options.option_text: requires high amount of energy to heat up.
options.explanation: Water has a high specific heat capacity, meaning it requires a large amount of energy to raise its temperature, which helps organisms maintain stable internal temperatures. Water expands when it freezes, needs high energy to vaporize, and absorbs some light wavelengths. Therefore requiring high energy to heat up correctly describes water's properties.

questions.question_text: An organic molecule which is an important part of structure of chromosome is

options.label: A
options.explanation: Chromosomes are composed of DNA and proteins, particularly histones, which are built from amino acids. DNA coils around histone proteins to form chromatin, the structural material of chromosomes. Since histones are proteins made of amino acids, amino acid is the organic molecule that is an important part of chromosome structure.

questions.question_text: In animal cells, glycogen is hydrolyzed quickly to release glucose for respiration. This is due to the presence of several

options.label: B
options.explanation: Glycogen is a highly branched polysaccharide with many alpha-1,6-glycosidic bonds at its branch points. These branches provide numerous ends where enzymes can rapidly break the molecule apart, releasing glucose quickly for respiration. The presence of several alpha-1,6-glycosidic bonds allows glycogen to be hydrolyzed rapidly.

questions.question_text: A student has conducted an experiment using different enzymes to assess the enhancement of reaction rates under different conditions. She represents her results as indicated in the following table:Enzymes usedCofactors usedRate enhancementOptimum temperature required °CXZn++1.4 x 101737YCu++7.7 x 10645ZNo cofactor4.6 x 10528MCo++1.7 x 10830Which one of the following is an acceptable conclusion of the experiment?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Enzyme 'X' could have enhanced the rate better at temperature slightly higher than 37°C.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Enzyme 'M' cannot enhance the rate of reaction further if the temperature exceeds 30°C.
options.explanation: Enzyme M has an optimum temperature of 30 degrees Celsius, so above this temperature its rate of reaction decreases as heat begins to denature the enzyme. Since 30 degrees is its optimum, the enzyme cannot enhance its rate further when the temperature exceeds 30 degrees Celsius. The other conclusions are not supported by the data.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The rate enhancement for enzymes 'Z' is less because it didn't use a cofactor.

options.label: D
options.option_text: As temperature increases the rate of chemical reaction decreases.

questions.question_text: This item is based on the following diagram which depicts structural formula of a biological molecule.[IMAGE: img_3.webp]

options.label: C
options.explanation: The structural formula image is not available, so the molecule cannot be identified with certainty. A fatty acid, consisting of a long hydrocarbon chain with a carboxyl group, is the small molecule typically drawn as a structural formula among the options, so fatty acid is selected as the best estimate. This question is defective because the image is missing.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an Ethiopian endemic plant?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Noug seed, also called niger seed, is an oil crop native to Ethiopia and considered endemic to the region. Avocado originated in the Americas, eucalyptus was introduced from Australia, and coffee, although native, is not strictly endemic. Noug seed is the Ethiopian endemic plant among the options given.

questions.question_text: When a biologist shares her research findings with other fellow biologists, she is

options.label: B
options.explanation: When a biologist communicates her research findings to other fellow biologists, she is reporting her results, a key stage of the scientific method that follows data analysis and drawing conclusions. Making a hypothesis, analyzing data and drawing conclusions are earlier steps in the scientific process, so sharing findings is reporting the result.

questions.question_text: Walia ibex is an endemic animal species in Ethiopia which is found in

options.label: D
options.explanation: The Walia ibex is an endemic wild goat found only in the Simien Mountains of northern Ethiopia, protected within the Simien Mountain National Park. Nechsar, Omo and Bale Mountain National Parks do not support the Walia ibex, so Simien Mountain National Park is the correct location for this species.

questions.question_text: All of the following sentences are correct about pollution EXCEPT

options.label: A
options.option_text: deforestation increases the amount of CO2 absorbed from the atmosphere.
options.explanation: Deforestation reduces the number of trees available to absorb carbon dioxide, thereby increasing, not decreasing, the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere. The statement that deforestation increases the amount of carbon dioxide absorbed is therefore incorrect. Decomposition, burning fossil fuels and burning wood all correctly increase atmospheric pollution.

options.label: B
options.option_text: decomposition of dead bodies increases the amount of CO2 in the atmosphere.

options.label: C
options.option_text: burning fossil fuels increases pollution due to the release of hydrocarbons.

options.label: D
options.option_text: burning of wood increases pollution by causing global dimming which blocks sunlight.

questions.question_text: This item is based on the table below which shows a list of molecules.NoMolecules1Calcium carbonate, glucose and methane2Carbon dioxide, linoleic acid and water3Linoleic acid, glucose and methane4Iron III oxide, glycine and glucoseIn the above table, which number holds only organic molecules?
Which of the following enzymes is correctly matched to the food stuffs it acts on?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pepsin is a protease enzyme secreted in the stomach that digests proteins into peptides. Maltase acts on maltose, amylase breaks down starch, and trypsin digests proteins in the small intestine, so they do not act on lipids, fats or starch respectively. Pepsin matched with protein is the correctly matched enzyme and foodstuff.

questions.question_text: Suppose your friend fails suddenly due to heart attack while he is playing football. The victim needs artificial breathing to keep him alive until medical support arrives. Which activity is strictly prohibited in this situation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Remove any obstacle from the mouth that might block the airway

options.label: B
options.option_text: Open the airway by removing any obstacles from the mouth

options.label: C
options.option_text: Make sure the airway is open and the head is tilted back

options.label: D
options.option_text: Give mouth-to-mouth resuscitation if he is conscious
options.explanation: Giving mouth-to-mouth resuscitation to a conscious victim is strictly prohibited because the person is breathing normally and such intervention could cause harm, aspiration or panic. Artificial respiration is only given when the victim is unconscious and not breathing. Clearing the airway and tilting the head back are safe first-aid measures.

questions.question_text: Consider the following figure which demonstrates air movements during breathing using the bell-jar model representing the lung.[IMAGE: img_4.webp]Which of the following breathing movements happens when air enters into and exits from the balloon lungs?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Air enters when the bell-jar thorax contracts.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Air enters when the rubber sheet is pushed up.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Air exits when Y-piece is rotated both clock wise and counter-clockwise.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Air exits when the balloon lungs have higher pressure than the external environment.
options.explanation: In the bell-jar model, air exits the balloon lungs when the pressure inside the balloons becomes higher than the external atmospheric pressure, forcing air out. Air enters when the rubber sheet is pulled down, increasing volume and lowering pressure. Therefore air exiting when balloon pressure exceeds the external environment is correct.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following structures of the heart is correctly matched with its function?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Right atrium - contracts and forces deoxygenated blood into the lungs

options.label: B
options.option_text: Left ventricle - contracts and forces oxygenated blood around the body
options.explanation: The left ventricle is the thickest chamber of the heart, and its powerful contraction forces oxygenated blood around the body through the aorta. The right atrium pumps blood into the right ventricle, not into the lungs, and the left atrium pumps blood into the left ventricle. The left ventricle match is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Right ventricle - contracts and forces blood into the left ventricles

options.label: D
options.option_text: Left atrium - contracts and forces blood into the right ventricles

questions.question_text: In the aerobic cellular respiration

options.label: A
options.option_text: Krebs cycle takes place in the cytoplasm.

options.label: B
options.option_text: glycolysis takes place in the mitochondria.

options.label: C
options.option_text: electron transport chain takes place in the cytoplasm.

options.label: D
options.option_text: pyruvate enters into the mitochondria for further stages.
options.explanation: In aerobic respiration, glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm, producing pyruvate that then enters the mitochondria for the Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation. The Krebs cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix, and the electron transport chain occurs on the inner mitochondrial membrane. Therefore pyruvate entering the mitochondria for further stages is correct.

questions.question_text: Consider the following diagram showing blood circulation system in the human body.[IMAGE: img_5.webp]In the above diagram, the parts indicated by numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4 are respectively

options.label: A
options.option_text: aorta, vena cava, pulmonary vein, pulmonary artery.

options.label: B
options.option_text: pulmonary artery, pulmonary vein, vena cava, aorta.
options.explanation: The blood circulation diagram is not available, so the identity of the numbered vessels cannot be verified from the image. Pulmonary artery, pulmonary vein, vena cava and aorta is selected as the best estimate of the standard labelling order. This question is defective because the diagram is missing and the letter mapping is unverifiable.

options.label: C
options.option_text: pulmonary vein, aorta, vena cava, pulmonary artery.

options.label: D
options.option_text: vena cava, pulmonary artery, aorta, pulmonary vein.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following descriptions of proteins is correctly matched with its function in a cell-membrane?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Peripheral proteins - anchor integral proteins to the cytoskeleton
options.explanation: Peripheral proteins are located on the surface of the cell membrane, where they anchor integral proteins to the cytoskeleton, helping maintain membrane shape and stability. Glycoproteins function in cell recognition, channel proteins transport ions and small molecules, and carrier proteins bind and transport specific molecules. Peripheral proteins anchoring integral proteins to the cytoskeleton is the correct match.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Glycoproteins - reduces the fluidity of the membrane

options.label: C
options.option_text: Channel proteins - larger molecules can pass through them

options.label: D
options.option_text: Carrier proteins - specific ions can pass along them

questions.question_text: Suppose a hypothetical cell of 15% solute concentration is put in a beaker containing 90% water and 10% solute. In which way will the water move?

options.label: A
options.option_text: From the cell to the beaker

options.label: B
options.option_text: From the beaker to the cell
options.explanation: The cell has a 15% solute concentration, meaning 85% water, while the beaker has 10% solute, meaning 90% water. Water moves from the region of higher water potential, the beaker, to the region of lower water potential, the cell. Therefore water will move from the beaker into the cell.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Both into and out of the cell

options.label: D
options.option_text: Both into and out of the beaker

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an example of a learned behaviour?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Classical conditioning is a learned behaviour in which an animal associates a neutral stimulus with a response through repeated pairing, as demonstrated in Pavlov's experiments. Nest-building, the knee-jerk reflex and weaving a web are innate behaviours that occur without prior experience. Therefore classical conditioning is the example of learned behaviour.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about transport of substances across the cell membrane?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Simple diffusion - large particles transported through channel proteins

options.label: B
options.option_text: Facilitated diffusion - particles move from high water potential to lower one

options.label: C
options.option_text: Passive transport - particles require energy in the form of ATP to derive the transport

options.label: D
options.option_text: Active transport - particles move from low to higher concentration using carrier proteins
options.explanation: Active transport moves particles from a region of low concentration to a region of higher concentration against the concentration gradient, using carrier proteins and energy in the form of ATP. Simple diffusion uses no proteins, facilitated diffusion moves down the gradient, and passive transport requires no energy. Active transport moving particles against the gradient is correct.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following processes of aerobic respiration takes place in the Krebs cycle?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Hydrogen atoms carried by reduced NAD and FAD are released and split into protons and electrons.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Two molecules of ATP are used to phosphorylate each molecules of glucose.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Two carbon group from acetyl coenzyme A reacts with a 4-carbon compound to form citrate.
options.explanation: In the Krebs cycle, the two-carbon acetyl group from acetyl coenzyme A combines with the four-carbon compound oxaloacetate to form the six-carbon molecule citrate. Releasing hydrogen atoms from reduced NAD and FAD occurs in the electron transport chain, while phosphorylating glucose and splitting fructose bisphosphate occur in glycolysis. The citrate formation description correctly matches the Krebs cycle.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Fructose 1, 6-bisphosphate is split into two molecules of the three-carbon sugar GP.

questions.question_text: In the course of evolution, which of the following is true about the human brain?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Modern humans have a brain size between 0.7% and 1.0% of their body mass.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Australopithecus have a brain size between 1.8% and 2.3% of their body mass.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The pre-humans brain uses 80% of the resting energy requirement.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Homo sapiens brain uses 25% of the resting energy requirement.
options.explanation: The human brain makes up only about two percent of body mass but uses about twenty percent of the body's resting energy requirement. Australopithecus and earlier pre-humans had smaller brains that used a smaller fraction of resting energy. Therefore the statement that the Homo sapiens brain uses 25% of resting energy is correct.

questions.question_text: All of the following are examples of innate behaviours EXCEPT

options.label: A
options.option_text: training killer whales at marine parks.
options.explanation: Innate behaviours are inborn, genetically programmed responses, such as increasing breathing during exercise, producing tears when dust enters the eyes and a fly seeking a more humid environment. Training killer whales at marine parks requires learning and conditioning, making it an acquired behaviour rather than innate, so it is the exception among the options.

options.label: C
options.option_text: producing tears when dust gets into the eyes.

options.label: D
options.option_text: a fly moving its maggot into more humid environment.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an example of in-sight learning?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Salivation of a dog when a bell was rung in the absence of food, which was paired with the conditioned stimulus.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Use of boxes, after several trials, by a chimpanzee placed in an enclosed area to obtain bananas placed on the top of an enclosure.
options.explanation: Insight learning is solving a new problem by reasoning and understanding relationships, suddenly applying a solution without trial and error, as when a chimpanzee uses stacked boxes to reach bananas placed high on an enclosure. Salivation with a bell is classical conditioning, modifying behaviours is training, and lack of response to deodorant is habituation.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Exhibition of modifications of natural behaviors of guide dogs, horses or zoo animals to desired behaviors.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Lack of response from a lady, which sat in a shop in which a strong deodorant was continuously released from a can.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an example of territorial behaviour of animals?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A male robin threatening an intruder
options.explanation: Territorial behaviour involves defending an area against intruders of the same species, as when a male robin threatens an intruder entering its territory. Finding a mate is courtship behaviour, huddling for warmth is social behaviour, and nesting in a tree is nesting behaviour. The male robin threatening an intruder is the territorial example.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Fixed action of zebra fish to find a mate

options.label: C
options.option_text: Penguins huddling to reduce heat loss

questions.question_text: One of the following renowned Ethiopian biologists has developed a vaccine for the rinderpest disease.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Professor Tilahun Yilma, an Ethiopian-born veterinarian and virologist, developed a recombinant vaccine for rinderpest using genetic engineering techniques. Professor Sebsebe Demissew is a botanist, and the other named professors are not associated with the rinderpest vaccine. Professor Tilahun Yilma is the biologist who developed the vaccine.

questions.question_text: A grade nine student has planned to study animal cells using a compound light microscope. She prepared a slide of stained human cheek cells for this purpose. Which one of the following activities should she first do?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Adjust the iris diaphragm until the maximum brightness is coming.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Set up the microscope with the lowest power objective in place.
options.explanation: When using a compound light microscope, the first step is to set up the microscope with the lowest power objective in place, making it easier to locate the specimen. Adjusting the iris diaphragm and switching to higher magnification lenses come later. Setting up the microscope with the lowest power objective in place is the first activity.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Using coarse focusing knob to rotate the nosepiece for a higher magnification lens.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Looking through the eyepiece lens to move the objectives down.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about plant cells? They have

options.label: A
options.option_text: Vacuole which controls all activities of the cell.

options.label: C
options.option_text: chloroplast which is filled with sap, liquids and minerals.

options.label: D
options.option_text: cell wall which gives support and strengthen to the cell.
options.explanation: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose that provides support and strengthens the cell, protecting its contents. The nucleus controls cell activities, vacuoles are filled with sap, and lysosomes are uncommon in plant cells. The cell wall giving support and strength to the cell correctly describes plant cells.

questions.question_text: A plant cell is placed in a solution which has lower solute concentration than its contents. After a few minutes the cell will become

options.label: A
options.explanation: A plant cell placed in a solution with a lower solute concentration than its contents is in a hypotonic solution. Water enters the cell by osmosis, filling the vacuole and pushing the cytoplasm against the cell wall, making the cell turgid. The strong cell wall prevents bursting, so turgid correctly describes the outcome.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about human food digestion?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The stomach physically breaks down the ingested food.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Mouth use protease enzyme to breakdown proteins.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Large intestine is the site of lipid hydrolysis.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The small intestine is site of absorption of digested molecules.
options.explanation: The small intestine is the main site of digestion and absorption, where digested molecules such as amino acids and monosaccharides are absorbed through the intestinal villi into the blood. The stomach churns food and digests proteins, the mouth digests starch, and the large intestine absorbs water. The small intestine being the absorption site is correct.

questions.question_text: Sickle cell anemia is caused by the replacement of glutamic acid by valine at a specific position in the beta chains of hemoglobin. This change is an example of which mutation?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sickle cell anaemia results from the substitution of the amino acid glutamic acid by valine in the beta chains of hemoglobin, caused by a single base change in the DNA. This type of mutation, where one base or amino acid replaces another, is called a substitution. The replacement is an example of a substitution mutation.

questions.question_text: Stanley Miller conducted spark-discharge experiment by taking a mixture of gases that he thought to represent the primitive atmosphere of the Earth. All of the following were found in his gas mixture EXCEPT

options.label: D
options.explanation: Stanley Miller used a mixture of gases representing the primitive atmosphere, including methane, ammonia, hydrogen and water vapour, which were sparked to produce organic molecules. Carbon dioxide was not part of Miller's original gas mixture. Therefore carbon dioxide is the gas not found in his mixture among the options.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences explains the Darwin theory of evolution?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Environment changes, creating a need for organism to change.

options.label: B
options.option_text: There is a natural variation in features that are heritable.
options.explanation: Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection states that individuals within a population show natural variation in heritable features, and those with favourable variations survive and reproduce more successfully. Organisms do not change because of a need and do not pass on acquired features. Natural variation in heritable features correctly explains Darwin's theory.

options.label: C
options.option_text: New features acquired in lifetime are passed to the offspring.

options.label: D
options.option_text: There is development of new feature in order to survive.

questions.question_text: Comparative anatomy provides evidence of evolution because it

options.label: A
options.option_text: looks at structural similarities of organisms.
options.explanation: Comparative anatomy provides evidence for evolution by examining structural similarities and differences between organisms, such as homologous structures that share a common evolutionary origin despite different functions. Fossils, impressions and embryos are evidence from palaeontology and embryology. Comparative anatomy specifically looks at the structural similarities of organisms.

options.label: B
options.option_text: has remains of animals and plants from the remote past.

options.label: C
options.option_text: has an impression of animal even if the actual parts are missing.

options.label: D
options.option_text: studies the development of the embryos of vertibrates.

questions.question_text: About 3 million years ago the Isthmus of Panama separated the shrimp population of the Caribbean Sea and created two populations of shrimps, one on either side of the isthmus. They still look remarkably similar, but they do not interbreed with each other. Which type of isolation is described by this scenario?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The Isthmus of Panama is a physical barrier that separated the shrimp population, creating two populations on either side that cannot interbreed. This separation by a geographic barrier is geographical isolation. Seasonal, behavioural and temporal isolation are reproductive isolating mechanisms not caused by a physical barrier, so the scenario describes geographical isolation.

questions.question_text: In a metabolic pathway, the end-product inhibition occurs when the

options.label: A
options.option_text: last product of the pathway inhibits the last enzymatic reaction.

options.label: B
options.option_text: first product of the pathway inhibits the last enzymatic reaction.

options.label: C
options.option_text: first product of the pathway inhibits the third enzyme of the reaction.

options.label: D
options.option_text: last product of the pathway inhibits the first enzymatic reaction.
options.explanation: End-product inhibition, also called feedback inhibition, occurs when the final product of a metabolic pathway accumulates and inhibits the first enzyme of the pathway, preventing overproduction. The last product does not inhibit the last reaction but regulates the initial step of the pathway. The last product inhibiting the first enzymatic reaction correctly describes end-product inhibition.

questions.question_text: The following graph shows the rate of reaction of catalase enzyme at a constant temperature and at different substrate concentration (in %).[IMAGE: img_6.webp]From the above graph, we can conclude that catalase was functional with its minimum turnover rate from substrate concentration of

options.label: B
options.explanation: The graph showing catalase rate against substrate concentration is not available, but catalase would show its minimum turnover rate at the lowest substrate concentration, where few substrate molecules are available to bind the enzyme. Among the options, the substrate concentration range 0.1 to 0.2 is the lowest, so it represents the minimum turnover rate. The graph is needed to verify.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct about the description of the cell theory?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Schleiden and Schwann stated that all cells come from pre-existing cells.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Virchow stated that cell is the unit of structure, physiology and organization of living things.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Modern cell theory states that cells contain hereditary information that passes from cell to cell.
options.explanation: Modern cell theory states that cells contain hereditary information, DNA, which is passed from cell to cell during cell division. Schleiden and Schwann stated that cells are the basic units of structure, while Virchow stated that cells arise from pre-existing cells. The statement that cells contain hereditary information passing from cell to cell is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Spontaneous generation theory states that all cells have basically different chemical composition.

questions.question_text: A student measured the diameter of onion epidermal cells at a magnification of 100X using a field of view adjusted to 2mm by stage micrometer. What would be the diameter of individual cells if 8 cells fit into the field of view of the microscope at 100X magnification?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The field of view is 2 millimetres, which equals 2000 micrometres. If 8 onion epidermal cells fit across this field at 100X magnification, each cell measures 2000 divided by 8, giving 250 micrometres. The diameter of the individual cells is therefore 250 micrometres.

questions.question_text: Which of the following characteristics of cells is found only in prokaryotic cell?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Division of labor within the cell

options.label: B
options.explanation: Prokaryotic cells characteristically possess a continuous loop of DNA, a single circular chromosome, without a nuclear membrane. Division of labour, large cell size and higher complexity are features of eukaryotic cells. Therefore the continuous loop of DNA is the characteristic found only in prokaryotic cells.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences is true about viruses?

options.label: A
options.option_text: AIDS is caused by a DNA virus.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Corona virus is a DNA virus.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Swine flu is caused by an RNA virus.
options.explanation: Swine flu is caused by the influenza A H1N1 virus, which has RNA as its genetic material, making it an RNA virus. HIV is also an RNA virus, while herpes simplex is a DNA virus, so both C and D are technically correct, making this question defective. Swine flu caused by an RNA virus is selected as the intended answer.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Herpes simplex is a DNA virus.

questions.question_text: The process by which organisms that are better adapted to their environment are more likely to survive and reproduce is known as:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is artificial selection is driven by human choice.

options.label: B
options.explanation: This is the definition of natural selection.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is genetic drift is a random change in allele frequencies.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is gene flow is the movement of alleles between populations.

questions.question_text: A population of rabbits lives in a snowy environment. Over time, rabbits with white fur become more common than those with brown fur. This is an example of:

options.label: A
options.explanation: The population phenotype is shifting toward white fur, which is one extreme.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Option B is stabilizing selection favors the average phenotype.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is disruptive selection favors both extremes.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is sexual selection involves mating preferences.

questions.question_text: The following steps are involved when HIV infects its host cell in the human body.Conversion of viral RNA into DNA and its incorporation into cell's DNAViral DNA's transcription into viral RNA and production of proteins.Assemblage of new viral particles from RNA, proteins, and Reverse TranscriptaseThe binding of gp120 of HIV to CD4 of a T-LymphocyteFusion of HIV with the plasma membrane of the host cellRelease of its RNA and reverse transcriptase into the cell.The logical order of the steps listed above would be:

options.label: A
options.explanation: HIV infection proceeds in order: gp120 binds CD4 on a T-lymphocyte, the virus fuses with the plasma membrane, its RNA and reverse transcriptase enter the cell, viral RNA is converted into DNA and incorporated into host DNA, viral DNA transcribes RNA and produces proteins, and new viral particles assemble. The order is correct.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following bacteria produces ammonium ion by forming a symbiotic association with peas and beans?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria live symbiotically in root nodules of legumes such as peas and beans, where they fix atmospheric nitrogen and convert it into ammonium ions usable by the plants. Azotobacter is a free-living nitrogen fixer, while Klebsiella and Pseudomonas do not form this symbiotic association. Rhizobium produces ammonium ions in association with peas and beans.

questions.question_text: This item is based on the following diagram which depicts the water cycle.[IMAGE: img_7.webp]In the above diagram, the letters A,B,C and D respectively represent:

options.label: A
options.explanation: In the water cycle, evaporation is the loss of water from water bodies, transpiration is water loss from plants, condensation forms clouds as water vapour cools, and precipitation returns water to the ground as rain or snow. The standard order evaporation, transpiration, condensation and precipitation is selected, but the diagram is not provided to verify letter positions.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following comparisons is true about primary and secondary successions? Secondary succession has:

options.label: B
options.option_text: reduced total biomass of the community.

options.label: C
options.option_text: has slower progress to reach to the climax.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Secondary succession occurs on soil already present after a disturbance such as fire, so it progresses faster to a climax community and tends to be more stable than primary succession, which starts on bare rock. Secondary succession has greater species diversity and biomass than primary succession. A more stable community correctly compares secondary succession.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences describes the tropical rainforest biome? It has:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Tropical rainforests have poor and thin soil because rapid decomposition and nutrient cycling remove nutrients quickly, with most nutrients stored in the vegetation rather than in the soil. Sparse succulent plants, frozen rocky soil and migrating animals describe desert, tundra and savanna biomes respectively. Poor and thin soil correctly describes the tropical rainforest.

questions.question_text: Fresh water biomes like streams and rivers are characterized by the presence of

options.label: B
options.explanation: Freshwater biomes such as streams and rivers are characterized by the presence of algae, plankton and fish, which thrive in these habitats. Corals, kelps and angler fish are marine organisms, so they are not typical of freshwater biomes. Algae, planktons and fish correctly characterize freshwater streams and rivers.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements correctly describes intra-specific and inter-specific competitions? In intra-specific competition the competition is less severe but in inter-specific competition it is more.

options.label: A
options.option_text: competition is for a few requirements but in inter-specific competition the competition is for all requirements.

options.label: B
options.option_text: competing individuals have similar adaptation but in inter-specific competition the adaptation is different.
options.explanation: In intraspecific competition, individuals of the same species have similar adaptations and compete for the same resources, making the competition more severe. In interspecific competition, individuals of different species have different adaptations. The statement that intraspecific competitors have similar adaptation while interspecific competitors differ is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: competing individuals belong to different species but in inter-specific competition the individuals are of the same species.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following stages of cell division is correctly described in meiosis II?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Prophase II - pairs of homologous chromosomes split up

options.label: B
options.option_text: Anaphase II - chromatids from each chromosome separate
options.explanation: In anaphase II of meiosis, the sister chromatids of each chromosome are pulled apart and separate, moving to opposite poles of the cell. Homologous chromosome pairing occurs in meiosis I, and crossing over occurs in prophase I. Chromatids from each chromosome separating correctly describes anaphase II of meiosis.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Metaphase II - chromosomes pair and exchange segments

options.label: D
options.option_text: Telophase II - two haploid cells are produced

questions.question_text: Which one of the following events is an example of a sex influenced trait?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pattern baldness is a sex-influenced trait because the allele is expressed differently in males and females due to hormonal differences, with males being more likely to express baldness. Lactation, undescended testicles and retinitis pigmentosa are not sex-influenced traits. Pattern baldness is the example of a sex-influenced trait.

questions.question_text: Which of the following processes takes place when lactate is produced?

options.label: A
options.option_text: NAD and FAD are regenerated from reduced NAD and FAD.

options.label: B
options.option_text: ATP is produced through oxidative phosphorylation.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Protons accumulation created in the inter-membrane space.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Reduced NAD supplies hydrogen and becomes oxidized itself.
options.explanation: When pyruvate is reduced to lactate during anaerobic respiration, reduced NAD transfers its hydrogen to pyruvate and becomes oxidized, regenerating the NAD needed for glycolysis to continue. ATP is not produced by oxidative phosphorylation during anaerobic respiration. Reduced NAD supplying hydrogen and becoming oxidized correctly describes lactate production.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following structures of the photosystem is correctly related with its function?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Chlorophyll a - a reaction center molecule
options.explanation: Chlorophyll a is the reaction centre molecule of the photosystem, where light energy is converted into excited electrons that pass to the electron transport chain. The antenna complex collects light, carotenoids are accessory pigments, and the thylakoid membrane contains the pigments. Chlorophyll a as the reaction centre molecule is the correct match.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Thylakoid - absorbs blue and red pigments

questions.question_text: What happens during the electron transport system of respiration? The

options.label: A
options.option_text: four-carbon compound undergoes molecular transformation to generate oxaloacetate.

options.label: B
options.option_text: hydrogen atoms carried by FADH and NADH are released and split into protons and electrons.
options.explanation: During the electron transport system, hydrogen atoms carried by reduced NAD and reduced FAD are released and split into protons and electrons, which pass along the electron transport chain. Forming oxaloacetate, losing carbon from citrate and decarboxylating five-carbon compounds are Krebs cycle reactions. The release and splitting of hydrogen atoms describes the electron transport system.

options.label: C
options.option_text: citrate loses a carbon atom to form a five-carbon atom compound and CO2.

options.label: D
options.option_text: five carbon compound is further decarboxylated to form a four-carbon compound.

questions.question_text: During light independent reactions of photosynthesis, glucose is synthesized through

options.label: A
options.option_text: synthesis of reduced NADP that provides hydrogen ion.

options.label: B
options.option_text: six turns of the Calvin cycle to make one molecule of glucose.
options.explanation: In the Calvin cycle, also called the light-independent reactions, carbon dioxide is fixed through a series of reactions, and six turns of the cycle are required to produce one molecule of glucose. Reduced NADP and ATP produced by the light reactions drive the cycle. Six turns of the Calvin cycle to make one glucose molecule is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: release of hydrogen ions at the electron transport chain.

options.label: D
options.option_text: transmission of electrons to the inside of the thylakoid.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following factors of photosynthesis is correctly matched with its effect?

options.label: A
options.option_text: CO2 concentration - limits the reactions by influencing rate of initial reaction with RuBP
options.explanation: Carbon dioxide concentration limits photosynthesis because carbon dioxide combines with RuBP in the first reaction of the Calvin cycle, so low carbon dioxide reduces the rate of carbon fixation. Temperature affects enzyme activity, rubisco acts in the Calvin cycle, and light intensity drives the light-dependent reactions. Carbon dioxide limiting the initial reaction with RuBP is correctly matched.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Low temperature - limits the rate of reactions by reducing the number of electrons in the chlorophyll

options.label: C
options.option_text: Low Rubisco - limits the number of reactions in the light dependent reaction

options.label: D
options.option_text: Light intensity - limits the rate of ATP synthase enzyme action in light dependent reactions

questions.question_text: Which one of the following monohybrid crosses can be a test cross?

options.label: B
options.explanation: A test cross involves crossing an organism showing a dominant phenotype with a homozygous recessive individual to determine its genotype. Crossing RR with rr uses a homozygous recessive parent, fitting the definition. The question is defective because options B and C are identical, both RR crossed with rr, and a true test cross requires an unknown genotype.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is different from the rest with regard to conservation of vegetation?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Replanting of land with endemic species

options.label: D
options.option_text: Large scale introduction of exotic plants
options.explanation: Conservation of vegetation involves using local practices, replanting endemic species and replanting indigenous tree species to preserve native biodiversity. Large scale introduction of exotic plants harms native ecosystems by introducing invasive species, so it is not a conservation practice. Therefore large scale introduction of exotic plants is different from the rest.

questions.question_text: In the nervous co-ordination system, which of the following statements explains the synapse? It is a

options.label: A
options.option_text: chemical that transmits nerve impulses across the nervous system.

options.label: B
options.option_text: part of the skull that encloses brain for the purpose of protection.

options.label: C
options.option_text: junction between two neurons or a neuron and a muscle.
options.explanation: A synapse is the junction between two neurons or between a neuron and a muscle or gland cell, where nerve impulses are transmitted by neurotransmitters. Neurotransmitters are the chemicals that carry the signal, while the skull protects the brain. The junction between two neurons or a neuron and muscle correctly explains the synapse.

options.label: D
options.option_text: short term change in the electrical potential on the surface of cells.

questions.question_text: Two students want to demonstrate a simple spinal reflex action using the knee jerk reflex. One of them sits down with one leg loosely crossed over the other. The other hits the crossed leg just below the knee cap gently but firmly using the edge of his hand. Which one of the following situations will happen during this demonstration? The

options.label: B
options.explanation: Striking the patellar ligament stretches the quadriceps muscle, triggering stretch receptors that send an impulse through sensory neurons to the spinal cord, which immediately returns a motor impulse causing the leg to kick. The response is a spinal reflex that does not require the brain. The hit ligament stretches the muscle.

options.label: C
options.option_text: lower leg to jerk downwards and inwards.

options.label: D
options.option_text: impulse travels to quadriceps muscle from the brain.

questions.question_text: Which of the following eye structures is correctly matched with its function?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Pupil - serves as the eye's protective outer layer.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Iris - controls the amount of light entering the eye.
options.explanation: The iris is the coloured ring of muscle that controls the amount of light entering the eye by adjusting the size of the pupil. The pupil lets light in, the cornea refracts light, and the choroid supplies nutrients to the retina. The iris controlling the amount of light entering the eye is correctly matched.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Cornea - provides nutrition to the retina.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Choroid - bends the light into the eye.

questions.question_text: In the CAM photosynthetic pathway

options.label: A
options.option_text: malate is stored in the mesophyll cells during the day.

options.label: B
options.option_text: glucose is synthesized in the bundle sheath cell during night.

options.label: C
options.option_text: ATP and NADPH are produced during the night.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the C4 stage and the Calvin cycle are separated in time.
options.explanation: In CAM plants, the C4 carbon-fixation stage and the Calvin cycle are separated in time: stomata open at night to fix carbon dioxide into malate stored in vacuoles, and during the day the Calvin cycle uses the stored carbon dioxide. This temporal separation is the correct statement.

questions.question_text: In Gram staining, if some bacteria retain the crystal violet after counter staining, then the bacteria is

options.label: A
options.explanation: In Gram staining, bacteria that retain the crystal violet dye after counterstaining are Gram positive because their thick peptidoglycan cell walls trap the dye. Gram negative bacteria lose the dye and appear pink after the counterstain. Retaining crystal violet after counterstaining identifies the bacteria as Gram positive.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences explains the mechanism of bacterium to produce disease?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Its hydrolase secrets enzymes which digest substances in the tissue.
options.explanation: Many pathogenic bacteria cause disease by secreting enzymes and toxins, such as hydrolases, that digest host tissues and damage cells, allowing the bacteria to spread through the body. Some bacteria enter cells and disrupt metabolism, but secreting enzymes that digest tissue is the mechanism described. The hydrolase secreting enzymes that digest tissue explains bacterial disease production.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It enters into the living cells and disrupts the metabolic systems.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It attaches with white blood cells and destroy the immune system.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Its genetic material is incorporated into the cell for instruction.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences explains the role of bacteria in genetic engineering? They are used to

options.label: D
options.explanation: In genetic engineering, bacteria are used as host cells that contain recombinant plasmids, the modified DNA molecules introduced into them. The bacteria replicate, producing many copies of the inserted gene and its protein product. Bacteria containing a recombinant plasmid describes their role, while restriction enzymes cut and open the DNA. Therefore containing a recombinant plasmid is correct.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences describes a virus? It

options.label: C
options.explanation: Viruses are acellular organisms, meaning they lack cellular structure, organelles and cytoplasm, and consist only of genetic material enclosed in a protein coat. They are obligate intracellular parasites that cannot respire or carry out metabolism independently. Describing a virus as acellular correctly distinguishes it from living cells.

questions.question_text: A transgenic organism is an organism that:

options.label: C
options.option_text: has received genetic material of another organism
options.explanation: A transgenic organism has received genetic material from another organism, meaning its genome contains genes transferred through genetic engineering techniques. This foreign DNA is expressed in the host, giving it new characteristics. An organism that has received genetic material of another organism correctly defines a transgenic organism.

questions.question_text: Which of the following explains how biology takes part in biosensor technology? Using microorganism to

options.label: B
options.explanation: Biosensors use biological components such as microorganisms, enzymes or antibodies to detect and monitor substances, including pollutants in the environment. Microorganisms in biosensor technology detect and monitor pollutants by producing measurable responses. Developing vaccines, extracting metals from ores and producing antibiotics are other biotechnology applications, not biosensor technology.

questions.question_text: In a textile industry, microorganism's commercial products play a significant role in removing stains like grease by changing:

options.label: A
options.option_text: the temperature of insoluble large stain molecules

options.label: B
options.option_text: the acidic or basic nature of the stain molecules

options.label: C
options.option_text: the color of stain molecules to another color

options.label: D
options.option_text: large insoluble stain molecules into small and soluble ones
options.explanation: Detergents and bio-industrial enzyme products made by microorganisms, such as lipases, break down large insoluble grease and stain molecules into small water-soluble molecules that can be washed away. Changing temperature, acidity, basicity or colour does not dissolve grease; only enzymatic breakdown of the large insoluble molecules into small soluble ones removes stains.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct about application of bio-pesticide in agriculture? It

options.label: A
options.option_text: breakdowns glyphosate by an enzyme introduced into plant cell culture.

options.label: B
options.option_text: uses bacteria and fungi or their metabolites to kill insects.
options.explanation: Bio-pesticides are pesticides derived from natural sources, especially bacteria and fungi or their metabolites, that are used to kill crop-damaging insects. Genetically engineered insect-resistant or herbicide-resistant crops and toxic chemicals produced by modified plant genes are products of genetic engineering rather than direct bio-pesticide application. Therefore bio-pesticides control insect pests using living organisms or their natural products.

options.label: C
options.option_text: produces insect resistant crops through modification of the plant genes using bacterial plasmids.

options.label: D
options.option_text: produces toxic chemicals by crops through modification of their genes.
