options.explanation: Exhaled air differs from inhaled air: nitrogen stays at about 80 percent, oxygen falls from about 21 to roughly 16 percent because some is used in respiration, and carbon dioxide rises to about 4 percent. Thus the sequence is 80%, 16% and 4%.

questions.question_text: Three students carried out different experiments in exhaled air as indicated below.Student I – uses cold glass and blue cobalt chloride paperStudent II – uses ice cubesStudent III – uses tube containing lime solution and strawBased on their setup, which student plans to demonstrate the presence of water vapour and carbon dioxide, respectively?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Exhaled air contains water vapour and carbon dioxide. Blue cobalt chloride paper turns pink in moisture, so student I using cold glass and cobalt chloride paper demonstrates water vapour. Student III blowing through lime water demonstrates carbon dioxide, which turns the lime solution milky.

questions.question_text: If your body cannot make enough red blood cells, which one of the following mineral-rich foods can correct this problem?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Iron is a vital component of haemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. When the body cannot make enough red blood cells, consuming iron-rich foods corrects the problem by supplying the raw material needed for haemoglobin synthesis.

questions.question_text: A biology teacher provided common names of three organisms: human being, dog and housefly, to his students to write the correct scientific names of each organism. In which of the following ways should the students write the correct scientific names, respectively?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Homo Sapiens, Canis Familiaris and Musca Domestica

options.label: B
options.option_text: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris and Musca domestica
options.explanation: Binomial nomenclature requires the genus name to be capitalized and the species name written in lowercase, with both parts italicized or underlined. Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris and Musca domestica follow this rule, so only option B writes all three scientific names correctly.

options.label: C
options.option_text: homo sapiens, Canis familiaris and Musca domestica

options.label: D
options.option_text: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris and musca domestica

questions.question_text: Identify the typical examples for division Gymnospermae and Angiospermae, respectively?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Gymnospermae are seed plants with naked seeds, such as junipers and pines, while Angiospermae are flowering plants whose seeds are enclosed within fruits, such as roses. Therefore juniper and roses correctly represent a gymnosperm and an angiosperm respectively.

questions.question_text: A student made a collection of plants having flowers and seeds from his locality and compared their embryo, leaves and stems using a hand lens. He found that all his collections contain a single seed leaf embryo, long and thin leaves with parallel veins, and stems with scattered vascular bundles. Which option contains plants that can be categorized under his collection?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Monocotyledonous plants have one seed leaf, leaves with parallel veins and stems with scattered vascular bundles. Grasses, orchids, teff and maize are all monocots, whereas roses, beans and sunflowers are dicots with two seed leaves and netted veins.

questions.question_text: This item is based on the following diagram of a simple food chain:Leaves → Grasshoppers → Rodents → LeopardsWhat will happen if the number of rodents significantly decreases?

options.label: A
options.option_text: an increase in the number of leopards.

options.label: C
options.option_text: no change in the number of leopard.

options.label: D
options.option_text: an increase in the number of grasshoppers.
options.explanation: In a food chain, energy and numbers flow from leaves to grasshoppers to rodents to leopards. If rodents significantly decrease, fewer grasshoppers are eaten, so the grasshopper population increases, while leopards, losing their prey, would decline.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a key process involved in the carbon cycle?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The carbon cycle moves carbon between organisms and the atmosphere through photosynthesis, cellular respiration, decomposition and combustion of fossil fuels. Evaporation mainly moves water in the water cycle and is not a key process in the carbon cycle.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about mitosis? It is a division of

options.label: A
options.option_text: somatic cells to make daughter cells with half chromosome.

options.label: B
options.option_text: sex cells to make identical daughter cells with doubled chromosome.

options.label: C
options.option_text: somatic cells to make identical daughter cells.
options.explanation: Mitosis is the division of somatic or body cells that produces two genetically identical daughter cells with the same chromosome number as the parent cell. It is responsible for growth, repair and replacement of worn-out cells in multicellular organisms.

options.label: D
options.option_text: sex cells to make different daughter cells.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following features is common for mitosis and meiosis? They both involve

options.label: A
options.option_text: replication of DNA and the formation of daughter cells.
options.explanation: Both mitosis and meiosis begin with replication of DNA during interphase, and both end with the formation of daughter cells. However, meiosis produces four genetically different haploid cells through two divisions, while mitosis produces two identical diploid cells.

options.label: B
options.option_text: production of daughter cells identical to the parent cell.

options.label: C
options.option_text: formation of cells with the same chromosome number as parent cell.

options.label: D
options.option_text: spermatogenesis and oogenesis processes in males and females.

questions.question_text: Which tissues of plant leaves are involved in waterproofing, major photosynthetic, and major gas exchange activities, respectively?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Guard cells, palisade mesophyll and epidermis

options.label: B
options.option_text: Guard cells, palisade mesophyll and spongy mesophyll

options.label: C
options.option_text: Waxy cuticle, palisade mesophyll and spongy mesophyll
options.explanation: The waxy cuticle on the leaf surface prevents water loss and provides waterproofing. The palisade mesophyll contains most chloroplasts and is the main site of photosynthesis. The spongy mesophyll has large air spaces that facilitate gas exchange.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Waxy cuticle, palisade mesophyll and epidermis

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the movement of water in plants? It moves

options.label: B
options.option_text: across the phloem tissue by diffusion.

options.label: C
options.option_text: across the tissues of a plant by osmosis.
options.explanation: Water moves through a plant largely by osmosis, passing from the soil into root hairs, then through root tissues and xylem to the leaves. Osmosis involves movement of water down its water potential gradient without direct expenditure of metabolic energy.

options.label: D
options.option_text: by using energy until it reaches to the xylem.

questions.question_text: What will happen to the growth of the plant when you remove indole-acetic acid (IAA) from the main shoot part of the plant?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Indole-acetic acid, an auxin, is produced at the shoot tip and suppresses the growth of lateral or side buds through apical dominance. Removing it releases this suppression, so the plant produces more side shoots and bushes out.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The main shoot of the plant elongates.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The growth of side shoots will slow down.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about animals? They are

options.label: C
options.explanation: Animals are multicellular heterotrophs that cannot make their own food, so they feed on other organisms. They respire, excrete waste, grow, reproduce and show motility, and these characteristics are the general criteria used to distinguish them from other living things.

questions.question_text: A grade 11 student observed and identified some animal groups having closed circulatory system, centralized nervous system with brain and sensory organs. Based on their identification, select one of the following animals that can belong to this group?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Squids, being cephalopod mollusks, have a closed circulatory system and a well-developed centralized nervous system with a brain and advanced sensory organs. Snails have an open circulatory system, while earthworms possess a simpler nervous arrangement without a true brain.

questions.question_text: What does it mean if an animal is poikilothermic? It

options.label: A
options.option_text: changes its body temperature with environmental condition.
options.explanation: Poikilothermic, or cold-blooded, animals such as fish, amphibians and reptiles cannot regulate their internal body temperature by metabolism. Their body temperature fluctuates with the surrounding environmental temperature, so it changes when the external conditions change.

options.label: B
options.option_text: increases its metabolic rate during cold and hot conditions.

options.label: C
options.option_text: keeps its body temperature constant regardless of external changes.

options.label: D
options.option_text: produces heat when temperature falls by activating the hypothalamus.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct about the catalytic activities of enzymes? They

options.label: A
options.option_text: change the overall nature of the products.

options.label: B
options.option_text: allow reactions in cells to take place quickly.
options.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up biochemical reactions by lowering the activation energy required. They remain unchanged after the reaction, are specific to particular substrates, and allow reactions in cells to take place quickly at body temperature.

options.label: C
options.option_text: alter themselves at the end of biochemical reactions.

options.label: D
options.option_text: increase the energy required to start a reaction.

questions.question_text: Four students draw four different big protein structure posters. The contents of each of their structure are displayed in the following table.StudentMain contents indicated in the structureIPolypeptide folded into α-helix and β-sheet, and hydrogen bondIIAmino acid sequences and peptide bondsIIIMultiple folded protein subunits in a multi-subunit complex and haem groupIVSide chain interaction of amino acids and overall 3-D shapeBased on the above information, which student drew secondary and quaternary structures, respectively?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Protein secondary structure describes the polypeptide folded into alpha helices and beta sheets stabilized by hydrogen bonds, as student I indicated. Quaternary structure involves the association of multiple folded polypeptide subunits into one functional protein complex, as student III indicated with the haem group.

questions.question_text: How does the induced-fit model explain enzyme specificity? They

options.label: A
options.option_text: change the shape of active site slightly to fit substrates precisely.
options.explanation: The induced-fit model explains that the enzyme's active site is flexible rather than rigid. When the correct substrate approaches, the active site changes its shape slightly to fit the substrate precisely, forming an enzyme-substrate complex that promotes the reaction.

options.label: B
options.option_text: have a rigid active site that can just bind to single substrate.

options.label: C
options.option_text: have multiple active sites that can fit to different substrates.

options.label: D
options.option_text: bind to whatever the shape of substrate that fits to allosteric site.

questions.question_text: What happens to the substrate molecule when competitive inhibitor binds with an enzyme? It

options.label: B
options.option_text: cannot bind with the active site.
options.explanation: A competitive inhibitor resembles the substrate and occupies the enzyme's active site directly. As a result, the genuine substrate molecule cannot bind to the active site, so enzyme activity is reduced until the inhibitor concentration falls.

options.label: C
options.option_text: binds to the allosteric site temporarily.

options.label: D
options.option_text: easily binds with the active site.

questions.question_text: What will happen to the reaction if you add a certain inhibitor or activator to the substrate having allosteric enzyme set up?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Inhibitor binds to active site to speed up the reaction.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Inhibitor binds to regulatory site to increase rate of reaction.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Activator binds to active site to initiate the reaction.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Activator binds to regulatory site to activate the reaction.
options.explanation: Allosteric enzymes possess regulatory sites distinct from their active sites. An activator molecule binds to this regulatory site and changes the enzyme's shape so that its active site becomes available, thereby activating or speeding up the reaction.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following classes of enzyme and type of reactions they catalyze is correctly matched?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Oxidoreductases - transfer functional groups from donor to acceptor

options.label: B
options.option_text: Transferases - transfer of electrons from one molecule to another

options.label: C
options.option_text: Ligases - cleave bonds by other means rather than hydrolysis
options.explanation: This question is defective because no option correctly matches enzyme classes with their reactions; ligases actually join molecules using ATP energy, while the wording given describes lyases. Option C is retained as the marked answer, but the correct definition of ligases is bond formation, not bond cleavage.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Lyases - catalyze the hydrolysis of various bonds

questions.question_text: If a given enzyme works only at temperature range of 20 and 45 °C and the potential of hydrogen ions that ranges from 4 to 9. Which one of the following works best during the optimization of these two factors for the enzyme activity?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Adjusting the temperature below 20°C makes the enzyme more active, hence the temperature at this value is optimal.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Adjusting the pH above 9 can increase the probability of collisions between the enzyme and the substrate.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Adjusting the temperature between 20°C and 45°C results little denaturation and increased number of collisions.
options.explanation: Enzymes have an optimum temperature and pH at which their activity is greatest. Within the working range of 20 to 45 degrees Celsius, raising temperature increases molecular collisions and reaction rate while avoiding denaturation, and pH within 4 to 9 keeps the enzyme active.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The optimum pH under which this enzyme is most active is found below 4.

questions.question_text: All of the following features define a chromosome EXCEPT

options.label: A
options.option_text: contains hundreds to thousands of genes.

options.label: B
options.option_text: exists in pairs in diploid organisms.

options.label: C
options.option_text: made up of DNA and protein.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A chromosome is a thread-like structure made of DNA and protein that carries hundreds to thousands of genes and exists in pairs in diploid organisms. The functional unit of inheritance is the gene, not the chromosome, so that description does not define a chromosome.

questions.question_text: Which structural and functional difference is observed between DNA and RNA?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Both DNA and RNA have the same nitrogenous bases but differ in pentose sugar.

options.label: B
options.option_text: RNA produces DNA through the process of transcription.

options.label: C
options.option_text: RNA stores the genetic material while DNA involves in protein synthesis.

options.label: D
options.option_text: DNA is very stable molecule while RNA is degraded quickly.
options.explanation: DNA is a highly stable double-stranded molecule that stores genetic information and is faithfully copied during replication. RNA is single-stranded and relatively short-lived, being produced and degraded rapidly as it carries out transcription and protein synthesis.

questions.question_text: All of the following events occur during telophase I of meiosis I cell division EXCEPT

options.label: A
options.explanation: Crossing over is an exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes that occurs during prophase I of meiosis, before telophase I. During telophase I the spindle fibres disappear, the chromosomes gather at the poles, and the nuclear envelope reforms, so crossing over is the exception.

options.label: B
options.option_text: each of the spindle fibers disappears.

questions.question_text: Suppose there was a cross between pea plants with flower positions axial (AA) and terminal (aa) and produced F1 generation. What will be the most probable number of heterozygous dominant individuals obtained if 1000 offspring were produced by self-crossing of F1 generation?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Crossing axial AA with terminal aa gives all heterozygous Aa offspring. Self-crossing these Aa plants produces the ratio one AA, two Aa and one aa, so heterozygotes form half of the progeny. In 1000 offspring, approximately 500 individuals are heterozygous dominant.

questions.question_text: If you have a pea plant of unknown genotype with a green pod color, you obtained all green pod colors of offspring phenotype after a test cross. What was the unknown genotype of the parent? It was

options.label: A
options.explanation: A test cross involves mating an organism of unknown genotype with a homozygous recessive individual. Since all offspring showed green pods, the unknown parent must have been homozygous dominant, because a heterozygous parent would have produced some recessive offspring showing the other pod colour.

questions.question_text: This item is based on the following examples of genetic inheritance patterns.1. Inflated and pinched pod forms will have inflated pod form.2. Red cow and white bull will have roan calf.3. AA and BB blood type people will have a child with AB blood type.4. Red and white roses will have a pink rose offspring.From the above patterns of inheritance, which of the following are exemplary for non-Mendelian inheritance?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Non-Mendelian inheritance does not follow simple dominant-recessive rules. The roan calf illustrates codominance, the AB blood type illustrates codominance, and the pink rose illustrates incomplete dominance. Example one, inflated pods, is simple Mendelian complete dominance, so it is excluded.

questions.question_text: Farmers want to maintain their sheep with long tails for the next generation through similar sheep from their locality in their breeding program. What process do these farmers apply to keep the desired traits in their program?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Inbreeding means breeding closely related individuals that carry similar desired traits to preserve those characteristics in subsequent generations. It is used by farmers to maintain uniform desirable qualities such as long tails in their sheep, rather than introducing unrelated genes.

questions.question_text: If progesterone remains high after ovulation, what will be the most likely outcome?

options.label: A
options.option_text: FSH will be produced rapidly which leads to a new cycle.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Oestrogen will be decreased, closing down the lining of the uterus.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Uterus lining will be maintained and prepared for pregnancy.
options.explanation: After ovulation, the corpus luteum secretes progesterone, which maintains the thickened lining of the uterus so that it remains ready for implantation of a fertilized egg. If progesterone stays high, the uterine lining is preserved and prepared for pregnancy.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Corpus luteum will be regenerated, inhibiting hormone production.

questions.question_text: The most reliable contraceptive method that prevents travelling of ovum from the ovaries through the fallopian tubes, but requires surgery is

options.label: D
options.explanation: Sterilization, such as tubal ligation in females, is a permanent surgical contraceptive method. It involves tying or cutting the fallopian tubes so that the ovum cannot travel from the ovaries through the tubes to meet sperm, thereby preventing fertilization.

questions.question_text: Among the following, which one increases the risk to be infected by sexually transmitted infections?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Have no history of sexually transmitted infections

options.label: B
options.option_text: Misuse of drugs that inhibit your judgment
options.explanation: Misusing drugs such as alcohol or substances that impair judgement increases risky sexual behaviour, including unprotected intercourse with multiple partners. This raises the chance of exposure to sexually transmitted infections, unlike condom use, protective contact and medical treatment, which lower risk.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Protective sexual contact and medical treatment

options.label: D
options.option_text: Consistent use of condoms during intercourse

questions.question_text: Two women were decided not to have pregnancy in the near future and they were offered two different contraceptive options. In woman I, the material fitted in her uterus did not allow the sperm to fertilize the egg. In woman II, the contraceptive prevented hormone production and the releasing of eggs from the ovaries. Which type of contraceptive methods did woman I and II used, respectively?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Post pill and copper-coated intrauterine device

options.label: D
options.option_text: Copper-coated intrauterine device and contraceptive injection
options.explanation: The copper-coated intrauterine device is fitted inside the uterus and prevents sperm from reaching and fertilizing the egg. Injectable contraceptives such as Depo-Provera contain hormones that suppress ovulation and prevent the release of eggs from the ovaries, matching woman II.

questions.question_text: The finding of the study conducted in two different villages showed that there are harmful practices that affect reproductive health. The common practices in village 1 were forcing underage girls to get married based on norms and sexual abuse or harassment. In village 2, abduction to make the girl a wife unwillingly was very common. Which one of the following options is correct about the two villages?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In village 1, gender-based violence, kidnapping and female genital mutilation are common.

options.label: B
options.option_text: In village 1, gender-based violence and early marriage are common.
options.explanation: Village one showed forced early marriage of underage girls and sexual abuse or harassment, which are forms of gender-based violence and early marriage. Village two showed abduction to force a girl into marriage. Neither village description mentions female genital mutilation or kidnapping as distinct practices.

options.label: C
options.option_text: In village 2, kidnapping and female genital mutilation are common.

options.label: D
options.option_text: In village 2, gender-based violence and female genital mutilation are common.

questions.question_text: How does drinking alcohol contribute to HIV transmission? By

options.label: A
options.option_text: improving the decision making ability of a person

options.label: B
options.option_text: driving more willingly to participate in risky behaviors
options.explanation: Alcohol and drugs impair judgement, lower inhibitions and make a person more willing to engage in risky sexual behaviours such as unprotected sex. This increases exposure to HIV infection, rather than improving decision making or affecting the virus directly.

options.label: C
options.option_text: impotency or loss of sexual drive both in male and female

options.label: D
options.option_text: increasing rate of the retrovirus multiplication capacity

questions.question_text: Select the option where the whole list contains renewable natural resources.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Coal, oil, natural gas and minerals

options.label: B
options.option_text: Coal, wind, hydro power and biomass

options.label: C
options.option_text: Sunlight, wind, hydro power and biomass
options.explanation: Renewable natural resources are replaced naturally at a rate equal to or faster than their consumption. Sunlight, wind, hydro power and biomass are all renewable, whereas coal, oil, natural gas and minerals are non-renewable because they cannot be regenerated within human time scales.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Sunlight, wind, hydro power and natural gas

questions.question_text: This item is based on the following list of activities.I. Establishing national parksII. Wild sanctuariesIII. Preparing wild life reservesIV. Practicing overgrazingWhich of the above activities CANNOT be used for the conservation of wild life?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Wildlife conservation uses national parks, sanctuaries and reserves to protect animals in their natural habitats. Overgrazing by livestock degrades vegetation and destroys wildlife habitats, so it cannot be used for conservation. No option was marked correct in the source, so C is the determined answer.

questions.question_text: Among the following options, identify the air pollutants that can cause acid rain and its effects, respectively.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Carbon dioxide and methane - melting of ice caps and rising of oceans

options.label: B
options.option_text: Sulphur dioxides and nitrogen dioxides - damaging plants and water
options.explanation: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides released from burning fossil fuels combine with water vapour in the atmosphere to form sulphuric and nitric acids. This acid rain damages plants, acidifies soils and water bodies, and harms aquatic life, making these gases the main culprits.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Perflourocarbons - causing skin cancer and cataracts

options.label: D
options.option_text: Chloroflourocarbons - increasing UV rays and respiratory disease

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the cause and effect of global warming, respectively?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Greenhouse gases and dropping of sea levels

options.label: B
options.option_text: Greenhouse gases and loss of biodiversity
options.explanation: Greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide trap heat in the atmosphere and cause global warming and climate change. The resulting rise in temperature alters habitats, disrupts ecosystems and drives species to extinction, causing loss of biodiversity rather than increasing diversity or dropping sea levels.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Burning of fossil fuels and increase in species diversity

options.label: D
options.option_text: Burning of fossil fuels and dropping of sea level

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of creating transgenic organisms? To

options.label: A
options.option_text: generate pathogenic organisms that fight against non-pathogenic ones

options.label: B
options.option_text: produce organisms that mimic human beings in every aspect of behaviors

options.label: C
options.option_text: promote expression of desired genes that improve nutritional quality of organisms
options.explanation: Transgenic organisms are created by inserting foreign genes into their genomes so that desired traits are expressed. The primary purpose is to promote the expression of useful genes, such as those improving nutritional quality, disease resistance or productivity in crops and livestock.

options.label: D
options.option_text: produce novel organisms that can affect reproduction across different species

questions.question_text: What is the role of biology in the investigation of a criminal case? To

options.label: A
options.option_text: detect flavor compounds in food and monitor environmental pollutants

options.label: B
options.option_text: examine potential sources of evidences using blood, saliva and hair
options.explanation: Biology plays an important role in forensic science by examining biological evidence found at crime scenes. Blood, saliva and hair can be analyzed through techniques such as DNA fingerprinting to identify suspects, establish relationships and link individuals to criminal cases.

options.label: C
options.option_text: sense pathogens and herbicides using immunochemical detection system

options.label: D
options.option_text: determine the production of complex organic compounds using mold fungus

questions.question_text: How does biological washing powder save energy? Because they

options.label: A
options.option_text: use lipase enzyme without other combination for any stain in clothes.

options.label: B
options.option_text: are effective in cleaning clothes at lower temperatures without boiling water.
options.explanation: Biological washing powders contain enzymes such as proteases and lipases that break down protein and fat stains. These enzymes work effectively at lower temperatures, so clothes can be washed in cool or warm water without boiling, saving significant amounts of household energy.

options.label: C
options.option_text: are effective in removing dirty ores in clothes without spraying acidic water.

options.label: D
options.option_text: use protease enzyme without other combination for any stain in clothes.

questions.question_text: What is biological warfare? The use of

options.label: A
options.option_text: selective genes to produce genetically modified organisms

options.label: B
options.option_text: cloning technique to make exact genetic copies of an organism

options.label: C
options.option_text: bacteria, fungi and viruses as a biological agent to control pests

options.label: D
options.option_text: infectious agents with the intent to kill humans, animals or plants
options.explanation: Biological warfare is the deliberate use of infectious agents such as bacteria, viruses and fungi as weapons to harm or kill humans, animals or plants. It is distinct from biotechnology applications like genetic modification, cloning or using organisms to control agricultural pests.

questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly describes the general features of bacteria? They are unicellular microbes with

options.label: A
options.option_text: true nucleus and are omnipresent in nature.

options.label: B
options.option_text: rigid cell wall and a diverse mode of nutrition.
options.explanation: Bacteria are single-celled prokaryotic microorganisms lacking a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria and Golgi bodies. They possess a rigid cell wall and display diverse modes of nutrition, including photosynthesis, saprophytism, parasitism and symbiosis.

options.label: C
options.option_text: mitochondria and a special type of chlorophyll.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Golgi bodies and genetic materials of a cell.

questions.question_text: Which group of archaea are found in volcanic vents and hot vapors that contain either obligate aerobes, facultative aerobes or obligate anaerobes?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hyperthermophiles are archaea that thrive in extremely hot environments such as volcanic vents and hot springs, where temperatures may exceed 80 degrees Celsius. Depending on the species they may be obligate aerobes, facultative aerobes or obligate anaerobes.

questions.question_text: From the fungal diseases given below, which one is transmitted sexually?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Candidiasis is a fungal infection caused by Candida yeast that can be transmitted through sexual contact, affecting the genital tract. Aspergillosis, tinea and dermatophytosis are other fungal infections but are not primarily classified as sexually transmitted diseases.

questions.question_text: This item is based on the following choices of feeding habit employed by organisms.I. Using nutrients dissolved in the surrounding mediumII. Manufacturing own nutrients by photosynthesisIII. Depending on other plants or animals for foodWhich method/s do protozoans use to get their nutrition? They employed

options.label: C
options.explanation: Protozoans are a diverse group of single-celled protists. Some, like Euglena, manufacture their own food through photosynthesis, while others depend on other organisms as predators, parasites or symbionts. They do not absorb nutrients dissolved in the surrounding medium as saprophytes do.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following diseases is correctly matched with its symptoms and method of transmission?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Chickenpox - runny and stuffy nose - respiratory droplets

options.label: B
options.option_text: Measles - paralysis and hydrophobia - bite from infected animals

options.label: C
options.option_text: Polio - commonly no sign and symptoms - fecal-oral-route
options.explanation: Polio is caused by a virus that spreads through the faecal-oral route, often through contaminated water or food. Most infected people show no signs or symptoms, although some develop paralysis. Chickenpox spreads by droplets, while measles and rabies have different symptoms and transmission.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Rabies - swollen and painful protid glands - through infected saliva

questions.question_text: In order to link a specific microorganism to a specific disease, Koch used mouse as experimental animal. He took a small amount of blood from a diseased mouse and injected into a healthy mouse, the latter quickly developed anthrax. Again he took blood from this second mouse and then injected it into another, again he observed the symptoms of anthrax. What was his first postulate related with this procedure?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The same microorganisms are present in every case of the diseases.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The isolated microorganisms can cause the same disease to susceptible animal.
options.explanation: Koch's third postulate states that the isolated and cultured microorganism must cause the same disease when introduced into a healthy susceptible host. Injecting blood from a diseased mouse into healthy mice that then develop anthrax demonstrates that the microorganism causes the disease.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The same pathogens are isolated and re-cultivated from experimental animal.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The microorganisms are isolated from the tissue of a dead animal and pure culture is prepared.

questions.question_text: Sleeping sickness is transmitted by

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sleeping sickness, or African trypanosomiasis, is caused by the protozoan Trypanosoma and is transmitted to humans by the bite of the tsetse fly. It is not transmitted through sexual contact, contaminated food or respiratory droplets.

questions.question_text: Considering the diverse application of microorganisms, which of the following best evaluates their overall importance? They have

options.label: A
options.option_text: abundant benefits that are essential for life on Earth.
options.explanation: Microorganisms provide abundant benefits that are essential for life on Earth. They recycle nutrients, decompose organic matter, fix nitrogen, produce oxygen, and are widely used in biotechnology for food production, medicine manufacture, waste treatment and genetic engineering, outweighing the diseases a few of them cause.

options.label: B
options.option_text: a great disadvantage and limited advantage.

options.label: D
options.option_text: few applications in the areas of biotechnology and medicine.

questions.question_text: Suppose a clinical nurse used a needle to treat a person with HIV/AIDS. What would be the most appropriate method of controlling such microbial infection?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Incineration is the destruction of contaminated materials by burning at very high temperatures, eliminating all microorganisms. It is the appropriate method for disposing of a needle used on an HIV-positive patient, because such sharp, heavily contaminated waste cannot be safely reused.

questions.question_text: As a clinical microbiologist, suppose you want to collect microbes from a food sample and isolate them via serial dilution. How do you determine the isolated colonies that grow on artificial media?

options.label: A
options.option_text: counting the number of strains on the plate

options.label: B
options.option_text: cross checking with other preserved specimens

options.label: C
options.explanation: After serial dilution and culturing, isolated colonies growing on artificial media can be identified by observing their morphological features. Colony characteristics such as size, shape, colour, margin and texture help the microbiologist recognize and distinguish different microbial species.

options.label: D
options.option_text: inoculating them into other infected animals

questions.question_text: What is the main difference between anabolism and catabolism in cellular metabolic pathways? Anabolism

options.label: A
options.option_text: absorbs energy while catabolism releases energy.
options.explanation: Anabolism and catabolism are the two parts of metabolism. Anabolic reactions build complex molecules from simpler ones and absorb or require energy, while catabolic reactions break down complex molecules into simpler ones and release energy, as in cellular respiration.

options.label: B
options.option_text: is destructive while catabolism is constructive process.

options.label: C
options.option_text: occurs during respiration while catabolism occurs in photosynthesis.

options.label: D
options.option_text: breaks down macromolecules while catabolism buildups them.

questions.question_text: In a hypothetical scenario where photosynthesis ceased to occur on the earth, the long-term consequences on the continuity of life would be

options.label: A
options.option_text: remained unaffected since other sources of energy exist.

options.label: B
options.option_text: collapsed that could lead to mass extinction.
options.explanation: Photosynthesis is the foundation of almost all food chains and produces the oxygen most life depends on. If it ceased, primary producers would disappear, food webs would collapse, atmospheric oxygen would decline, and carbon dioxide would accumulate, causing a cascade of extinctions.

options.label: C
options.option_text: balanced between CO2 and O2 appropriately.

options.label: D
options.option_text: disordered although animal life would flourish.

questions.question_text: What are the roles of grana and stroma in the process of photosynthesis? Grana is a site for

options.label: A
options.option_text: cyclic pathway while stroma is a site for non-cyclic pathway.

options.label: B
options.option_text: photolysis of water while stroma is a site for carbon fixation.
options.explanation: The grana are stacks of thylakoid membranes inside chloroplasts where the light-dependent reactions occur, including photolysis of water, which splits water releasing oxygen. The stroma is the fluid surrounding the grana where the Calvin cycle carries out carbon fixation and sugar synthesis.

options.label: C
options.option_text: generation of sugar while stroma is a site for photolysis of water.

options.label: D
options.option_text: production of NADPH while stroma is a site for chemiosmosis.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following comparisons between cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation is correct? Non-cyclic photophosphorylation

options.label: A
options.option_text: produces ATP, NADPH and O2, but cyclic produces ATP and NADPH.

options.label: B
options.option_text: uses oxygen as the final electron acceptor, but cyclic uses cytochrome b-c1 complex.

options.label: C
options.option_text: uses photosystem I as electron donor, but cyclic uses water as an electron donor.

options.label: D
options.option_text: involves both photosystems I and II, but cyclic uses only photosystem I.
options.explanation: Non-cyclic photophosphorylation involves both photosystem II and photosystem I, producing ATP, NADPH and oxygen, with electrons supplied by water. Cyclic photophosphorylation uses only photosystem I, generating ATP but no NADPH and no oxygen because electrons return to the same system.

questions.question_text: All of the following events happen in the reduction stages of the Calvin cycle EXCEPT

options.label: A
options.explanation: The Calvin cycle has three stages: carbon fixation, reduction and regeneration. In carbon fixation CO2 combines with RuBP, so this event belongs to the fixation stage, not the reduction stage. Reduction uses ATP and NADPH to convert 3-PGA into G3P sugar.

options.label: B
options.option_text: utilization of ATP and NADPH molecules.

options.label: C
options.option_text: conversion of 3-PGA into a sugar molecule.

options.label: D
options.option_text: donating of electrons to a 3C-intermediates to form G3P.

questions.question_text: What happens in the mitochondrion during the reactions of photorespiration?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Glycine is converted to serine with the release of CO2 and NH3.
options.explanation: During photorespiration, two molecules of glycine are transported into the mitochondrion, where they are converted into one molecule of serine, releasing carbon dioxide and ammonia. The other listed reactions occur in chloroplasts or peroxisomes rather than in the mitochondrion.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Glycolate is converted to glyoxylate with the release of H2O2.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Glycerate is converted to GP with the release of ADP.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Phosphoglycolate is converted to glycolate with the release of Pi

questions.question_text: How does photosynthesis ensure the continuity of life? By

options.label: A
options.option_text: constantly adding carbon dioxide to the atmosphere

options.label: B
options.option_text: maintaining carbon dioxide and oxygen balance in the atmosphere
options.explanation: Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and releases oxygen, keeping the two gases in a dynamic balance. This gas balance maintains atmospheric composition suitable for life and sustains food chains, thereby ensuring the continuity of life on Earth.

options.label: C
options.option_text: constantly removing oxygen from the atmosphere

options.label: D
options.option_text: adding natural gas and absorbing methane from the atmosphere

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the difference between substrate level phosphorylation and oxidative phosphorylation? Substrate level phosphorylation

options.label: A
options.option_text: occurs in the inner mitochondrial membrane while oxidative phosphorylation occurs in the cytosol.

options.label: B
options.option_text: occurs during glycolysis and Kreb's cycle while oxidative phosphorylation occurs during electron transport chain.
options.explanation: Substrate-level phosphorylation produces ATP directly when a phosphate group is transferred to ADP during glycolysis and the Krebs cycle. Oxidative phosphorylation generates most ATP during the electron transport chain, where energy from electrons drives proton flow through ATP synthase.

options.label: C
options.option_text: has the same source of energy as oxidative phosphorylation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: occurs in aerobic respiration while oxidative phosphorylation in anaerobic respiration.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about the energy liberation phase of glycolysis pathway? It

options.label: A
options.option_text: hydrolyses two ATP molecules and raises the free energy of glucose.

options.label: B
options.option_text: breaks six carbon molecules into two glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate molecules.

options.label: C
options.option_text: releases one water molecule and dihydroxyacetone phosphate molecule.

options.label: D
options.option_text: produces four ATP, two NADH and two molecules of pyruvate.
options.explanation: The energy liberation phase of glycolysis follows the investment phase. Each glucose molecule is split into two molecules of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate, which are oxidized, producing four ATP, two NADH and ultimately two molecules of pyruvate, giving a net gain of two ATP.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements describes an event of the process of electron transport system correctly?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Oxygen serves as a terminal electron acceptor in the production of ATP.
options.explanation: The electron transport chain transfers electrons from NADH and FADH2 through a series of carrier proteins to oxygen, which acts as the terminal electron acceptor. This movement creates a proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane that powers ATP synthesis.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Thirteen ATP molecules are invested when electrons are transferred from NADH/FADH2 to O2.

options.label: C
options.option_text: More than 90% of the total ATP is produced by substrate-level phosphorylation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It happens due to the difference in pH as the inside mitochondrial membrane is more acidic.

questions.question_text: In a complete oxidation of glucose molecule, how many net ATP molecules are produced by substrate level phosphorylation?

options.label: A
options.explanation: This question is defective because only one option is present and it states ten, which is incorrect. In the complete oxidation of glucose, substrate-level phosphorylation produces a net four ATP: two during glycolysis and two during the Krebs cycle. No valid option was available.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between aerobic and anaerobic respirations?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Aerobic respiration ends with different products while the same product results in anaerobic respiration.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Proteins are the main respiratory substrate for both aerobic and anaerobic respiration.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Aerobic respiration produces much more energy than anaerobic respiration.
options.explanation: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen to completely oxidize glucose through glycolysis, the Krebs cycle and the electron transport chain, producing up to 38 ATP per glucose. Anaerobic respiration lacks oxygen, incompletely oxidizes glucose and yields only two ATP, so aerobic respiration produces much more energy.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Glycolysis is the first pathway for aerobic while Kreb's cycle is for anaerobic respiration.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements disproves spontaneous generation theory based on a step wise experimental work?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Life is an inherent property of the universe and everlasting.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Different life forms on the Earth were created by a supreme being within six days.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Both macro and micro-organisms could arise from pre-existing organisms.
options.explanation: Spontaneous generation claimed that living organisms arise from non-living matter. Experiments by Redi, Spallanzani and Pasteur disproved this, demonstrating that all life arises from pre-existing organisms. This principle, known as biogenesis, was established through controlled experimental work.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Life has reached to the Earth in the form of spores with falling meteorite.

questions.question_text: Based on comparative anatomy, chimpanzee is the closest relative to humans because of the similarities in their

options.label: D
options.explanation: Comparative anatomy compares structural similarities between species. Humans and chimpanzees share a similar pentadactyl limb structure, having the same basic arrangement of bones in their forelimbs. DNA and haemoglobin comparisons belong to molecular biology rather than comparative anatomy.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following causes of variation allows infertile hybrids to become fertile in plant evolution?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Polyploidy involves possessing more than two complete sets of chromosomes. When an infertile hybrid doubles its chromosome number, homologous chromosomes become available to pair during meiosis, restoring fertility and allowing reproduction. This is important in plant evolution and speciation.

questions.question_text: This item is based on the following course of human evolution.1. Use of fire and other tools2. Increase in brain size3. Emergence of Homo sapiens4. Bipedal walking and arboreal lifeWhich of the following is the correct order of the above evolutionary time line markers?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Human evolution progressed from bipedal walking in early hominins, followed by an increase in brain size, then the use of fire and tools by Homo species, and finally the emergence of modern Homo sapiens. This sequence reflects the major milestones of human ancestry.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of genetic mutation?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Mutations are changes in the DNA sequence caused by factors such as ultraviolet radiation, chemical substances and errors during DNA replication. Extensive physical exercise does not damage DNA or cause genetic mutation, making it the correct exception in this question.

questions.question_text: Which genetic phenomenon is common for both bottleneck and founder effects?

options.label: A
options.option_text: High mutation rate that enhances adaptation

options.label: B
options.option_text: Genetic drift that reduces diversity in the population
options.explanation: Both the bottleneck effect and the founder effect are forms of genetic drift, in which random sampling dramatically reduces a population's size and genetic diversity. The surviving or founding individuals represent only a fraction of the original gene pool, so allele frequencies change by chance.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Gene flow that increases inbreed and disease's resistance

options.label: D
options.option_text: Natural selection that results from gradual evolutionary changes

questions.question_text: In a scenario where a male black lion population left its terrestrial territory and joined a white female lion population in an isolated Island to mate, there would be a

options.label: A
options.option_text: decrease in black lion population in the isolated Island.

options.label: B
options.option_text: genetic variation in terrestrial population due to immigration.

options.label: C
options.option_text: random introduction of new alleles into the Island population.
options.explanation: Immigration brings new alleles into a population through gene flow. When the black lion moved to the isolated island and mated with the white lion population, its alleles were randomly introduced into that population, increasing the island population's genetic variation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: change in allele frequencies of terrestrial population but not in Island.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of anthropogenic driving factor that contributes to species extinction?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Anthropogenic factors are caused by human activities. The expansion of agriculture destroys natural habitats, fragments ecosystems and drives many species to extinction. Earthquakes, volcanic eruptions and wildfires are natural drivers, although wildfires may also result from human activity.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct about nervous system? It

options.label: A
options.option_text: takes air into and out of the body to supply oxygen and remove carbon dioxide.

options.label: B
options.option_text: uses blood vessels to transport blood around the body through the heart.

options.label: C
options.option_text: consist of cells that produce and secret chemicals into the blood stream via duct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: receives and processes sensory information from internal and external parts of the body.
options.explanation: The nervous system is composed of the brain, spinal cord and nerves made of neurons. It receives sensory information from internal and external environments, processes and interprets this information, and coordinates responses by sending signals to muscles and glands.

questions.question_text: What is the best justification for the role of voltage-gated ion channels in nerve impulse transmission? They

options.label: A
options.option_text: actively respond to membrane potential changes, leading to depolarization.
options.explanation: Voltage-gated ion channels open and close in response to changes in membrane potential. When a stimulus reaches threshold, sodium channels open, allowing sodium ions to rush in, which causes depolarization and generates an action potential that travels along the axon.

options.label: B
options.option_text: block the ions movement across the membrane to sustain neuron.

options.label: C
options.option_text: allow potassium ions diffuse to the inside of the membrane, forming repolarization.

options.label: D
options.option_text: produce energy when the sodium ions move to the inside of the axon.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following ions are used to facilitate the release of neurotransmitters to the synaptic cleft before binding to postsynaptic receptor?

options.label: A
options.explanation: When an action potential reaches the presynaptic terminal, voltage-gated calcium channels open and calcium ions enter the neuron. This influx triggers the fusion of synaptic vesicles with the membrane, releasing neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft to bind postsynaptic receptors.

questions.question_text: Find the correct pathway of reflex arc that prevents you from physical damage upon the sudden touching of hot plate.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Sensory neuron → motor neuron → spinal cord → effector

options.label: C
options.option_text: Sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → effector
options.explanation: The reflex arc is the neural pathway for a rapid automatic response. Sensory neurons carry the impulse from the receptor to the spinal cord, where interneurons relay it to motor neurons, which then transmit the signal to the effector muscle to withdraw from the hot plate.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Interneuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → effector

questions.question_text: Select the option that contains the correct match of human ear structure and its function.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Eustachian tube - balancing air pressure of the middle ear and throat
options.explanation: The Eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the throat and balances air pressure on both sides of the eardrum. The semicircular canals detect motion and balance, the ear ossicles transmit vibrations, and the cochlea converts sound waves into nerve impulses.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Semicircular canals - concerned with production of nerve impulse

options.label: C
options.option_text: Ear ossicles - concerned with the detection of motion

options.label: D
options.option_text: Cochlea - transmits sound from the incus to the auditory nerve

questions.question_text: This item is based on the following list of events that happen during hearing.I. Transmission of amplified sound waves to the ear ossiclesII. Movement of sensory hair as a result of vibration of the fluid in the cochleaIII. Transmission of nerve impulse into the brain and response to the sound stimulusIV. The pinna directs sound waves into the eardrumBased on the above lists, which alternative shows the correct steps of the events of hearing?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hearing begins when the pinna directs sound waves into the eardrum. The vibrations are transmitted and amplified through the ear ossicles, then travel to the cochlea where they move sensory hairs in the fluid. Finally, nerve impulses are transmitted to the brain for response.

questions.question_text: Suppose low metabolic rate, cretinism and retarded mental and physical development are common problems of infants and childhood in a small village. Which condition in the endocrine system results in these problems?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cretinism, with low metabolic rate and retarded mental and physical development, results from extreme hypothyroidism during infancy and childhood. The thyroid gland fails to produce enough thyroxine, which is essential for normal growth, development and metabolic activity.

questions.question_text: If a woman is admitted to hospital for giving birth, which hormone is helping her in the delivery of her baby and releasing of milk?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Oxytocin is a hormone released by the posterior pituitary gland that stimulates uterine contractions during childbirth, helping the delivery of the baby. It also triggers the release of milk from the mammary glands during breastfeeding through the milk ejection reflex.

questions.question_text: How ultrafiltration takes place in the human kidney? By

options.label: A
options.option_text: increasing the concentration of urine in the muscular sac using a collecting duct

options.label: B
options.option_text: building the pressure of the knot of blood vessels in the Bowman's capsule
options.explanation: Ultrafiltration occurs in the renal corpuscle when the glomerulus, a knot of blood vessels inside Bowman's capsule, maintains high blood pressure. This pressure forces water, salts, glucose and urea through the capillary walls into the capsular space to form filtrate.

options.label: C
options.option_text: diffusing of glucose molecules into the first coiled tubule of microvilli

options.label: D
options.option_text: reabsorbing of water into the blood in the second coiled tubule using ADH

questions.question_text: Assume a patient with type II diabetes gets advice to practice regular exercise to raise the number of insulin receptors. Then, how does insulin regulate the blood glucose level if it is high in this patient? It stimulates

options.label: A
options.option_text: glycolysis, which converts glucose into pyruvate.

options.label: B
options.option_text: glycogenesis, which converts glucose into glycogen.
options.explanation: Insulin lowers high blood glucose by stimulating the uptake of glucose into liver and muscle cells, where it promotes glycogenesis, the conversion of glucose into glycogen for storage. Regular exercise increases insulin receptors, improving the sensitivity of the cells to insulin.

options.label: C
options.option_text: lipolysis that converts fatty acid into glucose.

options.label: D
options.option_text: gluconeogenesis that creates glucose from amino acids.

questions.question_text: Imagine the water content of the blood is low when you take in much salt with your food. What would happen in your kidney to regulate this situation? Osmoreceptor stimulates the

options.label: A
options.option_text: adrenal gland to release adrenalin that increases conversion of glycogen to glucose in the blood.

options.label: B
options.option_text: hypothalamus that release aldosterone and sodium ions to reabsorb back into the blood.

options.label: C
options.option_text: pituitary gland to release ADH to reabsorb water back into the blood.
options.explanation: When blood water content falls, osmoreceptors in the hypothalamus detect the change and signal the posterior pituitary gland to release antidiuretic hormone. ADH makes the collecting ducts more permeable to water, so more water is reabsorbed back into the blood.

options.label: D
options.option_text: ADH to release cortisone that promotes resistance to water stress.

questions.question_text: Several current studies point out that very large quantity of greenhouse gases have been added into Earth's atmosphere due to human activities. What would be the most likely responsible gas and its major sources, respectively?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Methane - aluminum smelting and semiconductor manufacturing

options.label: B
options.option_text: Carbon dioxide - fossil fuel combustion, deforestation, oil and gas usage
options.explanation: Carbon dioxide is the principal greenhouse gas added to the atmosphere by human activities. Its major sources include fossil fuel combustion, deforestation and industrial oil and gas usage. Rising CO2 levels intensify the greenhouse effect and drive global warming and climate change.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Sulphur hexafluoride - landfills, rice paddies, digestive tracts of cattle

options.label: D
options.option_text: Perfluorocarbons - electric transmission, magnesium and aluminum production

questions.question_text: The effect of increased climate change on agricultural productivity is associated with

options.label: A
options.option_text: land use change and expansion of monoculture farming that yields high productivity.

options.label: B
options.option_text: agroforestry system that increases the mixture of multipurpose trees and crops.

options.label: C
options.option_text: drought that triggers wild fire, which can consume millions of acres of forest.

options.label: D
options.option_text: reduction of available water that leads to decrease in biological resources.
options.explanation: Climate change causes shifts in rainfall patterns and increases drought, reducing the availability of water for crops. This leads to decreased agricultural productivity and a decline in biological resources, affecting food production and livelihoods in many farming communities.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following local community practices in Ethiopia is considered as an environmental action that addresses climate change mitigation? Culture of

options.label: A
options.option_text: respecting humanity that promotes eco-tourism industry

options.label: B
options.option_text: negotiating mechanism that is led by elders to reduce social unrest

options.label: C
options.option_text: planting millions of seedlings following the green legacy initiative
options.explanation: The Green Legacy Initiative involves planting millions of tree seedlings across Ethiopia. Trees absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, acting as carbon sinks, so mass tree planting mitigates climate change by reducing greenhouse gas concentrations and restoring degraded land.

options.label: D
options.option_text: treating different diseases with herbal remedies by traditional healers

questions.question_text: Which labeled part is responsible for controlling the diameter of the pupil according to the light source?[IMAGE: img_1.webp]

options.label: C
options.explanation: The iris contains circular and radial muscles that control the diameter of the pupil in response to light intensity, so part IV is the iris. No option was marked correct in the source, so the answer was determined from the structure of the eye.

questions.question_text: Consider the following diagram of pyramid of biomass.[IMAGE: img_2.webp]Which one of the following statements is correct about the above pyramid of biomass?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The whole organisms at first trophic level is eaten by the organisms above.

options.label: B
options.option_text: When organisms in stage II eat the producers, most of the producer's materials are turned into new secondary consumers.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Much of the biomass from stage II is used by stage III to release energy for living.
options.explanation: In a pyramid of biomass, each trophic level contains less biomass than the level below. Much of the biomass at one level is consumed as respiration energy by organisms at the next level, so only a small fraction becomes new biomass at stage III. No option was marked correct in the source.

options.label: D
options.option_text: At each stage of trophic level, the amount of biomass, which is passed on, supports a large

questions.question_text: Consider the following structure of the human heart.[IMAGE: img_3.webp]In the above diagram, which part is used for forcing oxygenated blood out of the heart and around the body?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The left ventricle has the thickest muscular wall and contracts powerfully to force oxygenated blood out of the heart through the aorta and around the body. Part IV is therefore the left ventricle. No option was marked correct in the source, so the answer was determined.

questions.question_text: From the magnitude of the equilibrium constant, Keq one can deduce that

options.label: A
options.option_text: large Keqvalue indicates that the reaction reaches equilibrium with very little reactants remaining.
options.explanation: The magnitude of the equilibrium constant reveals how far a reaction proceeds. A large Keq means products are strongly favoured, so very little reactant remains at equilibrium. Small Keq values favour reactants. Statement A correctly describes this deduction.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Small Keqvalues indicate the reaction yields very higher amounts of products near equilibrium.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Keqwill be larger when we have higher amounts of reactants over products.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Intermediate Keqvalue indicates that the reaction does proceed in the forward direction.

questions.question_text: The statement 'If a system at equilibrium is subjected to a stress, the system will readjust itself to reduce the effects of the stress' is known as

options.label: C
options.explanation: Le Chatelier's principle states that a system at equilibrium, when subjected to a stress, shifts its position to reduce or counteract that stress. Avogadro's principle, Faraday's law, and Boyle's law describe different scientific relationships. Therefore C is the correct name.

questions.question_text: The law of mass action states that

options.label: A
options.option_text: The Keqexpression is the ratio of the concentrations of reactants to the products raised to their coefficients.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The rate of a reaction is directly proportional to the product of the concentration of reactants raised to the power of their respective coefficients in the balanced equation.
options.explanation: The law of mass action states that for a general reaction aA + bB to cC + dD, the reaction rate is directly proportional to the product of the reactant concentrations, each raised to the power of its stoichiometric coefficient in the balanced equation. Option B gives this definition.

options.label: C
options.option_text: For a reaction at equilibrium, the reaction quotient, Q is always less than the equilibrium constant, Keq.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A chemical equilibrium is attained only when the reaction is started with reactants.

questions.question_text: For the reaction between gaseous NO and O2to for NO2(g), what will be the equilibrium constant expression,2NO(g) + O2(g)↔ 2NO2(g)

options.label: B
options.explanation: For the reaction 2NO(g) + O2(g) to 2NO2(g), the equilibrium constant expression is the product of the product concentrations raised to their coefficients divided by the reactant concentrations raised to theirs: Kc = [NO2]^2 / ([NO]^2[O2]). Option B writes this correctly.

questions.question_text: The equilibrium constant Kpfor the reaction 2SO2(g) ⇌ 2SO3(g) + O2(g) is 3.8 × 10-3Kpat 227 °C. What is the value of Kcfor the reaction at the same temperature?

options.label: D
options.explanation: For the decomposition 2SO3 to 2SO2 + O2, delta-n = 1. Kp = 3.8 x 10^-3 kPa = 3.75 x 10^-5 atm. Kc = Kp / RT = 3.75 x 10^-5 / (0.0821 x 500) = 9.1 x 10^-7 mol/L = 9.1 x 10^-4 mol/m3, option D. The printed equation is unbalanced.

questions.question_text: In the Galvanic cell given in the diagram belowIdentify the component parts correctly labelled for the letters a, b, c, d and choose the correct one among the followinga, b, c,andd, respectively

options.label: A
options.option_text: Copper anode, Zinc cathode, voltmeter , salt bridge

options.label: B
options.option_text: Zinc cathode, Copper cathode, Zinc anode, Copper cathode

options.label: C
options.option_text: Copper anode, Zinc anode, CuSO4(sol), voltmeter

options.label: D
options.option_text: Zinc anode, Copper cathode, ZnSO4(sol), salt bridge
options.explanation: In a Daniel cell, zinc is the anode immersed in zinc sulphate solution and copper is the cathode immersed in copper sulphate solution, with a salt bridge connecting the half-cells and a voltmeter in the circuit. Option D labels the parts correctly.

questions.question_text: The conversion of nitrogen gas into useful nitrogen compounds is known as

options.label: D
options.explanation: Nitrogen fixation is the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen gas into nitrogen compounds such as ammonia and nitrates, carried out by bacteria, lightning, and industrial processes. Photosynthesis, respiration, and oxidation do not describe this conversion. Option D.

questions.question_text: CO2is released into the atmosphere by one of the following processes

options.label: A
options.option_text: Animals eat plants and release CO2by photosynthesis

options.label: B
options.option_text: Plants consume atmospheric carbon dioxide during photosynthesis

options.label: C
options.option_text: Utilization of electrical energy as energy sources

options.label: D
options.option_text: Natural fires and volcanoes release CO2into the air
options.explanation: Natural fires and volcanic eruptions release carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. Photosynthesis consumes carbon dioxide, and using electrical energy or eating plants does not release it into the air. Therefore option D correctly identifies a process that releases CO2.

questions.question_text: One of the following isNOTa common application of silicon

options.label: A
options.option_text: in the control of the frequency of television transmissions

options.label: B
options.option_text: in the construction of transistors and microprocessors

options.label: C
options.option_text: in coating iron to prevent it from rusting
options.explanation: Silicon is used in transistors and microprocessors, in quartz frequency control for television transmissions, and in silicone-based polishes for car body parts. Coating iron to prevent rusting is done by galvanising with zinc, not silicon, so C is NOT a silicon application.

options.label: D
options.option_text: in the production of polish body parts cars

questions.question_text: One of the following isNOTamong the chemical properties of silicon

options.label: A
options.option_text: Silica is resistant to attack by all acids except HF, which it reacts to give SiF4and H2O2

options.label: B
options.option_text: Silicon reacts with CH3Cl at 300 °C in the Cu as a catalyst by further reactions with H2O yields the polymer [(CH3)2SiO2]n

options.label: C
options.option_text: Silicon occurs as silica (SiO2) and silicate compounds containing the silicate ion (SiO44-)
options.explanation: Statement C states that silicon occurs as silica and silicate minerals, which describes its occurrence in nature rather than a chemical property. Statements A, B, and D describe actual chemical reactions of silicon and silica. Therefore C is NOT a chemical property.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Silica dissolves in hot molten Na2CO3to give Na4SiO4and CO2

questions.question_text: The branch of chemistry that is involved in separation, identifying and determining the relative amounts of components in a sample of material is known as

options.label: A
options.explanation: Analytical chemistry is the branch concerned with separating, identifying, and determining the relative amounts of components in samples. Biochemistry studies living systems, inorganic chemistry studies non-carbon compounds, and physical chemistry studies energy and physical principles. Option A.

questions.question_text: Significant figures are figures with

options.label: A
options.option_text: measured values with the highest accuracy

options.label: B
options.option_text: measured values with the highest precision

options.label: C
options.option_text: exactly known digits with the last digit uncertain
options.explanation: Significant figures include all digits that are exactly known plus one final digit that is estimated or uncertain. They indicate the precision of a measurement. Option C gives this correct definition, while the other options confuse accuracy, uncertainty, or both.

options.label: D
options.option_text: measured values with the highest uncertainty

questions.question_text: For the determination of the density of a new ceramic, a student measured the mass of a piece on an analytical balance and obtained 3.8056 gram and its volume 2.5 mL by displacement of water in a graduated cylinder. The correct reported density of the ceramic should be

options.label: D
options.explanation: Density equals mass divided by volume: 3.8056 g / 2.5 mL = 1.5222 g/mL. The volume measurement has only two significant figures, which limits the answer, so the density must be reported as 1.5 g/mL with two significant figures. Option D.

questions.question_text: The scientific method is

options.label: A
options.option_text: a method of arriving at an organized body of knowledge based on reproducible experiments and observations
options.explanation: The scientific method is a systematic process for building organised, testable knowledge through reproducible experiments and observations. It is not a collection of guesses, an accidental discovery, or a fixed global set of rules. Option A correctly defines it.

options.label: B
options.option_text: a collection of scientific guesses and hypotheses by seeking patterns in the observations

options.label: C
options.option_text: the result of fortunate, accidental discovery in the development of science

options.label: D
options.option_text: the sum total of unique guidelines for the practice of science in the world

questions.question_text: One of the following isNOTa cause of uncertainty in measurement?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Measurement uncertainty is mainly caused by the observer, the measuring device, and environmental conditions. The type of material being measured does not itself create experimental uncertainty, making B the answer. Some textbooks, however, include sample properties as a contributing factor, so this item is arguable.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The environment where the measurement is made

questions.question_text: Hydrogen bonding occurs in compounds that contain H-N, H-O and H-F bonds. These bonds are stronger than the ordinary dipole-dipole interactions because

options.label: A
options.option_text: the H-N, H-O and H-F bonds are less polar than ordinary covalent bonds

options.label: B
options.option_text: the partially positive H of one molecule is attracted to the partially negative lone pairs on the N, O or F of another molecule
options.explanation: Hydrogen bonding occurs when the partially positive hydrogen atom of one molecule is attracted to the lone-pair electrons of a highly electronegative nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine atom in another molecule. This interaction is stronger than ordinary dipole-dipole attractions. Option B explains the cause.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the H-N, H-O and H-F bonds are non-polar and thus do not interact with neighboring molecules

options.label: D
options.option_text: the small sizes of N, O and F makes these atoms so electropositive that their covalently bonded H is highly negative

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of exception to the octet rule?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Phosphorus pentachloride, PCl5, has ten electrons around the central phosphorus atom, an expanded octet, so it is an exception to the octet rule. Carbon tetrachloride, ammonia, and water all obey the octet rule with eight valence electrons. Option C.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pair is true about the general properties of the different types of crystalline solidsType of solidHardnessMelting pointConduction of heat and electricityI. IonicHardHighGoodII. CovalentHardHighPoorIII. MolecularSoftLowGoodIV. MetallicSoft to hardLow to highGood

options.label: C
options.explanation: Statement II, covalent network solids being hard, high-melting, and poor conductors, is true, and statement IV for metallic solids is also true. However, no option combines II and IV. The key intends I and IV, treating ionic and metallic solids as good conductors. Question defective.

questions.question_text: When the boiling point of hydrides of group VIA elements, H2O, H2S, H2Se and H2Te are arranged in the order of increasing boiling point. The trend is H2Te< H2Se< H2S< H2O, water having the highest boiling point, this is due to

options.label: A
options.option_text: the basic different structures of each hydride

options.label: B
options.option_text: the small size of O compared to the other group VIA elements

options.label: C
options.option_text: hydrogen bonding present in H2O molecules
options.explanation: Water has the highest boiling point among the group VIA hydrides because water molecules form strong hydrogen bonds, which are far stronger than the weak intermolecular forces in H2S, H2Se, and H2Te. Option C correctly identifies hydrogen bonding as the cause.

options.label: D
options.option_text: increasing boiling points with increasing molecular mass

questions.question_text: Given the following catalyzed reactions2SO2(s) + O2(g) → 2SO3(g); V2O5(s) as a catalystOCl (aq) + I-(aq) → Ol-(aq) + Cl (aq); OH-(aq) as inhibitorCO (s) + H2(g) → CH4(g) + H2O (g); Ni (s) as a catalystCO (s) + H2(g) → HCHO (g); Cu (s) as a catalystWhich reaction(s) is/ are examples for homogeneous catalysis?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Homogeneous catalysis occurs when the catalyst is in the same phase as the reactants. Reaction II involves all aqueous species and a dissolved inhibitor, so it is homogeneous. Reactions I, III, and IV use solid catalysts and are heterogeneous. Only II qualifies; no single-option answer exists, so B is retained.
