questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a common reaction of tin?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Tin reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce tin(II) chloride and hydrogen gas, as shown by Sn (s) + 2HCl (aq) → SnCl2 (aq) + H2 (g). The other options describe reactions that do not occur readily: tin is not attacked by steam at ordinary temperatures, and cold chlorine produces SnCl4, not SnCl2.

questions.question_text: The monomer of natural rubber is

options.label: A
options.explanation: Natural rubber is a polymer of isoprene, chemically 2-methyl-1,3-butadiene, CH2=C(CH3)-CH=CH2. Polymerizing this conjugated diene monomer through addition of its double bonds yields polyisoprene. Chloroprene is the monomer of neoprene, and plain 1,3-butadiene gives synthetic polybutadiene rubber, not natural rubber.

questions.question_text: A chemistry teacher has added different reactants and reagents in three different test tubes as described below:I. Into the test tube A, he added ethanol, sodium dichromate, sulphuric acid.II. Into the test tube B, he added acetaldehyde, sodium borohydride and water.III. Into the tube C, he added methyl acetate and ethanol and sodium hydroxide. In which test tube would a reaction take place that provide acetic acid?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Test tube I produces acetic acid because acidified sodium dichromate oxidizes ethanol to ethanoic acid. Tube II gives ethanol since sodium borohydride reduces acetaldehyde, and tube III undergoes transesterification of methyl acetate to ethyl acetate. Because the only fully correct test tube, I alone, is not offered, the option containing I is selected.

questions.question_text: All of the following are examples of addition polymersEXCEPT

options.label: A
options.explanation: All three structures listed are addition polymers: polyvinyl chloride, polyethylene, and an ethylene-propylene copolymer are all formed by addition polymerization of alkene monomers. The question asks for an exception, but no condensation polymer is present, making it defective. Polyvinyl chloride is selected as the representative answer since it is the first listed.

questions.question_text: One of the following examples of polymers is correctly matched with its uses

options.label: B
options.explanation: Polyethylene, being an inert, non-toxic thermoplastic, is widely used to manufacture food containers, bottles and plastic bags. Polypropylene is not used for electrical insulation (PVC is), and polytetrafluoroethylene is used for non-stick coatings, not shoes. Polyvinyl chloride for pipes is also correct, so B is the cleaner match.

questions.question_text: Natural polymers are

options.label: A
options.option_text: polymers produced by condensation reaction of monomer units

options.label: B
options.option_text: polymers produced by the addition reaction of monomer units.

options.label: C
options.option_text: polymers produced by the substitution of one or more atoms in the monomer units.

options.label: D
options.option_text: polymers found in some substances like rubber in nature.
options.explanation: Natural polymers are macromolecules that occur in nature, such as rubber, cellulose, starch and proteins, rather than being synthesized industrially. They are not defined by the reaction type used to make them; condensation and addition both produce polymers. The definition focusing on naturally occurring substances like rubber is therefore correct.

questions.question_text: Oils are unsaturated fatty acids. The process of converting oils to solid fats involves

options.label: C
options.option_text: halogenations of the C-C double bonds.

options.label: D
options.option_text: hydrogenation of the C-C double bonds.
options.explanation: Oils are unsaturated fatty acid triglycerides containing carbon-carbon double bonds. Converting liquid oils into solid fats is achieved by hydrogenation, adding hydrogen across the C=C double bonds to produce saturated fats such as margarine. Saponification forms soaps, esterification forms esters, and halogenation adds halogens rather than saturating the oil.

questions.question_text: The difference between colloids and suspension is that

options.label: A
options.option_text: most colloids and suspensions appear cloudy.

options.label: B
options.option_text: colloidal particles are small enough and do not settle down unlike in a suspension.
options.explanation: The key distinction is that colloidal particles are small enough to remain dispersed and do not settle, whereas suspension particles are large and settle under gravity. Both colloids and suspensions may appear cloudy, and both are heterogeneous mixtures, so those statements describe similarities rather than differences between the two.

options.label: C
options.option_text: colloids are as transparent as solutions.

options.label: D
options.option_text: both colloids and suspensions are heterogeneous mixtures.

questions.question_text: The solubility of a substance is the amount of a substance that

options.label: A
options.option_text: dissolves more amount of solute than it can normally dissolve.

options.label: B
options.option_text: gives an unsaturated solution of substance at given temperature.

options.label: C
options.option_text: dissolves double the amount of solute than it can normally dissolve.

options.label: D
options.option_text: gives a saturated solution of the substance at a given temperature.
options.explanation: Solubility is defined as the maximum amount of solute that will dissolve in a given amount of solvent at a specified temperature, producing a saturated solution. It represents the quantity that gives a saturated solution at a given temperature. Unsaturated solutions dissolve less solute, so the saturated-solution definition is the correct one.

questions.question_text: A reflex arc is the neural pathway that controls an involuntary response to a stimulus. Which of the following is the correct order of components in a reflex arc?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Motor neuron → Receptor → Interneuron → Sensory neuron → Effector
options.explanation: Option A is the receptor comes first, and the sensory neuron is before the motor neuron.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Receptor → Sensory neuron → Interneuron → Motor neuron → Effector
options.explanation: This is the correct order of a reflex arc.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Receptor → Motor neuron → Interneuron → Sensory neuron → Effector
options.explanation: Option C is the sensory neuron is after the receptor, not the motor neuron.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Effector → Sensory neuron → Interneuron → Motor neuron → Receptor
options.explanation: Option D is the receptor starts the reflex arc, not the effector.

questions.question_text: 50 mL of the supernatant saturated solution of NaCl was taken in an evaporating dish (weight=w₀) and evaporated over a Bunsen burner until all the water has evaporated and dry sodium chloride is left in the evaporating dish. The evaporating dish with the dry sodium chloride is weighed (weight=w₁). Given the following information, w₀=47.5 g and w₁=66.2. Calculate the solubility of NaCl in water assuming 50 mL of the solution is equal to 50 mL of the solvent

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mass of sodium chloride deposited equals w1 - w0 = 66.2 g - 47.5 g = 18.7 g. This dissolves in 50 mL (50 g) of water. Scaling to 100 g of water gives 18.7 × (100/50) = 37.4 g. Therefore the solubility of NaCl is 37.4 g per 100 g of water at that temperature.

questions.question_text: One of the following given pairs represents examples of buffer systems

options.label: C
options.explanation: A buffer is a solution containing a weak acid and its conjugate base, or a weak base and its conjugate acid. NH4OH/NH4Cl is a weak base with its salt, and CH3COOH/CH3COONa is a weak acid with its salt, both resisting pH change. Strong acid/strong base mixtures do not form buffers.

questions.question_text: The reaction between a weak acid and strong base as represented by the reaction between acetic acid and NaOH gives a basic solution because

options.label: A
options.option_text: CH₃OO⁻ as a strong base picks up H+ and causes excess OH⁻ ions.
options.explanation: The solution is basic because the conjugate base CH3COO- hydrolyzes in water, accepting protons and leaving an excess of hydroxide ions. Though acetate is a weak base, not a strong one, its proton pickup is the correct explanation. The statement identifying acetate's hydrolysis as the cause of excess OH- ions is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Na+ is a strong acid and causes high concentration of H+.

options.label: C
options.option_text: CH₃COOH does not produce sufficient amount of H+ ions.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The OH⁻ ions from NaOH are not completely neutralized.

questions.question_text: An acid is a substance that

options.label: A
options.option_text: produces more OH ions in water than H+ ions.

options.label: C
options.option_text: donates a pair of electrons to a chemical species.

options.label: D
options.option_text: donates a proton in a chemical reaction.
options.explanation: According to the Brønsted-Lowry definition, an acid is a substance that donates a proton (H+) in a chemical reaction. Producing more OH- than H+, tasting bitter, and donating an electron pair are properties of bases or of Lewis definitions, respectively, so they do not describe an acid correctly.

questions.question_text: One of the following given mass of acids constitutes the corresponding equivalent of the acid

options.label: B
options.explanation: The equivalent mass of an acid is its molar mass divided by the number of replaceable hydrogen ions. For H2SO4, molar mass is 98 g and it supplies two H+, so its equivalent mass is 49 g. Therefore 98 g of H2SO4 constitutes 2 equivalents. HCl gives one equivalent per 36.5 g, and H3PO4 gives three equivalents per 98 g.

questions.question_text: One of the following pairs shows Brønsted-Lowry acids behavior in water?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Both HCl and NH4+ can donate protons, making them Brønsted-Lowry acids. H3O+ is an acid but NH3 is a base, HNO3 is an acid while NO3- is its conjugate base, and HPO42- is amphiprotic while PO43- is a base. Only the pair containing two proton donors qualifies.

questions.question_text: Covalent compounds are liquids or gases at room temperature and have statements low melting and boiling points. Which of the following statements explains these properties of covalent compounds?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The unit of particles in covalent compounds are ions.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The intermolecular forces of attraction in covalent compounds are strong.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Covalent compounds exist as separate molecules.
options.explanation: Covalent compounds exist as discrete molecules held together by weak intermolecular forces, which require little energy to overcome, giving low melting and boiling points. They are not ionic particles, the intermolecular forces are weak rather than strong, and weak forces do exist between molecules.

options.label: D
options.option_text: There are no forces of attraction between the molecules in covalent compounds.

questions.question_text: Both carbonyl sulphide, COS (SCO), S=C=O and carbon dioxide (CO2) O=C=O are linear molecules. COS is polar whereas CO2is non-polar. This is because

options.label: A
options.option_text: the C=O bonds in both COS and CO2 are polar.

options.label: B
options.option_text: CO2 has a net dipole moment of zero.
options.explanation: Carbon dioxide is linear and its two C=O dipoles point in opposite directions, canceling to give a net dipole moment of zero, making it nonpolar. Carbonyl sulphide is linear but the C=O and C=S bonds differ in polarity, so their dipoles do not cancel and COS remains polar.

options.label: C
options.option_text: sulphur is more electronegative than oxygen.

options.label: D
options.option_text: regions of high negative charge is distributed equally around the central atom in COS.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true about the formation of CH4 according to valence bond theory?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The 2s and three 2p orbitals in carbon hybridize to form four sp³ orbitals.
options.explanation: In methane, carbon's 2s orbital and its three 2p orbitals hybridize to form four equivalent sp3 orbitals, each overlapping with a hydrogen 1s orbital to form a sigma bond. The description matching this sp3 hybridization is the correct statement according to valence bond theory.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The 2s and two 2p orbitals in carbon hybridize to form three sp² orbitals.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Carbon can form two hybrid orbitals as it has got only two half-filled orbitals.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The 2s and one 2p orbitals in carbon hybridize to form two sp orbitals.

questions.question_text: Phosphorus (Z=15) has the electronic configuration 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p³, what kind of hybridization does phosphorus undergo in the formation of phosphorus pentachloride (PCl5)?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Phosphorus in PCl5 undergoes sp3d hybridization. The central phosphorus atom promotes one 3s electron to the 3d level, then mixes one 3s, three 3p and one 3d orbital to form five sp3d hybrid orbitals, which overlap with chlorine orbitals to give the trigonal bipyramidal shape.

questions.question_text: One of the following reactions illustrates the formation of coordinate covalent bond?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The reaction NH3 + HCl → NH4+ + Cl- illustrates coordinate covalent bond formation. Nitrogen donates its lone pair of electrons to the proton to form the N-H bond in the ammonium ion. The other reactions form ionic bonds (NaCl) or involve typical covalent bonds without lone-pair donation to a proton.

questions.question_text: In the production of NH3 by the Haber process according to the equation N2(g)+3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g) ΔH=-92KJ mol-1 What are the favorable conditions for the production of high yield of NH3?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The Haber process is exothermic and decreases in gas moles (4 moles to 2 moles). According to Le Chatelier's principle, high pressure shifts equilibrium toward fewer gas molecules, favoring NH3, and low temperature favors the exothermic forward reaction, giving a higher yield. Industrial plants compromise on temperature for speed.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements describes laboratory and industrial preparation of acetic respectively?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Reduction of ethanol by NaBH4 and fermentation of propanol.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Reduction of toluene by KMnO4 and reduction of ethanol by sodium dichromate.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The oxidation of ethanol by sodium dichromate and fermentation of ethanol.
options.explanation: Acetic acid is prepared in the laboratory by oxidizing ethanol with acidified sodium dichromate. Industrially, it is produced by fermentation of ethanol using Acetobacter bacteria. The other options describe reductions, incorrect oxidants, or fermentation of propanol, which are not correct laboratory and industrial preparations.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Oxidation of toluene by KMnO4 and fermentation of ethanol.

questions.question_text: One of the following reactions illustrates the formation of coordinate covalent bond?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The reaction NH3 + HCl → NH4+ + Cl- illustrates coordinate covalent bond formation. Nitrogen donates its lone pair of electrons to the proton to form the N-H bond in the ammonium ion. The other reactions form ionic bonds or involve ordinary covalent bonds without lone-pair donation to a proton.

questions.question_text: In the production of NH3 by the Haber process according to the equationN2(g)+3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g) ΔH=-92KJ mol-1What are the favorable conditions for the production of high yield of NH3?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The Haber process is exothermic and reduces gas moles from four to two. Le Chatelier's principle predicts that high pressure favors the forward reaction forming fewer gas molecules, while low temperature favors the exothermic production of ammonia. Both conditions together maximize the equilibrium yield of NH3.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements describes laboratory and industrial preparation of acetic respectively?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Reduction of ethanol by NaBH4 and fermentation of propanol.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Reduction of toluene by KMnO4 and reduction of ethanol by sodium dichromate.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The oxidation of ethanol by sodium dichromate and fermentation of ethanol.
options.explanation: Acetic acid is prepared in the laboratory by oxidizing ethanol with acidified sodium dichromate. Industrially, it is produced by fermentation of ethanol using Acetobacter bacteria. The other options describe reductions, incorrect oxidants, or fermentation of propanol, which are not correct laboratory and industrial preparations.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Oxidation of toluene by KMnO4 and fermentation of ethanol.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about carboxylic acids?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Methanoic, Ethanoic and Citric acids are monocarboxylic acids.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Carboxylic acid with the formation RCOOH.
options.explanation: Carboxylic acids have the general formula RCOOH, where R is an alkyl group. Methanoic and ethanoic acids are monocarboxylic but citric acid is tricarboxylic, propanedioic acid is not the simplest dicarboxylic acid (oxalic acid is), so only the general formula statement is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Citric acid is a typical dicarboxylic acid.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Propanedioic acid is the simplest dicarboxylic acid.

questions.question_text: What is the IUPAC name for the branched carboxylic acid: CH3-CH(Cl)-CH(CH3)-CH(CH3)-COOH

options.label: D
options.explanation: Number the chain from the carboxyl carbon: C1 is COOH, C2 carries a methyl, C3 carries a methyl, and C4 carries the chlorine substituent. The IUPAC name is therefore 4-chloro-2,3-dimethylpentanoic acid. Option D matches this structure, apart from the redundant locant for the acid group.

questions.question_text: Esters are characterized by the following propertiesEXCEPT

options.label: A
options.option_text: esters have lower boiling point compared to the carboxylic acid alcohols

options.label: B
options.option_text: esters have pleasant odors of perfumes and food flavoring

options.label: C
options.option_text: esters have higher boiling point than carboxylic acid and alcohol
options.explanation: Esters have lower boiling points than the corresponding carboxylic acids and alcohols of similar molar mass because esters lack hydrogen bonding. They do have pleasant fruity odors, are used as flavorings, and are soluble in organic solvents. The claim that esters have higher boiling points is the exception.

options.label: D
options.option_text: all esters are soluble in inorganic solvents and organic

questions.question_text: The sanitizer in wide use for protection against Covid-19 is labelled 83% alcohol. How can one scientifically check the concentration?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The concentration of alcohol in a hand sanitizer can be verified by experimentation, which means carrying out a controlled test, such as measuring density or using a hydrometer, to determine the actual concentration. Hypothesis formation, observation and data collection are steps that support, but do not directly test, the labeled claim.

questions.question_text: The correct electronic configuration for chromium (Cr, Z=24) is

options.label: C
options.explanation: Chromium (Z=24) is an exception to the normal filling order because a half-filled 3d subshell is especially stable, giving [Ar]4s1 3d5. None of the options shows this correct configuration. Option C contains 24 electrons with the standard [Ar]4s2 3d4 arrangement, so it is selected though it violates Hund's rule.

questions.question_text: According to Hund's rule equal energy (degenerate) orbitals are filled with

options.label: A
options.option_text: maximum number of unpaired electrons with parallel spins
options.explanation: Hund's rule states that degenerate orbitals of equal energy are each occupied by one electron of the same (parallel) spin before any orbital receives a second electron. This maximizes the number of unpaired electrons with parallel spins, which is the correct statement of the rule.

options.label: B
options.option_text: two electrons of opposite spins placed in the first orbitals

options.label: C
options.option_text: maximum number of unpaired electrons with opposite spins

options.label: D
options.option_text: two electrons of parallel spins placed in the first orbital

questions.question_text: In the modern periodic table

options.label: A
options.option_text: elements with similar properties are placed in the same period

options.label: B
options.option_text: non-metals are placed on the right side of the periodic table
options.explanation: In the modern periodic table, non-metals are located on the right-hand side, with metals on the left and metalloids along the dividing staircase. Elements with similar properties are placed in the same group, not period, and transition and inner-transition elements occupy the middle and separated bottom rows.

options.label: C
options.option_text: transition and inner-transition elements are placed in the middle of the periodic table

options.label: D
options.option_text: metals are placed on the right hand side of the periodic table

questions.question_text: The electrolysis of liquid (molten) NaCl in the set-up for the electrochemical cell is given in the following figure below.Which of the following statements is true about the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Na is oxidized at the anode

options.label: C
options.option_text: O2is produced at the anode due to the oxidation of water

options.label: D
options.option_text: The net reaction produces Cl2at the anode and Na at the cathode.
options.explanation: During electrolysis of molten sodium chloride, chloride ions are oxidized at the anode to produce chlorine gas, and sodium ions are reduced at the cathode to deposit sodium metal. The net reaction therefore produces Cl2 at the anode and Na at the cathode, which is the correct statement.

questions.question_text: In the reaction mixture of two species NH4OH and NH4Cl, which one of the following is true about the reaction mixture?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The presence of NH4+ion suppresses the dissociation of the weak based NH4OH.
options.explanation: In a mixture of NH4OH and NH4Cl, the common ion NH4+ from the salt suppresses the dissociation of the weak base NH4OH, shifting equilibrium toward undissociated NH4OH. This common-ion effect reduces OH- concentration, so the mixture acts as a basic buffer rather than becoming more basic.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The NH4+ion is a spectator ion in the reaction mixture.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The reaction equilibrium is shifted towards the right due to the presence of NH4+ions.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The presence of NH4+in the reaction mixture makes the solution more basic.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about Kwat different temperature? The ionic product of water KwequalsKw=1.0x10-14at 25 °CKw=2.92x10-14at 40 °C√Kw=1x10-7√Kw=1x10-7

options.label: A
options.option_text: At 40oC pure water is no more neutral

options.label: B
options.option_text: Water dissociates to a higher extent at 40oC than at 25oC.
options.explanation: The ionic product of water Kw increases from 1.0×10^-14 at 25°C to 2.92×10^-14 at 40°C, meaning water dissociates to a greater extent at higher temperature. Although both ion concentrations increase equally, water remains neutral since [H+] still equals [OH-].

options.label: C
options.option_text: Hydroxyl ion concentration is higher at 40othan hydrogen ion concentration

options.label: D
options.option_text: Hydrogen ion concentration at 25oC is higher than at 40oC.

questions.question_text: What is reduction? Reduction is

options.label: A
options.option_text: loss of electrons and decrease in oxidation number

options.label: B
options.option_text: gain of electrons and increase in oxidation number

options.label: C
options.option_text: gain of electrons and no change in oxidation number

options.label: D
options.option_text: gain of electrons and decrease in oxidation number
options.explanation: Reduction is the gain of electrons by a species, accompanied by a decrease in its oxidation number. Gain of electrons always lowers oxidation state, since oxidation numbers reflect the loss or gain of electrons. Any answer linking gain of electrons to an increased oxidation number is incorrect.

questions.question_text: During the electrolysis of dilute aqueous sulphuric acid, the ions present in solution are H+, OH-and SO42-. Which ions are preferentially discharged at the cathode and anode, respectively?

options.label: C
options.explanation: In dilute sulphuric acid, at the anode water is oxidized to oxygen: 2H2O → O2 + 4H+ + 4e-, because SO42- is not discharged. At the cathode, H+ is preferentially reduced: 2H+ + 2e- → H2. This pairing matches option C exactly.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is NOT correct about electrodes and electrochemical cells?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The overall cell potential is calculated by the formula E°cell=ECathode− EAnode

options.label: B
options.option_text: Electrons flow spontaneously from negative to positive electrodes

options.label: C
options.option_text: The difference in the electrical potential of the electrode is positive that is positive cell

options.label: D
options.option_text: E°cellis greater than zero for non-spontaneous process
options.explanation: For a spontaneous electrochemical process, the cell potential E°cell is greater than zero. Therefore the statement that E°cell is greater than zero for a non-spontaneous process is incorrect. The other statements about the cell potential formula, electron flow and positive cell potential are all correct.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following isNOTcorrect about electrodes and electrochemical cells?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The overall cell potential is calculated by the formula E°cell=E°cathode- E°anode

options.label: B
options.option_text: Electrons flow spontaneously from negative to positive electrodes.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The difference in the electrical potential of the electrode is positive that is positive cell.

options.label: D
options.option_text: E°cellis greater than zero for non-spontaneous process.
options.explanation: For a spontaneous electrochemical process, the cell potential E°cell is greater than zero. Therefore the statement that E°cell is greater than zero for a non-spontaneous process is incorrect. The other statements about the cell potential formula, electron flow and positive cell potential are all correct.

questions.question_text: The "like dissolves like" rule accounts for one of the following observation

options.label: B
options.explanation: The like-dissolves-like rule states that nonpolar substances dissolve in nonpolar solvents and polar substances dissolve in polar solvents. Benzene and carbon tetrachloride are both nonpolar, so benzene dissolves readily in CCl4. The other examples describe nonpolar solutes in polar solvents, which do not dissolve well.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The solubility of KBr in C7H8.

questions.question_text: Which of the following concentration units is correctly defined?

options.label: A
options.option_text: ppm (parts per million) = (mass of solute/ mass of solvent) x 106

options.label: B
options.option_text: mass percentage= mass of solute x 100
options.explanation: Mass percentage is defined as the mass of solute divided by the mass of solution, multiplied by 100. Options B and C are identical and both omit the division, but B represents the intended correct definition of mass percentage. Parts per million uses mass of solution, not solvent, and ppb uses a factor of 10^9.

options.label: C
options.option_text: mass percentage= mass of solute x 100

options.label: D
options.option_text: ppb (parts per billion)= (mass of solute/mass of solution) x 106

questions.question_text: The concentrated sulphuric acid H2SO4we use in the laboratory is 98% H2SO4by mass and has a density of 1.83 g/mL. Below are given the concentrations of the acid in various units, which of the given alternatives correctly describes the concentration of the acid?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Molarity 36.6 M, Normality 18.3 N, Mole fraction 0.1

options.label: B
options.option_text: Molarity 18.3 M, Normality 36.6 N, Mole fraction 0.9
options.explanation: Take 100 g of solution: it contains 98 g H2SO4 and 2 g water. Volume is 100/1.83 = 54.6 mL. Moles of H2SO4 = 98/98 = 1, so molarity = 1/0.0546 = 18.3 M. Normality = 2 × 18.3 = 36.6 N. Mole fraction = 1/(1 + 2/18) = 0.9. Option B matches all three values.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Molarity 1.83 M, Normality 3.66 N, Mole fraction 0.9

options.label: D
options.option_text: Molarity 18.3 M, Normality 3.66 N, Mole fraction 0.9

questions.question_text: How do you prepare 500mL of 1N Ca(OH)2solution?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By dissolving 74 g of Ca(OH)2in 500 mL of solution.

options.label: B
options.option_text: By dissolving 37 g of Ca(OH)2in 1 liter of solution.

options.label: C
options.option_text: By dissolving 37 g of Ca(OH)2in 500 mL of solution.
options.explanation: Calcium hydroxide has molar mass 74 g and supplies two OH- ions, giving an equivalent mass of 37 g. To prepare a 1 N solution, 37 g of Ca(OH)2 is dissolved and made up to 500 mL of solution. This gives the required 1 N concentration, matching option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: By dissolving 74 g of Ca(OH)2in 1 liter of solution.

questions.question_text: The Kaof acetic acid CH3COOH is 1.8 x 10-5. What is the percent ionization of 1M of CH3COOH?

options.label: C
options.explanation: For a weak acid, percent ionization equals (sqrt(Ka/C)) × 100. With Ka = 1.8×10^-5 and C = 1 M, sqrt(Ka) = 4.24×10^-3, giving 0.42 percent. None of the options matches this exact value; option C (4.2) is the closest and is selected as the intended answer.

questions.question_text: The mathematical expressions for Faraday's first law is summarized as

options.label: A
options.explanation: Faraday's first law states that the mass of substance deposited is proportional to the quantity of electricity passed, expressed as m = MIt/nF, where M is molar mass, I is current, t is time, n is electron change and F is the Faraday constant. Option A is closest to this standard expression.

questions.question_text: In the electrolysis of copper sulphate solution using graphite electrodes, O2is liberated at the anode and copper metal is deposited at the cathode. If the electrolysis of CuSO4is performed using copper electrode, what happens at the anode and cathode?

options.label: A
options.option_text: At the anode H2is liberated, whereas copper is deposited at the cathode.

options.label: B
options.option_text: At the anode the copper electrode dissolves and copper metal is deposited at the cathode.
options.explanation: With copper electrodes, the anode is the active electrode: copper oxidizes and dissolves into solution as Cu2+, while Cu2+ in solution is reduced and deposited as copper metal on the cathode. This is the principle of electrorefining, so no gas is liberated and copper simply transfers from anode to cathode.

options.label: C
options.option_text: No electrochemical reaction takes place involving copper.

options.label: D
options.option_text: At the anode copper is reduced, whereas copper is oxidized at the cathode.

questions.question_text: The statement 'the amount of a substance consumed or of produced in an electrolytic cell is directly proportional to the amount of electricity that passes through the cell' is known as

options.label: D
options.explanation: Faraday's law states that the amount of substance produced or consumed at an electrode is directly proportional to the quantity of electricity (charge) passing through the cell. Raoult's, Dalton's and Henry's laws concern vapour pressure, partial pressures and gas solubility respectively, not electrolytic deposition.

questions.question_text: Given the following electromotive series of selected metals with their standard reduction potentialsWhich of the following statements is correct about reactivity of the metals?

options.label: A
options.option_text: K is the strongest reduction agent among the metal silver.
options.explanation: Potassium has the most negative standard reduction potential, making it the strongest reducing agent; it is most easily oxidized. Copper is a weaker reducing agent, lead is less easily oxidized than aluminium, and the reaction Cu + Zn2+ is non-spontaneous because zinc is the stronger reducing agent.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Cu is the strongest reducing agent in the group.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Pb is more easily oxidized than Al.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The reaction Cu + Zn2+⇌ Cu2++ Zn is spontaneous.

questions.question_text: One of the following is NOT true about the effects of corrosion?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It causes enormous damage to buildings, bridges, ships and cars.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It causes deterioration of metals by spontaneous chemical process.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Corrosion forms protection oxide layers to prevent damage.
options.explanation: Corrosion is a destructive process that deteriorates metals, causing enormous damage to buildings, bridges, ships and cars, and costing billions of dollars annually. While certain metals form protective oxide layers, that is passivation and is not an effect of corrosion damage, so it is the incorrect statement.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Damage from corrosion costs billions of dollars annually.

questions.question_text: Which statement is true about catalysts?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A positive catalyst decreases the rate of a reaction by increasing the activation energy.

options.label: B
options.option_text: A catalyst slows down or speeds up a reaction, itself being consumed.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The role of a catalyst is to increase or decrease the rate of a reaction by lowering or increasing the activation energy.
options.explanation: A catalyst increases or decreases the rate of a reaction by lowering or raising the activation energy, respectively, and is not consumed in the process. Positive catalysts lower activation energy to speed reactions, while negative catalysts raise it to slow them. Catalysts do not change the equilibrium position.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A negative catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by decreasing the value of activation energy.

questions.question_text: According to the transition state theory

options.label: A
options.option_text: in the activated complex, the original bonds are weakened and the new bonds are partially formed.
options.explanation: According to transition state theory, reacting species collide and form an activated complex in which original bonds are weakened and new bonds are partially formed. This complex lies at a higher energy than both reactants and products, and the activation energy is the energy needed to reach it.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the collision between two reacting species results in the formation of an activated complex, which has less energy than both the reactants and products.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the standard reaction enthalpy (ΔH°) depends on the magnitude of the activation energy (Ea).

options.label: D
options.option_text: the activation energy is the energy that must be absorbed or released by reactants to reach the activated complex.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the rate reactant?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The value of a rate constant tells us how fast or slow a reaction is.
options.explanation: The rate constant k measures how fast a reaction proceeds: a large k indicates a fast reaction and a small k a slow one, for given concentrations. It depends on temperature and activation energy, not on reactant volumes, and the rate expression relates rate to concentrations of reactants.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It expresses the relationship between the rate of a chemical reaction and the volume of reacting species.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A small rate constant indicates a faster reaction and a larger rate indicates a slower reaction.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The value of a rate constant is independent of reaction conditions.

questions.question_text: The mathematical expression log k=(-Ea/2.303R)1/T + log A derived from the Arrhenius equation is of important as it shows

options.label: A
options.option_text: for a given value of activation energy the value of the rate constant increases as the temperature increases.
options.explanation: The Arrhenius equation in linear form, log k = (-Ea/2.303R)(1/T) + log A, shows that for a given activation energy, the rate constant k increases as temperature T increases. Larger activation energies give smaller k and slower reactions at the same temperature.

options.label: B
options.option_text: reactions with larger activation energies have higher values of k and are therefore faster.

options.label: C
options.option_text: for a given value of activation energy, the value of the rate constant decreases as the temperature increases.

options.label: D
options.option_text: reactions with larger activation energies, the value of the rate constant decreases as the temperature increases.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about isotopes? Isotopes of an element have

options.label: A
options.option_text: different number of neutrons and same number of protons.
options.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element that contain the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, so their atomic masses differ while their chemical properties are identical. They have the same atomic number and similar chemical properties, differing only in physical properties like mass.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the same atomic mass but different atomic numbers.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the same number of electrons and neutrons.

questions.question_text: For a first order reaction, the concentration versus time of the reaction mixture is given by the following graphIf a is the initial concentration of the reactant and if the half-life is the 1hr, after how many hours wouldbe the concentration of reactant produced to a/32?

options.label: D
options.explanation: For a first-order reaction, each half-life reduces the concentration by half. Going from a to a/32 requires halving five times: a/2, a/4, a/8, a/16, then a/32. With a half-life of one hour, five half-lives take 5 hours, so the concentration reaches a/32 after 5 hours.

questions.question_text: Silver (Z=47) has several known isotopes, but two occur naturally,107Ag and109Ag.Given the following mass spectrometric data, calculate the atomic mass of Ag

options.label: C
options.explanation: The atomic mass of silver is calculated as a weighted average of its naturally occurring isotopes: roughly 0.52 × 107 + 0.48 × 109, giving approximately 107.87 amu. Option C (107.86 amu) matches the standard atomic weight of silver. The other values are not consistent with the isotopic data.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes Heisenberg's uncertainty principle?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A particle with a mass moving at a given speed can be described by the wave characteristic of material particles.

options.label: B
options.option_text: If we measure the momentum of a particle precisely then its position will be correspondingly precise.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Both the location and the momentum of a subatomic particle like the electron cannot be precisely known.
options.explanation: The Heisenberg uncertainty principle states that it is impossible to know both the exact position and the exact momentum of a subatomic particle, such as an electron, simultaneously. Measuring one precisely makes the other uncertain. The other statements describe wave-particle duality rather than the uncertainty principle itself.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A small particle like the reaction can behave both as a particle and a wave.

questions.question_text: According to the Lewis definition of an acid, an acid is a substance that

options.label: B
options.option_text: dissociates in water to yield H3O+.

options.label: C
options.explanation: According to the Lewis definition, an acid is a substance that accepts an electron pair to form a coordinate covalent bond, while a base donates the electron pair. Accepting a proton is the Brønsted-Lowry definition, and donating OH- describes a base, so the electron-pair acceptor is the Lewis acid.

questions.question_text: Water is a weak electrolyte because

options.label: A
options.option_text: it can accept a proton from an acid and donate a proton to a base.

options.label: B
options.option_text: it has a very high ionic product, Kw.

options.label: C
options.option_text: it acts both as Bronsted-Lowry and base.

options.label: D
options.option_text: it undergoes a reversible dissociation with a very low ionic product, Kw.
options.explanation: Water is a weak electrolyte because it undergoes only slight reversible dissociation into H+ and OH- ions, as indicated by its very small ionic product, Kw = 1.0×10^-14 at 25°C. This low degree of ionization means water conducts electricity only weakly, unlike strong electrolytes that ionize fully.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between reversible and irreversible reactions?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In reversible reactions, the reaction goes to completion.

options.label: B
options.option_text: In irreversible reactions, there is a mixture of products and reactants.

options.label: C
options.option_text: In reversible reactions, there is equilibrium between reactants and products.
options.explanation: In reversible reactions, the forward and reverse reactions occur simultaneously until dynamic equilibrium is reached, with both reactants and products present. Irreversible reactions proceed to completion, consuming reactants fully. Therefore the statement that reversible reactions establish equilibrium between reactants and products is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: In irreversible reactions, there is equilibrium between reactants and products.

questions.question_text: Consider the reactions all given below are in gaseous state. For which of the following reactions is Kpless than Kc?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Kp = Kc(RT)^(Δn), where Δn is the change in moles of gas. When Δn is negative, Kp is less than Kc. For 2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3, gas moles decrease from 3 to 2, so Δn = -1 and Kp < Kc. The other reactions have zero or positive Δn.

questions.question_text: The heating curve shown below shows a substance in the solid, liquid and gas phase. Which segment represents only the liquid phase?[IMAGE: img_1.webp]

options.label: A
options.explanation: Segment 1 represents the solid phase warming, segment 2 is the melting plateau where solid and liquid coexist, segment 3 is the slanted portion after melting where the temperature rises while the substance is entirely liquid, segment 4 is the boiling plateau where liquid and gas coexist, and segment 5 is the gas phase. Therefore only segment 3, which lies between the melting and boiling plateaus, represents only the liquid phase, making option A correct.

questions.question_text: The general formula for saturated monocarboxylic acids is

options.label: A
options.explanation: Saturated monocarboxylic acids have the general formula RCOOH, with the functional group -COOH attached to an alkyl group. RCOR is a ketone, RCHO is an aldehyde, and ROR is an ether, so only RCOOH correctly represents a carboxylic acid.

questions.question_text: What is enthalpy change? It is

options.label: A
options.option_text: the amount of heat given out or absorbed in a reaction at constant pressure and volume

options.label: B
options.option_text: the amount of heat absorbed in a reaction

options.label: C
options.option_text: the amount of heat given out in a reaction

options.label: D
options.option_text: the amount of heat given out or absorbed in a reaction at constant pressure
options.explanation: Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure, since at constant pressure the heat exchanged equals the change in enthalpy. The statement specifying constant pressure and heat given out or absorbed is the correct definition of enthalpy change.

questions.question_text: What is oxidation? Oxidation is

options.label: A
options.option_text: the addition of electron(s) to the oxidizing agent

options.label: B
options.option_text: the reduction of the oxidation state of the oxidizing agent

options.label: C
options.option_text: the addition of hydrogen to a substance and the removal of oxygen from a substance

options.label: D
options.option_text: the loss of electrons by a species, accompanied by an increase in oxidation number
options.explanation: Oxidation is defined as the loss of electrons by a species, accompanied by an increase in its oxidation number. Adding electrons to an oxidizing agent is reduction, and adding hydrogen or removing oxygen describes the older hydrogen-oxygen definition. Loss of electrons with an oxidation-number increase is correct.

questions.question_text: What is meant by preferential discharge, if a number of ions are present in a solution? It means that the one which requires

options.label: A
options.option_text: highest energy will be liberated first at a given electrode

options.label: B
options.option_text: highest energy will be liberated last at a given electrode

options.label: C
options.option_text: least energy will be liberated first at a given electrode
options.explanation: Preferential discharge means that when several ions are present, the ion requiring the least energy (that is, the most easily discharged ion) is liberated first at a given electrode. Electrochemical series order determines which ion is discharged preferentially, the one requiring the least energy being selected first.

options.label: D
options.option_text: least energy will be liberated last at a given electrode

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a property of covalent compounds? Covalent compounds

options.label: A
options.explanation: Covalent compounds generally dissolve poorly in water because they are molecular substances with weak intermolecular forces, unlike ionic compounds. They are frequently gases, liquids or low-melting solids, are volatile, and have low melting and boiling points rather than high ones.

options.label: D
options.option_text: has high melting and boiling points

options.label: B
options.option_text: is crystalline solids at room temperature

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a covalent molecule?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Phosphorus trichloride, PCl3, is a covalent molecule in which phosphorus shares electrons with three chlorine atoms. NH4+ and CO3^2- are polyatomic ions, and NaCl is an ionic compound, so none of these is a covalent molecule. Only PCl3 qualifies.

questions.question_text: What is the concentration of a solution? It is

options.label: A
options.option_text: the amount of solute needed to make a concentrated solution

options.label: B
options.option_text: number of moles of solute and number of moles of solvent

options.label: C
options.option_text: the quantity of solute in a given quantity of solution
options.explanation: The concentration of a solution is the quantity of solute contained in a given quantity of solution or solvent. It expresses how much solute is dissolved in a specified amount of solution. The other options describe preparation steps rather than the definition of concentration.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the amount of solvent needed to dissolve a solute

questions.question_text: How many moles of C12H22O11(sucrose Molecular weight= 342.91 g/mol) is needed there to prepare 2.0 L of 0.3 M solution?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Molarity equals moles of solute divided by litres of solution. To prepare 2.0 L of a 0.3 M sucrose solution, the required moles are 0.3 M × 2.0 L = 0.6 moles. The molar mass is not needed because the question asks for moles, not grams.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a correct Lewis structure for diazomethane (CH2N2)?

At 75°C, the vapor pressure of pure water is 39 kPa. Which one of the vapor pressure of a solution obtained by dissolving 34.2 g sucrose in 180 mL of water? (Assume that the density of water is 1.000 g/mL)

options.label: D
options.explanation: Use Raoult's law: the vapour pressure of the solution equals the mole fraction of water times the vapour pressure of pure water. 34.2 g sucrose is 0.1 mol and 180 g water is 10 mol, so X_water = 10/10.1 = 0.990. P = 0.990 × 39 kPa = 38.6 kPa.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the colligative properties of electrolytes and non-electrolytes?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The effect of non-electrolytes on colligative properties is very low compared to electrolytes

options.label: B
options.option_text: The effect of non-electrolytes on colligative properties is the same as those of electrolytes
options.explanation: Electrolytes dissociate into multiple ions and therefore affect colligative properties more strongly than non-electrolytes, which produce one particle per molecule. The statement claiming non-electrolytes have the same effect as electrolytes is false. Non-electrolytes show smaller, not unchanged, colligative effects.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The effect of electrolytes on colligative properties is very high compared to non-electrolytes

options.label: D
options.option_text: The colligative properties of non-electrolytes are not considerably changed

questions.question_text: For the reaction shown below, which of the following is a conjugate acid-base pair?HC3O-(aq)+ H2O(l) ⇌ H3O++ CO32-

options.label: C
options.explanation: In the reaction HCO3- + H2O ⇌ H3O+ + CO3^2-, the conjugate acid-base pairs are HCO3-/CO3^2- and H2O/H3O+. Since HCO3- and H2O are the acid and base on the left side reacting together, option C is selected; the exact conjugate pair is not separately listed.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of synthetic cryolite in the extraction of aluminum by the Hall's process?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Cryolite increases the melting point of alumina.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Cryolite is used as a catalyst in the extraction of aluminum.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Cryolite increases the purity of the extracted aluminum.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Cryolite reduces the melting point of alumina.
options.explanation: In the Hall-Heroult process, synthetic cryolite (Na3AlF6) is added to alumina to lower its melting point from about 2072°C to roughly 950°C, making electrolysis feasible and economical. It does not act as a catalyst, increase the melting point, or improve the purity of the aluminium produced.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a chemical property of aluminum?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Aluminum is a good conductor of heat and electricity.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Aluminum has a lower density than any other commercial metal.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Aluminum liberates hydrogen gas from dilute acids like HCl and H2SO4.
options.explanation: Aluminium liberates hydrogen gas when it reacts with dilute hydrochloric or sulphuric acid, a chemical property showing its reactivity. Conducting heat and electricity, having low density, and being grey in colour are physical properties, not chemical ones.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Aluminum is a grey metal in color.

questions.question_text: How is tanning carried out? In tanning the hides or skins are

options.label: A
options.explanation: Tanning converts animal hides into leather by treating them with chromium salts (chrome tanning) or with plant tannins. The hides are first soaked in lime and water to remove hair and flesh, but the actual tanning step itself is treatment with chromium salts.

options.label: B
options.option_text: treated with dilute hydrochloric acid to remove the lime

options.label: C
options.option_text: soaked in water for several days

options.label: D
options.option_text: soaked in lime and water for several days

questions.question_text: How can a project of establishing an industry that consumes coal affect the environment?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Production of high level of lead in the atmosphere

options.label: B
options.option_text: By changing the pH of water

options.label: C
options.option_text: Increment in concentration of nitric oxide

options.label: D
options.explanation: Burning coal releases large quantities of carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas, causing a rise in global temperature through enhanced global warming. Coal combustion also releases sulphur oxides causing acid rain, and particulates, but the increase in atmospheric CO2 leading to global temperature rise is the direct major effect.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a fundamental quantity SI unit?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Length is one of the seven fundamental SI base quantities, along with mass, time, electric current, temperature, amount of substance and luminous intensity. Pressure, speed and force are derived quantities expressed in terms of fundamental units, so they are not fundamental SI units.

questions.question_text: Which of the following postulates of Dalton's atomic theory was modified by the modern atomic theory?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Atoms are neither created nor destroyed in chemical reactions

options.label: B
options.option_text: Compounds are formed when atoms of more than one element combine

options.label: C
options.option_text: Atoms are the smallest particles of all elements

options.label: D
options.explanation: Modern atomic theory modified Dalton's postulates that atoms are indivisible and indestructible, because atoms are divisible into protons, neutrons and electrons, and can be transformed in nuclear reactions. The postulates about atoms combining and being conserved in ordinary chemical reactions remain essentially valid.

questions.question_text: Which of the following includes all of the known atomic models?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Bohr Model, Thomson Model, Rutherford Model, Dalton's Atomic Model
options.explanation: The known atomic models include Dalton's solid-sphere atomic model, Thomson's plum-pudding model with electrons embedded in positive charge, Rutherford's nuclear model with a small dense nucleus, and Bohr's model with fixed electron orbits. Option C lists all four atomic models.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Valence Bond Model, Quantum Mechanical Model, Thomson Model, Rutherford Model

questions.question_text: The electron configuration of Cu (Z=29) is:

options.label: B
options.explanation: Copper (Z=29) normally would be [Ar]4s2 3d9, but a completely filled 3d subshell is especially stable, so one 4s electron is promoted to give [Ar]4s1 3d10. Option B, with a filled 3d10 subshell and 4s2, is the closest representation among the choices, though the exact exception configuration is not shown.

questions.question_text: What does Mendeleev's Periodic Law state? Properties of elements are

options.label: A
options.option_text: periodic functions of their electron configurations

options.label: D
options.explanation: Mendeleev's periodic law states that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic masses. He arranged elements by increasing atomic mass, leaving gaps for undiscovered elements. Modern periodic law uses atomic number, but Mendeleev's original law relied on atomic masses.

questions.question_text: What is the mole ratio of oxygen gas to carbon dioxide gas in the following reaction?C3H8(g) + 5O2(g) → 3CO2(g) + 4H2O (l)

options.label: A
options.option_text: 2 mole oxygen gas to 3 mole carbon dioxide

options.label: B
options.option_text: 7 mole oxygen gas to 5 mole carbon dioxide

options.label: C
options.option_text: 10 mole oxygen gas to 6 mole carbon dioxide

options.label: D
options.option_text: 5 mole oxygen gas to 3 mole carbon dioxide
options.explanation: In the balanced combustion equation C3H8 + 5O2 → 3CO2 + 4H2O, the coefficients show that five moles of oxygen gas react to produce three moles of carbon dioxide gas. Therefore the mole ratio of oxygen gas to carbon dioxide gas is 5 to 3.

questions.question_text: Among the following reactions, which one shows a coordinate covalent bond formation?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The formation of a hydrogen molecule from a hydride ion and a hydrogen species, H- + H → H:H, illustrates a coordinate covalent bond because the electron pair for the shared bond is supplied by the hydride ion's lone pair. Option B shows this donation of an electron pair to form the covalent bond.

questions.question_text: Consider the following chemical equation for the combustion of ethane (C2H6) in the presence of oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water:C2H6(g) + 7O2(g) → 4CO2(g) + 6H2O (l)In this reaction:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Water is formed at a rate equal to 2/3 the rate of formation of CO2

options.label: B
options.option_text: CO2is formed twice as fast as ethane is consumed
options.explanation: In the reaction 2C2H6 + 7O2 → 4CO2 + 6H2O, four moles of CO2 are formed while two moles of ethane are consumed. Since 4 is twice 2, carbon dioxide is formed twice as fast as ethane is consumed, which correctly relates the rates of these species.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The rate of consumption of ethane is 7 times faster than the rate of consumption of oxygen

options.label: D
options.option_text: The rate of formation of CO2equals the rate of formation of water

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors DOES NOT affect the rate of a reaction?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Enthalpy, the total heat content of the system, does not affect the rate of a reaction. Reaction rates depend on temperature, concentration of reactants, surface area, pressure and catalysts, because these influence the frequency and energy of molecular collisions, whereas enthalpy is a state function of the system.

questions.question_text: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?

options.label: A
options.explanation: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by lowering the activation energy, providing an alternative reaction pathway with a lower energy barrier. This allows a larger fraction of molecules to have sufficient energy to react. Catalysts do not change the equilibrium constant or the enthalpy change.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements correctly describes Boyle's Law?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The volume of a gas at a given temperature is proportional to the square root of the applied pressure

options.label: B
options.option_text: The volume of a gas at a given temperature is inversely proportional to the square root of the applied pressure

options.label: C
options.option_text: The volume of a gas at a given temperature is directly proportional to the applied pressure

options.label: D
options.option_text: The volume of a gas at a given temperature is inversely proportional to the applied pressure
options.explanation: Boyle's law states that at constant temperature, the volume of a fixed amount of gas is inversely proportional to its applied pressure. As pressure increases, volume decreases proportionally, so the product of pressure and volume remains constant for a given gas at constant temperature.

questions.question_text: What are intermolecular forces? They are forces due to the attraction between

options.label: C
options.explanation: Intermolecular forces are the attractive forces between molecules, such as dispersion forces, dipole-dipole interactions and hydrogen bonding. They are weaker than the intramolecular forces holding atoms together in a molecule. Forces between ions or between nuclei and electrons are different categories.

questions.question_text: Which of the following belongs to chemical bonding theories?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Molecular orbital theory and kinetic-molecular theory

options.label: B
options.option_text: Valence bond theory and valence shell electron pair repulsion theory

options.label: C
options.option_text: Kinetic-molecular theory and valence shell electron pair repulsion theory

options.label: D
options.option_text: Valence bond theory and molecular orbital theory
options.explanation: Valence bond theory and molecular orbital theory are the two main chemical bonding theories describing how atomic orbitals combine to form bonds. VSEPR theory predicts molecular geometry, and kinetic-molecular theory describes gas behaviour, so neither is a bonding theory.

questions.question_text: In which of the following molecules is the central atom sp2hybridized?

options.label: A
options.explanation: In sulphur dioxide, the central sulphur atom forms one double bond and one single bond to two oxygen atoms, using three electron domains, which gives sp2 hybridization. Carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and nitrous oxide all have linear geometry with sp hybridization of the central atom.

questions.question_text: For a reaction:½ A → the rate of disappearance of 'A' is related to the appearance of 'B' by the expression:

options.label: A
options.explanation: For the reaction 1/2 A → B, the rate law relates the rates: -(1/0.5)d[A]/dt = d[B]/dt, which gives -d[A]/dt = (1/2)d[B]/dt. Therefore the rate of disappearance of A is half the rate of appearance of B, matching the expression in option A.

questions.question_text: The half-life of a reaction is the time taken for the

options.label: A
options.option_text: rate constant to decrease by 50% of its initial value

options.label: B
options.option_text: complete conversion of a reactant into a product

options.label: C
options.option_text: reactant concentration to decrease by 50% of its initial value
options.explanation: The half-life of a reaction is the time required for the concentration of a reactant to decrease to half of its initial value. It applies to the reactant concentration, not to the rate constant, and does not imply complete conversion of reactants into products.

options.label: D
options.option_text: rate constant to increase by 50% of its initial value

questions.question_text: For the conversion of 3.5 yards into meter using the factor label method, which of the following is the correct step?

options.label: A
options.option_text: (3.5 yards/1)(3.5 feet/1 yard)(12 in/1 foot)(1 in/2.54 cm)(1 m/100 cm)

options.label: B
options.option_text: (3.5 yards/1)(3.5 feet/1 yard)(12 in/1 foot)(2.54 cm/1 in)(1 m/100 cm)
options.explanation: Using the factor-label method, 3.5 yards is converted by multiplying by (3 ft/1 yd), (12 in/1 ft), (2.54 cm/1 in), and (1 m/100 cm), with each factor cancelling the previous unit. Option B contains this correct sequence of conversion factors, treating the feet value as three.

options.label: C
options.option_text: (3.5 yards/1)(1 yard/3.5 feet)(12 in/1 foot)(2.54 cm/1 in)(1 m/100 cm)

options.label: D
options.option_text: (3.5 yards/1)(1 yard/3.5 feet)(12 in/1 foot)(1 in/2.54 cm)(1 m/100 cm)

questions.question_text: In the scientific method, a predictive statement that can be tested experimentally is:

options.label: B
options.explanation: A hypothesis is a tentative, testable predictive statement proposed in the scientific method that can be verified experimentally. Proof, truth and evidence are outcomes of testing rather than the initial predictive statement, so hypothesis is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT true about cathode rays? Cathode rays

options.label: A
options.option_text: contain particles, which are positively charged
options.explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons, which are negatively charged particles. They travel in straight lines from cathode to anode, are common constituents of all matter with a constant charge-to-mass ratio, and contain negatively charged particles. The claim that they are positively charged is not true.

options.label: B
options.option_text: are common constituents of all matter and their m/e is constant for all gases

options.label: C
options.option_text: contain particles, which are negatively charged

options.label: D
options.option_text: travel in straight lines from cathode to the anode

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct about the energy of a photon?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is directly related to the intensity of the light

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is directly proportional to the wavelength of the light

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is directly proportional to the observed frequency of the light
options.explanation: The energy of a photon is given by E = hf, where h is Planck's constant and f is the frequency. Since energy equals Planck's constant times frequency, photon energy is directly proportional to the observed frequency of the light, and inversely proportional to wavelength.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is inversely proportional to the observed frequency of the light

questions.question_text: Which of the following explains the emission spectra of atoms consisting of a series of fine lines?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The energy of the atoms is continuous with discrete frequencies

options.label: B
options.option_text: An electron that revolves around the nucleus emits specific energy values in an atom

options.label: C
options.option_text: An electron can have specific transition by energy changes corresponding to photon of specific wavelength

options.label: D
options.option_text: An electron undergoes a transition by energy changes corresponding to photon of specific wavelength
options.explanation: Atomic emission spectra consist of sharp lines because electrons in an atom undergo transitions between discrete energy levels, emitting a photon of specific wavelength corresponding to the energy change. Each line represents a specific electronic transition, giving the fine-line series characteristic of atoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a polyprotic acid?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Phosphoric acid, H3PO4, is a polyprotic acid because it can donate up to three protons in stepwise dissociations. Hydrofluoric acid, nitric acid and hydrochloric acid each donate only one proton, so they are monoprotic acids, not polyprotic.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does represent a general property of a base?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Soluble bases release hydronium ion in aqueous solution

options.label: B
options.option_text: Aqueous solution of bases turns methyl orange to red

options.label: C
options.option_text: Solutions of strong bases are good conductors of electricity
options.explanation: Solutions of strong bases are good conductors of electricity because strong bases dissociate completely, producing many ions that carry charge. Bases release hydroxide ions rather than hydronium ions, turn red litmus blue, and turn methyl orange yellow, so only the conductivity statement is a general property.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Aqueous solution of bases turns blue litmus paper to red

questions.question_text: What are salts? Salts are

options.label: A
options.option_text: Ionic compounds that derive their cations from a base and their anions from an acid
options.explanation: Salts are ionic compounds formed when the cation of a base and the anion of an acid combine, typically from neutralization reactions. They derive their cations from a base and their anions from an acid. The other statements incorrectly describe partial replacement or reactions with water alone.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Ionic compounds formed by partial replacement of ionizable hydrogen by metal cations

options.label: C
options.option_text: Ionic compounds formed by complete replacement of ionizable hydrogen by anions of the acid

options.label: D
options.option_text: Ionic compounds that result from the reaction between metal hydroxide and water

questions.question_text: The process in which a compound absorbs electrical energy and decomposes into its elements is

options.label: C
options.explanation: Electrolysis is the process in which electrical energy drives the decomposition of a compound into its elements or simpler substances, as in the electrolysis of molten NaCl into sodium and chlorine. Hydrolysis uses water, and solvolysis uses a solvent, while electroplating deposits metal, so electrolysis fits the definition.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about galvanic cells used in commercial lead storage batteries? In lead storage batteries,

options.label: A
options.option_text: half of the galvanic cells are connected in series

options.label: B
options.option_text: the galvanic cells are made up of PbO2of anodes

options.label: C
options.option_text: galvanic cells are connected in series
options.explanation: Commercial lead storage batteries consist of several galvanic cells connected in series so their voltages add, producing the high voltage needed to start a vehicle. Half-series connections, parallel connections, and a PbO2 anode description are all incorrect, so connecting the cells in series is the true statement.

options.label: D
options.option_text: galvanic cells are connected in parallel

questions.question_text: The self-ionization of water can be expressed by the equation:H2O(l) + H2O(l)⇌ H3O+(aq) + OH-(aq)Which of the following is the correct expression of the ionic product of water?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The ionic product of water, Kw, equals the product of the concentrations of hydronium and hydroxide ions, Kw = [H3O+][OH-]. At 25 degrees C Kw equals 1.0 x 10-14. Pure liquid water is excluded because its concentration is essentially constant. Option C is identical in meaning using HO- notation, making the question defective.

questions.question_text: What is the effect of a common ion in an electrolytic solution?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It decreases the solubility of a solute

options.label: B
options.option_text: It has no effect on the pH of a solution

options.label: C
options.option_text: It suppresses the ionization of a weak acid and raises the pH
options.explanation: The common ion effect suppresses the ionization of a weak acid when its conjugate base, a common ion, is added. The equilibrium shifts left, lowering the H+ concentration and thereby raising the pH. It does not lower the pOH, and common ions definitely do affect solubility and pH.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It suppresses the ionization of a weak base and lowers the pOH

questions.question_text: Sodium carbonate is a basic salt because it is a salt of

options.label: A
options.option_text: a weak acid and a weak base and the cation of the weak base can be hydrolyzed

options.label: B
options.option_text: a strong acid and a weak base and the anion of the strong acid can be hydrolyzed

options.label: C
options.option_text: a strong base and a weak acid and the anion of the weak acid can be hydrolyzed
options.explanation: Sodium carbonate is a basic salt formed from the strong base sodium hydroxide and the weak acid carbonic acid. Its anion, CO3 2-, hydrolyzes by accepting protons from water to regenerate the weak acid and release hydroxide ions, making the solution basic. The Na+ cation is not hydrolyzed.

options.label: D
options.option_text: a strong base and a strong acid and the anion of the strong acid can be hydrolyzed

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true for an acid-base titration?

options.label: A
options.option_text: An acid-base titration is a method of quantitative analysis for determining the concentration of an acid or base
options.explanation: An acid-base titration is a quantitative analytical method for determining the concentration of an acid or base by reacting it with a standard solution of known concentration. It is quantitative, not qualitative. Indicators do not catalyze the reaction, and titrations can be monitored with a pH meter without any indicator.

options.label: B
options.option_text: An acid-base titration is a method of qualitative analysis for determining the concentration of an acid or base

options.label: C
options.option_text: Indicators catalyze an acid-base titration to show the inflection point of the titration curve

options.label: D
options.option_text: Acid-base titrations cannot be carried out in the absence of indicators

questions.question_text: What is the change in internal energy (ΔE) for a reaction, in which the system absorbs 650 J of heat and 125 J of work is done on the system?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Using the first law of thermodynamics, ΔE = q + w. The system absorbs 650 J of heat, so q = +650 J, and work done on the system means w = +125 J. Therefore ΔE = 650 + 125 = 775 J. The positive internal energy change is 775 J, matching option C.

questions.question_text: Which statement describes the formation of a covalent bond? In covalent bond electrons are

options.label: A
options.explanation: A covalent bond forms when electrons are shared between non-metallic atoms, such as in H2, O2, and CH4, so each atom achieves a stable electron configuration. The transfer of electrons produces ionic bonds instead, and sharing does not occur between metallic atoms in this way.

options.label: B
options.option_text: transferred from non-metallic atoms to metallic atoms

options.label: D
options.option_text: transferred from metallic atoms to non-metallic atoms

questions.question_text: How do the elements of Group IIA form ions?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Group IIA elements, the alkaline earth metals with two valence electrons, form ions by losing both electrons, producing 2+ cations such as Mg2+ and Ca2+. They do not gain electrons because losing their two valence electrons gives a stable noble-gas electron configuration, matching the loss of two electrons.

questions.question_text: How is hydrogen bonding formed? It is formed when a hydrogen atom is bonded to

options.label: A
options.option_text: highly electronegative elements, chlorine, oxygen and nitrogen

options.label: B
options.option_text: highly electronegative elements, fluorine, oxygen and nitrogen
options.explanation: Hydrogen bonding forms when a hydrogen atom is covalently bonded to a highly electronegative element, specifically fluorine, oxygen, or nitrogen. These atoms attract the bonding electrons strongly, leaving hydrogen partially positive so it can attract lone pairs of nearby molecules. Chlorine and phosphorus are not normally involved.

options.label: C
options.option_text: highly electronegative elements, fluorine, chlorine and oxygen

options.label: D
options.option_text: highly electronegative elements, fluorine, oxygen and phosphorus

questions.question_text: Which one of the following types of energy change occurs from the combustion of carbon in oxygen?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The combustion of carbon in oxygen, C + O2 → CO2, is an exothermic reaction that releases heat energy as its primary energy output. Although some light may be emitted, the defining energy change from combustion is heat energy, so heat energy is the correct choice.

questions.question_text: What is the molar volume of a gas?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 0°C and pressure,1 kPa), which is equal to 22.4 L/mol

options.label: B
options.option_text: The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 25°C and pressure,1 kPa ), which is equal to 22.4 L/mol

options.label: C
options.option_text: The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature, 0°C and pressure,1 atm ), which is equal to 22.4 L/mol
options.explanation: Molar volume is the volume occupied by one mole of any ideal gas at STP. Standard temperature is 0 degrees C (273 K) and standard pressure is 1 atm, at which one mole of gas occupies 22.4 L/mol. The 25 degree C condition describes SATP, where the molar volume is about 24.5 L/mol.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 25°C and pressure,1 atm ), which is equal to 22.4 L/mol

questions.question_text: Which of the following assumptions of the kinetic molecular theory of gases explains the high compressibility of gases?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Particles are always in random motion

options.label: C
options.option_text: The actual volume of gas molecules in negligible
options.explanation: The high compressibility of gases is explained by the assumption that the actual volume of the gas molecules themselves is negligible compared with the total volume of the gas, leaving large amounts of empty space between molecules that can be compressed. Random motion, varied speeds, and no attraction do not explain compressibility.

options.label: D
options.option_text: There is no force of attraction between gas molecules

questions.question_text: Consider a bottle containing water, water vapor and air in equilibrium. If the temperature decreases slightly, the amount of water vapor:

options.label: A
options.option_text: will decrease and the vapor pressure will increase

options.label: B
options.explanation: Lowering the temperature of a liquid that is in equilibrium with its vapor decreases both the amount of water vapor present and the vapor pressure. Since vapor pressure rises with temperature, cooling reduces molecular kinetic energy, condensation dominates, and the vapor pressure falls, so both quantities decrease.

options.label: D
options.option_text: will increase and the vapor pressure will decrease

questions.question_text: Why do water droplets collect on the outside of a glass of water on a hot day?

options.label: A
options.option_text: There will be a condensation of water vapor on the glass
options.explanation: On a hot day, warm humid air contacts the cold surface of the glass.
