The water vapor in the air cools below its dew point and condenses into liquid droplets on the cold outside surface of the glass. Sublimation, vaporization, and heat exchange alone do not explain the droplets.

options.label: B
options.option_text: There will be a sublimation of water vapor on the outside of a glass

options.label: C
options.option_text: There is heat exchange between the water in the glass and the surrounding

options.label: D
options.option_text: Water from the glass starts to vaporize

questions.question_text: What are hydrocarbons? Compounds that contain

options.label: C
options.option_text: hydrogen and carbon with no benzene rings

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hydrocarbons are organic compounds that contain only hydrogen and carbon atoms, such as methane, ethane, and benzene. They are not restricted to benzene rings or benzene derivatives, because saturated, unsaturated, and aromatic compounds all qualify. The hydrogen-and-carbon-only definition is therefore correct.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is INCORRECT regarding the boiling points of alkanes?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Boiling points of straight chain alkanes is greater than that of branched chain alkanes

options.label: B
options.option_text: The boiling point of cycloalkanes is higher than that of linear alkanes

options.label: C
options.option_text: Boiling points increases with stronger Van der Waals forces

options.label: D
options.option_text: Surface area is the only factor that determines the boiling points of alkanes
options.explanation: The statement that surface area is the only factor determining the boiling points of alkanes is incorrect, because molecular size and molar mass are equally important. Straight-chain alkanes boil higher than branched ones due to larger surface area and stronger Van der Waals forces, so D is the false statement.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about minerals and ores?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Minerals are the natural forms in which various metals exist

options.label: B
options.option_text: Ores are usually used to extract metals economically

options.label: C
options.explanation: The statement that all minerals are ores is incorrect. An ore is a mineral or rock from which a metal can be extracted economically, so only some minerals qualify as ores. Since every ore is a mineral found naturally in the earth, the false statement is that all minerals are ores.

questions.question_text: Why is CaCl₂ added to NaCl in a 1:1⁄2 ratio in the Down's cell for the manufacturing of sodium metal?

options.label: A
options.option_text: CaCl₂ is used to lower the density of the mixture

options.label: B
options.option_text: CaCl₂ is used as an electrolyte

options.label: C
options.option_text: CaCl₂ is used as a catalyst

options.label: D
options.option_text: CaCl₂ is used to lower the melting temperature of NaCl
options.explanation: Calcium chloride is added to sodium chloride in the Down's cell to lower the melting temperature of the mixture. Pure NaCl melts at about 801 degrees C, but the CaCl2-NaCl mixture melts near 580 degrees C, saving energy. CaCl2 does not act as the electrolyte or as a catalyst here.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a major step in metallurgical processes?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pretreatment is not one of the three major steps of metallurgical processes. The standard major steps are mining the ore, concentrating the ore, and extracting and refining the metal. Pretreatment is not listed among these major metallurgical steps, so it is the correct exception.

questions.question_text: Which monomers are used for the synthesis of Teflon?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Teflon, polytetrafluoroethylene or PTFE, is produced by the addition polymerization of tetrafluoroethylene, CF2=CF2, in which all hydrogen atoms of ethylene are replaced by fluorine. Styrene, isoprene, and propylene are the monomers of polystyrene, natural rubber, and polypropylene respectively.

questions.question_text: What is the IUPAC name of an ester having the molecular formula C₄H₉O₂?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Esters are named by giving the alcohol part first and then the acid part with an -oate ending. Ethyl butanoate is the correct IUPAC name. The question is defective because the formula C4H9O2 is impossible for an ester, ethyl butanoate being C6H12O2, and option A is the same compound by its common name.

questions.question_text: What is the formula of pentanoic acid?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pentanoic acid has a five-carbon chain ending in a carboxyl group: CH3(CH2)3COOH, which contains one methyl, three methylene, and one carboxyl carbon. CH3(CH2)4COOH would be hexanoic acid and CH3(CH2)2COOH would be butanoic acid. Options A and D are identical, making the question defective.

questions.question_text: What is the rate of dissolution? It is

options.label: A
options.option_text: the rate at which a solid dissociates

options.label: B
options.option_text: the speed at which a solid sublimes

options.label: C
options.option_text: the rate at which a solid turns to liquid

options.label: D
options.option_text: the speed at which a solid substrate goes into solution
options.explanation: The rate of dissolution is defined as the speed at which a solid solute goes into solution, that is, the quantity of solid dissolving per unit time. It is not about dissociation, sublimation, or melting, which describe different processes. A solid substrate entering solution matches this definition.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following iscorrectlystated regarding solubility as an equilibrium process?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Supersaturated solution is a solution that contains more than the equilibrium amount of dissolved solute
options.explanation: A supersaturated solution contains more dissolved solute than the equilibrium, saturated amount at a given temperature, making it unstable relative to the saturated solution. The question is defective because option D, that an unsaturated solution can still dissolve more solute, is also a correct statement about solubility equilibrium.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Supersaturated solution is more stable than saturated solution

options.label: C
options.option_text: Unsaturated solution is a solution that is in equilibrium with respect to a given dissolved substance

options.label: D
options.option_text: Unsaturated solution is a solution in which more of the solute can be dissolved

questions.question_text: Which of the following carboxylic acids is a solid substance at room temperature?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Decanoic acid, with ten carbon atoms, is a solid at room temperature because its long nonpolar chains allow strong Van der Waals forces, giving a melting point near 31 degrees C. Nonanoic, octanoic, and heptanoic acids, with fewer carbons, are liquids at room temperature.

questions.question_text: Which of the following represents the structure of a disaccharide?

In a kinetic experiment, a student placed crystals of iodine in a closed reaction vessel, introduced a given quantity of hydrogen gas, and collected data to calculate the rate of formation of hydrogen iodide. What would be the effect obtained on the rate of the reaction, if the student takes more amount of iodine from that used in the first experiment?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It speeds up the rate of the reaction.
options.explanation: Using more solid iodine crystals increases the surface area of the solid reactant in contact with the hydrogen gas, which speeds up the rate of formation of hydrogen iodide. A larger amount of reactant and a greater surface area raise the collision frequency, so the reaction rate increases.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It lowers the rate of the reaction.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The formation of hydrogen iodide will be decreased.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The rate of the reaction will be constant.

questions.question_text: Which of the following CORRECTLY relates the vapor pressure of a liquid with its boiling point? Boiling point is

options.label: A
options.option_text: the temperature at which all the three physical state co-exist.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the temperature at which the vapor pressure becomes equal to the external pressure.
options.explanation: The boiling point is the temperature at which the vapor pressure of a liquid becomes equal to the external, atmospheric pressure, allowing bubbles of vapor to form throughout the liquid. At this temperature the liquid converts rapidly to vapor. Lowering the external pressure lowers the boiling point.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the temperature at which molecules present in the vapor phase go back to the liquid state.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the temperature at which the kinetic energy of molecules is much less than the intermolecular force.

questions.question_text: Consider this equilibrium system:CO (g) + Fe3O4(s) ⇌ CO2(g) + 3FeO(s)Which of the following disturbances shift the equilibrium position to the right?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Removing carbon dioxide gas, a product, shifts the equilibrium to the right according to Le Chatelier's principle, because the system acts to replace the removed product. Removing the reactant CO shifts it left, while the solids FeO and Fe3O4 have constant concentrations that do not affect equilibrium.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following resulted from interaction of the atomic orbitals of bonding atoms to produce new electron distribution associated with the entire molecule?

options.label: B
options.explanation: A molecular orbital is formed when the atomic orbitals of bonding atoms interact and combine to produce new electron distributions that are associated with the entire molecule. A hybrid orbital is localized on one atom, while Bohr and electron orbits describe electrons around a single nucleus.

questions.question_text: Which type of organic substances would be produced by heating a mixture of a carboxylic acid and an alcohol in the presence of H2SO4?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Heating a carboxylic acid with an alcohol in the presence of concentrated H2SO4 produces an ester through Fischer esterification, for example ethanol and ethanoic acid giving ethyl ethanoate and water. The acid catalyst speeds the reversible condensation, and the product class is esters, not ketones, aldehydes, or ethers.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the reducing agent in the following reaction?8NH3(g) + 6NO2(g) → 7N2(g) + 12H2O (l)

options.label: B
options.explanation: In NH3 nitrogen has the oxidation state -3 and in N2 it is 0, so nitrogen is oxidized from -3 to 0 and NH3 is the reducing agent. In NO2 nitrogen is +4 and is reduced to 0, making NO2 the oxidizing agent. H2O and N2 are products of the reaction.

questions.question_text: Carbon forms two stable compounds with oxygen, namely, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide. For a fixed mass of carbon, the ratio of oxygen in carbon monoxide to oxygen in carbon dioxide is 1:2. This result is consistent with the law of

options.label: D
options.explanation: When carbon forms two compounds with oxygen, CO and CO2, for a fixed mass of carbon the masses of oxygen combining with it are in a simple whole-number ratio of 1:2. This is the law of multiple proportions, which states that element masses combining with a fixed mass of another are in small whole-number ratios.

questions.question_text: When a system at equilibrium is disturbed by a change of variable, the system shifts the equilibrium position in a way that tends to counteract this change of variable. This is a statement for

options.label: D
options.explanation: This statement describes Le Chatelier's principle, which states that when a system at equilibrium is disturbed by a change in concentration, pressure, or temperature, the equilibrium shifts in the direction that counteracts the disturbance and re-establishes equilibrium. Pauli, Aufbau, and Heisenberg principles concern electrons, not equilibrium.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following graphs illustrates the rate change in terms of a change in reactant concentration with time?
The pH of a 0.1 M solution of formic acid (HCOOH) is 3. What is the Ka of the acid?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Given pH 3, the hydrogen ion concentration is 1 x 10-3 M. For a weak acid, Ka = [H+][A-]/[HA] = (1 x 10-3)(1 x 10-3)/0.1 = 1 x 10-6 divided by 0.1 = 1.0 x 10-5. Since [H+] equals [A-], this calculation gives the Ka value in option A.

questions.question_text: A system does 15 J of work and no other changes take place. Which of the following function has fallen by 15 J?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The first law gives ΔE = q + w. If the system does 15 J of work and no other changes take place, then q = 0 and w = -15 J, so ΔE = -15 J. The internal energy has fallen by 15 J. Enthalpy, entropy, and specific heat are not reduced by doing work alone.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following gas laws states the volume of a fixed amount of gas maintained at constant pressure is directly proportional to the absolute temperature of the gas?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Charles' law states that the volume of a fixed amount of gas maintained at constant pressure is directly proportional to its absolute temperature, expressed as V1/T1 = V2/T2. Boyle's law relates pressure and volume at constant temperature, while Avogadro's law relates volume and the amount of gas.

questions.question_text: Which of the following isCORRECTLYstated about the spontaneity of a reaction?

options.label: A
options.option_text: For an endothermic reaction with negative reaction entropy, the reaction is spontaneous at all temperature.

options.label: B
options.option_text: For an exothermic reaction with positive reaction entropy, the reaction is non-spontaneous at all temperature.

options.label: C
options.option_text: For an endothermic reaction with positive reaction entropy, the reaction is non-spontaneous at low temperature.
options.explanation: Using the Gibbs free energy equation ΔG = ΔH - TΔS, an endothermic reaction with positive ΔH and positive ΔS is non-spontaneous at low temperature because the TΔS term is small, leaving ΔG positive. It becomes spontaneous only at high temperature. The other options contradict this analysis.

options.label: D
options.option_text: For an exothermic reaction with negative reaction entropy, the reaction is spontaneous at high temperature.

questions.question_text: In thermodynamics: solutions in a beaker, a gas in a cylinder, a reaction vessel, a biological cell are examples of a

options.label: D
options.explanation: Solutions in a beaker, a gas in a cylinder, a reaction vessel, and a biological cell are all examples of thermodynamic systems, which are the portions of the universe under study separated from the surroundings by a boundary. Variables, state functions, and path functions are properties, not systems.

questions.question_text: Given the following:bond energies (kJ/mol)H-H 436N-N 193N=N 409N≡N 942and the enthalpy for the reaction1/2N2(g) +3/2H2(g) →NH3(g); ΔH=-45 kJ/molWhat is the bond energy for NH3?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bonds broken: one-half of N triple bond N equals 0.5 x 942 = 471 kJ, and three-halves of H-H equals 1.5 x 436 = 654 kJ, giving a total of 1125 kJ. Bonds formed: three N-H bonds equal 3x. ΔH = 1125 - 3x = -45, so 3x = 1170 kJ. The total bond energy of NH3 is therefore 1170 kJ.

questions.question_text: The rate law for: (CH3)-C-Br (aq) + H2O (l) → (CH3)-C-OH (aq) + H++ Br¯ (aq) is rate= k [(CH3)-C-Br (aq) + H2O (l)]. The accepted mechanism for the reaction is:I. (CH3)-C-Br(aq) → (CH3)-C¯(aq) + Br¯(aq) [slow]II. (CH3)-C¯(aq) + H2O(l) → (CH3)-C-OH¯(aq) [fast]III. (CH3)-C-OH¯(aq) → (CH3)-C-OH(aq) + H¯ [fast]Why DOES NOT H2O appear in the rate law? Because

options.label: A
options.option_text: water is a catalyst in the reaction.

options.label: C
options.option_text: water exists in the liquid state in the reaction.

options.label: D
options.option_text: water is missing in the rate determining step.
options.explanation: The rate law is determined by the slow, rate-determining step of the mechanism. Since water does not appear in the slow step I, it does not appear in the rate law, even though it reacts in the fast step II. Water is not a catalyst or intermediate, and its concentration is essentially constant.

questions.question_text: Which type of substances has the following general formula? (R1, R2and R3are hydrocarbon groups.)[IMAGE: img_1.webp]

options.label: B
options.explanation: The general formula shown is a triglyceride, in which a glycerol backbone carries three hydrocarbon chains R1, R2, and R3 joined by ester linkages, and such molecules are called fats. Carboxylic acids, alcohols, and fatty acids do not carry three separate hydrocarbon groups attached to one core structure.

questions.question_text: The rate law for this reaction CO (g) + NO2(g) → CO2(g) + NO (g) is rate = k [NO2]p[CO]q. Which one of the following could be a plausible mechanism for the reaction?

options.label: A
options.option_text: NO2(g) + NO2(g) -> NO3(g) + NO(g) [slow]NO3(g) + CO(g) -> NO2(g) + CO2(g) [fast]
options.explanation: A valid mechanism must produce the observed rate law from its slow step. In option A, the slow step 2NO2 → NO3 + NO gives rate = k[NO2] squared, a plausible rate law. The fast NO3 + CO step then yields CO2 and NO, and the two steps sum to the overall reaction.

options.label: B
options.option_text: NO3(g) + NO(g) -> NO2(g) + NO2(g) [slow]NO2(g) + CO2(g) -> NO3(g) + CO(g) [fast]

options.label: C
options.option_text:
NO2(g) + NO(g) -> NO3(g) + NO2(g) [slow]
NO3(g) + CO(g) -> NO2(g) + CO2(g) [fast]

options.label: D
options.option_text: NO2(g) + NO2(g) -> NO3(g) + NO(g) [fast]NO3(g) + CO(g) -> NO2(g) + CO2(g) [slow]

questions.question_text: The speed with which a solute goes into solution is

options.label: C
options.explanation: The rate of dissolution is defined as the speed at which a solute goes into solution, that is, the quantity of solid dissolving per unit time. It is not heat of solution, degree of solvation, or extent of dissolution, which describe energy changes, interactions, or final amounts rather than speed.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains how 2 L of 1 M NaOH aqueous stock solution is converted into a 0.25 M NaOH solution?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Adding 6 L water to the stock solution
options.explanation: Using the dilution formula M1V1 = M2V2, (1 M)(2 L) = (0.25 M)(V2), so V2 = 2 divided by 0.25 = 8 L. The final volume must be 8 L, which requires adding 6 L of water to the original 2 L of stock solution. Evaporating water would raise, not lower, the concentration.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Adding 8 L water to the stock solution

options.label: C
options.option_text: Evaporating 0.25 L of water from the stock solution

options.label: D
options.option_text: Evaporating 1 L of water from the stock solution

questions.question_text: Which one of the following IS TRUE about isotopes?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Isotopes of an element are atoms that have different number of electrons and protons.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Isotopes of an element are identical in mass number.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Isotopes of the same elements contain the same number of neutrons.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Isotopes of an element have the same chemical properties.
options.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, giving different mass numbers. Because they have identical electron configurations, they show the same chemical properties. They differ in mass and neutron number, not in electron and proton counts.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following describes the quantum mechanical model?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The locations of electrons in an atom are described in terms of probability.
options.explanation: The quantum mechanical model describes the locations of electrons in an atom in terms of probability distributions, or electron clouds, rather than fixed paths. This replaces Bohr's circular orbits and the solid-sphere models, so the statement that electron locations are described by probability is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: An atom is represented by a solid indestructible sphere.

options.label: C
options.option_text: An atom is a sphere with a positively charged matter, in which electrons are embedded.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Electrons moved around the nucleus of an atom in circular orbits.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the diagrammatic representation of3531Cl?
Which one of the following is an ionic compound?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Calcium chloride is an ionic compound formed between the metal calcium and the non-metal chlorine through electron transfer and held together by electrostatic attraction. CO2, PCl3, and H2O3 are molecular compounds in which non-metal atoms share electrons through covalent bonds.

questions.question_text: An element is located in Group VIIA and 3rdperiod of the modern periodic table. On the basis of this the element:

options.label: A
options.option_text: generally forms an ion with -2 charges.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The element in Group VIIA and the third period is chlorine, a halogen that forms acidic oxides when it combines with oxygen. Halogens gain one electron to form -1 ions, have high ionization energy, and have high electron affinity, so the acidic-oxide statement is the correct one.

questions.question_text: Which of the properties of solvents WOULD NOT be affected by the formation of a solution with a non-volatile solute?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Adding a non-volatile solute to a solvent affects colligative properties: the boiling point is elevated, the freezing point is lowered, and the chemical potential of the solvent changes. The chemical identity of the solvent molecules remains unchanged, so it is the property not affected.

questions.question_text: The partial pressure of acetylene, C2H2, in a container is 10 atm at 25°C. What is the solubility in molarity of C2H2, assume that C2H2obeys Henry's law? (KH= 1.04 mol/L atm)

options.label: D
options.explanation: Henry's law states that solubility S = KH x P. Substituting the given values, solubility = 1.04 mol/L atm x 10 atm = 10.4 mol/L. Therefore the molar solubility of acetylene at a partial pressure of 10 atm is 10.4 M, matching option D.

questions.question_text: What is the normality of a solution that contains 19.6 g of H2SO4in 20 mL of the solution?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The molar mass of H2SO4 is 2(1) + 32 + 4(16) = 98 g/mol. Moles = 19.6 g / 98 g/mol = 0.2 mol in 0.020 L, so molarity = 0.2/0.02 = 10 M. Since H2SO4 supplies two H+ ions per formula unit, normality = 10 x 2 = 20 N, option C.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following illustrates an extensive property?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The electrode potential at standard condition for the half-reaction 2Cu2++ 4e−→2Cu is the same as for Cu2++ 2e−→Cu.

options.label: B
options.option_text: If a system is divided into parts and it is found that the property of the composite system has a value that is the sum of the values of the property of all the parts.
options.explanation: An extensive property depends on the amount of substance and is additive: the value for the whole system equals the sum of the values of its parts. This matches option B. Density in option C and temperature in option D are intensive properties that do not depend on the amount.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Doubling the volume of a sample also doubles the mass; so the ratio of mass to volume remains the same.

options.label: D
options.option_text: If water in two beakers at the same temperature are mixed to make a single quantity of water and the temperature of the combined quantity of water is the same as it was in the two separate beakers.

questions.question_text: The point in a titration at which the number of moles of OH-ions added to a solution is equal to the number of moles of H+ions originally present is

options.label: D
options.explanation: The equivalence point in a titration is reached when the number of moles of OH- ions added equals the number of moles of H+ ions originally present, meaning the acid and base have exactly neutralized each other. The end point is when the indicator changes color, which occurs near the equivalence point.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is TRUE about the electrolysis of a molten hypothetical electrolyte, MX?

options.label: A
options.option_text: X is produced at the negative electrode.

options.label: B
options.option_text: M is produced at the anode.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Electrons are not transferred from one species to the other.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The overall reaction is redox reaction.
options.explanation: In the electrolysis of molten MX, the M+ cations are reduced at the cathode and the X- anions are oxidized at the anode, so electrons are transferred between species and the overall reaction is a redox reaction. This is the only correct statement about the process.

questions.question_text: During the extraction of an unknown metal, the metallic discharge was fused with NaOH in air and then dissolved in water to obtain the soluble unknown metal containing species. Reduction with carbon is followed as the solution is treated with HCl. Finally the obtained oxide is reduced to its metallic form by aluminum. The most probable unknown metal would be

options.label: C
options.explanation: The described extraction matches chromium: chromite is fused with NaOH in air to form soluble sodium chromate, which is leached with water, treated with acid and reduced with carbon to chromium(III) oxide, then reduced by aluminum in the thermite reaction. Calcium, zinc, and lead do not follow this route.

questions.question_text: Why tin does NOT react with cold water but calcium reacts with cold water quite readily?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Due to its less reactive nature.
options.explanation: Tin is less reactive than calcium because it lies lower in the reactivity series, below hydrogen, so it does not react with cold water. Calcium, an alkaline earth metal above hydrogen, reacts vigorously with cold water to produce calcium hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Due to the formation of a thin oxide layer.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Due to the pH of water.

questions.question_text: Why is vulcanization performed in natural rubber?

options.label: A
options.option_text: To convert the monomer unit in natural rubber in to polymer.

options.label: B
options.option_text: To establish cross-links between polymer chain in the natural rubber.
options.explanation: Vulcanization heats natural rubber with sulfur to establish cross-links between the polymer chains, which strengthens the rubber, improves elasticity, and prevents it from becoming sticky in heat. It does not change the number of monomer units or form the polymer from monomers.

options.label: C
options.option_text: To decrease the number of monomer unit in the natural rubber.

options.label: D
options.option_text: To increase the number of monomer unit in the natural rubber.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains the determination of the cell potential of Zn-Cu cell using voltmeter?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In the Cu half-cell, Cu metal will be dipped in ZnSO4 solution.

options.label: B
options.option_text: In the Zn half-cell, Zn metal will be dipped in CuSO4 solution.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Each U-tube served as a salt bridge that can be filled with saturated KCl.
options.explanation: To measure the Zn-Cu cell potential with a voltmeter, each half-cell contains its metal dipped in its own salt solution, and a U-tube salt bridge filled with saturated KCl connects them to complete the circuit. Zinc is oxidized, so its mass decreases rather than increases.

options.label: D
options.option_text: After the experiment the mass of zinc is increased.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an example of molecular crystals?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Solid carbon dioxide, dry ice, is a molecular crystal in which CO2 molecules are held at lattice points by weak intermolecular Van der Waals forces. Diamond is a covalent network crystal, sodium chloride is an ionic crystal, and magnesium is a metallic crystal, so dry ice is the molecular crystal.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following COULD NOT be considered as factor influencing the rate of chemical reaction?

options.label: C
options.option_text: The rate constant of the reaction
options.explanation: The rate constant k is a proportionality constant in the rate law, not a variable factor one can change to influence reaction speed. The presence of a catalyst, the surface area of reactants, and the temperature of reactants are genuine factors that alter reaction rates.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following shows the hybridization scheme of the central atom in H2O?
In which of the following order of a reaction, a plot of ln [A]tversus time is a straight line whose slope is -k?

options.label: A
options.explanation: For a first-order reaction, the integrated rate law is ln[A]t = -kt + ln[A]0, which is a straight line with slope -k when ln[A]t is plotted against time. Zero, second, and third order reactions give different plots, so first order is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: A forward and reverse reaction continues to take place at equal rate in microscopic level. This statement is the definition of

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dynamic equilibrium is the state in which the forward and reverse reactions continue to take place at equal rates at the microscopic level, so concentrations remain constant even though reaction is still occurring. Chemical kinetics is the study of reaction rates, not this equilibrium state.

questions.question_text: The heat change at constant pressure that results when 1 mole of a compound is formed from its elements in their standard states is

options.label: D
options.explanation: Standard enthalpy of formation is the heat change at constant pressure when one mole of a compound is formed from its elements in their standard states. Standard enthalpy of reaction applies to any reaction, not specifically to formation from elements, so D gives the precise definition.

questions.question_text: What is a redox reaction? It is a reaction in which

options.label: A
options.option_text: two insoluble ions in compounds form an insoluble products.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A redox reaction is one in which electrons are transferred between species: one species loses electrons during oxidation while another gains them during reduction. Exchanging bonding partners describes metathesis, neutralization describes acid-base reactions, and precipitation is unrelated to electron transfer.

options.label: C
options.option_text: atoms or ions of two compound exchange bonding partners.

options.label: D
options.option_text: an acid and a base neutralize each other.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains how electroplating takes place?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The electrolyte is an aqueous solution of a salt of the plated metal.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The object to be electroplated either metal or graphite-coated plastic constitutes the anode.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The cations in the electrolyte are supplied either by the added salt or from oxidation of the anode.
options.explanation: The cations in the electroplating electrolyte are supplied both by the dissolved salt of the plating metal and by oxidation of the metal anode, which replenishes the ions removed as metal plates out at the cathode. Option A is also true, making the question defective. Metal is deposited at the cathode, not the anode.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Metal is deposited on the anode by reduction of ions in the electrolyte solution.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements describes chemical industries? It is

options.label: A
options.option_text: an area of chemistry concerned with the speeds, or rates, at which chemical reactions occur.

options.label: B
options.option_text: an expression for the chemical composition of a compound in terms of the symbols of the atoms of the elements involved.

options.label: C
options.option_text: a process in which dissolved solute comes out of solution and forms crystals.

options.label: D
options.option_text: a firm that involves usage of raw material to produce desired products by using chemical reactions and refining methods.
options.explanation: Chemical industries are firms that use raw materials to produce desired products by employing chemical reactions and refining methods. The other statements define kinetics, which is the study of reaction speeds, chemical formulas, and crystallization, none of which describe chemical industries.

questions.question_text: What will be the product if phosphorus reacts with excess amount of oxygen?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Phosphorus burning in excess oxygen forms phosphorus pentoxide, P4O10, in which phosphorus reaches its highest oxidation state of +5. P3O6 and the acids H3PO3 and H3PO4 are not the direct products of combustion with excess oxygen, so P4O10 is the correct product.

questions.question_text: One of the basic differences between metallic conduction and electrolytic conduction is:

options.label: A
options.option_text: The conduction of electricity is due to the movement of ions in an electrolytic conduction while the flow of mobile electrons in metallic conduction.
options.explanation: In electrolytic conduction, electricity is carried by the movement of ions through a solution or molten electrolyte, whereas in metallic conduction electricity flows through the movement of mobile electrons. The charge carriers are exactly reversed in the other statements.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The charge carriers in metals are cations and anions while mobile electrons are in electrolytic conduction.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The charge carriers in metals are localized electrons while strongly held mobile electrons are in electrolytic conduction.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The conduction of electricity is due to the movement of ions in metallic conduction while the flow of mobile electrons in electrolytic conduction.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following gases is released from combustion of a fuel in an industrial machinery causing global warming?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Carbon dioxide released by burning fuels in industrial machinery is a major greenhouse gas that traps heat in the atmosphere and causes global warming. CO, NO, and SO2 are air pollutants, but they are not the principal greenhouse gas responsible for global warming.

questions.question_text: The number of digits to the right of the decimal point denotes:

options.label: B
options.explanation: The number of digits to the right of the decimal point in a measurement denotes the decimal places. Significant figures include all reliable digits plus one uncertain digit, conversion factors relate different units, and scientific notation expresses numbers as a coefficient times a power of ten.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would occur during the formation of ions?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Inner most shell electrons are involved.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Valence electrons are shared between atoms.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The electronic configuration of an atom forming the ion remains unaffected.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Valence electrons are transferred from one atom to another.
options.explanation: Ion formation involves the transfer of valence, outermost-shell electrons from one atom to another, as when sodium gives one electron to chlorine to form Na+ and Cl-. Sharing electrons forms covalent bonds, and inner-shell electrons are not involved in normal ion formation.

questions.question_text: In order to illustrate the structure and properties of a solid, a student put hundred marble balls in to a box that representing metal cations and the empty space between and around the marble representing the electron sea. Which one of the following bonding is represented by this model?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The model of marble balls representing metal cations surrounded by a sea of delocalized electrons depicts metallic bonding, where positively charged ions are immersed in a mobile electron sea. This electron sea explains electrical conductivity and malleability, unlike covalent, ionic, or dative bonding.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains dipole-dipole force?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A type of intermolecular force that exists between non-polar molecules.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The intermolecular attraction between oppositely charged poles of nearby polar molecules.
options.explanation: Dipole-dipole forces are intermolecular attractions between the oppositely charged poles of nearby polar molecules, where the positive end of one molecule attracts the negative end of another. London dispersion forces involve temporary induced dipoles, and metallic bonding involves ions and electrons, not molecular dipoles.

options.label: C
options.option_text: An attractive force resulting from temporary dipoles induced in molecules.

options.label: D
options.option_text: An electrostatic attraction between metal ions and valence electrons.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following reactions creates energy in our bodies during respiration?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Respiration releases energy in the body by oxidizing glucose with oxygen: C6H12O6 + 6O2 → 6CO2 + 6H2O, which is an exothermic reaction. The reverse reaction is photosynthesis, fermentation produces ethanol and carbon dioxide, and the last reaction does not occur during respiration.

questions.question_text: "A reaction that involves the exchange of positive and negative ions of each reactant". This is a definition of a

options.label: C
options.explanation: A double displacement, metathesis reaction involves the exchange of positive and negative ions of each reactant, such as AgNO3 + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO3. Single displacement exchanges only one ion, combination joins reactants, and decomposition breaks one substance into simpler products.

questions.question_text: What are the four quantum numbers for an electron in a 2s orbital?

options.label: C
options.explanation: For a 2s electron, the principal quantum number n = 2, the azimuthal quantum number l = 0 for an s orbital, the magnetic quantum number ml = 0, and the spin quantum number ms = +1/2. Therefore the correct set of four quantum numbers is 2, 0, 0, +1/2.

questions.question_text: A student uses a digital balance (±0.02), a thermometer (±0.1), a measuring cylinder (±0.05), and a beaker (±0.5) during an experiment. Which of the above instrument is more precise?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The digital balance with an uncertainty of ±0.02 has the smallest absolute error among the listed instruments, making it the most precise. Precision is judged by the size of the uncertainty: the smaller the uncertainty, the more precise the measurement.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains that light has BOTH wave and particle nature?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A beam of light is a stream of particles of electromagnetic energy, with energy proportional to the observed frequency of the light.
options.explanation: Option A states that a beam of light is a stream of particles, the photons, whose energy is proportional to the observed frequency of the light, thereby combining the particle nature and the wave nature of light. The other options describe only wave behavior or electron wave properties.

options.label: B
options.option_text: An electron that is bound to the nucleus behaves like a standing wave and its position is given in terms of probability.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Microscopic systems, such as atoms and molecules can possess wave properties.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Light consists of electromagnetic waves which have an oscillating electric and magnetic disturbance that spreads electromagnetic radiation.

questions.question_text: A nuclear breakdown in which particles or electromagnetic radiation is emitted is __________.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Radioactivity is the process by which unstable atomic nuclei spontaneously break down, emitting particles such as alpha or beta rays and electromagnetic radiation such as gamma rays. The question is ambiguous because radioactive decay also describes this breakdown, but radioactivity is selected as the standard definition.

questions.question_text: Which statement describes valence shell electron pair repulsion (VSEPR) theory?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Each degenerate orbitals are occupied by a single electron before the second electrons of opposite spin enters the orbitals.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Electron pairs will be as far apart from each other in three dimensional spaces as possible.
options.explanation: VSEPR theory states that the electron pairs in the valence shell of a central atom repel one another and arrange themselves as far apart as possible in three-dimensional space to minimize repulsion, determining molecular shape. The other options describe Hund's rule, hybridization, and valence bond orbital overlap.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Atomic orbitals are capable of combining to produce new electron distribution.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A covalent bond is formed when orbitals of two atoms overlap and the overlap region is occupied by a pair of electrons.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a colorless, flammable volatile liquid and miscible with non-polar solvents?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Benzene is a colorless, flammable, volatile liquid that is nonpolar and therefore miscible with non-polar organic solvents. Ethanol and methanol are polar and miscible with water, while methane is a gas at room temperature, so benzene uniquely matches the properties described.

questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of the compound with the following structure is:[IMAGE: img_2.webp]

options.label: D
options.explanation: Applying IUPAC rules, the longest chain is selected as hexane with three methyl substituents, and numbering gives the lowest possible locant set, 2,3,4. Therefore 2,3,4-trimethylhexane is correct, while option A numbers the same molecule incorrectly. The structure image was unavailable, so this is inferred from the naming options.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following petroleum products is used as a solvent and in dry cleaning?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Petroleum ether is the light petroleum fraction used as a solvent and in dry cleaning because it evaporates quickly and dissolves oils and greases. Kerosene and diesel oil are fuels, and paraffin wax is used for candles and coatings, not as a solvent for dry cleaning.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is NOT TRUE about laboratory preparation of ethylene by dehydration of ethanol?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The collected ethylene gas in the experiment decolorizes Br₂ in CCl₄.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Concentrated sulphuric acid is used as a dehydrating agent.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Combustion of ethylene produces a non-luminous flame.
options.explanation: Ethylene, an unsaturated hydrocarbon with a high carbon content, burns with a luminous, yellow, smoky flame rather than a non-luminous one, so statement C is NOT true. The other statements are correct: ethylene decolorizes bromine water and alkaline KMnO4, and concentrated H2SO4 dehydrates ethanol.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The collected ethylene gas in the experiment decolorizes alkaline KMnO₄.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an essential nutrient of plants?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Potassium is an essential plant nutrient, needed for enzyme activation, water balance, and photosynthesis, and it is supplied through fertilizers. Aluminum, lead, and sodium are not among the essential elements required for normal plant growth and development.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the main reason for the large difference in dipole-moment between the triatomic molecules water (H₂O) and carbon dioxide (CO₂)?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The presence of lone pairs of electrons in water (H₂O) partially reinforces bond polarities.
options.explanation: Water is bent because of the lone pairs on oxygen, so its bond dipoles do not cancel and the molecule has a large net dipole moment, whereas CO2 is linear and its equal bond dipoles cancel, giving zero. Option D wrongly claims the 180-degree CO2 bonds reinforce polarity; they cancel, making A correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The higher electronegativity difference among atoms in water (H₂O) than in carbon dioxide (CO₂).

options.label: C
options.option_text: The presence of multiple bonds in carbon dioxide (CO₂) while single bonds in water.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The bonds in carbon dioxide (CO₂) are directed 180° and bond polarity reinforces each other.

questions.question_text: How many non-bonding pairs of electrons are present in the valence shell of the central atom in ClF₃?
Which one would be observed in a laboratory activity that is applied on naphthalene?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Naphthalene, a nonpolar aromatic hydrocarbon, is soluble in benzene, which is also nonpolar. It is a molecular solid with a low melting point, does not conduct electricity in the molten state, and is nearly insoluble in water, so only the benzene-solubility statement is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It conducts electricity in molten state.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It shows relatively high melting point.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is CORRECT?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Valence bond model simply shows the linkage between atoms and the presence of lone pairs.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Lewis model predicts the shapes of molecules based on electron-pair repulsions around a central atom.

options.label: C
options.option_text: In Lewis model, electrons repel one another and a pair of bonding electrons lies far apart as possible.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Valence bond model explain molecular shape from the interaction of atomic orbitals.
options.explanation: The valence bond model explains molecular shape and bonding from the interaction of atomic orbitals, that is, their overlap and hybridization. The Lewis model simply shows linkages and lone pairs, while VSEPR predicts shapes from electron-pair repulsion, so the other statements mislabel these models.

questions.question_text: The energy required to completely separate one mole of a solid ionic compound into gaseous ions is an

options.label: C
options.explanation: Lattice energy is the energy required to completely separate one mole of a solid ionic compound into its individual gaseous ions. Ionization energy removes electrons from atoms, activation energy is needed to start a reaction, and bond energy breaks a covalent bond.

questions.question_text: Which of the following compounds reacts with basic oxide to form salt and water?

options.label: A
options.explanation: An acid reacts with a basic oxide to form a salt and water, as in CaO + 2HCl → CaCl2 + H2O. An acidic oxide plus a basic oxide gives only a salt, while bases and neutral oxides do not react with basic oxides to produce salt and water.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following reaction represents formation of an acid from its salt?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Sodium nitrite, a salt, reacts with concentrated sulfuric acid to form the acid HNO3 and sodium hydrogen sulfate: NaNO2 + H2SO4 → NaHSO4 + HNO3. This preparation uses a stronger or less volatile acid to displace the desired acid from its salt.

questions.question_text: The negative logarithm of the molar concentration of hydrogen ion to the base ten is known as

options.label: A
options.explanation: pH is defined as the negative logarithm to base ten of the molar hydrogen ion concentration, pH = -log[H+]. Kw is the ionic product of water, Ka is the acid dissociation constant, and pOH is the negative logarithm of the hydroxide ion concentration.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following galvanic cell is an example of secondary cell?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The lead storage cell is a secondary, rechargeable galvanic cell whose reactions can be reversed by passing an external current through it. Daniel's cell, the Leclanche dry cell, and the zinc-carbon dry cell are primary cells that cannot be recharged.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is responsible for electrolytic conductivity?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Ions strongly held in a fixed position.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Electrons held in a fixed position.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Electrolytic conductivity results from the movement of ions through an electrolyte solution or molten salt toward the electrodes under an applied potential difference. Free electrons cause metallic conductivity, while ions or electrons held in fixed positions cannot conduct.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statement is TRUE about gases?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The particles of gases are closely packed together.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The volume of a gas is kept constant as pressure increases.

options.label: C
options.option_text: When a gas sample is heated at constant pressure, its volume decreases.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The volume of a gas is equal to the volume of its container.
options.explanation: Gases fill their containers completely, so the volume of a gas is equal to the volume of its container. Gas particles are far apart, pressure and volume are inversely related by Boyle's law, and heating a gas at constant pressure increases its volume.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following mathematical expressions is derived from the combination of Boyle's law, Charles' law and Avogadro's law?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Combining Boyle's law, V proportional to 1/P, Charles' law, V proportional to T, and Avogadro's law, V proportional to n, gives V proportional to nT/P, the ideal gas relationship. Options A and C are identical, making the question defective, and A is selected as the intended expression.

questions.question_text: 180 g of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) is allowed to react with 156 gram of hydrochloric acid (HCl), according to the following reaction. Which of the following substances is the limiting reagent? (Atomic masses; Ca=40, Cl=35.5, O=16, C=12, H=1)CaCO3+ 2HCl → CaCl2+ CO2+ H2O

options.label: B
options.explanation: Moles of CaCO3 = 180 g / 100 g/mol = 1.8 mol, which requires 2 x 1.8 = 3.6 mol of HCl. Moles of HCl available = 156 g / 36.5 g/mol = 4.27 mol, which is more than needed. Therefore calcium carbonate is consumed first and is the limiting reagent.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following isomers differs in the arrangement of carbon atoms in the longest continuous carbon chain?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Structural isomers, specifically chain isomers, differ in the arrangement of carbon atoms in the longest continuous carbon chain, such as normal butane versus 2-methylpropane. Position isomers differ in the location of a functional group, and geometric, cis-trans isomers differ in spatial arrangement.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following methods can be used in the laboratory for the preparation of alkynes?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Dehydration of alcohols with concentrated sulphuric acid.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Heating of sodium salt of an organic acid with soda lime.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Dehydrohalogenation of adjacent dihalides with sodium hydroxide.
options.explanation: Alkynes are prepared in the laboratory by dehydrohalogenation of adjacent, vicinal dihalides with an alcoholic alkali such as sodium hydroxide, eliminating two molecules of hydrogen halide. Dehydration of alcohols gives alkenes, and hydrogenation of alkenes gives alkanes, so C is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Hydrogenation of alkenes with a metal catalyst.

questions.question_text: What are the molecular formulae of an alkene and alkyne containing seven carbon atoms, respectively?

options.label: A
options.explanation: An alkene has the general formula CnH2n, so a seven-carbon alkene is C7H14. An alkyne has the general formula CnH2n-2, giving C7H12 for seven carbons. The pair C7H14 and C7H12, in that order, matches option A.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the CORRECT method of preparation of alkenes in the laboratory?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Alkylation of sodium acetylide with a primary alkyl halide.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Heating of sodium salt of an organic acid with soda lime.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Reaction of halogenated alkane with sodium.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Dehydration of alcohols with concentrated sulfuric acid.
options.explanation: Alkenes are prepared in the laboratory by dehydrating alcohols, removing a water molecule with concentrated sulfuric acid as catalyst, so ethanol gives ethene and water. Alkylation of sodium acetylide, heating sodium salts with soda lime, and the Wurtz reaction do not produce alkenes, so dehydration is correct.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the CORRECT structure of benzene?
Which of the following is the product of fractional distillation of crude oil?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Fractional distillation of crude oil separates petroleum into fractions according to boiling point, and kerosene is one of these distilled fractions. Producer gas and water gas are fuel gases made from coke, while naphthalene is an aromatic product, not a petroleum distillation fraction, so kerosene is correct.

questions.question_text: What is the molecular formula and IUPAC name of a saturated monocarboxylic acid having six carbon atoms?

options.label: C
options.explanation: A saturated monocarboxylic acid with six carbon atoms has the formula C5H11COOH because the carboxyl carbon is one of the six carbons and the alkyl chain contains five. Its IUPAC name is hexanoic acid from the six-carbon parent chain, while heptanoic acid would contain seven carbons, so C is correct.

questions.question_text: Given the following structure:[IMAGE: img_1.webp]What is the IUPAC name for the above structure?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The ester shown has a methyl group attached to the alcohol oxygen and an ethanoate group from the acid part, so its IUPAC name is methyl ethanoate, commonly called methyl acetate. Ethyl ethanoate, propyl formate, and ethyl acetate describe different ester structures, so methyl ethanoate matches the given structure.

questions.question_text: During summer, the average value for the temperature measured in a certain chemistry laboratory is 298.15 K. How many decimal places are there in the measured value?
Which of the following is the CORRECT Lewis electron -dot symbol of MgO? (Atomic number: Mg = 12 and O = 8)

options.label: D
options.explanation: Magnesium loses two electrons to form Mg2+ while oxygen gains two electrons to become O2- with eight valence electrons shown as four electron pairs. The correct Lewis symbol therefore shows the Mg2+ ion beside the O2- ion, and only option D pairs Mg2+ with the O2- ion correctly.

questions.question_text: A student collected four beakers in his/her laboratory and added some small amounts of the following: naphthalene to the first, graphite to the second, iodine to the third and alcohol to the fourth. If they added equal volume of water to each of the above beakers and shake each beaker, which of the following will be their observation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: There will be dissolution in the first three beakers.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Water will dissolve iodine rather than graphite.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Water will dissolve the whole given chemicals in the four beakers.

options.label: D
options.option_text: There will be dissolution of alcohol in the fourth beaker.
options.explanation: Naphthalene, graphite, and iodine are nonpolar or covalent-network substances that dissolve poorly or not at all in water, while alcohol is miscible with water because its hydroxyl group forms hydrogen bonds with water molecules. Therefore only the fourth beaker shows dissolution of the alcohol, matching option D.

questions.question_text: Which of the following explanations about reversible and irreversible reactions is CORRECT?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A reaction that has only a forward reaction or a reverse reaction is known as a reversible chemical reaction.

options.label: B
options.option_text: A reaction that proceeds from reactant to product and from product to reactant is known as an irreversible reaction.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Chemical reactions that proceed only towards the formation of a product are known as irreversible reactions.
options.explanation: Irreversible reactions proceed only toward the formation of products and essentially go to completion, so the statement that such reactions are irreversible is correct. Reversible reactions proceed in both directions between reactants and products and reach equilibrium, so the definitions given in the other options are reversed and incorrect.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Chemical reactions that proceed only towards the formation of a product are known as reversible reactions.

questions.question_text: Consider the following three steps:Step 1: Electrolysis of water and fractional distillation of airStep 2: Passing hot mixture of gases through a condenserStep 3: Introducing hydrogen and nitrogen gases in a chamber containing iron particles at a temperature of 300 - 500 °C and a pressure of 15 - 25 MPaWhich of the following is theCORRECTsequence involved during the industrial production of ammonia using the Haber process?

options.label: A
options.explanation: In the Haber process, hydrogen from electrolysis of water and nitrogen from fractional distillation of air are obtained first, then the hydrogen and nitrogen pass over an iron catalyst at 300-500 degrees C and high pressure, and finally the hot gas mixture is condensed. The sequence is Step 1, Step 3, Step 2.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a physical property of nitric acid, HNO3?

options.label: A
options.option_text: On exposure to light, it turns brown.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Nitric acid is a corrosive chemical.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Nitric acid has a pungent smell.
options.explanation: A pungent smell is an odor, which is a physical property observed without changing the chemical identity of nitric acid. Turning brown on exposure to light involves decomposition to nitrogen dioxide, being corrosive reflects chemical reactivity, and forming many salts is chemical behavior, so the pungent smell is the physical property.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It forms large number of salts.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the CORRECT explanation about herbicides?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Selective herbicides control specific weed species, leaving the desired crop unharmed.
options.explanation: Selective herbicides kill specific weed species while leaving the desired crop unharmed, which correctly describes their action. Organochlorine compounds are not the most common herbicides, herbicides control weeds rather than insects, and they suppress rather than enhance plant growth, so option A is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Organochlorine compounds are the most common herbicide substances.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Herbicides are substances that are used to control unwanted insects.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Herbicides are substances that are used to enhance the growth of important plants.

questions.question_text: A student collected the following information from the community on the preparation of the local alcoholic drink "ARAKI":Step 1: Distillation of the liquid mixture in traditional waysStep 2: Adding a proportional amount of water to liquidity the tick dough - like mixture and leaving for 1-2 days for further fermentationStep 3: "Bikel" preparation from barely, the starter ("Tinsess") preparation by mixing the Bikel with Gesho (Rhamunspronoides) powder and fermentation of the starter for few daysStep 4: Baking of bread from different ingredients and breaking down the bread and mixing with the fermented starter and leaving for fermentation for couple of daysWhich of the following is the correct procedure for the preparation of Araki?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The correct Araki procedure prepares the Bikel starter with Tinsess, then bakes bread and mixes it with the fermented starter, adds water and allows further fermentation for one to two days, and finally distils the liquid mixture. This sequence is Step 3, Step 4, Step 2, Step 1.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following synthetic polymers is used to make squeeze bottles, plastic wrapping and electrical insulation?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Polyethylene is a tough, flexible addition polymer used for squeeze bottles, plastic wrapping films, and electrical insulation because it is a good electrical insulator and easy to mould. Polypropylene, polymethyl methacrylate, and polyvinyl chloride are used for different applications, so polyethylene is the correct choice.

questions.question_text: Which of the following descriptions of the property of a covalent compound is CORRECT?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Covalent compounds have low melting and boiling points.
options.explanation: Covalent compounds are held together by weak intermolecular forces between molecules, so they generally have low melting and boiling points. Most are gases, liquids, or low-melting solids at room temperature, are often insoluble in water, and are volatile, so the statement about low melting and boiling points is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Most covalent compounds are solids at room temperature.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Most covalent compounds are soluble in water.

questions.question_text: The attractive force between molecules is known as _________.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Intermolecular forces are the attractive forces acting between molecules, including dipole-dipole attractions, London dispersion forces, and hydrogen bonding. Nuclear forces act inside the nucleus, lattice forces hold ions in crystals, and intramolecular forces act within a single molecule, so intermolecular force is the correct term.

questions.question_text: The hybridization of the central atom xenon (Xe) in xenon tetraflouride, XeF4, is sp3d2. Which of the following is the shape of XeF4?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Xenon tetrafluoride has sp3d2 hybridization with six electron pairs around xenon, four bonding and two lone pairs. The two lone pairs occupy opposite axial positions of the octahedral arrangement, leaving the four fluorine atoms in one plane, producing a square-planar shape rather than octahedral, tetrahedral, or seesaw.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the CORRECT electron configuration of a peroxide ion, O22-?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The peroxide ion O22- contains 18 electrons. In the molecular-orbital configuration the sigma and pi bonding levels are filled, and the final two electrons occupy the highest antibonding sigma orbital, so the correct configuration ends with the sigma-star level holding two electrons. Options A and C carry identical texts, so A is selected.

questions.question_text: Consider the following reaction between nitrogen (N2) and oxygen (O2):N2(g) + O2(g) → 2NO(g)If the rate of disappearance of N2is 2.5 x 10-6M/s, what is the rate of reaction for the formation of NO?

options.label: A
options.explanation: For the reaction N2 + O2 = 2NO, two moles of NO are formed for every mole of N2 consumed. If nitrogen disappears at 2.5 x 10-6 M/s, the rate of NO formation is twice that value, 2 x 2.5 x 10-6 = 5.0 x 10-6 M/s, matching option A.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a Lewis acid?

options.label: C
options.explanation: A Lewis acid is a species that accepts an electron pair. Boron trifluoride, BF3, has an incomplete octet on boron and readily accepts a lone pair, so it is a Lewis acid. Sulfate, sulfite, and ammonia have complete octets and can donate electrons, making them Lewis bases, so BF3 is correct.

questions.question_text: The pH of a 0.10 M solution of an aqueous solution of a certain acid is 3. What is the value of acid ionization constant (Ka) of this acid?

options.label: B
options.explanation: From pH 3 the hydrogen-ion concentration is 1.0 x 10-3 M. For a weak acid, Ka equals the hydrogen-ion concentration squared divided by the acid concentration, Ka = (1.0 x 10-3)2 / 0.10 = 1.0 x 10-6 / 0.10 = 1.0 x 10-5, matching option B.

questions.question_text: The shift in the position of equilibrium caused by the addition of an ion already involved in the reaction is known as _________.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The common-ion effect is the shift in the position of equilibrium caused by adding an ion already present in the reaction, such as adding acetate ion to a solution of acetic acid. This addition suppresses ionization of the weak acid, so the correct term is the common-ion effect.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is CORRECT about equivalents of acids and bases?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The volume of an acid or base required to reach equivalence point during acid-base titration reaction.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The number of moles of an acid or base required to form a one molar aqueous acidic or basic solution.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is the amount of a substance that is required to react with one mole of hydroxide ions in redox reactions.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is the amount of a substance that is required to react with one mole of hydrogen ions in acid-base reactions.
options.explanation: An equivalent of an acid or base is the amount of substance that reacts with one mole of hydrogen ions, H+, in an acid-base reaction. For a base it is the amount reacting with one mole of hydroxide ions. Definitions involving equivalence-point volume, molarity, and redox reactions are not correct, so D is chosen.

questions.question_text: A 250 mL solution is formed from 24.5 g of sulfuric acid (H2SO4). What is the normality of this solution? (Mol. wt. H2SO4= 98 g/mol)

options.label: B
options.explanation: The moles of sulfuric acid are 24.5 g divided by 98 g/mol, giving 0.25 mol. Since H2SO4 furnishes two hydrogen ions per molecule, the equivalents are 0.25 mol x 2 = 0.50 equivalents. Normality equals equivalents divided by volume in liters, 0.50 / 0.25 L = 2.00 N, matching option B.

questions.question_text: Which of the following reaction is used for the preparation of bases?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Reaction of metal hydroxides with dilute acids.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Reaction of active metal oxides with water
options.explanation: Bases can be prepared by reacting active metal oxides with water, for example calcium oxide reacting with water to form calcium hydroxide, a typical base. Reactions of metal hydroxides with acids, heating salts with non-volatile acids, and heating carbonates with acids form salts rather than bases, so B is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Heating of a salt with a non-volatile acid.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Heating of carbonates with dilute acids.

questions.question_text: Which of the following salts is used in the treatment of waste water?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ferric chloride, FeCl3, is commonly added to waste water to coagulate suspended particles and help remove impurities, so it is used in waste-water treatment. Calcium carbonate, barium sulfate, and potassium nitrate do not serve this coagulation purpose, making FeCl3 the correct answer.

questions.question_text: A student prepared two beakers, each containing 100 mL of water. The student dissolved 10 mL of concentrated HCl in the first beaker and 10 mL of concentrated CH3COOH in the second beaker, which of the following would occur in the solution?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In the first beaker, a large fraction of HCl dissociates into ions and in the second beaker, a small fraction of CH3COOH dissociates into ions.
options.explanation: Hydrochloric acid is a strong acid, so a large fraction of HCl molecules dissociate into hydrogen and chloride ions in water. Acetic acid is a weak acid, so only a small fraction of CH3COOH molecules ionize. Therefore the first beaker shows extensive dissociation while the second shows very little.

options.label: B
options.option_text: In the first beaker, a small fraction of HCl dissociates into ions and in the second beaker, a large fraction of CH3COOH dissociates into ions.

options.label: C
options.option_text: There is no dissociation or ionization of the HCl and CH3COOH in both the first and second beakers.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The amount of HCl dissociated in the first beaker and the amount of CH3COOH dissociated in the second beaker are identical.

questions.question_text: Consider the following five-steps during the extraction of aluminum from its bauxite ore by the Hall process:I. Treating the mixture of an aqueous solution of sodium silicate and aluminate with an acidII. Heating aluminum oxide strongly in a furnaceIII. Heating the ore with sodium hydroxide solutionIV Conversion of aluminum oxide to soluble sodium aluminateV. Electrolysis of molten mixture of cryolite and aluminum oxideWhich of the following is the CORRECT sequence of production?

options.label: A
options.option_text: III, IV, I, II and V
options.explanation: In the Hall process the bauxite ore is first heated with sodium hydroxide to form soluble sodium aluminate, the aluminate solution is then treated with acid to precipitate aluminum hydroxide, which is heated strongly to give pure alumina, and finally the molten alumina-cryolite mixture is electrolyzed. The sequence is III, IV, I, II, V.

options.label: B
options.option_text: IV, II, I, III and V

options.label: C
options.option_text: V, I, II, IV and III

options.label: D
options.option_text: II, I, III, IV and V

questions.question_text: Which of the following food preservation methods leaves a product without loss of aroma or flavor?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Freeze-drying removes water by sublimation directly from the frozen product at low temperature and pressure, preserving aroma and flavor because delicate volatile compounds are not destroyed by heat. Vacuum-packing, freezing, and melting do not protect flavor as effectively, so freeze-drying is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: The electronic configuration of an element in the periodic table is 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d104p5. In which block does this element belong?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The electron configuration ends in 4p5, meaning the highest occupied subshell is a p subshell. Elements whose last electrons enter a p subshell belong to the p-block of the periodic table. Since the configuration is neither s, d, nor f block, the element lies in the p-block.

questions.question_text: Consider the following chart of general periodic properties in the periodic table.[IMAGE: img_2.webp]From the given periodic properties, which one CORRECTLY agrees with the periodic trend in the chart?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The chart displays a periodic property that decreases across a period from left to right. Atomic radius decreases across a period as effective nuclear charge increases and pulls the electrons closer to the nucleus, so the trend in the chart agrees with atomic radius. Electronegativity, electron affinity, and ionization energy all increase across a period.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is CORRECT about the formation of a covalent bond? A covalent bond is formed

options.label: A
options.option_text: between positively and negatively charged ions.

options.label: C
options.option_text: by the sharing of valence electrons.
options.explanation: A covalent bond forms when two non-metal atoms share one or more pairs of valence electrons, allowing each atom to achieve a stable electron configuration. Transferring electrons produces ionic bonds, while the other choices describe metallic behavior or nonsense, so the sharing of valence electrons is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: by the transfer of valence electrons.

questions.question_text: The molecule of carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) has four polar (C - Cl) bonds. However, CCl4is a non-polar molecule. Which of the following explains the reason for the observed property of CCl4?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The molecule is non-polar because of the presence of four polar C-Cl bonds in the molecule.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The molecule is non-polar because of the difference in electronegativity between carbon and chlorine.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Even though the bond in CCl4is polar, the net dipole moment of the molecule is different from zero.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Even though the bond in CCl4is polar, the net dipole moment of the molecule is zero.
options.explanation: Carbon tetrachloride has four polar carbon-chlorine bonds arranged tetrahedrally around the carbon atom. The bond dipoles are symmetrically arranged and cancel one another, so the net dipole moment of the molecule is zero and the molecule is non-polar. This explains why CCl4 is non-polar despite having polar bonds.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is responsible for the unusual high boiling points of HF, H2O and NH3?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hydrogen bonding occurs between molecules in which hydrogen is bonded to fluorine, oxygen, or nitrogen. HF, H2O, and NH3 all form hydrogen bonds between their molecules, which are much stronger than ordinary intermolecular forces and raise their boiling points unusually high compared with similar compounds, so hydrogen bonding is correct.

questions.question_text: From the assumption of kinetic molecular theory of gases, which of the following is CORRECT?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The pressure of a gas is the effect of the negligible volume of the gas compared to the total volume of the gas.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The average kinetic energy of gas particles is inversely proportional to the absolute temperature of the gas.

options.label: C
options.option_text: There are some forces of attraction or repulsion between gas particles.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Under ordinary conditions, the total volume of gas molecules is much smaller than the total volume of gas.
options.explanation: Kinetic molecular theory assumes gas molecules have negligible volume compared with the container, so under ordinary conditions the total volume of the molecules is much smaller than the total volume of the gas. Pressure arises from collisions, kinetic energy is proportional to absolute temperature, and no forces act between ideal gas particles.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is CORRECT about the phase change observed in water?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Water starts to evaporate at the boiling point and condenses at the melting point.

options.label: B
options.option_text: When a solid ice is heated, it is changed to liquid water without melting.

options.label: C
options.option_text: At the boiling point temperature, water exists in three different physical states.

options.label: D
options.option_text: At the melting point of ice, the temperature remains constant.
options.explanation: At the melting point of ice, heat energy is used to break the solid lattice rather than to raise the temperature, so the temperature remains constant while melting occurs. Evaporation is not restricted to the boiling point, ice cannot change to water without melting, and water does not exist in three states at the boiling point.

questions.question_text: Given the symbols of the three subatomic particles; electrons (e-), protons (p+) and neutrons (n0), which of the following is the CORRECT comparison of the absolute masses of protons, electrons and neutrons?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Mass of e-> mass of p+= mass of n0

options.label: B
options.option_text: Mass of e-= mass of p+> mass of n0

options.label: C
options.option_text: Mass of e-< mass of p+< mass of n0
options.explanation: Electrons are far lighter than protons, while protons and neutrons have nearly equal mass with the neutron slightly heavier than the proton. Therefore the correct order of absolute masses is electron mass less than proton mass less than neutron mass, matching option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Mass of e-> mass of p+> mass of n0

questions.question_text: In the modern periodic table, what is the name of the group that contains the most electronegative elements?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The halogens, group 17 of the periodic table, are the most electronegative elements, with fluorine being the most electronegative of all elements. Alkali metals, chalcogens, and noble gases have lower electronegativity values, so the group containing the most electronegative elements is the halogens.

questions.question_text: A given element has atomic number of 55 and mass number of 133. Which of the following describes CORRECTLY the property of this element?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The non-metallic character of the element is high.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The metallic character of the element is high.
options.explanation: An element with atomic number 55 and mass number 133 is caesium, a group 1 alkali metal.
