questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about different alternatives of conflict management?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Arbitration applies legal principles within the limits agreed upon by parties.
options.explanation: Arbitration is a binding process in which a neutral third party applies legal principles within limits agreed by the disputing parties. Litigation occurs in courts (B is false), negotiation involves direct discussion (C is false), and mediation is non-binding (D is false).

options.label: B
options.option_text: Litigation is a resolution that is conducted outside of the courts.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Negotiation involves indirect discussion between the disputing parties.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Mediation is a binding dispute resolution involving a neutral third party.

questions.question_text: The accused person has the right to get trials within the time specified by law and open place unless the case is related with national security and for the purpose of personal security of the alleged. This is referred as

options.label: B
options.explanation: Speedy and public trial means the accused is tried within the time fixed by law in an open court, except where national security or the safety of the accused requires otherwise. Presumption of innocence, habeas corpus and an impartial tribunal are related but different rights, so B is correct.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains best the struggles of the Ethiopian people to overthrow the Derg regime?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It was highly influenced by the successes of first Woyane Movement in Tigray and other peasant rebellions in the nation.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Derg government resigned from power voluntarily after it was convinced that people of the nation were not supporting it.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It was accompanied by the establishment of many political parties and the struggles of the people all over the nation.
options.explanation: The struggle to overthrow the Derg involved the establishment of many political parties and broad-based struggles of the people across the nation. It was not solely a TPLF and EPLF affair (D), not merely influenced by the first Woyane (A), and the Derg certainly did not resign voluntarily (B).

options.label: D
options.option_text: It was solely owned by the fighters of TPLF in Tigray and EPLF in Eritrea and Victory is attributed to them.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is among the basic advantages of cultural relativism?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It allows minority people to advance their culture to replace the dominant ones.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It creates conflicts of interest among the different cultures of the nation.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It gives an opportunity to people to enjoy their culture without restriction.
options.explanation: Cultural relativism holds that each culture should be understood and appreciated on its own terms, giving people the freedom to enjoy their culture without restriction. Options A, B and D describe domination, conflict and oppression, which contradict the tolerant, respectful nature of cultural relativism in a diverse society.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It allows dominant cultures to people enjoy to preserve their identity by oppressing others.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is WRONG about the concepts of justice and equity in a given society?

options.label: A
options.option_text: We can rationalize and justify the excessive benefit of some part of society through justice and equity.
options.explanation: Justice and equity cannot justify the excessive benefit of one part of society at the expense of others; that is the opposite of fairness. B, C and D correctly describe justice as correcting wrongs, governing relations between government and people, and equity as correcting unbalanced distribution, so A is the wrong statement.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Justice is fairness that are intended to correct some wrong or advance goodness.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Justice involves the relationship between government and the people and within the people.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Equity refers to the basic principles that use to correct unbalanced relationships and distribution of resources.

questions.question_text: Mr. Benjamin who acquires Ethiopian citizenships by naturalization can be

options.label: A
options.option_text: acquires the citizenship of another country.
options.explanation: Under Ethiopian nationality law, a person who acquired Ethiopian citizenship by naturalization may later acquire the citizenship of another country, which leads to the loss or renunciation of Ethiopian nationality, since dual citizenship is not permitted. Options B, C and D are absurd personal acts unrelated to citizenship law.

questions.question_text: While you are walking you observe the police woman beating a young boy. You intended to mediate them and advise her to bring the boy into the police station. The police woman turned into you and warned to go away 'since it is none of your business', otherwise you will be subjected to be a 'criminal'. Then you believed that indeed it is none of your business.

options.label: A
options.option_text: You were insensitive about the phenomena at all.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The young man was criminal and it was a right response to his crime.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The police woman is sensitive of injustice and doing her job.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Your sensitivity to injustice gradually waned away because of fear.
options.explanation: The bystander's sensitivity to injustice waned away because of the policewoman's threats, showing how fear can weaken moral sensitivity. Options A, B and C are wrong: the bystander was not insensitive from the start, the beating was not justified, and the policewoman's behaviour was not a fair response.

questions.question_text: An individual who has claimed the right to refuse to perform active military service on the grounds of freedom of thought, conscience, or religion is referred to as

options.label: A
options.explanation: A conscientious objector is a person who refuses to perform active military service on grounds of freedom of thought, conscience or religion. A whistle blower exposes wrongdoing, treason is betraying one's country, and arbitrary rule is government without law, so A is the correct term.

questions.question_text: The Ethiopian patriotic woman who made an extraordinary contribution in the second Italo-Ethiopian war by providing information, food, medicine, bullets, guns and clothes to Ethiopian fighters was

options.label: B
options.explanation: Shewareged Gedle was the patriotic woman who raised funds, collected and supplied information, food, medicine, clothes, bullets and guns to Ethiopian fighters during the second Italo-Ethiopian war and the occupation. Taitu Bitul, Asgedeech Assefa and Bati Dil Wonbera do not match the described contribution.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following sets represents dispositions which enhance the citizens' effectiveness in public participation?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Commitment, team spirit and dedication are dispositions that make citizens effective in public participation. Pride, cowardice and praise (A), self-interest, profit and rewards (C), and punishment, rewards and praise (D) centre on personal gain or fear, which weaken genuine commitment to collective civic engagement.

questions.question_text: Wisdom is the highest form of knowledge that has direct significance for private and public life. Which one of the following is a major benefit of wisdom?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It detaches one from the activities of life

options.label: B
options.explanation: The major benefit of wisdom is that it enhances reasoning and morality, enabling people to make sound and ethical decisions in private and public life. Options A, C and D claim wisdom detaches us from life or boosts only emotions and passion, which misrepresents wisdom's rational and moral value.

questions.question_text: How can we develop our reading habits?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Reading habits are developed by reading different texts repeatedly and regularly, which builds familiarity and interest in reading. Visiting nature, watching movies and talking with readers may be enjoyable, but only consistent practice of reading itself develops the habit, so A is correct.

questions.question_text: What is the major role of the judiciary in a presidential system?

options.label: D
options.explanation: In a presidential system the judiciary interprets the constitutionality of laws, reviewing whether legislation and executive acts comply with the constitution. Legislating, amending the constitution and counterbalancing the law are not the judiciary's functions, so D correctly identifies its major role.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about citizens' rights and obligations in a democratic system?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Rights and obligations have no relevance to a democratic system.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Rights and obligations coexist in the overall personality of citizens.
options.explanation: In a democratic system rights and obligations coexist within the overall personality of citizens; one cannot enjoy rights without fulfilling duties. Options A, C and D wrongly claim rights and obligations are irrelevant, demand rewards, or can exist separately, all of which contradict the balanced nature of democratic citizenship.

options.label: C
options.option_text: For each obligation to fulfill, citizens ask for rewards from the government.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Rights and obligations are contradictory and one can exist without the other.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains better the difference between the 1987 constitution of the Derg and the previous two imperial constitutions?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Since all the constitutions were enacted by despotic rulers, they were identical with each other.

options.label: B
options.option_text: While the constitution of Derg states that power is resided in the working people, the previous constitutions legalized the emperor's power.
options.explanation: The 1987 Derg constitution declared that power resides in the working people, whereas the previous imperial constitutions legalised the absolute power of the emperor. A wrongly treats them as identical, C mislabels their values, and D reverses which documents were ratified by representatives, so B best captures the difference.

options.label: C
options.option_text: While the 1987 constitution emphasizes the social democratic values, the previous constitutions emphasized liberal democratic values.

options.label: D
options.option_text: While the previous constitutions were ratified by the people's representatives, the 1987 constitution was written by few officials.

questions.question_text: What does the term "summary execution" It refers to

options.label: A
options.option_text: a death sentence against a person is carried out without fair and normal judicial system
options.explanation: Summary execution means a death sentence is carried out against a person without a fair and normal judicial process, in violation of due process of law. Options B, C and D describe lawful sentencing, commutation, or imprisonment, which are the opposite of the arbitrary killing that summary execution involves.

options.label: B
options.option_text: a death sentence decided on a person found guilty of a serious crime is committed to life in prison

options.label: C
options.option_text: a death sentence against a person is carried out based on due process of law.

options.label: D
options.option_text: a person found guilty is assumed a punishment of life imprisonment by legal court.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements demonstrates language equality?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Allowing equal opportunity is instrumental in developing and using one's own language.
options.explanation: Language equality is demonstrated when all citizens have equal opportunity to develop and use their own language. Options B and C would impose one language on everyone, while D describes a consequence of equality rather than a demonstration of it, making A the statement that best demonstrates language equality.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The language which is spoken by the majority shall be used by all citizens.

options.label: C
options.option_text: One's language must be the language of communication in a multi-ethnic state.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The respect of language equality is an assurance to the overall respect of human rights.

questions.question_text: Displacement of peasants from their own plots of land, while land lords possessed large farmlands in the history of Ethiopia demonstrates that

options.label: A
options.option_text: lack of equality to social respect.

options.label: B
options.option_text: lack of equality to rule and be ruled.

options.label: C
options.option_text: lack of equality of access to natural resources.
options.explanation: Peasants losing their plots while landlords held vast farmlands demonstrates lack of equality of access to natural resources, especially land. Options A, B and D describe social respect, political equality and cultural equality, but the core injustice here is unequal access to land as a natural resource.

options.label: D
options.option_text: lack of cultural equality in the society.

questions.question_text: The idea of a 'National Consensus' refers to the political phenomena when

options.label: A
options.option_text: the majority suppress the rights of minority in the nation.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the minority have little say on national affairs.

options.label: C
options.option_text: few decide on behalf of the majority on political affairs.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the possibility of agreement on basic state affairs.
options.explanation: National consensus refers to the possibility of agreement among the people on basic state affairs, such as the constitution and fundamental national values. Options A, B and C describe suppression, marginalisation and minority rule, which are the opposite of the inclusive agreement that consensus requires.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following alternatives represents a universal indicator of development?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Reducing the poverty of the people, assuring food security, high infant mortality rate and less life expectancy.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Lower life expectancy, higher infant mortality rate, reducing income of the people and higher national GDP.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Positive change in the material and spiritual life, less infant mortality rate, eradication of poverty and improved income of the people, and increased GDP.
options.explanation: Universal indicators of development include positive material and spiritual change, lower infant mortality, eradication of poverty, improved income and increased GDP. Options A, B and D wrongly include negative indicators such as high infant mortality, low life expectancy, food insecurity and social conflict, which signal underdevelopment.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Economic growth, lack of food security, advancement in social conflict, increased national GDP, and improved income of the people.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following reveals absence of fairness in taxation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Taxation is economic issue than the issue of justice and fairness.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Tax payers are free to determine the amount of their incomes.
options.explanation: Fairness in taxation requires that taxable income be assessed honestly and lawfully; allowing taxpayers to determine their own incomes obviously removes fairness. Option A wrongly separates taxation from justice, C is about comparing oneself with others, and D actually describes lawful tax collection, so B reveals absence of fairness.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The tax payers are comparing him with others.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The tax collector works according to the laws than the tax payers.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following alternatives describes best the positive or negative consequences of executing our responsibilities?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Punishment and rewards are not linked with the responses for out of execution of responsibilities rather they are legal measures.

options.label: B
options.option_text: If we take our responsibilities well, then we can be rewarded in the society and trusted by the public to be given greater responsibilities in the future.
options.explanation: Executing our responsibilities well brings positive consequences such as social reward, public trust and greater responsibility in the future, while failure may bring punishment. Options A, C and D wrongly disconnect rewards and punishment from how well responsibilities are carried out, so B describes the consequences best.

options.label: C
options.option_text: If one executes his/her responsibility, negligently, then the punishment or reward may not be the consequences of such responsibility.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Failing to be responsible doesn't necessarily lead to punishment and fulfilling one's responsibility often results in punishment.

questions.question_text: Mr.Jemane is known for his unserved responsibility for protecting public property. What can be the contributions of responsible persons like Mr.Jemane?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Accumulating personal wealth by using public property.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Ignoring the environment and denying of public property.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Overcoming wastage of public property and protecting the environment.
options.explanation: Responsible persons who protect public property contribute by overcoming wastage of public property and protecting the environment. Options A, B and D describe misusing public property, ignoring the environment, and sacrificing public interest for personal goals, all of which are irresponsible and harmful to the community.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Compromising public interest for the actualization of personal goals.

questions.question_text: How can we develop our professional skills at work place?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By leaving much of the work for others.

options.label: B
options.option_text: By working in harmony with others.
options.explanation: Professional skills at the workplace are developed by working in harmony with others, which encourages cooperation, learning and shared growth. Leaving work for others, trusting only one's own capacity, and acting on moods all prevent learning and teamwork, so B is the correct way to develop professional skills.

options.label: D
options.option_text: By acting according one's moods in the work place.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the correct sequence in the decision making process?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Identifying the problem, thinking possible solutions, leaving the opinions of others aside, identifying the outcomes, practicing the decision and evaluating the success or failure.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Identifying the problem, thinking possible solutions, identifying the alternatives, identifying the outcomes, writing the decision, and evaluating the success or failure.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Identifying the problem, thinking possible solutions, choosing best alternatives, identifying the outcomes, practicing the decision and evaluating the success or failure.
options.explanation: The correct sequence in decision making is identifying the problem, thinking of possible solutions, choosing the best alternative, identifying the outcomes, practising the decision, and evaluating success or failure. Options A, B and D break this sequence by ignoring alternatives, avoiding evaluation, or submitting to others' ideas.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Identifying the problem, abiding to the ideas of others, choosing best alternatives, identifying the outcomes, practicing the decision and evaluating the success or failure.

questions.question_text: Ato Mekasha is known for his effective use of resources and saving culture. What is the basic characteristic of persons like Mekasha?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Identifying and budgeting priority needs and minimizing extravagant practices at home.
options.explanation: A person with an effective saving culture identifies and budgets priority needs while minimising extravagant practices at home. Option C overstates saving by compromising present needs, B wrongly labels saving as stinginess, and D wrongly rejects all entertainment, so A best characterises balanced, effective saving behaviour.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Mekasha is stingy and his manner of life cannot be a role model in the society.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Keeping something for the future by compromising the needs of the present.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Avoiding any possibility of entertainment and related expenses for the purpose of saving.

questions.question_text: To develop the habit of saving the ideal instrument is

options.label: A
options.option_text: being committed to the norms of luxurious life in the big cities

options.label: B
options.option_text: being negligent to the real factual capacities and limits of one's income

options.label: C
options.option_text: knowing the life styles of one's neighbors and peer influence

options.label: D
options.option_text: knowing the balance between one's income and basic needs
options.explanation: The ideal instrument for developing a saving habit is knowing the balance between one's income and basic needs, which allows realistic budgeting of what can be saved. Committing to luxurious living, ignoring income limits, and following neighbours' lifestyles all undermine saving, so D is correct.

questions.question_text: If Abdissa and his colleagues want to organize a civil society, what will be the primary issue they should take into account?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The ethnic identity of their members

options.label: B
options.option_text: The worth of their civil society in the country
options.explanation: When organising a civil society, the primary consideration is the worth of the organisation to the country, namely its contribution to public good. Ethnic identity, political ideology and profitability are secondary or inappropriate, so B is the primary issue the founders should take into account.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The strength of their political ideology

options.label: D
options.option_text: The profitability of their civil society

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is best definition of community participation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Registered business organizations that contribute to the success of their companies.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The participation of members of any society which highly deteriorates the common good.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Engagement of individuals as members of different associations in political, economic and social activities.
options.explanation: Community participation is the engagement of individuals as members of different associations in political, economic and social activities. Options A, B and D wrongly restrict it to registered businesses, claim it harms the common good, or reduce it to seeking political power, so C gives the best definition.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The successful engagement of civil societies to assume political power through election.

questions.question_text: How can countries in the Nile Basin insure equitable use of the natural resource related to the river?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Equitable use of the River Nile's resources among basin countries can be ensured through peaceful cooperation and negotiation based on fairness and mutual benefit. Deciding not to use the river, deciding by majority vote, or relying only on historical records do not ensure equitable sharing, so A is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: By deciding not to make use of it at all.

options.label: C
options.option_text: By deciding based on majority vote

questions.question_text: One can imagine that hard work is one of the foundations of civilization in the world. How can hard work positively influence world civilization?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By ignoring tradition and advancing modernity

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hard work positively influences world civilisation through invention and discovery, which drive progress and the advancement of knowledge. Ignoring tradition, promoting globalisation, or cultivating foreign culture are not direct results of hard work, so B best expresses how diligence shapes civilisation.

options.label: C
options.option_text: By advancing the possibility of globalization

questions.question_text: The independence of developing nations like Ethiopia from the influence of developed nations can be actualized through

options.label: A
options.option_text: migration of citizens to developed nations

options.label: D
options.explanation: The independence of developing nations from the influence of developed countries is actualised through the contributions of self-reliant citizens who reduce dependency. Migration, accepting donations from superpowers, and dependence on others all increase reliance on foreign powers, so D correctly answers the question.

questions.question_text: Charlotte Gilman (1860-1935) is a well-known feminist who argued about the economic independence of women and wrote a book 'Women and Economics'. What was her contribution for the empowerment of women?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The economic freedom of women from their husbands' income, a mechanism of allowing to use 30% of their husbands' income.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The impossibility of the freedom of women from men unless they are engaged in armed struggles against men.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The separation of women and men and independence of women where women can support themselves without cooperation with men.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The possibility of women being independent from household affairs and promoting the engagement of women in income generating activities.
options.explanation: Charlotte Gilman's contribution to women's empowerment was showing that women can be independent of household affairs by engaging in income-generating activities, thereby achieving economic independence. Options A, B and C misrepresent her ideas, which were about peaceful economic empowerment, not armed struggle or complete separation from men.

questions.question_text: "When we evaluate human acts or practices, we consider neither the nature of acts or practices nor the motive for which people do what they do, but the consequences of their acts and practices." This is the central idea of

options.label: B
options.explanation: Judging acts only by their consequences, ignoring the nature of the act and the motive, is the central idea of utilitarian moral theory, which evaluates actions by their results and the greatest good. Divine command, Kant's rights approach and virtue theory focus on duty, rights or character, not consequences, so B is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Kant's rights approach of moral theory

questions.question_text: How can we characterize the interplay between rule of law, constitution and a constitutional culture?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Rule of law and constitutional culture are mutually exclusive.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Rule of law and a constitutional culture have reciprocal relations.
options.explanation: Rule of law and constitutional culture have reciprocal relations: a constitutional culture supports the rule of law, which in turn deepens constitutionalism. A wrongly calls them mutually exclusive, C wrongly makes one a precondition of the other, and D wrongly makes a written constitution a precondition of rule of law, so B is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Rule of law must be a prerequisite for constitutional culture.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A written Constitution is a precondition for the rule of law.

questions.question_text: A body which is set up by a mutual agreement of states to deal with foreign relations to maintain constant official contacts and to facilitate inter relationships among states referred to as

options.label: D
options.explanation: A diplomatic mission is a body established by the mutual agreement of states to conduct foreign relations, maintain constant official contacts and facilitate inter-state relationships. Diplomatic aggression, manipulation and arbitration are not bodies established for constant official contact, so D is the correct term.

questions.question_text: Mr. Mohammed is a licensed accountant and auditor in firm X. He found an imbalance of income and expenses. Furthermore, there were cases of tax fraud committed by the firm. This case demonstrates form of corruption which is potentially committed by the firm namely

options.label: D
options.explanation: An accountant discovering imbalances and tax fraud committed by the firm illustrates embezzlement, the misappropriation of funds or property, here tax money withheld from the state. Favouritism and nepotism involve preferences to relatives or friends, and bribery involves giving or receiving bribes, so D is the closest match.

questions.question_text: If you are a candidate for the House of People's Representatives in the national election of Ethiopia, which one of the following is a primary requirement for you to qualify as the best candidate?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The best candidate for the House of Peoples' Representatives should be judged primarily by their political philosophy and policies, which guide how they will serve the people. Appearance, the number of friends, and commitment to totalitarian rule are irrelevant or disqualifying, so B is the primary requirement.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Number of friends and supporters in your locality

options.label: D
options.option_text: Your commitment to a totalitarian rule

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about the constitutional base of gender equality in present day Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The constitution has no role in sex since it is natural.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Constitutional base prioritizes gender equality over sex.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The constitution determines gender for nationals.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The FDRE Constitution recognises gender equality, providing that women and men enjoy equal rights and prohibiting discrimination on grounds of sex. Options A, B and C wrongly claim the constitution ignores sex, prioritises gender equality over sex, or determines gender, so D correctly states the constitutional position.

questions.question_text: Mr. Habtamu is one of the self-reliant managers of organizations. Which one of the following are characteristic features of Mr. Habtamu in decision making about organizational affairs?

options.label: A
options.option_text: He is often one of the overconfident managers.

options.label: B
options.option_text: He commits errors but doesn't feel ashamed.

options.label: C
options.option_text: He makes decisions based on facts, experience and teamwork.
options.explanation: A self-reliant manager makes decisions based on facts, experience and teamwork, combining reliable information with consultation. Being overconfident, unashamed of errors, or avoiding criticism all contradict self-reliance, which requires objectivity, learning from mistakes and openness to feedback, so C is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: He refrains from self-criticisms and criticisms from others.

questions.question_text: One needs to be open-minded in the discussions or debates with others. Open-mindedness is about

options.label: A
options.option_text: being finds reasons to explain your behavior to offend others

options.label: B
options.option_text: being ready to listen and consider the ideas and arguments of others
options.explanation: Open-mindedness means being ready to listen to and consider the ideas and arguments of others, even when they differ from one's own. Justifying behaviour that offends others, doing whatever others want, and disapproving of others' opinions all contradict genuine open-mindedness, so B is the correct description.

options.label: C
options.option_text: a person who can be relied on to do whatever you want

options.label: D
options.option_text: the act of showing the disapproval of the opinions of others.

questions.question_text: Some people say that they do not need to save and think about the future. Most people in Ethiopia think like that and this negatively affects their saving. This is one of the effects of

options.label: D
options.explanation: Believing that there is no need to save and plan for the future is a consequence of religious dogmatism, which discourages forward-looking economic behaviour. Self-reliance, religious virtue and self-confidence actually encourage responsibility and saving, so D correctly identifies the cause of the negative attitude toward saving.

questions.question_text: An act of influencing policies and opinions on particular issues like environmental protection, rights of females, children rights and equality is known as

options.label: C
options.explanation: Influencing policies and public opinion on issues such as environmental protection, women's and children's rights and equality is known as lobbying. Discrimination, public rebellion and public unrest do not describe organised advocacy for policy change, so C is the correct term for this activity.

questions.question_text: Kiberwosen is a member in her village's iddir. She is also a candidate of election for the House of People's Representatives in the forthcoming election representing one of the competing parties. What is the nature of Kiberwosen's community participation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is both a social and a political participation.
options.explanation: Kiberwosen's membership in the village iddir is social participation, while standing as a candidate in the election is political participation, so her community participation is both social and political. Options B, C and D wrongly describe her involvement as neither, or exclusively one kind, of participation.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is neither a social nor an economic participation.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is exclusively a political participation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is exclusively a social participation.

questions.question_text: Ato Bedru is a well-known man of traditional medicine. He contributed by healing the physical and psychological sicknesses of people in the community. What can be said about the source of his knowledge?

options.label: A
options.option_text: He must be a magician and sorcerer with no source of knowledge.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The source of his knowledge comes from invisible spirits.

options.label: C
options.option_text: He accumulated his knowledge through formal education.

options.label: D
options.option_text: His knowledge is acquired from informal learning.
options.explanation: Ato Bedru's knowledge of traditional medicine was acquired through informal learning, passed down through experience, observation and community practice rather than formal education. Options A and B wrongly dismiss his knowledge as magic or spirits, and C wrongly attributes it to formal schooling, so D is correct.

questions.question_text: The respect of the principle of majority rule and minority rights is assured, when

options.label: A
options.option_text: the majority impose their policies and strategies on the minorities.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the law favors the rights of the minorities over the interests of majority over the majority.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the minority cooperate to look after their rights and oppose the majority.

options.label: D
options.option_text: there is a possibility to check the observance of the rights of the minority.
options.explanation: The principle of majority rule and minority rights is assured when there is a possibility to check the observance of minority rights, meaning the majority governs but minorities are protected. Options A, B and C describe domination, favouring minorities over the majority, or minority opposition, none of which balances majority rule with minority rights.

questions.question_text: What can we learn from the failed military coup d'état of 1960 in Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Political stability in a dictatorship can be achieved through coup d'état.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Political transformation needs thought and dialogue than coup d'état.
options.explanation: The failed 1960 coup teaches that political transformation requires thought and dialogue rather than military coups, which bring instability without lasting change. Options A, C and D wrongly claim coups bring stability or are sustainable solutions, so B draws the correct lesson from the failed attempt.

options.label: C
options.option_text: If the government is authoritarian and dictator, coup d'état is a sustainable solution.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Coup d'état is the solution for preventing recurrent public uprisings in Ethiopia.

questions.question_text: How can federalism be implemented in Ethiopia to serve the purpose of a multiethnic society?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By controlling the abuse of power in the distribution of powers between the federal government and the regional states.
options.explanation: Federalism serves a multiethnic society by controlling the abuse of power in distributing powers between the federal government and regional states, ensuring a fair division of authority. Options B, C and D describe domination by one level of government, extreme regional power, or centralised decision making, all of which undermine balanced federalism.

options.label: B
options.option_text: By allowing the federal government exercises freely its power over the regional affairs of constituent parts.

options.label: C
options.option_text: By allowing extensive powers and self-rule for regional governments that can control the federal government.

options.label: D
options.option_text: By centralizing decision making and decentralizing administration within the localities of regional governments.

questions.question_text: Information is definite knowledge acquired about a specific subject and needed to make informed decisions. There are different ways of gathering data and information like observation, interviews or reading from books, magazine, internet and newspapers. But the reliability of the information depends on nature of information that we acquire through different ways.

options.label: A
options.option_text: information we acquire from observation is more reliable than interviews and readings.
options.explanation: Of the listed methods, information acquired through direct observation is generally considered more reliable than interviews and readings, because it is firsthand and less subject to distortion. The stem is defective because it never completes the question, but A best fits the standard textbook position that observation is the most reliable.

options.label: B
options.option_text: information we acquire from observation, interviews and readings are equally reliable.

options.label: C
options.option_text: information we acquire through reading is more reliable than observation and interviews.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the information we gain from interviews is more reliable than observation and readings.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a way of fulfilling the constitutional obligations of citizens?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Looking after the rights of fellow citizens arbitrarily.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Subjugating those who violate the laws and rights of others.
options.explanation: Fulfilling constitutional obligations includes bringing those who violate the laws and rights of others under control, thereby upholding justice and order. Options A, C and D describe arbitrary action, blind support for the ruling party, and marginalising dissenters, none of which fulfil constitutional obligations.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Being the proponent of the governing party's ideologies.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Marginalizing those who have different opinions than ours.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an example of crimes against humanity?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The observance of fundamental human and democratic rights

options.label: B
options.option_text: Peaceful demonstrations according to the law

options.label: C
options.option_text: Commitment to the rights to life, liberty and freedom of expression

options.label: D
options.option_text: Repression of basic human rights like the right to life and liberty
options.explanation: Crimes against humanity include the repression of basic human rights such as the right to life and liberty, as committed on a large scale against civilians. Options A, B and C describe lawful protection of rights, peaceful demonstrations and respect for fundamental freedoms, which are the opposite of crimes against humanity.

questions.question_text: The knee-jerk reflex is an example of a monosynaptic reflex. This means that the reflex arc involves:

options.label: A
options.option_text: One sensory neuron and one motor neuron with no interneuron
options.explanation: This is the definition of a monosynaptic reflex.

options.label: B
options.option_text: One sensory neuron, one interneuron, and one motor neuron
options.explanation: Option B is a reflex with an interneuron is a polysynaptic reflex.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is this describes a complex polysynaptic reflex.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A direct connection between the receptor and the effector
options.explanation: Option D is the synapse between the sensory and motor neurons is still required.

questions.question_text: Kaleab and Tsigereda often discuss about their previous readings. Kaleab has a free access to his brother's library and numerous books in soft copy. Though Kaleab reads a lot he remembers only few of the ideas. Tsigereda on the other hand borrows selected books from the book shop and she takes notes regularly and use the influential ideas to broaden her understanding. What can be concluded from the above case?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Kaleab and Tsigereda are equally good readers.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Compared with Tsigereda, Kaleab is a better reader.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Kaleab's life is a life of reading and hence he is a good reader.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Compared with Kaleab, Tsigereda is a better reader.
options.explanation: Tsigereda is a better reader than Kaleab because she reads selected books, takes notes regularly and uses the influential ideas to broaden her understanding, whereas Kaleab reads many books but remembers only a few ideas. Options A, B and C wrongly claim they are equal or that Kaleab is better.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about the idea that 'the constitution is the supreme law of the land'?

options.label: A
options.option_text: All other laws within the nation must confront the constitution, all political powers are sources of the constitution and it is the suppression of people's sovereignty.

options.label: B
options.option_text: All other laws within the nation are replications of the constitution, it is the suppression of all political powers and denies the sovereignty of the people.

options.label: C
options.option_text: All other laws within the nation must conform to the constitution, the constitution is source of all powers, and it is the expression of people's sovereignty.
options.explanation: Constitutional supremacy means all other laws must conform to the constitution, the constitution is the source of all powers, and it expresses the sovereignty of the people. Options A, B and D misstate these elements, saying other laws confront or override the constitution or that it suppresses popular sovereignty, so C is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: All other laws within the nation must override the constitution, the constitution is the source of all powers, and it is the expression of people's sovereignty.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following characterizes the human and democratic situations in Ethiopia after the fall of monarchical power in 1974?

options.label: A
options.option_text: An era of gross violations of human and democratic rights of people.
options.explanation: After the fall of the monarchy in 1974, the military regime that followed was an era of gross violations of human and democratic rights, marked by repression and the Red Terror. Options B, C and D wrongly describe it as civilised, respectful of rights, or nonviolent, so A characterises the period accurately.

options.label: B
options.option_text: An era of civilized mechanisms to challenge the totalitarian rule.

options.label: C
options.option_text: An era of great respect of civil rights and political rights.

options.label: D
options.option_text: An era of nonviolence in social, economic and political aspects of life.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the major cause of the Bale Peasants' rebellion during the reign of Emperor Haile Selassie?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The need for the right of ruling the nation.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The need for freedom and improved life.
options.explanation: The major cause of the Bale peasants' rebellion during Haile Selassie's reign was the need for freedom and improved life, rooted in land expropriation, heavy taxation and oppression. Options A, B and D describe ruling the nation or various kinds of representation, which do not capture the peasants' core grievances.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The need for a proper national representation.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following alternatives best describes the nature of judiciary during the era of a military state structure in Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: There is a possibility of division of power between the federal and regional states.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It allows for the rights of constituent administrative regions in decision making.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is highly decentralized and has limited power in decision making at regional levels.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is highly centralized and the Supreme Court was a final decision making body in the nation.
options.explanation: During the military state structure, the judiciary was highly centralised and the Supreme Court was the final decision-making body, reflecting the centralised character of the Derg state. Options A, B and C wrongly describe federal-state division of power or decentralisation, which did not exist in the military era.

questions.question_text: The strategy of building mobile schools for pastoralist communities in Ethiopia shows

options.label: A
options.explanation: Building mobile schools for pastoralist communities shows the equal provision of social services, bringing education to groups whose mobile way of life makes fixed schools inaccessible. Options B, C and D wrongly describe it as marginalising groups, ethnic discrimination, or assessing public life, so A is correct.

questions.question_text: The act of chasing away the community from the normal distribution of goods is

options.label: D
options.explanation: Chasing the community away from the normal distribution of goods describes rent-seeking behaviour, in which individuals obtain economic benefits by manipulating access to markets rather than through production or fair exchange. Wholesale, market competition and retail sale are legitimate market activities, so D is the best available answer.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following alternatives best describes the requirements to develop peoples' sense of patriotism in nations like Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Oppression of rights, avoiding any responsibility, marginalizing the majority, abolishing the distribution of goods and services.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Affirmative action, unequal distribution of goods and services, stagnation in development, questioning common symbols and the sense of national unity.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Avoiding discriminations, enhancing goods and services, assuring equality among citizens, allowing access to public goods and developing a sense of national unity.
options.explanation: Developing patriotism requires avoiding discrimination, enhancing goods and services, assuring equality among citizens, allowing access to public goods and building a sense of national unity. Options A, B and D describe oppression, inequality, stagnation and favouritism, which destroy rather than develop patriotism.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Compromising equality, promoting development, favoring the majority, developing a sense of revenge among people.

questions.question_text: What will be the consequence if a society failed to adhere to the basic tenets of a democratic system?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The prevalence of human and democratic rights is guaranteed.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The communication between the ruling and the ruled will be threatened.
options.explanation: If a society fails to adhere to the basic tenets of democracy, communication between the rulers and the ruled will be threatened, weakening accountability and trust. Options A, C and D describe outcomes of a functioning democracy, so B correctly states the consequence of abandoning democratic principles.

options.label: C
options.option_text: There will be an unquestionable adherence to the rule of law by the government.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The political sphere will facilitate the healthy participation of people.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the breach of students' obligations in the school?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Being critical opponents to the irrational wills of school leaders in a rational way.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Showing maximum honesty and trustworthy in using public and private properties in the school.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Bullying and ridiculing fellow students for possible mistakes in the class rooms.
options.explanation: Bullying and ridiculing fellow students for mistakes is a breach of students' obligations, violating respect and the school's ethical standards. Options A, B and D describe responsible conduct: rational criticism, honesty, and respect for regulations, which are obligations rather than breaches, so C is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Respecting the written and unwritten regulations of school vicinity and rules of class rooms.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a highly threatened right of children in the history of 20th century Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.explanation: In the history of 20th century Ethiopia, the right to life was the most highly threatened right of children, as wars, famines and the Red Terror took the lives of many children. Options B, C and D concern name, nationality and parental care, which were less systematically threatened than life itself.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The right to have a proper name

options.label: D
options.option_text: To know and be cared for by parents

questions.question_text: Which one of the following characterizes the nature of diversity in Ethiopian society?

options.label: A
options.option_text: As a cultural reality, diversity was governed by a multicultural harmony in Ethiopia.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Diversity was the basic obstacle for Ethiopia's development.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Historically, Ethiopian society dealt with the issue of diversity fairly.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The phenomenon of diversity in Ethiopia requires careful consideration.
options.explanation: The diversity of Ethiopian society requires careful consideration, because managing ethnic and cultural diversity is complex and demands deliberate policy. Options A and C overstate historical harmony, while B wrongly blames diversity alone for lack of development, so D is the most accurate characterisation.

questions.question_text: Obang Owi is an assertive person. That means he has characteristics of

options.label: A
options.option_text: easily changing his mind flexibly, accepting what others say without debate, and lack self-confidence.

options.label: B
options.option_text: presenting his opinions with reason openly, disagrees with unacceptable claims, and considering convincing arguments from others.
options.explanation: An assertive person presents opinions with reason openly, disagrees with unacceptable claims, and considers convincing arguments from others, balancing confidence with respect. Options A, C and D describe passivity, aggression or arrogance, which are the opposite of assertiveness, so B correctly describes Obang Owi.

options.label: C
options.option_text: confrontation with others aggressively, arrogant to oppositions from others, stagnant to his opinions.

options.label: D
options.option_text: ridiculing the onions of others openly, opposing to advises of friends and stick to his stands strictly.

questions.question_text: Making decisions by oneself means

options.label: A
options.option_text: looking for alternatives and choosing which is useful for our personal desires, not of others.

options.label: B
options.option_text: decisions are done collectively and we cannot adhere to the opinions of others.

options.label: C
options.option_text: focusing on one's potentials and listening to opinions of others.
options.explanation: Making decisions by oneself means focusing on one's own potentials while listening to the opinions of others, combining independence with openness to advice. Options A, B and D describe self-serving choice, ignoring others, or rejecting outside ideas, which are not mature, self-reliant decision making, so C is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: making independent decisions by ignoring the ideas of others.

questions.question_text: What are impulsive purchases?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Purchasing necessary things for one's family needs.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Purchases which promote ones saving culture.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Planned purchases which are compatible with one's income.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Random purchases based on one's emotion rather than income.
options.explanation: Impulsive purchases are random purchases based on one's emotion rather than income, made without planning or regard for one's budget. Options A, B and C describe necessary, saving-promoting and planned purchases, which are the opposite of impulsive buying, so D is the correct definition.

questions.question_text: What is the relationship between the Ethiopian economy and globalization?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Since the effect of globalization is strong and we cannot control its effects, the Ethiopian economy cannot be liberated from globalization.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Since there is a form of economic globalization among countries, the Ethiopian economy may be affected by globalization.
options.explanation: Because economic globalisation exists among countries, the Ethiopian economy may be affected by globalisation, since no economy operates in isolation. Options A and C overstate or deny the impact, while D wrongly claims Ethiopia's indigenous system makes it immune, so B correctly describes the relationship.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Since globalization is not economical but of cultural phenomena, it has little impact on Ethiopian economy.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Since Ethiopia adopts its own indigenous economic system, globalization doesn't affect our economy.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a practical implication of new thinking in saving culture?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Using foreign products than local products

options.label: D
options.option_text: Replacing traditional saving by modern saving
options.explanation: A practical implication of the new thinking in saving culture is replacing traditional saving methods with modern saving, such as bank accounts and formal financial instruments. Preferring traditional saving, consuming local products, or using foreign products do not reflect modern saving practice, so D is correct.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following represents the increase in the quantity supplied of real GDP due to the increase in the price level?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The right wards shifts of the aggregate supply curve

options.label: B
options.option_text: The left wards shifts of the aggregate supply curve

options.label: C
options.option_text: The downwards movements along the aggregate supply curve

options.label: D
options.option_text: The upwards movements along the aggregate supply curve
options.explanation: An increase in the price level, other things constant, changes only the quantity of real GDP supplied, so the economy moves along the existing short-run aggregate supply curve rather than shifting it. Because firms earn higher profits at higher prices, they supply more output, which is shown as an upward movement along the curve from one point to another.

questions.question_text: When the economy is in the long run, which of the following is correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Sticky wages and workers misperception still holds true.

options.label: B
options.option_text: What the economy produces is the full employment real GDP.
options.explanation: In the long run, wages, prices and expectations fully adjust, so the economy produces at its potential or full-employment level of real GDP. Sticky wages and workers' misperceptions are short-run phenomena that disappear once adjustments occur, which is why producing the full-employment real GDP is the correct description of the long run.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The short run and the long run real GDP will be the same.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The level of real GDP the economy produces is less than the natural real GDP.

questions.question_text: What is the pressure on price when the quantity demanded of real GDP is greater than the quantity supplied of real GDP during the short run?

options.label: A
options.explanation: When the quantity of real GDP demanded exceeds the quantity supplied at the current price level, there is an excess demand or shortage. Buyers compete for the scarce output, which bids prices upward. Therefore the price level rises until the quantity demanded falls and the quantity supplied rises back to the equilibrium level.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about the economy when it is in long run equilibrium?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The economy produces the real GDP which is called the natural real GDP.
options.explanation: Long-run equilibrium occurs where aggregate demand, short-run aggregate supply and long-run aggregate supply all intersect, and at that point the economy produces its natural level of real GDP. This natural real GDP is the full-employment output consistent with the long-run aggregate supply curve, so it is the correct statement about long-run equilibrium.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The short run aggregate demand curve intersects the short run aggregate supply curve.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The long run aggregate demand curve intersects the short run aggregate supply curve.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Price temporarily deviates from equilibrium even if aggregate demand and aggregate supply remain unchanged.

questions.question_text: Which of the following represents an economic situation where there is an inefficient distribution of goods and services in the free market?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Market failure is the situation in which a free market produces an inefficient allocation of goods and services, so the market equilibrium does not maximize total surplus. Externalities, asymmetric information and free riding are causes of market failure rather than the failure itself, making market failure the term that directly describes the inefficient distribution.

questions.question_text: What impacts on our aggregate demand do you expect if the level of economic activities in other countries increase?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Rising economic activity in other countries raises their demand for our exports. Higher exports increase the net export component of aggregate expenditure, so the aggregate demand curve shifts rightward. Thus an increase in the level of economic activity abroad causes our aggregate demand to increase rather than to decrease or remain unchanged.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Aggregate demand first declines and then rises.

questions.question_text: Among the following, which one differentiates change in quantity demanded from change in aggregate demand?

options.label: A
options.option_text: As the price level falls, the quantity demanded of real GDP rises, ceteris paribus.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is represented as a movement from one point to another along different demand curve.
options.explanation: A change in the price level changes the quantity demanded, which is shown as a movement along an existing demand curve, whereas a change in any other determinant changes demand itself and shifts the whole curve. Option B captures this distinction by describing movement from one point to another along a given demand curve.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A positive change in any factors causes a rightward shift in the AD curve.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is a shift in aggregate demand curve from AD1 to AD2 on different curve.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about aggregate demand curve?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It represents the inverse relationship between the real GDP demanded and consumption expenditure, all else being equal.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is a schedule that represents the amount of real output that sellers collectively desire to sell at each price, ceteris paribus.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It shows the inverse relationship between the amount of real output buyers desire to buy at each price, all else being equal.
options.explanation: The aggregate demand curve is a schedule showing the total amount of real output that households, firms, the government and foreign buyers desire to purchase at each price level. It slopes downward because a higher price level reduces real wealth, raises interest rates and makes domestic goods expensive, so buyers want to buy less output.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It shows the inverse relationship between the amount of real output sellers desire to sell at each price, all else being equal.

questions.question_text: What is the implication of the Keynesian horizontal aggregate supply curve?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Firms can supply whatever amount demanded at the existing price because of unemployment.
options.explanation: A horizontal, Keynesian aggregate supply curve means firms can hire additional labor without raising wages because there is substantial unemployment in the economy. Consequently firms can supply whatever amount is demanded at the existing price level without experiencing rising average costs of production, which is the implication of the horizontal curve.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Firms can obtain much labour as they want as long as they pay more.

options.label: C
options.option_text: As output level changes, the average cost of production increases.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The labour market is in equilibrium with full employment of the labour force.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the main factor that affects the amount of output firms are willing to supply?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The price of related goods produced by other firms

options.label: B
options.option_text: The price they receive for their goods
options.explanation: The amount of output a firm is willing to supply is mainly governed by the price it can receive for its product, because a higher price raises the profitability of producing and selling each unit. The prices of related goods, foreign economic activity and future price expectations are secondary influences rather than the main factor.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The level of economic activity in other countries

options.label: D
options.option_text: The price they anticipate to prevail in the future

questions.question_text: Which of the following isNOTthe cause of market failure?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Private goods are rival and excludable, so markets can allocate them efficiently, and they are therefore not a cause of market failure. Monopoly restricts output and raises price, externalities spill costs or benefits onto third parties, and factor immobility prevents resources moving to their best uses, and all of these do cause market failure.

questions.question_text: Suppose Sol-ech - company receives positive externalities from COMP educated graduates subsidize computer education through scholarships, in which of the following group is this type of solution for market failure listed?

options.label: C
options.explanation: When a private firm receives external benefits from educated workers, it can act on its own to correct the market failure, for example by subsidizing computer education through scholarships. Because the solution is undertaken voluntarily by private agents rather than imposed by government or achieved through collective agreement, it belongs to the private market solutions category.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an example of public goods?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Wilderness is a public good because it is non-rival, meaning one person's enjoyment does not reduce its availability to others, and non-excludable, meaning it is difficult to prevent anyone from using it. Houses, food items and clothes are private goods that are rival and excludable and are normally traded in markets.

questions.question_text: Which of the following characterize Public goods?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Public goods have two defining characteristics: non-rivalry in consumption, so one person using the good does not reduce the amount available to others, and non-excludability, so it is impossible or very costly to exclude non-payers. These two features together distinguish pure public goods from private goods.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following factor is the reason for market inefficiency in the provision of public goods?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Because public goods are non-excludable, individuals can enjoy their benefits without paying for them, so most people have no incentive to contribute voluntarily. This free-rider problem means the market cannot charge a price for the good and therefore underproduces it, which is the fundamental reason for market inefficiency in providing public goods.

questions.question_text: Which of the following macroeconomic policy involves by which the government manipulates its expenditure and revenue side?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fiscal policy is the use of government expenditure and taxation, the revenue side of the budget, to influence the economy. By manipulating its spending and revenue, the government can change aggregate demand, redistribute income and stabilize the economy, so the correct policy is fiscal policy rather than monetary, income or exchange rate policy.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following instrument is considered by the contractionary fiscal policy when there is an excess demand and inflationary pressure in the economy?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Contractionary fiscal policy is used to reduce excess aggregate demand and inflationary pressure by decreasing government expenditure or increasing taxes. Cutting spending directly reduces aggregate demand, whereas reducing taxes would add stimulus, so the correct instrument is a decrease in government expenditure.

questions.question_text: A tight monetary policy is applied in circumstances where there is

options.label: A
options.explanation: A tight or contractionary monetary policy reduces the money supply and raises interest rates in order to slow aggregate demand and bring down the rate of inflation. It is therefore applied when inflation is high, not when high growth, high unemployment or slow growth is the main problem being addressed.

questions.question_text: If tight fiscal and monetary policies fail to address the problem of rising price level, what is the alternative policy that the government should consider?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Income policy directly restrains wage and price increases through guidelines, controls or agreements, so it is the alternative used when tight fiscal and monetary policies fail to stop inflation. Trade, exchange rate and interest rate policies do not directly control wages and prices in the same way.

questions.question_text: Which of the following exchange rate regime is the one that is determined by the government political and economic decisions?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Under a fixed exchange rate regime the value of the currency is set by the government at a particular rate against another currency, so it is determined by the government's political and economic decisions rather than by market forces. Floating, managed floating and crawling peg regimes are determined mainly by the market.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following difference is the cause for efficiency loss in the presence of negative externality?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Between marginal social benefit and marginal private benefit

options.label: B
options.option_text: Between marginal social cost and marginal private cost
options.explanation: With a negative externality, the marginal social cost exceeds the marginal private cost because producers do not bear the full cost of their actions. This divergence between social and private marginal cost causes overproduction and an efficiency loss, because too much of the good is produced relative to the socially optimal quantity.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Between private marginal cost and marginal external cost

options.label: D
options.option_text: Between private marginal benefit and marginal external benefit

questions.question_text: When an insurance company provides fringe benefits on the basis of an average rate over a set of employees and guarantees them to participate in the program, then this can be seen as a solution for which one of the following problem?

options.label: A
options.explanation: When an insurer charges an average rate and guarantees coverage to a whole group, it pools both good and bad risks, preventing high-risk individuals from being priced out or leaving the pool. This pooling arrangement reduces the information problem of adverse selection, where the insurer knows less than the insured about risk.

questions.question_text: Which of the following macroeconomic policies involves management of money supply and interest rate?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Monetary policy is the management of the money supply and interest rates by the central bank to influence aggregate demand, inflation and economic activity. Fiscal policy concerns government spending and taxes, while exchange rate and income policies address other objectives, so monetary policy is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the monetary policy tool that involves the purchase and sale of securities by the nation's central bank?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Open market operations are the purchase and sale of government securities by the central bank to change the amount of reserves in the banking system and thereby influence the money supply. The discount rate and required reserve ratio are different tools of monetary policy, and government spending is a fiscal tool.

questions.question_text: One of the following is considered to be fiscal policy tool. Which one is it?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Taxation is the main fiscal policy tool because the government changes tax rates and the tax structure to influence aggregate demand, income distribution and economic activity. Investment, grants in aid and transfer payments are not themselves fiscal policy tools in the way that taxation directly is.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about price ceilings?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is one of the income policies that keeps a price from declining from a certain limit.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is a maximum price set by law to make basic consumption goods affordable to buyers.
options.explanation: A price ceiling is a maximum price set by law that sellers may charge, intended to make basic consumption goods affordable to buyers. To be effective it must be set below the equilibrium price, and it creates a shortage, so the correct definition is that it is a maximum legal price used to protect buyers.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It should be set above the equilibrium price to make it more effective.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It discourages consumers from buying goods and services since they are now paying higher price.

questions.question_text: Suppose the value of an Ethiopian Birr in terms of Kenyan Shilling is getting higher. What is the impact of this on the Ethiopian export to Kenya?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It will make the price of Ethiopian goods in the Kenyan market cheaper.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It will make the price of Kenyan import in the Ethiopian market expensive.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It will increase Ethiopia's export earnings.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It will reduce Ethiopia's export earnings.
options.explanation: When the birr appreciates against the Kenyan shilling, Ethiopian goods become more expensive for Kenyan buyers and Kenyan goods become cheaper for Ethiopians. Kenyan buyers therefore buy fewer Ethiopian products, reducing the volume of exports and Ethiopia's export earnings from trade with Kenya.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following clearly defines taxation?

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is the only source of government revenue.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is levied without anything in direct return.
options.explanation: A tax is a compulsory, unrequited payment to government, meaning the payer does not receive a specific direct benefit in return. It is not voluntary, it is not the only source of government revenue, and it does not encourage the nonexistence of government, so the correct statement is that it is levied without anything in direct return.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains the tax principles called "canon of economy"?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Everyone should pay tax according to his ability.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The amount of tax that we are supposed to pay should be known in advance.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Every tax payer should pay the tax in his own convenient time.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The cost of tax collection should be as minimum as possible.
options.explanation: The canon of economy states that the cost of collecting a tax should be as low as possible, so that the government keeps most of the revenue it collects. Taxes should be levied at minimum collection cost, avoiding an expensive and wasteful administration, which distinguishes this canon from equity, certainty and convenience.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the implication of one of a good tax system that is referred to as broad based?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The system should impose tax on all people without discrimination.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The system should ensure that an income inequality is reduced.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The system should impose tax on income and properties and commodities.
options.explanation: A broad-based tax system spreads the tax over a wide variety of bases, such as income, property and commodities, so that no single base carries the whole burden. Imposing tax on income, properties and commodities is exactly what makes the system broad based, unlike a narrow system that taxes only income.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The system should ascertain that national income and living standard is increasing.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the advantage of fiscal decentralization?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Provide scale economies in the collection of taxes

options.label: B
options.option_text: Provide scale economies in the provision of public goods

options.label: C
options.option_text: Provision of public goods and services desired by local residents.
options.explanation: Fiscal decentralization brings taxing and spending decisions closer to local people, so local governments can provide the mix and level of public goods that residents in their area actually prefer. This responsiveness to local preferences is the main advantage compared with a uniform national provision of services.

questions.question_text: One of the following is considered to be the aim of fiscal decentralization. Which one is it?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Enhancing the role of private sector

options.label: D
