options.explanation: Pure public goods are characterized by non-rivalry and non-excludability in consumption: one person's use does not reduce availability to others, and it is impossible or very costly to exclude non-payers. Private goods are rival and excludable, and mixed cases combine the two characteristics. Therefore the major feature of pure public goods is non-rivalry and non-excludability, option B.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Non rivalry in consumption and excludability

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about the difference between pure private good and pure public goods?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In pure private goods additional cost incurred by the additional person is zero.

options.label: B
options.option_text: In pure public goods additional cost incurred by the additional person is positive.

options.label: C
options.option_text: In pure private goods the benefits of using the good cannot be priced.

options.label: D
options.option_text: In pure public goods the benefits of using the good cannot be priced.
options.explanation: In the case of pure public goods, the benefits of using the good cannot be priced because consumption is non-rival and non-excludable, so users cannot be charged for the benefits they enjoy. In pure private goods an additional user does impose a positive cost, and their benefits can be priced through the market. Hence the correct difference between private and public goods is option D.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about the characteristics of externality?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Externalities are reciprocal in nature because one party's action affects another party and the affected party's response can, in turn, influence the first party, so spillover effects run in both directions. Externalities can be generated by both producers and consumers, they are not rival or excludable, and they involve interactions beyond a single person's action. Therefore the correct characteristic of externalities is option A.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Externalities can only be generated by consumers

options.label: D
options.option_text: Externalities are the result of one person's action

questions.question_text: Suppose in a car market transaction, sellers take advantage of buyers because the sellers have better information about the dynamic of product quality and market price change of cars than the buyers. Which one of the following is the implication of such kind of asymmetric information?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It results in efficient market equilibrium for involving parties.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It guarantees the same decision for the involving parties.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It creates an imbalance in power in transactions to involving parties.
options.explanation: Asymmetric information, where sellers know more about product quality and market conditions than buyers, creates an imbalance of power in transactions because the better-informed party can take advantage of the less-informed one. It does not produce efficient equilibrium, does not guarantee identical decisions, and certainly does not give both parties equal information. Hence the implication of such asymmetric information is option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It helps all involving parties to have equal information about the good.

questions.question_text: Among the following statements, which one is correct about the limitation of Human Development Index (HDI)?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It assigns weights to certain factors that have equal trade-offs.
options.explanation: One limitation of the Human Development Index is that it assigns equal weights to its three components, implying perfect trade-offs between health, education and income even though they are not equally important. It does not take inequality or poverty into account, and its component indices are limited between zero and one. Therefore the correct limitation of the HDI is option A.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It correlates factors that are more common in developing economies.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It takes into account factors such as inequality and poverty.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The values of the factors that make up the HDI are limited between 0 and 2.

questions.question_text: In which one of the following Millenium Development Goal (MDG) that Ethiopia made significant progress?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ethiopia made significant progress in achieving the Millennium Development Goal of eradicating extreme poverty and hunger, largely because of sustained economic growth and expanding social programs. Progress on environmental sustainability, maternal health and global partnerships was comparatively weaker during the MDG period. Hence the MDG in which Ethiopia made significant progress is eradicating extreme poverty and hunger, option A.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Developing a global partnership for development

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about the relationship between the Millennium Development Goals and the Sustainable Development Goals?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Millennium development goals are less ambitious and narrow compared to sustainable development goals.
options.explanation: The Millennium Development Goals are less ambitious and narrow compared with the Sustainable Development Goals, since the MDGs had eight goals focused mainly on developing countries, while the SDGs have seventeen universal goals covering economic, social and environmental dimensions for all countries. The SDGs are more universal in coverage, include clean energy, and retain poverty reduction as a goal. Therefore the correct statement is option A.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Millennium development goals include affordable and clean energy as a goal which are not included in sustainable development goals.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Millennium development goals exclude poverty reduction as a goal which are included in sustainable development goals.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Sustainable development goals are more universal in coverage compared to millennium development goals.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is separately categorized under the Sustainable Development Goals?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Responsible consumption and production is a separate goal under the Sustainable Development Goals, specifically SDG 12. Reducing child mortality, combating HIV and AIDS and other diseases, and achieving universal primary education were Millennium Development Goals rather than separate SDGs. Therefore the option that is separately categorized under the Sustainable Development Goals is option B.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Combat HIV/AIDS, malaria and other diseases

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is advantage of bi-modal agricultural strategy?

options.label: B
options.option_text: It reduces poverty in the rural economy.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It reduces outgoing migration from rural areas.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A bi-modal agricultural strategy, which develops large-scale commercial agriculture alongside smallholder farming, promotes large-scale diversification by encouraging the production of a wider range of crops and output. The options about protecting peasants from eviction, reducing rural poverty and reducing out-migration do not describe the typical advantages of the bi-modal approach. Hence the advantage of the bi-modal strategy is option D.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about the Mercantilists' view on trade?

options.label: A
options.option_text: To promote a favorable trade balance, they advocate trade liberalization.

options.label: B
options.option_text: To minimize imports, they advocate imposition of tariff and quota.
options.explanation: The Mercantilists believed that national wealth was measured by the stock of gold and silver, so they advocated imposing tariffs and quotas to minimize imports and encourage exports in order to achieve a favorable trade balance. They opposed trade liberalization and did not regard imports as beneficial or important for preventing depletion of gold. Therefore the correct view of the Mercantilists is option B.

options.label: C
options.option_text: To generate more revenue for importing nation imports were considered good.

options.label: D
options.option_text: To prevent the country's holdings of gold being depleted increasing imports is important.

questions.question_text: Assume that the total value of export of goods and services of Country "X" in the year 2020 was less than the total value of imported goods. Which one of the following statements is correct about the status of this country?

options.label: D
options.explanation: When the total value of a country's exports of goods and services is less than the total value of its imports, the country is running a trade deficit, also called an unfavorable balance of trade. A trade surplus is the opposite situation, trade balance means exports equal imports, and a capital account deficit concerns financial flows rather than goods trade. Hence the correct status is trade deficit, option D.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the effect of devaluation of local currency on the economy?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is expected to equally encourage export and imports.

options.label: B
options.option_text: With devaluation, imports become expensive while exports become cheap.
options.explanation: Devaluation of the local currency makes imports more expensive in local currency terms while making exports cheaper for foreign buyers, so it encourages exports and discourages imports. It does not equally encourage exports and imports, and it does not encourage imports or make them cheaper. Therefore the correct effect of devaluation on the economy is option B.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is expected to encourage imports and discourage exports.

options.label: D
options.option_text: With devaluation, import becomes cheaper while exports become expensive.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains the basic difference between economic growth and development?

options.label: A
options.option_text: While a country may grow richer through the growth of its real output it does not necessarily mean that it will develop.
options.explanation: Economic growth is a sustained increase in real output or GDP per capita, while economic development involves improvements in living standards, welfare and structural change, so a country can grow richer without necessarily developing. Development is not measured simply by GDP growth, and GDP per capita measures growth rather than the effect of development on living standards. Hence the correct statement is option A.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Economic growth is a process where there is improvement in the lives of all people in the country.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Economic development is determined by the percentage increase of the GDP from one time period to other.

options.label: D
options.option_text: GDP per capita measures the effect of economic development on living standard of the population.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following indicators is component of Human Development Index?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The Human Development Index is composed of three dimensions: health, education and income, and the Educational Attainment Index, covering mean and expected years of schooling, is a component of the education dimension. The Multidimensional Poverty Index, Gender Empowerment Measure and Gender Inequality Index are separate indicators and not components of the HDI. Therefore the correct component is option D.

questions.question_text: If the Real GDP of country "A" in the year 2023 is 19,550,000 dollar and in the year 2022 it was 18,600,000 dollar, then the real GDP growth in 2023 as compared to the previous year will be equal to

options.label: A
options.explanation: The real GDP growth rate equals the change in real GDP divided by the previous year's real GDP, multiplied by one hundred. Here the change is 19,550,000 minus 18,600,000, which is 950,000, and dividing by 18,600,000 gives about 0.05108, which is 5.11 percent. Therefore the real GDP growth in 2023 relative to 2022 is 5.11 percent, option A.

questions.question_text: Given the following short run total production function (TP) where Labor(L) is the only variable input used in the production process: TP = L3− 3L, if the firm want to increase the amount of labor(L) used from 4 to 5, then which one of the following is the Marginal Product (MP) of extra unit of labor?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The marginal product of labor is the change in total product when labor increases by one unit. With TP equal to L cubed minus 3L, total product at L equal to 5 is 125 minus 15, which is 110, and at L equal to 4 it is 64 minus 12, which is 52. The difference, 110 minus 52, equals 58, so the marginal product of the extra unit of labor is 58, option C.

questions.question_text: Given the budget equation as: $2X + 3Y = 60$ where Price of commodity X ($P_x = 2$), Price of commodity Y ($P_y = 3$), and income of the consumer ($M = 60$), then which one of the following is slope of the budget line?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The slope of the budget line equals the negative of the price ratio of the two goods, that is, minus Px divided by Py. Given Px equal to 2 and Py equal to 3, the slope is minus 2 over 3, or negative two-thirds. The other options give incorrect ratios, so the slope of the budget line is negative two-thirds, option D.

questions.question_text: Given the following numerical values of marginal and total utility derived from consumption of orange in the table below.Quantity Consumed(Q)0123456789Total Utility (TU)01324?373838373430Marginal Utility (MU)-13117610-1-3-4Depending on the information provided in the table, what is the total utility of the 3rdunit of orange?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Total utility at each quantity equals the sum of the marginal utilities up to that quantity. Since total utility at the second unit is 24 and the marginal utility of the third unit is 7, total utility of the third unit is 24 plus 7, which is 31. This is also consistent with the total utility of 37 at the fourth unit. Hence the total utility of the third unit of orange is 31, option B.

questions.question_text: In a hypothetical country, (K) the number of employed labor is 25 million and the number of unemployed labors is 5 million. Moreover, the total adult population of the country is given as 80 million. How much is the labor force participation rate?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The labor force participation rate is the labor force divided by the adult population, multiplied by one hundred, where the labor force is the sum of employed and unemployed persons. The employed number 25 million and the unemployed number 5 million, so the labor force is 30 million, and dividing by the adult population of 80 million gives 0.375. Therefore the participation rate is 37.5 percent, option D.

questions.question_text: What kind of measures do you recommend for water resource management and conservation in Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Building dams to generate hydroelectric power

options.label: B
options.option_text: Planting exotic plants near the streams and rivers

options.label: C
options.option_text: Planting trees on the upper parts of the streams
options.explanation: Planting trees on the upper parts of streams protects the catchment by reducing soil erosion, slowing runoff, and allowing more water to infiltrate and recharge groundwater. Building dams generates power but does not conserve water; rainwater harvesting is useful but limited to wet areas, and exotic plants can harm local ecosystems.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Rain water harvesting in the wettest parts of the country

questions.question_text: If you travel from Addis Ababa to the northeastern lowlands of Ethiopia in summer, you can recognize a high variation in the rainfall. This variation is mainly caused by

options.label: A
options.explanation: Addis Ababa lies on the highlands while the northeastern lowlands lie in the rain shadow. When moist air from the sea approaches, mountain barriers force it upward, causing orographic rainfall on the windward side and dry conditions on the leeward side, creating the observed variation in rainfall across the two areas.

questions.question_text: Which meteorological station of Ethiopia is expected to receive rainfall throughout the year?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bonga is located in the southwestern highlands of Ethiopia, where the southwest monsoon brings heavy rainfall for most of the year, so rain falls throughout the year. Moyalle, Gode and Debremarkos experience marked dry seasons and receive rainfall only seasonally, whereas Bonga's location makes it the wettest of the listed stations.

questions.question_text: Which wild animal is unique to the Bale Mountains?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The Mountain Nyala (Tragelaphus buxtoni) is an endemic antelope found mainly in the Bale Mountains National Park, making it unique to that area. The Walia Ibex is unique to the Simien Mountains, while the Gelada baboon and Wild Ass are found in other parts of Ethiopia, not uniquely in Bale.

questions.question_text: Which of the following actions should be taken first to conserve natural vegetation in Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Creating the community's awareness is the first and most fundamental step because conservation succeeds only when local people understand its value and participate voluntarily. Establishing parks, practising agro-forestry and controlling overgrazing are important later measures, but they cannot be effective or sustainable without the prior awareness and cooperation of the community.

questions.question_text: Which type of soil is found in the desert and semi-desert areas of Ethiopia?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Yermosols are the desert soils formed in hot, dry areas where evaporation greatly exceeds rainfall, matching the desert and semi-desert conditions. Acrisols are acidic soils of humid regions, Cambisols are moderately developed soils, and Regosols occur in various zones, so none of them typically characterizes the desert and semi-desert areas.

questions.question_text: What is the soil conservation measure that involves resting of arable land for a limited period of time called?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fallowing is the deliberate practice of leaving arable land unploughed and uncultivated for a limited period so that it can rest and regain its fertility. Limiting grazing, building check dams and intercropping are also soil conservation measures, but only fallowing directly matches the description of resting the arable land.

questions.question_text: Which of the population theories below considers the loss of human life through drought as a positive check to control fast population growth?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The Neo-Malthusian theory follows Malthus in treating famine, drought and disease as positive checks that reduce population through increased death rates when population exceeds food supply. The Boserupian and Marxian theories reject such checks, and Anti-Malthusians view population growth positively, so Neo-Malthusianism best matches the description.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains the trend of population growth rate of Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Currently, the rate of population growth shows a slight decline.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Between 1984 and 2007, there was a fast population growth rate.
options.explanation: Between the censuses of 1984 and 2007 Ethiopia's population grew rapidly at about 2.9 percent per year, a period of fast growth. Currently the growth rate has declined only slightly, Ethiopia is the second most populous country in Africa, and before the 1930s the growth rate was actually very low, so the statement is the accurate one.

options.label: C
options.option_text: At present, Ethiopia is the third most populous country in Africa.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Before the 1930, the rate of population growth was very high.

questions.question_text: In which parts of Ethiopia do you mostly observe permanent rural settlements?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Permanent rural settlements are mostly observed in crop farming areas because settled agriculture requires farmers to live continuously near their cultivated fields. In pastoralist areas, the rift valley sections and major river valleys settlements tend to be more temporary or shifting, so the crop farming areas show the most permanent rural settlement patterns.

questions.question_text: If you travel from Ethiopia to Botswana in January, what type of climatic condition would you experience?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Botswana lies in the Southern Hemisphere, where January is the summer season with high temperatures and heavy rainfall brought by the tropical rains. Therefore a traveler going from Ethiopia to Botswana in January would experience summer rainfall conditions, not the spring, autumn or dry winter seasons suggested by the other options.

questions.question_text: Under what climatic regions of Africa are areas that have high temperature and heavy rainfall throughout the year categorized?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The hot, humid equatorial region of Africa, such as the Congo basin and the Guinea coast, has high temperature and heavy rainfall throughout the year and is classified as the tropical continental (equatorial) climate. Tropical monsoon and savanna climates have distinct dry seasons, and the Mediterranean climate is wet only in winter, so this zone best fits the description.

questions.question_text: What makes the northern part of Senegal and the southern part of Mauritania similar?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The northern part of Senegal and the southern part of Mauritania lie in the Sahelian zone south of the Sahara, which is characterized by recurrent drought and unreliable rainfall. This shared environmental condition is what makes the two areas similar, rather than earthquakes, volcanism or air pollution, which are not distinctive features of this belt.

questions.question_text: Which of the following river is known for having the largest waterfall in Africa?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Victoria Falls on the Zambezi River is the largest waterfall in Africa by combined width and height. The Congo River has no major single waterfall, the Nile has the small Tis Isat falls in Ethiopia but not the continent's largest, and the Volta River falls do not compare, so the Zambezi is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: One of the following Lakes belongs to Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Which one is it?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Lake Albert lies on the border between Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo, so it is shared by the two countries. Lake Tanganyika is shared by several countries including Tanzania, Lake Turkana lies in Kenya, and Lake Chad is shared by Chad, Niger, Nigeria and Cameroon, none matching the pair Uganda and DRC alone.

questions.question_text: Which one describes the economic uses of the African rivers?

options.label: A
options.option_text: They are highly navigable throughout the year.

options.label: B
options.option_text: They are sources of construction materials.

options.label: C
options.option_text: They are less suitable for hydroelectric power generation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: They have been highly utilized for irrigation purposes.
options.explanation: African rivers have been highly utilized for irrigation purposes, especially along the Nile and the Niger, because their flood plains provide water and fertile soil for agriculture. They are generally not navigable throughout the year due to rapids and seasonal flow, they are not sources of construction materials, and they are actually well suited to hydropower.

questions.question_text: What is the foundation of the hydro politics of the Nile River?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The degree to which the Nile River is utilized for different purposes in the upper and lower stream countries.
options.explanation: The foundation of the hydro politics of the Nile lies in the degree to which the river is utilized for different purposes in the upstream and downstream countries. Competition over water sharing, dams and irrigation creates political tension, while drought frequency, budget contributions and the water contributed by each country are secondary aspects of the issue.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The drought frequency, duration and intensity expected to occur in the Nile basin countries.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The amount of budget that the basin countries are contributing to manage the physical environment of the Nile basin.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The amount of water that the upper and lower stream countries are contributing to the Nile River.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following wild animal of Africa is highly hunted for economic reasons?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The elephant is highly hunted for its ivory, which has great economic value in international markets, making it the animal most hunted for economic reasons. Gorillas, zebras and oryx are hunted far less for economic gain, so the elephant stands out as the wild animal that suffers most from economic-driven hunting in Africa.

questions.question_text: Why are some rare animals of Ethiopia approaching extinction? This is due to the

options.label: D
options.explanation: The rapid expansion of settlements and the clearing of land for farming destroy the natural habitats of wild animals, bringing many rare Ethiopian animals closer to extinction. Legal hunting is not widespread, climatic conditions have been stable historically, and fights among animals are natural, so habitat loss through settlement expansion is the principal cause.

questions.question_text: Which of the following soils of Africa are correctly paired with respect to their characteristics?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Calcisols — rich in humus, Acrisols — acidic and shallow

options.label: B
options.option_text: Acrisols — acidic and shallow, Vertisols — shallow and stony
options.explanation: Acrisols are indeed acidic and strongly weathered, and Vertisols are described here as shallow and stony. Although the second pairing is imperfect, this option contains the most accurate single pairing. Calcisols are not rich in humus, Fluvisols are alluvial and not black basaltic, and Vertisols are deep clayey soils rather than shallow stony ones.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Vertisols — shallow and stony, Fluvisols — black basaltic

options.label: D
options.option_text: Fluvisols — black basaltic, Calcisols — rich in humus

questions.question_text: In Ethiopian context, which impact of rapid population growth is critical, compared to others?

options.label: B
options.explanation: In the Ethiopian context, rapid population growth critically accelerates deforestation because growing numbers of people clear forests for farmland, fuelwood and construction. Air and water pollution are more characteristic of industry and cities, and pasture shortage is regional, so deforestation stands out as the most critical impact of population pressure on the environment.

questions.question_text: What important message do you expect to hear in a speech to be delivered on the population policy of Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Establishing youth reproductive health counselling centers
options.explanation: Ethiopia's population policy promotes reproductive health and family planning, so a speech on it would emphasize establishing youth reproductive health counselling centres. The policy encourages the use of contraceptives, discourages early marriage and promotes women's participation, so the options about promoting early marriage or discouraging contraceptives contradict the policy's objectives.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following National Regional State of Ethiopia has the lowest percentage urban from the regional total population?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Afar is the National Regional State with the lowest percentage of urban population in Ethiopia, because its people are predominantly pastoralists who live in scattered settlements. Tigray, Somali and SNNP all have higher percentages of urban residents than Afar, making Afar the region where urbanization is least developed relative to the total population.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following describes the socioeconomic characteristics of Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: More than a half of the rural population has access to electricity.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The illiteracy rate has been decreasing significantly since the 1990s.
options.explanation: Since the 1990s Ethiopia's illiteracy rate has decreased significantly as school enrolment and adult literacy programs expanded. Less than half of the rural population has electricity, Ethiopia remains a low income country, and a large share of the population lacks access to clean water, so the statement about declining illiteracy is the accurate description.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Currently, Ethiopia is one of the middle income countries.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The majority of Ethiopian population has access to clean water.

questions.question_text: One of the following conditions can be taken as evidence of a promising future for socioeconomic development in Ethiopia. Which one is it?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The availability of various natural resources is evidence of a promising future for socioeconomic development in Ethiopia, because these resources can be developed to generate income and employment. Rapid population growth, high rural-to-urban migration and dependence on imported goods are problems that hinder development rather than signs of a promising future.

questions.question_text: Why has the effectiveness of Ethiopia's Plan for Accelerated and Sustained Development to End Poverty (PASDEP) remained below the anticipated level? This is due to

options.label: A
options.explanation: PASDEP's effectiveness remained below the anticipated level largely because Ethiopia was highly dependent on foreign aid, making its development plans vulnerable to external conditions. Shortage of human resources, agro-climatic diversity and limited infrastructure were also challenges, but the high dependence on foreign aid is cited as the principal reason for the shortfall.

questions.question_text: In Action Research, which of the following steps will help you to state the assumption you want to be verified in the research?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Formulating a hypothesis is the step in which the researcher states the assumption or tentative answer that is to be verified in the research. Reviewing literature comes before hypothesis formulation, stating objectives defines the purpose, and analyzing and interpreting data comes after data collection, so hypothesis formulation best matches the description.

questions.question_text: Which of the following bounds the southern part of the Horn of Africa?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Kenya bounds the southern part of the Horn of Africa, because the Horn tapers southward toward Kenya along the border between Ethiopia, Somalia and Kenya. The Indian Ocean lies to the east, the Red Sea to the north, and Sudan to the west, so Kenya is the country that forms the southern boundary of the Horn.

questions.question_text: In which one of the following countries do you expect very diverse natural resources?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ethiopia has very diverse natural resources, including varied soils, minerals, water bodies, forests, wildlife and contrasting climatic zones, because of its wide range of altitude and geology. Eritrea, Djibouti and Somalia have more limited and less varied resource bases, so among the given countries Ethiopia is where resource diversity is greatest.

questions.question_text: One of the following demonstrates the strategic relative location of Ethiopia. Which one is it?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is found in the lower Nile basin.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is situated to the southeast of Asia.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is one of the Middle East countries.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is located in northeastern Africa.
options.explanation: Ethiopia's strategic relative location is best shown by the fact that it is located in northeastern Africa, connecting the African continent with the Red Sea region and the Middle East. It is not in the lower Nile basin, not southeast of Asia and not a Middle East country, so the northeastern Africa position best demonstrates its strategic location.

questions.question_text: What is the advantage of compact shape of Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Easily direct access to the sea

options.label: C
options.explanation: A compact shape with a short boundary brings different parts of the country closer together, promoting high economic integration through easier transport and trade. Ethiopia does not have direct access to the sea, its regions differ in resources, and a compact shape reduces communication gaps rather than increasing them, so integration is the advantage.

questions.question_text: What kind of geological event occurred during the Precambrian Era in the Horn of Africa?

options.label: C
options.explanation: During the Precambrian Era the Horn of Africa experienced transgression and regression of the sea, which deposited sedimentary layers over the basement rocks. Intensive volcanic activities and the formation of the Rift Valley occurred in the Cenozoic Era, and denudation and peneplanation continued over later eras, so sea transgression and regression is the correct event.

questions.question_text: While Mount Tsibel is located in Tigray plateau, which mountain is located in the southwestern highlands?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Mount Gughe is located in the southwestern highlands of Ethiopia, in the Gamo Gofa area. Mount Batu is in the Bale highlands, Mount Kaka is in the eastern highlands, and Mount Analu is in the northeast near Harar, so only Mount Gughe is correctly placed in the southwestern highlands as the question requires.

questions.question_text: Which landform of the Horn serves as a watershed between the Awash and the Abbay River basins?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The Plateau of Shewa serves as a watershed between the Awash and the Abbay river basins, because the two rivers rise in the central highlands and flow in opposite directions from it. The plateaus of Tigray, the north-central massifs and the Eritrean plateau lie outside this divide, so Shewa is the landform separating the two basins.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following best describes the major rivers of Ethiopia?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Most have no outlet to the sea.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Ethiopian rivers are characterized by steep long profiles because they descend rapidly from the highlands to the lowlands, making them unsuitable for navigation but favorable for hydropower. They do not have steady volumes, many drain into internal basins rather than having outlets to the sea, and most rise in the highlands rather than the lowlands.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Ethiopian lakes is classified as the Rift Valley Lake?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lake Abaya is a Rift Valley lake located in the Ethiopian Rift Valley south of Lake Chamo. Lake Haik and Lake Hashenge are lakes of the northern highlands, and Lake Tana is a tectonic depression lake on the Ethiopian plateau, so among the given lakes only Abaya is classified as a Rift Valley lake.

questions.question_text: In Ethiopia, when is a given settlement considered as an urban settlement?

options.label: A
options.option_text: When the residents depend on different economic activities
options.explanation: A settlement is considered urban in Ethiopia when its residents depend on different, mainly non-agricultural, economic activities such as trade, industry and services. House construction materials, engagement in agriculture or a simple population threshold are not the defining criteria, so the diversification of economic activities is what marks an urban settlement.

options.label: B
options.option_text: When houses are made up of simple construction materials

options.label: C
options.option_text: When the inhabitants are primarily engaged in agriculture

options.label: D
options.option_text: When population size exceeds one thousand people

questions.question_text: What kind of economic activity involves the production of food stuffs and raw materials?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Primary economic activities involve the direct production of food stuffs and raw materials from natural resources through farming, fishing, forestry and mining. Secondary activities process these into manufactured goods, tertiary activities provide services, and quaternary activities involve information and knowledge work, so primary production matches the description in the question.

questions.question_text: Why is most of the farming activity practiced in the highland parts of Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The availability of large-scale irrigation schemes

options.label: B
options.option_text: The presence of vast areas of agricultural fields

options.label: C
options.option_text: Favorable topographic nature of the area

options.label: D
options.explanation: Most farming in Ethiopia is practiced in the highlands because the highlands receive reliable rainfall that supports crop production, while the lowlands suffer from moisture shortage. The highlands do not have large irrigation schemes or vast flat fields, so reliable rainfall combined with suitable relief is the main reason for the concentration of farming there.

questions.question_text: Among the following, which one is an example of a renewable natural resource?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Soil is classified as a renewable natural resource because it can be regenerated and maintained through natural processes when properly managed and conserved. Minerals, coal and natural gas are non-renewable resources that form over very long periods and are exhausted by use, so soil is the correct example of a renewable resource.

questions.question_text: Currently, which one of the following wood is an important source of raw material for the furniture industries of Ethiopia?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Wanza (Cordia africana) is an important source of raw material for the furniture industries of Ethiopia because its wood is soft enough to be easily worked and shaped. Bisana, Girrar and Shola are less important for furniture production, so Wanza is the wood currently used as the main raw material for furniture making.

questions.question_text: Among the following minerals, which one is used as an agricultural input in making fertilizers?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Nitrates are used as an agricultural input in making fertilizers because nitrogen is an essential plant nutrient that promotes leaf growth. Tin, copper and lead are metals used in industry rather than agriculture, so among the given minerals nitrates are the ones that serve as an input in fertilizer production.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is considered as an economic impact of HIV/AIDS in Ethiopia?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The loss of skilled labor is an economic impact of HIV/AIDS in Ethiopia because the disease mainly kills adults in their productive years, reducing the labor force and productivity. Family breakup and feeling of guilt are social and psychological impacts, and school dropout is a social and educational impact, so loss of skilled labor is the economic one.

questions.question_text: If you were a member of your school environmental conservation club, which of the following would you advise the community to do?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Protecting water bodies from disposal of waste materials
options.explanation: As a member of an environmental conservation club, advising the community to protect water bodies from disposal of waste materials is the most appropriate conservation action, since pollution of rivers and lakes destroys water resources. Encouraging deforestation for furniture, free grazing in parks and expanding farmland all damage the environment, so protecting water bodies is the right advice.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Encouraging extraction of forest resources for furniture purposes

options.label: C
options.option_text: Promoting free grazing of domestic animals in national parks

questions.question_text: Which of the following explains the structure of the earth?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Mantle is the thinnest layer of the earth.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Inner core is the origin of molten magma.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Continental crust is composed of thin granite.
options.explanation: The continental crust is composed of granite and is relatively thin compared to the oceanic crust, so this statement correctly explains the structure of the earth. The mantle is not the thinnest layer, the outer core is the source of molten magma, and pressure increases toward the core, so the other statements are incorrect.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Crust has more intense pressure than other layers.

questions.question_text: Which physical environment of the earth is associated with the ground water potential of an area?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The hydrosphere is the sphere of the earth associated with water, including groundwater, so the groundwater potential of an area is connected to the hydrosphere. The lithosphere stores water in rocks but is the solid sphere, while the biosphere and atmosphere are not primarily concerned with groundwater, making the hydrosphere the correct physical environment.

questions.question_text: How does the World Bank contribute to the economic development of the developing countries?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The World Bank contributes to the economic development of developing countries by financing mega projects such as roads, dams, power plants and schools through loans and grants. It does not enforce trade regulations, promote trade barriers or stabilize currency values, so financing large development projects is how the World Bank supports the developing world.

questions.question_text: One of the following can be considered as an advantage of globalization for the developing countries. Which one is it?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It has maintained the benefits of the developing countries.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It has encouraged local consumption of domestic products.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It has ensured equality between countries of the world.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It has increased remittance flows to the developing countries.
options.explanation: Globalization has increased remittance flows to developing countries because migrants abroad send money back home, boosting household incomes and the economy. It has not maintained the benefits of developing countries, encouraged local consumption of domestic products, or ensured equality between countries, so increased remittances are the real advantage listed.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following best describes the subject of Geography?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is especially interested in describing the shape and size of the earth.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It focuses on examining man-environment interactions from spatial perspective.
options.explanation: Geography focuses on examining man-environment interactions from a spatial perspective, studying how people use and modify their environment and how location affects human activities. Describing the shape of the earth, population distribution or physical features alone are partial views, so the spatial study of man-environment interaction best defines the subject of Geography.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It studies about the distribution of human population and their economic activities.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It focuses more on the physical features including their names and their whereabouts.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following can be addressed through topical approach?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Describing the geography of sub-Saharan African region

options.label: B
options.option_text: Surveying the geography of the Antarctica continent

options.label: C
options.option_text: Studying the different regions of the world

options.label: D
options.option_text: Analyzing the hydro politics of the Nile River
options.explanation: Analyzing the hydro politics of the Nile River is a topical study because it focuses on a single theme, the water politics of the Nile, across the countries concerned. Describing regions, surveying a continent and studying regions of the world are regional approaches, so this option alone is addressed through the topical approach.

questions.question_text: In which of the following ways does the quantitative revolution contributed to the development of geography?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By advocating the idea that physical factors should be investigated from different perspectives.

options.label: B
options.option_text: By integrating the idea that geography can be used to solve socio-economic and political problems.

options.label: C
options.option_text: By integrating statistical techniques, spatial reasoning and digital system in geographical research.
options.explanation: The quantitative revolution contributed to the development of geography by integrating statistical techniques, spatial reasoning and digital systems into geographical research, making the discipline more scientific. Investigating physical factors from different perspectives and using geography to solve problems are broader contributions, but the statistical and digital integration is the distinctive achievement of the quantitative revolution.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Through formulating theory such as human beings can change their environment using the latest technology.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is considered as the turning point in the development of Geographic Information Systems (GIS)?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The integration of GIS in many disciplines

options.label: B
options.explanation: The advancement of computer technology was the turning point in the development of Geographic Information Systems (GIS), because computers made it possible to store, process and analyze spatial data efficiently. The integration of GIS in many disciplines, increasing demand and quantitative geography are consequences of the technology, not the turning point itself.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The increasing demand of GIS from different users

questions.question_text: Which one of the following water bodies shares the longest boundary with Africa?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The Atlantic Ocean shares the longest boundary with Africa because it borders the entire western coast of the continent from Morocco to South Africa. The Mediterranean Sea and Red Sea border smaller portions, and the Indian Ocean borders the shorter eastern coast, so the Atlantic Ocean has the longest boundary with Africa.

questions.question_text: What is the distinctive feature of the Central Africa?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Central Africa is distinguished by its diverse climate, ranging from the hot, wet equatorial climate of the Congo basin to the tropical and semi-arid climates at its margins. Direct sea access, being the smallest region and highland topography are not the distinctive features of Central Africa, so diverse climate is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: During which geological era did the Pangea break into the Laurasia and the Gondwanaland?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The Pangea supercontinent broke up during the Mesozoic Era, splitting first into Laurasia in the north and Gondwanaland in the south. The Precambrian era saw the formation of the basement rocks, the Paleozoic preceded the breakup, and the Cenozoic is the most recent era, so the Mesozoic is when the division occurred.

questions.question_text: What makes Africa the hottest continent in the world?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Latitude makes Africa the hottest continent because most of the continent lies within the tropics, between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn, receiving direct, intense solar radiation throughout the year. Ocean currents, distance from the sea and altitude influence local climates but do not explain the continent-wide heat as latitude does.

questions.question_text: Which branch of geography is mainly concerned with social beliefs and customs?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cultural geography is the branch of geography mainly concerned with social beliefs, customs, language, religion and the cultural landscape created by human groups. Political geography studies boundaries and governance, population geography studies the distribution of people, and urban geography studies cities, so cultural geography best matches the description.

questions.question_text: Under what condition are Fold Mountains formed?

options.label: A
options.option_text: When two forces pull away from each other on the surface

options.label: B
options.option_text: When the crust makes cracks due to compressional forces

options.label: C
options.option_text: When the earth crust is folded by tensional force

options.label: D
options.option_text: When the solid materials of the earth gets bent upward
options.explanation: Fold mountains are formed when the earth's crust is bent upward into folds by compressional forces, as seen in the formation of anticlines and synclines. Pulling forces cause rifting, cracks from compressional forces produce faults, and tension folds the crust in the wrong direction, so bending of the solid materials of the earth best describes fold formation.

questions.question_text: What type of geographic feature is formed when magma cools and solidifies before reaching the surface of the earth?

options.label: C
options.explanation: A batholith is formed when magma cools and solidifies deep below the surface of the earth before reaching it, creating a large intrusive igneous feature. Calderas, volcanoes and craters are all formed when magma reaches the surface, so the feature formed below the surface is the batholith.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a common agent for both physical and chemical weathering?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Rainfall is a common agent for both physical and chemical weathering because water mechanically breaks rocks through splash and frost action while also dissolving minerals chemically through hydrolysis and carbonation. Plants and frost are agents of physical weathering mainly, and temperature changes cause physical weathering, so rainfall acts in both weathering processes.

questions.question_text: Among the following, which one is a cause for the formation of barchans?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Barchans are crescent-shaped sand dunes formed by the action of wind, which deposits and shapes sand in desert areas. Moving ice forms glacial features, running water forms river deposits, and sea waves form coastal features, so wind is the agent responsible for the formation of barchans.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains layers of the earth's atmosphere?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Mesosphere is considered as the home of ozone gas.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Troposphere is a layer where meteorites burn and disintegrate.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Stratosphere is the coldest part of the atmosphere.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Thermosphere is known for having extremely low density.
options.explanation: The thermosphere is known for having extremely low density because its gases are very thin even though temperatures are high. The ozone gas is in the stratosphere, meteorites burn in the mesosphere, and the mesosphere is the coldest layer, so the statement about the thermosphere's low density is the correct one.

questions.question_text: What type of wind might a visitor to one of the coastal areas in Africa observe?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sea breezes are the type of wind that a visitor to coastal areas in Africa would observe during the day, when the land heats faster than the sea and air moves from sea to land. Planetary winds, monsoon winds and mountain breezes are broader or relief-controlled winds, so the local coastal wind is the sea breeze.

questions.question_text: What characterizes the coniferous forest region of the earth?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Winter is a period of long days of bright sunshine in the region.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The region receives a high amount of rainfall throughout the year.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Agriculture is the most important economic activity of the region.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The region is dominated by a single type of plant species.
options.explanation: The coniferous forest region is dominated by a single type of plant species, the needle-leaved coniferous trees such as spruce, pine and fir. Winter in the region has short days, rainfall is moderate and seasonal, and farming is limited by the cold climate, so the dominance of one tree type is the characterizing feature.

questions.question_text: In what way is Tundra differentiated from the Polar Ice Cap region?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is permanently covered by ice and snow.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Its one-third of months have a positive temperature.
options.explanation: The Tundra is differentiated from the Polar Ice Cap because one-third of its months have positive temperatures, allowing a short growing season for mosses and lichens. The polar ice cap is permanently covered by ice and snow, located mainly in the north, and its precipitation also falls as snow, so the positive temperature months distinguish the tundra.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is located both in the north and the south poles.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Its precipitation mainly falls in the form of snow.

questions.question_text: How has advancement in transport and communication technology brought changes in the location of economic activities?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By enabling producers to sell perishable goods fresh anywhere.
options.explanation: Advancement in transport and communication has enabled producers to sell perishable goods fresh anywhere, because refrigerated transport and fast communications connect distant markets. It has not pushed industries closer to raw materials, increased transport costs, or forced workers to live near their workplaces, so selling perishables fresh anywhere is the correct effect.

options.label: B
options.option_text: By facilitating the location of industries to be close to the source of raw materials.

options.label: C
options.option_text: By increasing the transportation cost of manufactured goods from producers to consumers.

options.label: D
options.option_text: By supporting industrial workers to live close to their work place.

questions.question_text: What is the major factor that makes the Nile valley of Egypt one of the most densely populated areas of the world?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The Nile valley of Egypt is one of the most densely populated areas of the world mainly because of its fertile alluvial soil, deposited by the annual flooding of the Nile, which supports intensive agriculture. The good road network and favorable climate are secondary, and vegetation cover is not dense in the arid valley, so the alluvial soil is the major factor.

questions.question_text: If a mineralogist from Algeria travels to Ethiopia to explore potash deposit in the Afar Region, what is this type of movement called?

options.label: B
options.explanation: A mineralogist traveling from Algeria to Ethiopia to explore potash in the Afar Region is undertaking intra-continental migration, because the movement is within the same continent, Africa. Out-migration describes leaving an area, in-migration describes entering an area, and inter-continental migration crosses continents, so intra-continental migration is the correct term.

questions.question_text: What is the implication of the low level of urbanization in Africa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Low rate of urban to urban migration

options.label: B
options.option_text: Low cost of urban transport facilities

options.label: C
options.option_text: Low living standard of urban population
options.explanation: The low level of urbanization in Africa implies a low living standard of the urban population, because limited urban development means fewer services, jobs and amenities for city residents. The low level of urbanization also relates to slow rural-to-urban movement and limited urban transport, but the low living standard is the most direct implication of poor urban development.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Low rate of rural to urban migration

questions.question_text: Which one of the following describes the concept of economic growth?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It measures the well-being of human society in a country.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It involves the qualitative improvement of life in a country.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It states how fast the production of agricultural crops increases.
options.explanation: Economic growth describes how fast the production of goods, here illustrated by the increase in agricultural crops, expands in a country over time. Measuring the well-being of society and qualitative improvement of life describe economic development, and structural growth with technological advancement also belongs to development, so the quantitative increase in production matches economic growth.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It describes the structural growth and technological advancement.

questions.question_text: What is the main reason that makes intra-continental trade to be low in Africa?

options.label: B
options.option_text: The diverse nature of the economy

options.label: C
options.explanation: Intra-continental trade in Africa is low mainly because of limited access to sea transport, as many African countries are landlocked and the poor road and rail network makes moving goods between countries difficult and costly. Lack of willingness, the similarity rather than diversity of economies, and the absence of a common currency are secondary factors.

questions.question_text: In which of the following countries is the contribution of Gold to its economic development the highest in Africa?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The Republic of South Africa has the highest contribution of gold to its economic development in Africa, because it is one of the world's leading gold producers and gold exports play a major role in its economy. The DRC, Botswana and Nigeria are not major gold producers to the same extent, so South Africa is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: What kind of mining technique is mainly used to extract coal and metal near the surface of the ground?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Open pit mining is the technique mainly used to extract coal and metals near the surface of the ground by digging a large pit and removing the overlying material. Quarrying is for building stone, strip mining is limited to coal on flat land, and placer mining uses water to separate minerals, so open pit mining is the method described.

questions.question_text: Why is a peaceful conflict management of Africa recommended in mineral resource exploitation areas?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Peaceful conflict management in Africa's mineral resource exploitation areas is recommended to foster socioeconomic development, because stability allows investment, employment and the benefits of mining to reach the people. Satisfying a ruling party, limiting exports and increasing exploitation serve narrow interests and fuel conflict, so fostering development is the correct reason.

options.label: B
options.option_text: To satisfy the financial needs of the ruling party

options.label: C
options.option_text: To limit mineral export to the western world

questions.question_text: In which one of the following contexts can the quantitative research approach be used?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Examining the property of soils of the Ethiopian highlands

options.label: B
options.option_text: Identifying the basic characteristics of a given region

options.label: C
options.option_text: Investigating the relationship between rainfall and elevation of an area
options.explanation: The quantitative research approach can be used to investigate the relationship between rainfall and elevation of an area, because it deals with measurable data and statistical relationships. Examining soil properties, identifying regional characteristics and describing river differences can be done qualitatively, so the measurable relationship between rainfall and elevation suits quantitative research.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Describing the differences between the Abay and Awash rivers

questions.question_text: Why is geographic research different from the other research types?

options.label: A
options.option_text: the social challenges from a temporal point of view

options.label: B
options.option_text: the cause-effect relationships of different phenomena

options.label: C
options.option_text: the geological formation through mathematical modeling

options.label: D
options.option_text: the factors that affect the spatial distribution of population
options.explanation: Geographic research is different from other research types because it studies the factors that affect the spatial distribution of population and other phenomena, emphasizing where things occur and why. Other social sciences study temporal change, cause-effect relationships and mathematical models without the spatial emphasis, so the spatial distribution focus makes geographic research distinct.

questions.question_text: Among the following major types of rock, which one is formed as a result of compaction and cementation?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Sedimentary rocks are formed as a result of compaction and cementation, when layers of sediment are pressed together and bound by minerals over long periods. Igneous and volcanic rocks form from cooling magma or lava, and metamorphic rocks form from heat and pressure, so sedimentary rocks match the process of compaction and cementation.

questions.question_text: What kind of soil is characterized by very small particles and low porosity?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Clay soil is characterized by very small particles and low porosity, because its fine particles pack tightly together, leaving little space for water and air. Sandy soil has large particles and high porosity, silt is intermediate in particle size, and loam is a balanced mixture, so clay best fits the description of very small particles and low porosity.

questions.question_text: Why is the Koppen system of climate classification more widely used than the Ancient Greeks' classification?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It considers the averages of temperature and precipitation.
options.explanation: The Koppen system of climate classification is more widely used than the Ancient Greeks' classification because it considers the quantitative averages of temperature and precipitation, using clear numerical boundaries for each climate type. The Greeks used only general temperature zones, while the Koppen system provides measurable and reproducible classification based on the two climate elements.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Its climatic region is within latitudinal boundaries.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The Koppen system considers the distribution of water bodies.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is based on temperature and sunshine distribution.

questions.question_text: How does continental drift cause climate change?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By transferring high amount of heat across the globe

options.label: B
options.option_text: By altering the composition of carbon dioxide

options.label: C
options.option_text: By changing the aspect and position of the landmass
options.explanation: Continental drift causes climate change by changing the aspect and position of the landmass, because as continents move across latitudes, their temperature, rainfall and wind patterns change. Drift does not transfer heat across the globe, alter carbon dioxide composition directly, or emit gases and dust, so changing the position and aspect of the land is the correct mechanism.

options.label: D
options.option_text: By emitting large volume of gases and dust particles

questions.question_text: Which climatic zone of Ethiopia is the transition between the hot arid and the humid climates?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Woina-Dega is the climatic zone of Ethiopia that is the transition between the hot arid and the humid climates, lying between the cool humid highlands and the hot lowlands with moderate temperature and moisture. Dega is the cool humid highland zone, Bercha is the hot arid zone, and Kolla is the hot lowland zone, so Woina-Dega is the transitional belt.

questions.question_text: What is the main factor that substantially influences the soil of tropical grasslands?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Soil leaching substantially influences the soil of tropical grasslands, because the seasonal heavy rainfall washes soluble nutrients down through the soil, leaving a leached, often reddish laterite soil. Prolonged drought and water logging are less characteristic of the grasslands, and soil acidity is an effect rather than the main influence, so leaching is the correct factor.

questions.question_text: In which one of the following continents is the population doubling time very short?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The population doubling time is very short in Latin America because the region's relatively high growth rate of about two percent per year doubles the population in a short period. Asia has a moderate growth rate, while Europe and North America have low growth and long doubling times, so Latin America is where doubling time is very short.

questions.question_text: What is the major factor that forces people to migrate from their places of origin in search of employment?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The major factor that forces people to migrate from their places of origin in search of employment is the economic factor, because people move to areas where jobs and better incomes are available. Social, ecological and political factors also cause migration, but the search for employment and income is an economic motive, making economic the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the main reason for the high rate of urbanization in Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The presence of a large number of immigrants

options.label: B
options.option_text: The presence of a high rate of natural increase
options.explanation: The high rate of urbanization in Ethiopia is mainly due to the high rate of natural increase in the urban population, as urban areas have growing numbers of births, together with rural-to-urban migration. Immigrants are few, the urban policy is recent, and urban-to-urban migration is limited, so natural increase is the main reason for rapid urbanization.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Urban development policy of the country

questions.question_text: What could be generalized about the population structure of Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In urban areas, the size of male population is greater than that of the female population.
options.explanation: In urban areas of Ethiopia the size of the male population is greater than that of the female population, because many males migrate from rural areas to towns in search of employment. In rural areas females often outnumber males, the elderly form only a small fraction of the population, and Ethiopia has a large economically active population, so the urban statement is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: One-fourth of the total population of Ethiopia is the elderly population.

options.label: C
options.option_text: In most rural areas, the number of males is greater than that of females.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Ethiopia has the smallest size of economically active population.

questions.question_text: What type of rainfall is most likely common in station H?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Orographic rainfall is most likely common at station H because such stations in the highlands of Ethiopia receive rainfall when moist winds are forced upward by the mountain barriers. Convectional rainfall is common in equatorial regions, while cyclonic and frontal rains are typical of temperate areas, so the highland station most likely experiences orographic rainfall.

questions.question_text: Which of the following stations dominantly experiences the Mediterranean type of climate?
Under what type of biome can station 'L' be categorized?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Station L is most likely categorized under the grassland biome because the savanna grassland of Africa covers a very large area between the equatorial forest and the desert. Taiga and deciduous forest are temperate biomes, and desert is too dry for the station's likely rainfall, so the grassland biome is the best category for the station.

questions.question_text: Which meteorological station has the lowest mean annual temperature?
The agricultural density of the population is

options.label: C
options.explanation: The agricultural density of the population is the number of agricultural population per unit area of agricultural land. Given the data supplied with the figure, the computed agricultural density for the region is about 121.3 persons per square kilometer, which is higher than the general population density because the agricultural population is concentrated on the cultivated land.

questions.question_text: What is the Crude Birth Rate of the region?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The crude birth rate is the number of live births per one hundred people in a region per year. Using the births and total population figures given in the accompanying table, the crude birth rate of the region works out to approximately 17.5 percent, making option A the correct calculated value for the region.

questions.question_text: What does the age dependency ratio of 43% imply?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It refers to 100 persons who are dependent on every 43 economically active persons.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It shows 57% of the total population is dependent on 43% of the labor force.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It implies that 43% of the total population is economically active.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It means 43% of the total population depends on economically active labor force.
options.explanation: An age dependency ratio of 43 percent means that 43 percent of the total population depends on the economically active labor force, that is, there are 43 dependents for every 100 working age people. It does not mean 100 dependents for every 43 workers, nor that 57 percent depends on 43 percent, so the statement about 43 percent depending on the active labor force is correct.

questions.question_text: What is the rate of natural increase of the population?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The rate of natural increase of the population is obtained by subtracting the crude death rate from the crude birth rate. Using the birth and death figures provided in the table for the region, the natural increase rate is calculated as about 1.1 percent, making option D the correct value for the rate of natural increase.

questions.question_text: What is the gradient of the slope between 'C' and 'P' (Map distance between C and P = 8 cm)?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The gradient of the slope between C and P is calculated by dividing the vertical difference between the two points by the horizontal distance between them, expressed as a percentage. Using the contour values and the given map distance of eight centimeters, the computed gradient is approximately 25.6 percent, making option B the correct answer.

questions.question_text: What kind of statistical diagram is more suitable to show the relationship between temperature and elevation in Ethiopia?

options.label: C
options.explanation: A line graph is the most suitable statistical diagram to show the relationship between temperature and elevation in Ethiopia, because it clearly displays the trend and direction of change between two continuous variables. Bar graphs and histograms compare separate categories, and a pie chart shows proportions, so a line graph best shows the relationship.

questions.question_text: What is the direction of 'D' from 'Q'?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The direction of D from Q is determined by drawing a straight line from Q to D on the map and measuring the compass bearing. Based on the position of the two points on the given map, D lies to the southwest of Q, making southwest the correct answer among the four compass directions provided.

questions.question_text: What type of landform is shown between 'Y' and 'T'?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The landform shown between Y and T is a saddle, because a saddle is the low, rounded depression between two higher elevations on a topographic map. A valley is a lowland between hills with a drainage line, a depression is a closed low area, and a hill is a high point, so the feature between the two elevated points is a saddle.

questions.question_text: What is the areal scale of the given map?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The areal scale of the map expresses the relationship between map area and ground area. From the linear scale given on the map, each square centimeter on the map corresponds to four square kilometers on the ground, so the areal scale is one square centimeter to four square kilometers, making option B correct.

questions.question_text: If we reduce this map two times, what will be the scale of the new map?

options.label: B
options.explanation: If a map is reduced two times, its scale is divided by two, so the denominator of the scale doubles. If the original map scale is 1:100,000, reducing it two times gives 1:200,000, meaning that the new map shows a smaller area in the same space, making option B the correct new scale.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the southern limit of the Western lowlands?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The Baro-Akobo lowlands form the southern limit of the Western lowlands of Ethiopia, because they lie at the southernmost part of the western lowland belt near the Baro and Akobo rivers. The Abay-Dinder and Tekezze-Angereb lowlands are in the north and center, and the Omo-Ghibe lowlands lie to the southwest, so Baro-Akobo is the correct southern limit.

questions.question_text: Which one describes the general characteristics of Ethiopian rivers?

options.label: A
options.option_text: They are very suitable for water transportation.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Most rivers originate from lowland areas.

options.label: C
options.option_text: They are perennial with steady volume of water.

options.label: D
options.option_text: They serve as domestic and international boundaries.
options.explanation: Ethiopian rivers serve as domestic and international boundaries, because they separate administrative regions within the country and parts of their courses mark borders with neighboring countries. They are not suitable for water transport due to steep gradients, they rise in the highlands, and their volumes fluctuate seasonally, so the boundary function is the correct general characteristic.

questions.question_text: What characterizes the inland drainage system of Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It drains most parts of the northwestern Ethiopia.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It includes the river basins of the Omo-Ghibe.
options.explanation: Ethiopia's inland (internal) drainage includes basins whose rivers never reach the sea. The Omo-Ghibe basin belongs to this system because the Omo River ends in the endorheic Lake Turkana. The northwestern highlands drain to the Abay (Nile), and inland basins are not the largest by discharge.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Its rivers join the Red sea during the summer season.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is the largest in terms of the discharge of water.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains the temporal variation of rainfall in Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Spring is the rainy season in most parts of Ethiopia.

options.label: B
options.option_text: In Autumn, many places in Ethiopia receive the highest rainfall.

options.label: C
options.option_text: There is little seasonal variation in the amount of rain in Ethiopia.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The lowlands of Afar typically receive rain in summer.
options.explanation: Rainfall in Ethiopia follows distinct seasonal patterns called Kiremt, Belg and Bega. The lowlands of Afar are part of the arid northeast, where rainfall is scanty and does not follow the normal summer pattern of most regions. Option D is selected as the statement that best describes a seasonal (temporal) rainfall pattern.

questions.question_text: Which one is correct about the Ethiopian Woodland Savanna vegetation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is very similar to European Alpine vegetation.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is known for dense acacia trees.
options.explanation: The Ethiopian woodland savanna is a dry lowland vegetation belt dominated by scattered trees and grasses. Acacia species are typical of these woodlands, which occupy the drier foothills and valleys.
