Alpine vegetation belongs to high altitudes, and riverside growth describes gallery forests, so the acacia statement is the most accurate.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It grows mainly along the river banks.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is found both in the highlands and lowlands.

questions.question_text: If you were asked by a tourist who wanted to see Chelad bahir in Ethiopia, which specific national park would be your recommendation?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Chelad bahir (Chew Bahir/Lake Stephanie) lies in the southwestern Rift Valley, close to the Omo region. Among the listed national parks, Nechisar in the south is the nearest park serving that area. The site is technically a wildlife reserve rather than a national park, so the intended answer is Nechisar Park.

questions.question_text: If you are asked to propose a strategy for conservation of wildlife where hunting is strictly forbidden, what would be your suggestion as conservation area?

options.label: A
options.explanation: In wildlife conservation, national parks are protected areas set aside for the full protection of animals and plants where hunting is strictly forbidden. Sanctuaries and game reserves permit regulated hunting, while zoological gardens keep animals in captivity. Therefore, a conservation area where hunting is completely banned is a national park.

questions.question_text: Which measure of soil conservation should be widely used against soil erosion in arid and semi-arid areas of the Horn?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Arid and semi-arid areas of the Horn suffer mainly from wind erosion, especially during the dry season. Shelter belts, rows of trees or shrubs planted as windbreaks, protect the soil from being blown away. Terracing suits steep slopes, intercropping improves fertility, and check dams control gullies in the wetter zones.

questions.question_text: Which of the following igneous rock has clearly observed crystals and coarse grains?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Granite is an intrusive igneous rock formed when magma cools slowly deep below the surface. Slow cooling allows large mineral crystals to grow, giving it clearly visible coarse grains. Obsidian and basalt cool rapidly at the surface and are glassy or fine grained, while marble is a metamorphic rock.

questions.question_text: One of the following is a poorly drained and aerated soil type. Which one is it?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Clay soils consist of very fine particles packed closely together, leaving little space for air and water to move. As a result, they are poorly drained and poorly aerated and often waterlogged. Sandy soils drain freely, loam is well balanced, and silt is intermediate, so clay is the correct choice.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about natural causes of climate change?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Continental drift changes the flow of ocean currents and winds.
options.explanation: Natural climate change results from processes such as continental drift, which alters the positions of continents and thereby changes ocean currents and wind patterns over geological time. Volcanic eruptions generally inject dust and aerosols that cool the air, and current major climate change is dominated by human activities, not natural causes.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Volcanic eruption leads to atmospheric heating.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Natural causes are becoming the major causes of climate change.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Ocean currents via releasing water vapor have a net cooling effect.

questions.question_text: How do you explain the spatio-temporal distribution of temperature in Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Annual range of temperature is greater than the daily range.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Temperature decreases from the center to the peripheries.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Daily range of temperature is the highest during winter season.
options.explanation: In Ethiopia, because of its tropical location, the annual range of temperature is small, while the daily range is relatively large. During the dry winter (Bega) season, clear skies and little cloud cover allow strong daytime heating and rapid night-time cooling, so the daily range of temperature is highest then. Highlands never show the highest annual range.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Highlands exhibit the highest annual range of temperature.

questions.question_text: Which climatic zone of Ethiopia experiences hot temperature, small cloud cover and very windy conditions throughout the year?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bereha is the hot arid climatic zone of Ethiopia, lying below about 500 metres in the lowlands. It experiences high temperatures, small cloud cover and strong winds throughout the year. Woina Dega, Dega and Wurch are cooler highland zones, so they cannot match these characteristics.

questions.question_text: Why are some regions of the world more sparsely populated than others? This is because of the

options.label: D
options.explanation: Regions with rugged topography, such as high mountains, deep valleys and steep slopes, are difficult to farm, build on and travel across, so they remain sparsely populated. Fertile soil, favourable climate and farming opportunities attract dense settlement. Therefore, rugged topography best explains why some parts of the world are thinly populated.

questions.question_text: What type of migration results when governments move war and natural disaster-affected people to new places?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Resettlement is the organized movement of people, often by the government, from disaster-affected or war-torn areas to new places. Refugees and evacuees move on their own for safety, while transhumance is seasonal herding. Government relocation of affected people to new homes is therefore described as resettlement.

questions.question_text: How do we generalize the level of the world's urbanization across continents?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Africa has the highest level of urbanization.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Asia has a higher level of urbanization than Latin America.

options.label: C
options.option_text: North America is the most urbanized continent.
options.explanation: Levels of urbanization differ across continents. North America has the highest proportion of people living in urban areas, around four-fifths of its population. Africa and Asia remain less urbanized, and urbanization in most developing regions is still moderate, so North America is the most urbanized continent.

options.label: D
options.option_text: There is a high level of urbanization in the developing world.

questions.question_text: How do we describe rural and urban settlements?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Rural areas are known by dense population.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Urban settlements are towns and cities whose streets and layouts are planned, with concentrated populations and a complex division of labour. Rural settlements are dispersed and tied to farming, with fewer planned features. Rural areas are not densely populated, so planned streets best describe urban settlements.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Urban areas have a low division of labor.

questions.question_text: Why was hilltops mainly preferred for the establishment of old urban centers of Ethiopia? This was due to their

options.label: B
options.explanation: Old Ethiopian towns were commonly built on hilltops mainly for security. High, defensible positions gave clear views of approaching enemies and natural protection from attack. Water, fertile soil and beauty could be found in many places, but defence was the decisive reason for choosing hilltop sites for the old urban centres.

questions.question_text: What is the size of Africa compared to the sizes of other continents?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is the largest continent next to the Asian continent.
options.explanation: Africa is the second largest continent, covering about 30 million square kilometres, and is surpassed only by Asia. It is roughly one-fifth of the earth's land surface, not half, and it is about the same size as North America rather than double or four times Antarctica. Therefore Africa is largest next to Asia.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It constitutes half of the total land surface of the earth.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It nearly doubles the total size of North America.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is four times larger than the size of Antarctica.

questions.question_text: How do the relative compact shape and unbroken coastline of Africa impact its development?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Its compact shape discourages intra-continental movements.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Its unbroken coastline makes the continent rich in natural harbors.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Its unbroken coastline encourages external communications.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Its compact shape relatively eases administration and defense.
options.explanation: Africa's relatively compact shape and unbroken coastline mean there are few natural harbours and limited coastal indentations, but its compact form keeps the interior close to the coasts. This compactness makes administration, movement and defence relatively easier than on deeply divided continents, so the shape eases administration and defence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following distinguishes the regions of Africa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Eastern Africa is the smallest in terms of area.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Western Africa has the highest urban population.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Central Africa is the most sparsely populated.
options.explanation: Among the regions of Africa, Central Africa, dominated by the equatorial Congo basin, has the lowest population density and is the most sparsely populated. Western Africa has the largest number of countries and the biggest population, Eastern Africa is not the smallest region, and Northern Africa is the smallest in area.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Northern Africa has the highest number of countries.

questions.question_text: Which region of Africa lies both in the northern and southern hemispheres?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Eastern Africa is the region that lies in both the northern and southern hemispheres, because the equator passes through countries such as Kenya, Uganda and Somalia. Northern Africa lies entirely north of the equator, Southern Africa is almost wholly south, and Western Africa is mostly in the northern hemisphere.

questions.question_text: Among the following geological events, which one happened during the Cenozoic Era?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Formation of plateau and volcanic mountains
options.explanation: During the Cenozoic Era, major earth movements, uplift and volcanic activity shaped the present landscape. The Ethiopian plateau and its volcanic mountains were formed during this era as part of the rift valley development. Laurasia and Gondwanaland formed much earlier, while sea transgression and regression belong to older eras.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The slow sinking and rising of landmass

options.label: D
options.option_text: Transgression and regression of the sea

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the African plateaus?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Plateaus account for more than half of the landscape of the continent.
options.explanation: Africa is called a plateau continent because plateaus cover well over half of its surface. High plateaus are concentrated in Eastern and Southern Africa, while Northern and Western Africa are mainly low-lying plains. The Bihé plateau in Angola is a high plateau, not a low one, so option A is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Bihé plateau is an example of low plateaus.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Eastern Africa is largely areas of low plateaus.

options.label: D
options.option_text: High plateaus are abundantly found in Northern and Western Africa.

questions.question_text: Which wind type is dominantly affecting the tropical climate of Africa?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The tropical climate of Africa is largely controlled by the trade winds, which converge at the Intertropical Convergence Zone and bring seasonal rainfall. The Guinea monsoon affects only part of West Africa, while polar easterlies and westerlies influence middle and high latitudes. Trade winds are therefore the dominant wind system of the tropics.

questions.question_text: How do you describe the seasonal temperature condition of Africa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Months from March to May exhibit low temperature in the most parts of the northern Africa.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Sahara Desert experiences a relatively high temperature between June to August.
options.explanation: In June, July and August the sun is overhead in the northern hemisphere, so the Sahara Desert receives its highest temperatures. Southern Africa experiences high temperatures from December to February because that is its summer, while northern Africa is coolest when the sun is over the Tropic of Capricorn.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Southern Africa experiences low temperature from December to February.

options.label: D
options.option_text: When the sun is overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn, northern parts of Africa experience the highest temperature.

questions.question_text: One of the following is the main feature of warm temperate continental climatic region of Africa. Which one is it?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Its main source of rainfall is from the Atlantic Ocean.
options.explanation: The warm temperate continental climatic region of Africa, found mainly on the South African plateau, is dry with a large daily temperature range. Its rainfall is linked to Atlantic Ocean moisture, while the region is not the largest climatic region nor located in northern Africa. It receives low, not high, rainfall.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is mostly found in the northern parts of Africa.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It occupies the largest climatic region of Africa.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It has a high rainfall and low air temperature.

questions.question_text: Which part of Africa is highly prone to drought?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The Sahel, lying immediately north of the tropics between the desert and the savanna, receives low and unreliable rainfall and is therefore the part of Africa most prone to drought. The northern and southern tips have Mediterranean rainfall, and Central Africa is wet, so the belt north of the tropics is the answer.

questions.question_text: Which drainage system of Africa has only one major river and flows northwards?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The Mediterranean Sea drainage system of Africa is fed mainly by the Nile, the continent's only major river flowing northwards into the Mediterranean. The Indian Ocean and Atlantic systems contain many rivers, while inland drainage has no outlet to the sea. Hence the Mediterranean system fits the description given.

questions.question_text: Among the following lakes of Africa, which one is a non-rift valley lake?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Lake Victoria is not a rift valley lake; it lies in a shallow depression between the eastern and western arms of the East African Rift and is thought to have formed by basin downwarping. Lakes Tanganyika, Turkana and Kivu all lie within rift valley troughs, so Victoria is the non-rift valley lake.

questions.question_text: In what ways does the presence of many waterfalls, rapids and steep courses of African rivers tend to mainly benefit the socioeconomic development of the continent?

options.label: A
options.explanation: African rivers often cross steep courses with many waterfalls and rapids, and this provides excellent potential for generating hydroelectric power. Fast-flowing water cannot easily serve navigation, and fishing and irrigation benefit more from calm rivers. Electricity generation is therefore the main socioeconomic benefit of falls and rapids.

options.label: B
options.option_text: By creating conducive environment for fishing

questions.question_text: How do you analyze the hydro politics of the Nile River?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Lower course countries are the least beneficiary of the River water.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Great Ethiopian Renaissance Dam will benefit the neighboring countries.
options.explanation: The Great Ethiopian Renaissance Dam on the Blue Nile will generate electricity and enable regulated downstream flow, benefiting neighbouring countries through power trade and reduced flooding. Historically Egypt and Sudan were the main beneficiaries, the Blue Nile supplies most of the water, and Nile basin utilization has been unequal.

options.label: C
options.option_text: White Nile is the largest supplier of water to the Nile River.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Historically, Nile basin countries have been fairly utilizing the River water.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of human influence on land use?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Land use is influenced by both natural conditions and human activities. Agricultural programs, such as cultivation, settlement expansion and irrigation schemes, are human influences that modify how land is used. Soil quality, moisture availability and environmental conditions are natural factors, so agricultural programs represent the human influence.

questions.question_text: If carefully and scientifically managed, which of the following resources tends to regenerate?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Soil is a renewable resource because, if carefully and scientifically managed, it can regenerate and maintain its fertility through natural processes. Petroleum, natural gas and coal are non-renewable fossil fuels formed over millions of years, so they cannot regenerate within a human timeframe even with careful management.

questions.question_text: Among the most common woods of Ethiopia, which one has been traditionally used for making water pipes and baskets?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bamboo is a fast-growing woody grass traditionally used in Ethiopia for making water pipes, baskets, fences and simple furniture. Its hollow, strong and flexible stems make it ideal for such crafts. Olea, kerero and zigba are timber trees used mainly for building and woodwork rather than pipes and baskets.

questions.question_text: What is the main environmental policy focus area of the Ethiopian green legacy program?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Policy related to soil and agriculture

options.label: D
options.option_text: Policy allied to forest, woodland and tree resources
options.explanation: The Green Legacy Initiative of Ethiopia is an environmental policy mainly focused on planting trees and restoring forest, woodland and tree resources. Its aim is to combat deforestation, land degradation and climate change through massive afforestation campaigns. Energy, soil, agriculture and water policies exist, but forests and trees are the central focus.

questions.question_text: Which of the following planet is situated very close to the Sun?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Of the planets listed, Earth is the one situated closest to the Sun. The order of the planets from the Sun begins with Mercury and Venus, then Earth, followed by Mars, Jupiter, Saturn and Uranus. Jupiter, Saturn and Uranus are all far beyond the Earth's orbit.

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes the core structure of the earth?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is mainly composed of silicate minerals.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is as hot as the surface of the sun.
options.explanation: The earth's core is extremely hot, with temperatures reaching about 5000 degrees Celsius, comparable to the temperature at the surface of the Sun. It is composed mainly of iron and nickel, not silicate minerals, its inner part is solid, and the mantle accounts for the largest volume.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It accounts for the largest volume of the earth.

questions.question_text: One of the following explains the Continental Drift Theory. Which one is it?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Laurasia was the northern part of the supercontinent.
options.explanation: According to Wegener's Continental Drift Theory, the single supercontinent Pangaea split into two great landmasses: Laurasia in the north and Gondwanaland in the south. The theory was developed by Wegener, not Malthus, and Gondwanaland was the southern part, not the whole supercontinent, so Laurasia is the northern part.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The theory was developed by Thomas Robert Malthus.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Gondwanaland was once a single super continent.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The drifting of continents was centered upon Europe.

questions.question_text: On which of the earth sub-systems listed below, can human cultural imprints be found?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The anthroposphere is the earth's sub-system that includes human beings and their cultural imprints, such as buildings, farms, roads and settlements. The atmosphere, lithosphere and hydrosphere are natural sub-systems. Since cultural marks are made by people, they are found in the anthroposphere.

questions.question_text: If you find a large number of herbivore and carnivore animals in a certain geographical area in Africa, what can you generalize about the type of the climate of the area?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Large numbers of herbivores such as elephants, giraffes, zebras and antelopes, together with carnivores like lions and leopards, are typical of the tropical savanna climate of Africa. The savanna's seasonal rainfall and grasslands support abundant wildlife. Deserts, highlands and equatorial forests support fewer large grazing animals, so savanna climate is the answer.

questions.question_text: Despite many efforts, wild life resources of Africa are deteriorating from time to time. If you are asked to prioritize and implement conservation measures, which one is the most important one?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Establishing national parks and game reserves

options.label: C
options.explanation: Wildlife deterioration continues despite protected areas, so the most important measure is raising the awareness of local communities. People who understand the value of wildlife and follow conservation rules are less likely to hunt illegally or destroy habitats. National parks, vegetation preservation and hunting laws are needed, but lasting change begins with community awareness and participation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Regulating the practice of illegal hunting

questions.question_text: Which soil type is mainly located in the tropical monsoon climatic region of Africa?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Acrisols are strongly weathered acid soils with a clay-rich subsoil that are mainly associated with the tropical monsoon and seasonally wet climatic regions of Africa. Calcisols form in dry areas, while Lixisols and Luvisols occur in other belts. Acrisols therefore best match the tropical monsoon region.

questions.question_text: How do you describe the population size and growth of Africa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It has the lowest rate of population growth rate.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Its population doubling time is the longest.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is the least populated continent.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It has a negative net migration rate.
options.explanation: Africa has the highest rate of population growth and the shortest doubling time, and it is the second most populous continent after Asia. It is not a destination of mass immigration; instead, emigration exceeds immigration, giving the continent a negative net migration rate, which is the correct description.

questions.question_text: Among the following, which one describes the international migration in Africa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Brain drain is bringing more opportunities than challenges.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It has modified the sociocultural assets of North Africa.
options.explanation: International migration in Africa has a long history and has affected the social and cultural characteristics of regions, including North Africa, through trade, labour movement and cultural exchange. Brain drain mainly creates challenges, immigration to the continent is not currently the highest, so the statement about modified sociocultural assets is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Its practice has a short history in the continent.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Currently, there is the highest number of immigrants to the continent.

questions.question_text: Let's say your birth place has a rapid rate population growth which pushes the residents of the area to permanently leave their place of living. What do you think might your place of birth benefit from these permanent migrants?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It solves the problem of labor shortage

options.label: B
options.option_text: It results in high concentrations of elders

options.label: C
options.option_text: It decreases pressure on natural resources
options.explanation: When many people permanently leave a place of birth because of rapid population growth, the origin area benefits because pressure on natural resources such as land, water and forests decreases. It does not solve labour shortage, increase population growth, or necessarily concentrate elders, so reduced resource pressure is the main benefit.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It increases the rate of population growth

questions.question_text: What could be generalized about the economic growth and development trend of Africa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Rapid population growth acts as an engine to many African economies.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Different economic sectors of the continent are being integrated.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Manufactured products dominated the export items of the continent.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Most African countries exhibit a negative trade balance.
options.explanation: Most African countries export primary products and import manufactured goods, so the value of imports usually exceeds that of exports, giving a negative trade balance. Population growth does not drive most African economies, economic sectors are poorly integrated, and manufactured goods do not dominate exports. A negative trade balance is therefore the generalization.

questions.question_text: Which feature best explains the socio-economic condition of developed countries?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Developed countries are characterized by high levels of urbanization, with most people living in towns and cities, and a high proportion of the workforce in secondary and tertiary activities. They have a small proportion of children, not a large one, so high urbanization best explains their socioeconomic condition.

questions.question_text: What is the main implication of the large size of young population in Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The country has the smallest proportion of non-productive population.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The country needs a high expenditure for the provision of basic social services.
options.explanation: A large young population in Ethiopia means many children and youth need schools, health services, food and housing, so the government must spend heavily on basic social services. It does not mean a small non-productive population, slower growth momentum, or rapid development, since dependents must first be supported.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It has a low potential to increase the momentum of population growth.

options.label: D
options.option_text: There is a rapid socio-economic and technological development of the country.

questions.question_text: What motivated the government of Ethiopia to develop anti-natalist population policy? The need to

options.label: A
options.option_text: reduce the rate of urban-rural migration

options.label: C
options.option_text: balance the number of male and female population

options.label: D
options.option_text: raise the economic and social status of women
options.explanation: Ethiopia's anti-natalist population policy aims to slow rapid population growth partly by raising the economic and social status of women through education, employment and family planning. Empowering women helps lower birth rates. The policy is not meant to encourage growth, balance sexes, or reduce rural-urban migration directly.

questions.question_text: How does the International Monetary Fund (IMF) contribute to the economic development of nations?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By promoting countries to set tariffs and quotas

options.label: C
options.explanation: The International Monetary Fund contributes to economic development by promoting monetary cooperation and stabilizing exchange rates through financial assistance and policy advice to member countries. It does not promote tariffs, quotas or state ownership, and it is not focused on green campaigns. Exchange-rate stabilization is its main contribution.

options.label: D
options.option_text: By encouraging state ownership of enterprises

questions.question_text: As a citizen of Ethiopia, what is your view about the advantage your country gained as a result of globalization?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It marks the domination of imported products.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It increases the flow of remittance.
options.explanation: For Ethiopia, globalization has increased the flow of remittances sent home by the diaspora, providing foreign currency and supporting families. It has also exposed the country to imported products and foreign cultures, which are disadvantages, not advantages. Increased remittance flow is therefore the benefit Ethiopia gains from globalization.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It helps to exercise the western cultures.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It encourages a high consumption of domestic products.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about the scope of Geography?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is delimited to the geospheres of the earth.
options.explanation: Geography is the study of the earth and its spheres, including the lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, biosphere and anthroposphere, so its scope is delimited to these geospheres. It is not limited to capitals, physical features or the universe, which are narrower or unrelated ideas. Thus geography's scope covers the geospheres.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is limited to describing the capital cities of countries.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is merely focused on the distribution of physical features.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It emphasizes the physical arrangements of the universe.

questions.question_text: Why has the quantitative revolution been introduced to the subject matter of Geography?

options.label: A
options.option_text: To change the empirical nature of geography to a descriptive one

options.label: B
options.option_text: To explain and interpret spatial phenomena in a subjective manner

options.label: C
options.option_text: To enable geography to become law making science
options.explanation: The quantitative revolution introduced mathematics and statistical methods into geography to make it a law-making science capable of testing hypotheses and establishing spatial generalizations. Geography moved from descriptive to analytical study. Its purpose was not to become subjective or to use literary language, but to apply scientific, mathematical techniques.

options.label: D
options.option_text: To use the language of literature instead of mathematical language

questions.question_text: How does Geography tend to bridge natural and social sciences?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By offering different mathematical equations to natural sciences

options.label: B
options.option_text: By borrowing spatial concepts from natural and social sciences

options.label: C
options.option_text: By investigating how different fields of study are interrelated
options.explanation: Geography bridges the natural and social sciences by investigating how the physical environment and human activities are interrelated. By studying interactions between natural and social phenomena, geography connects disciplines such as geology, climatology, economics and sociology. It is this study of interrelationships that makes geography a bridge between the two branches of science.

options.label: D
options.option_text: By sharing methods and contents with different fields of studies

questions.question_text: If you observe a point where a strong river cuts into the course of a weaker river in your locality, which of the features listed below represents the observed case?

options.label: B
options.explanation: River capture occurs when a stronger river cuts into and captures the headwaters of a weaker neighbouring river. The sharp bend where the capturing river changes direction at the point of capture is called the elbow of capture. A misfit stream is the beheaded river, while wind gap and reverse drainage are related but different features.

questions.question_text: Which branch of human geography is concerned with the dynamic nature of places over time?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Historical geography is the branch of human geography that studies how places and their characteristics change through time. It examines the dynamic nature of places over history, linking past events to present landscapes. Political, urban and cultural geography focus more on current spatial patterns than on change over time.

questions.question_text: In which of the following conditions does folding happen?

options.label: A
options.option_text: When two forces move away from one another

options.label: B
options.option_text: When molten materials are forced out to the surface

options.label: C
options.option_text: When two plates move in parallel directions

options.label: D
options.option_text: When two different forces act towards each other
options.explanation: Folding happens when compressional forces act towards each other, pushing rock layers together and bending them into folds. When forces pull apart, tension stretches the crust, and when plates move in parallel, faulting and shearing occur. Molten materials rising to the surface produce volcanism, not folding. Thus opposite forces cause folding.

questions.question_text: What type of erosion is commonly found in coastal areas?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Coastal areas are eroded mainly by sea waves, which crash against cliffs and shorelines, wearing them away. Glaciation affects high mountains and polar regions, wind erosion dominates deserts, and streams erode valleys inland. Since the question concerns coasts, erosion by sea waves is the common type found there.

questions.question_text: What is a crescent-moon shaped small hill of sediments that is formed by the action of wind called?

options.label: C
options.explanation: A barchan is a crescent-moon shaped sand dune formed by wind in desert areas, with its horns pointing downwind. Loess is fine wind-blown dust, a beach is a shore deposit of sand or pebbles, and sand dune is a general term. The crescent-shaped hill described is a barchan.

questions.question_text: Which structure of the atmosphere is known by containing the lowest percentage of atmospheric mass?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The thermosphere is the outermost atmospheric layer, extending high above the earth, where the air is extremely thin and contains the lowest percentage of the atmosphere's mass. The troposphere holds most of the mass, the stratosphere contains ozone and the mesosphere lies between, all denser than the thermosphere.

questions.question_text: Which of the following refers to how energy from the sun is transmitted to the surface of the earth?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The sun's energy travels through empty space to the earth by radiation, the transfer of heat as electromagnetic waves. Convection transfers heat through moving fluids, conduction through direct contact, and advection is horizontal fluid movement. Since space between the sun and earth is nearly empty, radiation is the only means of transfer.

questions.question_text: What is the common feature of planetary winds?

options.label: A
options.option_text: They change their directions on a daily basis

options.label: B
options.option_text: They affect small areas for short periods of time

options.label: C
options.option_text: They cover a wide area of the earth
options.explanation: Planetary winds, such as the trade winds and westerlies, are global winds that blow over wide areas of the earth throughout the year. They follow regular paths controlled by pressure belts and the earth's rotation. They do not change daily, affect small areas, or occur only along coasts, so covering a wide area is their common feature.

options.label: D
options.option_text: They are common along the coastal areas.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about ocean currents?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Ocean current is the vertical movement of ocean water.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Warm ocean currents cause precipitation to the surrounding areas.
options.explanation: Warm ocean currents warm the air above them, increasing evaporation and causing precipitation in nearby coastal areas. Cold currents cool the air and reduce rainfall and temperatures. Ocean currents move water horizontally, and warm currents raise, not lower, surrounding temperatures. Therefore, warm currents causing precipitation is the correct statement.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Cold ocean currents increase the temperature of the nearby areas.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Warm ocean currents tend to reduce the surrounding temperature.

questions.question_text: What was the central argument of Malthusian Population Theory?

options.label: D
options.option_text: Rapid population growth leads to underdevelopment
options.explanation: Malthus argued that population grows faster than food supply, because population increases geometrically while food production increases arithmetically, so rapid population growth eventually leads to poverty and underdevelopment. He did not say food grows geometrically or recommend manmade birth control. Underdevelopment caused by rapid growth was his central argument.

questions.question_text: How do you explain the settlement pattern of the Ethiopian population?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The Shewa and Harerge plateaus host fewer urban populations.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Many urban areas in Ethiopia lie along major transport routes.
options.explanation: In Ethiopia, most towns and cities have developed along major transport routes such as roads and railways, which provide access to markets and services. The Shewa and Harerge plateaus contain many urban centres, peripheral areas have sparse permanent settlement, and northern highlands are densely settled, so urban areas along transport routes is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Peripheral areas are mainly associated with permanent settlement.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Most highland areas in northern Ethiopia have temporary settlements.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the main impact of rapid population growth in Ethiopia?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Rapid population growth in Ethiopia increases pressure on farmland, leading to overgrazing, deforestation and soil degradation, especially in the highlands. Air and water pollution and traffic congestion are more typical of urban-industrial problems. As an agrarian country, soil degradation is the main impact of rapid population growth in Ethiopia.

questions.question_text: How do you describe the economic growth and development trend of Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Many settlements have access to all-weather roads.
options.explanation: Ethiopia's road network has expanded rapidly, so many settlements now have access to all-weather roads, improving market access and mobility. The country does not have the highest literacy rate in Africa, and malnutrition and school dropouts are worse in rural areas than urban ones. Thus the road statement is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The country has the highest literacy rates in Africa.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Malnutrition is a serious problem in urban areas than in rural areas.

options.label: D
options.option_text: School dropouts are higher in urban areas than in rural areas.

questions.question_text: What should policy makers in Ethiopia do to boost the economy?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Encouraging state control of the economy

options.label: B
options.option_text: Encouraging population growth of the country

options.label: D
options.explanation: To boost the economy, Ethiopian policymakers should diversify export items, reducing dependence on a few primary products and earning more stable foreign currency. State control, encouraging population growth and importing luxury goods would not improve the economy, so promoting diversification of exports is the recommended policy.

questions.question_text: Why was the Plan for Accelerated and Sustained Development to End Poverty (PASDEP) not successful as planned in Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Because of a lack of study support from experts

options.label: B
options.option_text: Due to the then global financial crisis
options.explanation: PASDEP was partly unsuccessful because the global financial crisis that began in 2008 reduced foreign aid, investment and export earnings. It did not fail because of lack of expert study support, recurrent flooding, or labour shortage. The worldwide economic crisis undermined the plan's targets and implementation.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Because of the recurrent flooding in the country

options.label: D
options.option_text: Due to shortage of working labor force

questions.question_text: Which one of the following describes the distribution of pressure over the surface of the earth?

options.label: A
options.option_text: When the sun is overhead north of the equator, pressure belts shift southward.

options.label: B
options.option_text: When the sun is overhead at the equator, pressure belts shift northward by small degrees.

options.label: C
options.option_text: When the sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer, pressure belts shift southward.

options.label: D
options.option_text: When the sun is overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn, pressure belts shift southward.
options.explanation: Pressure belts shift with the overhead sun. When the sun is overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn in December, the belts shift southward. When it is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer, they shift northward, and at the equator they stay near the equator. Therefore the southward shift at the Tropic of Capricorn is correct.

questions.question_text: Which one of the statements below explains the characteristics of a region?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A region has distinct physical elements.

options.label: B
options.option_text: A region can be either artificial or natural.
options.explanation: A region can be either natural, such as a climatic or drainage region, or artificial, such as a political or administrative region. Regions do not need to be large, may lack clear boundaries, and can be defined by human as well as physical elements. The statement that a region is natural or artificial is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: To be a region an area needs to be large.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A region has a clear boundary.

questions.question_text: One of the following describes the tropical zone of the earth. Which one is it?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is found between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.
options.explanation: The tropical zone of the earth lies between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn, around the equator, where the sun's rays are nearly overhead and temperatures are high. It is covered by rainforest, savanna and other vegetation, not mostly desert, and is dominated by agriculture, not manufacturing.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is mostly covered by semi-desert and desert vegetation.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is characterized by low temperature year round.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is dominated by manufacturing economic activity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best explains the Tundra region?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It has the highest daily range of temperature.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is mostly located in the southern hemisphere.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It receives a long daily duration of sunlight in summer.
options.explanation: The tundra region, found mainly in the far north, experiences long periods of continuous daylight in summer, the midnight sun, because of the earth's tilt. It is mostly in the northern hemisphere, has a small daily temperature range, and is inhabited by people with a simple traditional lifestyle. Long summer daylight is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is inhabited by people whose life style is advanced.

questions.question_text: What change is mainly brought due to the development of transport and communication technologies?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Distance and time have got great impact on the production

options.label: B
options.option_text: Production of perishable products near major urban centers

options.label: C
options.option_text: Location of industries near resources and energy supplies

options.label: D
options.option_text: Working for companies without physically being there
options.explanation: Advances in transport and communication, especially the internet, allow people to work for companies located elsewhere without physically being present, through telecommuting or remote work. Distance and time no longer greatly limit production, perishable goods and industry are less tied to specific locations, so working without being there is the main change.

questions.question_text: Among the following, which one is primarily used to gather population data from a segment of the whole population?

options.label: C
options.explanation: A sample survey gathers population data from a selected segment, or sample, of the whole population, rather than counting everyone. A census counts every person, while divorce records and vital registration are continuous administrative records. Therefore, a sample survey is the source used to collect data from a part of the population.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the sparsely populated part of the world?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The interior basins of Indonesia, covered by dense equatorial rainforest, are difficult to settle and farm, making them sparsely populated. East and South Asia, northeastern North America and peninsular Europe are all densely populated regions. Therefore, the Indonesian basins represent the sparsely populated part of the world among the options.

questions.question_text: What is the main role of the tertiary economic activities in a given country's development?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Tertiary economic activities provide services rather than producing or processing goods. They include trade, transport, education, health and banking, which support development by serving people and other sectors. Making decisions, growing crops and processing raw materials belong to quaternary, primary and secondary activities respectively.

questions.question_text: Which of the following country is the leading in fish processing industry in Africa?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Morocco, with its long Atlantic coast and large Atlantic and Mediterranean fishing grounds, is the leading country in fish processing industry in Africa. Nigeria, South Africa and Egypt also have fishing industries, but none matches Morocco's scale of fish canning and processing. Thus Morocco is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Which statement best explains the practice of placer mining in Africa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is one of the modern and highly productive ways of mining.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is a process of quarrying useful stones for construction purpose.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is commonly practiced in areas situated far from river valleys.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is a process of extracting mineral deposits from excavated soils.
options.explanation: Placer mining is the traditional method of extracting valuable minerals, such as gold, from loose sediments and soils, usually in or near river valleys where water washes the ore from the deposits. It is not highly productive, does not involve quarrying stone, and is commonly practised in valleys, so extracting minerals from excavated soils is correct.

questions.question_text: In which of the following contexts can the qualitative research be the preferred approach?

options.label: A
options.option_text: If the association among variables is to be quantified.

options.label: B
options.option_text: If continuous variables are to be analyzed.

options.label: C
options.option_text: If there is no need of hypothesis testing.
options.explanation: Qualitative research is exploratory and deals with meanings, descriptions and non-numerical data, so it is preferred when there is no need for hypothesis testing. Quantifying associations, analysing continuous variables and verifying theories all require quantitative methods, which use numerical data and statistical testing.

options.label: D
options.option_text: If a given theory is to be verified.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about research method and methodology?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Research method justifies the philosophical foundation of the research.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Research methodology is limited to collecting and organizing data to solve problems.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Research method has a wider scope than research methodology.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Research methodology guides to conduct scientific research.
options.explanation: Research methodology is the broad system of principles and procedures that guides how scientific research is conducted. It is wider than research method, which refers to the specific techniques for collecting data. The philosophical foundation is justified by methodology, and methodology is not limited to data collection, so it guides scientific research.

questions.question_text: If you were commissioned to conduct an empirical study, which basic element of research might enable you to identify gaps to be filled by your study?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Reviewing related literature enables a researcher to see what has already been studied and to identify gaps, or unanswered questions, that the new study should fill. Hypothesis development, scope delineation and sampling design come later in the research process. Literature review is therefore the element that reveals research gaps.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Delineating the scope of the study

questions.question_text: How is the relative location of the Horn of Africa described?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is adjoined by the Red Sea in the northeast.
options.explanation: The Horn of Africa is bounded by the Red Sea to the northeast, the Indian Ocean to the east and southeast, and it lies southwest of Asia. Sudan borders it to the west, not the southwest. Hence the description that it is adjoined by the Red Sea in the northeast is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is bounded in the northwest by the Indian Ocean.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is situated to the southeast of Asia.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is bordered by the Sudan in the southwest.

questions.question_text: What would be the challenge of a country with a large areal size?

options.label: C
options.explanation: A country with a large areal size faces the challenge of effectively controlling and securing its long borders, which are difficult to patrol and defend. Ethnic diversity and varied agro-ecological zones can be opportunities, and arable land is not necessarily scarce. Difficulty of border control is therefore the main challenge.

questions.question_text: What major event took place in the Horn during the Paleozoic Era?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Climatic change with a massive deposition
options.explanation: During the Paleozoic Era, the Horn region experienced major climatic changes accompanied by massive sedimentary deposition. Ice-age glaciation followed by widespread deposition formed thick sedimentary layers in the region. Structural formation and orogenic movements belong to later eras, and invertebrate marine creatures appeared earlier, so climatic change with massive deposition is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Significant structural formation in the Horn

options.label: D
options.option_text: A continued and massive orogenic movement

questions.question_text: Which station has the highest annual range of temperature?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Annual range of temperature is the difference between the hottest and coldest months. Station III records 23°C and 11°C, giving a range of 12°C, which is the highest. Station I ranges only 1°C, Station II 10°C, and Station IV 10°C, so Station III has the greatest annual range.

questions.question_text: What type of natural vegetation is predominant at station II?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Station II has a hot climate with very low rainfall, around 260 millimetres, and a long dry season. Such dry conditions support only drought-resistant plants called xerophytes, which can store water or reduce water loss. Conifers, maquis and alpine plants require cooler or wetter conditions, so xerophytes predominate at Station II.

questions.question_text: What type of ecosystem is represented by station I?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Station I has high temperatures throughout the year and heavy rainfall every month, with no real dry season. These hot, wet conditions are typical of the tropical rainforest ecosystem, which supports dense evergreen forest. Grasslands need a dry season, and deciduous and coniferous forests need cooler climates, so Station I is a tropical rainforest.

questions.question_text: Which station best represents the winter rainfall region of Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Station I receives its highest rainfall from October to December, which is the winter rainfall season of the eastern highlands. Station II is dry throughout the year, and Stations III and IV receive most rain in summer. Since winter rainfall peaks at Station I, it best represents the winter rainfall region of Ethiopia.

questions.question_text: What can be generalized about the population structure of the region?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The region has higher percentage of economically dependent child population.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The number of economically active population of the region is lower than the Sub-Saharan Africa.

options.label: C
options.option_text: As compared to developing countries the region has higher percentage of old population.
options.explanation: The region has 19% old population and only 16% children. Developing countries typically have a small proportion of old people, so this region, with a higher percentage of elderly, resembles a developed population structure. It has more males than females, so the statement about a higher old population is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The region has higher number of female population than male.

questions.question_text: What is the crude birth rate of the population?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The crude birth rate is the number of live births per 1000 people in a year. Dividing 380,139 live births by the total population of 37,742,154 and multiplying by 1000 gives about 10.07, or approximately 10 births per 1000 people. Therefore the crude birth rate is 10/1000.

questions.question_text: What is the population growth rate of the region?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The population growth rate equals births plus net migration minus deaths, divided by population. Net migration is 10/1000 of 37,742,154, about 377,422. So 380,139 minus 323,220 plus 377,422 gives 434,341, which divided by 37,742,154 equals about 1.15%, closest to 1.14%. Option D is correct.

questions.question_text: The maternal mortality rate of the region is

options.label: A
options.explanation: The maternal mortality rate is the number of maternal deaths per 1000 women of reproductive age. Dividing 9,619 deaths of mothers by 9,061,821 reproductive women and multiplying by 1000 gives about 1.06, approximately 1 per 1000. Therefore the maternal mortality rate of the region is 1/1000.

questions.question_text: What is the geographic grid of point 'V'?

options.label: A
options.explanation: A geographic grid is given with latitude first and longitude second. Option A, 9°6'S 33°42'E, follows the standard order of latitude before longitude and uses correct southern latitude and eastern longitude for a region south of the equator. The answer requires reading the exact position of point V from the map figure.

questions.question_text: What is the altitude of point 'N'? (Distance between upper and lower contours is 8mm and distance of the point 'N' from upper contour is 5mm)

options.label: D
options.explanation: Interpolating between the upper and lower contours, point N lies 5 millimetres from the upper contour out of an 8 millimetre gap. With a 20 metre contour interval, the drop is 5/8 of 20 metres, or 12.5 metres below the 1460 metre upper contour, giving 1447.5 metres. The figure shows the contour values.

questions.question_text: Which of the following marginal information is depicted on the map?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Marginal information includes the title, scale, direction arrow, legend and other notes shown around a map. Among the options given, the title of the map is the marginal information depicted on the figure. Reading the map extract shows this title printed at the top, while the other listed items are not shown.

questions.question_text: Which type of slope is shown by line 'KL'?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The type of slope shown along line KL is judged from the spacing of the contour lines. Contours that are closer together at the top and spread out below indicate a convex slope. Reading the spacing along line KL on the figure shows this convex profile, so option C is selected.

questions.question_text: What is the most appropriate technique to display statistical data of portion of parts in relation to a single whole?

options.label: C
options.explanation: A pie chart is the most appropriate technique for showing statistical data of parts in relation to a single whole, because each sector represents a proportion of the total. Bar graphs, line graphs and histograms compare magnitudes or trends but do not directly show parts of a whole, so a pie chart is best.

questions.question_text: What is the areal scale of the map?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The areal scale expresses the relationship between area on the map and area on the ground. From the linear scale on the figure, one centimetre on the map equals about 1.5 kilometres on the ground, so one square centimetre equals about 2.25 square kilometres, closest to 2.3 square kilometres among the options.

questions.question_text: Which soil types of Africa have high humus content?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Nitosols are deep, clay-rich soils of volcanic regions with a high content of humus and good fertility, making them among the most productive soils of Africa. Ferrasols are heavily leached with little humus, and Lixisols and Luvisols have moderate humus. Therefore Nitosols are the soils with high humus content.

questions.question_text: Which statement explains the size of the African population?

options.label: A
options.option_text: is more populous than North America
options.explanation: Africa is the second most populous continent, with over a billion people, which is far more than the population of North America. It is not the third most populous, does not have two-thirds of the world's people, and has far more than half of Oceania's population. Africa is therefore more populous than North America.

options.label: C
options.option_text: has two-thirds of the world's population

options.label: D
options.option_text: has half of the population of Oceania

questions.question_text: Which one describes a population characteristic of southern African as compared to other regions?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Southern Africa has the highest crude death rate among the regions of Africa, mainly because of the heavy burden of HIV/AIDS and related diseases. The region also shows lower life expectancy and lower natural increase than other African regions, but the crude death rate is the population characteristic that is highest in southern Africa compared with other regions.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following describes the sex structure of the African population?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In the Sub-Saharan Africa, the sex ratio is below the world's mean
options.explanation: In Sub-Saharan Africa, the sex ratio is below the world's mean, meaning that there are slightly more females than males in the population. In Uganda and Guinea the numbers of males and females are not equal or balanced in the way described, so the statement about the sex ratio being below the world's mean is the correct one.

options.label: B
options.option_text: In Uganda, there is a balanced number of males and females

options.label: C
options.option_text: In the Sub-Saharan Africa, there are more males than females

options.label: D
options.option_text: In Guinea, the number of female births exceeds that of male births

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the main disadvantage of migration in the receiving country?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ethnic tension is the main disadvantage of migration in the receiving country, because the inflow of people from different cultural and ethnic backgrounds can create friction with the local population. Cultural integration, reduced labor shortage and racial interaction are advantages of migration, so ethnic tension is the disadvantage described.

questions.question_text: Which statement describes the concept of economic development?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Increase in the amount of total agricultural production

options.label: B
options.option_text: Improvement in the living condition of the people
options.explanation: Economic development is described as an improvement in the living condition of the people, because it involves qualitative changes such as better health, education and income distribution, not merely more production. Increases in agricultural output, manufactured goods and industrial product describe economic growth rather than development, so the improvement in living conditions is the correct definition.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Increase in the total amount of manufactured goods

options.label: D
options.option_text: Progress in the process of industrial domestic product

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a good opportunity for the development of the African continent? The availability of

options.label: D
options.explanation: The availability of abundant natural resources is a good opportunity for the development of the African continent, because these resources can be exploited to generate income, employment and industrial growth. Skilled labor, political stability and foreign aid are also important, but the continent's vast natural resource endowment is the specific opportunity mentioned in the question.

questions.question_text: Which one shows the agricultural production of Africa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Africa is rich in tropical crops demanded in world markets
options.explanation: Africa's agricultural production is rich in tropical crops that are demanded in world markets, such as coffee, cocoa, palm oil, rubber and tea. The continent does not produce huge amounts of temperate crops, is not dominated by commercial crops, and relies mainly on rain-fed rather than irrigated farming, so the statement about tropical cash crops is the correct one.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The continent produces huge amounts of temperate zone crops

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is dominated by the production of commercial crops

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is mainly carried out through irrigation systems

questions.question_text: What is the effect of latitude on ecosystem diversity? Ecosystem diversity

options.label: A
options.option_text: increases as we go from the equator to the poles

options.label: B
options.option_text: decreases from the poles towards the equator

options.label: C
options.option_text: remains similar wherever we go mainly due to the effect of altitude

options.label: D
options.option_text: decreases gradually when we travel from the equator to Tundra
options.explanation: Ecosystem diversity decreases gradually when traveling from the equator to the Tundra, because the warm, wet equatorial regions support the richest variety of plants and animals while the cold polar regions support the least. Diversity therefore decreases with increasing latitude, so the statement about the decrease from the equator to the Tundra is correct.

questions.question_text: Which statement refers to the trends of population growth of the world?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The total number of human population was about 4 billion at the beginning of the 1900s

options.label: B
options.option_text: Population growth was quite low before 5000BC mainly because of war and use of contraceptives

options.label: C
options.option_text: Rapid population growth was recorded for the first time when humans started to domesticate animals
options.explanation: Rapid population growth was recorded for the first time when humans started to domesticate animals and take up settled agriculture, which allowed food production to increase and support more people. The world population was not about four billion in 1900, and population has not increased constantly since 5000BC, so the domestication statement is the correct one.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Population growth has been constantly increasing since 5000BC because of economic diversification

questions.question_text: Which physical factor positively influences the distribution of human population?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Optimum temperature and rainfall positively influence the distribution of human population, because favorable climatic conditions support agriculture, water supply and human settlement. Industrial expansion and natural increase are human factors, and high relief with very high humidity discourages settlement, so optimum temperature and rainfall is the correct physical factor.

options.label: C
options.option_text: High natural increase of human population

options.label: D
options.option_text: High relief with very high humidity

questions.question_text: Which one of the following describes the level of urbanization in the world?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Africa has higher urban population than other developing regions

options.label: B
options.option_text: Developing regions have higher urban population than the world's average

options.label: C
options.option_text: Japan has the highest percentage of urban population

options.label: D
options.option_text: Europe has the second highest percentage of urban population
options.explanation: Europe has the second highest percentage of urban population in the world, after North America, reflecting its long history of industrial and urban development. Africa has a low level of urbanization, developing regions are below the world average, and Japan is not the highest percentage, so the statement about Europe being second is correct.

questions.question_text: Among the following zones of Ethiopia, which one is densely populated?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Gedeo is one of the most densely populated zones of Ethiopia, because its fertile volcanic soils and high rainfall support intensive agriculture and large rural populations. East Hararge, Assosa and Agnewak are much more sparsely populated, so Gedeo is the zone among the listed ones that is densely populated.

questions.question_text: What will happen by 2030 if the current population growth rate of Ethiopia continues in the same trend?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The size of the population will be quadrupled

options.label: B
options.option_text: The population density will remain the same

options.label: C
options.option_text: The population will be evenly distributed across the country

options.label: D
options.option_text: The population will exert pressure on the available infrastructure
options.explanation: If the current population growth rate of Ethiopia continues in the same trend, the population will exert pressure on the available infrastructure, because a rapidly growing population requires more roads, schools, hospitals and housing than the economy can provide. The population will not quadruple or become evenly distributed, so the pressure on infrastructure is the correct outcome.

questions.question_text: Which economic system is criticized for allowing some groups to accumulate huge wealth and play a decisive role in the economy?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The free market economic system is criticized for allowing some groups to accumulate huge wealth and play a decisive role in the economy, because unregulated private enterprise concentrates income in the hands of a few. Command and mixed economies involve state regulation, and the traditional system is based on customs, so the free market system matches the description.

questions.question_text: What is the main task of the World Trade Organization?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It enforces regulations related to free trade agreements
options.explanation: The main task of the World Trade Organization is to enforce regulations related to free trade agreements, because it supervises and liberalizes international trade among member countries. It does not produce exportable items, protect workers' rights, or impose sanctions directly on sovereign states, so enforcing free trade regulations is the correct main task.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It provides a framework on how to produce exportable items

options.label: C
options.option_text: It practically protects professional workers' rights

options.label: D
options.option_text: It directly puts sanctions in a sovereign country when it violates laws

questions.question_text: What is the method of extracting metallic minerals from soil called?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Placer mining is the method of extracting metallic minerals from soil and loose sediments by using running water to separate the heavier metal particles such as gold from the lighter material. Quarrying is for building stone, strip mining removes overburden in layers, and surface mining is a broad term, so placer mining best matches the extraction of metals from soil.

questions.question_text: What is the major cause of Africa being unable to exploit its potential resources?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Political instability is the major cause of Africa being unable to exploit its potential resources, because conflicts and unstable governments discourage the investment and security needed for resource development. Resource misallocation and inadequate revenue are consequences of instability, and climate does not prevent exploitation, so political instability is the correct major cause.

questions.question_text: Which continent is included in the Eurasian plate?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Part of Asia is included in the Eurasian plate, because the Eurasian plate covers the whole of Europe and most of Asia including India and Arabia in some classifications. North Africa belongs to the African plate, Australia has its own plate, and South America belongs to the South American plate, so part of Asia is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Which landmass is formed through the convergence of two oceanic plates?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The Mariana volcanic feature, the Mariana Trench and its island arc, is formed through the convergence of two oceanic plates, where one oceanic plate subducts beneath another. The Himalayas formed from continental collision, the East African rift from divergence, and the San Andreas Fault from transform movement, so the Mariana feature is the correct landmass.

questions.question_text: What is the principal agent for the chemical weathering of rocks?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Rain water is the principal agent for the chemical weathering of rocks, because water dissolves minerals, reacts with carbon dioxide to form carbonic acid, and drives hydrolysis and oxidation. Glaciers and thermal expansion cause physical weathering, and cold temperature slows chemical reactions, so rain water is the principal chemical weathering agent.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following country is found in the 'ring of fire' zone?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Peru is found in the 'ring of fire' zone, because it lies along the Pacific coast of South America where the Pacific plate subducts beneath the continental plate, causing frequent earthquakes and volcanoes. Norway, Brazil and the United Kingdom are far from the Pacific ring of fire, so Peru is the correct country.

questions.question_text: Which statement shows the trend of world climate change?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Temperature has declined in temperate regions since the 1970s

options.label: B
options.option_text: Precipitation has increased all over the globe since the 1980s

options.label: C
options.option_text: The average global temperature has increased over the past century
options.explanation: The average global temperature has increased over the past century, showing the warming trend of world climate change. Temperatures have not declined in temperate regions since the 1970s, precipitation has not increased all over the globe, and the climate does not fluctuate at the same rate, so the statement about rising average global temperature is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The global climate fluctuates at the same rate

questions.question_text: Which one is the effect of climate change in the tropical parts of the world?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The frequency of drought is an effect of climate change in the tropical parts of the world, because warming alters rainfall patterns and makes dry spells longer and more frequent in the tropics. Rainfall becomes less predictable, crop yields fall and snow cover is irrelevant in the tropics, so the increased frequency of drought is the correct effect.

questions.question_text: What are non-renewable resources? They are

options.label: A
options.option_text: replaceable resources if human beings utilize them properly

options.label: C
options.option_text: resources evenly distributed across the earth's surface

options.label: D
options.option_text: rare resources that will end at some time in the future
options.explanation: Non-renewable resources are rare resources that will end at some time in the future, because they are formed over millions of years and cannot be replaced on a human timescale once they are used. They are not replaceable if used properly, do not replenish quickly, and are not evenly distributed, so the description of resources that will eventually end is correct.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following relates to the economic policies of Ethiopia?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Promoting regional administration in economic management
options.explanation: Promoting regional administration in economic management relates to the economic policies of Ethiopia, because the country's federal system devolves economic planning and administration to regional states. Ethiopia does not encourage over-exploitation of fossil fuels, has not fully controlled the economy by the state, and does not shift urban labor to a rural economy, so the regional administration statement is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Focusing on shifting urban labor force to rural-based economy

options.label: D
options.option_text: Emphasizing on an economic system fully controlled by the state

questions.question_text: In which geological Era is the rift valley of Ethiopia formed?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The rift valley of Ethiopia was formed in the Cenozoic Era, when volcanic activity and the separation of the Arabian plate from Africa during the last tens of millions of years created the rift. The Paleozoic, Mesozoic and Precambrian eras are much older, so the Cenozoic Era is when the Ethiopian rift valley formed.

questions.question_text: Which part of the earth's physical environment is referred to as the 'life zone'?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The biosphere is the part of the earth's physical environment that is referred to as the 'life zone', because it is the sphere where all living organisms, plants and animals, exist. The atmosphere, lithosphere and hydrosphere are non-living physical spheres that support life but are not themselves the life zone, so the biosphere is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the basic characteristic of metamorphic rock?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is produced from igneous rock through pressure
options.explanation: Metamorphic rock is produced from igneous or sedimentary rock through pressure and heat, so the statement that it is produced from igneous rock through pressure is the basic characteristic.
