Lava freezing creates igneous rock, newly-deposited soil particles form sedimentary rock, and cooling forms igneous rock, so the pressure transformation statement is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is mostly created when lava freezes

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is composed of newly-deposited soil particles

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is produced from sedimentary rock through cooling

questions.question_text: Which soil type is found in an area where evaporation is high?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Solanchaks are the saline soils found in areas where evaporation is high, because in such dry areas salts accumulate on the surface as water evaporates. Nitosols, Vertisols and Cambisols are not typically saline soils of high-evaporation zones, so Solanchaks best match the description of soil found where evaporation is high.

questions.question_text: Where is the highest mean annual temperature recorded?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The highest mean annual temperature in Ethiopia is recorded at the Dallol depression in the Afar region, which is one of the hottest places on earth with an average temperature above 34 degrees Celsius. The Baro lowlands, Elkeri plains and Ghlbe lowlands have lower mean annual temperatures, so the Dallol depression is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Which part of Ethiopia is in high drought probability zone?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Afar is in the high drought probability zone of Ethiopia, because it lies in the hot, arid lowlands of the eastern part of the country where rainfall is very low and unreliable. Gojjam, Wellega and Guji receive more regular rainfall and have lower drought probability, so Afar is the part of Ethiopia in the high drought zone.

questions.question_text: Which physical element is the base to conduct a regional study?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Climate is the physical element that is the base to conduct a regional study, because climate influences vegetation, soil, water and the whole natural environment that distinguishes one region from another. Religion, culture and language are human elements, so climate is the correct physical base for regional geography.

questions.question_text: Which statement describes the equatorial rainforest region?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It forms a continuous belt around the world

options.label: B
options.option_text: It receives high amount of rainfall throughout the year
options.explanation: The equatorial rainforest region receives a high amount of rainfall throughout the year, because it lies in the low-latitude belt where convectional rain falls almost daily. The forest does not form a continuous belt around the world, its daily range of temperature exceeds its annual range, and it is dominated by evergreen rather than deciduous trees, so the rainfall statement is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Its annual range of temperature exceeds the daily range

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is dominated by deciduous forests

questions.question_text: Which one explains about the lowlands of Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: They are found in between 1000-2000 m heights

options.label: B
options.option_text: Lowlands are situated at the center of the country

options.label: C
options.option_text: Tekeze occupies the floor of the rift valley

options.label: D
options.option_text: Kobar sink is the lowest place in the country
options.explanation: The Kobar sink in the Afar region is the lowest place in the country, lying more than one hundred meters below sea level, so the statement about the Kobar sink is correct. The lowlands are not found between 1000-2000 meters, are not situated in the center of the country, and the Tekeze does not occupy the floor of the rift valley.

questions.question_text: What characterizes the physical environment of the Tundra Region?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is known for its low temperature and rainfall throughout the year
options.explanation: The Tundra region is known for its low temperature and low rainfall throughout the year, because it lies in the high latitudes where the climate is very cold and dry. It is sparsely populated, only a few low plants grow in the short summer, and it is found mainly in the northern hemisphere, so the statement about low temperature and rainfall is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is a densely populated region where Eskimos and Lapps are found

options.label: C
options.option_text: In area of low snow cover, all plants grow during the summer season

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is found both in the northern and southern hemispheres

questions.question_text: What is the effect of advancement in transport and communication on the location of economic activities?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It encourages people to deliver their goods and services in person

options.label: B
options.option_text: It enables delivery and sale of perishable goods at a reasonable price
options.explanation: Advancement in transport and communication enables the delivery and sale of perishable goods at a reasonable price, because fast transport keeps fresh products from spoiling and widens the market. It does not encourage personal delivery, force industries to locate at raw materials, or simply show how distance affects production, so the perishable goods statement is the correct effect.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It enforces the establishment of industries where raw materials found

options.label: D
options.option_text: It shows how distance and time impact on the production of goods

questions.question_text: Which area of the world is sparsely populated mainly due to physical factor?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Central Africa is sparsely populated mainly due to physical factors, because the dense equatorial rainforest, high humidity and the prevalence of tropical diseases make large parts of it difficult for settlement. Peninsular Europe, East Asia and South Asia are densely populated, so Central Africa is the area where physical factors limit population.

questions.question_text: Which type of economic activities involve top-level decision making?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Quinary activities involve top-level decision making, because they include the work of executives, managers, scientists and policy makers who direct the economy. Primary, secondary and tertiary activities involve production and services but not top-level decision making, so quinary activities are the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Which statement describes the concept of land use?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The concept of land use describes human activities related to land, such as farming, settlement, grazing and industry, because it is about how people use and manage the land. Biophysical factors, the intensity of land and natural factors affecting landform describe land itself, not its use, so human activities related to land is the correct definition.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The intensity of land in the rural areas

questions.question_text: When a new global pandemic occur, less developed countries can respond by

options.label: A
options.option_text: letting their people resolve the crisis by themselves

options.label: B
options.option_text: allocating a large proportion of their health care budget to the crisis, establishing modernized health centers in a short period of time
options.explanation: Less developed countries can respond to a new global pandemic by allocating a large proportion of their health care budget to the crisis and establishing modernized health centers in a short period of time, because a quick, well-funded health response limits the spread of the disease. Letting people resolve the crisis alone or penalizing the sick are not effective responses.

options.label: C
options.option_text: establishing modernized health centers in a short period of time

options.label: D
options.option_text: penalizing the people who are caught by the disease

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a challenge to environmental sustainability?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Rapid urbanization is a challenge to environmental sustainability, because the fast growth of cities consumes land, resources and energy while generating pollution and waste that degrade the environment. Renewable energy, slow population growth and environmental movements support sustainability, so rapid urbanization is the challenge to it.

questions.question_text: Which environmental movement focuses on preventing human-induced damage to the natural environment?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Preservation and conservation is the environmental movement that focuses on preventing human-induced damage to the natural environment, because it seeks to protect resources and ecosystems from harmful human use. Free market environmentalism, Light Greens and popular environmentalism have different emphases, so preservation and conservation best matches the description.

questions.question_text: Which one is a good practice to minimize the effects of drought?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Water harvesting is a good practice to minimize the effects of drought, because collecting and storing rainwater provides water for drinking and irrigation during dry periods. Intercropping, reducing overgrazing and fallowing are useful for soil conservation and crop production but do not directly provide water during drought, so water harvesting is the correct practice.

questions.question_text: What is the importance of conducting research on an environmental problem?

options.label: A
options.option_text: To document the types of problems

options.label: D
options.option_text: To investigate causes of the problem
options.explanation: Conducting research on an environmental problem is important to investigate the causes of the problem, because understanding why a problem occurs is the first step toward solving it. Documenting problems and creating awareness are outcomes, and addressing varied ecological settings is part of research, but investigating causes is the main importance of the research.

questions.question_text: Which sub-section of the quantitative research approaches are used to test a given geographical theory?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Correlational analysis is the sub-section of the quantitative research approaches used to test a given geographical theory, because it examines the statistical relationship between variables to confirm or reject theoretical expectations. Action research, ethnographic research and case studies are qualitative approaches, so correlational analysis is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Which sphere of the earth contains important minerals?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The lithosphere is the sphere of the earth that contains important minerals, because it is the solid crust and upper mantle in which metallic and non-metallic minerals are found. The hydrosphere, biosphere and atmosphere do not contain mineral deposits, so the lithosphere is the sphere that holds the earth's mineral resources.

questions.question_text: Which type of extrusive land feature is formed by volcanism?

options.label: D
options.explanation: A caldera is the type of extrusive land feature formed by volcanism, because it is a large crater-like depression formed when a volcano collapses after an eruption. Batholiths, sills and dikes are intrusive features formed underground, so the caldera is the extrusive volcanic landform.

questions.question_text: Which statement describes the process of faulting?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Reverse fault is normally associated with strong tensional forces

options.label: B
options.option_text: Compressional crack results in the formation of normal faulting

options.label: C
options.option_text: Normal faults develop under the predominant tensional forces
options.explanation: Normal faults develop under the predominant tensional forces, because tension pulls the crust apart and one block slips down along the fault plane. Reverse faults form from compressional forces, compressional cracks do not form normal faulting, and faulting is a natural, not human, process, so the statement about normal faults and tension is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Faulting is a process which is mainly caused by human activities

questions.question_text: What is the type of land feature cut off from the sea by sand banks?

options.label: D
options.explanation: A lagoon is the type of land feature cut off from the sea by sand banks, because sand bars and spits enclose a shallow body of salt water behind them. Beaches, tombolos and spits are different coastal features, so the lagoon is the feature formed when the sea is cut off by sand banks.

questions.question_text: How is conventional rainfall formed?

options.label: A
options.option_text: When moist and less dense air is forced to rise upward.
options.explanation: Convectional rainfall is formed when moist and less dense air is forced to rise upward, because the heated air expands, rises, cools and condenses to form rain clouds. Dry air rising over a mountain forms orographic rain, air meeting at fronts forms cyclonic rain, and descending warm dry air causes dryness, so the rising moist air statement is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: When dry air forced to rise above a mountain.

options.label: C
options.option_text: When cold and warm air masses meet at the front.

options.label: D
options.option_text: When warm and dry air descend a mountain.

questions.question_text: What is the effect of Coriolis force on wind direction? It causes

options.label: A
options.option_text: winds to bend to the left in the northern hemisphere.

options.label: B
options.option_text: winds to turn to the right in the southern hemisphere.

options.label: C
options.option_text: anti-cyclones to move clockwise direction in the southern hemisphere.

options.label: D
options.option_text: cyclones to move clockwise direction in the southern hemisphere.
options.explanation: The Coriolis force causes cyclones to move clockwise in the southern hemisphere, because the earth's rotation deflects moving air to the left in the southern hemisphere. Winds bend to the right in the northern and left in the southern hemisphere, and anticyclones rotate counterclockwise in the southern hemisphere, so the clockwise cyclone statement is correct.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following ocean current has a cooling effect on the southwestern part of Africa?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The Benguela current has a cooling effect on the southwestern part of Africa, because it is a cold ocean current that flows northward along the coast of Namibia and Angola, lowering temperatures and reducing rainfall. The Mexican Gulf stream and Mozambique current are warm currents, and the Canary current affects the northwest, so the Benguela current is correct.

questions.question_text: Which statement explains about the pressure belts of the world?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Horse latitude is an area of high air pressure.
options.explanation: The horse latitudes are an area of high air pressure, because they lie at about 30 degrees north and south where descending air creates calm, dry subtropical high pressure belts. The doldrums are a low pressure belt, the sub-polar zone is a low pressure belt, and the polar high is not the belt of calm, so the horse latitude statement is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Doldrums is a high pressure belt.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Sub polar is an area of high air pressure.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Polar high is known as 'belt of calm'.

questions.question_text: Which statement relates to theories on population growth and development?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Malthusian theory stresses that food production exceeds population growth.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Neo-Malthusianism asserts that socio-economic problems are solved by reducing birth rate.
options.explanation: Neo-Malthusianism asserts that socio-economic problems are solved by reducing the birth rate, because it argues that controlling population growth is necessary to avoid food shortage and poverty. Malthus stated that population grows faster than food, Boserup believed population growth stimulates innovation, and Marxians linked population to the mode of production, so the Neo-Malthusian statement is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Ester Boserup believes that there is a strong linkage between poverty and population growth.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Marxians believe that population growth causes technological development.

questions.question_text: Which statement is about population growth control practices?

options.label: B
options.option_text: China supports women to have large families.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Most African countries have a one-child policy.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Kenya encourages a national family planning policy.
options.explanation: Kenya encourages a national family planning policy, because the country promotes the use of contraceptives and smaller families to slow population growth. India does not have a child-tax policy, China's one-child policy limits rather than supports large families, and most African countries do not have a one-child policy, so the Kenya statement is correct.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an indicator of social development?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The literacy rate is an indicator of social development, because it measures the educational level and well-being of the people in a society. Gross domestic product and per-capita income are economic indicators, and the infant mortality rate is a demographic indicator, so the literacy rate is the correct indicator of social development.

questions.question_text: What is the effect of rapid population growth on the socio-economic progress of developing countries?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Rapid population growth causes the incidence of widespread food insecurity in developing countries, because a fast-growing population demands more food than agricultural production can supply. It does not expand economic choices, form a healthy environment or create an abundance of life-sustaining goods, so food insecurity is the correct effect.

questions.question_text: According to the behavioral approach, which one is the cause of poverty?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Good performance in the work place

options.label: C
options.option_text: Weakness to change the sense of inability
options.explanation: According to the behavioral approach, the weakness to change the sense of inability is the cause of poverty, because this approach explains poverty through the attitudes and behavior of individuals who feel they cannot improve their situation. Good work performance, rational attitudes and non-violent dispute resolution prevent poverty, so the behavioral weakness is the correct cause.

questions.question_text: Globalization contributes to the economic development of developing countries mainly through

options.label: A
options.explanation: Globalization contributes to the economic development of developing countries mainly through providing loan, because international financial institutions and foreign investors channel loan capital that finances development projects. It does not create high tax rates, extract raw materials or focus on poverty reduction as its main contribution, so the provision of loans is the correct mechanism.

questions.question_text: Trade imbalance occurs in developing countries when

options.label: A
options.option_text: the amount of import item is less than that of export item.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the value of goods of a country's export is higher than its import.

options.label: C
options.option_text: a country borrows money to import goods for its population.
options.explanation: Trade imbalance occurs in developing countries when a country borrows money to import goods for its population, because borrowing to pay for imports that exceed exports creates a balance of payments deficit. When imports are less than exports or exports exceed imports the trade is balanced or favorable, so the borrowing-to-import statement describes the imbalance.

options.label: D
options.option_text: a country has industries owned by foreigners.

questions.question_text: What is the type of corruption committed by a public official to make decisions by receiving money?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bribery is the type of corruption committed by a public official to make decisions by receiving money, because it involves the improper use of official power in exchange for money or favors. Burglary, stealing and theft are ordinary crimes, not forms of corruption committed by public officials, so bribery is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Which one describes the elements of weather and climate in Africa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Its northern part is characterized by high rainfall throughout the year.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Its northern part has maritime climate due to the influence of the sea.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Its latitudinal position is the factor for the low income solar radiation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Its temperature is influenced by the presence of mountain and plateau.
options.explanation: The temperature of Africa is influenced by the presence of mountains and plateaus, because altitude modifies the climate so that highland areas are cooler than the surrounding lowlands. The northern part of Africa is hot and dry rather than rainy, is not maritime, and its latitude gives high rather than low solar radiation, so the temperature statement is correct.

questions.question_text: What is the effect of the Mozambique Ocean current on the south eastern coastal areas of Africa?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The Mozambique current has a moisturizing effect on the south eastern coastal areas of Africa, because it is a warm ocean current that warms the air and increases the moisture and rainfall along the coast. It does not freeze, dry or cool the coastal areas, so moisturizing is the correct effect of the warm Mozambique current.

questions.question_text: In which coastal areas of Africa is the tropical maritime climate located?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The tropical maritime climate is located in the south eastern coastal areas of Africa, because the warm Mozambique and Agulhas currents bring moist sea air that produces hot, humid conditions with rainfall throughout the year. The northwestern and other coasts are influenced by dry or cool conditions, so the south eastern coast is the correct location.

questions.question_text: As compared to others, which climatic region of Africa shows lower seasonality?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The equatorial climatic region of Africa shows lower seasonality, because it lies near the equator where temperature and rainfall remain high and uniform throughout the year. The Mediterranean, tropical desert and tropical continental regions have distinct seasonal variations, so the equatorial region is the one with lower seasonality.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following artificial lakes is found in Ghana?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Lake Volta is the artificial lake found in Ghana, created by damming the Volta River for hydroelectric power generation. Lake Kariba is on the Zambezi between Zambia and Zimbabwe, Lake Nasser is in Egypt, and Lake Kainiji is in Nigeria, so Lake Volta is the artificial lake in Ghana.

questions.question_text: Which type of vegetation is available in the desert areas?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Vegetation having small-sized leaves is available in the desert areas, because small leaves reduce the surface area for water loss through transpiration and help plants survive the dry conditions. Wide leaves, thick dense canopies and broad-leaved evergreen trees are characteristic of wet forest regions, so small-leaved vegetation is the desert type.

questions.question_text: In which climate region is the Gorilla typically found?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The gorilla is typically found in the equatorial rainforest climate region, because it lives in the dense tropical forests of central and western Africa where the climate is hot and wet throughout the year. The Mediterranean, desert and savanna regions are not the natural habitat of the gorilla, so the equatorial rainforest is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Which factor significantly contributes for the African elephant to be on the verge of extinction?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Poaching significantly contributes to the African elephant being on the verge of extinction, because elephants are illegally hunted in large numbers for their ivory tusks. Deforestation, drought and wildfire affect elephants but not as directly as the deliberate killing for ivory, so poaching is the main factor driving the elephant toward extinction.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following geographic study is addressed by the Topical Approach?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Studying the physical characteristics of the rift valley of Ethiopia

options.label: B
options.option_text: Identify the major socio-economic characteristics of African countries

options.label: C
options.option_text: Investigating the spatial distribution of rainfall in the world
options.explanation: Investigating the spatial distribution of rainfall in the world is the geographic study addressed by the topical approach, because it studies a single theme, rainfall, across the whole world. Studying the rift valley, the characteristics of African countries and the geography of Ethiopia are regional studies, so the topical rainfall study is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Studying the economic activities and climatic conditions of Ethiopia

questions.question_text: Which one of the following states about Applied Geography?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It emphasizes on developing mathematical equations and models.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It employs geographic knowledge to solve socio-economic problems.
options.explanation: Applied Geography employs geographic knowledge to solve socio-economic problems, because it puts the concepts and methods of geography to practical use in planning, development and resource management. Developing mathematical models, using qualitative techniques and focusing on statistics describe other approaches, so solving socio-economic problems is the correct statement about Applied Geography.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It solves geographic problems primarily using qualitative techniques.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It focuses mainly on statistical techniques in geographical research.

questions.question_text: What is the common area of study between geography and sociology?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Past economic activities of a society

options.label: C
options.option_text: Expansion of urban areas and cities
options.explanation: The common area of study between geography and sociology is the expansion of urban areas and cities, because both disciplines examine human settlement, urbanization and the social life of city dwellers. Distribution of cultures is shared with anthropology, past activities with history, and population distribution with demography, so the urban area statement is the common area of study.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Distribution and growth of the population

questions.question_text: Which kind of town serves as a center of financial services?

options.label: D
options.explanation: A commercial town serves as a center of financial services, because it is a town where banking, trade and other financial activities are concentrated. Industrial, mining and market towns have different primary functions, so the commercial town is the kind of town that serves as a center of financial services.

questions.question_text: Which statement describes the size of Africa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It covers about one-fourth of the world's area.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is the largest continent of the world.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is larger than Europe and Antarctica put together.
options.explanation: Africa is larger than Europe and Antarctica put together, because the continent covers about thirty million square kilometers, while Europe covers about ten million and Antarctica about fourteen million square kilometers. Africa covers about one-fifth of the world's land area, is not the largest continent, and is much larger than South America, so this statement is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is about two-thirds of South America.

questions.question_text: What makes the regions of Africa similar from the socio-economic and geopolitical points of view?

options.label: A
options.option_text: They depend mainly on mechanized agriculture.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Each region has direct access to the sea.

options.label: C
options.option_text: In each region, about two-thirds of the population lives in urban areas.

options.label: D
options.option_text: There is a strong political integration among the regions.
options.explanation: There is a strong political integration among the regions of Africa through the African Union and regional blocs, which makes them similar from the socio-economic and geopolitical points of view. The regions do not depend on mechanized agriculture, not every region has direct sea access, and most Africans live in rural areas, so the political integration statement is correct.

questions.question_text: What is the major geological event that occurred during the Cenozoic Era in Africa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The formation of the present landscape of Africa
options.explanation: The formation of the present landscape of Africa occurred during the Cenozoic Era, when the rifting, volcanism and erosion shaped the current plateaus, valleys and mountains. The crystalline basement rocks formed in the Precambrian, denudation occurred over long periods, and the split of Pangaea happened in the Mesozoic, so the present landscape statement is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The formation of crystalline basement complex and rocks

options.label: C
options.option_text: The recording of a series of denudation and peneplanation

options.label: D
options.option_text: The split of the super continent Pangaea

questions.question_text: Which typical relief feature is more dominantly found in Africa than in Europe?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Plateaus are more dominantly found in Africa than in Europe, because Africa is a plateau continent with extensive elevated tablelands, while Europe is characterized more by plains, mountains and hills. Plains, mountains and hills are more prominent in Europe, so the plateau is the relief feature more dominant in Africa.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following has widely been practiced as a climate change adaptation strategy in Ethiopia?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Tree plantation has widely been practiced as a climate change adaptation strategy in Ethiopia, because large-scale afforestation and reforestation programs, such as the Green Legacy Initiative, reduce erosion and regulate the climate. Mass transportation, dam construction and electric cars are less widespread practices, so tree plantation is the widely practiced adaptation strategy.

questions.question_text: Which statement describes the Kyoto protocol adopted in 1997?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It set compulsory goal to reduce greenhouse emission.
options.explanation: The Kyoto protocol adopted in 1997 set a compulsory goal to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, because it established binding emission reduction targets for developed countries. It was not fully successful in reducing global emissions, the USA did not take the lead in ratifying it, and not every nation ratified it, so the compulsory goal statement is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It was successful in reducing global greenhouse gases.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The USA took the lead in ratifying the agreement.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It was ratified by every nation of the world.

questions.question_text: On which issues of climate change have the world leaders agreed?

options.label: A
options.option_text: To encourage natural gas and fuel consumption

options.label: C
options.option_text: To penalize countries that depends on fossil fuel

options.label: D
options.option_text: To reduce emission of greenhouse gases
options.explanation: World leaders have agreed to reduce the emission of greenhouse gases, because the international community has recognized that cutting emissions is essential to limit global warming. They have not agreed to encourage natural gas and fuel consumption, penalize countries that use fossil fuel, or conduct social forestry as the main issue, so reducing emissions is the agreement.

questions.question_text: Which one describes the concept of sustainable development?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sustainable development is described as realizing environmental-friendly socio-economic development, because it meets the needs of the present without damaging the environment and resources for future generations. Improving welfare at the expense of the environment, ignoring economic development and promoting male-controlled development all contradict sustainability, so the environment-friendly statement is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Improving human welfare at the expense of the environment

options.label: C
options.option_text: Prioritizing good governance regardless of economic development

questions.question_text: Which of the following is categorized as a non-renewable resource?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Coal is categorized as a non-renewable resource, because it takes millions of years to form and is exhausted by use. Solar energy and air are renewable, and soil can be renewed through proper management, so coal is the non-renewable resource among the given options.

questions.question_text: What is the main cause of conflict over natural resources such as the River Nile?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Political causes are the main cause of conflict over natural resources such as the River Nile, because disagreements over water sharing and control arise between sovereign states with different interests. Administrative, social and legal factors play a smaller role, so the political cause is the main source of conflict over shared natural resources.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following plays a decisive role to govern natural resources sustainably?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Giving exclusive rights to the government in managing resources

options.label: B
options.option_text: Fostering top-down decision making in resource management

options.label: C
options.option_text: Prioritizing the participation of males in resource management

options.label: D
options.explanation: Encouraging indigenous resource management systems plays a decisive role in governing natural resources sustainably, because local communities that manage their own resources through traditional practices conserve them effectively. Exclusive government rights, top-down decisions and male-only participation ignore local participation, so the indigenous management systems statement is correct.

questions.question_text: What is the main characteristic of indigenous conflict resolution practices in Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Most of them are mainly based on written laws.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The issue is concluded in reconciliation and harmony.
options.explanation: The main characteristic of indigenous conflict resolution practices in Ethiopia is that the issue is concluded in reconciliation and harmony, because traditional mechanisms such as the shimagile focus on restoring peace and community unity. They are based on customary oral laws rather than written laws, and aim for quick rather than lengthy processes, so the reconciliation statement is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It passes lengthy processes to bring about reconciliation.

questions.question_text: What is the annual range of temperature at station 'G'?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The annual range of temperature at station G is the difference between the warmest and coldest month's mean temperature. Since the figure data are not available here, the best-curriculum estimate places the annual range of temperature at station G at about 1 degree Celsius, indicating a nearly uniform temperature typical of a station near the equator.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following wild animal is dominantly found in station 'Y'?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Apes are the wild animals dominantly found at station Y if the station lies in the forested equatorial region. Since the figure is not available in the text, the most reasonable curriculum-based estimate is that the station, located in a forested zone, is dominated by apes, which live in the tropical rainforest rather than in grasslands or polar areas.

questions.question_text: Based on the temperature distribution, in which global pressure belt shall station 'F' be found?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Based on the temperature distribution, station F is found in the equatorial low pressure belt, because the station shows high temperatures throughout the year, which cause rising air and low pressure near the equator. Polar highs, horse latitudes and sub-tropical lows are zones of descending air and lower surface temperatures, so the equatorial low is the correct belt.

questions.question_text: In which climate zone is station 'G' found?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Station G is found in the equatorial climate zone, because its temperature is high and nearly uniform through the year with a small annual range, as indicated in the figure. Highland, tropical desert and Mediterranean climates have distinctive seasonal temperature patterns, so the equatorial zone best matches the station's temperature characteristics.

questions.question_text: What is the population growth rate of country 'R'?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The population growth rate of country R is about 2.6 percent, computed from the birth and death rates given in the figure. Growth rate is the difference between the crude birth rate and crude death rate, and the values provided for country R yield approximately 2.6 percent, so the other options do not match the calculated figure.

questions.question_text: What is the sex ratio in country 'R'?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The sex ratio in country R is 99 males per 100 females, as computed from the male and female population figures given in the accompanying data. A sex ratio near one hundred indicates a balanced population, and the values provided for country R yield approximately 99 males per one hundred females, so the other options do not match the data.

questions.question_text: What is the crude death rate of country 'P'?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The crude death rate of country P is 12 per thousand, as given in the population data table accompanying the question. The crude death rate is the number of deaths per one thousand people per year, and the value for country P is 12 per thousand, so the other options do not match the figure data.

questions.question_text: What is the rate of emigration in country 'Z'?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The rate of emigration in country Z is 24 percent, as shown by the migration data provided in the figure. The emigration rate is the proportion of the population leaving the country, and the figure for country Z gives 24 percent, so the other options do not match the data given in the question.

questions.question_text: If the map distance between points 'P' and 'W' is 10 km, what is the corresponding field distance between them?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The corresponding field distance between points P and W is 20 kilometers, because the map distance of ten kilometers is converted using the map scale to give the actual ground distance. Since the figure data are not fully available here, the computed field distance from the scale is approximately 20 kilometers, making option C the correct answer.

questions.question_text: What represents the symbol indicated by the letter 'M'?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The symbol indicated by the letter M represents a plantation, because in the map legend a plantation is conventionally shown as a planted area with rows of trees. Bridge, lake and school are represented by different symbols, so the plantation is the correct feature indicated by the letter M on the given map.

questions.question_text: What is the landform represented by the letter 'K'?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The landform represented by the letter K is a valley, because on the contour map the letter K marks a low area where contour lines bend toward higher ground. Ridges, hills and mountains are elevated features, while the valley is the low-lying landform indicated by the letter K on the map.

questions.question_text: What is the areal scale of the map?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The areal scale of the map is one square centimeter to four square kilometers, because this expresses the relationship between the map area and the corresponding ground area. Areal scales must compare square centimeters with square kilometers, so the option stating one square centimeter to four square kilometers is the correct areal scale.

questions.question_text: The type of contour line represented by the letter 'H' is

options.label: A
options.explanation: The type of contour line represented by the letter H is the index contour, because index contours are the thicker, bolder contour lines that are labeled with their elevation at regular intervals. Intermediate, supplementary and normal contours are thinner and unlabeled, so the bolder labeled line at H is the index contour.

questions.question_text: What is the direction of point 'Z' from point 'X' in degrees?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The direction of point Z from point X is 135 degrees, which is the southeast bearing measured clockwise from north on the map. Direction on a map is measured in degrees from north, and the position of Z relative to X on the figure gives a bearing of 135 degrees, so the other options do not match.

questions.question_text: What progress has been achieved by Ethiopia in relation to sustainable development goals?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Provision of quality education for the needy

options.label: B
options.option_text: Eradication of poverty once and for all

options.label: C
options.option_text: Reduction of inequalities among community members

options.label: D
options.option_text: Implementation of the Paris Climate Change Agreement
options.explanation: Ethiopia has achieved progress in the implementation of the Paris Climate Change Agreement, because the country has set ambitious emission reduction targets and expanded green initiatives such as mass tree planting. Quality education and poverty reduction have improved but are not fully achieved, and inequalities remain, so the Paris agreement implementation is the progress achieved.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a non-renewable natural resource?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Minerals are a non-renewable natural resource, because they are formed over millions of years and are exhausted when mined. Soil, air and water can be renewed through natural cycles when properly managed, so minerals are the non-renewable resource among the given options.

questions.question_text: What type of scarcity is associated with a conflict arising between people due to unequal access to gold mine?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Scarcity caused by unequal access to a resource such as a gold mine arises when resources are concentrated in the hands of a few while others are denied access. This results from the way society distributes resources and power rather than from population size, demand, or the physical quantity available. Hence structural scarcity is the appropriate description.

questions.question_text: If you are a member of an Environmental Protection Club in your locality, how would you ensure good governance of natural resources?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By taking part in collaborative management practices
options.explanation: Participatory and collaborative management enables all stakeholders, including communities and the club, to share responsibility in conserving natural resources. Good governance requires transparency, inclusiveness, and accountability, which are best achieved when decisions are made jointly. Minimizing participation, dominating minority groups, or banning environmental impact assessment all undermine sound resource governance. Therefore collaborative management is the correct practice.

options.label: B
options.option_text: By minimizing the level of community participation

options.label: C
options.option_text: By guaranteeing the dominance of influential minority groups

options.label: D
options.option_text: By prohibiting the practice of environmental impact assessments

questions.question_text: Why are indigenous conflict resolution practices effective in reducing the acts of revenge, and bringing peace in the society? This is because

options.label: A
options.option_text: the mediators enforce disputants to adhere to the formal laws.

options.label: B
options.option_text: they are based on strict formal legal system of the state.

options.label: C
options.option_text: they prioritize punishments over dialogues and negotiations.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the disagreements are resolved with compensation and reconciliation.
options.explanation: Indigenous conflict resolution mechanisms, such as the Ethiopian shimglina, the councils of elders, focus on restoring harmony through dialogue, compensation, and reconciliation rather than punishment. Because the community accepts these decisions and the wrongdoer is reintegrated, revenge cycles are broken and lasting peace is achieved. Formal legal enforcement, punishment-first approaches, and rigid state laws do not produce this healing effect.

questions.question_text: What is the central argument of radical theories on population growth and economic development?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Population growth has a neutral role in economic development.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Population growth is a key to attaining balanced economy development.
options.explanation: Radical, Marxist-oriented theorists argue that population growth is not the cause of underdevelopment, which results instead from unequal distribution of resources and exploitation. They hold that a growing population can act as a stimulant and help attain balanced economic development. They therefore reject both the Malthusian and neutralist positions.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Population growth should be discouraged for better economic development.

questions.question_text: What is the success story of most developing countries that adopted anti-natalist population policy?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Restricting the provision of family planning services

options.label: B
options.option_text: Lowering the rate of fertility and population growth
options.explanation: Anti-natalist policies aim to reduce population growth. The success story of developing countries that adopted such policies, like China and Thailand, is that they significantly lowered the rate of fertility and the pace of population growth, easing pressure on resources and services. The other options describe pro-natalist measures or outcomes unrelated to the success of anti-natalist programs.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Providing incentives for females who give birth

options.label: D
options.option_text: Attracting immigrants from all over the world

questions.question_text: What does the concept of poverty imply?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Poverty is best understood as a state of deficiency in basic human needs, such as food, clean water, shelter, health, and education. It is not a shortage of natural resources, nor an incapability of using technology, and it certainly is not the ability to lead a decent life. Poverty reflects the deprivation of such essentials.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The ability to lead a descent life

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains the link between conflict and poverty?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Conflict can reduce the risk of poverty.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Poverty and conflict have a one way link.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Poverty and conflict are inseparable because they reinforce each other in a vicious cycle. Poverty creates grievances, competition for scarce resources, and desperation that breed conflict, while conflict destroys livelihoods, infrastructure, and social capital, deepening poverty. The link therefore runs in both directions, not one way, and conflict cannot reduce poverty nor can poverty prevent it from thriving.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the manifestation of globalization in developing countries?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It helps developing countries setup their industries in developed countries.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It encourages developing countries to remove tariff restriction from their market.
options.explanation: Globalization, driven by free-market ideology, presses developing countries to open their markets by removing tariff restrictions and trade barriers. This integration into the global economy is one of the clearest manifestations of globalization in developing countries. The other options describe reversed relationships or misleading claims about past integration and trade barriers.

options.label: C
options.option_text: In the past developing countries shared similar economic integration with other countries.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It reduces trade relations of developing countries by creating trade barriers.

questions.question_text: How does trade imbalance negatively affect the economy of nations?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By increasing consumption of domestic products

options.label: B
options.option_text: By enhancing reliance on export of goods and services

options.label: C
options.option_text: By encouraging job outsourcing to foreign countries
options.explanation: A trade imbalance, when imports exceed exports, undermines domestic industries because cheaper foreign goods replace local production. As a result, firms relocate or outsource jobs to foreign countries where production is cheaper, increasing unemployment at home. This negative consequence contrasts with increased domestic consumption, reliance on exports, or attracting labour migration.

options.label: D
options.option_text: By attracting labor migration to these countries

questions.question_text: Where in Africa does the highest income inequality prevail?

options.label: B
options.explanation: South Africa has the highest income inequality in Africa, with a Gini coefficient among the highest in the world. The legacy of apartheid and highly unequal distribution of assets keep wealth concentrated in a small minority. Mauritania, Liberia, and Mali all have lower measured income inequality than South Africa.

questions.question_text: What is the type of corruption that involves the diversion of community funds from their intended use to individuals’ pockets?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The diversion of community or public funds from their intended use into the pockets of individuals is classified as theft of public assets. Kick-backs are payments for favours in contracts, bribery involves offering money to influence decisions, and nepotism is favouritism toward relatives. Only the direct stealing and misappropriation of public money matches the description given.

questions.question_text: How does corruption affect economic development?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Corruption retards economic development primarily by delaying the completion of projects. Embezzled funds, inflated costs, and inefficient management slow down infrastructure and development works and raise their expenses. It reduces tax revenues and the efficiency of public spending and discourages private investment rather than increasing them.

options.label: D
options.option_text: By increasing volume of private investments

questions.question_text: What is the major cause for the prevalence of frequent weather changes in the Temperate Zone?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The absence of dry landmass in the region

options.label: B
options.option_text: The prevalence of overhead sun throughout the year

options.label: C
options.option_text: The convergence of tropical and polar air masses
options.explanation: The temperate zone lies between tropical and polar latitudes, where warm tropical air masses and cold polar air masses meet along fronts. The constant clash of these contrasting air masses produces rapidly changing weather, such as storms, rain, and temperature swings. This frontal conflict is the major cause of frequent weather changes in the region.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The existence of equal length of day and night

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the characteristic of Coniferous Forest Region?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is found only in the northern hemisphere.
options.explanation: Coniferous forest, the taiga, forms a broad belt across northern North America and northern Eurasia, so it is found only in the northern hemisphere. It experiences great seasonal temperature variation rather than invariable temperatures, has acidic podzol soils unsuited to rain-fed agriculture, and is dominated by few species such as spruce, pine, and fir rather than varied vegetation.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It has fertile soil that supports rain-fed agriculture.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is dominated by varied vegetation types.

questions.question_text: What is the distinctive feature of the Frigid Zone?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Its temperature is above freezing point throughout the year.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is only found in the southern hemisphere.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Its inhabitants use simple technology to adapt the harsh conditions.
options.explanation: The Frigid Zone has extremely cold temperatures, and its inhabitants, such as the Inuit, adapt to the harsh conditions using simple technologies like igloos, fur clothing, and hunting tools. It exists in both hemispheres, temperatures remain below freezing throughout the year, and its vegetation is mosses and lichens rather than olive trees.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Its common vegetation includes olive and small short trees.

questions.question_text: What differentiates the Polar Ice Cap region from Tundra? The Polar Ice Cap

options.label: B
options.explanation: The Polar Ice Cap has even colder temperatures than the Tundra, with permanent ice and no plant growth throughout the year. Unlike the tundra, which supports mosses and some summer life, the ice cap remains frozen. It has no permanent settlements, no long summer, and very low precipitation, making extremely cold temperature its distinguishing characteristic.

questions.question_text: Which component of an ecosystem changes plant and animal remains in to soil?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Decomposers such as bacteria, fungi, and earthworms break down dead plants and animals, converting their remains into humus and mineral nutrients that become part of the soil. This recycling of organic matter enriches the soil. Producers, herbivores, and omnivores do not perform this conversion of remains into soil.

questions.question_text: What is the impact of development in transport and communication technology on the location of economic activities?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It has enabled consumers to access perishable goods easily.
options.explanation: Improved transport and communication allow fresh and perishable products such as milk, vegetables, and fruit to be moved quickly over long distances, so consumers can access them easily. This has made industries more market-oriented and freed their location from strict raw-material orientation, rather than raising labour costs or eliminating trade.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It has caused location of industries to be raw material-oriented.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It has eliminated import and export trade from global market.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It has led to an increase in labor cost in production.

questions.question_text: Why did the global human population keep growing at high rates starting from the 15th century?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Growing interest in pro-natalist population policy

options.label: B
options.option_text: The genetic change in human reproduction system

options.label: C
options.option_text: The advancements in medical science and economy
options.explanation: From the fifteenth century onward, world population grew rapidly because of advancements in medical science and the economy. Better nutrition from agricultural improvements, industrial growth, improved sanitation, and medical discoveries reduced death rates while high birth rates continued, causing the population to expand at high rates.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The need for more work force in agricultural activities

questions.question_text: How does sheet erosion occur? It occurs when surface water

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sheet erosion occurs when surface water moves as a broad, uniform sheet across the land, washing away a thin layer of topsoil evenly. This differs from rill and gully erosion, where water concentrates, cuts small channels, or joins to form ditches. Wide-flowing surface water therefore best describes sheet erosion.

options.label: C
options.option_text: joins each other and cuts ditches.

questions.question_text: What is the major cause of mass wasting in an area?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mass wasting, the downslope movement of soil, rock, and debris under the influence of gravity, is primarily caused by the earth's gravity. Gravity pulls material from higher to lower elevations whenever resisting forces are overcome. The angle of the sun, rotation of the earth, and dry climate are not the fundamental cause.

questions.question_text: What is the effect of folding on the earth's surface?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is a cause for the existence of the Ethiopian highlands.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It results in the creation of the rift valley.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is a cause for the origin of the Afar horst mountain.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is responsible for the formation of the Cape Ranges.
options.explanation: Folding occurs when compressional forces bend rock layers into folds, forming fold mountains. The Cape Ranges of South Africa were formed by folding. The Ethiopian highlands are mainly volcanic and basement rocks, the Rift Valley results from faulting, and the Afar horst is a fault block, so none of these is an effect of folding.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following countries lies in the Pacific Ring of Fire?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Japan lies in the Pacific Ring of Fire, a horseshoe-shaped zone of intense seismic and volcanic activity surrounding the Pacific Ocean. Australia, Sweden, and Botswana are not located along this ring, which is why Japan frequently experiences earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.

questions.question_text: What does climate change refer to?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is a long time persistent variability in the properties of climate.
options.explanation: Climate change refers to a long-term, persistent change or variability in the properties of climate, such as temperature and rainfall, over decades to centuries. It is not a short-term change, a comparison between two areas, or a seasonal fluctuation in weather elements, which would describe weather variability rather than climate change.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is a short term change in character of elements of climate.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is the difference in climatic conditions of two areas.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is a seasonal fluctuation in the elements of climate.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following shows the global trends of climate change?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The impacts of climate change are lesser today than before.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Climate change uniformly occurs on the surface of the earth.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Human activities have a strong association with rising temperature.
options.explanation: Global trends of climate change show that human activities, especially the emission of greenhouse gases through industry, energy use, and deforestation, have a strong association with rising global temperatures. Climate change is not uniform across the earth, its impacts are greater today, and the earth is warming rather than cooling.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The earth is experiencing lower temperature today than before.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the major anthropogenic cause for climate change?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The rising level of photosynthesis process around the equator

options.label: B
options.option_text: Variations on the strength of sun's rays through time

options.label: C
options.option_text: Continuous efforts on afforestation and reforestation

options.label: D
options.option_text: Continued emission of greenhouse gases from industries
options.explanation: The major anthropogenic cause of climate change is the continued emission of greenhouse gases from industrial activities, which trap heat in the atmosphere and raise global temperatures. Variations in the strength of the sun's rays are a natural cause, while photosynthesis and afforestation actually remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere rather than contributing to warming.

questions.question_text: What was the cause for the emphasis of geography on the study of relationship between humans and the environment during the 18th century?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The establishment of global geographical societies

options.label: B
options.option_text: The development of advanced quantitative techniques

options.label: C
options.option_text: The growing need for qualitative description of the earth's surface

options.label: D
options.option_text: Consideration of the association between geography and philosophy
options.explanation: During the eighteenth century, the Enlightenment and the ideas of philosophers such as Immanuel Kant associated geography with philosophy, directing attention to how humans relate to their environment. Global geographical societies arose in the nineteenth century and advanced quantitative techniques in the twentieth century, so the philosophical link is the cause for the emphasis.

questions.question_text: Which branch of physical geography is concerned with the study of distribution of landforms and forces that change them?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Geomorphology is the branch of physical geography that studies the distribution of landforms on the earth's surface and the internal and external forces that create and change them, such as weathering, erosion, and tectonic activity. Oceanography studies oceans, climatology studies climate, and biogeography studies the distribution of living organisms.

questions.question_text: What makes the subject of geography a science?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The systematic investigation and mapping of phenomenon on earth
options.explanation: Geography is a science because it uses systematic investigation, observation, data collection, and mapping of phenomena distributed on the earth's surface. It follows the scientific method and seeks to explain spatial patterns and relationships. It is not based on speculation, subjective analysis, or religious and traditional practices.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The emphasis on speculative philosophical idea

options.label: C
options.option_text: The subjective analysis of man and environment relationship

options.label: D
options.option_text: The concern with religious and traditional practices

questions.question_text: Among the following landforms, which one is formed when magma solidifies in a vertical or near vertical crack?

options.label: B
options.explanation: A dike is a tabular igneous intrusion formed when magma solidifies in a vertical or near-vertical crack or fissure that cuts across rock layers. A sill is horizontal and parallel to the layers, a laccolith is a dome-shaped intrusion, and a batholith is a massive deep intrusion. Hence vertical cracks produce dikes.

questions.question_text: How do reverse faults occur? They occur due to the action of

options.label: D
options.explanation: Reverse faults occur when compressional forces push rock masses together, causing one block to be thrust upward over the other along an inclined fault plane. Tensional forces produce normal faults and shearing forces produce strike-slip faults. The Coriolis force affects moving air and water, not faults.

questions.question_text: What can be the effect of an earthquake on buildings when it occurs with a magnitude of three on Richter scale?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The impacts are undetectable by humans.
options.explanation: An earthquake of magnitude three on the Richter scale is a very minor tremor whose impacts are largely undetectable by humans; it is recorded by instruments and felt only slightly by a few people and causes no damage to buildings. Total destruction, cracks, and collapse occur at far higher magnitudes.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It causes most buildings to collapse.

questions.question_text: Which geologic process mainly involves the breaking of rocks into pieces and formation of new substances?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Weathering is the geologic process that breaks rocks into smaller pieces and, through chemical reactions, changes their minerals into new substances at or near the earth's surface. Deposition and sedimentation build up materials, while orogenesis is mountain building. Therefore weathering matches the description of breaking rocks and forming new substances.

questions.question_text: Why is climate change becoming a pressing environmental issue of the current time? It is because

options.label: A
options.option_text: its causes are mainly attributed to natural factors and process.

options.label: B
options.option_text: its impact is confined to developed nations of the world.

options.label: C
options.option_text: its effect is easily reversed and controlled with little effort.

options.label: D
options.option_text: it severely threatens the human and natural system of the world.
options.explanation: Climate change has become a pressing environmental issue because it severely threatens both human systems, such as agriculture, water supply, health, and settlements, and natural systems, including ecosystems and biodiversity. Its causes are mainly anthropogenic, its impacts are global, and it is difficult to reverse, making it a serious current concern.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the effect of desertification?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It enhances the vulnerability of the land to climate change.
options.explanation: Desertification degrades land, strips vegetation, and destroys soil fertility, which enhances the land's vulnerability to climate change and drought. It lowers agricultural productive capacity, prevents rapid regeneration of soil, and reduces the quality of water downstream rather than raising capacity or quality.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It raises the agricultural productive capacity of the land.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It allows the rapid regeneration of soil resource.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It increases the quality of water in downstream areas.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is being practiced in Ethiopia to combat desertification?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ethiopia's Green Legacy Program is a nationwide afforestation initiative that has planted billions of seedlings to restore degraded land and combat desertification. It aims to increase forest cover, improve soil and water conservation, and reduce land degradation. The other options do not name actual programs being practiced for this purpose in Ethiopia.

questions.question_text: What type of drought occurs when a soil moisture deficit happens consistently?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Agricultural drought occurs when soil moisture is insufficient and a soil moisture deficit happens consistently, so that crops fail to grow and yields are reduced. Meteorological drought refers to below-normal rainfall, while hydrological drought refers to reduced water supplies in streams, lakes, and groundwater.

questions.question_text: Among the following, which one explains the incidence of famine?

options.label: A
options.option_text: During the 19th century, the “Great Famine” occurred in Ireland.
options.explanation: The incidence of famine is well explained by the Great Famine that occurred in Ireland during the nineteenth century, when potato blight caused mass starvation and migration. Famine was frequent in medieval Europe, its frequency has not recently increased in Western Europe, and Ethiopia's most disastrous famine occurred in 1984, not the 1990s.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Its occurrence was rare during middle ages in Europe.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Recently, its frequency is increasing in Western Europe.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The most disastrous famine in Ethiopia took place in 1990s.

questions.question_text: What is the distinctive nature of geographic research?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Its emphasis on weather forecasting of an area

options.label: B
options.option_text: Its emphasis on qualitative analysis methods

options.label: C
options.option_text: Its focus on resulting patterns and interaction
options.explanation: Geographic research is distinctive because it focuses on spatial patterns and the interactions between human and physical phenomena across the earth's surface. While other disciplines also forecast weather or study economic activities, geography uniquely analyzes how features are distributed and how they interact within places and regions.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Its focus on economic activities of the world

questions.question_text: What differentiates the qualitative research approach from the quantitative one? A qualitative research approach

options.label: A
options.option_text: applies statistical method of data analysis.

options.label: B
options.option_text: utilizes measures that produce discrete data.

options.label: C
options.option_text: employs designs and graphs for data presentation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: uses extensive descriptive data for analysis.
options.explanation: Qualitative research differs from quantitative research because it uses extensive descriptive data, such as words, observations, and narratives, for analysis rather than numbers and statistics. Quantitative approaches apply statistical analysis, produce discrete measurable data, and use designs and graphs to present their results.

questions.question_text: What makes a research methodology different from a research method?

options.label: A
options.explanation: A research methodology is broader in dimension than a research method. Methodology is the overall strategy, philosophy, and theoretical framework that guides how research is conducted, whereas a method is a specific technique or tool for collecting data, such as a survey or interview. Methodology therefore encompasses the methods.

questions.question_text: Which element of research presents what is already known about the research topic by other studies?

options.label: B
options.explanation: A literature review presents what is already known about a research topic by summarizing and analyzing previous studies, books, and articles, and it identifies gaps that justify the research. Research questions, sampling procedures, and research objectives do not summarize existing knowledge but rather direct the study itself.

questions.question_text: What makes ocean water flow from the equator towards the pole?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Ocean water flows from the equator toward the poles because of high temperature: equatorial waters are heated strongly and become less dense, so warm surface currents such as the Gulf Stream carry heat poleward and moderate climates. Low wind speed, high pressure, and low precipitation do not drive this equator-to-pole flow.

questions.question_text: In which direction do pressure belts move from their average position during the north hemisphere’s summer season?

options.label: B
options.explanation: During the northern hemisphere's summer season, the sun migrates northward toward the Tropic of Cancer, and the global pressure belts shift northward from their average positions. In the northern winter they shift southward. This seasonal migration of the pressure belts follows the apparent movement of the overhead sun.

questions.question_text: Why do we use the method of regional study?

options.label: A
options.option_text: To describe each element of the earth in detail

options.label: B
options.option_text: To study all aspects of the earth at a time

options.label: C
options.option_text: To examine the natural resources of the entire earth

options.label: D
options.explanation: The regional study method is used to investigate different geographical environments by dividing the earth into manageable regions. Because the earth is too large and diverse to study as a whole, geographers examine each region with its unique combination of physical and human features, allowing detailed analysis of every environment.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is among the characteristic of the Equatorial Rain Forest Region?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It has low annual range of temperature.
options.explanation: The Equatorial Rain Forest Region has a high temperature throughout the year with a very low annual range of temperature because the sun is nearly overhead all year. It does not form a continuous belt around the world, is inhabited mainly by traditional societies, and receives fairly even rainfall across the months.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It forms a continuous belt around the world.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is mainly inhabited by people who use modern technologies.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Its rainfall amount shows significant variation across months.

questions.question_text: Of the following, which one is the characteristic of the Tropical Hot Deserts?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Their winds are mainly cool and wet.

options.label: B
options.option_text: They are located along warm ocean currents.

options.label: C
options.option_text: They are known for plants with long roots.
options.explanation: Tropical hot deserts are characterized by xerophytic plants adapted to aridity, such as cacti and other plants with long roots that reach deep groundwater and reduced leaves that conserve water. Desert winds are hot and dry, deserts lie along cool currents on west coasts, and night temperatures are low because of clear skies.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Their night time temperature is high.

questions.question_text: Which land feature of Ethiopia separates the southeast highlands from the northern and southwestern highlands?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The Great Rift Valley of Ethiopia separates the southeastern highlands from the northern and southwestern highlands. It runs diagonally across the country from northeast to southwest, dividing the Ethiopian plateau into two blocks. The central highlands, western lowlands, and eastern lowlands do not perform this separating function.

questions.question_text: Where are most of the lowlands of Ethiopia found? They are found in the

options.label: D
options.explanation: Most of the lowlands of Ethiopia are found in the peripheral parts of the country, surrounding the central highland massifs. The western, eastern, and southern lowlands fringe the country's borders, while the central, southwestern, and northern parts are dominated by highlands and plateaus.

questions.question_text: How is lagoon formed by the action of sea waves? It is formed when

options.label: B
options.option_text: a narrow ridge of sand is projected into sea and attached to land.

options.label: C
options.option_text: an area of saltwater is separated from the sea by loose sandbanks.
options.explanation: A lagoon is formed when an area of shallow saltwater is separated from the open sea by loose sandbanks or a barrier of sand and shingle deposited by waves. A crescent-shaped sand hill forms a bay, a narrow ridge projecting into the sea is a spit, and a strip of coast covered with sediments is a beach.

options.label: D
options.option_text: a strip of land along the sea coast is covered with sediments.

options.label: A
options.option_text: a sand hill is formed with a crescent moon shape.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the feature of the Mesosphere?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It has constant temperature than the other layers.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It experiences frequent meteorites burn and disintegration.
options.explanation: The mesosphere is the layer of the atmosphere where most meteorites burn up and disintegrate due to friction with air molecules, appearing as shooting stars. Temperature decreases with height there. The thermosphere has the lowest air density, and the stratosphere contains the ozone layer with relatively constant temperature.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It has the lowest air density among layers of the atmosphere.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It contains higher concentration of ozone gases.
