questions.question_text: What is the major cause of frontal rainfall in high latitude areas?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Convergence of warm and cold air masses
options.explanation: Frontal rainfall in high-latitude areas is caused by the convergence of warm and cold air masses along fronts. When warm air is forced to rise over the colder, denser air, it cools, condenses, and produces rain. Elevated landmasses, dense forest coverage, and high year-round temperatures are not the cause.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Presence of large number of elevated landmasses

options.label: C
options.option_text: Concentration of dense forest coverage in the area

options.label: D
options.option_text: Existence of high temperature throughout the year

questions.question_text: What is the characteristic of the cumulonimbus cloud type?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is the major type of low clouds.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is thin and appears in sheets in sky.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is free from strong winds and tornados.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is associated with lightning and heavy rain.
options.explanation: Cumulonimbus clouds are tall, dense, vertical clouds associated with thunderstorms, producing heavy rain, lightning, thunder, and sometimes hail and tornadoes. They develop from strong convection and grow from low to high altitudes. They are not thin sheet clouds and are indeed associated with strong winds and severe weather.

questions.question_text: A hypothetical town is located along the beach where its temperature is modified by the local wind. Which type of wind does this town commonly experiences during the daytime?

options.label: B
options.explanation: During the daytime, the land heats up more quickly than the sea, so air over the land rises and creates low pressure, while cooler air over the sea flows inland as a sea breeze. This moderates the temperature of a beach town during the day. Land breezes and mountain breezes blow at night.

questions.question_text: Why do many parts of Ethiopia experience a cooler temperature despite the country’s location in the tropics? This is due to

options.label: A
options.option_text: the effect of cool ocean currents.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the larger land area of the country.

options.label: C
options.option_text: larger forest coverage of the country.

options.label: D
options.option_text: higher elevated landmass of the country.
options.explanation: Ethiopia lies within the tropics, yet much of it is cooler because the country consists largely of a high elevated landmass, with extensive plateaus and highlands above 1,500 metres. Temperature decreases with altitude, so the highlands enjoy temperate, cool conditions despite the tropical latitude.

questions.question_text: Why are coastal regions cooler than inland regions? This is because

options.label: A
options.option_text: rapid temperature change occurs on the land than the sea.
options.explanation: Coastal regions are cooler than inland regions because the land heats up and cools down more rapidly than the sea. The sea warms slowly and loses heat slowly, moderating coastal temperatures, while inland areas far from the sea experience stronger heating and cooling, producing hotter conditions.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the sea heats more quickly than the land.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the sea loses heat more quickly than the land.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the land has more consistent temperature than the sea.

questions.question_text: In which one of the following continents were the least COVID-19 cases reported in 2021?

options.label: D
options.explanation: In 2021, Africa reported the fewest COVID-19 cases among the continents despite its large population, which is attributed to a younger population, early containment measures, and limited international travel links. North America, Europe, and South America all recorded far higher numbers of cases during that year.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a reddish-brown toxic gas that causes air pollution?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Nitrogen dioxide is a reddish-brown toxic gas produced mainly by vehicle exhausts and industrial combustion. It irritates the respiratory system and contributes to acid rain and smog. Sulphur dioxide is colourless with a pungent smell, methane is odourless, and carbon monoxide is a colourless, odourless, poisonous gas.

questions.question_text: What causes soil contamination?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Keeping a farmland ideal for several years

options.label: B
options.option_text: Releasing of organic substance into the soil

options.label: C
options.option_text: Raw material leakage into the soil from industries
options.explanation: Soil contamination is caused by the leakage of raw materials, chemicals, and wastes from industries into the soil, introducing toxic substances such as heavy metals and solvents. Keeping a farmland fallow, releasing organic substances, and rotating crops are beneficial soil-management practices that do not contaminate the soil.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Rotation of different crops on the same farmland

questions.question_text: How can the problems of environmental sustainability be reduced?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By minimizing the emission of greenhouse gasses
options.explanation: The problems of environmental sustainability can be reduced by minimizing the emission of greenhouse gases, which mitigates climate change and its impacts on ecosystems and societies. Intensive application of agricultural inputs degrades soil and water, reducing food consumption harms well-being, and abstaining from all non-renewable energy is impractical.

options.label: B
options.option_text: By promoting intensive application of agricultural inputs

options.label: C
options.option_text: By reducing people’s per-capita food consumption

options.label: D
options.option_text: By abstaining from using non-renewable energy sources

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the characteristic of environmental education?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is a short term training on environmental issues.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is limited to the natural aspect of an environment.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It aims at encouraging maximum resource utilization.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is an interdisciplinary education for human being.
options.explanation: Environmental education is an interdisciplinary education that draws on the natural sciences, social sciences, and humanities to help people understand environmental problems and develop responsible attitudes and skills. It is a lifelong process rather than short-term training, covers both natural and human aspects, and encourages sustainable rather than maximum resource use.

questions.question_text: Which type of environmental movement recommends promotion of property rights as a tool for conserving the environment?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Free market environmentalism advocates using property rights and market-based mechanisms to conserve the environment. It argues that clear ownership of resources gives owners a direct incentive to manage them sustainably. Preservationism, dark greens, and popular environmentalism rely more on regulation, protection, or community action than on property rights.

questions.question_text: What is the common environment-friendly indigenous knowledge practice in wet highland landscape of Western Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Construction of stone terraces along the hills
options.explanation: In the wet highland landscapes of western Ethiopia, the common environment-friendly indigenous knowledge practice is the construction of stone terraces along hillsides, which slows runoff, prevents soil erosion, and conserves water and soil fertility. This sustainable technique has been used by highland farmers for generations to protect their steep cultivated slopes.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Preservation of medicinal plants and animals

options.label: D
options.option_text: Consideration of land as a sacred resource

questions.question_text: Which one of the following differentiates climate change mitigation strategies from adaptation? Mitigation strategies

options.label: A
options.option_text: consider climate change as an opportunity rather than a challenge.

options.label: C
options.option_text: strive to reduce the use of fossil fuels.
options.explanation: Climate change mitigation strategies differ from adaptation because they strive to reduce the use of fossil fuels and the emission of greenhouse gases at their source, for example by shifting to renewable energy. Adaptation instead adjusts to the effects of climate change and can be reactive or autonomous.

questions.question_text: Of the following, which one indicates the strength of the Kyoto Protocol (2005)?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It introduced compulsory targets in reducing emission of greenhouse gases.
options.explanation: The strength of the Kyoto Protocol of 2005 is that it introduced compulsory, legally binding targets for developed countries to reduce their emission of greenhouse gases. It established emission-reduction commitments for industrialized nations, whereas developing countries were not bound by mandatory reduction targets at that time.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It established financial support for developing nations to address climate change.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It involved all nations in the reduction of emission of greenhouse gases.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It forced developing countries to become carbon neutral in their activities.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct about the status of international conventions and agreements on climate change?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Several countries see climate change as a good opportunity for sustainable development.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Most countries recognize the use of renewable energy sources as a remedy for climate change.
options.explanation: Most countries recognize the use of renewable energy sources as a remedy for climate change, and international conventions and agreements have promoted a shift toward clean energy. Developed countries historically contribute more to the occurrence of climate change, and the global climate issue was recognized well before the year 2000.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Developing countries are contributing more to the occurrence of climate change.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Issue of climate change at global scale came into being starting from the year 2000.

questions.question_text: How does the expansion of hydroelectric power in Ethiopia help to reduce climate change?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By expanding of manufacturing industries in the country

options.label: B
options.option_text: By discouraging the use of other energy sources than electricity

options.label: C
options.option_text: By reducing reliance on non-renewable energy sources
options.explanation: The expansion of hydroelectric power in Ethiopia helps reduce climate change by reducing reliance on non-renewable energy sources such as coal, oil, and wood. Because hydroelectricity generates little greenhouse gas, substituting it for fossil fuels lowers carbon emissions and also reduces pressure on forests and other biomass fuels.

options.label: D
options.option_text: By transforming the economy from agriculture to a service-based one

questions.question_text: What is the core issue in the concept of sustainable development?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Applying a traditional way of resource conservation

options.label: D
options.option_text: Keeping harmony between environment and development
options.explanation: The core issue in the concept of sustainable development is keeping harmony between the environment and development, so that present needs are met without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs. It balances economic growth, social equity, and environmental protection rather than maximizing resource use or promoting privatization.

questions.question_text: What is the focus of the social dimension of sustainable development?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Reducing the utilization of environmental resources

options.label: B
options.option_text: Prioritizing of human needs over the environment

options.label: C
options.option_text: Ensuring fair access to local services
options.explanation: The social dimension of sustainable development focuses on ensuring fair access to local services and resources, such as education, health, and clean water, for all people, especially the poor and marginalized. It emphasizes equity and well-being rather than prioritizing human needs over the environment or offering special support for investors.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the shortcoming of applying sustainable development?

options.label: B
options.explanation: A shortcoming of applying sustainable development is its broadness in nature: the concept is so wide and flexible that it means different things to different people and is difficult to define, measure, and implement consistently. This vagueness makes the practical application and evaluation of sustainability goals challenging.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Its exceptional benefit for all people

options.label: D
options.option_text: Its uniformity in understanding its goals

questions.question_text: What is the prime importance of soil in agriculture?

options.label: D
options.option_text: Provision of essential nutrients for plants
options.explanation: The prime importance of soil in agriculture is that it provides essential nutrients, water, and anchorage for plants, enabling crops to grow. It holds and supplies mineral elements such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium to plant roots. Other functions like water regulation and carbon storage are secondary to plant nutrition.

questions.question_text: Globally which region is highly affected by HIV/AIDS?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Sub-Saharan Africa is the region most highly affected by HIV/AIDS globally, carrying the overwhelming majority of the world's HIV infections and AIDS-related deaths. Factors include limited access to health services, poverty, and high infection rates. Southeast Asia, Oceania, and Latin America have far lower prevalence rates.

questions.question_text: How does the economic policy of Ethiopia contribute to development?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Raises public awareness on sustainable resource utilization
options.explanation: Ethiopia's economic policy contributes to development by raising public awareness of sustainable resource utilization, promoting the balanced use of natural resources so that development continues without exhausting the resource base. This encourages responsible management by the community rather than government-led control, free access, or prioritizing projects over conservation.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Encourages citizens free access to resources

options.label: D
options.option_text: Prioritizes development projects over resource conservation

questions.question_text: Which continent was a part of Gondwanaland?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Antarctica was a part of Gondwanaland, the ancient supercontinent that also included Africa, South America, Australia, India, and Madagascar. The fossil and geological similarities among these continents support their former connection. Europe, North America, and Asia were part of the northern landmass Laurasia rather than Gondwanaland.

questions.question_text: Why was Alfred Wegener's continental drift theory NOT easily accepted by the scientific community of the time? This was due to

options.label: A
options.option_text: the lack of direct evidence for the movement of continents.
options.explanation: Alfred Wegener's continental drift theory was not easily accepted because he could not provide a direct, convincing mechanism or direct evidence for the movement of continents. His evidence, such as matching coastlines and fossils, was indirect, and geologists doubted that continents could plow through the oceanic crust.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the presentation of coastline similarity as an indicator of continental drift.

options.label: C
options.option_text: his belief that Pangaea was broken before the Cenozoic Era.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the collection of most data from northern hemisphere.

questions.question_text: How do transform fault boundaries occur? They occur when

options.label: A
options.option_text: plates move away from each other.

options.label: B
options.option_text: two plates move towards each other.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Transform fault boundaries occur when two tectonic plates slide past each other horizontally, neither creating nor destroying crust. The grinding movement causes shallow earthquakes, as along the San Andreas Fault. Convergent boundaries move toward each other, divergent boundaries move apart, and static plates do not form boundaries.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following describes chemical weathering? It is the

options.label: A
options.option_text: peeling of rocks owing to temperature change.

options.label: B
options.option_text: process of cementation and deposition of rocks.

options.label: C
options.option_text: change in minerals of rocks into new substance.
options.explanation: Chemical weathering involves the change of minerals in rocks into new substances through chemical reactions such as oxidation, hydrolysis, and carbonation, often involving water and acids. Peeling due to temperature change is exfoliation, frost expansion is physical weathering, and cementation and deposition are sedimentary processes.

options.label: D
options.option_text: expansion and breaking of rocks due to frost.

questions.question_text: What issues were underlined by the 1994 Cairo International Conference on Population and Development?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Recognition of family planning as a sole means of reducing population

options.label: B
options.option_text: The effect of rapid population growth of developed countries on the environment

options.label: C
options.option_text: Understanding population from inequitable and inhuman viewpoint

options.label: D
options.option_text: The impact of consumption on the environment in developed nations
options.explanation: The 1994 Cairo International Conference on Population and Development emphasized the impact of consumption and production patterns in developed nations on the environment and recognized that reproductive health and women's rights are central to population policy. It rejected a purely family-planning-only approach and viewed population issues with equity and human dignity.

questions.question_text: What was the strategy used by Kenya to control population growth?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Kenya's strategy to control population growth was the adoption of family planning programs, beginning with the 1967 Family Planning Policy and strengthened in later national population policies, which promoted contraceptive use to reduce fertility. The one-child policy is associated with China, not Kenya.

questions.question_text: Which economic factor of development measures the progress of production?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Technology is the economic factor of development that measures the progress of production, because improved technology raises productivity, efficiency, and output. Social values, natural resources, and capital expenditure influence development but do not directly measure the progress of production as technology does.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an environmental implication of population growth?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Improvement in the provision of transport services

options.label: B
options.option_text: Increase in the number of unemployed people

options.label: D
options.explanation: The environmental implication of population growth is the rapid depletion of natural resources, as more people consume more water, land, forests, and minerals and generate more waste and pollution. Unemployment and the deterioration of social values are social and economic implications rather than environmental ones.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an indicator of a socially developed nation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Lower percentage of population living below poverty line.
options.explanation: An indicator of a socially developed nation is a lower percentage of its population living below the poverty line, reflecting widespread well-being and equity. Higher percentages of underweight children, higher discrimination, and lower access to sanitation all indicate social underdevelopment rather than social development.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Higher percentage of underweight children in a population.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Higher prevalence of discrimination among population groups.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Lower proportion of population with access to sanitation service.

questions.question_text: How does a clinical health intervention model help achieving environmental health outcomes?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By reducing the occurrence of environmental hazards

options.label: B
options.option_text: By protecting human beings from environmental adversaries

options.label: C
options.option_text: By treating the already existing diseases
options.explanation: A clinical health intervention model helps achieve environmental health outcomes by treating the already existing diseases, providing curative care to people who have fallen ill. This is a reactive approach, in contrast to prevention-oriented approaches that reduce environmental hazards, protect people from adversaries, or control disease-causing agents before illness occurs.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct with regard to the principles of environmental health?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Environmental health risk is declining today compared to the past.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Air pollution is the largest environmental health risk in the world.
options.explanation: According to environmental health principles, air pollution is the largest environmental health risk in the world, causing millions of premature deaths annually. Environmental health risks are generally increasing, their impacts differ among countries, and proximity to green areas is associated with lower, not higher, health risks.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The health impact of environment is similar among countries.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Proximity to green areas is associated with higher health risks.

questions.question_text: What distinguishes a population census from other sources of population data?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It collects data from merely a segment of the population.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is conducted at specified time interval.
options.explanation: A population census is distinguished from other sources of population data by being a complete enumeration of the population conducted at a specified time interval, usually every ten years, on a specific reference date. It covers the entire population rather than a segment, is expensive, and is a primary rather than supplementary source.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is used to supplement data collected by other sources.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is less expensive compared to other sources of data.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following conditions characterizes a rural settlement? It is a settlement where

options.label: B
options.option_text: the service sector leads the economy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A rural settlement is characterized by the dominance of isolated homesteads and dispersed farmhouses, low population density, and an economy based primarily on agriculture. Urban settlements have the highest density, a leading service sector, and a diverse economic base. Hence isolated homesteads identify a rural settlement.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains quaternary economic activities?

options.label: A
options.option_text: They involve specialized knowledge and skills.
options.explanation: Quaternary economic activities involve specialized knowledge and skills, including research, information technology, education, and scientific development. They are distinct from primary activities that extract raw materials, secondary activities that modify materials, and tertiary activities that distribute and provide products and services.

options.label: B
options.option_text: They focus on modification of raw materials for consumption.

options.label: C
options.option_text: They are mainly engaged in extraction of raw materials.

options.label: D
options.option_text: They are concerned with distribution and provision of products.

questions.question_text: Of the following, which one is a natural cause of land use changes?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Topography is a natural cause of land use changes because landforms, slope, and altitude influence how land is used and can change land use through processes like erosion, flooding, and soil deposition. Cultivation culture, farming mechanisms, and land policy are human factors that also shape land use.

questions.question_text: Among the following, which one is an indirect use of natural vegetation? It serves as a

options.label: B
options.explanation: An indirect use of natural vegetation is serving as a home or habitat for wild animals, which maintains biodiversity and ecological balance. Direct uses are extracting food, fuel wood, and construction materials. Indirect uses are the ecological and environmental services vegetation provides without being consumed directly.

questions.question_text: Which common natural vegetation of Ethiopia is widely used for making water pipe and fences?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bamboo is the natural vegetation of Ethiopia widely used for making water pipes, fences, baskets, and construction materials. It grows abundantly in the highlands and is versatile and renewable. Juniperus, Podocarpus, and Olea are valuable timber trees used mainly for lumber and building rather than pipes and fences.

questions.question_text: What is the main advantage of phosphates to a country?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The main advantage of phosphates to a country is their use in fertilizer making, since phosphorus is an essential plant nutrient. Phosphate rock is processed into phosphate fertilizers that boost agricultural productivity. It is not primarily an energy source, a construction material, or an aesthetic resource.

questions.question_text: During which month does the station ‘K’ have the lowest average temperature record?

options.label: D
options.explanation: According to the climate data for station K, the lowest average temperature of 28 degrees Celsius is recorded in November, whereas the other months show temperatures of 29 degrees or higher, with the warmest months reaching 32 degrees. Hence November is the month with the lowest average temperature record.

questions.question_text: What do the closely spaced isobars imply on weather maps?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Closely spaced isobars on a weather map imply a high pressure gradient, meaning that pressure changes rapidly over a short distance. This steep gradient produces strong winds, since air rushes from high to low pressure. Widely spaced isobars indicate a gentle gradient and weak winds.

questions.question_text: What is the Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) of the region?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The Infant Mortality Rate is the number of deaths of infants below one year per live births in a year, expressed here per 100. With 2,300,000 live births and 78,000 deaths below age one, the rate equals 78,000 divided by 2,300,000 times 100, which is 3.39 percent, approximately 3.4 percent.

questions.question_text: What is the Net Migration Rate (NMR) of the region?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The Net Migration Rate is the difference between immigrants and emigrants divided by the total population, multiplied by 1,000. Net migration equals 509,100 minus 323,100, or 186,000. Dividing by 67,400,000 and multiplying by 1,000 gives 2.76 per 1,000, approximately 2.8 per 1,000, so option C is correct.

questions.question_text: What is the relief feature indicated by letter ‘H’ on the map?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Letter H on the map marks a saddle, a low-lying area or depression between two higher elevations or ridges. On a contour map a saddle appears where contour lines dip between two high points, forming a U-shaped pattern. Valleys, ridges, and closed depressions have different contour patterns.

questions.question_text: If the map distance between two consecutive lines of latitude is 3.5 cm, what will be the scale of this map? (Hint: 1°=111 km)

options.label: A
options.explanation: The distance between two consecutive lines of latitude is ten minutes, which equals 10 divided by 60 times 111 km, that is 18.5 km or 1,850,000 cm on the ground. Given a map distance of 3.5 cm, the scale is 3.5 to 1,850,000, which simplifies to 1 to 528,571, approximately 1:529,000.

questions.question_text: What is the type of contour line represented by letter ‘G’ on the map?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Letter G points to a contour line that is drawn thicker and bolder and labeled with its elevation, which identifies it as an index contour. Index contours appear at regular intervals, usually every fifth contour, to make reading elevations easier. Regular, intermediate, and supplementary contours are not the labeled bold lines.

questions.question_text: Economic inequality is the disproportionate distribution of total national income among households. Which one of the following is correct about the alternative measurements of income inequality?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Kuznets ratio is a measure of the degree of inequality between high income and low-income groups in the country.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Gini-coefficient value equals to zero implies perfect inequality.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The higher is the value of Gini coefficient, the lower the inequality.

options.label: D
options.option_text: In the Lorenz curve if income distribution were perfectly unequal, it would be represented by the 45-degree line.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about the situation of global and regional poverty?

options.label: A
options.option_text: There are clear indications that the conditions of global poverty has worsened over the past half century.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Extreme poverty remains wide spread in developing world in past decades.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Sub-Saharan Africa showed a remarkable achievement in eradicating poverty from 1950 to 2000.

options.label: D
options.option_text: China has experienced virtually no rate of poverty reduction in the past decades.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the main reason why women face poverty?

options.label: A
options.option_text: They have less access to education, formal sector employment and social security.

options.label: B
options.option_text: They are more likely to obtain formal employment in private companies.

options.label: C
options.option_text: They have unlimited control over household income and resources.

options.label: D
options.option_text: They have equal access to the resources that are necessary to create stable income.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the objective of the third five-year plan (1968-1973) during the Imperial Period?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Developing strong infrastructure particularly in transportation and communication

options.label: B
options.option_text: Accelerating agriculture development by promoting commercial agriculture

options.label: C
options.option_text: Diversifying of production and introduction of modern processing methods

options.label: D
options.option_text: Raising manufacturing and agro-industrial performance and expansion of educational opportunities

questions.question_text: The 1974 revolution by Derg resulted in the establishment of a socialist state which aimed at the nationalization and restricting of the Ethiopian economy. The regime changed the previous national development strategy placing the major emphasis on a centrally planned economy. Which one of the following is correct about the major changes?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The agriculture-led development was deployed as the main development strategy.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The rural land and other productive assets were privatized, and land was distributed among farmers.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The commercial farms were put under government control, and land tenancy was abolished.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Rural lands are transferred to large manufacturers due shift to industry-led development policy.

questions.question_text: To measure the general price level of an economy policy makers, use the GDP deflator, Consumer's Price Index (CPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI). Which one of the following is correct about these measures?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The ratio of Nominal GDP to real GDP is equivalent to CPI.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The ratio of Real GDP to GDP deflator is equivalent to Nominal GDP.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The ratio of Nominal GDP to real GDP is equivalent to PPI.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The ratio of Nominal GDP to real GDP is equivalent to GDP deflator.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about the role of investment on economic growth?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It boosts economic growth by increasing consumption expenditure.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It leads to lower economic growth by reducing saving.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It leads to higher economic growth by increasing capital stock.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It limits economic growth by postponing gains in to longer period.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct about the relationship between consumption and saving?

options.label: A
options.option_text: When income is more than consumption there is a positive saving.

options.label: B
options.option_text: When income equals to consumption there is a positive saving.

options.label: C
options.option_text: When income is more than consumption there is a dissaving.

options.label: D
options.option_text: When income is less than consumption there is a positive saving.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following correctly defines investment?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is the amount of goods purchased for current consumption.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It involves reducing saving for purchasing consumer goods.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is the amount of goods purchased and not consumed in present time.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It involves increasing consumption by selling fixed assets.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following best describes the ability of one country to produce one of the two goods at the lower cost relative to its trading partner?
Which one of the following is among the top priorities of the Ethiopian government in the recent development of the agricultural sector?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Nationalization of all private and commercial farms

options.label: B
options.option_text: Government control of virtually all agricultural input and output markets

options.label: C
options.option_text: Small and large-scale irrigation development and financing inputs

options.label: D
options.option_text: Forced food-grain quota deliveries at predetermined price

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the focus area of macroeconomics?

options.label: A
options.option_text: What factors determine the productivity of manufacturing firms?

options.label: B
options.option_text: How does the increase in selling price affect profitability of firms?

options.label: C
options.option_text: What is the cause of inflation and how it can be determined?

options.label: D
options.option_text: Why do outputs and employment of manufacturing firms fail?

questions.question_text: Which one of the following correctly explains the concept of aggregate demand?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The total amount of goods produced in an economy at a given period.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The total spending by different sectors of the economy at a given period.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The sum of individuals demands for a given product with in a year.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The total amount of spending by an individual with in a year.

questions.question_text: What explains the upward slope of the aggregate supply curve?
Which one of the following is correct about the short-run market equilibrium?

options.label: A
options.option_text: At equilibrium the aggregate demand is greater than the aggregate supply.

options.label: B
options.option_text: At equilibrium the aggregate demand is equals to the aggregate supply.

options.label: C
options.option_text: At equilibrium the aggregate demand is less than the aggregate supply.

options.label: D
options.option_text: At equilibrium the aggregate demand and aggregate supply equals to zero.

questions.question_text: Suppose an open economy interacting with the rest of the world through trade and investment. Which one of the following is a desirable outcome for this economy?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A decrease in overall price level of good and services over a certain period

options.label: B
options.option_text: An increase in the value of import more than the value of export

options.label: C
options.option_text: A decrease in the level of output with in an economy over a given time period

options.label: D
options.option_text: An increase in unemployment with in an economy over a given period of time

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about economic growth?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Short run growth occurs when there is a sustained increase in per capita income.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Structural change is characterized by a decrease in share of industry in GDP.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Long-run economic growth is associated with structural change in the economy.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Structural change is characterized by an increase in share of agriculture in GDP.

questions.question_text: Among the followings, which one is NOT the possible reason behind why some countries are rich while the others are poor?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Difference in productivity of factor inputs

options.label: D
options.option_text: Difference in location of the country

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is categorized under consumption expenditure on goods?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Expenditure by households on medical care

questions.question_text: Total spending in the economy rises from one year to the next due to either the economy is producing a larger output or outputs are being sold at higher prices. To measure these effects, economists use real GDP and Nominal GDP. Which one of the following is correct about the two measures?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Change in real GDP reflects only changes in the amounts being produced.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Nominal GDP values the economy's production of goods and services at a constant base year price.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Change in nominal GDP reflects only changes in the amounts being produced.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Real GDP values the economy's production of goods and services at current price.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct about product differentiation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is the characteristic of firms operating under perfectly competitive market structure.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It shows that fancied differentiation occurs when there are differences in input use.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It shows that real differentiation occurs when there are differences in product specification.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is one way that firms operating in a pure monopoly market can acquire market power.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct about collusive oligopoly?

options.label: A

What was the event that served as a major trigger for power struggle and foreign intervention in the Ethiopian politics between 1906 and 1910?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The death of Ras Mekonnen who was expected to succeed Menelik
options.explanation: Ras Mekonnen died in 1906, the very year Menelik suffered his first stroke. As the most probable successor to the emperor, his death left the succession uncertain and threw the court into rivalry. Fearing chaos, Britain, France and Italy also intervened, signing the Tripartite Treaty of 1906 to protect their interests.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The removal from the palace of Taytu and her appeal to the legations for support

options.label: C
options.option_text: The death of Ras Tesemma who had served as Iyasu's regent

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about the period of dual rule (or "diarchy") in Ethiopian politics of early 20th century?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The traditionalists fought in support of greater foreign involvement in Ethiopian affairs

options.label: B
options.option_text: It was all about the coronation of Ras Teferi as king

options.label: C
options.option_text: The former Shoan generals except Fitawrari Habte Giorgis

options.label: D
options.option_text: Political power was equally divided between Empress Zewditu and Ras
options.explanation: Under the diarchy, Empress Zewditu retained supreme political power while Ras Teferi, the heir and regent, managed the day-to-day administration. Power was therefore divided between the two: Zewditu represented the conservative traditionalists, while Teferi pushed modernist reforms, a division that continued until 1930.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was a key development in the emergence of autocracy in Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Imposition of an obligation on regional lords to mobilize their armies in times of external aggression

options.label: B
options.option_text: The adoption of a Constitution in 1931 aimed at resolving the problems of regional lords and succession

options.label: C
options.option_text: The appointment by the monarch of relatives to administrative and financial posts
options.explanation: Autocracy grew when the monarch appointed his relatives to key administrative and financial posts. This concentrated power in the hands of loyal family members, weakened independent regional lords, and helped Haile Selassie build a centralized state in which he alone controlled appointments and revenues.

questions.question_text: In which of the following anti-colonial movements was forced cotton production the major issue?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The Maji Maji Rebellion broke out in German East Africa in 1905 after the Germans forced Africans to grow cotton for export. This forced cotton cultivation, combined with oppressive labour demands, drove the people to rise up in one of the largest anti-colonial revolts in African history.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was an immediate trigger for the Ethiopian War of 1935-1936?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Declaration by Fascist Mussolini to avenge the defeat of Adwa

options.label: B
options.option_text: The concentration of huge Italian troops in Eritrea and Somalia

options.label: C
options.option_text: The Italian decision to build a railway from Eritrea to Somaliland

options.label: D
options.option_text: The Wal Wal Incident that took place in the Ogaden
options.explanation: The Wal Wal Incident of December 1934 was the immediate trigger. Italian forces, already stationed inside Ethiopia, clashed with Ethiopian troops at the wells of Wal Wal in the Ogaden. After this confrontation, Italy rejected arbitration and began its full-scale invasion of Ethiopia in October 1935.

questions.question_text: Who was designated as viceroy of the Emperor and nominated as head of the Black Lion Organization in 1936-37?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Ras Imiru Haile Selassie was designated as the emperor's viceroy when Haile Selassie went into exile and was also nominated head of the Black Lion Organization. He led the organized resistance from Gore in the southwest until he surrendered to the Italians in December 1936.

questions.question_text: Which of following is correct about the Italian rule in Ethiopia during the Occupation of 1936-1941?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The Italians allowed activities by other European merchants

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Italian government introduced the basic elements of democracy

options.label: C
options.option_text: The Italians kept the former administrative divisions largely intact

options.label: D
options.option_text: The Italian style appointed three consecutive viceroys as governors
options.explanation: During the occupation from 1936 to 1941, Italy ruled Ethiopia through three successive viceroys: Badoglio, Graziani and the Duke of Aosta. Each governed Italian East Africa with its headquarters at Asmara, and their rule was characterized by repression rather than democracy or open trade.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the Black Lions Organization?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It was formed long before Emperor Haile Selassie left the country
options.explanation: The Black Lion Organization was formed before Emperor Haile Selassie left the country in 1936, uniting Holeta graduates and foreign-educated intellectuals who resolved to continue the armed struggle under Ras Imiru rather than go into exile.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It actively engaged in fighting around the town of Gore, Illubabor

options.label: C
options.option_text: It was mainly composed of graduates of Holeta Military Academy

options.label: D
options.option_text: It continued the resistance struggle until the Italians were ousted

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the establishment of the United Nations Organization (UNO)?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The UN Security Council has five permanent members from the very beginning in 1945

options.label: B
options.option_text: The idea of replacing the League of Nations by another organization was first expressed in the Atlantic Charter
options.explanation: The idea of creating a new world organization to replace the League of Nations was first expressed in the Atlantic Charter of August 1941. President Roosevelt and Prime Minister Churchill there called for a wider and permanent system of general security, a proposal later realized when the UN was founded in 1945.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The Soviet Union preferred the continuation of the League of Nations to the UNO

options.label: D
options.option_text: It was established in November 1944 at the Dumbarton Oaks near Washington

questions.question_text: Which one of the following properly describes the differing positions of groups of African states prior to the formation of the OAU in 1963?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The Casablanca Group emphasized the immediate creation of the United States of Africa
options.explanation: The Casablanca Group, led by Ghana, Guinea, Mali and Egypt, favoured immediate continental political union and called for the creation of the United States of Africa. The more moderate Monrovia and Brazzaville groups preferred gradual functional cooperation among independent African states.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Monrovia Group promoted the formation of four regional organizations

options.label: C
options.option_text: The Anglophone and Francophone countries were advocates of unity along linguistic lines

options.label: D
options.option_text: The Brazzaville Group was opposed to the establishment of a continental organization

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the process of European colonial expansion in Africa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Many African territories were acquired throughout right conquest

options.label: B
options.option_text: Europeans took control by signing genuine treaties with African rulers

options.label: C
options.option_text: Without exception, European explorers served as government agents

options.label: D
options.option_text: European evangelical missionaries hastened colonial conquest
options.explanation: European missionaries generally hastened colonial conquest. They entered Africa before the armies, learned the languages, wrote reports about local resources, and influenced their governments to intervene. Their presence and information helped prepare the way for formal colonial rule.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was a major feature of long distance trade in 19th century-Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Women took part in long-distance trade as caravan merchants

options.label: B
options.option_text: Christian merchants of north-western Ethiopia were called Afkala

options.label: C
options.option_text: Long distance trade was conducted only in certain regions and fixed market days

options.label: D
options.option_text: The head of caravan traders had the title of Negadras
options.explanation: In nineteenth-century Ethiopia, the leader of a caravan of traders held the title of Negadras. The Negadras supervised the caravan, organized the merchants, and represented their interests, making this office a central feature of long-distance trade in the region.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was NOT true about long-distance trade in the Ethiopian region?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It helped the introduction of Islam into the Gibe region

options.label: B
options.option_text: It encouraged division of labour and specialization of production

options.label: C
options.option_text: It was conducted on the basis of laws formally agreed upon by all regional rulers
options.explanation: Long-distance trade was not conducted under laws formally agreed upon by all regional rulers. Instead, it operated on local customs, the goodwill of chiefs, and traditional market arrangements. The other statements describe genuine results of this trade, such as the spread of Islam and regional specialization.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It linked people in the northern regions with those in the south-western regions

questions.question_text: Which of the following was a major factor for the downfall of Emperor Tewodros II of Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The frequent resistance of regional lords to his authority exhausted his army
options.explanation: The constant rebellions of regional lords drained Tewodros' army and resources. Wagshum Gobaze, Kassa Mircha and Menelik repeatedly rose against him, forcing him to move his army around the country and wear it out, which finally led to his defeat at Magdala in 1868.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The effort to manufacture big guns at Gafat dissipated the money needed to buy other weapons

options.label: C
options.option_text: The attempt to separate state and religion as a modern state aroused opposition

options.label: D
options.option_text: The fact that he was not born from a royal family undermined his legitimacy

questions.question_text: Which of the following best explains the administrative policy of Emperor Yohannes IV?

options.label: A
options.option_text: He persisted like Tewodros with the use of force to impose royal authority

options.label: B
options.option_text: He removed from power all local chiefs who rebelled against him

options.label: C
options.option_text: He recognized the title of 'king of kings' only for Menelik of Shoa

options.label: D
options.option_text: He shared power with vassals as long as they paid regular tribute
options.explanation: Unlike Tewodros, Yohannes IV ruled by sharing power with his vassals. He gave Menelik of Shoa, Ras Adal of Gojjam and others autonomy over their regions as long as they paid regular tribute and remained loyal, a policy that brought relative stability to his reign.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the relation between Egypt and Ethiopia under Yohannes IV in the 1870s?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Christianity helped Yohannes to gain European support against Muslim Egypt

options.label: B
options.option_text: Egypt succeeded to enlist considerable local collaboration against Yohannes

options.label: C
options.option_text: Until 1875 Yohannes sought diplomacy to avert Egyptian incursion
options.explanation: Until 1875, Yohannes IV tried to resolve the dispute with Egypt peacefully through diplomatic means. He sought to avoid war even as Egypt moved toward invasion. Only after Egypt attacked did he fight and defeat the Egyptians at Gundet and Gura in 1875 and 1876.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Egypt posed a major military threat to Ethiopia from its colony of Sudan

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the Battles of Gundet and Gur'a?

options.label: A
options.option_text: They were major victories for Ethiopia despite relatively high sacrifices
options.explanation: The battles of Gundet (1875) and Gura (1876) were major Ethiopian victories over the invading Egyptian forces. Ethiopia won both engagements, although the victories came at the cost of relatively heavy Ethiopian casualties, and they did not entirely remove the Egyptian presence from the region.

options.label: B
options.option_text: They ousted the Egyptian forces once and for all from the Red Sea coast

options.label: C
options.option_text: They were fought to repulse the Egyptians from the eastern region of Harar

options.label: D
options.option_text: They were decisive victories of the Afar people

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was a result of the Hewett Treaty between Ethiopia and Britain of 1884?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It made the Mahdist Sudan hostile to the Ethiopian state

options.label: B
options.option_text: It discouraged diplomatic relations between Ethiopia and France

options.label: C
options.option_text: It prevented the restoration of Egyptian controlled Bogos to Ethiopia

options.label: D
options.option_text: It allowed Ethiopia free transit of goods through Massawa
options.explanation: Under the Hewett Treaty of 1884 between Ethiopia and Britain, Ethiopia was allowed free transit for its goods through Massawa. The treaty also restored the Bogos region to Ethiopia and was signed partly to secure Ethiopian cooperation against the Mahdist forces in Sudan.

questions.question_text: What was the immediate consequence of Ethiopian victory at Adwa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The reaffirmation of the Treaty of Wuchale by the Treaty of Addis Ababa
options.explanation: After Adwa, the Treaty of Addis Ababa of 1896 formally replaced the Treaty of Wuchale, which Italy had used to claim a protectorate over Ethiopia, and Italy recognized the full independence of Ethiopia. The option wording is misleading because the treaty annulled, not reaffirmed, the earlier agreement.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The signing of treaties that fixed the current boundaries of Ethiopia

options.label: C
options.option_text: Agreement by Italy to return some territories from their Eritrean colony to Ethiopia

options.label: D
options.option_text: The beginning of fresh preparations in Italy for military revenge against Ethiopia

questions.question_text: Which of the following projects of modernization is attributed to the reign of Emperor Menelik II?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The introduction of a parliamentary form of government

options.label: B
options.option_text: Establishment of Municipal police force called Tomabulle

options.label: C
options.option_text: Construction of a railway line to facilitate transportation
options.explanation: Emperor Menelik II began the construction of a railway line from Djibouti to Addis Ababa to facilitate transportation and trade. This was one of his major modernization projects, along with building the new capital at Addis Ababa and establishing banks, schools and hospitals.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about units of chronology in history?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A period of one hundred years is known as millennium

options.label: B
options.option_text: The year from 2000 to 2099 is similar to the 20th century

options.label: C
options.option_text: Historical calendars count dates both backward and forward
options.explanation: Historical calendars count dates both backward and forward from a fixed reference point. Dates before the reference are counted backward as BC or BCE and dates after it are counted forward as AD or CE. A hundred years makes a century, not a millennium.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Very recent events are mostly referred to as B.P.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct statement about the human evolution?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Lucy's fossil is the oldest of Australopithecine fossils

options.label: B
options.option_text: Homo habilis was an upright walking human being

options.label: C
options.option_text: Australopithecines had small brains in large faces
options.explanation: Australopithecines were characterized by small brains, around four hundred to five hundred cubic centimetres, set in large protruding faces. This combination distinguishes them from later hominins, which developed larger brains relative to their facial size.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Charles Darwin advocated the creationist theory

questions.question_text: One of the following is believed to be the earliest state in the Horn of Africa region?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Punt is considered the earliest state in the Horn of Africa, as it is mentioned in Egyptian records from the third millennium BC. The Egyptians traded with Punt for goods such as gold, myrrh and frankincense long before Damat and Aksum emerged.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the languages of Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Languages belonging to a given super-family are geographically contiguous
options.explanation: Languages belonging to a given super-family are geographically contiguous; related languages tend to be found in neighbouring areas. Ethiopia's languages belong to the Afro-Asiatic and Nilo-Saharan super-families, whose members cluster in the regions where the speakers live.

options.label: B
options.option_text: A large number of Semitic languages are disappearing

options.label: C
options.option_text: They fall under two super-families and five families

options.label: D
options.option_text: They are the basic units out of which the nation is constituted

questions.question_text: In which part of Africa was the civilization of the Shona people located?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The Shona people's civilization was located in southern Africa. It is famous for the Great Zimbabwe, a large stone complex built from the eleventh century onward, which served as the centre of a powerful trading kingdom.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about the relationships among ancient civilizations?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The territory of Persia was limited to what is today Iran

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Ancient Chinese invaded their neighbors including India

options.label: C
options.option_text: The Kush kingdom conquered Egypt in the 8th century B.C.
options.explanation: The Kushite kingdom of Nubia conquered Egypt in the eighth century BC, establishing the twenty-fifth or Ethiopian dynasty. Kushite pharaohs such as Piye and Taharqa ruled Egypt until the Assyrians drove them back south in the seventh century BC.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The city-state of Carthage defeated the Romans in the Punic wars

questions.question_text: Among the achievements of the ancient civilizations which one of the following legacies has enhanced international peace in Modern World?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The Roman Senate with senators elected for life

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Greek sports event known as the Olympics
options.explanation: The Greek Olympics, revived in the modern era in 1896, have enhanced international peace by bringing athletes of all nations together in peaceful sporting competition. The Olympic Games promote friendship, mutual understanding and cooperation among peoples, serving as a symbol of global unity.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The Persian kingdom's 'pony express' postal system

options.label: D
options.option_text: The Egyptian religious belief of life after death

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the Aksumite kingdom?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It was converted to Christianity by Egypt's design

options.label: B
options.option_text: It built large stalae with income from agricultural tax

options.label: C
options.option_text: Its prosperity depended on the Red Sea trade
options.explanation: Aksum's prosperity depended heavily on the Red Sea trade. Through the port of Adulis, Aksum exchanged ivory, gold, spices and other goods with Egypt, Arabia, Persia, India and Rome, and this commerce was the economic foundation of the kingdom.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It was the first state in Ethiopian history

questions.question_text: Why did the Aksumite Kingdom decline and eventually collapse?

options.label: A
options.option_text: the rise of Islam hastened the expulsion of Aksum from South Yemen

options.label: B
options.option_text: the destruction of Adulis led to the loss of revenue from the Red Sea trade
options.explanation: Aksum declined and collapsed partly because the destruction of Adulis cut the kingdom off from the Red Sea trade. With the loss of the port, Aksum lost the revenue that sustained its economy, weakening the state until it finally disintegrated.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the internal rebellion of the Beja weakened Asumite military power

options.label: D
options.option_text: the shift of political center from north to south precipitated foreign invasion

questions.question_text: Which of the following properly explains the rise and early expansion of Islam?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It was successful because its religious leaders were also political leaders
options.explanation: Islam expanded quickly because its religious leaders were also political leaders. The Prophet Muhammad combined religious and political authority, uniting believers under one faith and one government, and his successors continued to lead both the religion and the expanding empire.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Islam spread over vast territories in a short period of time through peaceful conversion

options.label: C
options.option_text: Islam expanded quickly because it taught that all religions are equal

options.label: D
options.option_text: Attack by the Quraysh speeded up the expansion

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about developments during the Fascist occupation of Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Lt. Colonel Belay Haile-ab served as a military leader of The Black Lion Organization
options.explanation: Lt. Colonel Belay Haile-ab served as a military leader of the Black Lion Organization during the Italian occupation. He fought in the resistance and was involved in actions such as the attack on Italian forces at Nekemte in June 1936.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Dejazmnatch Balcha was captured and publicly hanged at Buta Jirra

options.label: C
options.option_text: The so-called Jewist-Abegnoch abandoned the resistance

options.label: D
options.option_text: The Black Lion Organization conducted conventional warfare

questions.question_text: What was the immediate cause of the Second World War (WWII)?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The invasion of Poland by Nazi Germany
options.explanation: The immediate cause of the Second World War was the invasion of Poland by Nazi Germany on 1 September 1939. This act of aggression led Britain and France to declare war on Germany, marking the start of the global conflict.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The unexpected annexation of Czechoslovakia and Lithuania by the German army

options.label: C
options.option_text: The Japanese attack of the US Naval base at Pearl Harbour

options.label: D
options.option_text: The signing of the Non-Aggression Pact between Germany and the Soviet Union

questions.question_text: According to the structure of the United Nations Organization, which one of the following bodies falls under the Security Council?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The Military Staff Committee falls under the Security Council. It advises the council on military matters and helps coordinate military action taken to maintain international peace and security, working with the armed forces contributed by member states.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about Super Power politics after WWII?

options.label: A
options.option_text: China was among the leading Super Powers

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Soviet Union effectively became Super Power in 1949
options.explanation: The Soviet Union effectively became a superpower in 1949, when it tested its first atomic bomb. This nuclear capability ended the American monopoly on atomic weapons and confirmed the USSR as a second superpower rivaling the United States in the Cold War.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The status was accorded only to the USA, the USSR, and the UK

options.label: D
options.option_text: Five Super Powers had emerged each with a veto power at the Security Council

questions.question_text: What were the two blocs or camps into which the world was divided after WWII?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The backward Third World and the advanced First World

options.label: B
options.option_text: The oppressor colonial masters and the oppressed colonized people

options.label: C
options.option_text: The capitalist West and the socialist East
options.explanation: After the Second World War, the world was divided into two rival camps: the capitalist West, led by the United States, and the socialist East, led by the Soviet Union. This division shaped international politics during the Cold War.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The largely poor South and the extremely rich North

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about the peasants of Ethiopia in the post-Liberation period?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Many became tenants as a result of extensive land alienation
options.explanation: In the post-liberation period, many Ethiopian peasants became tenants as a result of extensive land alienation. Land was increasingly concentrated in the hands of landlords and officials, forcing peasants to work as tenants who paid rent rather than owning the land they farmed.

options.label: B
options.option_text: They began to produce largely for the market

options.label: C
options.option_text: They continued to pay official dues to landowners and government officials

options.label: D
options.option_text: They benefitted from free medical service

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the Ethio-Eritrean federation and subsequent union?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The union enabled Eritreans to enjoy democratic rights

options.label: B
options.option_text: The federation required Eritrea to adopt the Ethiopian flag

options.label: C
options.option_text: The federation was demanded by the Unionist Party
options.explanation: The closest statement is that the Unionist Party supported union with Ethiopia and backed the idea of federation as a compromise. However, the wording is inaccurate: the party actually demanded unconditional union, while the federation itself was established by United Nations Resolution 390(V) of 1950, not by a referendum.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The federation was formed on the basis of a referendum

questions.question_text: Which of the following was true about military rule in Ethiopia following the 1974 popular Revolution?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It conducted a successful 'Red Star' campaign against Eritrean separatists

options.label: B
options.option_text: It established a multiparty parliamentary system of government on

options.label: C
options.option_text: It failed to prevent the secession of Eritrea from Ethiopia
options.explanation: The military regime that ruled Ethiopia after the 1974 revolution ultimately failed to prevent the secession of Eritrea. Although the Derg fought the Eritrean separatists for years, its forces were eventually defeated, and Eritrea gained its independence in 1993.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It replaced the feudal socio-economic system by a new capitalist system

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about Pan-Africanism?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It aspired initially to return African slaves to their homeland

options.label: B
options.option_text: It started in the form of opposition of black peoples against racism
options.explanation: Pan-Africanism began as a movement of black peoples in opposition to racism and oppression, especially among Africans in the diaspora in the Americas and Europe. From this struggle, it grew into a call for the unity and independence of all African peoples.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It came into being with the First Pan-African Conference at Accra

options.label: D
options.option_text: It appeared as an idea first among the peoples of colonial West Africa

questions.question_text: Among the French colonies of West Africa which of the following became independent in 1958 by voting 'No' to continued association with France?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Guinea was the only French colony that voted No in the 1958 referendum, rejecting continued association with France in the French Community. Under the leadership of Sekou Toure, Guinea chose immediate independence instead. In response, France withdrew its financial and technical support from the new republic.

questions.question_text: What was the root cause of the conflict between the Christian Kingdom and the Muslim Sultanates from 1270 to 1529?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The inability of Christian merchants to pass through Muslim territories to the coast

options.label: B
options.option_text: The attempt of the Christian Kingdom to control Muslim territories along the trade route
options.explanation: The root cause of the conflict was the attempt of the Christian kingdom to control the Muslim sultanates and their territories along the trade routes. Control of these wealthy territories and routes was vital economically, so the Christian state repeatedly tried to bring them under its authority.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The imposition of huge taxes on Muslim merchants by the Christian Kingdom

options.label: D
options.option_text: The monopolization of the import-export trade by the Christian Kingdom

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the conflict between the Christian Kingdom and the Sultanate of Adal in the early 16th century?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Both the Christian state and Adal were encouraged to fight by outsiders.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Sultan Mohammed started the conflict in the 1460s after refusal to pay the annual tribute.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Imam Ahmed ibn Ibrahim unified the warring Muslim groups by instilling the spirit of Jihad against Christians.
options.explanation: Imam Ahmed ibn Ibrahim, known as Ahmed Gragn, unified the warring Muslim groups by instilling the spirit of jihad against the Christians. Under his leadership, Adal launched a devastating invasion of the Christian kingdom from 1529 onward.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The Christian Kingdom initiated the conflict in the 15th century to crush the growing power of Adal.

questions.question_text: What is the most likely factor for the population movement of the Oromo starting from the 1520s?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The need for grazing land for increasing cattle populations.
options.explanation: The most likely factor for the Oromo population movement from the 1520s was the need for grazing land for their increasing cattle populations. As their herds grew, the Oromo moved into new areas to find pasture, spreading across the highlands and beyond.

options.label: B
options.option_text: To gain economic benefits by controlling trade routes.

options.label: C
options.option_text: To bring more territory under the Gadaa system of rule.

options.label: D
options.option_text: To spread their religion based on the worship of Waaqa.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about political developments in the Christian Kingdom after the death of Imam Ahmed in 1543?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Sarsa Dengel succeeded in dislodging the Ottoman Turks from the Red Sea coastal areas.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Gelawdewos died while fighting the Oromo, who utilized hit-and-run military tactics.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Encroachment by the Ottoman Turks on the Red Sea coast became a serious threat.
options.explanation: After the death of Imam Ahmed in 1543, encroachment by the Ottoman Turks on the Red Sea coast became a serious threat to the Christian kingdom. The Ottomans occupied Massawa and other ports, while the Oromo continued their expansion in the highlands.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The rapid movement of the Oromo population came to an end abruptly.

questions.question_text: What was the most likely reason for Susenyos' conversion to Catholicism?

options.label: A
options.option_text: To attract support from numerous high-level dignitaries who had been converted.

options.label: B
options.option_text: To gain Portuguese military assistance to create a strong monarchy.
options.explanation: Susenyos converted to Catholicism mainly to gain Portuguese military assistance to create a strong monarchy. He hoped that Portuguese support would help him defeat his rivals and strengthen his control, but his conversion provoked bitter religious conflict and eventual civil war.

options.label: C
options.option_text: To purify the heresies observed in Orthodox Christianity.

options.label: D
options.option_text: To fulfill the promise made by Libne Dingil to the Portuguese.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the achievements of the Gondarine Period?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The establishment of Gondar led to the integration of Shewa with the Christian Kingdom

options.label: B
options.option_text: Gondar city constructed new buildings quite different in style from the Aksumite architecture
options.explanation: During the Gondarine period, Gondar's rulers constructed new buildings quite different in style from Aksumite architecture. The castles, palaces and churches of Gondar introduced a distinctive Gondarine style, influenced by Portuguese and Indian building techniques, and became a center of art and literature.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The capital city was so busy with trade activity to give attention to paintings and calligraphy

options.label: D
options.option_text: The establishment of permanent capital made Gondar the main center of education and music

questions.question_text: What was the factor that made England to be the place of origin for the Industrial Revolution?

options.label: A
options.option_text: was endowed with vital coal mine and iron ore
options.explanation: England became the origin of the Industrial Revolution partly because it was endowed with vital coal mines and iron ore. These natural resources provided the fuel and raw materials needed for the steam engines, factories and machinery that powered industrial growth.

options.label: B
options.option_text: was ruled by an extremely tyrannical monarchy

options.label: C
options.option_text: had unstable government for almost a century

options.label: D
options.option_text: possessed small but highly talented people

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the Second Industrial Revolution in comparison to the First?

options.label: A
options.option_text: developed sailing ships for transportation on high seas

options.label: B
options.option_text: saw the transformation of power-operated machinery
options.explanation: The Second Industrial Revolution saw the transformation of power-operated machinery. Unlike the first phase, which relied on steam, the second phase introduced electricity, petroleum and the internal combustion engine, leading to new industries such as chemicals, steel, and automobiles.

options.label: C
options.option_text: utilized steam power that moved railway locomotives

options.label: D
options.option_text: used wind and water as a source of power for factories

questions.question_text: One of the following is a major feature of the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade. Which one?

options.label: A
options.option_text: abolished due to the humanitarian feeling of the Europeans

options.label: B
options.option_text: friendly to the slaves until they were finally sold in America

options.label: C
options.option_text: called piratic trade during its first phase in the 16th century
options.explanation: During its first phase in the sixteenth century, the trans-Atlantic slave trade was largely carried out by pirates and privateers, and so it was called a piratic trade. It was initiated by the Portuguese, not the British, and was never friendly to the slaves.

options.label: D
options.option_text: initiated by the British Empire in the early 19th century
