questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT correct about the consequences of the Trans-Atlantic slave trade?

options.label: A
options.option_text: brought to Africa large number of fire-arms intensifying conflicts

options.label: B
options.option_text: hastened capitalist economic development to the African continent
options.explanation: The statement that the slave trade hastened capitalist economic development in Africa is NOT correct. On the contrary, the trade devastated African societies by removing millions of young people and fuelling wars, while the profits enriched Europe and the Americas instead.

options.label: C
options.option_text: produced cheap industrial products ruining African craftsmanship

options.label: D
options.option_text: resulted in the loss of about 15 million young African people

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the Christian kingdom after 1270?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The mobile royal camps led to the deterioration of security.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The kingdom made extensive territorial gains to the south.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The new rulers deviated significantly from the political traditions of Aksum.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The gult system led to the emergence of powerful regional lords.
options.explanation: After 1270, the gult system, which granted rights over land and the labour of its inhabitants, led to the emergence of powerful regional lords. These lords accumulated wealth and followers, becoming strong enough to challenge the central authority of the Christian kingdom.

questions.question_text: How did the European overseas explorations and 'discoveries' influence the course of events subsequently?

options.label: A
options.option_text: They facilitated long-distance trade which marked the beginning of early capitalism in Europe.
options.explanation: The European overseas explorations facilitated long-distance trade, which marked the beginning of early capitalism in Europe. The wealth and commerce generated by contact with new regions stimulated commercial growth, the rise of merchants and the expansion of markets across Europe.

options.label: B
options.option_text: They enabled Spain and Portugal to be dominant up until the 19th century.

options.label: C
options.option_text: They facilitated long-distance trade which benefited both Europe and the 'discovered' peoples.

options.label: D
options.option_text: They led to conquest which contributed to the civilization of the conquered peoples.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the major cause for the conflict between the Christian kingdom and the Sultanate of Adal?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The growing economic decline of the Christian kingdom.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The refusal of the Muslims to be tributary to the Christians.
options.explanation: The major cause of the conflict between the Christian kingdom and the Sultanate of Adal was the refusal of the Muslims to continue paying tribute to the Christians. This refusal challenged the tributary relationship and led to repeated military confrontations between the two powers.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The destruction of Muslim states led by the Sultanate of Ifat.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The spread of Christianity in the Muslim lowland areas.

questions.question_text: Identify the correct statement about the consequence of the war between the Sultanate of Adal and the Christian kingdom.

options.label: A
options.option_text: The Sultanate was able to maintain authority for about a century.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The two contesting powers were weakened at the end of the war.
options.explanation: As a consequence of the war between the Sultanate of Adal and the Christian kingdom, both contesting powers were greatly weakened. The long and destructive conflict exhausted their armies and resources, paving the way for the Oromo expansion and the rise of the Ottomans in the region.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The destructive war prevented foreigners from coming to Ethiopia.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The Christians succeeded in acquiring new converts in the lowlands.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the attempt to introduce Catholicism into 17th-century Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The abdication of power by Susenyos hastened the suppression of Catholicism
options.explanation: The abdication of Susenyos in 1632 hastened the suppression of Catholicism. His son Fasiladas, who succeeded him, immediately expelled the Jesuit missionaries and restored Orthodox Christianity, bringing the attempt to impose Catholicism in seventeenth-century Ethiopia to an end.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The civil war brought about permanent changes in Church practices

options.label: C
options.option_text: The nobility used Catholicism to undermine the authority of the king

options.label: D
options.option_text: The missionaries exerted enormous efforts to convert the ordinary people

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about Gondar City in the 17th and 18th centuries?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The fact that it was a permanent capital enabled the monarchs to effectively control regional lords

options.label: B
options.option_text: Most of the palaces and churches were built during the reign of the first three Gondarine kings

options.label: C
options.option_text: As an urban space, various religious and cultural groups were intermingled in the city
options.explanation: As an urban space, Gondar brought together various religious and cultural groups, including Christians, Muslims, and Jews, also known as Beta Israel, as well as foreign residents such as Armenians and Portuguese. This mixing made the city a center of diverse cultural interaction.

options.label: D
options.option_text: There were no foreigners due to the prevailing 'closed door' policy

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the Zemene Mesafint?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The prevalence of war prompted peasants to work for surplus production

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Orthodox Church continued to be a source of spiritual and political unity

options.label: C
options.option_text: Regional lords made continuous wars to control trade and become kings

options.label: D
options.option_text: The Yejju dynasty ruled northern Ethiopia in the name of puppet kings of Gondar
options.explanation: During the Zemene Mesafint, the Yejju dynasty of Oromo origin ruled northern Ethiopia in the name of puppet kings of Gondar. Real power lay with the Yejju regents, while the nominal kings were largely controlled by them.

questions.question_text: Which of the following kingdoms, formed by the Soninke people attained greatness from the Trans-Saharan Trade?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The kingdom of Ghana, formed by the Soninke people, attained greatness through the trans-Saharan trade. Ghana controlled the gold and salt trade across the Sahara, and its rulers grew wealthy by taxing the goods passing through their territory.

questions.question_text: Which of the following properly expresses the ideas of Enlightenment thinkers?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In politics, they encouraged the rise of radical political revolutions.

options.label: B
options.option_text: In economics, they supported the advancement of a few wealthy individuals.

options.label: C
options.option_text: In education, they appreciated the teachings of church schools.

options.label: D
options.option_text: In law and the punishment of crime, they criticized the injustices of feudal autocracy.
options.explanation: Enlightenment thinkers criticized the injustices of feudal autocracy, particularly in law and the punishment of crime. Thinkers like Cesare Beccaria argued against cruel punishments and arbitrary justice, calling for more humane and rational legal systems based on reason.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the major effect of the American War of Independence?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It led to the creation of thirteen American states.
options.explanation: The American War of Independence led to the creation of thirteen American states, which formed the new United States. The war freed the colonies from British rule and established an independent republic governed under a federal constitution.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It contributed to the eruption of the French Revolution.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It recognized Native Americans as equal citizens.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It hastened the abolition of slavery.

questions.question_text: Why did the colonial powers surrounding Ethiopia sign the Tripartite Treaty of 1906?

options.label: A
options.option_text: They suspected the Germans would intervene if they did not take action.

options.label: B
options.option_text: They were told that the death of Ras Mekonnen would create political chaos.

options.label: C
options.option_text: They anticipated conflict over succession because Menelik did not have a male heir.
options.explanation: The colonial powers signed the Tripartite Treaty of 1906 because they anticipated conflict over succession, since Menelik II had no male heir. They wanted to safeguard their territorial interests in the Horn of Africa in case the emperor's death provoked a power struggle.

options.label: D
options.option_text: They feared that Menelik's illness might lead to the total disintegration of the nation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the appointment of Lij Iyasu as Menelik's heir?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It was supported by Taflu wholeheartedly.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It was directly challenged by the Shoan nobility.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It was opposed by the Council of Ministers.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It was meant to bring stability.
options.explanation: The appointment of Lij Iyasu as Menelik's heir was meant to bring stability to the succession. Menelik, weakened by illness, designated his grandson as his successor so that there would be an orderly transfer of power after his death.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following properly describes Lij Iyasu's approach to government?

options.label: A
options.option_text: He wanted to ensure the continuity of the system under Menelik

options.label: B
options.option_text: He left the matter of education entirely to the Church

options.label: C
options.option_text: He sought to accord equal status to Ethiopian Muslims
options.explanation: Lij Iyasu sought to accord equal status to Ethiopian Muslims, treating them as equal citizens alongside Christians. This policy angered the Orthodox Church and the Shoan nobility, who used his religious stance as a reason to depose him in 1916.

options.label: D
options.option_text: He wanted to reduce taxes and tax rates for everybody

questions.question_text: Which of the following signaled the emergence of autocracy following the coronation of Haile Selassie I?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Collection of enormous revenue through provincial customs posts

options.label: B
options.option_text: Maintenance of the autonomous status of Begemdir and Jimma provinces

options.label: C
options.option_text: Recognition of both political and economic privileges of regional rulers

options.label: D
options.option_text: Proclaiming a constitution that accorded divine sanction to emperor's rule
options.explanation: Following his coronation, Haile Selassie's proclamation of a constitution that declared the emperor's person sacred and his power indisputable signaled the emergence of autocracy. The 1931 Constitution formally concentrated supreme power in the emperor's hands.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was NOT the fundamental cause of the First World War (WWI)?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Economic depression was NOT a fundamental cause of the First World War. The causes were the system of military alliances, the arms race, and the rivalry for colonies and markets, while the major economic depression came only after 1929.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the League of Nations?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It refused to grant admission to Germany as full member

options.label: B
options.option_text: The USA continued to be an active member during Wilson's presidency

options.label: C
options.option_text: One of its objectives was to settle international disputes peacefully
options.explanation: One of the League of Nations' main objectives was to settle international disputes peacefully. Member states agreed to submit their disputes to the League and to work together to maintain peace, although the League ultimately failed to prevent aggression in the 1930s.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The idea of creating it was raised well before WWI

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about the domestic policy of the Soviet Union from 1917 to 1937?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The New Economic Policy was intended to build socialist economy

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Soviets allowed the people exercise democratic political rights

options.label: C
options.option_text: The Bolshevik party established alliance with the white Russians

options.label: D
options.option_text: The government speedily undertook large-scale industrialization
options.explanation: From 1917 to 1937, the Soviet government speedily undertook large-scale industrialization. Through the Five-Year Plans, the state built heavy industry, factories and infrastructure, transforming the country from an agrarian into an industrial power, though at great human cost.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is correct about resistance to colonial rule in Africa from 1900 to 1939?

options.label: A
options.option_text: During the inter-war period African resistance took the form of demand for political and economic rights
options.explanation: During the inter-war period, African resistance to colonial rule mainly took the form of demands for political and economic rights. Africans organized strikes, protests, independent churches and political movements to press for better conditions rather than waging large-scale armed revolts.

options.label: B
options.option_text: During the inter-war period Africans fought among themselves more than they fought the colonial system

options.label: C
options.option_text: Real resistance actually began after the Second World War

options.label: D
options.option_text: It was guided by the spirit of Ethiopianism which referred to a struggle for total liberation

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the Ethio-Italian War of 1935-1936?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The Ethiopians had lost both the first and the second battles of Tembien
options.explanation: The Ethiopians lost both the first and second battles of Tembien in early 1936. These Italian victories forced the Ethiopian army to fall back, and the war ended with the Italian occupation of Addis Ababa in May 1936.

options.label: B
options.option_text: From the outset, Britain and France stood firmly on the side of Ethiopia

options.label: C
options.option_text: Initially the Ethiopians retreated to elongate the communication line

options.label: D
options.option_text: Italian aggression was first launched by Graziani from the east

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the Italian Occupation of Ethiopia from 1936 to 1941?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The Italian viceroy in Addis Ababa enjoyed considerable autonomy from Rome

options.label: B
options.option_text: Fascist rule was mostly restricted to towns and cities

options.label: C
options.option_text: Asmara was chosen as the headquarters of Italian East Africa
options.explanation: Asmara was chosen as the headquarters of Italian East Africa, the colony that united Ethiopia, Eritrea and Italian Somaliland under Italian rule from 1936 to 1941. The Italian viceroys administered this vast territory from Asmara, which served as the colonial capital.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Ethiopia was administered as a separate colonial entity

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the importance of history?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It allows us to accurately anticipate future events

options.label: B
options.option_text: It encourages us to repeat the wrong doings of society in the past

options.label: C
options.option_text: It enables us to understand events and processes of the past
options.explanation: The importance of history is that it enables us to understand events and processes of the past. By studying what happened and why, we gain insight into how societies developed and how present conditions came about, which helps us make better decisions.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It helps us to study of the past, the present, and the future

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the role of sources in the study of history?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Objectivity means presenting stories that come from official sources

options.label: B
options.option_text: Oral testimony by participants is as good as information obtained from others

options.label: C
options.option_text: Secondary sources are fictional materials with some historical facts

options.label: D
options.option_text: Primary sources have direct relation to the events in time and place
options.explanation: Primary sources have a direct relation to the events they describe in time and place. They are produced at or near the time of the events by participants or witnesses, making them the most immediate evidence for reconstructing the past.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the study of Ethiopian history?

options.label: A
options.option_text: European travelers have left behind plenty information about the south

options.label: B
options.option_text: Oral sources are key for the study of the south
options.explanation: Oral sources are key for the study of the south of Ethiopia, because written documents about the southern regions are scarce. The traditions, songs and testimonies passed down orally preserve the history of these peoples.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Historical studies dealing with northern Ethiopia are comprehensive

options.label: D
options.option_text: Information is totally unavailable for the ancient period as a whole

questions.question_text: Which of the following Australopithecine species is discovered in Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Australopithecus afarensis was discovered in Ethiopia, notably at Hadar in the Afar region, where the famous skeleton known as Lucy was found in 1974. This species lived about 3.9 to 2.9 million years ago and walked upright.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT true about the earliest states in human history?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In some states rulers claimed divine rights that made them God's agents on earth

options.label: B
options.option_text: Cities with literate persons was a prerequisite for state formation

options.label: C
options.option_text: Agricultural surplus production preceded state formation

options.label: D
options.option_text: Residents of a city were regarded as equal citizens
options.explanation: It is NOT true that residents of a city were regarded as equal citizens in the earliest states. On the contrary, these societies were stratified, with kings, priests, nobles and scribes above the common people, and great inequality between different social groups.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the Romans and the Germans in the Middle Ages?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The Romans maintained dominance in the European trade after Germanic invasions

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Germanic invasion of Rome led to the disappearance of some towns
options.explanation: The Germanic invasions of the Roman Empire led to the disappearance of some towns in Europe. As trade declined and cities were destroyed or abandoned, towns shrank or vanished, and the economy became more rural and localized during the early Middle Ages.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The Germans unified the divided Romans into a powerful empire

options.label: D
options.option_text: The Romans regarded the Germans as highly civilized people

questions.question_text: Which of the following characterizations is true about the Byzantine Empire?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It favoured the Catholic Church over the Orthodox Church

options.label: B
options.option_text: It Church officials dominated all decision making

options.label: C
options.option_text: The Continent of Africa was beyond its reach

options.label: D
options.option_text: The other name for it was the Eastern Roman Empire
options.explanation: The Byzantine Empire was another name for the Eastern Roman Empire. After the division of the Roman Empire, the eastern half, with its capital at Constantinople, continued for nearly a thousand years and is known as the Byzantine Empire.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was a major feature of India in the Medieval Period?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Religion exercised a strong influence on the Indian culture
options.explanation: Religion exercised a strong influence on Indian culture in the medieval period. Hinduism, and later Islam under the Delhi Sultanate and the Mughal emperors, shaped Indian art, architecture, law, education and daily life across the whole subcontinent.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The regional lords hired bands of warriors known as Samurai

options.label: C
options.option_text: The invention of fire arms was accompanied by the discovery high quality gun powder

options.label: D
options.option_text: Officials for political power were selected on the basis of talent

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was a feature of early capitalist economic activities in Europe?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Governments were unwilling to support long distance trade

options.label: B
options.option_text: The increased use of money strengthened the feudal system economically

options.label: C
options.option_text: Factories were located in rural areas in order to get raw materials easily

options.label: D
options.option_text: The bourgeoisie employed peasants from the countryside as labourers
options.explanation: In early capitalist economic activities in Europe, the bourgeoisie employed peasants from the countryside as labourers. Merchants supplied rural workers with raw materials and paid them for finished goods, a system known as the putting-out or domestic system.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about pre-Aksumite states?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Most of the inscriptions about Damat are found in South Arabia

options.label: B
options.option_text: Among the most valued imports of Egyptians from Punt was myrrh
options.explanation: Among the most valued imports the Egyptians obtained from Punt were myrrh and frankincense, used in religious ceremonies and medicine. Egyptian records and reliefs, such as those of Queen Hatshepsut, describe expeditions to Punt for these precious goods.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Damat had a very strong contact with the kingdom of Egypt

options.label: D
options.option_text: The precise location of the land of Punt is what is today Eritrea

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the Harar Emirate?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It was ruled by the Egyptian governor for about a decade

options.label: B
options.option_text: It allowed the Egyptians conduct trade activities inside the wall

options.label: C
options.option_text: It built the stone wall in defense of the Christian incursion

options.label: D
options.option_text: It emerged out of the family of the former Adal Sultanate
options.explanation: The Harar Emirate emerged out of the family of the former Adal Sultanate. After the decline of Adal, the emirs of Harar claimed descent from its ruling family and continued the region's Islamic traditions until the Egyptian occupation in 1875.

questions.question_text: The correct statement about the Eastern Question is that:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Britain and France hastened the collapse of Ottoman Turkey

options.label: B
options.option_text: Russia and Austria collaborated against the Ottoman Turkey

options.label: C
options.option_text: France, Germany and Italy were deeply involved in the question

options.label: D
options.option_text: Ottoman Turkey's decline gave rise to the use of the term
options.explanation: The Eastern Question referred to the problems created by the decline and weakening of the Ottoman Empire. European powers struggled over the territories and influence left as the Ottoman state lost control of its possessions in the Balkans and the eastern Mediterranean.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about the impact of industrial capitalism on the Europeans concerning the continent of Africa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It heightened the need for raw materials and market places
options.explanation: Industrial capitalism heightened Europe's need for raw materials and market places in Africa. As European industries grew, they demanded more raw materials such as cotton, minerals and rubber, and sought new markets for their manufactured goods, which drove the scramble for Africa.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It strengthened African resistance to the European encroachment

options.label: C
options.option_text: It created unprecedented political harmony among the Europeans

options.label: D
options.option_text: It encouraged the growth of the Trans-Saharan Slave Trade

questions.question_text: Among the many reasons for the coming of the European explorers to Africa, which of the following is correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Alerting native Africans of the imminent danger coming ahead

options.label: B
options.option_text: Assessment of the available material resources and the population
options.explanation: Among the reasons for the coming of European explorers to Africa was the assessment of the available material resources and the population. Explorers gathered information about geography, resources, rivers and peoples, information that later helped European powers conquer the continent.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Provision of service for European armed forces conquering Africa

options.label: D
options.option_text: Facilitation of conditions for the conquering armies of Europe

questions.question_text: One of the following is true about the rise to power of Emperor Tewodros II. Which one?

options.label: A
options.option_text: He gained victory over the Egyptians at the battle of Debarki

options.label: B
options.option_text: He suffered several defeats before he was crowned emperor

options.label: C
options.option_text: He became a bandit after he was denied governorship of Quara
options.explanation: Kassa Hailu, the future Tewodros II, became a bandit after he was denied the governorship of Quara. He then gathered a following and defeated his opponents in battle, rising to become emperor of Ethiopia in 1855.

options.label: D
options.option_text: He has strong claim of descent for power from the royal house

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the reforms of Tewodros?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Gafat became a central place for the manufacturing of cannons
options.explanation: Among the reforms of Tewodros II, Gafat became a central place for the manufacturing of cannons. The emperor gathered skilled artisans at Gafat to cast cannons and manufacture firearms as part of his effort to build a strong, modern army.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Orthodox Church opposed Tewodros for abandoning the faith

options.label: C
options.option_text: Reunification was denounced by the majority of peasant population

options.label: D
options.option_text: Recognition of local dynasties suddenly disrupted the old practices

questions.question_text: The correct statement about the approach of Johannes IV in his internal administration is that

options.label: A
options.option_text: he showed liberal attitude to tolerate the followers of Islamic faith

options.label: B
options.option_text: he allowed Menelik to make independent dealings with foreigners

options.label: C
options.option_text: he fought like Tewodros repeated wars against rebellious regions

options.label: D
options.option_text: he shared power with regional lords as long as they remained loyal
options.explanation: Yohannes IV's approach in his internal administration was to share power with regional lords as long as they remained loyal. He granted Menelik of Shoa and other vassals considerable autonomy in return for their loyalty and payment of tribute.

questions.question_text: The correct statement about the expansion of Menelik II to the south, south-west and south-east is that

options.label: A
options.option_text: it occurred long before the beginning of European colonial conquest

options.label: B
options.option_text: it followed the same approaches followed by his two predecessors

options.label: C
options.option_text: it aimed at building his military power from the valuable trade
options.explanation: Menelik II's expansion to the south, southwest and southeast aimed at building his military power from the valuable trade. By controlling the trade in ivory, gold and other goods, Menelik acquired wealth to buy modern firearms for his army.

options.label: D
options.option_text: it sought to liberate the people from oppressive local domination

questions.question_text: One of the following shows correctly Menelik's foreign relations during the territorial expansion. Which one?

options.label: A
options.option_text: European powers refused to accept the legitimacy of Menelik's territorial gains after Adwa

options.label: B
options.option_text: The expansion before Adwa was partly a preparation for the struggle against colonialism
options.explanation: Menelik's expansion before the Battle of Adwa was partly a preparation for the struggle against colonialism. By strengthening his hold on the south and building a large, well-armed army, Menelik prepared Ethiopia to confront Italian aggression.

options.label: C
options.option_text: After the victory at Adwa Menelik had nothing to fear from outsiders

options.label: D
options.option_text: The colonial powers encouraged the expansion in all directions

questions.question_text: Which of the following was the consequence of Ethiopian victory at Adwa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It guaranteed economic independence of the country

options.label: B
options.option_text: It created a permanent state of enmity between Ethiopia and Italy

options.label: C
options.option_text: It discouraged European travel to Ethiopia from coming to Ethiopia

options.label: D
options.option_text: It guaranteed political independence of Ethiopia
options.explanation: The Ethiopian victory at Adwa guaranteed the political independence of Ethiopia. Italy recognized Ethiopia's full independence through the Treaty of Addis Ababa, and Ethiopia remained the only African country to preserve its independence during the Scramble for Africa.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was a feature of the foreign relations of the Aksumite State?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The vast majority of the Aksumite society was engaged in commerce

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Aksumite State controlled South Arabia from the 3rd to the 6th centuries
options.explanation: A feature of Aksum's foreign relations was that it controlled parts of South Arabia from the third to the sixth centuries. Aksumite kings campaigned across the Red Sea and ruled territories in Arabia, while Aksum also traded widely with Rome, India and the Arab world.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The Aksumite civilization was derived from directly from immigrants from South Arabia

options.label: D
options.option_text: The major source of rivalry between Aksum and Merve was ivory trade

questions.question_text: What was the major external factor for the fall of Aksum?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Impoverishment and economic collapse due to the incessant drought and famine

options.label: B
options.option_text: The near complete removal of Aksum from the Red Sea trade by the Muslim-Arab Empire
options.explanation: The major external factor for the fall of Aksum was its removal from the Red Sea trade by the Muslim-Arab Empire. As the Arabs expanded and controlled the sea routes, Aksum was cut off from commerce, lost revenue, and gradually declined.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The conversion of the monarch to Christianity which led to fierce resistance of the people to the rulers

options.label: D
options.option_text: The disastrous defeat suffered by the first military expedition of King Kaleb against the Himaryates

questions.question_text: To what major factor is the rise of the Zagwe Dynasty attributed?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The successful resistance of the Agaw to imposition of Christianity by Aksum

options.label: B
options.option_text: The economic and military might the Agaw had built due to long distance trade through Zeila

options.label: C
options.option_text: The involvement of the Agaw in Aksumite bureaucracy and military leadership
options.explanation: The rise of the Zagwe dynasty is attributed to the involvement of the Agaw in the Aksumite bureaucracy and military leadership. Having long served in these institutions, the Agaw gained the strength and position to establish their own dynasty as Aksum declined.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The collaboration of the Agaw people with the Beja invaders against the Aksumite state

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a major achievement of the Zagwe dynasty?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The major achievement of the Zagwe dynasty was the construction of rock-hewn churches, most famously at Lalibela. These churches, carved out of solid rock, are a unique and remarkable example of medieval Ethiopian architecture and are still used today.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The emphasis on building strong military power

options.label: C
options.option_text: The participation in the Crusades against Muslims

options.label: D
options.option_text: The translation of the Bible from Greek to Geez

questions.question_text: What was the most direct cause for the decline and downfall of the Agaw dynasty?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The loss of revenue from external trades that weakened the state

options.label: B
options.option_text: The problem of succession which always led to violence

options.label: C
options.option_text: Formidable incursions from the Sudanese jihadists

options.label: D
options.option_text: The challenge to their legitimacy from Amhara and Tigrai lords
options.explanation: The most direct cause for the decline of the Agaw, or Zagwe, dynasty was the challenge to their legitimacy from the Amhara and Tigrai lords. Because the Zagwe were not of the Solomonic line, their rule was seen as illegitimate, and Yekuno Amlak overthrew them in 1270.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pieces of art was the work of Leonardo da Vinci?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The Last Supper is a famous mural painting by Leonardo da Vinci, created in the late fifteenth century in Milan. It depicts the final meal of Jesus with his disciples and is one of the most celebrated works of Renaissance art.

questions.question_text: What was the feature shared in common by the Muslim Sultanates of the Ethiopian region in the medieval period?

options.label: A
options.option_text: they were allocated in the north-western lowlands of Ethiopia

options.label: B
options.option_text: their populations predominantly depended on agriculture

options.label: C
options.option_text: rulers exercised both political and religious authority
options.explanation: The Muslim sultanates of the Ethiopian region shared the feature that their rulers exercised both political and religious authority. The sultans combined secular and spiritual leadership, governing their people while also serving as heads of the Islamic faith in their territories.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Muslim and Christian populations were of fairly equal size

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the respective role of the routes through which Islam was introduced into Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Dahlk was both a staging point and the oldest Muslim state in the Ethiopian region

options.label: B
options.option_text: The port of Zeila was used by Islamic warriors committed to Jihad

options.label: C
options.option_text: the Dahlak Islands were the major point of entry to central Ethiopia

options.label: D
options.option_text: The port of Zeila was the most important for entry into the interior
options.explanation: The port of Zeila was the most important point of entry for Islam into the interior of Ethiopia. Through Zeila, traders and missionaries carried Islam into the eastern and southeastern highlands, giving rise to the Muslim sultanates of the region.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the Omotic States of southern Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The kingdom of Damot reached its peak during the reign of King Motalami
options.explanation: The kingdom of Damot reached its peak during the reign of King Motalami, who is recorded in the traditions of the region. Damot was one of the oldest and most powerful states in southern Ethiopia, wealthy from gold production and trade with Aksum.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The kingdom of Welayta was first mentioned during the reign of Amde Seyon

options.label: C
options.option_text: The kingdom of Enerya had successfully resisted the expansion of the Oromo

options.label: D
options.option_text: The kingdom of Kafa was incorporated by a section of Mecha Oromo

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the relationship between the Christian Kingdom and the Omotic States of the south?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Welayta had absolutely no relationship with the Christian Kingdom up until the time of Menelik

options.label: B
options.option_text: The name Limmu-Enarya signifies the annexation of Enarya into the Christian Kingdom

options.label: C
options.option_text: Damot put up a successful resistance against the Christian Kingdom up until the time of Menelik

options.label: D
options.option_text: The kingdom of Bizamo was incorporated into the Christian Kingdom in the 16th century
options.explanation: The kingdom of Bizamo, located on the south bank of the Abay River, was incorporated into the Christian kingdom in the sixteenth century. It was conquered during the reign of Emperor Sarsa Dengel, who brought it under the control of the Christian state.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was a factor for the Oromo population movement of the 16thcentury?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The desire to expand Oromo religion

options.label: B
options.option_text: The desire to find new pastures for cattle
options.explanation: The Oromo were pastoralists whose livelihoods depended on cattle, and by the sixteenth century population growth pushed them to seek new grazing lands for their herds. Options A, C, and D describe religious, fiscal, and political motives that do not reflect the chiefly economic, cattle-centered character of the movement.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The need to expand the tax base of the Oromo

options.label: D
options.option_text: The demand to establish political control over new areas

questions.question_text: What challenge did Emperor Serse Dingil face beyond the Mereb River in the 1570s?

options.label: A
options.explanation: In the 1570s Sarsa Dengel campaigned in the north against the Ottoman Turks, who had advanced beyond the Mereb River and seized areas such as Debarwa in the northern highlands. The na'ibs of Arkiko were themselves agents of Turkish authority, while the other options describe internal problems not connected to the frontier threat.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Disobedience from the na'ibs of Arkiko

options.label: C
options.option_text: Mutiny among royal regiments in the province

questions.question_text: What achievements earned Iyasu I the nickname "Iyasu the Great"?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The successful campaign against the Funj Sultanate in the west

options.label: B
options.option_text: Revision of works related to the legal code and taxation
options.explanation: Iyasu I earned the title the Great mainly for his administrative and religious reforms, including the revision of the legal code and taxation and the reorganization of the church. He did not defeat the Funj, introduce new architecture, or restore Gondarine rule over the southwest, which is why those alternatives are incorrect.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Introduction of new forms of architecture in the city of Gondar

options.label: D
options.option_text: Restoration of Gondernine rule over south-western Ethiopia

questions.question_text: What helped the Ching dynasty in China to gain the support of the indigenous Han ruling class?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The continuation of Chinese administrative practices by the Ching
options.explanation: The Qing, as a Manchu dynasty, kept Chinese administrative practices, the examination system, and Confucian bureaucracy largely intact, which won acceptance from the Han scholar-official class. Rejecting unequal treaties, cutting peasant taxes, or opening China to foreign influence would have alienated rather than gained that support.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The successful rejection of the "Unequal Treaties" by the Ching

options.label: C
options.option_text: The reduction of the tax on the Chinese peasantry

options.label: D
options.option_text: The opening of China for foreign trade and civilization by the Ching

questions.question_text: What was the fundamental source of conflict between Charles I and the English Short Parliament?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Disagreement on the authority of the king to sign treaties without consulting Parliament

options.label: B
options.option_text: Dispute as to whether or not Presbyterians can be head of the English Church

options.label: C
options.option_text: Disagreement on the nature of union between England and Scotland

options.label: D
options.option_text: Dispute over raising taxes to suppress the rebellion in Scotland
options.explanation: Charles I summoned the Short Parliament in 1640 to raise funds to suppress the Scottish rebellion, but Parliament refused to grant money until its grievances were addressed, so the king dissolved it. Treaty signing, church leadership, and the Anglo-Scottish union were not the central cause of this particular confrontation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a dominant idea among Enlightenment thinkers?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Man can attain salvation only through good work

options.label: B
options.option_text: Humans can achieve progress through the application of reason
options.explanation: Enlightenment thinkers held that human beings could improve society and understand the world through the systematic application of reason. Progress through reason is the central idea of the movement. Salvation through works, democracy, and religion's social value are religious or political claims rather than the dominant Enlightenment assumption.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Democracy is the best form of government

options.label: D
options.option_text: Religion is important for social cohesion

questions.question_text: What was behind the outbreak of the Latin American revolutions in the early 19thcentury?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Implementation of the Monroe Doctrine by the US

options.label: B
options.option_text: Re-division of Latin America between the Spanish and Portuguese

options.label: C
options.option_text: Decline of French rule in the Atlantic colonies

options.label: D
options.option_text: Ideas generated by the Enlightenment thinkers
options.explanation: The Latin American revolutions of the early nineteenth century were inspired by Enlightenment ideas of liberty, equality, and self-government, which colonial elites adopted as justification for breaking with Spain. The Monroe Doctrine came later, and neither Franco-Spanish redivision nor the decline of French rule in the Atlantic explains the uprisings.

questions.question_text: What was the common feature of the 1848 revolutions in Europe?

options.label: A
options.option_text: They were inspired by the idea of establishing a liberal government
options.explanation: The revolutions of 1848, often called the Revolutions of the Liberals, shared the common inspiration of establishing liberal, constitutional government with civil liberties and representative institutions. They were not all led by youth coalitions, did not look mainly to America, and though many failed, failure through leadership division was an outcome rather than the defining feature.

options.label: B
options.option_text: They were primarily led by a coalition of youth groups and bourgeoisie

options.label: C
options.option_text: They drew inspiration from the successful revolutions in America

options.label: D
options.option_text: They ultimately failed because of divisions among the leadership on future goals

questions.question_text: Who was responsible for the end of the Funj Sultanate?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The Funj Sultanate of Sennar was brought to an end in 1821 when armies sent by Mohammed Ali of Egypt conquered the region and annexed it. The Abdallabi were subordinate chiefs within the sultanate, Amara Dunqas was its founder, and Iyasu II of Ethiopia never destroyed it, so these options are incorrect.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following explains Egypt's prosperity under the Mamluks?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The successful participation of Egypt in the Crusades

options.label: B
options.option_text: The decline of Ottoman control over the Mediterranean

options.label: C
options.option_text: Egypt's participation in the trans-Saharan trade
options.explanation: Egypt prospered under the Mamluks largely because of its profitable participation in the trans-Saharan trade, which brought gold, slaves, and goods through its territory. The Mamluks fought the Crusaders rather than profiting from them, Ottoman control grew later, and no Red Sea canal was built during their rule.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The construction of a canal across the Red Sea

questions.question_text: Which of the following people was responsible for invading India in the 14thcentury?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The Mongols invaded India repeatedly during the fourteenth century, culminating in the great expedition of Timur (Tamerlane) in 1398 which devastated northern India. The Han were Chinese, Arab conquests of India occurred centuries earlier, and the Huns invaded in the fifth century, so none of the others fit the period.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a Central Cushitic language?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bilen is a Central Cushitic (Agaw) language spoken in Eritrea and is correctly classified as Central Cushitic. Gedeo and Burji are Highland East Cushitic languages, while Beja belongs to the Northern Cushitic branch, which is why they are not Central Cushitic.

questions.question_text: Where was the ancient state of Punt located?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The Eastern coast of the Red Sea

options.label: B
options.explanation: Punt was an ancient trading partner of Egypt situated in Northeast Africa, along the Red Sea coast of the Horn region. It was not on the Eastern coast of the Red Sea, which would place it in Arabia, nor on the Swahili Coast or along the Ethio-Sudan borderlands, which are far from the attested location.

questions.question_text: What factors facilitated the rise of the Zagwe Dynasty?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The popularity that the Agaw gained because of the rock hewn churches

options.label: B
options.option_text: The increased interaction of the Agaw elite with the Aksumite court
options.explanation: The rise of the Zagwe dynasty was facilitated by the long interaction of the Agaw ruling elite with the Aksumite court, through which they absorbed Aksumite culture and political tradition. The rock-hewn churches came after the dynasty's founding, and trade-route shifts better explain Aksum's decline than the Zagwe ascent.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The spread of Christianity among the Agaw populations

options.label: D
options.option_text: The shift of the major trade routes from Massawa to Zeila

questions.question_text: Which of the following was characteristic of Renaissance Humanism?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Desire to recreate the Roman Empire

options.label: C
options.option_text: Focus on how to achieve salvation

options.label: D
options.explanation: Renaissance humanism was characterized by renewed interest in everyday human conditions, the individual, and classical learning, in contrast to the exclusively otherworldly focus of the Middle Ages. It did not aim to recreate the Roman Empire, study Islamic literature, or concentrate on achieving salvation, which remained a religious rather than humanist concern.

questions.question_text: How did the Solomonic rulers of the medieval period in Ethiopia try to solve the problem of royal succession?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By inventing a system of a caretaker administration that ruled for a few years until final selection of a king is made

options.label: B
options.option_text: By designing a system in which the decisions of the Church leaders on succession became final

options.label: C
options.option_text: By developing a prison system for male royal prison system in which male descendants of a monarch were kept
options.explanation: The Solomonic rulers developed the practice of confining male members of the royal family on Mount Wehni, keeping potential rivals under control and thereby reducing succession struggles. No caretaker administration or church-controlled succession existed, and the dynasty never established a clear, effective rule of succession, so the prison system is the right answer.

options.label: D
options.option_text: By establishing a clear rule of succession

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was a characteristic feature of the Muslim sultanates of Medieval Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Their economy was mainly dependent on trade
options.explanation: The Muslim sultanates of medieval Ethiopia were largely commercial states whose economies depended heavily on long-distance trade through ports like Zeila. Their rulers exercised considerable power, most subjects were Muslims, and although immigrant Arab elites were influential, trade dependence is the most accurate and distinctive characteristic among the choices.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Their rulers exercised limited power and authority

options.label: C
options.option_text: Their populations were made up of Muslims and Christians

options.label: D
options.option_text: Their ruling class were immigrants from Arabia

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about the Kingdom of Kafa?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It was ruled by a king who had limited power

options.label: B
options.option_text: It was created by invaders from neighbouring Enarya

options.label: C
options.option_text: It had a dynasty that came from the Manjo clan

options.label: D
options.option_text: It had developed an efficient system of defending its territory
options.explanation: The Kingdom of Kafa developed an efficient system of defending its territory, using natural barriers and a well-organized army to protect its borders. Its kings actually wielded strong power, it was not created by invaders from Enarya, and its dynasty did not come from the Manjo clan, which is a distinct social group.

questions.question_text: What was the main cause for the expansion of the Christian kingdom during the medieval period?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Determination to restore the lost territories of the Aksumites

options.label: B
options.option_text: Ambition to acquire slaves for export to Arabia

options.label: C
options.option_text: Desire to expand its resource base
options.explanation: The medieval Christian kingdom expanded mainly from the desire to enlarge its resource base, gaining tribute, trade goods, and agricultural land from conquered southern and eastern regions. Restoring Aksumite territory, acquiring slaves for Arabia, and spreading Christianity were secondary or religious motives rather than the principal economic cause.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following factors intensified the conflict between the Christian kingdom and the Sultanate of Adal in the 15thand early 16thcenturies?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The shift of the Christian political center to Shewa

options.label: B
options.option_text: The introduction of new weapons like muskets
options.explanation: The introduction of new weapons such as muskets intensified the fifteenth and early sixteenth century conflict between the Christian kingdom and Adal by making warfare far more destructive. Turkish presence on the coast, the Shewan center, and pastoralist pressure existed but were not the direct technological factor that escalated the fighting.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The establishment of the Turks along the Red Sea coast

options.label: D
options.option_text: The pressure created by the migration of lowland pastoralists

questions.question_text: What was the factor that led to the decline of the gada institution among the Oromo of the Gibe region?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Political influence of Sudanese states of the Ethio-Sudan border

options.label: B
options.option_text: The shift of the economy from pastoralism to agriculture
options.explanation: Among the Oromo of the Gibe region, the shift from pastoralism to settled agriculture weakened the gada institution and promoted kingship, because fixed cultivation and growing wealth favored permanent rulers over rotating age-grade leaders. Warfare, Menelik's conquest, and Sudanese influence came later or were less decisive in ending gada.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Warfare and the rise of powerful war leaders

options.label: D
options.option_text: The conquest of the region by the forces of Menelik

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a correct description of long-distance trade routes of 19thcentury Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The route Jiren-Rogge-Harar-Massawa is not a correct description of nineteenth-century Ethiopian trade routes because it improbably links the southwestern trading center of Jiren with Harar in the far southeast and then Massawa in the north. The other listed routes follow realistic geographic chains used by merchants of the period.

questions.question_text: What was Giuseppe Garibaldi's role in the unification of Italy?

options.label: A
options.option_text: He brought together the Pope and Cavour to work for unification

options.label: B
options.option_text: He inspired and led a popular uprising for Italian unification
options.explanation: Garibaldi inspired and personally led popular uprisings for Italian unification, most famously the Expedition of the Thousand, whose Redshirts conquered Sicily and Naples and enabled the union of the south with Piedmont. He did not reconcile Pope and Cavour, secure Napoleon III's diplomacy, or advance unification mainly through writings, which were the work of Mazzini.

options.label: C
options.option_text: He secured Napoleon III's diplomatic support for Italian unification

options.label: D
options.option_text: He deepened Italian national consciousness through his writings

questions.question_text: How did the Congress of Vienna of 1815 lay the ground for the German unification?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It made Prussia the leading German state of the confederation

options.label: B
options.option_text: It brought the different German states under one customs union

options.label: C
options.option_text: It made German an official language for the confederation

options.label: D
options.option_text: It created a German confederation led by Austria
options.explanation: The Congress of Vienna created a German Confederation of thirty-nine states presided over by Austria, providing a framework that later facilitated unification. Prussia's leadership, the customs union, and an official German language emerged later through other developments, so they cannot be credited to the Congress itself.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was a consequence of the American Civil War?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The American Civil War accelerated the industrialization of the American economy, especially in the North, which expanded wartime manufacturing, railroads, and government-supported industry. Slavery was abolished rather than tolerated, the South was not colonized in any literal sense, and racism certainly did not end across the country, so the other choices fail.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Colonization of the south by the north

options.label: C
options.option_text: Toleration of slavery in some parts of the south

options.label: D
options.option_text: End of racism across the whole of the United States

questions.question_text: Which of the following processes contributed to the emergence of the "Eastern Question"?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The discovery of oil in territories ruled by the Ottoman Empire

options.label: B
options.option_text: The rivalry between the Ottomans and Russians for control of the Mediterranean

options.label: C
options.option_text: The spread of nationalism among the Slavic peoples of the Ottoman Empire
options.explanation: The Eastern Question emerged from the decline of the Ottoman Empire, and the rise of nationalism among its Slavic peoples in the Balkans intensified the rivalry of the great powers over its fate. Ottoman-Russian rivalry over the Mediterranean and Austrian expansion were consequences of the problem rather than its origin, and oil discovery came much later.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The expansion of the Austrian Empire to lands that were previously under the control of the Ottomans

questions.question_text: How did Tewodros II come to power?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By defeating his opponents through military means
options.explanation: Tewodros II came to power by defeating his rivals through military means, subduing the regional lords of the Zemene Mesafint era and crowning himself emperor in 1855. Church support and the Fikare Iyesus prophecy aided his legitimacy later, and British assistance played no part in his rise.

options.label: B
options.option_text: By gaining the support of the Orthodox Church

options.label: C
options.option_text: By claiming he was the Tewodros of The Fikaré Iyesus

questions.question_text: What was the significance of the Battle of Assam for Kassa Mircha of Tigray?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It convinced the British to support him in his bid to become emperor

options.label: B
options.option_text: It helped him defeat a major rival and hence become emperor
options.explanation: At the Battle of Assam (Assem) in 1871 Kassa Mircha of Tigray defeated Emperor Tekle Giyorgis II, his principal rival, and this victory cleared his path to the throne, on which he was crowned as Yohannes IV in 1872. British support and army modernization were not direct results of that battle, and he already governed Tigray before it.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It convinced him to modernize his army if he wanted to become emperor

options.label: D
options.option_text: It helped him become the sole governor of the province of Tigray

questions.question_text: What strategy did Menelik use in his expansion to the south prior to 1889?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Overwhelming force across the whole region

options.label: B
options.option_text: Force for state societies but negotiation among non-state peoples

options.label: C
options.option_text: A combination of diplomacy and force across the whole region
options.explanation: Menelik II's southern expansion combined diplomacy and force across the whole region, negotiating submission where possible and using military conquest where resistance persisted. He did not apply overwhelming force everywhere, nor did he reserve force for non-state peoples only or restrict peaceful methods to Christians, so this strategy best fits the record.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Peaceful methods among Christians but force in non-Christian areas

questions.question_text: Why did Article 17 of the Wuchale Treaty become a source of conflict between Ethiopia and Italy?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Because the Italian version stated that Ethiopia has agreed to become an Italian protectorate
options.explanation: Article 17 of the Wuchale Treaty became a source of conflict because the Italian version stated that Ethiopia agreed to conduct its foreign affairs through Italy, effectively making it an Italian protectorate, while the Amharic version allowed the option. Boundary, Massawa, and duration disputes were not what made the article so explosive.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Because the Amharic and Italian versions did not agree on the boundaries of the two states

options.label: C
options.option_text: Because the Italian version suggested that Menelik had agreed to give Mereb Melash to Italy

options.label: D
options.option_text: Because the Amharic and Italian versions did not agree how long Italy should stay at Massawa

questions.question_text: The monomers that make up proteins are called:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is nucleotides are the monomers of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Option B is monosaccharides are the monomers of carbohydrates.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is fatty acids are components of lipids.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct?

options.label: A
options.explanation: One litre is defined as exactly one cubic decimetre, so 1 L = 1 dm3. This follows because 1 L equals 1000 cm3 and 1 dm3 also equals 1000 cm3, so the two units are identical. Answer A.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following southern states exercised extensive influence in areas south of the Abbay before the 14thcentury?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Before the fourteenth century the state of Damot exercised extensive influence in the areas south of the Abbay River, controlling rich gold-producing territories and commanding tribute from the region. Bizamo, Hadiya, and Enarea were important southern states, but Damot is the one renowned for wide influence south of the Abbay before 1300.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was a feature of European society during the "Dark Ages"?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The movement of large number of people from the countryside to the cities

options.label: B
options.option_text: The decline of Christianity and rise of traditional religious beliefs

options.label: C
options.option_text: The rise in the power of local rulers at the expense of kings and emperors
options.explanation: During the so-called Dark Ages local rulers, counts, and feudal lords grew powerful at the expense of kings and emperors as central authority collapsed after the fall of Rome. People did not move to cities, Christianity did not decline, and political power did not shift to Scandinavia, so these alternatives misdescribe the period.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The shift of regional political power from Italy northwards to Scandinavia

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was a feature of early capitalism in Europe?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The withdrawal of the special privileges granted to cities by rulers

options.label: B
options.option_text: The growth of conflict between states and merchants over control of markets

options.label: C
options.option_text: The shift of the economy from trading to banking and manufacturing

options.label: D
options.option_text: The rise in importance of the bourgeoisie in economic and cultural life
options.explanation: Early capitalism in Europe was marked by the rising importance of the bourgeoisie in economic and cultural life, as merchants and manufacturers accumulated wealth and influence. Cities kept their privileges, states and merchants generally cooperated, and the economy did not shift from trade to banking and manufacturing at this early stage, so D is correct.

questions.question_text: What was the cause of the conflict between the Christian highland kingdom and the Muslim sultanates in the Medieval period?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The desire of the ruling classes to collect war booty

options.label: B
options.option_text: The determination by both parties to spread their religions

options.label: C
options.option_text: The desire to control the lucrative Zeila trade route
options.explanation: The conflict between the Christian highland kingdom and the Muslim sultanates was mainly caused by rivalry over control of the lucrative Zeila trade route, through which gold, ivory, and slaves flowed to the coast. Religion was used to justify war, but the economic prize of the trade route was the decisive cause.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The need to control the salt producing regions of Afar

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was NOT a consequence of the Oromo population movement of the 16thcentury?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The adoption of aspects of the gada system by the Christian state

options.label: B
options.option_text: The shift of some Oromo people to sedentary agriculture

options.label: C
options.option_text: The assimilation of large number of groups by the Oromo

options.label: D
options.option_text: The loss of territory by the Christian highland kingdom
options.explanation: The adoption of aspects of the gada system by the Christian state was not a consequence of the sixteenth-century Oromo population movement. The movement did cause the Christian kingdom to lose territory, led many Oromo toward sedentary agriculture, and brought about the assimilation of numerous groups, but the Christian state never adopted gada institutions.

questions.question_text: Why did the Jesuits fail to keep Ethiopia a Catholic country during the reign of Susenyos? Because:

options.label: A
options.option_text: they failed to bring in the military support they had promised to Susenyos

options.label: B
options.option_text: their attempt led to widespread opposition by the population
options.explanation: The Jesuits failed to keep Ethiopia Catholic because their religious reforms, especially departures from Orthodox tradition, provoked widespread opposition from the population and nobility, forcing Susenyos to restore the Orthodox Church in 1632. Military promises, noble support, and tabot disputes were secondary issues; popular resistance was decisive.

options.label: C
options.option_text: they sought to secure the support of the nobility for their cause

options.label: D
options.option_text: they disagreed with Susenyos over the abolition of thetabot(Ark)

questions.question_text: Which of the following southern African peoples were cattle herders?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The Khoi (Khoikhoi) of southern Africa were cattle herders who raised livestock, whereas the San were hunter-gatherers, the Hausa were West African traders and farmers, and the Swahili were coastal traders. Thus the Khoi alone among these peoples fit the description of cattle herders in southern Africa.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was a term used for the second phase of the Trans-Atlantic slave trade?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The second phase of the trans-Atlantic slave trade is called the free slave trade, when restrictions and monopolies of the chartered trading companies were removed and independent traders competed freely. The first phase was the monopolistic trade, and the later abolition-era trade in other goods was called legitimate trade, so the others are wrong.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following was a distinct feature of industrial capitalism in Europe in the 19thcentury?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The emergence of big share companies that traded all over the world

options.label: B
options.option_text: The transformation of communication through advances in air and railway transportation

options.label: C
options.option_text: The replacement of human and animal labor by new inanimate sources of power
options.explanation: A distinct feature of industrial capitalism in nineteenth-century Europe was the replacement of human and animal labor with new inanimate sources of power, such as steam, which drove the factory system. Share companies, railways, and air transport are features too, but mechanical power replacing muscle power is the defining characteristic described.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The shift of production from the factory to household workshops

questions.question_text: What was the fundamental cause of the American Civil War?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The formation of closer relationship with the French by the colonists

options.label: B
options.option_text: Attempts by the British to tighten control over the colonies
options.explanation: This question is defective because it asks about the American Civil War, yet all four options describe the American Revolution against Britain, such as British control over the colonies and George III. If read as the Revolution, the fundamental cause was British attempts to tighten control over the colonies, so option B is the closest usable answer.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Opposition by the colonies to British policy on slavery

options.label: D
options.option_text: The unpopularity of George III in the colonies

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about modernization in Ethiopia under Menelik II?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It failed mainly for lack of finance

options.label: B
options.option_text: It was not supported by large sections of the population

options.label: C
options.option_text: It was advanced by the Cabinet established in 1907
options.explanation: Modernization under Menelik II was advanced by the establishment of the Cabinet, or Council of Ministers, in 1907, which brought a measure of organized administration to the government. The reforms did not fail mainly for lack of finance, were not limited to missionary schools, and did receive broad acceptance, making C the accurate statement.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It was limited to the building of schools by foreign missionaries

questions.question_text: What was the consequence of Bismarck's system of alliances for European politics?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It helped Germany expand its influence in Europe as well as Asia

options.label: B
options.option_text: It encouraged resort to diplomacy rather than war

options.label: C
options.option_text: It established a balance of forces in Europe, thus averting war

options.label: D
options.option_text: It led to the establishment of two hostile military camps in Europe
options.explanation: Bismarck's system of alliances divided Europe into two hostile military camps, the Triple Alliance of Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Italy, and the opposing Triple Entente. Rather than averting war or promoting diplomacy, the rigid alliance system increased tensions and ultimately helped trigger the First World War.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was a consequence of the First World War?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The establishment of British and French dominance in the Middle East
options.explanation: A major consequence of the First World War was the establishment of British and French dominance in the Middle East through mandates over the former Ottoman provinces. Poland was partitioned after 1772, Austria and the Czarist empire collapsed, and the German armed forces were restricted rather than completely broken up.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The partition of Poland among the victorious powers

options.label: C
options.option_text: The strengthening of the Austrian and Czarist empires

options.label: D
options.option_text: The complete break-up of the German army and navy

questions.question_text: Why did the Russian working class support the 1917 Revolution? Because:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Conscription of workers had been introduced

options.label: B
options.option_text: Living conditions of workers had worsened
options.explanation: The Russian working class supported the 1917 Revolution chiefly because their living conditions had sharply worsened under the strains of war, with shortages, inflation, and hardship in the cities. Conscription and war losses affected soldiers and workers too, but deteriorating living conditions are the fundamental grievance that drove workers to revolution.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Many conscript workers had lost their lives

options.label: D
options.option_text: the Czar had imposed a war tax on workers

questions.question_text: What strategy did Italy use to undermine Ethiopian unity before the invasion of 1935?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Preventing Ethiopia from producing arms locally

options.label: B
options.option_text: Signing a treaty of peace and friendship with Ethiopia

options.label: C
options.option_text: Bribing Ethiopian officials to weaken the imperial government
options.explanation: Before invading in 1935, Italy tried to undermine Ethiopian unity by bribing Ethiopian officials, funding subversive activities, and encouraging separatist movements to weaken the imperial government. The other actions, such as peace treaties or League support, would have strengthened rather than undermined Ethiopian unity, so C is the correct strategy.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Supporting Ethiopia's application to the League of Nations

questions.question_text: Why was the Fascist rule limited largely to the urban centers during the period of Italian occupation of Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: the small Italian army could only control the towns

options.label: B
options.option_text: the countryside was a base for the resistance
options.explanation: Fascist rule during the Italian occupation was largely confined to urban centers because the countryside served as the base of the Ethiopian resistance, especially the Patriots, who harassed the occupiers and made rural control impossible. The size of the Italian army, services, and soldiers' attitudes were secondary compared to active resistance in the countryside.

options.label: C
options.option_text: urban services were concentrated in the towns

options.label: D
options.option_text: Italian soldiers hated service in the countryside

questions.question_text: What was the fundamental factor for the outbreak of the Second World War?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The spread of racism in Germany and Italy

options.label: B
options.option_text: The arms race between the Triple Alliance and the Triple Entente

options.label: C
options.option_text: The feeling of victimhood felt by Germans about the Versailles Treaty
options.explanation: The fundamental factor behind the outbreak of the Second World War was the sense of grievance and victimhood felt by Germans over the harsh Versailles Treaty, which Hitler exploited to demand revision and expansion. Racism and appeasement were contributing factors, while the pre-1914 alliance rivalry belongs to the First World War.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The policy of appeasement pursued by Britain and France

questions.question_text: What was the immediate factor for the outbreak of the Second World War?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The invasion of Manchuria by the Japanese

options.label: B
options.option_text: The attack on Pearl Harbour by the Japanese

options.label: C
options.option_text: The signing of the Nazi-Soviet non-aggression pact

options.label: D
options.option_text: The invasion of Poland by the German army
options.explanation: The immediate cause of the Second World War was the German invasion of Poland on 1 September 1939, which led Britain and France to declare war on Germany. The Japanese invasion of Manchuria, the attack on Pearl Harbor, and the Nazi-Soviet pact were significant events but not the immediate trigger of the war in Europe.

questions.question_text: What was the importance of the Tehran Conference of 1943 in the formation of the United Nations?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The Charter of the UN was signed by member states there

options.label: B
options.option_text: The details of the UN structure were worked out there

options.label: C
options.option_text: The idea of forming the UN received support from the great powers there
options.explanation: The importance of the Tehran Conference of 1943 was that the idea of forming a new world organization received the support of the great powers, as Roosevelt discussed his plan for a United Nations with Stalin and Churchill. The structure was worked out at Dumbarton Oaks and the Charter signed at San Francisco, so those options are wrong.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The idea of creating the UN was first discussed there

questions.question_text: Which of the following countries was a member of the Warsaw Pact?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hungary was a member of the Warsaw Pact, the Soviet-led military alliance of Eastern European communist states founded in 1955. Turkey, Greece, and Norway were members of the opposing Western alliance, NATO, and therefore could not belong to the Warsaw Pact.

questions.question_text: How does a historian establish the value of a source for his work?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By carrying out a critical evaluation of the source he/she uses
