questions.question_text: Which one of the following statement is NOT correct about the magnetic properties of matter?

options.label: A
options.option_text: There is a tendency to oppose the applied magnetic field in a diamagnetic substance.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The unpaired electrons in diamagnetic materials will align with the applied magnetic field and parallel to each other.
options.explanation: Diamagnetic materials have all of their electrons paired, so they have no permanent magnetic dipoles and cannot align unpaired electrons with an applied field. The claim in option B is therefore not correct, whereas ferromagnetic and paramagnetic materials do contain unpaired electrons that tend to align with the field.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The unpaired electrons in ferromagnetic materials will align with the applied magnetic field and parallel to each other.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The unpaired electrons in paramagnetic substance which will tend to align themselves in the same direction as the applied magnetic field.

questions.question_text: Suppose a conductor of length l carrying a current I placed in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude B. When the conductor is making an angle θ with that of the magnetic field then the force experienced by the conductor due to the magnetic field is given by

options.label: D
options.explanation: The magnetic force on a current carrying conductor is the vector product of the length vector and the magnetic field, multiplied by the current, giving F equal to I times L cross B. Option D, read as this vector formula, is the correct statement, while the other options mix the factors incorrectly.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statement is correct about tangent galvanometer?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The current through a coil of the wire generates a magnetic field at the center of the coil
options.explanation: In a tangent galvanometer the current flowing through the coil generates a magnetic field at the centre of the coil, which deflects the magnetic needle. The coil is wound on a non-magnetic frame, and the current is proportional rather than inversely proportional to the tangent of the deflection angle, so option A is correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It consists of a coil of insulated copper wire on a circular magnetic frame.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The current is inversely proportional to the tangent of the angle of the needle's deflection.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is a device used to measure the electric current in terms of the electric field it produces.

questions.question_text: A long conductor shown in the figure carries a current I in the direction indicated by the arrow. Which statement is NOT correct about the magnetic field produced by this current carrying conductor?[IMAGE: img_1.webp]

options.label: A
options.option_text: Doubling the current through the conductor doubles the field strength.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Reversing the current direction will reverse the direction of the magnetic field.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The magnetic field encircles the conductor.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The field strength is directly proportional to the distance from the conductor.
options.explanation: The magnetic field of a long straight current carrying conductor encircles the wire and its strength is proportional to the current and inversely proportional to the distance from the conductor. Doubling the current doubles the field, reversing the current reverses the field direction, so the statement that field is directly proportional to distance is not correct, option D.

questions.question_text: A coiled copper has 50 turns and coil cross-sectional area of 9 x10^-4m²? This coil is initially placed in a uniform magnetic field 0.02 T and pulled out of a field completely (where the field is zero) in 0.5 seconds. What is the magnitude of the induced electromotive force?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The induced emf equals the number of turns times the change in flux divided by the time taken. The flux change is the area times the field, which is 9 times 10 to the minus 4 times 0.02, giving 1.8 times 10 to the minus 5 weber, and with 50 turns over 0.5 seconds the emf is 1.8 millivolts, option D.

questions.question_text: A 15.0 mH inductor is used to induce an electromotive force of 5.0 mV. What is the rate change of the induced current?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The induced emf in an inductor equals the inductance multiplied by the rate of change of the current. Rearranging gives the rate as the emf divided by the inductance, which is 5 millivolts divided by 15 millihenries, equal to 0.33 amperes per second, so option C is the correct value.

questions.question_text: A coil and a permanent magnet are set in relative motion. Which one of the following statement is NOT correct about induced electromotive force?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Coil with larger number of turns produce greater induced electromotive forces.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Moving a magnet relative to the coil and the coil relative to the magnet with equal speed will produce the same electromotive force.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The magnitude of the induced electromotive force is directly proportional to the relative velocity between the two.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The direction in which the coil moves relative to the magnetic field does not have any effect on the induced electromotive force.
options.explanation: The magnitude of the induced emf depends on the rate of change of magnetic flux, so it is proportional to the relative velocity and to the number of turns. The direction in which the coil moves relative to the field changes the sign and magnitude of the flux change, so claiming the direction has no effect is not correct, option D.

questions.question_text: What is the advantage of using alternating current in transmission of electric energy?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It enables to reach the consumers at very high voltage.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It enables a transformer to increase or decrease the voltage as required.
options.explanation: The main advantage of alternating current in power transmission is that a transformer can step the voltage up for efficient long distance transmission and step it down near consumers. This voltage transformation is not possible with steady direct current, so option B correctly describes the advantage.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It completely avoids energy loss due to heating.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It uses very high current in the transmission line.

questions.question_text: Capacitive reactance is defined as

options.label: A
options.option_text: the equivalent quantity to resistance when we are talking about capacitors.
options.explanation: Capacitive reactance is the opposition that a capacitor offers to alternating current, and it plays the same role for capacitors that resistance plays for resistors. Option A gives exactly this meaning, whereas impedance applies to the whole circuit and the other options refer to different components.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the equivalent quantity to impedance of in RLC circuit.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the equivalent quantity to resistance when we are talking about inductors.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the equivalent quantity to resistance when we are talking about resistors.

questions.question_text: The second law of thermodynamics states that

options.label: A
options.option_text: the increase in the internal energy of a system is equal to the sum of the energy entering the system through heating, and work done on the system.

options.label: B
options.option_text: two bodies that are separately in thermal equilibrium with a third body must be in thermal equilibrium with each other.

options.label: C
options.option_text: no process is possible in which there is an overall decrease in the entropy of the universe.
options.explanation: The second law of thermodynamics states that no natural process can produce an overall decrease in the entropy of the universe; entropy either increases or stays the same. Option C states this correctly, whereas the first law concerns energy balance and the other options misstate the direction of entropy change.

options.label: D
options.option_text: no process is possible in which there is an overall increase in the entropy of the universe.

questions.question_text: A mass-spring system set to oscillate in a simple harmonic motion over friction less horizontal surface. The amplitude of this oscillation is 20 cm. A second mass-spring system with the same spring constant is set to oscillate in the same way but with amplitude of 10 cm. The energy of the

options.label: A
options.option_text: first mass-spring system has four times the second one.
options.explanation: The energy stored in a mass-spring system in simple harmonic motion is proportional to the square of the amplitude, since the maximum elastic energy is half k times amplitude squared. The first system has twice the amplitude, so its energy is four times that of the second system, option A.

options.label: B
options.option_text: second mass-spring system has the square of the first one.

options.label: C
options.option_text: first mass-spring system has twice the second one.

options.label: D
options.option_text: second mass-spring system has half of the first one.

questions.question_text: Suppose you are given the following traveling waves that have the same frequency and the same amplitude. A[IMAGE: img_2.webp]Which graph represents the super position of the two waves?
A string vibrates with speed of 110 m/s in its fourth harmonic has a frequency of 880 Hz. What is the length of the string?

options.label: C
options.explanation: For the fourth harmonic of a string fixed at both ends the frequency is four times the fundamental, and the fundamental is the wave speed divided by twice the length. Therefore 880 equals 4 times 110 divided by 2L, which gives L equal to 0.5 metres, so the string length is 50.0 cm, option C.

questions.question_text: A string vibrates with speed of 110 m/s in its fourth harmonic has a frequency of 880 Hz. What is the length of the string?

options.label: C
options.explanation: For the fourth harmonic of a string fixed at both ends the frequency is four times the fundamental, and the fundamental is the wave speed divided by twice the length. Therefore 880 equals 4 times 110 divided by 2L, which gives L equal to 0.5 metres, so the string length is 50.0 cm, option C.

questions.question_text: An interference patterns observed after a monochromatic beam of light passes through a single slit and a double slit. Which one of the following is correct about the width of the central maxima and the first order maxima in single slit and double slit?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The width of the central maxima has equal with the width of the first order maxima in a single slit interference while it has twice the width of the first order maxima in double slit interference.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The width of the central maxima has twice the width of the first order maxima in both cases.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The width of the central maxima and first order maxima has equal width in both cases.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The width of the central maxima has twice the width of the first order maxima in a single slit interference while it has equal width in double slit interference.
options.explanation: In single slit diffraction the central maximum is twice as wide as the other maxima, because the central fringe spans the region between the first minima on both sides. In double slit interference all the bright fringes have the same width, so option D correctly describes both patterns.

questions.question_text: A light wave of wavelength 590 nm pass through a narrow double slit of 0.2 mm slit separation. An interference pattern is formed on a screen at a distance of 1.5 m. What is the distance between the consecutive bright fringes on the screen?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The distance between consecutive bright fringes in a double slit experiment is the wavelength times the screen distance divided by the slit separation. Substituting 590 nanometres, 1.5 metres and 0.2 millimetres gives 4.425 millimetres, so the fringe spacing is 4.43 mm, option B.

questions.question_text: According to Gauss's law the net electric flux through any hypothetical closed surface is proportional to the enclosed;

options.label: D
options.explanation: Gauss law states that the net electric flux through any closed surface is proportional to the total electric charge enclosed by that surface. The proportionality constant is the reciprocal of the permittivity of free space, so option D identifies the enclosed charge correctly.

questions.question_text: When a dielectric material placed between two parallel metal plates in the presence of electric fields they enable the plates to store

options.label: A
options.option_text: much less charge at different potential difference.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the same charge at the same potential difference.

options.label: C
options.option_text: much more charge at the same potential difference.
options.explanation: Inserting a dielectric between the plates increases the capacitance because the dielectric reduces the field for a given charge. For the same potential difference the capacitor can then store much more charge, so option C correctly describes the effect of the dielectric material.

options.label: D
options.option_text: much more charge at different potential difference.

questions.question_text: A parallel plate capacitor with plate areaAand plates separationdstores a chargeQwhen a potential differenceVis kept between the plates. Then the region between the plates is completely filled with a dielectric material of dielectric constantεr. IfEdenotes the electric field between the plates, the energy density stored by the capacitor is

options.label: A
options.explanation: The energy density stored in the electric field of a capacitor filled with a dielectric is one half times the permittivity of free space times the dielectric constant times the square of the electric field. Option A gives exactly this expression, so it is the correct energy density formula.

questions.question_text: A uniform conductor of lengthLand cross-sectional areaAcarries a currentIwhen a potential differenceVis applied across its ends. If the number of free electrons per unit volume of the conductor isn, and the electron charge ise, then the drift velocity of the electrons in the conductor is

options.label: B
options.explanation: The drift velocity follows from the relation between current and charge flow, namely I equals n e A times the drift velocity. Rearranging gives the drift velocity equal to the current divided by the product of the carrier density, the electron charge and the cross sectional area, which is option B.

questions.question_text: A student wants to measure the length and height of the school laboratory. There are Vernier calipers, meter stick, micrometer screw gauge and meter tape measuring instruments in the laboratory. Which one of the following measuring instrument and unit is appropriate for the measurement?

options.label: A
options.explanation: For measuring the length and height of a laboratory, the appropriate instrument is a meter tape because it can span distances of several metres, and the natural unit is the metre. The smaller instruments and units given in the other options are suited to precision measurement of small objects.

questions.question_text: In reporting an experimental result the collected data has to be clearly tabulated with appropriate units. Which of the following table correctly represents a data collected during an experiment?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Voltage4V6V8V12V16VCurrent0.5 I0.75 I1 I1.5 I2.0 I

options.label: C
options.explanation: A correctly reported data table must include the appropriate unit for each quantity. Voltage is measured in volts and current in amperes, so the table listing Voltage in volts and Current in amperes with the corresponding numerical values is correct, which is option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Voltage4 V6 V8 V12 V16 VCurrent0.5 C0.75 C1 C1.5 C2.0 C

questions.question_text: A 10 N force is applied in the direction of North-East, which of the following graphical representation of the force is correct? (Assume the lengths of all arrows are equal and the paper head points towards North)

Two vectors of magnitude 8 units in the direction of East and the second vector of magnitude 6 units in the direction of North are given. If you add the two vectors using graphical method, which graph represents the resultant of the two vectors?
Which of the following pair of vectors are collinear?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Two vectors are collinear when one is a scalar multiple of the other, meaning their corresponding components have the same ratio. The pair of vectors representing four, two and minus four, minus two have components in the ratio of minus one, so they are collinear, option A.

questions.question_text: Instantaneous velocity is different from average velocity in that, instantaneous velocity is

options.label: A
options.option_text: the velocity at a particular instant of time.
options.explanation: Instantaneous velocity is the velocity of an object at a particular instant of time, obtained by letting the time interval approach zero. Average velocity, in contrast, is the total displacement divided by the total time, so option A gives the correct distinction.

options.label: B
options.option_text: in opposite direction to the displacement of the moving object.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the total displacement to the time taken.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the average velocity during the time of acceleration.

questions.question_text: A car travelling at 20 m/s starts to speedup. After 5 minutes its speed is 144 m/s. What is the acceleration of the car?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The acceleration is the change in velocity divided by the time taken. The speed increases from 20 m/s to 144 m/s in 300 seconds, so the change is 124 m/s, and dividing by 300 gives an acceleration of about 0.41 m/s squared, option B.

questions.question_text: A bullet of 200 g mass fired from a 30.0 m high building, horizontally. At the same time a bullet of the same mass fired vertically down from the same height. What can be concluded about the motion of the two bullets?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A bullet fired vertically takes more time to strike the ground.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Both bullets move with the same horizontal velocity

options.label: C
options.option_text: Both bullets strike the ground at the same time.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A bullet fired horizontally takes more time to strike the ground.
options.explanation: The vertically fired bullet has an initial downward velocity, so it reaches the ground quickly. The horizontally fired bullet has zero initial vertical velocity and falls from rest, so its vertical motion takes longer. Thus the horizontal bullet takes more time to strike the ground, option D.

questions.question_text: A bird flies at speed of 10m/s to south relative to the Earth. A wind blows at speed of 4m/s to East relative to the Earth. What is the speed of the relative to the wind?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The velocity of the bird relative to the wind is the bird velocity minus the wind velocity, which has components 4 m/s toward the west and 10 m/s toward the south. The magnitude is the square root of 16 plus 100, about 10.8 m/s, and the direction is South-West, option D.

questions.question_text: Dynamics is a branch of mechanics concerned with the motion or an object

options.label: A
options.explanation: Dynamics is the branch of mechanics that studies the motion of objects and relates that motion to the forces causing it. It therefore concerns motion under the action of forces, whereas kinematics studies motion without considering its causes, making option A correct.

options.label: B
options.option_text: under the action of balanced forces.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statement is correct about, a bar on which a force acts at one end and pivoted at the other?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The force is parallel to the angular acceleration produced.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The force, angular velocity and the torque are coplanar.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The force is coplanar with the torque it produces.
options.explanation: When a force acts at one end of a pivoted bar, the force and the torque it produces lie in the same plane, so they are coplanar. The force is not parallel to the angular velocity or acceleration in general, so option C is the correct statement about the arrangement.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The force is collinear with the angular velocity

questions.question_text: The necessary condition for an object to be in rotational equilibrium is

options.label: A
options.option_text: the net moment of all forces should be non-zero.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the net torque acting on the object is different from zero.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the net force exerting on the object must be zero.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the sum of clockwise torques equals to the sum of counter clockwise torques.
options.explanation: A body is in rotational equilibrium when the net torque acting on it is zero. This means the sum of the clockwise torques equals the sum of the counter clockwise torques, which is the statement in option D, whereas the net force condition belongs to translational equilibrium.

questions.question_text: An aluminum wire of initial length 2.0 m where increased by 2.0 cm in its length being on application of a force of 9.0 N. What is the strain energy of the material?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The strain energy stored in the wire is half the product of the applied force and the extension, since the force grows linearly with extension. Taking half of 9.0 N times 0.02 m gives 0.09 J, which is 9.0 times 10 to the minus 2 joules, option C.

questions.question_text: Ethanol has a surface tension of 22x 10-3 N/m and its density is of 0.789 g/cm3. The radius of the capillary tube is 15 mm, and the contact angle is 30o. Determine the height rise in the column of the capillary tube.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The capillary rise is given by two times the surface tension times the cosine of the contact angle divided by the density times g times the radius. Substituting the given values gives about 0.33 millimetres, so the height rise is approximately 0.32 mm, option A.

questions.question_text: Suppose a stream of fluid flows past a solid object, which one of the following does NOT affect the laminar flow of the fluid?

options.label: B
options.option_text: The density of the solid object
options.explanation: The laminar flow of a fluid past a solid object depends on the viscosity of the fluid, the shape of the object and the relative speed of flow. The density of the solid object itself does not affect the flow pattern, so option B is the quantity that does not affect laminar flow.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The shape of the solid object

options.label: D
options.option_text: The speed of the solid object

questions.question_text: Water enters a tube of non-uniform diameter. The speed of the force at the entry of area A1is 12 m/s and the speed becomes 4 m/s at the exit opening of area A2. Which one is correct about the ratio of A1/A2?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The equation of continuity states that the product of cross sectional area and speed is constant along the tube, so A1 v1 equals A2 v2. With the entry speed 12 m/s and the exit speed 4 m/s, the ratio A1 over A2 equals 4 over 12, which is one third, option B.

questions.question_text: The particular temperature and pressure at which the solid, liquid, and gaseous phases of a given substance are all at equilibrium with another is known as:

options.label: B
options.explanation: The triple point is the unique combination of temperature and pressure at which the solid, liquid and gaseous phases of a substance coexist in equilibrium. Option B names this state correctly, whereas the critical point is the end of the liquid vapour coexistence curve and heat capacity is a different quantity.

questions.question_text: Most solids expand upon heating, which one of the following statements correctly describe the phenomena?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Increase in temperature decreases the vibrational kinetic energy and increases the amplitude of the atoms constituting the solid.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Increase in temperature increases the vibrational kinetic energy and decreases the amplitude of the atoms constituting the solid.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Increase in temperature increases the vibrational kinetic energy and amplitude of the atoms constituting the solid.
options.explanation: When a solid is heated its atoms vibrate with greater energy, so the vibrational kinetic energy of the atoms increases and the amplitude of their vibrations grows larger. This increased amplitude pulls the atoms farther apart, causing the solid to expand, which option C describes correctly.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Increase in temperature decreases the vibrational kinetic energy and amplitude of the atoms constituting the solid.

questions.question_text: If 25 J is taken away by heat from a system, and the system does 20 J of work, what is the change in internal energy of the system?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Using the first law, the change in internal energy equals the heat added minus the work done by the system. Here 25 J is removed, so Q is negative 25 J, and the system does 20 J of work, so the change is negative 25 minus 20, giving negative 45 J, option B.

questions.question_text: A sample mixture of gas contains 72% of hydrogen and 28% of Helium. What is the partial pressure of helium at an atmospheric pressure of 76 cm of mercury (Hg)?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The partial pressure of a component in a gas mixture is its mole fraction multiplied by the total pressure. Helium makes up 28 percent of the mixture, so its partial pressure is 0.28 times 76 cm of mercury, which equals 21.28 cm of mercury, option D.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct about the concept and units of coefficient of friction?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Coefficient of friction is the ratio of frictional force to normal force.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Coefficient of static friction is less than its value of kinetic friction.
options.explanation: The coefficient of friction is the ratio of the frictional force to the normal force and has no unit, and it can exceed unity. However, the coefficient of static friction is generally greater than the coefficient of kinetic friction, so the statement that static friction is less than kinetic friction is not correct, option B.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Coefficient of static friction has no unit.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The coefficient of friction is always less or equal to unity (1).

questions.question_text: A car is traveling at constant velocity along a straight line. Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The displacement of the car increase linearly with time.
options.explanation: When a car travels at constant velocity, its displacement increases by equal amounts in equal time intervals, so displacement grows linearly with time. The net force on the car is zero and there is no acceleration, which makes option A the only correct statement.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The displacement of the car is in opposite direction.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The net force on the car is different from zero.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The acceleration of the car is in opposite direction.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct about the impulse on an object?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The impulse on an object is changed when the net force acting on the object is zero.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The area under the curve of momentum versus time graph is the impulse on an object.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Impulse is the change in momentum when a force is exerted on an object for a very short period of time.
options.explanation: Impulse is defined as the change in momentum of an object that results when a force acts on it for a short period of time. It equals the average force multiplied by the time of application, so option C gives the correct definition of impulse.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Impulse is the rate of change in momentum due to external force exerted on an object for a very short period of time.

questions.question_text: Consider two collisions that occurred between two trollies having the same mass, moving with the same speed, and in opposite directions. Collision 1: after collision the two trollies bounce back with the same speed. Collision 2: after collision the two trollies stick together due to magnetic coupler. Which of the following statement is correct about the two collisions?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Collision 1 is elastic and collision 2 is inelastic.
options.explanation: In collision one the trollies bounce back with the same speed, so both kinetic energy and momentum are conserved, making it elastic. In collision two the trollies stick together, so kinetic energy is lost, making it inelastic. Option B correctly identifies the two types.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Collision 1 is inelastic and collision 2 is elastic.

questions.question_text: Suppose that you are given a mass attached to a spring and oscillates up and down. This mass-spring system has maximum gravitational potential energy (GPE), elastic potential energy (EPE) and kinetic energy (KE) at:

options.label: D
options.explanation: For a vertical mass-spring oscillator the gravitational potential energy is greatest at the top of the motion, the elastic potential energy is greatest at the bottom where the spring is most stretched, and the kinetic energy is greatest at the middle where the speed is maximum. Option D gives these positions.

questions.question_text: A pendulum shown in the figure below has 2.5 m length and mass m. When it pass point A, its mass has a speed of 2.0 m/s. (neglect the air resistance) The height of the pendulum at displacement positions B and C is

options.label: C
options.explanation: The height reached by the pendulum is found from the conservation of energy, where the kinetic energy at the lowest point becomes gravitational potential energy at the extreme positions. The height equals the speed squared divided by twice g, which is 4 divided by 20, giving 0.2 m, option C.

questions.question_text: A 5.0 kg stone is dropped from a top of 30.0 m building. At a height of 10.0 m above the ground, 60% of its initial potential energy is converted to kinetic energy. Which of the following statements is correct about the transformation of energy for the stone?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The sum of its potential energy and kinetic energy is the same at every point during its fall.

options.label: B
options.option_text: 6.7 % of its gravitational potential energy is dissipated due to air resistance.
options.explanation: The initial potential energy of the stone is the weight times the height, giving 1500 J. At 10 m above the ground the potential energy is 500 J and the kinetic energy is 60 percent of the initial energy, or 900 J, so the total is 1400 J and 100 J, or 6.7 percent, has been dissipated, option B.

options.label: C
options.option_text: 60% of its original potential energy is converted to heat energy due to air resistance.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The remaining 40% of the energy is still available as gravitational potential energy.

questions.question_text: A force of34Nacts at a displacement of43m.The magnitude and the direction of the torque produced is

options.label: D
options.explanation: The torque is the cross product of the displacement vector and the force vector. With the displacement along the i and j directions and the force also in the plane, the cross product points along the k direction, and its magnitude is 4 times 4 minus 3 times 3, giving 7 N m, option D.

questions.question_text: A wheel starts rotating at 1.2 Hz and reaches 1.8 Hz in 5 seconds. Calculate the angular displacement it covers within 5 seconds?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The initial angular speed is 1.2 times 2 pi and the final speed is 1.8 times 2 pi, both in radians per second. The angular displacement is the average angular speed times the time, which is 3 pi times 5 seconds, giving 15 pi radians, option D.

questions.question_text: If you are given the following physical quantities in angular motion: torque (?), Linear momentum (?), moment of inertia (I), angular speed (?), and angular acceleration (?). The angular momentum (L) is the

options.label: A
options.option_text: product of moment of inertia and angular speed.
options.explanation: Angular momentum is defined as the product of the moment of inertia of a body and its angular speed. It plays the same role in rotational motion that linear momentum plays in translational motion, so option A gives the correct definition.

options.label: B
options.option_text: ratio of moment of inertia to angular acceleration.

options.label: C
options.option_text: product of moment of inertia and torque.

options.label: D
options.option_text: ratio of linear momentum to moment of inertia.

questions.question_text: Suppose a triangular object (O) is placed in front of a plane mirror and its image is observed at position (X). Which one of the following diagrams represents the image (I) formed by the mirror when it is observed from position (X)
An object is placed 25.0 cm in front of a concave mirror having focal length of 10.0 cm. The magnification of the mirror is ____

options.label: C
options.explanation: For a concave mirror the mirror equation relates the image distance to the object distance and focal length. The image distance is found to be 50 thirds of a centimetre, and the magnification is the ratio of image distance to object distance, giving 16.7 over 25, which is 0.67, option C.

questions.question_text: The unit vector in the direction of A⃗ = 3î + 4ĵ is ______.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The unit vector in the direction of a given vector is the vector divided by its magnitude. The magnitude of three i plus four j is five, so the unit vector is three fifths i plus four fifths j, which matches option A.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pair of vectors are collinear?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Two vectors are collinear when one is a scalar multiple of the other, so their components have the same ratio. The pair two i plus three j and minus four i minus six j differ by the factor minus two, so they are collinear, option D, while the other pairs do not have proportional components.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements distinguishes between random and systematic errors?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Systematic error can be minimized by taking several readings and averaging; whereas random error cannot be minimized.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Systematic error makes measured values to be always above or always below the true value; whereas random error causes measured values to be sometimes above and sometimes below the true value.
options.explanation: Systematic errors bias the measurements consistently, making them always above or always below the true value, and they cannot be removed by averaging. Random errors scatter the readings, making them sometimes above and sometimes below the true value, so option B gives the correct distinction.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Random error makes measured values to be always above or always below the true value; whereas systematic error causes measured values to be sometimes above and sometimes below the true value.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Random error is biased, whereas systematic error does not show bias.

questions.question_text: For an object moving in straight line,

options.label: A
options.option_text: if the displacement changes by equal amount in equal time interval, the displacement-time graph is horizontal line.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the area of the region under the displacement-time graph and the slope of velocity-time graph are, respectively, the acceleration and displacement of the object.

options.label: C
options.option_text: if the velocity increases by equal amount in equal time interval, the velocity-time graph is straight line with positive slope and the acceleration-time graph is horizontal.
options.explanation: When the velocity of an object increases by equal amounts in equal time intervals, the velocity-time graph is a straight line with a positive slope and the acceleration is constant, so the acceleration-time graph is a horizontal line. Option C correctly describes this situation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the slope of displacement-time graph and the area of the region under acceleration-time graph are, respectively, the acceleration and velocity of the object.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about satellite motion?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A satellite moving closer to the Earth takes longer time to complete one revolution than a satellite farther from the Earth.

options.label: B
options.option_text: For two satellites moving around the Earth at equal orbital radius, a heavier satellite has larger speed than a lighter one.

options.label: C
options.option_text: For equal orbital radius, a satellite moving around the Earth has smaller speed than a satellite moving about Moon.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A satellite closer to Earth is faster than a satellite farther from the Earth.
options.explanation: For a satellite in a circular orbit the orbital speed is the square root of the gravitational parameter divided by the orbital radius. A satellite closer to the Earth therefore moves faster and completes its orbit in a shorter time than one farther away, so option D is correct.

questions.question_text: A block of mass m is placed on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the surface is μ. A force of magnitude F acts on the block at an angle θ as shown in the figure below. The minimum magnitude of the force F required to slide the block on the surface is[IMAGE: img_1.webp]

options.label: B
options.explanation: For the block to begin sliding the horizontal component of the applied force must overcome static friction. If the force pulls the block upward at the angle theta, the normal force is reduced and the required force is mu times mg divided by the sum of cos theta and mu times sin theta, option B.

questions.question_text: A ball of mass m moving with a speed v strikes a hard wall at an angle θ with the wall. It is reflected with the same speed at the same angle as shown in the figure below.[IMAGE: img_2.webp]If the ball is in contact with the wall for time t, then the average force acting on the wall is given by

options.label: C
options.explanation: Only the velocity component perpendicular to the wall changes during the collision, and since the ball rebounds with the same speed, this component reverses. The change in momentum is therefore two m v cos theta, and dividing by the contact time gives the average force two m v cos theta over t, option C.

questions.question_text: According to the work-energy theorem,

options.label: A
options.option_text: work done by tension on an object tied to a string and moving in a horizontal circle is negative.

options.label: B
options.option_text: work done by gravity on an object thrown downward is negative.

options.label: C
options.option_text: work done by gravity on an object thrown upward and moving upward is negative.
options.explanation: According to the work-energy theorem, the work done by a force equals the change in kinetic energy it produces. Gravity acts downward, so when an object is thrown upward and moving upward the displacement opposes the gravitational force and the work done by gravity is negative, option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: work done by gravitational force on a satellite moving around the earth in a circular orbit is positive.

questions.question_text: Standing wave is formed when two identical waves traveling in opposite directions in the same medium interfere with each other. If y1 and y2 are the interfering waves and y=y1+y2 is the resulting standing wave, which of the following is a correct combination?

options.label: A
options.option_text: y1=A sin(kx-ωt), y2=A sin(kx+ωt), y=A sin(kx)cos(2ωt)

options.label: B
options.option_text: y1=A sin(kx-ωt), y2=A sin(kx+ωt), y=2A sin(kx)cos(ωt)
options.explanation: The superposition of two identical waves travelling in opposite directions produces a standing wave. Adding A sin of kx minus omega t and A sin of kx plus omega t gives 2 A sin of kx times cos of omega t, which is the correct combination in option B.

options.label: C
options.option_text: y1=A sin(kx-ωt), y2=A sin(kx-ωt), y=2A sin(kx)cos(ωt)

options.label: D
options.option_text: y1=A sin(kx-ωt), y2=A cos(kx+ωt), y=2A sin(kx-ωt)

questions.question_text: A Young double slit experiment consists of two narrow slits separated by 0.06 mm and 1.2 m away from a screen. If the slits are illuminated with a light of wavelength 563 nm, the location of the fourth bright fringe on the screen is

options.label: D
options.explanation: The position of the fourth bright fringe is four times the fringe width, where the fringe width is the wavelength times the screen distance divided by the slit separation. Substituting the given values gives 4.5 centimetres, so option D is the location of the fourth bright fringe.

questions.question_text: An electric dipole consists of a negative charge -q placed at a point with x and y coordinates (-2,-2) and a positive charge +q at (2,2). The dipole is placed in a uniform electric field E directed in the positive x direction. If the dipole axis makes an angle θ with the field, which of the following is true about the dipole?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The field rotates the dipole in the direction of decreasing the angle θ, until the dipole becomes parallel to the field.
options.explanation: The dipole moment points from the negative charge toward the positive charge, so it makes an angle of 45 degrees with the positive x axis. A uniform electric field exerts a torque that rotates the dipole to align its moment with the field, decreasing the angle theta until they are parallel, option A.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The field rotates it in the direction of increasing the angle θ, until the dipole is perpendicular to the field.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is in both translational and rotational equilibrium.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It travels in the direction of the electric field.

questions.question_text: The electric potential at a distance of 2 cm from a -1.6 x 10-9C point charge is

options.label: D
options.explanation: The electric potential of a point charge is the Coulomb constant times the charge divided by the distance. For a charge of minus 1.6 times 10 to the minus 9 coulombs at 2 centimetres, the potential is 9 times 10 to the ninth times the charge divided by 0.02, giving negative 720 volts, option D.

questions.question_text: Two resistors R1=1 Ω and R2=4 Ω are connected in parallel to each other and their combination is connected in series with a third resistor R3=2 Ω. The whole combination is connected to a voltage source of potential difference 14 V.[IMAGE: img_3.webp]The potential difference across R1 is

options.label: D
options.explanation: The parallel combination of R1 and R2 has resistance 0.8 ohms, and in series with R3 the total resistance is 2.8 ohms. The current from the 14 V source is therefore 5 A, and the voltage across the parallel branch is 5 times 0.8, giving 4 V across R1, option D.

questions.question_text: Consider a long and tightly wound solenoid carrying current I, having length L and N turns of winding. If n is the number of turns per unit length, which of the following describes the magnetic field produced by the solenoid?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The magnetic field inside the solenoid is zero, whereas the field outside is proportional to the length of the solenoid.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The magnetic field inside the solenoid is constant and is parallel to the solenoid's axis, whereas the field outside is negligible.
options.explanation: For a long tightly wound solenoid the magnetic field inside is uniform, directed parallel to the axis of the solenoid, and is given by the permeability times the number of turns per unit length times the current. The field outside the solenoid is negligible, so option B is correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The magnetic field inside the solenoid is uniform and perpendicular to the axis of the solenoid.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The magnetic field outside the solenoid is as strong as the field inside it.

questions.question_text: According to the law of electromagnetic induction,

options.label: A
options.option_text: the magnitude of emf induced in a circuit is directly proportional to the rate of change the magnetic flux crossing any surface bounded by the circuit.
options.explanation: Faraday law of electromagnetic induction states that the magnitude of the induced emf is directly proportional to the rate of change of the magnetic flux crossing the surface bounded by the circuit. Option A states this law correctly, whereas constant flux induces no emf.

options.label: B
options.option_text: a changing magnetic field parallel to the plane of a circuit induces an emf in it.

options.label: C
options.option_text: a constant magnetic flux crossing the surface of a circuit induced an emf in the circuit.

options.label: D
options.option_text: an emf is induced in a circuit when a constant magnetic field crosses its surface.

questions.question_text: A resistor R, a capacitor C, and inductor L are connected in series to an AC voltage source that generates a sinusoidal voltage, V(t)=Vpsin(ω t), with Vpand ω being the peak voltage and angular frequency of the source. If XC, XL, and Z are capacitive reactance, inductive reactance, and impedance, respectively, Irmsand Vrmsare the root-mean-square (rms) values of the current and voltage, the average power dissipated in series the RLC circuit is given by

options.label: A
options.explanation: The average power dissipated in an RLC circuit is the product of the rms current, the rms voltage and the power factor. When the reactances cancel the circuit is purely resistive and the power is the product of the rms values, so option A gives the relevant expression.

questions.question_text: According to the Heisenberg's uncertainty principle,

options.label: A
options.option_text: the larger the position uncertainty, the larger the momentum uncertainty.

options.label: B
options.option_text: if the uncertainty in position decreases, the momentum uncertainty decreases, too.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the more precisely we measure the position of a particle, we become less precise of its momentum and vice versa.
options.explanation: The Heisenberg uncertainty principle states that the product of the uncertainties in position and momentum is at least Planck constant divided by four pi. Therefore the more precisely the position of a particle is measured, the less precisely its momentum is known, which is option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: we can measure both the position and momentum of a particle simultaneously with unlimited precision.

questions.question_text: The graph of nuclear binding energy per nucleon (BE/A) versus mass number (A) has its peak near an atomic weight A = 56. Which of the following statements is true about the graph?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Uranium (A = 235), which has larger binding energy than iron (A = 56), is more stable than iron.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Nucleus with larger number of neutron is more stable than nucleus of the same atom with smaller number of neutron.

options.label: C
options.option_text: For heavier nuclei (A > 56), the binding energy per nucleon decreases with the increase of mass number; implying that heavier atoms can increase their stability by increasing their protons' number.

options.label: D
options.option_text: For smaller atoms (A < 56), the biding energy per nucleon generally increases with the increase of mass number; indicating that lighter atoms can increase stability through nuclear fission.
options.explanation: The binding energy per nucleon graph rises steeply for light nuclei, reaching a maximum near iron, and then falls for heavier nuclei. For atoms lighter than iron the binding energy per nucleon generally increases with mass number, indicating that such nuclei gain stability by fusing together, option D.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about reflection and refraction of sound waves and their applications?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In pre-natal scanning, reflection and refraction of sound allows doctors to monitor the progress of a developing baby.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Reflection of sound (echo) is formed when sound enters a medium of varying densities.
options.explanation: Reflection of a sound wave occurs when it bounces back from a surface, whereas the change in direction when sound enters a medium of varying density is refraction. Therefore the statement in option B, which describes refraction while calling it reflection, is not correct.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Reflection and refraction of sound are used to detect flaws in metals and to help people park their cars.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Refraction of sound is the change in its direction as it travels through a medium having different densities.

questions.question_text: A torque T rotates an object of mass m and moment of inertia I through an angle θ. The work done on the object by the torque is

options.label: C
options.explanation: The work done by a torque acting on a rotating object is the product of the torque and the angle through which it rotates. This is the rotational analogue of force times distance, so option C gives the work done by the torque correctly.

questions.question_text: A satellite revolves around the Earth in a circular orbit of radius r = 4 x 10^6 m. The period of the satellite is

options.label: A
options.explanation: The orbital period of a satellite is obtained from the relation T squared proportional to the cube of the orbital radius divided by the gravitational parameter of the Earth. Substituting the given radius yields a period on the order of thousands of seconds, and none of the printed values matches, so the item is defective.

questions.question_text: One of the following statements is a correct description of the charging processes?

options.label: A
options.option_text: During charging a neutral object by induction using a negatively charged rod, charge flows from the rod to the object.

options.label: B
options.option_text: When a neutral metallic sphere is charged by induction using a negatively charged rod, the sphere acquires a net negative charge.

options.label: C
options.option_text: When a positively charged object is momentarily brought into contact with a neutral metallic sphere, the sphere acquires a net positive charge.
options.explanation: When a positively charged object is brought into contact with a neutral metallic sphere, charge is transferred until both have the same potential, so the sphere acquires a net positive charge. Option C correctly describes charging by conduction, whereas induction does not transfer charge from the rod.

options.label: D
options.option_text: When a plastic rod is rubbed with wool, the two objects acquire a net charge of the same sign.

questions.question_text: A parallel plate capacitor is charged with a battery. The battery is then disconnected, and a dielectric material is inserted between the plates of the capacitor. Which of the following is correct about the effect of the dielectric?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The potential difference between the plates remains the same and the charge increases.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The charge on the plates decreases and the energy stored increases.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The electric field between the plates and the energy stored decrease.
options.explanation: After the battery is disconnected the charge on the capacitor cannot change, but inserting a dielectric increases the capacitance. Since the voltage equals the charge divided by the capacitance, the voltage and the electric field decrease, and the stored energy, which is charge squared over twice the capacitance, also decreases, option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The capacitance remains the same and the electric field between the plates increases.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct about the resistance of a conductor with a circular cross-section?

options.label: A
options.option_text: At a given temperature, the resistance of copper and silver wires of the same length and diameter is the same.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The resistance of the conductor increases as its length increases and its diameter decreases.
options.explanation: The resistance of a conductor is proportional to its length and inversely proportional to its cross sectional area, which depends on the square of the diameter. Increasing the length therefore increases the resistance and increasing the diameter decreases it, so option B is the correct statement.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The resistance of the conductor increases as its length and diameter increases.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The resistance of the conductor decreases as it is heated.

questions.question_text: A student wants to investigate Ohm's law using an ammeter (A) and a voltmeter (V) to measure current through and potential difference across a resistor R. Moreover, she employs a rheostat to vary the potential difference across the resistor. Which of the following connections is the correct set up of the circuit to perform the experiment?

Circular paths followed by two charges q1 and q2 moving with the same speed in uniform magnetic field directed into the page (X) are shown in the figure below. If the two charges have the same mass, which of the following is correct about the sign and the magnitude of charges?[IMAGE: img_4.webp]

options.label: A
options.option_text: q1 is negative, q2 is positive and |q1|<|q2|.
options.explanation: The circular paths of the two charges depend on the signs of the charges and their magnitudes, as shown in the figure. Without the figure the direction of curvature and the radii cannot be determined, so the item is defective and the first option is retained.

options.label: B
options.option_text: q1 is negative, q2 is positive and |q1|>|q2|.

options.label: C
options.option_text: q1 is positive, q2 is negative and |q1|<|q2|.

options.label: D
options.option_text: q1 is positive, q2 is negative and |q1|>|q2|.

questions.question_text: The primary coil of a transformer has 250 turns and its secondary coil consists of 1500 turns. If 220 V is applied to its primary coil, the voltage induced in the secondary coil and the ratio of current in the primary coil to the current in the secondary coil, respectively, are

options.label: A
options.explanation: The transformer voltage ratio equals the turns ratio, so the secondary voltage is 220 times 1500 over 250, which is 1320 V. The ratio of the primary current to the secondary current is the inverse turns ratio, which is 1500 over 250, equal to 6, so option A is correct.

questions.question_text: A diode is an electronic component that

options.label: A
options.option_text: is useful to convert a DC voltage to AC voltage.

options.label: B
options.option_text: allows electric current to pass through it in one direction.
options.explanation: A diode is a semiconductor component that allows current to pass through it in one direction only, when it is forward biased. It blocks current in the reverse direction, so option B correctly describes the behaviour of a diode.

options.label: C
options.option_text: allows the flow of current when its p-type region is connected to the negative terminal of a cell.

options.label: D
options.option_text: allows current to pass through it either from cathode to anode or from anode to cathode.

questions.question_text: Three forces, each having equal magnitudes of 10 N, are applied to an object on a horizontal surface. A force F1 makes an angle of 30° above positive x-axis, F2 makes 30° above the negative x-axis, and the third force F3 is directed along the positive x-axis. The magnitude and direction of their resultant force are, respectively

options.label: D
options.explanation: The x components of the two inclined forces cancel, leaving 10 N along the positive x axis from the third force. The y components of the two inclined forces each equal 10 sin 30, so the vertical sum is 10 N, and the resultant of 10 and 10 has magnitude 14.1 N at 45 degrees, option D.

questions.question_text: A student throws a ball vertically upward with a speed of 20 m/s. The maximum height reached by the ball and its velocity 3.0 s after it was thrown are, respectively

options.label: D
options.explanation: The maximum height of the ball is the initial speed squared divided by twice g, which is 400 divided by 20, giving 20 m. After 3 seconds the velocity is 20 minus 30, giving negative 10 m/s, so the ball is moving downward at 10 m/s, option D.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following units is NOT a possible unit of electric field strength?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Electric field strength can be expressed in newtons per coulomb, volts per metre, or joules per coulomb metre, all of which describe force per unit charge or its equivalent. Joule per coulomb is the unit of electric potential, not field strength, so option B is not a possible unit.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements does NOT describe magnetic nature of a material?

options.label: A
options.option_text: There is no a single magnetic North or magnetic South Pole.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Magnetic dipoles of a material aligned parallel when the magnetic material is placed in external magnetic field.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Magnetic molecules in a magnet will align when they are heated or hammered.
options.explanation: Magnetic materials lose their alignment when they are heated or hammered, because the thermal vibrations or impacts disrupt the aligned magnetic molecules. Therefore the statement that heating and hammering align the magnetic molecules does not describe the magnetic nature of a material, option C.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Magnetic molecules (dipoles) are oriented randomly when a material lose its magnetism.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct about conduction in semiconductors?

options.label: A
options.option_text: N-type semiconductor is made from half-filled shell atoms doped with accepter atoms.

options.label: B
options.option_text: P-type semiconductors have holes as minority charge carriers in the crystal lattice of the material.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The majority charge carriers in N-type semiconductors are electrons due to doping.
options.explanation: In an N-type semiconductor the majority charge carriers are electrons, which are contributed by doping the semiconductor with atoms having five valence electrons. Option C states this correctly, whereas acceptor doping produces a P-type material in which holes are the majority carriers.

options.label: D
options.option_text: When atoms with half-filled electrons are doped with atoms of five valance electrons, the majority charge carriers are holes.

questions.question_text: What is the acceleration due to gravity at an altitude twice the radius of the Earth? ($g_E$ is the gravitational acceleration on the surface of the Earth).

options.label: B
options.explanation: The acceleration due to gravity varies inversely with the square of the distance from the centre of the Earth. At an altitude equal to twice the Earth radius the distance from the centre is three times the radius, so the acceleration is the surface value divided by nine, option B.

questions.question_text: Four capacitors are connected in a capacitor network as shown in the figure below.[IMAGE: img_1.webp]The equivalent capacitance between terminals a and b in μF is

options.label: A
options.explanation: The equivalent capacitance of the network depends on how the four capacitors are connected, as shown in the missing figure. Without the diagram the series and parallel combination cannot be evaluated, so the item is defective and the first option is retained.

questions.question_text: A 64 V battery is connected to a series combination of 3 kΩ bulb and 4 kΩ electric iron. If the total current in the circuit is 8 mA, what is the internal resistance of the battery?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The total resistance in the circuit is the emf divided by the current, which is 64 volts divided by 8 milliamps, giving 8 kilohms. The external resistors contribute 7 kilohms, so the internal resistance of the battery is 1 kilohm, option A.

questions.question_text: A solenoid with 5000 turns and length 1m carries 15A of current. If no iron core is inserted in the solenoid, what is the magnetic field strength at the center of the solenoid?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is the permeability of free space times the number of turns per unit length times the current. Substituting four pi times 10 to the minus 7, 5000 turns per metre and 15 amperes gives three pi times 10 to the minus 2 tesla, option C.

questions.question_text: A small source emits sound waves which are spherical. The intensity of the sound wave measures at a distance r = 3.0 m from the source is 1.5 W/m². At what distance from the source would the intensity be one-fourth as much as it is at r = 3.0 m?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The intensity of sound from a point source is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the source. For the intensity to be one fourth of its value, the distance must be multiplied by the square root of four, so the required distance is twice 3.0 m, which is 6.0 m, option D.

questions.question_text: Consider a system of two point masses M1 and M2 with M1 = 0.5 M2. The two masses are located on the x-y plane as shown in the figure below.[IMAGE: img_2.webp]Which one of the following alternatives indicates the position of center of mass of the system?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The centre of mass of the two masses depends on their positions, which are given in the missing figure. Without seeing the locations of the two masses the weighted average position cannot be computed, so the item is defective and the first option is retained.

questions.question_text: Light ray is allowed to enter from air medium $(n_{air}=1)$ into water medium (index of refraction $n_w=\frac{4}{3})$ at an angle of $30^\circ$ with the normal to air-water interface (boundary). Which one of the following is correct about the ray of light?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The sine of the angle of refraction of the light ray in water is equal to 0.5.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The sine of the angle of refraction of the light ray in water is equal to 0.38.
options.explanation: Snell law states that the index of refraction of air times the sine of the incident angle equals the index of refraction of water times the sine of the refraction angle. Therefore the sine of the refraction angle is 0.5 divided by 4 thirds, which equals 0.375, approximately 0.38, option B.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The speed of the light ray in water is $1.33$ times that of its speed in air.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The speed of the light ray in water is $0.9$ times that of its speed in air.

questions.question_text: A fluid travelling over an object's surface exerts less pressure than if the fluid was static. This is a statement of

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bernoulli principle states that where the speed of a moving fluid is high, the pressure it exerts is low, so a fluid travelling over a surface exerts less pressure than a static fluid. Option A names this principle correctly.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following activities of experiment is NOT necessary to determine the specific latent heat of vaporization of water?

options.label: B
options.explanation: To determine the specific latent heat of vaporization of water, one measures the mass of water vaporized, the heating time and the power or temperature behaviour of the heater. Measuring the volume of the water is not necessary, so option B is the activity that is not required.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct about critical and boiling points of a substance?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The critical point and the boiling point of a substance occur at the same specific temperature and pressure.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Both critical temperature and boiling point of a substance can be increased or decreased based on the pressure of the surrounding.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The boiling point of a substance can be different based on the pressure of the surrounding whereas critical point occurs at one specific pressure and temperature.
options.explanation: The boiling point of a substance depends on the surrounding pressure, so it can change with the pressure. The critical point, however, occurs at one specific temperature and pressure for a given substance, so option C correctly contrasts the two.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The critical temperature of a substance can be increased or decreased based on the pressure of the surrounding whereas boiling point does not vary with the pressure of the surrounding.

questions.question_text: A 30 kg rigid object has a moment of inertia 45 kg⋅m2about its center of mass. What is the object's moment of inertia when it rotates through an axis 2 m away and parallel to the axis through its center of mass?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The parallel axis theorem gives the moment of inertia about a parallel axis as the value through the centre of mass plus the mass times the square of the separation. Adding 30 kg times 4 square metres to 45 gives 165 kg m squared, option B.

questions.question_text: Two coplanar forces acts on a uniform beam as shown in the figure below.[IMAGE: img_3.webp]The moment of force on the beam is

options.label: A
options.explanation: The moment of the forces on the beam depends on the magnitudes of the two forces and their distances from the pivot, which are shown in the missing figure. Without the diagram the net torque cannot be computed, so the item is defective and the first option is retained.

questions.question_text: Water flows at the rate of 500.0 cm³/s at small cross-section 5 cm². The larger cross-section is 25 cm². What is the ratio of the speed of the water at A₁ to A₂.[IMAGE: img_4.webp]

options.label: B
options.explanation: Using the equation of continuity the speed at the smaller cross section divided by the speed at the larger one equals the larger area divided by the smaller area. This ratio is therefore 5, which is not among the printed options, so the item is defective and option B, the reciprocal, is retained.

questions.question_text: An ideal monoatomic gas expands adiabatically from an initial volume of 2 liters at a temperature of 300 K to 16 liters of volume. What is the final temperature of the gas? (Use the ratio of specific heat capacity at constant pressure to that at constant volume to be 5/3.)

options.label: B
options.explanation: For an adiabatic expansion of a monoatomic ideal gas the temperature is proportional to the volume raised to the power one minus gamma. Using gamma equal to 5 thirds, the final temperature is 300 times the ratio 2 over 16 raised to two thirds, which equals 300 times one quarter, giving 75 K, option B.

questions.question_text: Consider a particle performing a circular motion around a circle of radiusrwith an angular velocity $\omega$ and the particle's projection on the horizontal diameter of the circle (between points Q and R) as shown in the figure below?[IMAGE: img_5.webp]Which one of the following statements is correct about the motion of the particle and its projection on $\overline{QR}$

options.label: A
options.option_text: The projection of the particle on $\overline{QR}$ swings between points Q and R with constant speed.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The circular motion of the particle can be taken as a simple harmonic motion.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The projection of the particle on $\overline{QR}$ demonstrates simple harmonic motion.
options.explanation: The projection of a particle performing uniform circular motion onto a diameter oscillates back and forth between the two ends of the diameter. Since its acceleration is proportional to and opposite to its displacement, this projection performs simple harmonic motion, so option C is correct.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The projection of the particle on $\overline{QR}$ demonstrates motion with constant acceleration.

questions.question_text: Air molecules vibrate in a pipe of length L closed at one end but open at the other. If the speed of sound through the pipe is$V$, which one of the following statements is correct about the resonance effects of vibration of air molecules in the pipe?

options.label: A
options.explanation: In a pipe closed at one end and open at the other, the fundamental standing wave has a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end, so the pipe length is one quarter of the wavelength. The fundamental frequency is therefore the speed divided by four times the length, option A.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The fundamental wave length of resonance is equal to $2L$.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The resonance frequency of the first harmonics is ${\frac{V}{L}}$.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The wavelength of the third harmonic is equal to $L$.

questions.question_text: A monochromatic light of wave length $\lambda$ passes through double slits separated by a distanced. If the path difference between the lights is a and being an integer (0, 1, 2, 3, ...). Which one of the following would be observed on screen behind the slits?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Constructive interference occurs when the path difference between the waves from the two slits is an integer multiple of the wavelength, so the waves arrive in phase and reinforce. Option B gives this condition, while half-integer multiples of the wavelength produce destructive interference.

options.explanation: Moving the box up the slope at constant velocity requires an effort that balances the weight component down the slope, mg sin theta, plus the friction force, mu mg cos theta. The correct order is "Are you talking about this tall, slim, pretty girl in the neighborhood?" because it follows standard question word order with the verb first.

options.label: D

questions.question_text: Gaga: Who is a famous Ethiopian singer you admire?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Many people admire Tilahun Gesesse. They say he is the king of Ethiopian music.

options.label: B
options.option_text: There are lots of famous Ethiopian singers. Truly speaking, it is a long list.

options.label: C
options.option_text: I think I admire Sudanese singers more than I do Ethiopians. You may hate me.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A famous Ethiopian singer I admire is Muluken Melese. He's wonderful.
options.explanation: When Gaga asks which famous Ethiopian singer the person admires, the response should directly name a singer. The answer naming Muluken Melese as an admired singer and praising him as wonderful answers the question directly, while the other options avoid naming a specific singer or talk about other matters.

questions.question_text: Birru: Shall we report the case to the deputy manager?

options.label: A
options.option_text: I think it would be safe if you report it.
options.explanation: When Birru asks whether they should report the case to the deputy manager, the appropriate response is to give an opinion on the matter. Recommending that it would be safe to report the case directly answers the question, while the other options ask irrelevant questions or make unrelated remarks.

options.label: B
options.option_text: What is the deputy manager doing?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Who knows, they could be friends.

options.label: D
options.option_text: What is the problem with them?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Which country in the world is attractive to you.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Which place in the world do you want to visit?
options.explanation: The dialogue is a conversation about travel, so the question Abush asks should be a general question about visiting places. Asking which place in the world the person wants to visit is the most natural and general opening question, while the other options are more specific or about liking rather than visiting.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Which place in the world do you like most?

options.label: D
options.option_text: Which country are you planning to visit?

questions.question_text: Policeman: Tell me what you saw happening at the scene of the incident.

options.label: A
options.option_text: The scene was full of people as Usual, it seems they don't have anything to do.

options.label: B
options.option_text: I saw a crowd of people some of who were aimlessly wandering around.

options.label: C
options.option_text: I was surprised to see this girl with beautiful long hair trying to talk to me.

options.label: D
options.option_text: First, he snatched her purse and in no time vanished into the village.
options.explanation: When the policeman asks what happened at the scene of the incident, the witness should describe the event. The response that describes how a person snatched a purse and vanished gives a clear account of the incident, while the other options describe crowds or unrelated observations instead of the event.

questions.question_text: Tsehay: You know, inflation has got out of control. It has become hard to afford bread.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Inflation? But there are people who have got money to burn.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Sure, but another problem is that you can't even find items you want
options.explanation: When Tsehay complains that inflation has made bread unaffordable, the response should continue the discussion about the cost of living. Adding that another problem is the shortage of items continues the complaint logically, while the other options change the topic or dismiss the problem.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The government started to control greedy business people in town.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Inflation is everywhere in the world. There is no need to worry about it.

questions.question_text: Boss: Sorry but novice employees have not been included in the scheme this time.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Why is it that you hate novice employees?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Novice employees are really hard working.

options.label: C
options.option_text: That is not clear. Can you explain why?
options.explanation: When the boss says novice employees were not included in the scheme, the employee wants to understand the reason. Asking for an explanation directly addresses the boss's statement, while the other options make accusations or ask about the scheme's start date instead of the exclusion.

options.label: D
options.option_text: When does the scheme start operation?

questions.question_text: Peter: I am suspecting myself of catching the current virus. Shall I go and take rest?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Where have you been to these days?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Oh no! I would advise you to get tested.
options.explanation: When Peter says he suspects he has the virus and asks whether to rest, the appropriate response is to advise him about his health. Recommending that he get tested directly addresses his concern, while the other options change the subject or comment on the name of the virus without giving advice.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Don't say that. The name itself is scary,

options.label: D
options.option_text: Do you mean COVID-19? It is a bad virus.

questions.question_text: Staff: Why hasn't the manager himself come? We wanted him to give him to give us explanation.

options.label: A
options.option_text: What are your major complaints? Let me know them in detail.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The manager wanted me to represent him at this meeting.
options.explanation: When the staff ask why the manager has not come himself, the response should explain the manager's absence. Stating that the manager sent a representative explains the situation, while the other options ask about complaints or make unrelated remarks instead of answering the question.

options.label: C
options.option_text: This is not the time to boycott. It is the time to work hard.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The main reason is that he has visitors right this time.

questions.question_text: Holala: Do you think life could have been possible without water?

options.label: A
options.option_text: We don't seem to value water because it is free.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Is there anything more important than water?

options.label: C
options.option_text: In fact, water is very useful for human beings.

options.label: D
options.option_text: No way! We would be dehydrated to death.
options.explanation: When Holala asks whether life could have been possible without water, the response should answer the question directly.
