Saying that life would not be possible because we would be dehydrated to death directly answers the question, while the other options make general comments about the value of water.

questions.question_text: Audience: Sir, can I ask a question before you go?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Finally, I would like to say to you all thank you for your attention.
options.explanation: When a member of the audience asks if he can ask a question before the speaker goes, the speaker is concluding his presentation. Thanking the audience for their attention is the natural way to end the talk and respond to the interruption, while the other options move on to new topics.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Let me move on to talk about the availability of raw materials.

options.label: C
options.option_text: I would also like to talk about our plan for the next fiscal year.

options.label: D
options.option_text: My last point relates to the benefits we could provide to you.

questions.question_text: Tilahun: Let's go and get them back by force.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Isn't it mad that violence has become so rampant these days?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Do you know the cause of the conflict! What went wrong?

options.label: C
options.option_text: How and when do you intend to go there? Let's know.

options.label: D
options.option_text: I see your point but force may not be a good solution.
options.explanation: When Tilahun proposes getting things back by force, the response should react to the proposal. Pointing out that force may not be a good solution gives a reasonable and peaceful reaction, while the other options ask about the cause or the plan without objecting to the use of force.

questions.question_text: Tigist: Of all jobs, why did you choose to be a hostess?

options.label: A
options.option_text: You don't know what it took me to become one.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Many of the girls in my city are also hostesses

options.label: C
options.option_text: I am interested in visiting different places.
options.explanation: When Tigist asks why the person chose to be a hostess, the response should give the reason for the choice. Expressing interest in visiting different places explains the attraction of the job, while the other options talk about the difficulty of becoming one or about other girls, which do not answer the question.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Sure. There are a lot of other jobs to take.

questions.question_text: Hussein: What do you mean by 'education is not financially rewarding?

options.label: A
options.option_text: I am saying that doing a degree is materially and physically demanding. Okay?

options.label: B
options.option_text: You know, there are so many people who haven't had any job for ten or so years.

options.label: C
options.option_text: What I'm trying to say is that most well-educated people are economically poor.
options.explanation: When Hussein asks what is meant by saying education is not financially rewarding, the response should explain the meaning. Clarifying that most well-educated people are economically poor explains the statement directly, while the other options discuss the demands of education or the number of years of study.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Come on. Imagine the number of years it takes to get a master's or a PhD. degree.

questions.question_text: Melkam: Do we need to send delegates and try to convince them?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Well, as far as I can see, there is no point in doing that. Just ignore them.
options.explanation: When Melkam asks whether they need to send delegates to convince people, the response should give an opinion on the suggestion. Saying that there is no point in doing that and advising to ignore them directly answers the question, while the other options ask about skills or make unrelated comments.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Convincing someone needs some kind of special skill. Doesn't it?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Who are they making all this trouble? They don't like to see us change.

options.label: D
options.option_text: We have been friends for generations. Why do they forget that?

questions.question_text: Kuku: BMC Company is going bankrupt and they have advertised to sell it.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Well. I would find this good for it. Better heads could come in to manage.
options.explanation: When Kuku says the BMC Company is bankrupt and advertised for sale, the response should comment on the news. Saying that better heads could come in to manage the company gives an opinion on the sale, while the other options ask about the company's age or mention another company without commenting on the news.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The only solution to this problem is unity among the people.

options.label: C
options.option_text: I was there a couple of weeks ago. How old is that company now?

options.label: D
options.option_text: KMD has done the same thing. That is not good news at all.

questions.question_text: Chimsa: I feel the atmosphere is murky around. Can't you sense some danger looming?

options.label: A
options.option_text: We hope things will improve soon. It is just a temporary problem.

options.label: B
options.option_text: That is the case in many parts of the country. How frustrating!

options.label: C
options.option_text: For how long is this going to continue? A week, a month, a year?

options.label: D
options.option_text: We really should finish this work today and leave immediately.
options.explanation: When Chimsa says he senses danger looming, the response should react to the feeling of danger. Suggesting that they finish the work and leave immediately responds to the sense of danger, while the other options hope for improvement or complain about the situation without acting.

questions.question_text: Risom: Have you seen Ghidey's new jacket? Very beautiful!

options.label: C
options.option_text: Sure. What is it made of?
options.explanation: When Risom praises Ghidey's new jacket, the response should engage with the topic of the jacket. Asking what the jacket is made of shows interest in the item, while the other options change the subject or express dislike for jackets, which do not continue the conversation naturally.

questions.question_text: Journalist: Welcome to our program of "Politics and Politicians".

options.label: A
options.option_text: I have been following this program regularly.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Thank you for inviting me. It is my pleasure to be here.
options.explanation: When the journalist welcomes the guest to the program, the guest should respond politely to the welcome. Thanking the journalist for the invitation and expressing pleasure at being there is the appropriate response, while the other options change the subject or ask about the program.

options.label: C
options.option_text: To be honest, I am not a politician deep in the heart.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Tell me. What is the program of "Politics and Politicians" about?

questions.question_text: Alambo: Elders of the village should impose sanctions on these young people.

options.label: A
options.option_text: How many elders do we have here? Do you know?

options.label: B
options.option_text: What did you say? I'm sorry, l'm not quite with you.
options.explanation: When Alambo says the elders should impose sanctions on young people, the listener may not have understood the statement. Asking for clarification by saying he is not quite with the speaker responds to the statement, while the other options agree or comment on young people without engaging with the proposal.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Young people have become out of control. It's sad.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Young people today? They don't even listen to elders.

questions.question_text: Titi: Shall I quit my education and get married?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In my view, you'd better get your degree first.
options.explanation: When Titi asks whether she should quit her education and get married, the response should give advice on the decision. Advising her to get her degree first gives a reasonable recommendation, while the other options make general comments about marriage or ask an irrelevant question.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Marriage is an important chapter in one's life.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Many girls are getting marked these days.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Did you fail the course you were taking?

questions.question_text: Hawulet: Tell me, what is it that offends Melat?

options.label: A
options.option_text: lf you tell her she is not beautiful, she'll get mad.
options.explanation: When Hawulet asks what offends Melat, the response should describe what makes her angry. Explaining that telling her she is not beautiful makes her mad directly answers the question, while the other options give general statements about people who offend her or things she does not like.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Actually, there are some people who offend her.

options.label: C
options.option_text: There are many things she doesn't like.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Melat is such a nice girl. I'll ask her.

questions.question_text: Evictees: We love you! We appreciate! Thank you for your kind assistance!

options.label: A
options.option_text: It gives me much pleasure to be of some help at this critical time
options.explanation: When the evictees thank the speaker for assistance, the speaker should respond to the thanks. Expressing pleasure at being able to help at a critical time is the appropriate response, while the other options talk about bringing evictors to justice or giving care, which do not respond to the thanks.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The agents behind your eviction will soon be brought to justice

options.label: C
options.option_text: I understand being evicted is very tormenting and disgraceful.

options.label: D
options.option_text: I hope you will give special care to children and the elderly.

questions.question_text: Obang: My computer has suddenly shut down. What has happened to it?

options.label: A
options.option_text: I hope that wouldn't be a virus.
options.explanation: When Obang says his computer suddenly shut down, the response should react to the problem. Hoping that it is not a virus shows concern about the cause of the shutdown, while the other options talk about other computers or ask about the computer's age, which do not address the problem directly.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Mine has never been like that.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Were you typing stuff on it?

options.label: D
options.option_text: Is that a very old computer?

questions.question_text: Ambassador: My son wants to get a driving license? What is the requirement here?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Excuse me but how many sons have you got, Mr. Ambassador?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Driving a car is not very difficult. He shouldn't worry as such.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Oh, I see. Driving a car is one of the dreams of young people.

options.label: D
options.option_text: As a rule, everybody would need to be 18 to get one in this country.
options.explanation: When the ambassador asks about the requirement for a driving license, the response should give the requirement. Stating that a person needs to be eighteen to get a license answers the question directly, while the other options talk about driving being easy or the dreams of young people, which do not give the requirement.

questions.question_text: Shashitu: Tell me, are there twins in your family?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Not at all. We have none.
options.explanation: When Shashitu asks whether there are twins in the family, the response should answer yes or no. Saying "Not at all. We have none" directly answers the question, while the other options confuse twins with sisters, brothers, or saying "I don't have twins" which is awkward for a family question.

questions.question_text: Until the world is fully vaccinated against COVID-19, global economy will not be able to resume activity.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Global economy will revive as soon as everybody is vaccinated against COVID-19.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Full vaccination against COVID-19 is necessary for global economy to resume functions.
options.explanation: The sentence states that the global economy will not resume until the world is fully vaccinated. This implies that full vaccination is a necessary condition for the economy to resume, so the option stating that full vaccination is necessary for the economy to resume functions conveys the same meaning.

options.label: C
options.option_text: We should all be vaccinated against COVID-19 for global economy to resume activity.

options.label: D
options.option_text: All nations should be vaccinated against COVID-19 for the global economic crisis to go.

questions.question_text: The next time you are about to express disapproval to your youngster, remember to stay aware and sensitive to her/his emotional needs.

options.label: A
options.option_text: If you have to make children stop what they are doing, do it without hurting their feeling.
options.explanation: The sentence advises being aware and sensitive to a child's emotional needs when expressing disapproval. This means that when making children stop something, one should do it without hurting their feelings, so the option that conveys this meaning without hurting feelings is the correct restatement.

options.label: B
options.option_text: If you don't like what your child is doing, ask her/him about her/his emotional needs.

options.label: C
options.option_text: If you want to prevent a child from doing something, use her/his emotional feeling.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Knowledge of emotional needs is important to guide a child in the right way.

questions.question_text: They heard it on the radio that the ________ where expensive electronic materials was on fire. I heard that the damage it inflicted is estimated at five million birr.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sentence refers to a place where expensive electronic materials were stored and caught fire. A warehouse is a building where goods are stored, so it is the correct word for the place that was on fire, while an auditorium, classroom and hall are not places for storing materials.

questions.question_text: I will never forget my stay in this company. I enjoyed working with you as my boss and I ____________ meeting you again sometime in my life.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The phrase "look forward to" is the correct expression to show that the speaker is happily expecting to meet the person again, and it is always followed by the gerund "meeting." "Wish" and "like" do not collocate with the gerund in this way, and "will wait until" does not fit the meaning.

questions.question_text: We will need to revolutionize our work culture. Everyone should be convinced that _____________comes through hard work and embrace for that. Otherwise, we remain poor forever.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The sentence says that prosperity comes through hard work, meaning that wealth and success are achieved by working hard. "Prosperity" is the correct word because it means success and economic well-being, while popularity, reputation and authority have different meanings that do not fit the context of hard work.

questions.question_text: Your room is still _________! Remember, I told you to get your stuff organized when I visited you last time. If I found the same next time, make sure you would be out.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The speaker is complaining that the room is not organized and wants the person to get their stuff organized. "Untidy" means messy and not in order, which fits the context perfectly, while suffocated, crowded and unclean describe different problems that do not match the demand to organize the room.

questions.question_text: It rained all of a sudden and brought the game to an unexpected ___________. The good thing, however, was that it stopped in fifteen minutes and the match continued.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The sentence says the rain suddenly brought the game to an unexpected stop, but the match continued after fifteen minutes. "Halt" means a stop or pause, which fits the context of a temporary interruption, while finish means the end, and circumstance and confusion do not describe a stop in the game.

questions.question_text: New schools have been opened in almost all corners of Ethiopia during the last two decades and _______ has increased by nearly ten-folds. We now have almost all school age children in the system.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The sentence says the number of students in schools has increased nearly tenfold since many schools were opened. "Enrolment" means the number of students registered in schools, which is the correct word, while education, quantity and schooling do not refer specifically to the number of students in the system.

questions.question_text: If you have to go abroad for your education, one of the things you have to be worried about is____________. You have to be sure of where you are going to stay before you leave this country.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The sentence says the traveler must be sure of where to stay before leaving the country. "Accommodation" means a place to live or stay, which is the correct word for the worry described, while facilities, provisions and stipend refer to services, supplies and money rather than lodging.

questions.question_text: We are fed up of people killing each other in this country. We want to see all ethnic groups with one another and lead a peaceful life as they once did.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sentence expresses the wish that all ethnic groups live peacefully together with one another as they once did. "Reconciled" means to be restored to harmony after disagreement, which fits the context of peaceful living, while compromised, intervened and mediated describe other actions that do not fit the sentence.

questions.question_text: Despite our resistance, he decided to quit his studies and take up music. He has now been doing it for two months and I don't even want to know the progress he is making in this regard.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The sentence says the person left his studies to take up music and has been doing it for two months. "Play" fits the context because it means performing music, so the sentence means he decided to play music, while start and major in do not combine naturally with music, and sing is not the correct verb.

questions.question_text: A very important lesson I learnt from Kokeb is that you don't have to rely on anyone. People respect you when you are self-sufficient, particularly financially.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The sentence says the speaker learned that one does not have to rely on anyone and that people respect self-sufficiency. "Depend" means to rely on someone for support, which is the correct word for the meaning, while entreat, trouble and beg describe different actions that do not match the idea of relying on others.

questions.question_text: Problems in this country are getting more and more complex from time to time. However, ways should be sought to overcome them and start thinking about development.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The sentence says ways should be sought to overcome the complex problems of the country. "Solve" means to find an answer to a problem, which is the correct word for overcoming problems, while overpower, handle and defeat describe different actions that do not match the idea of solving problems.

questions.question_text: If he is visually impaired , tell him he should learn how to use braille. Otherwise, things will be hard for him when it comes to reading and writing.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The sentence says that if the person is visually impaired, he should learn to use braille for reading and writing. "Disabled" means having a physical or mental condition that limits activity, and "visually disabled" is a correct term, while damaged, unable and weakened do not describe a permanent visual condition.

questions.question_text: lt is important to conserve some of our peace building traditions and pass them down to the coming generation. On the other hand, there are others that should be done away with.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sentence says it is important to conserve peace building traditions and pass them down to the coming generation. "Keep" means to preserve or retain, which matches the meaning of conserve, while appreciate, stock and enjoy describe different actions that do not fit the context of preserving traditions.

questions.question_text: Why are you worried about her? I know she is capable . Just leave her alone and you will see how beautifully she would do it.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The sentence says the speaker is not worried about the woman because she is capable of doing the task beautifully. "Competent" means having the ability and skill to do something, which matches the meaning of capable, while diligent, bright and clever describe hard work and intelligence rather than ability.

questions.question_text: Your persistent complaints have now started to irritate me. How come that your eyes cannot see anything positive of what is going on?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The sentence says the persistent complaints have started to irritate the speaker. "Annoy" means to make someone slightly angry or uncomfortable, which matches the meaning of irritate, while itch, disgust and prick describe physical sensations or stronger feelings that do not match the context.

questions.question_text: I beard a big bang in the middle of the night. Did the firearms in the depot go off or was it something else?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sentence asks whether the firearms in the depot went off with a big bang in the night. "Explode" means to burst with a loud noise, which matches the meaning of going off, while burn down, catch fire and heat up describe slower processes that do not produce the sudden big bang described.

questions.question_text: Ethiopia could manage climate change and HIV/AIDS infection

options.label: A
options.option_text: by slowing industrialization to reduce carbon emission.

options.label: B
options.option_text: by reducing rural residents through urbanization.

options.label: C
options.option_text: by using environment-friendly technologies and activities.
options.explanation: The question asks how Ethiopia could manage climate change and HIV/AIDS infection. Using environment-friendly technologies and activities addresses climate change directly, and combining them with public health measures addresses both problems, while slowing industrialization or getting foreign assistance alone are less effective and not the correct answer.

options.label: D
options.option_text: by getting assistance from the international community.

questions.question_text: According to the passage, the drought and famine of Wollo demonstrates the relationship between climate change and

options.label: D
options.explanation: According to the passage, the drought and famine of Wollo demonstrate the relationship between climate change and lack of governance, because the famine was worsened by the failure of the government to respond and manage the crisis. Infrastructure, peasantry and overpopulation are mentioned less directly, so lack of governance is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: According to the passage, resettlement

options.label: B
options.option_text: creates better environment for giving health services.

options.label: D
options.option_text: increases HIV/AIDS infection and environmental degradation.
options.explanation: According to the passage, resettlement increases HIV/AIDS infection and environmental degradation, because moving people to new areas spreads disease and destroys the environment through clearing land. The passage does not say resettlement helps technology, health services or food security, so the negative consequences are the correct answer.

questions.question_text: The resettlement and villagization programs implemented by the military government

options.label: C
options.explanation: The resettlement and villagization programs implemented by the military government were forced displacement of people, because people were moved from their homes against their will. The passage does not say the programs reduced degradation or raised productivity, so describing them as forced displacement is the correct answer.

options.label: D
options.option_text: helped in dealing with climate change.

questions.question_text: Studies made by Mz-Hasab Research Center confirmed a strong relationship between

options.label: A
options.explanation: Studies made by the Mz-Hasab Research Center confirmed a strong relationship between HIV/AIDS and climate change, because the two problems are linked through the displacement and poverty caused by environmental change. Education, agriculture and industrialization are not the focus of the studies, so the link between HIV/AIDS and climate change is correct.

questions.question_text: The authors think that to prepare the population to be able to cope with climate change one of those given below is a priority.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The authors think that to prepare the population to cope with climate change, mass education on climate change is a priority, because people can adapt only if they understand the problem. Regional cooperation, infrastructure and industry are important but are not the priority that the authors recommend for preparing the population.

questions.question_text: According to the authors, NAPA is

options.label: A
options.option_text: blamed for inefficiency and lacks responsiveness.
options.explanation: According to the authors, NAPA is blamed for inefficiency and lacks responsiveness, because it has not been effective in addressing climate change needs. The passage does not describe NAPA as redundant, doing fine, or successfully achieving its objectives, so the criticism of inefficiency is the correct description.

questions.question_text: Ethiopia has been experiencing the effects of climate change recurrently for many years. This implies Ethiopia has problems related to

options.label: A
options.option_text: agricultural resources to feed its people.

options.label: B
options.option_text: preventing causes of climate change and its consequences.
options.explanation: Ethiopia's recurrent experience of climate change effects implies that the country has problems preventing the causes of climate change and its consequences, because it cannot avoid the repeated damage. The passage focuses on managing and preventing climate change effects, so preventing the causes and consequences is the correct implication.

options.label: C
options.option_text: water resources to make portable water available to its people.

options.label: D
options.option_text: preventing infectious diseases such as HIV/AIDS.

questions.question_text: According to the authors one of those given below is recommended to help deal with climate change.

options.label: D
options.explanation: According to the authors, prioritizing environmental rehabilitation is recommended to help deal with climate change, because restoring degraded environments reduces the effects of climate change. Gender equity, modernization and urbanization are not the main recommendations, so environmental rehabilitation is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: In which of the sentences in Paragraph one is the concept of diversity best reflected?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The concept of diversity is best reflected in the sentence of paragraph one that describes the variety of backgrounds and characteristics among people. Among the given options, sentence three most directly mentions the differences that make people diverse, so it is the sentence that best reflects the concept of diversity.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is NOT implied in what the author states reasons for diversity?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The kind of family one comes from

options.label: B
options.option_text: The social origin of the individual

options.label: C
options.option_text: The kind of people one met in life

options.label: D
options.explanation: The author gives reasons for diversity such as the kind of family one comes from, the social origin of the individual, and the kind of people one met in life, which are all external influences. One's behavioral characteristics are not listed as a reason for diversity, so this option is NOT implied by the author.

questions.question_text: What is the author's viewpoint towards diversity?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Diversity is the major cause of war and other evils in the world.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The fact that we share the same planet works against diversity.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Life would have been much better if everything were uniform.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Without diversity, the world wouldn't have been interesting.
options.explanation: The author has a positive view of diversity and believes that without diversity the world would not have been interesting. The other options describe diversity as a cause of war, something that works against unity, or something that should be removed, which contradict the author's positive viewpoint.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following could most likely be a culture shock to a foreigner visiting Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Being invited to a meal where raw meat is served as a part.
options.explanation: Being invited to a meal where raw meat is served would most likely be a culture shock to a foreigner visiting Ethiopia, because eating raw meat is not common in many cultures. The other options involve common urban scenes that are less shocking to visitors, so the raw meat meal is the most likely culture shock.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Watching shoeshine boys cleaning shoes by the road.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Encountering young people fighting in the street.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Coming across people drinking Tella together.

questions.question_text: In Paragraph 3, the author says, "With the latter, it seems everyone loses out in one way or ..." What does "with the latter" show?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The phrase "with the latter" refers to the harmful way of dealing with differences, and the author says everyone loses out when differences are used to create disadvantages for others. Among the options, "creating disadvantages for others" best matches the meaning of the phrase in the paragraph.

questions.question_text: What does the word "this" in Paragraph 3, line 2, refer to?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The word "this" in paragraph 3 refers to breaking cultural barriers, because the author discusses overcoming the barriers that divide people. The other options mention cultural barriers themselves or answers to curbing clashes, but "this" points to the action of breaking the barriers, so this is the correct reference.

questions.question_text: According to the author, what is a possible advantage of diversity of human beings?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It has relived us of worrying about eating differently.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It has allowed us to have enough of what we live on.
options.explanation: According to the author, a possible advantage of diversity is that it has allowed us to have enough of what we live on, because different peoples produce different foods and goods that can be shared. The other options about eating differently or living on one part of the planet do not describe an advantage of diversity.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It has allowed us to live on one part of the planet.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It has proved a solution to reducing conflicts.

questions.question_text: Given the objective realities in the world today, what can we say about the author's remarks at the end of Paragraph 3?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Given the objective realities in the world today, the author's remarks at the end of paragraph 3 are rather realistic, because they acknowledge both the value and the difficulty of managing diversity. The remarks are balanced and truthful rather than pessimistic, critical or optimistic, so realistic is the correct description.

questions.question_text: What is the paradox about diversity being a blessing to humanity in enhancing equity in the various sectors?

options.label: A
options.option_text: To most societies today, their diversity has become a source of atrocity.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Most countries have exploited their diversity for peace and development.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Diversity has been among the source of unfair distribution of resources.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A lot of countries have used diversity as a basis of difference and hostility.
options.explanation: The paradox about diversity being a blessing is that a lot of countries have used diversity as a basis of difference and hostility, despite its potential to enhance equity. The other options describe the positive use of diversity or unfair distribution, but the paradox is the hostile misuse of diversity.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following, according to the writer, is NOT among the important tools used in fighting some of the common problems facing humanity today?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Using our diverse heritages in a positive way

options.label: B
options.option_text: Shaping others so they adore our perceptions
options.explanation: Shaping others so they adore our perceptions is NOT among the tools the writer recommends for fighting common problems, because it means forcing others to accept our views rather than respecting them. Using diverse heritages positively, respecting worship and tolerating differences are the tools the writer recommends.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Respecting the way other people worship

questions.question_text: You now seem to have lost all the excess weight. You look really sportive. __________ do you go to the gym?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The sentence asks how frequently the person goes to the gym, so "How often" is the correct question word. "How many times" would require a number in the answer, "Which place" asks about location, and "With who" asks about people, none of which fit the context of frequency.

questions.question_text: I say we should not question the competence of the new team. Each member is ________ those we had in the last round. They may have another problem and that should be studied.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The comparison shows that each member is equal in experience to those in the last round, so the correct structure is "as experienced as," which is used for equality between two things. "Much experienced as," "so experienced" and "very experienced as" are grammatically incorrect forms of comparison.

questions.question_text: We do not understand why he always comes so late. If he arrives on time like his friends, he _________ the opportunity to meet us and get the necessary assistance.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sentence is a conditional statement about a situation that is possible, so the second conditional structure "would have" is correct after "if he arrives on time." "May be having," "ought to have" and "will have" do not fit the conditional pattern with "if" and the desired meaning.

questions.question_text: I know one thing for sure. ________ hand in hand and worked for the unity of the country. If everyone goes his way, we get smaller and weaker for the enemy to engulf us.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The expression "It is time we joined" is used to say that something should happen now, and it is followed by a past verb form, so "joined" is correct. The sentence then continues with "and worked," matching the structure, while the other options do not use the correct "It is time" pattern.

questions.question_text: Have you heard that the police arrested Mr. Gwangu, _________ was our school Director? He may have involved in some corruption.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The relative pronoun "who" is used to refer to a person, Mr. Gwangu, and it acts as the subject of the relative clause "was our school Director." "That" can refer to people but is less formal, "which" is for things, and "whom" is the object form, so "who" is correct.

questions.question_text: Conflicts ________ take place between the pastoralists and farmers in this area every time the dry season comes. The government has to find a means of solving the shortage of water which is the main cause of the problem.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The sentence describes conflicts that regularly take place every time the dry season comes, expressing a habitual future event. "Will" is used to state a fact about what happens in the future, while "shall," "may" and "would" express intention, possibility or condition rather than a certain repeated event.

questions.question_text: The fundraising project in our kebele has been more successful than ever before. An insider told me they_________ raise 10 million birr in six months.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The sentence reports what an insider said in the past, so the reported action is expressed in the past form "were able to," which matches the past reporting verb "told." "Are able to," "would be able to" and "may be able to" do not agree with the past tense of the report.

questions.question_text: I believe you and there may not be any mosquitoes at this time of the year. But ________it is always good to be on the safe side? So, get the rooms sprayed with insecticides.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The speaker wants to confirm that it is always good to be on the safe side, so the tag question "isn't it true" is used to ask for agreement. "Can I just say that," "can I disagree" and "may I agree" are not natural ways to confirm a statement in this context.

questions.question_text: We learnt there is a very important conference you are holding towards the end of this month. _______as they could gain some knowledge?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Is it possible that our students attend it
options.explanation: The speaker politely asks whether it is possible for the students to attend the conference so they can gain knowledge. "Is it possible that our students attend it" is a polite and correct way to make the request, while the other options are less polite or grammatically awkward.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Shall our students possibly attend it

options.label: C
options.option_text: Our students could attend it please

questions.question_text: I appreciate what you said about the root causes of the problem and how we can possibly solve it. But for our record, _____

options.label: A
options.option_text: what is your name and where you come from?

options.label: B
options.option_text: could you tell us your name and where you come from?
options.explanation: The speaker politely asks for the person's name and origin for the record, so "could you tell us your name and where you come from" is the correct polite request. The other options use direct question forms or combine the two questions awkwardly.

options.label: C
options.option_text: where do you come from and your name, please?

options.label: D
options.option_text: are you willing to tell us what's your name and your address?

questions.question_text: Everything was in a mess _______ I arrived. It was not even possible to find out what had happened because she never came back.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The sentence describes the state of affairs at the time the speaker arrived, so "when" is the correct conjunction meaning at that time. "While" describes a duration, "since" expresses cause or time from, and "after" describes a sequence, none of which fit the moment of arrival.

questions.question_text: The area was ragged and mountainous. ____________, its weather was so harsh that we could hardly move around and see places.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sentence adds another negative feature of the area after describing it as ragged and mountainous, so "In addition" is the correct connector that adds information. "All along," "Even then" and "However" express duration, concession and contrast, which do not fit the additive meaning.

questions.question_text: The crowd kept rallying every day and the scene gradually started turning violent ___________ the people thought the government didn't take them seriously. Now things reached a point where they are completely out of control.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The sentence gives the reason why the scene turned violent, so "because" is the correct conjunction introducing the cause. "As a consequence of" and "Consequently" express result rather than cause, and "because of" must be followed by a noun phrase, not a clause, so "because" is correct.

questions.question_text: Tensions between the two countries seem to _________ from time to time but they would never fight. This has become a tradition and would only remain a war of words.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The sentence says tensions rise from time to time but never lead to war, so "heighten" is the correct word meaning to increase or become stronger. "Regenerate" means to revive, "worsen" is too strong for a tension that never leads to war, and "improve" has the wrong meaning.

questions.question_text: It is sad that COVID-19 has already caused a lot of damage to many countries of the world. _______ due to the vaccines administered all over the world, there are signs that the rate of infection is declining.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The first sentence states that COVID-19 has caused a lot of damage, and the second sentence gives the contrasting good news that infections are declining. "However" is the correct connector showing this contrast, while "But" is more abrupt, "On the contrary" is too strong, and "Surprisingly" does not show contrast.

questions.question_text: The school _______ a lot of job this year. This was mainly because every member of the school community was cooperative in supporting the administration.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The sentence reports that the school has accomplished a lot of work this year, an action connected to the present, so the present perfect "has done" is correct. "Had done" refers to a past before another past, "is doing" is ongoing, and "does" is a habitual present, none of which fit the completed work this year.

questions.question_text: We were all busy reading the fiction our teacher asked us to read when we ________ a huge explosion that seemed to be from upstairs. Many of us fell on the floor and it was as if we were all dead all dead.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The sentence describes a past event that happened while the people were reading, so the simple past "heard" is the correct verb form. "Would hear" expresses a past habit, "hear" is present, and "were" is the wrong verb, so "heard" fits the past narration correctly.

questions.question_text: If she________ persistent dry cough and fever, I would have called 8335 but that wasn't the case. It just looked like an ordinary flu.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The sentence is a third conditional about a past situation that did not happen, so the if-clause uses the past perfect "had had." "Has had" is present perfect, "would have" is used in the main clause, and "did have" is simple past, so "had had" is the correct conditional form.

questions.question_text: I have _______ things to do before I leave for the meeting. So, I have to lock myself in and work with no interruption.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The speaker has many things to do before the meeting, so "a lot of" is the correct quantifier for a large number of countable things. "Much" is used with uncountable nouns, "a few" means a small number, and "some" is indefinite, none of which express the large number intended.

questions.question_text: I am trying to move to Australia to live with my elder brother. I hope my life ________ be different there.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The sentence expresses hope about the future in Australia, so "will" is the correct modal to make a prediction about what life will be like. "Should" expresses obligation or expectation, "is going to" is used for planned events, and "might" expresses possibility, so "will" is the correct future form.

questions.question_text: I would be happy if we can meet this afternoon but _______ it is going to rain. If it doesn't, come to Eliana at 3:30.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The speaker thinks it is probably going to rain, so "it looks as if" is the correct expression meaning it appears that something will happen. "Very unlikely" and "I am sure" express opposite degrees of certainty, and "it is as though" is used for hypothetical comparisons, so "it looks as if" is correct.

questions.question_text: Are those two girls from the same family? They look alike and _____ I see them together, even in odd kind of places.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The sentence emphasizes how often the two girls are seen together, even in odd kinds of places, so a high-frequency expression is needed. Most of the time fits this meaning. Some of the time weakens the idea, while infrequently and hardly do contradict the intended frequency.

questions.question_text: I haven't started my homework yet but I________ it by 4:00 in the afternoon. Submission time is 4:15 p.m.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The time expression by 4:00 in the afternoon, combined with the 4:15 deadline, requires the future perfect tense to describe an action completed before a future point. Will have done fits this pattern exactly. The other options use incompatible forms such as will done or present and conditional constructions.

questions.question_text: Despite their longtime friendship, Biftu and Tola are not in good terms. _______________, they had a problem and now they have broken up. I don't know what had happened.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The speaker explains that Biftu and Tola are no longer on good terms. However, as I understand introduces an explanation while as I understand hedges the claim, matching the closing I don't know what had happened. The other options either add unrelated information or imply a return to an earlier interrupted topic.

questions.question_text: My son Scored A's in all the courses he took this semester. I am really__________________him.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The speaker is pleased because his son earned A's in all his courses. Proud of is the correct prepositional phrase for feeling pleasure in someone's achievements. Satisfied by, famous for, and keen on either misuse prepositions or do not express the proud-parent emotion described in the sentence.

questions.question_text: We all contributed what is within our reach ________________ help the needy children in our school. We bought them the stationery they needed for the whole year.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The clause explains the purpose of contributing what was within reach, namely helping needy children. So as to is the correct purpose expression before a base verb. So that to, because of to, and because to are all ungrammatical, so A is the only acceptable completion of the sentence.

questions.question_text: I can see your point of argument but _________________ the officials are honest when it comes to denouncing corruption. One of them was caught red-handed by the police a fortnight ago.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The second sentence reports that one official was caught red-handed, which supports doubt about the officials' honesty. I am not convinced that matches this skeptical attitude. It is unacceptable is ungrammatical here, everybody says that contradicts the evidence, and I don't doubt that affirms the opposite.

questions.question_text: Of all the stuff she bought yesterday, I like the books ______________ she got from the library. I started reading one of them and the story is really thrilling.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The clause she got from the library modifies the books, which are things rather than people. The relative pronoun which correctly refers to things. Whom refers to people, whose shows possession, and those cannot introduce a relative clause, so D is the only correct choice.

questions.question_text: I am glad we decided to let Birke move in because we are saving her life. ________________ , we are disappointing her mom who wants her around regardless of any risk that may come.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The speaker first gives a positive reason for letting Birke move in, saving her life, and then introduces a negative consequence, disappointing her mother. On the other hand signals this contrast between two sides. In this circumstance, consequently, and anyway do not express opposition between the two clauses.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Are Bajaj and motor cycles used for transportation in your village

options.label: B
options.option_text: What are the means of transportation in your village

options.label: C
options.option_text: Are horse and mules used for transportation in your village
options.explanation: The student replies Yes, then names horses, mules, and donkeys as the main means of transport. This answer fits a question asking whether horses and mules are used. Open-ended questions would not be answered with Yes, and the option about Bajaj and motorcycles is answered later in the response.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Can you tell us the means of transportation in your village

questions.question_text: Is he seriously threatening to kill you? Don't take this as a joke. _____________ need to report it to the police.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The speaker urges the listener to take the threat seriously and report it to the police. The thing is you need to report it is an idiomatic way to emphasize the main point. It is that you and it is important you are awkward, while you might makes the urgent advice too weak.

questions.question_text: They have now arrested the two brothers _____________ led the coup against King Bozambo of Jombaria. Rumors have it that they had seen hiding in a little village in the country.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The relative clause led the coup modifies the two brothers, who are people and function as the subject of the verb. The subject relative pronoun who is required. Whom is the object form, those cannot introduce relative clauses, and which refers to things, so D is correct.

questions.question_text: Our office wants to employ secretaries on a contractual basis but with a possible extension. The salary and other benefits are amazingly attractive. I encourage you to apply if you _________________ neatly type at least 60 words per minute.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The conditional sentence describes the ability required for the job, typing at least sixty words per minute. Can expresses ability and fits naturally after if. Would, may, and will express willingness, permission, or future intention rather than the capacity required, so D is the best choice.

questions.question_text: I am taking my own bed sheets with me ______________ the hotel doesn't provide clean ones. It is always good to be careful.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The speaker takes bed sheets as a precaution against the possibility that the hotel provides unclean ones. In case expresses precaution against a possible future event. If and if perhaps introduce conditions without the same precautionary sense, and just since is ungrammatical in this context.

questions.question_text: Unless there is something fishy about his business, Elias ________________ millionaire now. He just had that small kiosk when I left the village half a year ago.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Since Elias owned only a small kiosk half a year ago, it seems impossible that he is a millionaire now unless his business is dishonest. Can't be expresses logical impossibility with confidence. Must not be, may not be, and is not are weaker or incorrect for this strong negative deduction.

questions.question_text: We ________________ in the same office since 2010 but she has never acted like that before. She must have got out of bed on the wrong si1de.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The time expression since 2010 indicates an action that began in the past and continues to the present, requiring the present perfect tense. Have worked matches this structure. Are working and work do not combine with since, and worked belongs to the simple past without connection to now.

questions.question_text: The question is interesting. _________________ family do I like most? The answer is "Million's". They are very disciplined, close and cooperative. Everybody envies them.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The answer Million's identifies the family from a known set, so a choice between particular families is being made. Which is used for selecting among a limited group, while what asks for an open answer. Who refers to people, and whose indicates possession, so which fits best.

questions.question_text: I can see you are not very happy these days. ________________ what is bothering you?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The speaker politely asks to learn what is bothering the listener. Would you mind telling me is a courteous, grammatically complete request that leads naturally into what is bothering you. What is the problem and honestly, I want to know are less polite or incomplete, and the final option is unrelated.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It could happen but is it serious

questions.question_text: Nurses and doctors _________________ every three days to see the progress the migrants are making. Reports show that most of them are now recovering which is a good thing to hear.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The phrase every three days describes a repeated, habitual action in the present, requiring the present simple passive. Are dispatched fits this pattern. Have been dispatched is present perfect, were dispatched is past, and dispatched is active, so none suits the recurring present schedule.

questions.question_text: Where is the correct place to write the date in a formal letter?

options.label: B
options.explanation: In a formal letter, the date is written directly beneath the sender's address and above the recipient's address. Immediately after the sender's address is therefore the correct location. The other placements, before the recipient's address, on the same line, or before the sender's address, violate standard letter format.

options.label: C
options.option_text: on the same line as the sender's address

questions.question_text: When you write a formal letter, where would you write your address and contact details?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sender's address and contact details belong at the top of the letter in the Sender's Address section. The recipient's address, salutation, and complimentary close occupy fixed positions and do not contain the writer's own contact information. Therefore the sender's address is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Where would you write a request for an action in the format of a formal letter?

options.label: A
options.option_text: in the Body of the letter
options.explanation: A formal letter requests an action within its main content section, the Body. Requests for action belong in the body because it carries the purpose of the letter. The subject line, complimentary close, and salutation perform other functions and are not used to state a request.

questions.question_text: According to the passage, how does transportation play a critical role in the livability of a community?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Access to affordable transportation increases a community's participation in public life
options.explanation: The passage links livability to transportation by stating that access to affordable transportation increases participation in public life. Option A restates this relationship directly. The other options reverse cause and effect or add ideas such as recreation and economic growth that the passage presents differently.

options.label: B
options.option_text: When people obtain services, their economic growth is ensured

options.label: C
options.option_text: Access to recreation ensures the economic growth of a community

options.label: D
options.option_text: Participation in public life makes transportation affordable

questions.question_text: What is the key message conveyed about education in the passage?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The human mind is a better tool for advanced education

options.label: B
options.option_text: Advance in agriculture is fundamental to a country's development

options.label: C
options.option_text: Education is the basis of all aspects of development and growth
options.explanation: The passage conveys that education underlies all aspects of development and growth. Option C expresses this key message directly. The other choices highlight specific areas such as agriculture or health, or discuss the human mind, rather than presenting education as the foundation of progress.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Advances in health is possible due to fair public administration

questions.question_text: a. You can use it to talk with your friends or family, for example.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The paragraph opens with the topic sentence that a mobile phone is a very useful device, followed by the observation that everyone has one, an example of talking to friends and family, and a closing point about making calls in many ways. This order, b d a c, forms a coherent paragraph; the other sequences begin awkwardly.

questions.question_text: a. The first thing you need is egg.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The paragraph introduces the omelet as a favorite food, notes that it is one of the easiest things to do in the kitchen, announces the intention to show how to make it, and finally lists the first ingredient. This order, b c d a, produces a coherent recipe introduction. The remaining options place sentences illogically.

questions.question_text: a. Schools help us to be consistent, punctual, and obedient.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The paragraph begins with the topic sentence that school is where new things are learned, gives reading and writing as an example, adds the character benefits of consistency, punctuality, and obedience, and concludes with in short. This order, d c a b, is coherent; the other options start with conclusions or examples before the topic.

questions.question_text: a. They make their home in buildings, gardens, etc.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The paragraph starts by stating that ants are found everywhere, then describes them as very hardworking insects, mentions where they make their homes, and closes with their summer food collection. This order, b d a c, flows logically. The other options place the home or feeding information before the introductory statement.

questions.question_text: with here you return I or until either go wait can me

options.label: A
options.option_text: Wait until I can either go or you return with me here.

options.label: B
options.option_text: You can either go with me or wait here until I return.
options.explanation: The jumbled words can be rearranged into the natural English sentence You can either go with me or wait here until I return. This order keeps the correlative pair either or together, places here after the verb wait, and ends with the time clause. The other arrangements are awkward or change the intended meaning.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Until I return you can either go or wait here with me.

options.label: D
options.option_text: With me here you can either wait or go until I return.

questions.question_text: to want visit always I have Casablanca

options.label: A
options.option_text: I wanted to always have visit Casablanca.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Always I wanted to have visit Casablanca.

options.label: C
options.option_text: I have always wanted to visit Casablanca.
options.explanation: The jumbled words form the sentence I have always wanted to visit Casablanca. The present perfect with always correctly expresses a lasting wish. Option C places always between have and the past participle wanted. The other options misplace always or use the incorrect form have visit.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Casablanca I have always wanted to visit.

questions.question_text: people all idea to whose invite was these it

options.label: A
options.option_text: Whose idea was it to invite all these people?
options.explanation: The words form the interrogative sentence Whose idea was it to invite all these people? This is the only grammatically correct question with proper inversion of was and it. The other options either keep statement word order after whose or place it awkwardly, producing ungrammatical or unnatural questions.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It was whose idea to invite all these people?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Whose idea it was to invite all these people?

options.label: D
options.option_text: To invite all these people it was whose idea?

questions.question_text: Wheel chair user: Could you tell me where the computer center is on this building?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Oh sure, the 3rd room from here.
options.explanation: The wheelchair user asks for directions to the computer center, so the appropriate response provides the location. Oh sure, the 3rd room from here answers the question directly and leads to the user's thanks. The other options talk about the wheelchair, which is irrelevant to the request for directions.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Don't leave your wheelchair in my office.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Leave your wheelchair in my office.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Can I help you push the wheelchair?

questions.question_text: You : There is a job vacancy announced in our office. Do you want to apply?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Is that going to be a good job?

options.label: B
options.explanation: A jobless friend hearing about a vacancy would first want to know which position is advertised. For the position of what is the natural clarifying question before deciding to apply. Asking about salary or deadline is premature, and the first option does not respond to the offer to apply.

questions.question_text: You : I don't want people standing too close to me,_____

options.label: C
options.explanation: The speaker requests that people not stand too close and adds a polite conditional. If you don't mind forms a courteous request, and the stranger's reply No, I don't confirms a yes-no question. When you don't mind and do you mind change the structure, and if you mind inverts the politeness.

options.label: A
options.option_text: If I were him, I wouldn't study music.

options.label: B
options.option_text: If I were him, I'd study music further.
options.explanation: Misrak confirms Samson's statement with Correct and adds that the person has enormous musical talent. Samson's remark must therefore endorse studying music, as If I were him, I'd study music further does. The other options question or discourage music study and would not earn this agreement.

questions.question_text: Mother : I don't have much to complain about you, but one thing that ________

options.label: A
options.option_text: annoys me most about you is that you spend little time using the social media

options.label: B
options.option_text: strikes me most about you is that you have very good friends

options.label: C
options.option_text: pleases me most about you is that you always finish your work before bed time

options.label: D
options.option_text: bothers me most about you is that you spend much time watching TV
options.explanation: The daughter apologizes and promises not to watch any program until her final examination is over. This promise responds to a complaint about spending too much time watching television. Option D states that complaint directly. The other options praise her or complain about the opposite behavior, which the apology does not address.

questions.question_text: You: What does our new English teacher look like?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The question asks what the teacher looks like, so the answer should describe physical appearance. He's short, but well-built gives a complete overall description. Has grey hair also describes appearance but is only one feature, while speaking fluently and being thirty describe ability and age rather than looks.

questions.question_text: Instructor: I _____ some of the challenges you face as freshman students.

options.label: A
options.option_text: would like to give a lecture on
options.explanation: The instructor announces the topic of the session, and the students ask whether questions may be asked at the end. I would like to give a lecture on some of the challenges introduces this plan correctly. The other options are ungrammatical, describe rather than announce, or repeat the students' own question.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Can we ask questions at the end?

questions.question_text: You: Do you know that there are more girls in schools these days than there in the past?

options.label: A
options.option_text: This is due to the fact that parents are more aware of the need for girls' education
options.explanation: The colleague agrees that more girls attend school now and offers the reason that parents are more aware of the need for girls' education. Option A gives a plausible cause for the increase. The other choices are ungrammatical, contradict the statement, or give reasons that do not explain the change.

options.label: B
options.option_text: This is due to the fact that girls need more education these days

options.label: C
options.option_text: Yes, more boys than girls love schools these days

options.label: D
options.option_text: Sure, schools are much crowed these days than were in the past

questions.question_text: Journalist: Let's talk about marriage culture among this society. To begin with, could you tell us a few things about marriage culture here?

options.label: A
options.option_text: divorce is strictly prohibited by law in this culture
options.explanation: The host begins to describe the marriage culture with a complete statement. Option A is the only fully grammatical sentence, explaining that divorce is strictly prohibited. The other options end with unfinished connectors such as In other words and What I mean is, making them incomplete, although the phrasing is slightly awkward.

options.label: B
options.option_text: a man cannot have two wives. In other words,

options.label: C
options.option_text: a marriage is primarily arranged by go-betweens. This means a boy and a girl can get married if they wish. What I mean is

options.label: D
options.option_text: a boy and a girl can get married if they wish. What I mean is

questions.question_text: Father: Hana is a careful girl

options.label: A
options.option_text: whereas, here sister is more intelligent.

options.label: C
options.option_text: when her sister does not take risks?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The father contrasts careful Hana with her younger sister Lulit. Whereas her sister takes risks expresses this contrast directly, showing that the two sisters differ in their willingness to take chances. The other options contain spelling errors, take question form, or fail to contrast the two girls' behaviors.

questions.question_text: Teacher: _______, but the way you behaved in class.

options.label: A
options.option_text: What concerns me more about your exam is not what you did
options.explanation: The teacher says that the thing concerning him most is not the exam but the way the student behaved in class. Option A completes this contrast with not what you did, but the way you behaved in class. The other options mention behavior or scores in ways that do not complete the contrast.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Your behavior, more than you exam, was my concern

options.label: C
options.option_text: What concerns me more was about your behavior

options.label: D
options.option_text: What concerns me more was your score

questions.question_text: Teacher: Your brother is very honest.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The teacher says the brother is honest, using the verb to be. So am I agrees with this statement, meaning I am honest too. The pattern so plus verb requires am. So do I would need a main action verb, and me either and so I am are incorrect agreement forms.

questions.question_text: Journalist: How serious was the damage caused by the earthquake?

options.label: A
options.option_text: to illustrate the details of the disaster

options.label: B
options.option_text: as an example of the scale of the disaster

options.label: C
options.option_text: to summarize the scale of the disaster

options.label: D
options.option_text: to give you an idea of the scale of the disaster
options.explanation: The community leader gives thousands homeless as evidence of the disaster's severity. Thousands were left homeless, just to give you an idea of the scale of the disaster explains the purpose of the figure naturally. The other options suggest summarizing or illustrating details rather than indicating overall scale.

questions.question_text: Teacher: Do you plan a marriage before college?

options.label: A
options.option_text: No, but marriage is inevitable at some point in the future
options.explanation: Asked whether he plans to marry before college, the student gives a sensible negative answer while acknowledging that marriage will come later. No, but marriage is inevitable at some point in the future answers the question clearly. The other options are illogical, describe children instead, or give congratulations unrelated to the question.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Sure. I love to have two children when I get married

options.label: C
options.option_text: Congratulations! I'll be 20 ten days from today

options.label: D
options.option_text: Yes, but nothing precedes college at the moment

questions.question_text: Sports Journalist: Do you have an athlete to admire?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Don't you admire Darartu Tulu yourself?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Athletes work in competitive situations. Admire them.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Darartu Tulu is a courageous athlete you should admire.

options.label: D
options.option_text: I admire Darartu Tulu; she is such a well-behaved model athlete of all time.
options.explanation: The journalist asks whether the listener admires an athlete, and the reply begins with Yes. I admire Darartu Tulu gives a direct affirmative answer naming a specific athlete. The other options ask the journalist a question, give general advice, or use should instead of answering with Yes.

questions.question_text: Customer: I'd like to withdraw 5,000 Birr, please.

options.label: A
options.option_text: What is the interest rate on your account

options.label: B
options.option_text: Could you write your name here, please

options.label: C
options.option_text: How would you like the money
options.explanation: The customer has already stated the intention to withdraw five thousand birr. The cashier's natural follow-up is to ask how the money should be given, How would you like the money, referring to denominations. Asking about interest, a signature, or whether a withdrawal is wanted is redundant at this stage.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Do you want to make a withdrawal

questions.question_text: Teacher: Could you tell me ___________?

options.label: A
options.option_text: why an elephant, an intelligent animal, is your favorite animal

options.label: B
options.option_text: what intelligent animal is your favorite animal

options.label: C
options.option_text: why you chose an elephant as your favorite animal

options.label: D
options.option_text: what your favorite animal is and why you chose the it
options.explanation: The student answers It's an elephant and then gives the reason that elephants are intelligent. This matches a question asking what the favorite animal is and why it was chosen. Option D completes that question correctly. The other options ask only why or are ungrammatical and do not fit the two-part answer.

questions.question_text: Supervisor: _____? There are errors of all kind in your essay.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Could you tell me about your writing

options.label: B
options.option_text: Are there errors of any kind in your essay

options.label: C
options.option_text: Do you care about your writing
options.explanation: The supervisor points out that the essay contains many errors and implies that the student has not cared enough about the writing. Do you care about your writing fits this reproach. The student's apology and promise to proofread confirm carelessness. The other options are redundant questions or inappropriate remarks.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Am I going to hate your writing

questions.question_text: Friend: Can you guess where this huge soup mug was made?

options.label: A
options.option_text: could have been made in Spain
options.explanation: The friend asks for a guess about where the mug was made. The reply Not exactly signals uncertainty, so a speculative form is needed. Could have been made in Spain expresses this polite guess about the past. Was probably made and must have been made are stronger, and was made states a definite fact.

options.label: C
options.option_text: must have been made in Spain

questions.question_text: Friend: We haven't met Blen over the last six weeks, have we?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Perhaps we could ask her for dinner this evening
options.explanation: The friend notes that Blen has not been seen for six weeks, and the reply No leads to a suggestion. Perhaps we could ask her for dinner this evening proposes an action, and the friend's Good idea confirms a suggestion. The other options ask questions or state facts instead of making a proposal.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Does she have a very tight work schedule?

options.label: C
options.option_text: I met her last Saturday at the cinema

options.label: D
options.option_text: Blen is your best friend, isn't she?

questions.question_text: Bezawit: When do you wash your clothes? I think you haven't time in the afternoon

options.label: A
options.option_text: I think it is too cold to wash clothes

options.label: B
options.option_text: I have washed it when the sun rises

options.label: C
options.option_text: I will have washed it by the evening
options.explanation: Bezawit observes that Samrawit has no time in the afternoon and asks when she washes clothes. I will have washed it by the evening answers by using the future perfect to indicate completion before evening. The other options are ungrammatical, mention cold weather, or say it is not time, none of which answers when.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is not time to wash clothes

questions.question_text: Neighbor: Help! The building is on fire.

options.label: C
options.explanation: When someone shouts that a building is on fire, the urgent appropriate response is to summon the fire service. Call a fire brigade! matches this emergency. Smelling burning and needing a doctor are irrelevant, and calling an ambulance is wrong because the need is to fight the fire itself.

questions.question_text: Kedir: Do you like jogging?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Yes, I go jogging three days a week
options.explanation: The question asks whether the listener likes jogging. Yes, I go jogging three days a week answers affirmatively and gives supporting detail about jogging itself. Playing chess and watching football describe different activities, and being a gym member does not directly confirm enjoyment of jogging.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Yes, I'm a member of a gym

questions.question_text: Which of the statements below is true about cleaner-burning fuels?

options.label: A
options.option_text: They make many paper packaging unrecyclable

options.label: B
options.option_text: They affect the growth of trees and plants

options.label: C
options.option_text: They reduce the amount of sulfur dioxide produced
options.explanation: Paragraph one states that companies reduced the amount of sulfur dioxide emitted by switching to cleaner-burning fuels. This means such fuels cut sulfur dioxide output. The other options attribute unrelated effects, such as making packaging unrecyclable, affecting plant growth, or polluting landfills, which the passage does not say.

questions.question_text: Why is the process of manufacturing recycled paper better for the environment than the process of new paper manufacturing is?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The waste of the recycled paper manufacturing can be added to construction materials

options.label: B
options.option_text: The process does not require as much water as is required in new paper manufacturing
options.explanation: Paragraph five explains that manufacturing recycled paper uses less water, fewer trees, and causes less pollution than making paper from virgin pulp. This directly supports option B. The other options describe sludge, treated wastes, or construction materials, none of which is given as the environmental advantage of recycling.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The by-product of the recycled paper manufacturing process is sludge

questions.question_text: Which of the following is similar in meaning to " glossy " as used in paragraph 2?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Glossy describes paper that is shiny and smooth, as with the colored magazine inserts mentioned in paragraph two. Smooth is the closest synonym. Rough, harsh, and soft describe texture or feel but do not convey the shiny, polished quality that glossy suggests.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true according to paragraph 2?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The paper produced, particles and chemicals are the environmental concerns of the paper industry
options.explanation: Paragraph two opens by stating that particles and chemicals are not the only environmental concerns of the paper industry, and adds that the paper they produce is a growing problem.
