Option A combines exactly these three concerns. The other options add corrugated cardboard, cellophane, or fuels, which the paragraph does not list.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Chemicals, corrugated cardboard and the paper produced are the environmental concerns of the paper industry

options.label: C
options.option_text: Particles, wax-coated cellophane and chemicals are the environmental concerns of the paper industry

options.label: D
options.option_text: Cleaner burning fuels, chemicals and the paper produced are the environmental concerns of the paper industry

questions.question_text: Which of the following can be the best title for the passage?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The passage explains how manufacturing paper pollutes the environment, why recycling is important, what can and cannot be recycled, what recycled paper is used to make, and the benefits of recycling. Since recycling paper is the central theme running through all paragraphs, Recycling Paper is the most accurate title.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of non-recyclable material?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Paragraph two states that most junk mail is not recyclable. Junk mail inserts therefore fit the description of non-recyclable material. Newspapers, egg cartons, and paper bags are listed or implied as recyclable, so C is the only option naming a non-recyclable item.

questions.question_text: Recycled paper can be used to make one of the following products. Which one is it?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Paragraph three lists products made from recycled paper, including newspapers, egg cartons, paper bags, tissues, and food and clothing boxes. None of the four options matches these products exactly. Food packaging can is the closest to food boxes, so B is chosen even though the question is flawed.

questions.question_text: Why is paper considered an environmental problem by paper manufacturers themselves?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Much of the paper produced, if not recycled, is dumped into landfill
options.explanation: Paragraph two says the paper companies produce is a growing environmental problem because the majority of the sixty-seven million tons used yearly ends up in landfills. Option A states that much paper, if not recycled, is dumped in landfills. Option D omits the recycling condition, and the others describe different wastes.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Many paper companies release untreated wastes

options.label: C
options.option_text: Much of the paper produced cannot be recycled

options.label: D
options.option_text: Much of the paper produced is dumped into landfills

questions.question_text: Which word used in paragraph 2 refers to a site for sanitary waste disposal ?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Paragraph two uses landfill to mean a site where waste is buried for disposal, referring to where most paper ends up. This matches a sanitary waste-disposal site. Plain, particles, and cellophane name other items or ideas and do not refer to a place for burying waste.

questions.question_text: What does them as used in 'This makes them non-recyclable...' (Paragraph 2) refer to?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sentence This makes them non-recyclable follows the statement that many kinds of paper packaging contain wax or wax-coated cellophane. Them therefore refers to kinds of paper packaging. Newspapers, corrugated boxes, and food packaging are mentioned as recyclable and are not the direct antecedent.

questions.question_text: As used in paragraph 1, which word from those given below is similar in meaning to 'gorge' ?

options.label: D
options.explanation: In paragraph one, gorge means to eat greedily or fill oneself with food, as in the example of carnivores eating much meat at once. Stuff conveys this idea of filling oneself. Hunt, cheat, and gather refer to capturing, deceiving, or collecting, none of which matches the meaning of gorge.

questions.question_text: Why are 'voluntary vegetarians' mentioned in paragraph 5 in the passage?

options.label: A
options.option_text: to supplement the author's argument against the consequence of an increase in affluence
options.explanation: Paragraph five mentions voluntary vegetarians after explaining that affluence increases the amount of animal protein eaten in the average diet. Their existence shows that in wealthy societies vegetarianism becomes a matter of choice, reinforcing the argument about the consequences of increased affluence. The other options contradict the paragraph.

options.label: B
options.option_text: to indicate that economic necessity is no longer significant in choosing what to eat

options.label: C
options.option_text: to disprove the belief that there is an increase in the amount of animal protein eaten in the average diet

options.label: D
options.option_text: to support the author's argument against animal protein in one's diet

questions.question_text: Which of the following can be the best title for the passage?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The passage discusses vegetarianism broadly, covering evolutionary arguments, religious and enforced vegetarianism, voluntary choice in the West, and veganism. Vegetarianism therefore names the full topic. Enforced Vegetarianism and Voluntary Vegetarianism describe only parts of the passage, and Becoming a Vegetarian focuses on personal change.

questions.question_text: Which statement is true according to paragraph 4?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Followers of the Ethiopian Coptic church abhor the taking of life on more than 200 days

options.label: B
options.option_text: Enforced vegetarianism is common among eighteen percent of the world's population
options.explanation: Paragraph four discusses enforced vegetarianism in Africa and Asia and notes that about eighteen per cent of the world's population eats little animal protein. Option B links enforced vegetarianism to this figure, matching the paragraph. Option A is true but belongs to paragraph three, and the other statements contradict paragraph four.

options.label: C
options.option_text: In Africa and Asia, the cost of meat is seldom beyond what the poor can afford to buy

options.label: D
options.option_text: Vegetarianism has become a matter of individual choice in Africa and Asia

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the consequence of the spread of wealth in Europe and the West?

options.label: A
options.option_text: an increase in the amount of animal protein eaten
options.explanation: Paragraph five states that with the spread of affluence, the amount of animal protein eaten in the average diet is increasing. This directly identifies option A as the consequence of wealth in Europe and the West. The other options describe decreases or increased vegetarianism, which contradict the passage.

options.label: B
options.option_text: a decrease in the amount of animal protein produced

options.label: C
options.option_text: an increase in the mount of vegetable eaten

questions.question_text: Of the words given below, which one from paragraph 3 can be replaced by 'dislike' ?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Paragraph three says that Trappist monks abhor the taking of life and are entirely vegetarian. Abhor means to hate or dislike intensely, so it can be replaced by dislike. Prohibit means forbid, exploit means use unfairly, and impose means force, none of which matches the aversion abhor expresses.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a reason why vegetarianism eventually gained public acceptance?

options.label: A
options.option_text: increase in our understanding of the appetizing nature of meat

options.label: B
options.option_text: decline in the spread of a concentrated form of nutrient

options.label: C
options.option_text: increase in our awareness of the benefits of vegetarianism
options.explanation: Paragraph five lists the reasons voluntary vegetarians adopt their diet, including moral ideas, economics, and the belief that a vegetarian diet is healthier. Option C expresses increased awareness of the benefits of vegetarianism. The other options describe a decline in nutrients or in meat's appeal, which the passage does not support.

options.label: D
options.option_text: decline in the flavors and smell of meat

questions.question_text: Choose from those given below an example of the evolutionary argument referred to in paragraph 2.

options.label: A
options.explanation: Paragraph two refers back to evolutionary arguments made in paragraph one, which claim that human teeth evolved to deal with tubers and seeds rather than flesh. Foragers' teeth is the clearest example of this argument. Hunters' digestive system appears in the same argument but describes what humans do not have, so A is more direct.

questions.question_text: 'Disheartening' as used in paragraph 2 can be replaced with which one of the following words?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Disheartening means causing a loss of hope or confidence, as when people find giving up meat discouraging. Depressing is the closest synonym. Impressing, engraving, and interesting have unrelated meanings and do not capture the discouragement that disheartening conveys in paragraph two.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about carnivores as implied in paragraph 1?

options.label: A
options.option_text: They cannot eat tubers and seeds because of their teeth

options.label: B
options.option_text: They can eat much at a time and stay for days on that
options.explanation: Paragraph one says humans cannot gorge on meat and then go without eating for days as many carnivores do. This implies that carnivores can eat a large amount at once and survive for days afterward. Option B states this directly. The other options describe teeth, hunting, or daily diets not supported by the paragraph.

options.label: C
options.option_text: They hunt poultry and fish to get as much meat as they need

options.label: D
options.option_text: They have meat, poultry and fish as part of their everyday diet

questions.question_text: Both public and private authorities can manage transportation systems, which can involve maintaining and updating infrastructure to ensure the system runs smoothly.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Maintaining and updating infrastructure ensures the transportation systems run smoothly
options.explanation: The original sentence's key idea is that maintaining and updating infrastructure ensures the transportation systems run smoothly. Option A restates this purpose clause accurately. Option B wrongly makes infrastructure the managed item, and options C and D reverse the relationship between authorities, infrastructure, and smooth running.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Maintaining and updating infrastructure can be managed by public and private authorities

options.label: C
options.option_text: Maintaining and updating infrastructure ensures public and private authorities run smoothly

options.label: D
options.option_text: Public and private authorities ensure updating infrastructure runs smoothly

questions.question_text: In the West or in Europe, there is a great variety of food for people to buy if they want to.

options.label: A
options.option_text: There is no need for a great variety of food in the West or in Europe

options.label: B
options.option_text: People in the West or in Europe buy a great variety of food

options.label: C
options.option_text: There is no food shortage in the West or in Europe
options.explanation: The sentence states that a great variety of food is available for people to buy in the West and Europe. This implies that food is plentiful and that there is no shortage. Option C captures this meaning. The other options add claims about needing, buying, or wanting variety that go beyond the original statement.

options.label: D
options.option_text: People in the West or in Europe want a great variety of food

questions.question_text: Slapping small children on the face is a _____ act.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Slapping small children on the face is an act that causes pain and is morally wrong, so it is cruel. Cruel means causing suffering to others. Generous and gentle are opposites of this behavior, and compulsory means required, which has no relation to the action described.

questions.question_text: Clean air ______ the well-being of people everywhere.

options.label: A
options.explanation: Clean air supports and maintains the health and happiness of people, so it sustains their well-being. Sustain means to keep something in existence or support it. Maintains is similar but less natural with well-being, while differentiates and substantiates have unrelated meanings, making A the best collocation.

questions.question_text: Worldwide, a large number of organizations ______ children who have lost their parents in death.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Organizations support children who have lost their parents by providing financial help, which is called sponsoring. Sponsor fits the institutional context of the sentence. Foster usually describes families raising children, respect is unrelated, and offer requires an object such as help or support, so D is correct.

questions.question_text: Ethiopia is working hard towards strengthening its ______ relations with many countries.

options.label: A
options.explanation: Relations between countries that involve embassies, treaties, and representatives are called diplomatic relations. Diplomatic is the correct adjective. Automatic, dramatic, and aromatic share a suffix but have entirely different meanings and cannot describe international relations between Ethiopia and other nations.

questions.question_text: Many children are often reported missing; you should teach your child not to talk to a _______.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Since many children are reported missing, parents should teach their children not to talk to someone they do not know. Stranger names exactly this person. A smuggler trades illegally, a saboteur damages property, and a sniffer detects scents, so none of these describes the unknown person children should avoid.

questions.question_text: These days, many of our old traditions have nearly become ______. One such example is paying dowry in marriage.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Old traditions such as paying dowry are disappearing, so they have nearly become extinct. Extinct means no longer in existence, as with species or customs that have died out. Excise, extra, and external do not describe the disappearance of traditions, making B the only fitting word.

questions.question_text: School buses should always be driven by a/an _______ driver.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A person who has official permission to drive must operate school buses, so the driver should be licensed. Licensed means holding a formal permit to drive. Engaged, entrusted, and enthused do not indicate legal authorization to drive vehicles carrying children, so D is the correct adjective.

questions.question_text: The bad weather ______ our plan to travel to Dire-Dawa this afternoon.

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bad weather prevented the planned trip by interrupting it, so it disrupted the plan. Disrupt means to interrupt or throw into confusion. Dislodged means forced from position, disturbed means troubled or interrupted, and disappointed means failed expectations, none of which fits a plan ruined by weather.

questions.question_text: There was a cheerful receptionist at the hotel; she always enjoyed amusing her guests.

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cheerful describes someone who is happy and pleasant, and the receptionist enjoyed amusing her guests. Friendly is the closest synonym, describing a warm, pleasant manner. Thoughtful and hopeful describe consideration and optimism, while mournful means sad, the opposite of cheerful.

questions.question_text: Seventy is a compulsory retirement age in some developed countries. Do you mean they are retired to retire at the age of 70?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Compulsory retirement age means people are required to retire, so they are forced to retire. Forced expresses this lack of choice. Rebuked means scolded, guided means directed helpfully, and advised means recommended, none of which conveys the obligation that compulsory describes.

questions.question_text: The police arrested the man who often has his lunch at this afternoon and makes off .

options.label: D
options.explanation: Makes off means to run away quickly, especially after doing something, so the man leaves in haste. Option D matches this meaning. Snores and sleeps describe staying asleep, and leaves slowly is the opposite of hurrying away, so none of these fits a man arrested by police.

questions.question_text: The use of real life situations made the activity so interactive that everyone in the class loved it.

options.label: D
options.explanation: An activity that everyone loves because all participants take part is participatory. Interactive means allowing people to take part, and participatory is its closest synonym. Distributive, argumentative, and fascinating describe other qualities such as sharing, debating, or being interesting, none of which matches interaction.

questions.question_text: There is no point in complaining about his immature behavior; he is always.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Immature behavior is typical of a child, so a person behaving that way is childlike. Childlike means resembling a child in behavior. Premature means too early, young refers to age rather than behavior, and grown-up is the opposite of immature, making D the best synonym.

questions.question_text: Zeineb took after her mother; she was as intolerant of liars as her mother was.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Took after means resembled or was similar to. Zeineb looked and behaved like her mother, especially in disliking liars. Resembled expresses this similarity exactly. Resumed means continued, preserved means kept intact, and reassembled means put back together, none of which matches taking after someone.

questions.question_text: Regular exercises and balanced diet have many beneficial health effects.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Beneficial effects are ones that produce good results, so they are useful. Useful means helpful or advantageous. Benign means harmless, benevolent means kind and generous, and operational means working, so none of these captures the idea that exercise and diet bring health advantages.

questions.question_text: Our population size has tremendously swelled over the last few decades. Do you know why?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Swelled means became larger in size or number, so the population increased. Increased is the direct synonym. Jumped and leaped suggest sudden upward movement and are less precise for population growth, while escaped means got away, which is unrelated to a growing population.

questions.question_text: Our teacher ______ in any language other than English in class.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Let is followed by an object and a bare infinitive without to, so doesn't let us speak is grammatical. Allow requires to, make takes a bare infinitive, and like needs an infinitive or gerund, making the other options incorrect. Option D is the only correct structure for the sentence.

questions.question_text: There are two newspapers on my table, _____ of which has an interesting thing to read.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sentence refers to two newspapers, and neither of which has an interesting thing to read correctly uses neither for two items with a singular verb. No one and a single are not used with of which, and either would suggest one of the two rather than none, so C fits best.

questions.question_text: "Just a moment, please!" "The room _______," said the teacher.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The teacher asks the person to wait because the room is being cleaned at that moment. Is being cleaned is the present continuous passive, expressing an action in progress now. Has been cleaned is finished, is cleaned states a routine, and is cleaning lacks a passive object, so D is correct.

questions.question_text: ______ does it take students to do their bachelor's degree in Physics?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The question asks about the amount of time needed for a bachelor's degree, so How long is correct. How long asks for a duration. How many asks for a countable number, how far asks for distance, and how much asks for an amount, so only B fits the idea of time.

questions.question_text: We ______ study in small groups when we were in the secondary school.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The sentence describes a past habit of studying in small groups during secondary school. Used to expresses past habits or states and is followed by the base verb study. Have used to is ungrammatical, were used to requires a gerund, and had used does not fit the habitual meaning.

questions.question_text: Dad doesn't care much, but mom gets angry if I don't ______ her text message.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The correct collocation is reply to her text message, meaning to respond to it. Option B supplies the preposition to. Reply for is wrong, and the bare reply does not form a complete construction, so B is the only grammatical choice among the options.

questions.question_text: I couldn't hear what the teacher was saying during the lesson, but I think I ______ him to be louder.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The speaker could not hear the teacher and thinks it would have been reasonable to ask for more volume. Could have asked expresses this missed past possibility. Could ask and would ask describe present or future actions, and would have asked suggests a refusal that did not happen, so A fits best.

questions.question_text: I ______ hear a knock on the door. Are you expecting a guest at this moment?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sentence describes a present sensation of hearing. The modal "can" expresses ability or possibility in the present, so "I can hear a knock on the door" is correct. "Shall" and "will" are future auxiliaries, and "could" is the past form, none of which fit the immediate present situation described here.

questions.question_text: You will repeat this course ______ you work harder; your last two test scores were unsatisfactory.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The clause means the course will be repeated if the listener does not work harder. "Unless" means "if not", so "You will repeat this course unless you work harder" is correct. "Until" refers to time, "otherwise" requires a clause before it, and "if" would invert the meaning.

questions.question_text: Olang : I'm the only child for my family. How about you?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Standard adjective order places opinion adjectives like "beautiful" before size adjectives like "tall", and number words come first: "two beautiful, tall sisters". Option D follows this conventional order. Options B and C misplace the size and opinion adjectives, and A places the number after the adjectives, which is incorrect.

questions.question_text: Teacher : _______ do you often prefer to study?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The question asks about the time of day for studying. "What time of the day do you often prefer to study?" is the correct and natural phrasing. "Which time in the day" and "During what time of the day" are awkward or non-idiomatic, so "What time of the day" is the best choice.

options.label: C
options.option_text: During what time of the day

questions.question_text: ______ my grade was satisfactory, I feel I studied hard this semester.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sentence presents a contrast: the grade was satisfactory, yet the speaker still felt they studied hard. "Although" introduces a concession clause and is followed by a subject and verb, so "Although my grade was satisfactory" is grammatically correct. "Despite" requires a noun phrase, not a full clause.

questions.question_text: There is no point in sitting and complaining; _____, I study hard, score a good grade and join the department of my choice.

options.label: B
options.option_text: if I were you, I will

options.label: C
options.option_text: if I were you, I can

options.label: D
options.explanation: The structure "if I were you" is a hypothetical condition, so the main clause needs a conditional form. "If I were you, I'd study hard" uses the contracted "I would", which is appropriate. The other options use "will", "can" or bare "I" without a proper conditional verb form.

questions.question_text: _______, this noise will die down soon; surely, it has been a terribly noisy night.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The speaker expresses a wish that the noise will stop soon. "Hopefully" conveys this sense of optimistic expectation, fitting the sentence "Hopefully, this noise will die down soon". "Essentially", "sadly" and "truthfully" do not express the hoped-for outcome that the context requires.

questions.question_text: If you continue practising speaking English like this, you _______ speak it fluently very soon.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The sentence describes a future ability resulting from continued practice. "Will be able to" expresses future capability, so "you will be able to speak it fluently very soon" is correct. "Can" and "are able to" express present ability, and "shall" does not convey the developing future skill.

questions.question_text: You: I'm going to sell my car. What's your advice?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The friend explains that used-car prices have declined sharply. This fact argues against selling the car now for a low price. I disagree expresses this view. Agree would support selling, don't care shows indifference, and argue alone does not complete the sentence grammatically.

questions.question_text: I was _______ scared to go out in the dark alone. That is why I couldn't join you for dinner.

options.label: A
options.explanation: Absolutely is an intensifier used with strong or extreme adjectives. "Absolutely scared" is a natural collocation meaning very frightened, whereas "surely", "definitely" and "certainly" are modal adverbs that do not intensify the adjective in this way. The degree sense of "absolutely" best fits the sentence.

questions.question_text: She doesn't speak French very well, _______?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Question tags for negative statements use the positive form of the auxiliary. The statement "She doesn't speak French very well" is negative, so the tag must be positive: "does she". "Don't she" is grammatically wrong, and "won't she" and "will she" incorrectly use the future auxiliary.

questions.question_text: _____ you see the dictionary on the table when you _______ the office this morning?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The time marker "this morning" refers to a completed past action, so the past simple is required. "Did you see the dictionary on the table when you entered the office this morning?" correctly uses "did" for the question and the past form "entered" for the subordinate clause.

questions.question_text: Finally, I _______ marrying my classmate who I never talked to when we were in high school. Isn't this amazing!

options.label: B
options.explanation: The phrasal verb "ended up" followed by a gerund means to finally be in a situation or do something unexpectedly. "I ended up marrying my classmate" fits the meaning. "Wound up" is informal and less standard, "summed up" means summarized, and "chose" does not fit the phrasing with the gerund.

questions.question_text: The witness was _______ biased that whatever he said was unbelievable.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The construction "so + adjective + that" expresses cause and result. "The witness was so biased that whatever he said was unbelievable" is the correct pattern. "As much", "as such" and "such" do not combine with an adjective in this result-clause construction.

questions.question_text: I cannot afford to go out this weekend, I have _______ assignments on my table.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The speaker cannot afford to go out because there are too many assignments to complete. "Too many" is used with countable plural nouns like "assignments" and expresses an excessive amount. "Too few" and "very little" express insufficient quantity, which contradicts the meaning.

questions.question_text: I don't have a long standing acquaintance with Lojo, but I already feel that I _______ her for years.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The present perfect "have known" expresses a state that began in the past and continues to the present, matching "for years". "Had known" is past perfect, "knew" is simple past, and "have been knowing" is not used because "know" is a stative verb that does not take the continuous form.

questions.question_text: I have read _______  I did last year; it has been a terribly busy year for me.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Comparing quantities requires the comparative form. "Fewer" is used for countable nouns like "books", and "than" introduces the comparison: "I have read fewer books this year than I did last year". The pair "fewer...as" is incorrect, and "few books this year than" is ungrammatical.

questions.question_text: Unwise use of drugs can sooner or later _______ a serious ailment, if not death.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The phrase "result in" means to cause or lead to a particular outcome. "Unwise use of drugs can sooner or later result in a serious ailment" is correct. "Rises from", "arises from" and "results from" express origin or cause, which is the opposite of the intended meaning.

questions.question_text: She has just had a haircut; she _______ 20 in this new hair style, doesn't she?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The construction "looks as if she were" expresses an appearance that is contrary to fact, using the subjunctive "were". "She looks as if she were 20 in this new hair style" is correct. "Looks at" refers to looking toward something, "looks like" needs a noun, and "as if she becomes" is ungrammatical.

questions.question_text: I _______ the importance of hard work long before I joined university.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The past perfect "had realized" expresses an action completed before another past action, joining university. "I had realized the importance of hard work long before I joined university" is correct. "Had been realizing" is continuous with a stative verb, and the other options do not sequence the events properly.

questions.question_text: _______ English is much harder than speaking it.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Parallel structure requires matching the gerund forms. "Writing English is much harder than speaking it" pairs the gerund "writing" with "speaking". "To write" is an infinitive and breaks the parallelism, while "Getting writing" and "Having writing" are not correct verb forms for this sentence.

questions.question_text: My grade this semester is _______ than my first semester's.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The comparative form with "than" requires "better", not "good" or "best". "Much" intensifies the comparative: "My grade this semester is much better than my first semester's". "So much better" lacks the comparative structure, and "so good" and "best" do not combine with "than" in a comparison of two items.

questions.question_text: I have no time to spare! I will _______ myself a sandwich and get back to work quickly.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The verb "make" is used with a reflexive pronoun and a food item: "I will make myself a sandwich". "Cook" implies applying heat and is less natural for assembling a sandwich, "prepare" is possible but less idiomatic, and "do" does not collocate with making food in this way.

questions.question_text: You can borrow my new book, but you _______ show it to anybody in your class.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The speaker forbids showing the book to anyone, expressing strong prohibition. "Mustn't" conveys prohibition: "you mustn't show it to anybody". "Won't" expresses refusal, "don't" is a simple negative, and "needn't" means not necessary, none of which convey the required prohibition.

questions.question_text: Can you guess what _______ in this room now?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The question refers to something being done in the room now, requiring the present continuous passive voice. "What is being done in this room now?" uses the passive form correctly. "Is being doing" is ungrammatical, "has been doing" is active perfect, and "is doing" is active, not passive.

questions.question_text: Why should some people expect to be given food _______ clothes for free?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The conjunction "as well as" adds one item to another, meaning "and also". "Why should some people expect to be given food as well as clothes for free?" correctly adds clothes to food. "In accordance with" means in agreement with, and "in spite of" means despite.

questions.question_text: Look, _______ books, newspapers, shoes and socks scattered everywhere on the floor, why don't you keep your room tidy?

options.label: B
options.explanation: Look, there are books, newspapers, shoes and socks scattered everywhere uses "there are" to state the existence of multiple items. "Those were", "those are" and "these are" would require specific references, but the sentence merely points out that items exist scattered on the floor.

questions.question_text: I'm worried about my driving test, I think I _______ hear bad news again.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The speaker expresses uncertainty about receiving bad news. "May" expresses possibility: "I think I may hear bad news again". "Have to" expresses obligation, "will" and "am going to" express firm predictions, but the worried, uncertain tone calls for the possibility modal "may".

questions.question_text: Hana met Solomon in the corridor and asked him, "_______ for someone?" He answered, "Yes, I wanted to speak to Hilina; she isn't in her office."

options.label: D
options.explanation: The dialogue asks whether Solomon is looking for someone at that moment. "Are you looking for someone?" uses the present continuous for an action happening now, matching the immediate context. "You look", "Have you looked" and "Do you look" do not express the ongoing search.

questions.question_text: I don't have a car, _______, I don't even have a driving license.

options.label: A
options.explanation: Furthermore adds additional supporting information. "I don't have a car; furthermore, I don't even have a driving license" adds another related fact. "Incidentally" and "By the way" introduce digressions, and "Therefore" signals a result, which does not fit the additive meaning.

questions.question_text: Which of the following questions expects Jimma is 350 kilometers away from Addis Ababa as the best answer?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Is 350 kilometers the distance of Jimma from Addis Ababa?

options.label: B
options.option_text: How far is Jimma from Addis Ababa?
options.explanation: The answer "Jimma is 350 kilometers away from Addis Ababa" states a distance, so the question must ask about distance. "How far is Jimma from Addis Ababa?" is the correct question. "How long" asks about duration, and the "Is..." questions require yes or no answers.

options.label: C
options.option_text: How long is Jimma from Addis Ababa?

options.label: D
options.option_text: Is Jimma 350 kilometers away from Addis Ababa?

questions.question_text: Which one is _______, a lemon or a blueberry?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The comparison is between two items, a lemon and a blueberry, so the comparative form is needed. "More bitter" is the correct comparative: "Which one is more bitter, a lemon or a blueberry?" "Most bitter" is superlative for three or more, and the other options are ungrammatical.

questions.question_text: Who a theory scientist Big-Bang Stephen Hawkings the world the to introduced prominent

options.option_text: Stephen Hawkings introduced the world to a Big Bang theory who was a prominent scientist.

options.label: B

questions.question_text: In a formal letter the recipient's address will be

options.label: B
options.option_text: at the bottom of the letter.

options.label: C
options.option_text: in the top right hand corner.

options.label: D
options.explanation: In a formal letter, the recipient's address is written below the sender's address, on the left-hand side of the page. It is not placed below the recipient's name, at the very bottom, or in the top right corner, which is reserved for the sender's address. Therefore the recipient's address appears below the sender's address.

questions.question_text: If you happen to read a formal letter having a salutation which reads as "Dear. Mrs. Petya," which one of the following could be the most appropriate closing?

options.label: B
options.explanation: In formal letter writing, "Dear Mrs. Petya" addresses the recipient by name, so the complementary close must be "Yours sincerely" in British convention. "Yours faithfully" is used with "Dear Sir or Madam", while "Yours Truly" and "Yours Obediently" are not standard closings for this salutation.

questions.question_text: In a formal letter which of the following could be optional?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The subject heading in a formal letter is optional and may be included to summarize the letter's content. The salutation, recipient's address and date line are all essential components of a properly formatted formal letter, so the subject heading is the element that could be omitted.

questions.question_text: Mr. Solomon is the most dedicated teacher we have ever known for three major reasons. To begin with, he rarely comes to class without a thorough preparation on the day's lesson. Moreover, he is humorous while teaching which, in my view, a quality is that a good teacher is expected to have. The fact that he treats every student equally is the other feature of Mr. Solomon that we all admire.

options.label: D
options.option_text: As a result every one of us in our class wants to emulate him when we become teachers.
options.explanation: The paragraph describes Mr. Solomon's dedication, preparation, humor and fairness, and ends by summarizing his qualities. Option D, "As a result every one of us in our class wants to emulate him", provides an appropriate concluding statement. The other options contain grammatical errors or focus on only one of his qualities.

questions.question_text: The number of students taking this year's national exam is _______ that of last year. The figure is constantly increasing every year.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The second sentence states the figure is constantly increasing every year, so this year's number of students must be larger than last year's. "Greater than" is the correct comparison for the noun "number". "Fewer than" and "less than" mean smaller, contradicting the increasing trend.

questions.question_text: __________ you stop your being promiscuous, your chance of being affected by sexually transmitted diseases will be so high.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The sentence warns that if the person does not stop being promiscuous, the risk of disease will be high. "Unless" means "if not", so "Unless you stop being promiscuous, your chance... will be so high" is correct. "If" would require a negated clause, and "Could" and "Should" are modals that do not fit.

questions.question_text: The Wall of Harat _________ in 16 th century

options.label: D
options.explanation: The Wall of Harar was built in the sixteenth century, a completed action in the past. The past simple passive "was built" is correct. "Were built" is wrong because the subject is singular, "has been built" is present perfect, and "was being built" implies an ongoing past action.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Mekonnen Bar who is found at Addis Ababa, is famous for its cake.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Any animal which lives in a jungle, does not have to be considered as dangerous.
options.explanation: Option B, "Any animal which lives in a jungle, does not have to be considered as dangerous", is the most grammatical sentence. Option A misuses "who" for a bar and "found at" instead of "in", C wrongly uses "that" for a nonrestrictive clause, and D uses "whom" as a subject instead of "which".

options.label: C
options.option_text: AIDS, that is caused by a virus called HIV, has remained to be a fatal disorder for nearly three decades.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Nairobi whom is the capital of Kenya is the head for many international organizations.

questions.question_text: By this time next year, we _______ to university should we succeed in this exam.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The phrase "By this time next year" requires the future perfect tense for an action completed before a future time. "We will have been admitted to university" uses the future perfect passive correctly. The other options lack the future perfect passive form needed for this sentence.

questions.question_text: Scientists are expected to _______ research in the all-out effort of combating fatal diseases in the times to come.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The natural collocation is "do research". "Scientists are expected to do research" is idiomatic English. "Make research" is not a standard collocation, "have done" and "have made" are perfect infinitive forms that do not fit the future-oriented context of "in the times to come".

questions.question_text: Any student _______ misbehaves in class should be penalized.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The relative pronoun must function as the subject of the clause "misbehaves in class". "Who" is the correct subject pronoun for people: "Any student who misbehaves in class should be penalized". "Which" is for things, "whom" is the object form, and "who so ever" is nonstandard.

questions.question_text: If you have taken, in your previous institution, most of the courses that are given here you _______ be exempted from taking them again though I am not quite sure.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The speaker is not certain about the exemption, indicated by "though I am not quite sure". "Could" expresses possibility: "you could be exempted". "Should" and "must" express stronger obligation, and "had better" expresses advice, none of which match the uncertain possibility expressed in the sentence.

questions.question_text: It was _______ marvelous time that we spent with the visiting team last Sunday.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The construction "such + a + adjective + noun + that" introduces a result clause. "It was such a marvelous time that we spent with the visiting team" is correct. "So" would need an adjective alone without "a", and "such" without "a" is ungrammatical before a singular countable noun.

questions.question_text: I have prepared myself for this national exam. Thus, it is in my firm belief that I _________

options.label: B
options.explanation: The speaker expresses firm belief about a future event after preparing for the exam. "It is my firm belief that I will succeed" uses the simple future tense correctly. "Will be succeeding" is the future continuous, "have succeeded" is present perfect, and "am succeeding" is present continuous, all inappropriate for a future prediction.

questions.question_text: ___________ countries were ranked 1-10 as the most peaceful?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The question asks which countries were ranked, requiring an adjective questioning which specific ones. "Which countries were ranked 1-10 as the most peaceful?" is correct. "Whose" asks about possession, "In which" requires a different structure, and "What" is too general for choosing among countries.

questions.question_text: Had I studied very hard, I ________ last year's exam with ease.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The clause "Had I studied very hard" is a past unreal conditional, so the main clause uses "would have + past participle". "I would have passed last year's exam with ease" is correct. "Will have passed" is not used in conditionals, "would pass" is present conditional, and "would not have passed" reverses the meaning.

questions.question_text: Mekdes mostly finds it _______ to wake up early in the morning which leads her into unnecessary conflict with her school teachers.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The sentence says Mekdes finds waking up early difficult, which causes conflict with teachers. "Tasking" means demanding or hard work, so "finds it tasking to wake up early" fits. "Demotivating" and "confusing" do not describe difficulty with the action, and "crying" is not an adjective used this way.

questions.question_text: _________ her being late for the exam, the invigilator did not prevent her from taking it.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The phrase "In spite of her being late" uses a possessive gerund construction after "in spite of". "In spite of" is directly followed by a noun phrase. "Despite the fact that" needs "the fact that", "Even if" and "Even though" require full clauses, so "In spite of" is the correct choice.

questions.question_text: ___________ my car had run out of petrol, I had to park it on the side road and go on foot.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The car running out of petrol caused the speaker to park and walk. "Because" introduces the reason: "Because my car had run out of petrol, I had to park it". "In spite of", "Even though" and "Despite" express contrast, but here the clauses are in a cause-and-effect relationship.

questions.question_text: Zebiba has lived in Agaro _______ ten years.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The preposition "for" is used with a duration of time in the present perfect tense. "Zebiba has lived in Agaro for ten years" is correct. "Since" requires a starting point in time, not a duration, and "in" is not used with a length of time in this way.

questions.question_text: Unless a concerted effort is exerted in the fight against global warming, no _______ the most uncomfortable planet to live on.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The sentence describes a future result if no effort is made against global warming. The future simple "will be" fits the conditional structure beginning with "unless". "Will have been" is future perfect, "could have been" is a past conditional, and "might be" is less definite than the predicted outcome intended here.

questions.question_text: By the time one of the strikers of the Ethiopian national football team scored the last goal in the penalty shoot-out, the cheers and applauds from the spectators _______ like thunder.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The cheers and applause were heard, so the verb must relate to sound. "Sounded like thunder" is the correct collocation describing a loud noise. "Felt", "heard" and "looked" do not describe how the noise itself was perceived as thunder-like.

questions.question_text: No one should abuse his/her power _______ corruption.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The phrase "abuse one's power for corruption" means to misuse power for the purpose of corruption. The preposition "for" indicates the purpose or end, so "abuse his/her power for corruption" is correct. "To" is not used this way, and the other options are modals that do not fit.

questions.question_text: In his debut appearance to his club last week, Abdulkerim _______ two goals.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The sentence describes a past achievement in a specific situation, scoring two goals in the debut match. "Was able to" expresses successful completion of a past action: "Abdulkerim was able to score two goals". "Could" indicates general ability, "can" is present, and "might be able" is future possibility.

questions.question_text: Oh ! The time is now just 3:00 pm and if you go now, you _______ her in the office.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The speaker predicts the outcome if the listener goes now. "You will meet her in the office" makes a definite future prediction based on the present time of 3:00 pm. "Might meet" and "could meet" express weaker possibility, and "would meet" is conditional, so "will meet" is the best fit.

questions.question_text: I have visited several countries in my twenty years of tenure as a civil servant. Nonetheless, no country have I come across like Ethiopia which has _______ hospitable climate of all.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The phrase "of all" signals a superlative comparison among many countries. "The most hospitable climate of all" is the correct superlative form. "The best" does not modify "climate" appropriately, "the most better" is ungrammatical, and "the better" is comparative, not superlative.

questions.question_text: Ms. Adanech strictly warned her students that missing classes without having due reason will be costly. She is of the opinion that everybody _________ attend class regularly.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The sentence expresses Ms. Adanech's opinion, so "should" is the appropriate modal for advice or opinion. "She is of the opinion that everybody should attend class regularly" is correct. "Has to" and "must" express obligation, and "needs to" is similar, but "should" matches the opinion context.

questions.question_text: It is now just 4:30 pm. Most likely, by now the exam _______ finalized.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The time marker "by now" with "Most likely" requires the present perfect for an action completed up to the present. "By now the exam has been finalized" uses the present perfect passive correctly. "Had been" is past perfect, "has" lacks the passive participle, and "is being" is present continuous.

questions.question_text: It was announced yesterday that there would be a staff meeting tomorrow at 9:00 am and we all have been urged that no one miss it. I think, we _______ attend.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The announcement urges everyone not to miss the meeting, creating an obligation. "We must attend" expresses the strongest obligation. "Should" is weaker advice, "have to" expresses external obligation but is less forceful, and "do not have to" means it is not necessary, contradicting the context.

questions.question_text: Mr. Gole looks usually presentable with his dressing style. As an instance, the white shirts he casually wears make him _______ gorgeous.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The intensifier "quite" means to a considerable degree and modifies the adjective "gorgeous". "The white shirts he casually wears make him quite gorgeous" is correct. "Quiet" is a different word meaning silent, "unlikely" is not an intensifier, and "verily" is archaic and not used this way.

questions.question_text: The refugees from neighboring Somalia _______ temporarily _________ at Dollo-Ado refugee camp for a few months.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The sentence describes refugees currently sheltering at the camp, so the present continuous is appropriate. "The refugees are temporarily sheltering at Dollo-Ado refugee camp" uses "are/sheltering" correctly. "Were" is past, "had been sheltering" is past perfect continuous, and "have been sheltering" focuses on duration from the past.

questions.question_text: Last year at this time I _______ hard for the exam that I am taking right now.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The time marker "Last year at this time" refers to a specific moment in the past, requiring the past continuous for an action in progress. "Last year at this time I was studying hard" is correct. "Studied" is simple past, "study" is present, and "had studied" is past perfect.

questions.question_text: Ms. Letay _______ with the Ministry of Revenue for the last ten years.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The phrase "for the last ten years" indicates a period continuing up to the present, requiring the present perfect. "Ms. Letay has been with the Ministry of Revenue for the last ten years" is correct. "Had been" is past perfect, "was" is simple past, and "is" is simple present, all inappropriate here.

questions.question_text: It was his endurance that _______ the famous athlete Haile Gebreselassie break over twenty five records in his middle and long distance running.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The verb "made" is followed by the bare infinitive in the structure "make someone do something". "It was his endurance that made Haile Gebreselassie break over twenty-five records" is correct. "Allowed" requires "to break", "let" is possible but less formal, and "makes" is present tense, not past.

questions.question_text: Zeineb had to leave the meeting early, _______ she had an already settled appointment with her physician.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The subordinate clause explains the reason Zeineb left early, so "as" meaning "because" is correct. "Zeineb had to leave the meeting early, as she had an already settled appointment" is correct. "Despite" expresses contrast, "so long as" expresses a condition, and "in fact" introduces a clarification, not a reason.

questions.question_text: By the time the thunder exploded through the heavy rain, every one of us became _______ of it and tumbled out of our bed, trembled.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The phrase "became afraid of" is the natural collocation. "Every one of us became afraid of it" expresses fear of the thunder. "Frightened of" is possible but "afraid of" is the standard expression with "became", and "shocked" and "shaken" are not typically followed by "of".

questions.question_text: People who are promiscuous must know that they are in trouble _________, What I want to advise them is that it is high time for them to drop such a bad habit.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The speaker gives a conclusion or follow-up statement after warning about the danger. "So, what I want to advise them is that it is high time for them to drop such a bad habit" uses "so" to connect the warning to the advice. "So that" expresses purpose, and "As" and "Because" express reasons.

questions.question_text: In which of the following sentences does the order in which the adjectives have to appear look appropriate?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The thin person, who is wearing a pair of jeans tattered trousers, is Mr. Degu.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The short, thin person, with a pair of tattered jeans trousers, is Mr. Degu.
options.explanation: Option B, "The short, thin person, with a pair of tattered jeans trousers, is Mr. Degu", places the adjectives "short" and "thin" before the noun in natural order. The other options scramble the adjective and noun order, such as "jeans tattered trousers" or "thin tattered jeans pair of trousers", producing unnatural phrasing.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Mr. Degu, wearing a tattered pair of jeans trousers, which are thin and short is a person.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The person, with a thin tattered jeans pair of trousers, who is short, is Mr. Degu.

questions.question_text: I remember quite well what the anti-Apartheid icon Nelson Mandela once said, " _________ Africans are sinking, the rest of the world is letting them sink. When someone lets you sink, you must learn how to swim."

options.label: D
options.explanation: The quotation contrasts the situation of Africans sinking with the world letting them sink. "While" introduces a contrast between simultaneous situations: "While Africans are sinking, the rest of the world is letting them sink". "On the contrary" and "where as" do not fit grammatically, and "even though" implies concession.

questions.question_text: _______ our economy is showing a tremendous progress, the fact that there are millions of citizens whose livelihood is below the doldrums of poverty compels us to accelerate our fight against destitution and wretchedness.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The sentence contrasts economic progress with persistent poverty, so a concessive phrase is needed. "In spite of our economy showing a tremendous progress" introduces the contrast correctly. "Despite of" is ungrammatical, "However" requires a separate sentence, and "Despite" is less idiomatic in this clause structure.

questions.question_text: I have read _______ books on how to make life peaceful with a partner and have found them very useful.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The speaker has read an unspecified number of useful books, so "some" is the correct determiner. "I have read some books on how to make life peaceful" is correct. "Any" is used in negatives or questions, "much" is for uncountable nouns, and "no" contradicts finding the books useful.

questions.question_text: Andargachew: You are casually dressed. Your neck tie goes with your suit. Where is it from?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Great. It is made from cotton.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Thanks dear; it is from Turkey.
options.explanation: The question asks where the necktie is from, meaning its place of origin. "Thanks dear; it is from Turkey" directly answers the question about origin. The other options respond about material, loveliness, or size, which do not answer where the tie is from.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Wow, it is quite medium in size.

questions.question_text: Estifanos: Sarah, what are you planning for the coming year?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The question asks about plans for the coming year. "I am going to marry" expresses a future intention, which directly answers a question about plans. The other options use future continuous forms or mention business, but "I am going to" is the most direct answer about a plan for the coming year.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Emm...I am starting my own Business.

options.label: C
options.option_text: I will have registered for my second degree.

options.label: D
options.option_text: I will be having my own small restaurant.

questions.question_text: Dina: What you told me about the man, saying that "he spent his life hitch hiking" is not clear.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Let me say that again. He spent his life hitch-hiking.

options.label: B
options.option_text: let me rephrase what I just said. He spent his life asking for drivers to give him a lift.
options.explanation: The speaker wants to clarify the meaning of "hitch hiking", which means asking drivers for a lift. "He spent his life asking for drivers to give him a lift" correctly explains the phrase. The other options repeat the phrase, describe helplessness, or say he never had a bicycle, which do not clarify the meaning.

options.label: C
options.option_text: To make it clear, the man is best known for his being helpless.

options.label: D
options.option_text: In other words, he has never had even a bicycle. He rather prefers others to give him a ride.

questions.question_text: Interviewer: If in case I am employed, can you tell me about some of the issues which I should know beforehand about my job?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The fact that you are raising such an issue is indeed very nice of you.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is totally unnecessary to ask about this issue now.

options.label: C
options.option_text: What about yourself? Is there anything that you want(s) to know about you?

options.label: D
options.option_text: Occasionally you would have to stay in office after 5 pm and this would require your commitment.
options.explanation: The interviewer asks about issues to know before starting the job. The answer must provide relevant job information, and "Occasionally you would have to stay in office after 5 pm and this would require your commitment" gives useful details about the working conditions. The other options avoid the question or respond awkwardly.

questions.question_text: Jemal: Where do you think Ethiopia will be within a decade when its giant water reservoir, The Great Renaissance Dam Project, becomes fully operational?

options.label: A
options.option_text: I wonder if this iconic project is finalized on time, it will make Ethiopia the economic power house of Africa.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Ethiopia will have found itself being the water tower of East Africa.
options.explanation: The question asks where Ethiopia will be in a decade when the dam is operational. "Ethiopia will have found itself being the water tower of East Africa" uses the future perfect to describe the predicted state. The other options doubt completion or mention transport, which do not answer about Ethiopia's position.

options.label: C
options.option_text: I think Ethiopia will have faster water transport system thanks to this big dam.

options.label: D
options.option_text: I am sure that the dam will be completed within a foreseeable future.

questions.question_text: Molla: One of the disadvantages of staying unmarried is losing the love and comfort one may have to get from the marital bond. What else?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In addition to providing with love and comfort, marriage helps someone to have peace.

options.label: B
options.option_text: On the other hand, being married is believed to have several advantages.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The other disadvantage of staying out of marital wedlock is losing the social harmony that one may have to enjoy.
options.explanation: The speaker lists disadvantages of staying unmarried and asks "What else?". "The other disadvantage of staying out of marital wedlock is losing the social harmony that one may have to enjoy" adds another disadvantage of staying unmarried. The other options mention advantages of marriage or its disadvantages, not additional disadvantages of staying unmarried.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The other disadvantage of marriage is that it makes the two parties stay in it even after going disenchanted.

questions.question_text: Hailu: Do you know that in the Gikiyu clan, somewhere in the Southern Part of Africa, the female is the figure head of her family?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Funnily enough there should be so many clans of such a type where female domination is rampant.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Believe it or not, I have never heard the presence of such a clan in Africa.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Do you know the Gikiyu? I had once the opportunity of visiting them.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It may sound strange, but no surprise this time that there appear to be many societies which are matriarchal.
options.explanation: The speaker states that in the Gikiyu clan the female is the head of the family. The reply "It may sound strange, but no surprise this time that there appear to be many societies which are matriarchal" acknowledges and contextualizes the statement. The other options express disbelief or change the subject.

questions.question_text: Tourist: Can you tell me about the Ethiopian traditional costumes?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Men and women usually dress in the same way.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Well, the traditional clothes are mostly made of cotton.
options.explanation: The tourist asks about Ethiopian traditional costumes, and "Well, the traditional clothes are mostly made of cotton" provides relevant information about the costumes. The other options claim men and women dress the same, discuss permission for foreigners, or mention modern clothes, which do not describe the costumes.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Traditional Ethiopian cloth is allowed to be worn by foreigners.

options.label: D
options.option_text: No No, modern cloth is worn by the public during holidays.

questions.question_text: Interviewer: Given the employment opportunity, I want to be given scholarship opportunity having served for two years.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Can you tell me about your interests?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Would you mind telling me your position in your previous company?
options.explanation: The interviewee mentions having served for two years and requests a scholarship. The interviewer's question "Would you mind telling me your position in your previous company?" logically follows the mention of previous service. The other questions about interests, past scholarships, or future plans do not relate to the interviewee's statement.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Have you ever been given scholarship opportunities before?

options.label: D
options.option_text: Where would you like to be after ten years?

questions.question_text: Venus: Have you ever been to Gambela, Melat?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Ok, let me say it louder.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The question "Have you ever been to Gambela, Melat?" may not have been heard or understood, so "Please repeat that" asks the speaker to say it again. "Is that clear?", "let me say it louder" and "Let me put it another way" are replies of the original speaker, not responses to being asked a question.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Let me put it another way.

questions.question_text: Kiflom: In terms of size, which one is bigger, the Aswan Dam or the Great Ethiopian Renaissance Dam?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The Great Ethiopian Renaissance Dam is the biggest of all man made dams in Africa.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Aswan Dam is not as big as the Great Ethiopian Renaissance Dam.
options.explanation: The question asks which dam is bigger. "The Aswan Dam is not as big as the Great Ethiopian Renaissance Dam" answers that the GERD is bigger. The other options mention being the biggest in Africa, being as expensive, or water capacity, which do not directly compare the two dams' sizes.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The Great Ethiopian Renaissance Dam is as expensive as that of the Aswan Dam.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The Great Ethiopian Renaissance Dam can consist of 74 billion cubic liters of water.

questions.question_text: Wario: I wish you could tell me as to what I should do to be a successful entrepreneur.

options.label: A
options.option_text: I would say that success cannot be achieved only through dreaming.
options.explanation: Wario asks what to do to be a successful entrepreneur. "I would say that success cannot be achieved only through dreaming" gives practical advice about working toward success. The other options question the difficulty, suggest remaining an employee, or recommend life skills training, which are less direct responses to the question.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Is it hard to be an entrepreneur?

options.label: C
options.option_text: I strongly suggest that you become an employee only.

options.label: D
options.option_text: To give you an idea, it is better to take part in life skills trainings.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Do you think it is possible that self-automated cars will litter the roads of Addis Ababa?
options.explanation: The dialogue is incomplete, with only Zuber's question line present and the reply missing from the source data. Without the response, the exact question cannot be verified, so the first option is retained as a best-effort answer and this question is flagged for missing context.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Do you think modernizing our Agriculture should be our priority in the future?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Are you of the opinion that cell phones are improving the lives of Ethiopians?

options.option_text: Would it be healthy to think of everything in terms of personal agenda?

questions.question_text: Semira: Do you think technology-led economy will take the upper hand in Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: There is a good chance for it to prevail, I think.
options.explanation: The question asks whether a technology-led economy will prevail in Ethiopia. "There is a good chance for it to prevail, I think" directly gives an opinion that it likely will. The other options express regret, conditionality, or surprise, which do not directly answer the question about the likelihood.

options.label: B
options.option_text: I wish it had been like that, but the fact was totally different.

options.label: C
options.option_text: If so, Ethiopia will get the chance to liberalize its economy.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Really? If so, we must be lucky.

questions.question_text: Journalist: Can you tell me what happened to your country in recent times?

options.label: A
options.option_text: the fact that it was banned from its AU membership.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the reason why my country was banned from AU's membership.

options.label: C
options.option_text: for this reason, AU suspended my country from membership.
options.explanation: The journalist asks what happened to the country recently. "For this reason, AU suspended my country from membership" provides a statement of what happened. The other options begin with "the fact that", "the reason why" or "thanks to that", which are incomplete phrases that do not form a complete answer.

options.label: D
options.option_text: thanks to that it could have been suspended from its AU membership.

questions.question_text: Student: I was a bit sick. As a result, I missed the final exam.

options.label: A
options.option_text: These days, many students are not appearing for an exam.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Whether you like it or not you should have fallen ill.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Even if that is so; you are expected to produce an evidence for it.
options.explanation: The student explains that illness caused missing the exam. The reply "Even if that is so; you are expected to produce an evidence for it" acknowledges the excuse but notes that evidence is required. The other options discuss other students, ask what the student is doing, or say the student should have fallen ill, which do not respond appropriately.

questions.question_text: TadeTech: Look over there! Is that part of the plane that got crashed at Bishofu some years back?

options.label: A
options.option_text: neither looks part of a plane

options.label: B
options.option_text: looks like part of a helicopter

options.label: C
options.option_text: looks like part of a plane
options.explanation: The question asks whether the object is part of the crashed plane. "Looks like part of a plane" responds that it appears to be plane wreckage. The other options mention helicopters or use "neither" and "either" incorrectly, while "looks like part of a plane" is the natural affirmative response to the question.

options.label: D
options.option_text: looks like part of a helicopter either

questions.question_text: From the excerpts below A-D, identify the one stated in a formal register

options.label: A
options.option_text: Yeah, I am okay. And you?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Good morning, Mr. Tsegaye. How are you today?
options.explanation: The formal register uses polite, respectful language with titles and surnames. "Good morning, Mr. Tsegaye. How are you today?" is the only option in formal register. The other options use informal greetings like "Yeah, I am okay", "Hi Samson" or casual questions about plans, which are informal.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Are you going to Friendship Park tomorrow?

questions.question_text: Zemzem: Do you have any idea as to why the yesterday's board of director's meeting was cancelled?

options.label: A
options.option_text: I wish it had not been cancelled.

options.label: B
options.option_text: I am sorry. I don't know.
options.explanation: The question asks whether the listener has any idea why the meeting was cancelled. "I am sorry. I don't know" politely states that the listener has no information. The other options express wishes about cancellation or deny that it happened, which do not answer the question about the reason.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Sorry, it should have been cancelled.

questions.question_text: Osman: What do you think could be the reason for the environmental degradation that we are witnessing these days?

options.label: A
options.option_text: this is due to human being's unnecessary intervention in the environment
options.explanation: The question asks for the reason behind environmental degradation. Only option A identifies a cause: unnecessary human intervention in the environment. The other options describe consequences or solutions rather than reasons, so they do not directly answer the question asked.

options.label: B
options.option_text: such a disaster can be halted only through a concerted effort

options.label: C
options.option_text: environmental degradation is the serious reason for the prevalence of destitution

options.label: D
options.option_text: drought and famine are its adverse consequences.

questions.question_text: School Principal: Dear teachers, what do you think should we do to help our students succeed in the upcoming National Exam?

options.label: A
options.option_text: I believe that it is not that difficult and helping our students is our moral obligation.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Personally, I would suggest that they be encouraged to study hard by their own only.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Personally, I think we can help by providing those trainings on how to become self-regulated and self-directed learners.
options.explanation: The principal asks what teachers should do to help students succeed. Option C directly answers by proposing concrete help: providing training on becoming self-regulated and self-directed learners. The other options either avoid the question, make general statements about obligation, or use ungrammatical phrasing.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Unless students are helped, it is less likely for the majority to succeed only by their own effort.

questions.question_text: Firtuna: Did you attend the 12th anniversary of The Great Ethiopian Renaissance Dam celebrated at Guba last April?

options.label: A
options.option_text: I wish I had, but unfortunately, I was out of Ethiopia.
options.explanation: Firtuna asks whether you attended an event in the past. Option A correctly uses the past perfect wish form, I wish I had, to express regret about not attending. Option D wrongly uses I wish I have, and options B and C contradict yes with past intentions.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Oh, yes I was about to attend it.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Oh! Yes, I could have attended it.

options.label: D
options.option_text: I wish I have attended it, but couldn't make it because of personal reasons.

questions.question_text: Ezra: When are you planning to marry this year or next year?

options.label: A
options.option_text: I am going to marry, whenever I get enough money.

options.label: B
options.option_text: I will have got married next year
options.explanation: The question asks when the speaker plans to marry. Only option B addresses the timing directly, indicating the marriage will be completed by next year. The others dodge the question, use unclear conditions, or introduce irrelevant details, so B is the best available choice despite awkward phrasing.

options.label: C
options.option_text: I am going to have my initial ceremony whenever I give birth to my first child.

options.label: D
options.option_text: I am going to marry unless I turn twenty five.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Would you mind telling me your position in your previous company?
options.explanation: The stem provides an interviewer's line but no reply or context. Among the options, option A is the most typical polite job-interview question, seeking specific information about the candidate's previous position. Without surrounding dialogue, the intended answer cannot be determined with certainty, so A is selected as the best general choice.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Can you tell me about your interests?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Where would you like to be after ten years?

options.label: D
options.option_text: Have you ever been given scholarship opportunities before?

questions.question_text: Asmerom: I am now just 17, and ready to seat for this forthcoming National Exam.

options.label: A
options.option_text: By this time next year, you may have joined grade 12.

options.label: B
options.option_text: By the end of this year, you would have passed the exam and joined freshman.

options.label: C
options.option_text: By the time you are 21 or so, you will graduate from a university.
options.explanation: Asmerom says he is seventeen and about to sit the national exam, so he will join university in the coming year. Option C gives a grammatically sound future prediction of graduation around age twenty-one. Option D has the right age logic but misuses the future perfect tense, making C the best choice.

options.label: D
options.option_text: By the time you join university, you will have been only 18.

questions.question_text: Physician: Your Blood Pressure is becoming a bit higher than what is known to be normal.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Dr. If you like me, I hope you will advise me on what to do and what not to do.
options.explanation: The physician has just informed the patient that his blood pressure is rising. The natural patient response is to request guidance, as option A does by asking for advice on what to do and what not to do. The other options do not respond appropriately to the diagnosis.

options.label: B
options.option_text: I hope you will not ask me to stop sipping some alcoholic drinks.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Some times this happens, and no doubt it will come to its normalcy after a few days.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Had I known that I could have called and asked you for some piece of advice.

questions.question_text: Dr. Getachew gave us a good lecture yesterday, and I wish you had been present. The fact that Dr. Getachew would give us a good lecture was in my wish and accordingly he gave us attend.

options.label: A
options.option_text: The fact that Dr. Getachew would give us a good lecture was in my wish and accordingly he gave us attend.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Dr. Getachew was able to deliver us a nice lecture yesterday that was indeed as per my dream, and the fact that you attended it was nice of you.

options.label: C
options.option_text: We were given an interesting lecture yesterday by Dr. Getachew, but unfortunately you missed it.
options.explanation: The original sentence reports that Dr. Getachew gave a good lecture yesterday and the listener unfortunately was not present. Option C restates this meaning clearly and accurately. The other options distort the facts, claiming the listener attended or that the lecture was only a wish.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It was in my wish that Dr. Getachew could have given us a good lecture and you could have attended it, but neither of you did so.
