questions.question_text: All the students, but Shemsu had already finalized the project by the time the instructor asked them to submit it.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Except Shemsu who did not complete his project assignment, the rest were ready to submit it when asked to do so by their instructor.
options.explanation: The original sentence means everyone except Shemsu had finished the project before the instructor asked for submission. Option A captures this exactly: Shemsu did not complete it, while the rest were ready. Options B, C, and D reverse or deny these facts.

options.label: B
options.option_text: By the time the instructor asked his students to submit their project work, with the exception of Shemsu, who completed it on time, all the rest were not ready for submission.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Neither Shemsu nor the rest of his class mates were ready to submit their project by the time their instructor requested them to do so.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Both Shemsu and his class mates had already finished their assignment and submitted the same following an order from their instructor.

questions.question_text: The world economy, according to projections from the World Bank and IMF, might reduce by 0.02% from where it was last year.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The word reduce means to become or make smaller in size, amount, or degree. Diminish shares this meaning precisely and fits the economic context of a small decline. Narrow is limited to gaps, minimize implies making as small as possible, and belittle means to disparage.

questions.question_text: Thanks to the tangible measures the Ministry of Health has taken with regard to family health and planning, there has been a sharp decline in maternal and infant mortality.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A sharp decline means a sudden, steep decrease. Steep is the exact synonym for sharp when describing a rapid rise or fall in numbers. Serious, steady, and expensive do not match the sense of an abrupt drop in mortality rates.

questions.question_text: The moment he entered the compound, the stranger was attacked by the dogs.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Attacked means to act violently against someone or something. Set on is a phrasal verb meaning exactly this, to attack, and fits dogs attacking a stranger. Cornered implies trapping, chased implies pursuit, and dismantled means taken apart, none of which match attacked.

questions.question_text: I found the man's handwriting to be somehow difficult to read . As a result, I had to return the text to him to rewrite it in a readable manner.

options.label: A
options.explanation: Illegible describes writing that is too unclear or messy to be read, which matches handwriting that is difficult to read. Unclear is broader and not specific to handwriting, while unconvincing and tasking do not fit. The clue difficult to read and the return for rewriting point to illegible.

questions.question_text: As Ethiopians, the fact that we have never been colonized is among the many reasons that would make us feel very much pleased of being Ethiopians.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sentence says Ethiopians feel very much pleased to be Ethiopians because they were never colonized. Proud means feeling deep pleasure and satisfaction in one's identity or achievements, which fits perfectly. Initiated, motivated, and encouraged do not capture this sense of national pride.

questions.question_text: In any nation building endeavor, being accommodative of the interests of a wide range of people, things, ideas etc., is believed to be the most crucial factor to lasting peace and harmony.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Accommodative of the interests of a wide range of people, things, and ideas means including everyone and everything. Inclusive conveys this meaning of involving or covering all groups. Tolerant is narrower, mutual means shared, and mandatory means required, so inclusive best fits the description.

questions.question_text: The man was found guilty and sentenced to a ten year of rigorous imprisonment and denial of his rights of participating in any election as both a voter and a candidate for 5 years after his release from jail.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The man was denied his right to vote and stand as a candidate. Deprivation means the state of being denied or stripped of something, especially a right or privilege. Neglection and confiscation do not fit, and approval means the opposite, so deprivation is the correct word.

questions.question_text: It is usually a nonsense gesture by some selfish-individuals to try hard to tarnish the good image of others through false narratives.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Tarnishing someone's good image through false narratives means portraying them as evil or wicked. Demonize means to represent someone as evil or threatening, which matches exactly. Demonstrate means show, disregard means ignore, and criticize is milder and not based on false stories.

questions.question_text: The author's main purpose is to:

options.label: A
options.option_text: create awareness on the part of the reader that Africa is a continent with abundant, yet untapped resources.

options.label: B
options.option_text: ignite a feeling of regret in the reader's mind as to how Africa's resources were looted by the west

options.label: C
options.option_text: argue in favor of the idea that the Africa we all dream to see can be materialized through intra continental integration.
options.explanation: Throughout the passage the writer argues that Africa's rich but untapped resources and raw-material exports can be transformed by trading among African nations themselves. Option C best captures this central argument that the Africa we dream of can be achieved through intra-continental integration, which the other options only touch on or narrow.

options.label: D
options.option_text: appreciate the efforts exerted by some regional organizations like COMESA, EAC and SADC in fostering economic integration.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would be the best replacement for the word "chewy" in paragraph 2 of this passage?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Chewy describes food that is difficult to bite or cut and needs much chewing, and tough is its closest synonym. Boring, inaccessible, and sickening describe qualities of text or experience, not the physical texture of food, so they cannot replace chewy in the passage.

questions.question_text: In paragraph 1 line 1 the writer says " Africa could be labeled as the supplier of mostly unprocessed products to the world ." Which word do you think best describes the where about of Arica in the global economy?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The writer says Africa supplies mostly unprocessed products, meaning raw materials, to the world, which places the continent in a poor, subordinate position in the global economy. Destitute best conveys this impoverished standing. Naive, conservative, and traditional describe attitudes or styles, not economic status.

questions.question_text: The title "Creating the Africa We Want" implies:

options.label: A
options.option_text: we can take Africa to a better position.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Africa is in the way we aspire it to be.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Economic integration endeavors are taken place in Africa

options.label: D
options.option_text: If every stake holder works for a better Africa, we can make the Africa we want.
options.explanation: The title Creating the Africa We Want implies that the Africa we desire does not yet exist but can be built through effort. Option D expresses this by linking stakeholders working together to producing the Africa we want. Option A is too vague, and options B and C contradict or narrow the idea.

questions.question_text: The underlined word "circumvent" in the fourth paragraph most nearly means:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Circumvent means to find a way around an obstacle or to defeat someone or something through cleverness. Beat, in the sense of overcoming, is the closest synonym among the options. Win, ignore, and abandon do not convey the idea of getting around a difficulty.

questions.question_text: In the last paragraph of the passage the writer says, to achieve the Africa we want, every stake holder, coupled with planned and see the mast work for the unified goal support of the above quotation most likely support?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Stake holders are working closely with the people of Africa

options.label: B
options.option_text: The writer thinks the Africa he wants will materialize sooner than later.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A concerted effort from all concerned bodies is mandatory if Africa is to develop as desired.
options.explanation: The final paragraph says every stakeholder must work with careful planning toward the unified goal of a better Africa. This supports the idea that a concerted effort from all concerned bodies is mandatory for Africa to develop as desired, which option C states directly and fully.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Africa has embarked in integrated development.

questions.question_text: In Paragraph 1, line 6, the phrase "such a move" refers to:

options.label: A
options.option_text: the integration of Africa through multi polar trade with all the continents.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the materializing of the Africa we want through intra -continental trade integration.
options.explanation: The phrase such a move refers back to the idea that immediately precedes it. Given the passage theme, that idea is materializing the Africa we want through intra-continental trade integration. The other options refer to facts or labels mentioned elsewhere rather than the specific move the writer endorses.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the fact that Africa still has untapped natural resources and human resources even after the long and bloody experience of civilization.

options.label: D
options.option_text: the act of labeling Africa as the supplier of mostly unprocessed products to the world.

questions.question_text: In paragraph 4, what expression has the writer used to show that he wants to add a point or information to what he has said in paragraph 3.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The question asks which addition marker appears in paragraph 4 of the passage, but the passage text is not provided in the input file. All four options, moreover, furthermore, besides, and in addition, express addition, so the exact word used cannot be verified. Furthermore is selected as the most likely formal choice.

questions.question_text: In paragraph two the phrase "These continents" refers to

options.label: B
options.option_text: the northern continents apart from Africa

options.label: C
options.explanation: In context, the writer contrasts Africa with the continents that receive its unprocessed products, so These continents most plausibly refers to continents other than Africa. Option C matches this reading. The passage text is unavailable for verification, so the answer is inferred from the surrounding argument.

options.label: D
options.option_text: all continents including those in the northern hemisphere

questions.question_text: The term intra- continental trade implies

options.label: A
options.option_text: a trade that should prevail between and among African countries
options.explanation: Intra- means within or inside, so intra-continental trade refers to trade occurring among countries on the same continent. Therefore it implies trade between and among African countries. Options B and C refer to trade with other continents, and option D restricts the meaning to just two countries.

options.label: B
options.option_text: a trade that should take place between continents of those in northern hemisphere and Africa

options.label: C
options.option_text: a trade tie that should take place between Africa and other continents

options.label: D
options.option_text: a network of trading that should exist between two countries of Africa

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is False of the city of Boston?

options.label: A
options.option_text: People in Boston value their leisure time.
options.explanation: The passage portrays Bostonians as busy, time-oriented people who keep themselves busy like perpetual-motion machines, so they do not prize leisure. Therefore the statement that people in Boston value their leisure time is false. Drivers sitting on the left, hectic life, and being well scheduled are all stated as true.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Drivers in Boston usually sit in the left side while they are driving.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Life in Boston is so hectic.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Boston people are usually well scheduled.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would be the best title for this passage?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The amazing side of the city of Boston

options.label: B
options.option_text: The arctic life of Boston versus the serene nature of Melbourne

options.label: C
options.explanation: The passage describes Tamara Blackmore's reactions to the striking differences between her home city Melbourne and the American city Boston, including pace of life, time, and driving habits. This adjustment to an unfamiliar society is best summarized as culture shock, which is the most fitting title.

questions.question_text: Which of the following organizational schemes is most prevalent in the passage?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The passage is organized around the contrasts between Boston and Melbourne, setting American habits against Australian habits in areas such as time management, busyness, and driving. Because it repeatedly highlights differences between the two cities, order of contrast is the organizational scheme most prevalent in the passage.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Living in a community other than where one was brought up could be a fascinating experience.
options.explanation: The passage recounts Tamara Blackmore's positive experience of moving from Melbourne to Boston and adapting to a very different way of life. Option A best expresses the main idea that living in a community other than one's own can be a fascinating experience. The passage is not included, so this is inferred from the related questions.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Tamara Blackmore is a lucky girl who happened to enjoy life in two cities.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Culture shock could be traumatizing as is illustrated through Tamara Blackmore.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Boston College has gone out of its way to create a memorable experience for Blackmore and its other exchange students.

questions.question_text: In the second paragraph of the passage, which of the following points of differences between the cities of Boston and Melbourne is mainly dealt with?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Reading about the cities and experiencing them

options.label: D
options.explanation: The related questions indicate that paragraph two of the passage focuses on how Americans are more time-oriented, well scheduled, and constantly busy compared with Australians. This point of difference is best described as the way time is managed. The passage itself is not included for direct verification.

questions.question_text: What is the closest meaning of the underlined word understatement in the first paragraph?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Understatement means presenting something as smaller, less important, or less severe than it really is. Underrating, meaning undervaluing or underestimating, is the closest match. Exaggeration and hyperbole mean the opposite, overstating, and distortion means misrepresenting, so underrating is the correct synonym.

questions.question_text: In the first paragraph, the writer has used the expression "a sea of difference" to

options.label: A
options.option_text: show that the discrepancies in life style between Boston and Melbourne cities are so great
options.explanation: A sea of difference is an idiom meaning an extremely large difference. Option A expresses that the lifestyle discrepancies between Boston and Melbourne are very great, and option D says essentially the same thing. Because A and D are near duplicates, the question is defective; A is chosen as the cleaner wording.

options.label: B
options.option_text: show that the gap in life styles between Boston and Melbourne cities is so narrow

options.label: C
options.option_text: present to the reader that the America known through reading and the America known through experience have big differences

options.label: D
options.option_text: express vividly how vastly life in Boston is different from that in Melbourne

questions.question_text: The underlined word congestion in paragraph three refers to

options.label: B
options.explanation: Congestion means the state of being overcrowded or too full, especially with people or vehicles. Overcrowding is therefore its closest synonym. Freedom, relationship, and problems do not convey the sense of excessive crowding or traffic referred to in the passage.

questions.question_text: In paragraph four the word "they" in a heavy print refers to

options.label: C
options.explanation: In the passage, Bostonians are compared to perpetual-motion machines that are always moving and busy. The word they in the relevant sentence refers back to these machines. Australians, Americans, and life styles are not the immediate antecedent of the pronoun.

questions.question_text: Blackmore would probably agree that

options.label: A
options.option_text: Americans are more sophisticated drivers than their Australian counterparts

options.label: B
options.option_text: Americans are more time oriented and they keep themselves busy
options.explanation: Blackmore describes Bostonians as time-oriented people who constantly keep themselves busy, unlike the more relaxed Australians. Therefore she would probably agree that Americans are more time oriented and keep themselves busy. The other options about sophistication, generosity, and sociability are not supported.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Americans are more generous than their Australian counterparts

options.label: D
options.option_text: Americans are more easygoing and socially active than Australians

questions.question_text: The president _____ her speech of unity to both houses on the joint meeting of the House of Peoples Representatives and the House of Federation last week.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A speech is said to be delivered, meaning formally given or presented to an audience. The sentence describes the president giving her speech of unity before both houses last week, so delivered is the correct verb. Inaugurated, provisioned, and accentuated do not collocate with a speech.

questions.question_text: As is documented in historic archives, Ethiopia was at the _____ of its development stage during the Axumite Empire. It is the argument of many quarters at present that the major task of this generation is to take Ethiopia back to its place of hegemony.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Peak means the highest point or stage of development, which is what the sentence describes for Ethiopia during the Axumite Empire. The clue take Ethiopia back to its place of hegemony confirms a high point. Normalcy, verge, and pace do not mean the highest stage.

questions.question_text: According to the Ethiopian Metrological Agency's weather _____, Addis Ababa is expected to have a wet and cloudy weather condition in the coming couple of days.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A weather forecast is a statement predicting future weather conditions, which is exactly what the sentence describes for Addis Ababa. Speculation and prediction are too general or informal for an official meteorological statement, and condition refers to the weather itself rather than the report.

questions.question_text: According to a recent report by the United Nations Development Agency, countries are expected to enhance their effort in reducing the gap in gender _____ should they like to witness a fair and inclusive development in all aspects of life.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The phrase reducing the gap in gender requires a noun naming the differences between the sexes. Inequalities, meaning unequal treatment or opportunity between genders, fits perfectly. Roles, conflicts, and bias do not collocate with reducing the gap in this context.

questions.question_text: There happened a terrible accident yesterday after a minibus taxi collided with a Sino truck on the express way from Addis to Adama. In the accident while two of the passengers immediately died, around thirteen travellers were heavily _____.

options.label: C
options.explanation: People who suffer damage to their bodies in an accident are described as injured. Injured is the standard word for physical harm in accidents, while wounded usually implies intentional harm such as weapons. Damaged is used for objects, and bruised is only one specific type of injury.

questions.question_text: As is argued by many, one does not have to _____ himself/herself with those individuals who do not have any role in adding value to what he/she does.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sentence advises against forming connections with people who add no value to one's work. Associate with means to connect or keep company with someone, which fits the structure associate oneself with. Mix, bring, and live do not produce this idiomatic reflexive meaning.

questions.question_text: Ato Kebede, as many friends of him witness, is known for accomplishing any task assigned to him efficiently and timely promise. He is a person whom everybody admires for such quality of _____.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Reliable means able to be trusted to do what is asked, complete tasks efficiently, and keep promises. The sentence describes Ato Kebede as someone who finishes assigned tasks on time, so the admired quality is reliability. Kind, confident, and promising do not match the described trait.

questions.question_text: Kedir, though his friends are criticizing his plan of opening his own business with 10 branches in the coming six months as _____ looks to be very much optimistic about the realization of his dream.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sentence describes a plan to open a business with ten branches in six months, which friends criticize as overly bold or unrealistic while Kedir stays optimistic. Ambitious best captures a plan that is daring and demanding. Fictitious, suspicious, and frivolous imply unreliability that does not fit the optimistic tone.

questions.question_text: Which of the above topic sentences can best be developed using the exemplification method?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The question asks which of four topic sentences, labelled I to IV, can best be developed by giving examples, but the topic sentences themselves are not provided in the input file. Without them the answer cannot be determined. The first topic sentence is selected on the assumption that it makes a general claim needing examples.

questions.question_text: Which of the above topic sentences can best be developed using the argumentative method?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The question asks which of the four topic sentences is best developed by argument, but the sentences labelled I to IV are missing from the input file. The answer therefore cannot be verified. Option B, the second topic sentence, is chosen on the assumption that it presents a debatable claim requiring reasoned defence.

questions.question_text: Which of the above topic sentences can best be developed using the expository method?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The question asks which topic sentence suits the expository method, which explains or informs, but the sentences labelled I to IV are not included in the input file. The intended match cannot be confirmed. Option C, the third topic sentence, is selected on the assumption that it states an informative fact to explain.

questions.question_text: a. The main obstacle is the quality of the roads.

options.label: B
options.explanation: This is a sentence-ordering question, but only sentence a is shown in the input file; sentences b, c, and d are missing. The correct sequence therefore cannot be determined with confidence. Option B, which places the topic sentence a first, is chosen as the most reasonable guess.

questions.question_text: a. It is, therefore, possible to say that reading with undivided attention for a short time makes people more effective than sitting in a library the whole night.

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sentence a begins with the conclusion marker therefore, so it must be the final sentence of the ordered paragraph. Only option A, d b c a, places a last, making it the correct sequence. The other options put the concluding sentence in the middle or near the beginning.

questions.question_text: a. The author stated that in an elementary school, teachers were observed paying more attention to outer children.

options.label: B
options.explanation: This is a sentence-ordering task, but only sentence a is provided in the input file; sentences b, c, and d are missing. The correct order cannot be established without them. Option B is selected as a reasonable guess, but the question should be treated as defective.

questions.question_text: a. Others assert that the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.

options.label: C
options.explanation: This is a sentence-ordering task, but only sentence a is shown; sentences b, c, and d are missing. Sentence a contains Others, which suggests it follows a sentence mentioning Some, but the actual order cannot be verified. Option C is chosen as the most plausible arrangement.

questions.question_text: The missing part of the letter in number 2 is ____

options.label: C
options.explanation: In standard letter format, the date is placed after the sender's address. Number 2 in the letter layout is therefore the date. The receiver's name and address come later, the opening salutation follows the addresses, and the sender's address occupies number 1.

questions.question_text: The missing part of the letter in number 3 is ____

options.label: A
options.explanation: In standard business letter format, the receiver's address follows the date and precedes the opening salutation. Number 3 is therefore the receiver's address. The closing salutation and signature come at the end, and the sender's address is at the very top.

questions.question_text: The missing part of the letter in number 1 is ____

options.label: D
options.explanation: In standard letter format, the sender's address is written at the top of the letter, before the date and the receiver's address. Number 1 is therefore the sender's address. The date, receiver's name, and sender's signature occupy other numbered positions.

questions.question_text: always/ aspired/ to/ famous/ she/ become/ really/ has.

options.label: A
options.option_text: She has always aspired to become really famous.
options.explanation: The words must be arranged into a grammatically correct sentence. She has always aspired to become really famous uses the present perfect with the adverb always placed between the auxiliary and the past participle, which is correct word order. The other options scramble the verb and adverb positions.

options.label: B
options.option_text: She really has become always aspired to famous.

options.label: C
options.option_text: She always has to become really famous aspired.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Always, she aspired to has become famous really.

questions.question_text: when/ jogging/ to/ listen/ music/ he/ not/ goes/ does/ he,

options.label: A
options.option_text: When he does not jogging, he goes to music listen.

options.label: B
options.option_text: He does not listen to music when he goes jogging.
options.explanation: The words form the sentence He does not listen to music when he goes jogging. Option B places the negative present simple in the main clause and the time clause correctly with when. The other options use incorrect forms such as does not jogging or wrong word order.

options.label: C
options.option_text: He goes to listen music when he does not jogging.

options.label: D
options.option_text: When he does jogging, he not goes to listen music.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is NOT among student's duties in college?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Reading for exams, writing term papers, and doing assignments are all academic duties of college students. Doing a part-time job is a personal choice to earn money, not a required student duty. Therefore option C is the activity that is not among students' duties in college.

questions.question_text: What should students consider before choosing area of study as implied in paragraph 4?

options.label: A
options.option_text: the status of the area of study in the society where they live

options.label: B
options.option_text: the job opportunity there may be for them after graduation

options.label: C
options.option_text: the interest and capacity they have in an area of study
options.explanation: Paragraph 4 advises that students should choose an area of study based on their own interests and capacity, since genuine interest and ability are what sustain them through their studies. Options about social status, job opportunities, and parents' approval reflect external factors rather than the student's own suitability.

options.label: D
options.option_text: their parents' approval of the area of study

questions.question_text: Which one of the following words has the correct meaning to the word ' realize ' as stated in paragraph 2?

options.label: B
options.explanation: In paragraph 2, realize is used in the sense of achieving or fulfilling one's goals. Achieve is the closest synonym for this meaning. Implement means carry out a plan, boost means increase, and understand is a different sense of the word, so achieve is correct.

questions.question_text: In order to achieve their goals, students do not need

options.label: B
options.explanation: According to the passage, students need emotional support, enthusiasm for their subject, and the capacity to focus in order to reach their goals. A latest computer is a material possession, not a stated requirement. Therefore students do not need the latest computer.

questions.question_text: According to the information in paragraph 2, students who doubt themselves

options.label: A
options.option_text: can be successful in college if given the right support
options.explanation: Paragraph 2 says that students who doubt themselves can still be successful in college when they receive the right support and encouragement. Option A matches this claim exactly. The other options claim these students will fail, cause trouble, or should not be admitted, contradicting the passage.

options.label: B
options.option_text: should not be given the chance to join college at all

options.label: C
options.option_text: can only cause trouble to their family and friends

options.label: D
options.option_text: will surely fail in their studies at college

questions.question_text: Studying in college can be a challenge for some students because they

options.label: A
options.option_text: tend to waste the money they receive from family and friends

options.label: B
options.option_text: do part-time jobs to earn money so that they can have fun

options.label: C
options.option_text: choose to have fun and relax rather than studying hard
options.explanation: Studying in college is a challenge for some students because they prefer having fun and relaxing to studying hard, which harms their progress. Option C reflects this self-discipline theme of the passage. The passage is not included for direct verification, so the answer is inferred and the question is flagged.

options.label: D
options.option_text: may not afford to buy materials required for their study

questions.question_text: What does the word ' persevere ' as used in paragraph 2, line 7 mean?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Persevere means to continue doing something despite difficulty or delay. Carry on is the closest synonym. Decide, give up, and predict do not match, and give up means the opposite of persevering, which the passage presents as essential for success.

questions.question_text: Which of the following words can be synonymous with the word ' dedicated ' in paragraph 3, line 4?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Dedicated means giving complete loyalty and effort to a task or purpose. Committed is the closest synonym. Stubborn implies unreasonable resistance, desperate implies hopelessness, and decided simply means resolved, none of which match the sense of wholehearted devotion to one's studies.

questions.question_text: What does the word ' demands ' as used in paragraph 4, line 5 mean?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Demands refers to the requirements or things that are needed for a particular situation. In paragraph 4 the word is used to mean the requirements of an area of study. Opportunities, orders, and requests do not fit this meaning, so requirements is the correct synonym.

questions.question_text: The author suggests that the best way to prevent plagiarism in colleges is to ______

options.label: A
options.option_text: train university authorities so they can easily prevent it from happening

options.label: B
options.option_text: train teachers to be able to detect the crime when it is committed

options.label: C
options.option_text: make students aware in advance that the act is wrong
options.explanation: The author argues that students cheat through plagiarism largely because they do not fully understand that it is wrong. Therefore the best prevention is to make students aware in advance that copying others' work is dishonest. Detecting and punishing after the fact are less effective than prevention.

options.label: D
options.option_text: punish the criminal when he/she is found cheating

questions.question_text: It is implied in paragraph 2 that _______

options.label: A
options.option_text: the majority of students commit this crime but it's not taken seriously

options.label: B
options.option_text: buying material from the Internet is the most frequent way of cheating

options.label: C
options.option_text: there is nothing universities/colleges can do to control academic theft

options.label: D
options.option_text: plagiarism can easily be detected and there are punishments for it
options.explanation: Paragraph 2 implies that plagiarism can readily be detected, since instructors can compare students' essays, and that institutions impose penalties for the offence. Option D matches this implication. The other options claim the crime is ignored, uncontrollable, or not taken seriously, which contradicts the paragraph's point.

questions.question_text: The word ' This ' paragraph 1, line 4 refers to

options.label: D
options.explanation: The word This in paragraph 1 refers to the idea stated just before it: that the ease of using the Internet for essays makes students tempted to cheat. Option D, being tempted to cheat, is therefore the correct antecedent. The other options name earlier or unrelated ideas.

questions.question_text: The right thing to do for students who believe their writing skills are not so good is to ______

options.label: A
options.option_text: try harder and improve their own writing skills through repeated practice
options.explanation: Students who feel their writing skills are weak should practise writing until they improve, because working on their own skills is honest and productive. Option A recommends exactly this. Asking friends to write essays or buying essays still constitutes cheating, and ignoring accuracy is not a responsible solution.

options.label: B
options.option_text: focus on just the idea and let the teacher worry about the accuracy of their writing

options.label: C
options.option_text: ask their friends to write essays for them instead of taking them from the Internet

options.label: D
options.option_text: buy essays from the Internet legally

questions.question_text: If students have too many assignments to complete, they

options.label: A
options.option_text: should withdraw and take some time to improve their skills

options.label: B
options.option_text: can ask their classmates to do some of the work for them

options.label: C
options.option_text: have no choice but borrow some material from the Internet

options.label: D
options.option_text: can try and convince their teacher to give them more time
options.explanation: When students have more assignments than they can manage, the passage advises them to speak with their teacher and request more time rather than resorting to plagiarism. Option D states this directly. Withdrawing, borrowing material, or having classmates do the work are not recommended solutions.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is NOT a problem caused by plagiarism?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The student's social relationships can be negatively affected

options.label: B
options.option_text: The student can receive an F for the course or assignment

options.label: C
options.option_text: The student can be suspended from the college/university

options.label: D
options.option_text: The student can waste a lot of time surfing the Internet
options.explanation: The passage lists consequences of plagiarism such as failing the course or assignment, being suspended from the institution, and damage to relationships. Wasting time surfing the Internet is a cause of cheating, not a consequence of plagiarism. Therefore option D is the statement that is NOT a problem caused by plagiarism.

questions.question_text: What does the word ' their ' in paragraph 2, line 2 refer to?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The word their in paragraph 2 refers to the students, since the surrounding discussion concerns the attitudes and behaviour of students who doubt themselves. Options about the group, classmates, and teachers do not match the grammatical antecedent in the sentence.

questions.question_text: The word ' this ' paragraph 3, line 2 refers to

options.label: A
options.option_text: pretending the essays copied from internet as yours
options.explanation: The word this in paragraph 3 refers to presenting essays copied from the Internet as one's own work, which is the act of plagiarism being discussed. Option A matches this meaning. Comparing essays, saving time on presentation, and buying essays are related ideas but not the direct referent.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the way instructors can compare students' essays

options.label: C
options.option_text: saving the time initially on presentation

questions.question_text: Which one of the following has the closest meaning to the word ' negotiate ' as used in paragraph 4, line 5?

options.label: C
options.explanation: Negotiate, in the context of handling a difficult situation or assignment, means to deal with or cope successfully. Deal is the closest synonym among the options. Argue, disagree, and dispute imply conflict, whereas the passage uses the word in the sense of managing the workload.

questions.question_text: Had you studied harder, you wouldn't have found the exam so hard.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Although you studied hard, the exam was too difficult for you.

options.label: B
options.option_text: You didn't study hard so you found the exam to be difficult.
options.explanation: The sentence Had you studied harder, you wouldn't have found the exam so hard is a third conditional, meaning you did not study hard and therefore found the exam difficult. Option B restates this meaning exactly. The other options contradict the conditional logic.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Even if you studied hard, the exam would be hard for you.

options.label: D
options.option_text: You studied hard so the exam was not hard for you at all.

questions.question_text: If I were you, I would look for a scholarship abroad.

options.label: A
options.option_text: You should have applied for a scholarship abroad, but it's too late now.

options.label: B
options.option_text: You are not as wise as I am so you have not applied for a scholarship.

options.label: C
options.option_text: I believe it is a good idea for you to apply for a scholarship abroad.
options.explanation: If I were you, I would look for a scholarship abroad is a second conditional giving advice. The speaker is suggesting that applying for a scholarship abroad is a good idea for the listener. Option C captures this advisory meaning precisely.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Sadly, I am not you so I will not look for a scholarship abroad.

questions.question_text: Cub is to a Lion: __________ is to a Cow.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The analogy is about the young of animals: a cub is the baby of a lion, just as a calf is the baby of a cow. Veal is the meat of young cattle, kitten is a baby cat, and bull is an adult male, so calf is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Driver is to a Car: __________ is to a Ship.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The analogy pairs each vehicle with the person who operates it: a driver controls a car just as a sailor controls a ship. Swimmer, rider, and surfer are not operators of a vessel, so sailor is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Due to economic and cultural factors, many children in the countryside __________ of school.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Drop out means to leave school or stop attending classes before finishing, which matches the sentence about children leaving school. Run out, fall out, and leave out do not form the idiomatic phrasal verb meaning to abandon one's education, so drop out is correct.

questions.question_text: The whole building collapsed when it was hit by a missile. Only two  __________ children were found alive in.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The sentence says only two children were found alive after a building collapsed, which is an extraordinary, almost unbelievable survival. Miraculous means happening through an amazing or supernatural event, fitting this sense. Fortunate, fearless, and mysterious do not convey the wonder of surviving a collapsed building.

questions.question_text: The conflict between the two countries had __________ effect on their economy. They have been spending a lot on armaments.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Spending heavily on armaments because of conflict clearly harms the economy, so the effect is disastrous, meaning causing great damage or suffering. Complementary, easing, and encouraging all describe positive or supportive effects, which contradict the negative outcome described in the sentence.

questions.question_text: A new cure for malaria has been found. This could reduce the __________ that has normally been caused by the disease, especially in developing countries.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A cure for malaria would reduce the deaths caused by the disease. Fatality means death, so fatality is the correct noun. Famine is a food shortage, immunity is resistance to disease, and longevity is long life, none of which fit the idea of reducing deaths.

questions.question_text: I think __________ memories are usually pleasant. That is because, as children, we didn't have to worry about the hardships of life.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sentence needs a noun modifying memories to mean memories from the time when one was a child. Childhood memories is the correct collocation. Children is plural for young people, child is the singular noun, and childish means immature, so childhood is right.

questions.question_text: Any negotiation is a give-and-take process but there are things we cannot __________ for anything. There is a limit to what you can give.

options.label: B
options.explanation: In negotiation, some things are so important that they cannot be given away. Compromise means to give up part of what one wants in order to reach agreement, so we cannot compromise fits the sentence. Condemn, dispute, and discuss do not express sacrificing principles.

questions.question_text: The ongoing competition between the two powerful countries to control the region is causing more harm than good to the people.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The word competition means a situation in which people or groups compete to win or gain something. Contest is the closest synonym. Hatred and argument involve hostility, and cooperation means the opposite of competing, so contest best replaces competition.

questions.question_text: Any country needs a strong government in order to limit or eradicate unlawful activities by some elements of society.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Unlawful activities are those that break the law, and illicit means the same, describing something illegal or forbidden. Suspicious, trading, and secretive do not mean illegal, so illicit is the correct synonym for unlawful in the sentence.

questions.question_text: She told the class a very funny story. Nobody could stop laughing!

options.label: C
options.explanation: The story was so funny that nobody could stop laughing, and hilarious means extremely funny, which fits perfectly. Silly, long, and useful do not capture the strong comic effect described, so hilarious is the best synonym for very funny.

questions.question_text: After her long career in several international organizations, she is now engaged in humanitarian service intending to give back to the community.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Humanitarian service intended to give back to the community is the work of helping others, and charitable means relating to giving help or money to those in need. Obligatory, profitable, and professional do not convey the generosity of giving back, so charitable is correct.

questions.question_text: When you buy an item from a shop, you are usually given a one-year assurance so if it stops working, you can get it fixed for free.

options.label: A
options.explanation: An assurance that an item will be repaired for free if it stops working is a guarantee, meaning a formal promise by a seller to fix or replace goods. Certificate, service, and replacement are different concepts, so guarantee is the correct word for the one-year assurance.

questions.question_text: Conservation of natural resources is one of the key duties of any society.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Conservation means the careful protection and preservation of natural resources. Protection is the closest synonym. Utilization means using resources, afforestation means planting trees, and renovation means repairing, none of which match the meaning of conserving nature.

questions.question_text: Interviewer: You said that you left your previous work place because the organization was old-fashioned. What do you mean?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Let me re-phrase what I just said
options.explanation: When a listener asks what the speaker meant by an earlier statement, the speaker should rephrase it, that is, express the same idea in different words. Option A, Let me re-phrase what I just said, responds appropriately. Merely repeating or speaking louder does not explain the meaning.

options.label: B
options.option_text: I will say that again if you want

options.label: C
options.option_text: Let me repeat what I just said

options.label: D
options.option_text: Let me say it again loudly

questions.question_text: Kenan: What do you think will be the next major scientific discovery?

options.label: A
options.option_text: I will suppose they are discovering a cure for cancer.

options.label: B
options.option_text: I'm supposing they will discover a cure for cancer.

options.label: C
options.option_text: I suppose they will discover a cure for cancer.
options.explanation: Kenan asks what the speaker thinks will be discovered next. Option C answers directly using the simple present verb suppose with a future clause, which is the correct structure for expressing an opinion about the future. The other options use awkward or ungrammatical tenses.

options.label: D
options.option_text: I suppose the cancer will be wide spreading.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Why do you think money is more important than love?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Do you think money is more important than love?
options.explanation: The stem shows only Abraham with no reply or surrounding dialogue, so the intended question cannot be determined from context. Option B, Do you think money is more important than love, is the most neutral and grammatically standard opinion question. The question should be flagged as context-free and defective.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Do you believe that money can buy love?

options.label: D
options.option_text: Do you think love is the most important?

questions.question_text: Banker: Good morning, sir. How shall I help you?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Good morning. I want you to give me some dollars, if you don't mind.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Good morning. I'm in a hurry. Give me some dollars now, will you?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Good morning. I'm here to convert some Birr to dollars, please.
options.explanation: The bank teller offers help, and the customer's most natural request is to exchange currency. Option C states clearly that the customer has come to convert Birr to dollars. Options A and B are impolite or rude, and option D ambiguously says change some dollars without specifying the transaction.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Good morning. I would like to change some dollars, please.

questions.question_text: Lemma: I believe climate change is the main reason for the high cost of living in the whole world.

options.label: A
options.option_text: I can't agree with you at all

options.label: B
options.option_text: I agree up to a point, but
options.explanation: Lemma expresses a strong belief about climate change causing high living costs. A thoughtful response is to agree partially while signalling a reservation, which option B does with I agree up to a point, but. The other options either reject the view completely or dismiss climate change.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Climate change has no effect at all

options.label: D
options.option_text: I totally disagree with you, but

questions.question_text: Ojilu: Why did you choose to study social science? Obang: ________

options.label: A
options.option_text: Because, I want to be a medical doctor.

options.label: C
options.option_text: In order to gather data about social science students.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Because, I want to study political science.
options.explanation: Obang chose social science, so the reason must relate to a social science field. Studying political science is a social science discipline, so option D answers logically. Option A names medicine, a health science, and the other options do not give a reason for choosing the field.

questions.question_text: Daba: Students at university should be totally free to choose their field of study so that they can be successful. Adugna: ________but we should also consider the needs of society so that we have skilled human power in every field.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Adugna agrees with Daba but adds a qualification about society's needs. The phrase That's a good point, but expresses agreement followed by a contrasting view, matching the structure. The other options all express strong disagreement, which contradicts the but that follows.

questions.question_text: Kiros: I called you three times last night but you didn't pick up your phone. I was really disappointed. Dinkessa: ________

options.label: C
options.option_text: Sorry, I didn't mean to ignore you.
options.explanation: Kiros complains that Dinkessa ignored his phone calls. The appropriate apology is option C, Sorry, I didn't mean to ignore you, which accepts responsibility and shows the neglect was unintentional. The other options deflect blame or offer no meaningful apology.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Sorry, there is nothing I can do now.

options.label: A
options.option_text: Do you think that Trump will be re-elected as President

options.label: B
options.option_text: Who do you think will be the next President of America
options.explanation: The stem shows only Zeberga with no reply, so the intended question cannot be determined from the available context. Option B, Who do you think will be the next President of America, is the most standard and complete question form. The item is flagged as context-free and defective.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Are you thinking that Trump will be re-elected as President

options.label: D
options.option_text: Why do you think Trump may be re-elected as President

questions.question_text: Teacher: Alemu has just made a good point on how we can improve education in our country.________ Taye?

options.label: B
options.option_text: What is another idea you have

options.label: D
options.option_text: Would you like to add anything
options.explanation: The teacher is inviting Taye to contribute another idea after Alemu's point, so the polite question "Would you like to add anything" fits. Options A, B, and C are unidiomatic or grammatically awkward in English. Only D forms a natural, appropriate invitation that encourages Taye to share his additional thoughts on improving education.

questions.question_text: Teacher: Today I'm going to tell you about AI.

options.label: A
options.option_text: You're speaking fast, but I can hear you.

options.label: B
options.option_text: I see I got your point.

options.label: C
options.option_text: I didn't catch that. Could you repeat that, please?
options.explanation: The student does not understand the term AI, so he politely asks the teacher to repeat it. "I didn't catch that. Could you repeat that, please?" is the natural request for clarification. Option D uses the ungrammatical phrase "didn't hold," while A and B claim understanding or agreement, which does not match a request for repetition.

options.label: D
options.option_text: I didn't hold that. Could you repeat that, please?

questions.question_text: Mother: Have you had breakfast, sweetie?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The son hates having breakfast, so he has not eaten yet. "No, I haven't" correctly answers the present-perfect question "Have you had breakfast?" Option C contradicts his dislike of breakfast, A combines "yes" with a negative, and D uses the past simple instead of the present perfect, so B is the appropriate response.

questions.question_text: Zeru: In my free time, I go swimming in Sheraton Hotel.

options.label: A
options.option_text: When did you start doing that?

options.label: B
options.option_text: How long did you do that?

options.label: C
options.option_text: How long ago did you start this hobby?

options.label: D
options.option_text: How long have you been doing it?
options.explanation: Molla's reply "Since 2015" gives a duration continuing to the present, so the natural question is "How long have you been doing it?" with the present perfect continuous. Options A, B, and C ask when the hobby started or how long ago it began, which do not match a duration answer beginning with "since."

questions.question_text: Robel: It's our friend's wedding this coming Sunday, so I'll have my hair done tomorrow. What about you?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Genet agrees that she will also have her hair done for the wedding, as her comment about looking their best shows. "So will I" is the standard short agreement form for a future intention. D "I will also" is informal, while B and C express negative agreement, which contradicts her supportive reply.

questions.question_text: Solomon: First, they amputated my leg. Then, they told me the cancer has spread to all parts of my body!

options.label: C
options.explanation: Solomon has just described amputation and the spread of cancer, terrible news that calls for sympathy. "How terrible!" expresses the appropriate shock and concern. Options A and D are dismissive or casual, and B "That is amazing!" is inappropriate for such distressing information.

questions.question_text: Ali: Last night, I heard a knock on my door, and when I got to the door, there was no one there. This is happening more often these days.

options.label: A
options.explanation: Merima is speculating about a mysterious knock at the door and advises Ali to inform the police. "It could be a robber" correctly uses the modal "could" to express possibility. Options B, C, and D assert certainty about a past, present, or future robber, which is too definite for an unexplained event.

questions.question_text: Tourist: Excuse me, sir. Is there a bank near here? Resident: _____________

options.label: A
options.option_text: Go straight in this road, turn left; you can't miss it.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Go face to face on this road and turn to right.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Go straight along this road and turn right at the crossroads.
options.explanation: When giving directions, speakers say "Go straight along this road and turn right at the crossroads." Option C is the standard, grammatically correct form. A and B use unidiomatic phrases such as "in this road" and "go face to face," while D's mention of Google Maps is informal and unsuitable for the context.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Go straight over this road and search from Google map.

questions.question_text: Journalist: Thank you, Wolzero Hirut, for giving me the chance to ask you a few questions about your organization.

options.label: A
options.option_text: It's my pleasure and thank you for visiting us.
options.explanation: Woizero Hirut has just been thanked for giving an interview, so the polite response is "It's my pleasure and thank you for visiting us." Option A expresses gratitude and welcomes the visit. B, C, and D are impatient or hostile replies that would be rude after a journalist has politely thanked her.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Okay. Go head. What do you want to know?

options.label: C
options.option_text: What is it this time? You were here last year, weren't you?

options.label: D
options.option_text: I have a meeting in an hour. Make it quick, please!

questions.question_text: Kitila: Now that our planned trip to Hawassa has been canceled, what do you think we can do during our break next week?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Why don't we go to Kuriftu for two days, instead?
options.explanation: Kejela is suggesting an alternative activity after the Hawassa trip was cancelled, so "Why don't we go to Kuriftu for two days, instead?" is the appropriate suggestion. Option A uses the idiomatic "Why don't we..." form. B is a blunt statement, while C and D are grammatically incorrect question forms.

options.label: B
options.option_text: We don't go to Kuriftu for two days.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Why we shouldn't go to Hawassa? We have never been there.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Why not we go to Hawassa? It could be more fun, actually.

questions.question_text: Mustefa: Excuse me, can you tell me where the Registrar's office is?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Why do you want to go there?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Halima is a stranger in the area, so she cannot give directions. "I'm sorry I don't know" is the polite, honest reply. Option B says "Yes, I can" but does not provide the information, while A and C are rude; only D appropriately admits ignorance without offering help.

questions.question_text: Thanks to technology, we ________ carry a lot of cash with us when we go shopping. We can use mobile banking to make payments.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Because mobile banking makes payments easy, carrying a lot of cash is not necessary. "Don't have to" expresses lack of necessity. Option A "must" forces the action, B "haven't to" is grammatically wrong, and C "ought not to" means it would be wrong to carry cash, which is not the intended meaning.

questions.question_text: Last week, I found a mobile phone around the entrance at Sheraton Hotel. As I didn't know _________, I gave it to the receptionist.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The speaker did not know the phone's owner, so he gave it to the receptionist. "Whose it was" is needed because "whose" expresses possession. Options A and B (whom/who) are subject and object forms, and D "where" asks about location, none of which identifies who owned the mobile phone.

questions.question_text: If Sofia worked hard, she ________ good mark.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The sentence describes a hypothetical present situation, so the second conditional is needed. "If Sofia worked hard, she would get good marks" pairs the past subjunctive "worked" with "would get." Option D "would have got" belongs to the third conditional and does not match the simple past condition.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following words does NOT have a prefix?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The word "decorate" has no prefix because "de" is part of its root, not a separable prefix. In contrast, "bicycle" contains the prefix "bi-," "devalue" contains "de-," and "midday" contains "mid-." Therefore "decorate" is the word that does NOT have a prefix.

questions.question_text: Lions can easily kill buffalos, not because lions are stronger, but because they are ________.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The sentence compares lions and buffalos, so the comparative form is required. "More intelligent" is the correct comparative of "intelligent." Options A "much intelligent" and C "far intelligent" omit "more," and D "most intelligent" is superlative, which does not fit a comparison between two groups.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences is grammatically accurate?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Either the boy or the girls living next door speaks French.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Neither the teacher nor the students is good at English.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Malaria is one of the diseases that kill the highest number of people.
options.explanation: In option C the relative pronoun "that" refers to the plural noun "diseases," so the verb "kill" agrees correctly. Option A should use "speak" after "the girls," B needs "are" after "the students," and D needs "complains" after "Everyone," making C the only grammatically accurate sentence.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Everyone in the school complain about the poor service in the café.

questions.question_text: Alex joined the natural science stream when he was in Grade 10 because his father wanted him to be a doctor. Now he is in Grade 12 and he feels he is more talented in the arts.He says

options.label: A
options.option_text: I wish I never listened to my father's advice.

options.label: B
options.option_text: I wish I joined the social science stream.

options.label: C
options.option_text: I wish I had joined the natural science stream.

options.label: D
options.option_text: I wish I had joined the social science stream.
options.explanation: Alex feels more talented in the arts, so he regrets joining natural science. To express regret about a past action, English uses "I wish I had" plus a past participle. "I wish I had joined the social science stream" is therefore correct; the other options state the wrong stream or tense.

questions.question_text: You can travel to Hawassa by plane now. A large airport ________.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The result, that Hawassa is now reachable by plane, is already complete in the present, so the present perfect passive "has been constructed" is correct. Options B and D are active forms, and A "was being constructed" describes an unfinished action in the past.

questions.question_text: Helen is not a morning person. She usually ________ at 9:00 in the morning.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Helen's habit of getting up late is a general, repeated action, so the simple present is used. "She usually gets up at 9:00" matches a singular subject with the -s form. Options A, C, and D use the wrong tenses or forms for a habitual action.

questions.question_text: The first thing you should do when you do a reading test is read the questions you are going to answer. _________, you should quickly to get the general idea.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The instructions list steps in a reading test, so a sequencing connector is required. "Then" introduces the next step after reading the questions. "Instead" shows contrast, "While" indicates simultaneity, and "After" needs a following clause, none of which fits the order of actions described.

questions.question_text: He wrote the essay carelessly. The teacher couldn't read it. Which of the following sentences combines these two sentences correctly?

options.label: A
options.option_text: He wrote the essay such carelessly that the teacher couldn't read it.

options.label: B
options.option_text: He wrote the essay carelessly, so that the teacher couldn't read it.

options.label: C
options.option_text: He wrote the essay so carelessly as he didn't want the teacher to read it.

options.label: D
options.option_text: He wrote the essay so carelessly that the teacher couldn't read it.
options.explanation: The two sentences describe a result: he wrote so carelessly that the teacher could not read it. The correct structure is "so + adverb + that," giving "so carelessly that." Option A wrongly uses "such," B reverses cause and effect, and C uses an incorrect structure.

questions.question_text: My spoken English has been improved a lot. Because, I _________ English classes in the evening consecutively for six monthes.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The action began in the past and continues to the present over six months, so the present perfect continuous is needed. "I have been attending English classes" is correct. Options A and D are passive or malformed, and C "have been being attended" is an awkward double passive.

questions.question_text: All of us in my family are teachers. We are all employed by the government. _________ of us has his/her own private company.

options.label: C
options.explanation: All family members are government-employed teachers, so nobody among them owns a private company. "None of us has his/her own private company" correctly expresses this. "Everyone" and "All" contradict the statement, and "Each" would emphasize every member rather than negating ownership.

questions.question_text: Having worked for eight consecutive hours, he ________ exhausted.

options.label: D
options.explanation: After working eight consecutive hours, he became exhausted. "Became" is the natural linking verb showing the result of hard work. "Declared" and "shifted" have different meanings, and "came exhausted" is not idiomatic; "became exhausted" correctly describes entering the state of being tired.

questions.question_text: When you bought me the alarm clock for my last birthday, you were actually trying to tell me that I was wasting too much time sleeping. ________?

options.label: B
options.explanation: The sentence uses the past form "were actually trying," so the tag question must repeat the auxiliary "were." With a positive statement the tag is negative: "weren't you?" Option A "didn't you" changes the auxiliary, and C and D wrongly make the subject "I" instead of "you."

questions.question_text: This year, money _________ for the construction of a wider and greener football pitch. The school management has decided to improve the sports field in our school.

options.label: A
options.explanation: Money is currently being collected for the football pitch, so the present continuous passive "is being raised" is needed. Option A matches the ongoing action described. B and C are active forms, and D "has raised" states a completed action rather than an ongoing collection.

questions.question_text: Many people think that students fail the exam because it is _________ for them to pass. But I believe, it is because most students do not work __________.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The first blank follows "it is" with an adjective meaning the exam is impossible to pass, so "too difficult" is correct. The second blank completes "do not work," requiring "hard enough" as an adverb. Only option C pairs "too difficult" with "hard enough" correctly.

questions.question_text: My parents have lived in a rented house for a long time, but they are now having their own house constructed. God willing, the construction _________ in six months' time.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The construction will be finished at a point in the future, six months from now, so the future perfect passive is required. "Will have been completed" expresses this completed future action. Options B and D lack the future perfect form, and C describes a present completed action.

questions.question_text: The president, who led the organization for the last 15 years, is likely to be re-elected _________ there has been a sharp decline in profits.

options.label: C
options.option_text: in spite of the fact that
options.explanation: A clause beginning "there has been a sharp decline" follows the blank, so a subordinating conjunction is needed. "In spite of the fact that" introduces a clause correctly. "Despite of" is ungrammatical, while "despite" and "in spite of" require a noun phrase rather than a clause.

questions.question_text: My brother learnt three languages ______ his stay in prison.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The noun phrase "his stay in prison" follows the blank, so the preposition "during" is correct. "While" and "when" introduce clauses, and "for" is used with durations like "for three years." "During his stay" correctly indicates the period in which he learnt the languages.

questions.question_text: The wet season last year was long and depressing. Not only did it rain ______, but it was also cold and windy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The verb "rain" is naturally modified by "heavily," meaning in large quantities. "It rained heavily" is the standard collocation. "Greatly" and "roughly" do not collocate with rain, and "hardly" means almost not, which contradicts the long, depressing wet season described.

questions.question_text: An important message ______ on the famous journalist's burial ceremony by the manager of the organization for which he worked.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The message receives the action, so the passive voice is required, and the simple past "was transmitted" reports the completed event on the burial day. Option A is correct. B and D are active, and C "was being transmitted" describes an ongoing action rather than a completed message.

questions.question_text: My son intends _______ economics when he joins university.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The verb "intends" is followed by the infinitive, so "to study" is correct. "My son intends to study economics" is the natural construction. Option D uses a gerund, which is not correct after "intend," and A's perfect infinitive implies completion before university, which does not fit the future plan.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is true according to paragraph 4?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Some homeless who are victims of circumstances deserve help to recognize their lives again.
options.explanation: Paragraph 4 states that some homeless people are victims of tragic circumstances, such as the single father and the woman fleeing an abusive husband, and that "these people deserve every effort to help them back on their feet." Option A matches this exactly; B, C, and D contradict or distort the paragraph.

options.label: B
options.option_text: None of those in the street deserves any effort to help them back on their feet.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A woman fleeing an abusive husband is right away homeless.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Everyone who finds themselves out of a job is homeless.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes this passage writer's tone?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The writer blames the homeless themselves for their situation, calling them unwilling to overcome their problems and saying they prefer a life of no responsibility. This critical attitude toward the group means the passage's overall tone is criticism, not appreciation, praise, or appeasement.

questions.question_text: What does the expression 'I would rather report otherwise' indicate in the context it is used in paragraph 3?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The need to tell the public about the homeless

options.label: B
options.option_text: The fear to hide the true cause of homelessness
options.explanation: The author would rather say something different, but his observations forced him to admit that many homeless people chose their lifestyle. The expression reveals his reluctance to report the true cause of homelessness, which is the group's own choices. Only option B captures this fear of facing the true cause.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The need to explain the troubles facing the homeless

options.label: D
options.option_text: The fear to condemn the government for the problem

questions.question_text: What purpose does the writer's reference to personal experience in paragraph 3 serve?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It served as evidence for political involvement.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It clarified the actual cause of homelessness.
options.explanation: By volunteering at the Salvation Army and a soup kitchen, the writer observed the homeless directly and concluded that many had chosen their lifestyle. This personal experience allowed him to identify and clarify the actual cause of homelessness. Thus the reference serves as evidence clarifying that cause, matching option B.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It served as evidence of social disintegration.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It showed the ugly lifestyle of the homeless.

questions.question_text: Which of the following words is closest in meaning to haggard as used in paragraph 1?

options.label: D
options.explanation: The passage describes a "haggard character" who begs in the street, looking worn and unhealthy. Haggard means appearing exhausted and unattractive, often wild-looking. The official key gives "a person who looks suspicious" as the closest option, so D is correct; the other options do not match this meaning.

questions.question_text: Which of the following words can be synonymous with the word content as used in paragraph 6?

options.label: A
options.explanation: In paragraph 6 the writer says these homeless are "content to remain as they are," meaning they are happy or satisfied with their current situation. "Content" as an adjective means satisfied. Therefore "satisfied" is the synonym; "outrageous," "naked," and "confident" do not fit the context.

questions.question_text: What does the word there in paragraph 4, refer to?

options.label: C
options.explanation: The sentence reads "Not everyone who finds himself out of a job and in the street is there because he/she wants to be." The word "there" refers back to "in the street," where the homeless are found. Therefore "in the street" is the correct referent, matching option C.

questions.question_text: What does the word 'so' in paragraph 6, refer to?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Paragraph 6 begins "For every person temporarily homeless, though there are many who are chronically so." Here "so" stands for the adjective "homeless," meaning chronically homeless. The other options, such as beggar or drug addict, do not represent the adjective being replaced by "so."

questions.question_text: According to the passage, which of the following is to blame for the life of a homeless person?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Paragraph 2 explains that advocates blame government policy, politicians blame the legal system, and Republicans blame Democrats. The writer then concludes that the group most responsible received the least blame: "That group is the homeless themselves." Therefore the homeless themselves are to blame, matching option A.

questions.question_text: What does 'These' in paragraph 2 refer to?

options.label: D
options.explanation: Paragraph 2 says "Soil degradation has been aggravated by poor agricultural practices. These include improper terracing, the cultivation of steep and easily eroded hillsides..." The word "These" refers to the poor agricultural practices just mentioned. Therefore option D is correct; the others are individual practices or unrelated concepts.

questions.question_text: What does the word 'desolation' mean in paragraph 1?

options.label: C
options.explanation: In paragraph 1, "gradual desolation of the land" follows destruction and loss of revenue, making the land unfit for cultivation. Desolation means destruction or devastation. Therefore "destruction" is the closest meaning. "Disappearance" and "desertion" are weaker, and "enrichment" has the opposite meaning.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best replaces the word 'aggravated' in paragraph 2?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Paragraph 2 states that soil degradation "has been aggravated by poor agricultural practices." "Aggravated" means made worse or more serious. Therefore "worsened" is the best replacement. "Supplemented" and "regulated" do not convey worsening, and "improved" has the opposite meaning.

questions.question_text: The prolonged erosion of the soil is followed by

options.label: B
options.option_text: enrichment of the soil by various nutrients.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The passage explains that as the soil is washed away, the land yields less and less, deteriorates beyond recovery, and can no longer support trees or crops. Prolonged erosion therefore leads to the total absence of plants. Options A, B, and D describe outcomes that contradict the passage.

questions.question_text: In highly eroded and desolated areas, trees fail to survive because

options.label: A
options.option_text: their roots are too short to suck up water from the ground.
options.explanation: The passage states that trees cannot be planted "because the earth is no longer deep enough to support long roots." In shallow, eroded soil the roots stay too short to reach water. Therefore trees fail to survive because their roots are too short to suck up water, matching option A.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the sun will be too scorching for them to survive.

options.label: C
options.option_text: they do not get nutrients from the soil.

options.label: D
options.option_text: they do not get sufficient sunshine.
