options.option_text: To encourage only cash transactions under the mattress
options.explanation: Option D is informal hoarding limits both personal and national benefit.

questions.question_text: Community participation is most effective when citizens:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is passivity limits development.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Actively identify local problems, contribute ideas and resources, and work together with local authorities
options.explanation: Correct – This describes the model promoted in Unit 10.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Refuse to cooperate with any official structure
options.explanation: Option C is constructive engagement is preferred.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is community focus is essential.

questions.question_text: Why is developing the habit of critical reading and information evaluation important for citizens?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Because all information from any source is equally reliable
options.explanation: Option A is sources vary greatly in reliability.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Because citizens need to distinguish truth from falsehood in order to make informed decisions and resist manipulation
options.explanation: Correct – This is a central message of Unit 11.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Because reading is useful only for examinations
options.explanation: Option C is the value extends far beyond school exams.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Because critical thinking is unnecessary in a democracy
options.explanation: Option D is critical thinking strengthens democracy.

questions.question_text: In a system based on the rule of law, government officials are expected to:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Act according to their personal wishes without legal limit
options.explanation: Option A is unlimited power is the opposite of rule of law.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Exercise power only within the limits set by the Constitution and ordinary laws
options.explanation: Correct – This is the definition applied to governments.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Ignore court decisions that they dislike
options.explanation: Option C is court decisions must be respected.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Change the Constitution by decree whenever convenient
options.explanation: Option D is constitutional change follows special procedures.

questions.question_text: When personal interest conflicts with public interest, a responsible public official should:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is this leads to corruption.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Declare the conflict and put the public interest first
options.explanation: Correct – This is the expected standard.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is concealment itself is unethical.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Use public resources to resolve the personal interest
options.explanation: Option D is this constitutes abuse of office.

questions.question_text: The main purpose of the criminal justice system is to:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Punish every offender with the maximum possible severity regardless of circumstances
options.explanation: Option A is proportionality and individual circumstances matter.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Uphold the law, protect society, ensure fair trial and, where appropriate, rehabilitate offenders
options.explanation: Correct – This reflects the balanced approach in the curriculum.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is equality before the law is required.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is victims’ rights are also important.

questions.question_text: A patriot’s concern for the international community is best shown by:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is isolation is neither realistic nor desirable.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Supporting international peace, cooperation and the peaceful resolution of conflicts while defending national interests
options.explanation: Correct – This is the position taught in Unit 5.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Opposing all forms of international cooperation
options.explanation: Option C is cooperation is valued.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Prioritizing only short-term national advantage at the expense of regional stability
options.explanation: Option D is long-term stability serves national interest.

questions.question_text: Fulfilling civic and moral responsibilities sometimes involves personal cost. The curriculum teaches that citizens should:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Avoid any responsibility that involves sacrifice
options.explanation: Option A is avoidance undermines civic life.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Accept reasonable costs when the action serves justice, the common good or the protection of others’ rights
options.explanation: Correct – This is the mature attitude promoted.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Demand payment for every civic duty
options.explanation: Option C is many civic duties are unpaid.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Fulfill duties only when it is convenient
options.explanation: Option D is convenience is not the standard.

questions.question_text: The relationship between rights and obligations in the FDRE Constitution is best described as:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Citizens have only rights and no obligations
options.explanation: Option A is duties are clearly stated.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Rights and obligations are balanced; the enjoyment of rights is linked to the fulfillment of corresponding duties
options.explanation: Correct – This balanced view is taught throughout the curriculum.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is rights are fundamental.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Rights can be exercised without any regard for the rights of others
options.explanation: Option D is rights are limited by the rights of others and by law.

questions.question_text: Affirmative action measures are justified in the Ethiopian context primarily because:

options.label: A
options.option_text: They create permanent special privileges for certain groups
options.explanation: Option A is it is not meant to be permanent privilege.

options.label: B
options.option_text: They help overcome historical disadvantages and create genuine equality of opportunity
options.explanation: Correct – This is the justification given in Unit 3.

options.label: C
options.option_text: They are intended to reverse discrimination against the majority
options.explanation: Option C is it addresses disadvantage, not majority-minority reversal for its own sake.

options.label: D
options.option_text: They replace the principle of merit entirely
options.explanation: Option D is merit remains important; affirmative action levels the starting point.

questions.question_text: A just tax system should be based on the principle that:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Everyone pays exactly the same amount regardless of income
options.explanation: Option A is flat amounts ignore differences in capacity.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Those with greater ability to pay contribute a fairer share while the tax burden remains equitable
options.explanation: Correct – This reflects the equity principle taught.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Only the poor should pay taxes
options.explanation: Option C is ability to pay is the standard.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Tax collection can ignore transparency and accountability
options.explanation: Option D is transparency is essential for legitimacy.

questions.question_text: In the age of abundant information, the most important skill for a citizen is:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Accepting every piece of information without question
options.explanation: Option A is uncritical acceptance is dangerous.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The ability to evaluate sources, verify facts and seek reliable knowledge
options.explanation: Correct – This is a key competency in Unit 11.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is media literacy, not avoidance, is required.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Relying only on rumours from informal networks
options.explanation: Option D is rumours are often unreliable.

questions.question_text: Why is a democratic system considered necessary according to the Grade 12 Civics curriculum?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Because it allows one person to hold absolute power permanently
options.explanation: Option A is absolute power characterizes authoritarianism, not democracy.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Because it protects citizens’ rights, ensures accountability and provides mechanisms for peaceful change of government
options.explanation: Correct – These are the core justifications given in Unit 1.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Because it eliminates the need for a constitution
options.explanation: Option C is a constitution is essential to democracy.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Because it restricts freedom of expression
options.explanation: Option D is democracy protects and expands freedoms.

questions.question_text: How does the rule of law contribute to effective conflict management?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By allowing the stronger party to impose its will without legal limits
options.explanation: Option A is this produces injustice and further conflict.

options.label: B
options.option_text: By providing peaceful, predictable and impartial procedures for resolving disputes
options.explanation: Correct – This is the function emphasized in Unit 2.

options.label: C
options.option_text: By encouraging citizens to take the law into their own hands
options.explanation: Option C is self-help violence undermines the legal order.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is conflicts are natural; the goal is peaceful management.

questions.question_text: The FDRE Constitution’s recognition of the equality of nations, nationalities and peoples primarily aims to:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is the goal is unity within diversity, not separation.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Ensure equal rights, dignity and self-administration while maintaining the unity of the country
options.explanation: Correct – This is the constitutional and curricular position.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Grant superior status to one group over others
options.explanation: Option C is equality, not hierarchy, is the principle.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is diversity is protected and valued.

questions.question_text: Judicial independence is essential because:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Judges should be free to ignore the Constitution
options.explanation: Option A is judges remain bound by the Constitution and law.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It enables courts to decide cases impartially without interference from the executive or legislature
options.explanation: Correct – This is the core rationale for independence.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It allows the judiciary to make laws instead of the parliament
options.explanation: Option C is law-making remains the function of the legislature.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It removes all accountability of judges
options.explanation: Option D is judges are still accountable through ethical and legal mechanisms.

questions.question_text: A true patriot is expected to demonstrate:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Blind support for every government policy without question
options.explanation: Option A is critical yet loyal citizenship is valued.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Love of country expressed through responsible citizenship, defence of sovereignty and contribution to national progress
options.explanation: Correct – This matches the curriculum’s description.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is constructive international relations are encouraged.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Indifference to the welfare of fellow citizens
options.explanation: Option D is concern for others is part of patriotism.

questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly illustrates the three levels of responsibility taught in the curriculum?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Only personal responsibility matters; social and constitutional duties are optional
options.explanation: Option A is all three levels are important.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Personal (self-care and self-development), social (duties to family and community) and constitutional (duties to the state and society under the law)
options.explanation: Correct – This is the framework presented in Unit 6.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Responsibility exists only toward the government
options.explanation: Option C is responsibility is multi-dimensional.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is social responsibility is explicitly taught.

questions.question_text: According to the Civics curriculum, work is important primarily because:

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is a punishment for human beings
options.explanation: Option A is work is valued positively.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It is a means of personal fulfillment, social contribution and national development
options.explanation: Correct – This is the central message of Unit 7.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is necessary only for the poor
options.explanation: Option C is work is relevant to all citizens.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It has no moral or social value
options.explanation: Option D is moral and social value is strongly affirmed.

questions.question_text: A self-reliant person is best described as someone who:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Refuses all forms of cooperation with others
options.explanation: Option A is healthy self-reliance includes cooperation.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Takes initiative, develops personal capacity and seeks solutions rather than remaining dependent
options.explanation: Correct – This matches the definition in Unit 8.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Expects others to solve every problem
options.explanation: Option C is this describes dependency.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is continuous learning supports self-reliance.

questions.question_text: Effective personal financial management begins with:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is this leads to insecurity.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Planning, budgeting and setting aside savings before non-essential spending
options.explanation: Correct – This is the recommended practice in Unit 9.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Borrowing continuously without a repayment plan
options.explanation: Option C is uncontrolled borrowing creates problems.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is future orientation is essential.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a legitimate form of community participation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Using violence to force local decisions
options.explanation: Option A is violence is illegitimate.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Participating in local development associations, attending public meetings and contributing labour or ideas to community projects
options.explanation: Correct – These are the forms encouraged in Unit 10.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Refusing to pay any local contributions while demanding services
options.explanation: Option C is rights and duties go together.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Spreading false information to divide the community
options.explanation: Option D is division harms the community.

questions.question_text: Why does the curriculum encourage the development of regular reading habits?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Because reading is useful only for passing examinations
options.explanation: Option A is its value extends far beyond school.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Because reading expands knowledge, improves critical thinking and enables lifelong learning
options.explanation: Correct – This is the rationale in Unit 11.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Because books are the only source of information
options.explanation: Option C is multiple sources exist, but reading remains vital.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Because reading isolates a person from society
options.explanation: Option D is reading enriches social and civic life.

questions.question_text: In a constitutional democracy, the power of government is limited primarily by:

options.label: A
options.option_text: The personal will of the leader
options.explanation: Option A is personal will is constrained by law.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The Constitution, the rule of law, separation of powers and the rights of citizens
options.explanation: Correct – These are the classic limiting mechanisms.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The absence of any written rules
options.explanation: Option C is written and unwritten constitutional rules both matter.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The ability of the government to ignore public opinion
options.explanation: Option D is public opinion and elections are important controls.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a curative (reactive) anti-corruption measure?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is this is preventive.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Investigation, prosecution and punishment of corrupt acts after they have occurred
options.explanation: Correct – Investigation and sanction are curative.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Transparent procurement systems designed to prevent corruption
options.explanation: Option C is this is preventive system design.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is asset declaration is mainly preventive and deterrent.

questions.question_text: The pursuit of gender equality in Ethiopia requires:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is historical context is relevant for corrective measures.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Eliminating discrimination, ensuring equal opportunities and addressing barriers that prevent women’s full participation
options.explanation: Correct – This is the approach of the curriculum and Constitution.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Granting women rights that men do not have permanently
options.explanation: Option C is the goal is equal rights, not permanent reverse privilege.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Keeping women out of public decision-making
options.explanation: Option D is full participation is the objective.

questions.question_text: When citizens encounter injustice, the curriculum encourages them to:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is silence can perpetuate injustice.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Use peaceful, legal and democratic means to challenge the injustice and seek redress
options.explanation: Correct – Peaceful legal struggle is the recommended path.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is violence is rejected.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is injustice should be challenged.

questions.question_text: Why does the curriculum stress objectivity when studying Ethiopian history?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Because history should be rewritten to serve only one group’s interest
options.explanation: Option A is partisan history divides.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Because a balanced and evidence-based understanding of the past helps promote national reconciliation and informed patriotism
options.explanation: Correct – This is the pedagogical purpose stated in Unit 5.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Because the past has no relevance to the present
options.explanation: Option C is history informs present choices.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Because only foreign historians can be objective
options.explanation: Option D is ethiopian scholars and citizens can and should pursue objectivity.

questions.question_text: Citizens’ responsibility toward natural resources and cultural heritage includes:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Exploiting resources without any regard for sustainability
options.explanation: Option A is unsustainable use harms future generations.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Using resources wisely, preventing destruction and transmitting cultural heritage to future generations
options.explanation: Correct – This is the duty taught in Unit 6.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Leaving all protection solely to the government
options.explanation: Option C is shared responsibility is required.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Selling heritage items freely to the highest bidder without restriction
options.explanation: Option D is heritage protection involves legal and ethical limits.

questions.question_text: Punctuality and proper use of time are important civic and professional values because:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Time has no economic or social value
options.explanation: Option A is time is a valuable resource.

options.label: B
options.option_text: They increase productivity, reliability and respect for others’ time
options.explanation: Correct – This is emphasized in Unit 7.

options.label: C
options.option_text: They are relevant only in private life
options.explanation: Option C is the value applies in both private and public spheres.

options.label: D
options.option_text: They are unnecessary in a developing country
options.explanation: Option D is it is especially important for development.

questions.question_text: Morally sound decision-making capacity is important for self-reliance because:

options.label: A
options.option_text: It allows a person to act impulsively without reflection
options.explanation: Option A is reflection is required.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It enables individuals to choose actions that are both effective and ethically justifiable
options.explanation: Correct – This links self-reliance with ethical competence.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It removes the need to consider consequences
options.explanation: Option C is consequences must be considered.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It is useful only for political leaders
options.explanation: Option D is the capacity is needed by every citizen.

questions.question_text: How does a culture of saving among citizens contribute to national development?

options.label: A
options.option_text: By reducing the amount of money available for investment
options.explanation: Option A is saving increases, rather than reduces, investable resources.

options.label: B
options.option_text: By mobilising domestic resources that can be channelled into productive investment and reducing dependence on external borrowing
options.explanation: Correct – This is the macroeconomic rationale taught in Unit 9.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is saving balances present and future consumption.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is banks are key intermediaries in the process.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the relationship between human rights and democratic rights in the Ethiopian Constitution?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Human rights apply only to citizens while democratic rights apply to everyone
options.explanation: Option A is human rights belong to all human beings.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Human rights are inherent to all persons while democratic rights are mainly political rights of citizens that enable participation in governance
options.explanation: Correct – This reflects the constitutional and curricular distinction.

options.label: C
options.option_text: There is no distinction between the two categories
options.explanation: Option C is a useful analytical distinction is made.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Democratic rights can be suspended permanently without justification
options.explanation: Option D is rights may be limited only under strict constitutional conditions.

questions.question_text: Transparency in government is important because it:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Allows officials to hide their decisions from the public
options.explanation: Option A is secrecy undermines accountability.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Enables citizens to know how public power and resources are used and thereby strengthens accountability
options.explanation: Correct – This is a core democratic principle linked to rule of law.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Is relevant only during election periods
options.explanation: Option C is it is a continuous requirement.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Reduces the need for ethical behaviour by officials
options.explanation: Option D is transparency reinforces rather than replaces ethics.

questions.question_text: Tolerance of diversity in Ethiopian society means:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Accepting only one’s own culture and rejecting all others
options.explanation: Option A is this is intolerance.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Respecting different languages, religions, cultures and opinions while living together peacefully
options.explanation: Correct – This matches the curriculum’s teaching.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Forcing minority groups to abandon their identity
options.explanation: Option C is forced assimilation contradicts constitutional values.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Avoiding any interaction with people from different backgrounds
options.explanation: Option D is interaction and mutual understanding are encouraged.

questions.question_text: Equal access to justice requires that:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Only wealthy citizens can afford to use the courts
options.explanation: Option A is this creates inequality before the law.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Legal institutions and remedies are available to all persons without discrimination based on wealth, status or other irrelevant grounds
options.explanation: Correct – This is the standard promoted in the curriculum.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The judiciary serves only the interests of the government
options.explanation: Option C is the judiciary must be independent and impartial.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Ordinary citizens have no right to bring cases
options.explanation: Option D is citizens have the right to seek legal remedies.

questions.question_text: Voluntarism is considered a patriotic and civic virtue because it:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Is performed only for personal financial gain
options.explanation: Option A is true voluntarism is unpaid.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Involves freely giving time, skill or resources for the benefit of the community or nation without expecting payment
options.explanation: Correct – This is the definition used in the curriculum.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Replaces the need for professional public services
options.explanation: Option C is it complements rather than replaces formal systems.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Is limited only to young people
options.explanation: Option D is people of all ages can volunteer.

questions.question_text: Individual responsibility in the fight against HIV/AIDS includes:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is information is essential for responsible action.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Protecting oneself and others through informed behaviour, testing, treatment adherence and avoiding stigma
options.explanation: Correct – These are the practical responsibilities taught.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Believing that the disease concerns only certain groups
options.explanation: Option C is hIV/AIDS can affect anyone.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Refusing any form of community support for affected persons
options.explanation: Option D is support and non-discrimination are required.

questions.question_text: In any economic system, the dignity of work is upheld when:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Workers are treated merely as instruments of production
options.explanation: Option A is instrumental treatment violates dignity.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Labour is respected, fair conditions are provided and workers can develop their capacities
options.explanation: Correct – This is the ethical standard presented.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Only physical labour is valued and mental work is ignored
options.explanation: Option C is both physical and mental work have value.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Work is regarded as having no moral significance
options.explanation: Option D is work has clear moral and social value.

questions.question_text: One negative consequence of prolonged dependency at the individual level is:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is the opposite usually occurs.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Weakening of personal capacity, motivation and sense of responsibility
options.explanation: Correct – This is the caution given in Unit 8.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is dependency reduces productive contribution.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is decision-making capacity is often diminished.

questions.question_text: Extravagance is discouraged in the Civics curriculum mainly because it:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Helps the national economy grow faster
options.explanation: Option A is waste reduces rather than increases productive capacity.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Wastes resources that could be saved or invested productively and can lead to personal and social problems
options.explanation: Correct – This is the teaching of Unit 9.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Is a sign of high moral character
options.explanation: Option C is moderation and prudence are valued.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Has no effect on future security
options.explanation: Option D is future security is directly affected.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common obstacle to effective community participation?

options.label: A
options.option_text: High levels of civic awareness and trust
options.explanation: Option A is these factors promote participation.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Apathy, lack of information, exclusion of certain groups and absence of transparent local institutions
options.explanation: Correct – These are typical barriers discussed in the curriculum.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Strong local organisation and inclusive leadership
options.explanation: Option C is these enable participation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Equal opportunity for all residents to speak and contribute
options.explanation: Option D is this is a condition for success, not an obstacle.

questions.question_text: Critical thinking as a civic skill involves:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Accepting every claim that appears in social media
options.explanation: Option A is uncritical acceptance is dangerous.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Examining evidence, questioning assumptions and forming reasoned judgments
options.explanation: Correct – This is the skill promoted in Unit 11.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is open yet rigorous evaluation is required.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Relying solely on emotion when making public decisions
options.explanation: Option D is reason and evidence should guide judgment.

questions.question_text: A key indicator that an election is free and fair is:

options.label: A
options.option_text: The ruling party controls the entire electoral process without independent oversight
options.explanation: Option A is independent oversight is essential.

options.label: B
options.option_text: All eligible citizens can vote freely, parties compete on a reasonably level field, and the counting and announcement of results are transparent and credible
options.explanation: Correct – These are internationally and constitutionally recognised standards.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Opposition parties are prevented from campaigning
options.explanation: Option C is open campaigning is required.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Results are predetermined before voting takes place
options.explanation: Option D is predetermination destroys legitimacy.

questions.question_text: Equality before the law means that:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Laws apply differently according to a person’s wealth or status
options.explanation: Option A is this is discrimination.

options.label: B
options.option_text: All persons are subject to the same laws and are entitled to equal protection of those laws
options.explanation: Correct – This is the standard definition.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Government officials are above the law
options.explanation: Option C is no one is above the law.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Only certain groups enjoy legal protection
options.explanation: Option D is protection is universal.

questions.question_text: How does the curriculum view the relationship between affirmative action and merit?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Affirmative action completely replaces merit as a criterion
options.explanation: Option A is it does not abolish merit.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Affirmative action is a temporary measure to create conditions in which merit can operate more fairly among previously disadvantaged groups
options.explanation: Correct – This is the balanced position taught.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Merit should never be considered in public appointments
options.explanation: Option C is merit remains important.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Affirmative action is intended to lower standards permanently
options.explanation: Option D is the goal is fairness, not permanent lowering of standards.

questions.question_text: In a just criminal justice system, the rights of victims should include:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is victim welfare matters.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Respect, information about the process, protection from further harm and the possibility of appropriate redress
options.explanation: Correct – These are widely accepted victim rights.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The power to determine the final sentence without any court
options.explanation: Option C is sentencing remains a judicial function.

options.label: D
options.option_text: No role whatsoever in the proceedings
options.explanation: Option D is victims have a recognised place in the process.

questions.question_text: Patriotic commitment to national unity in Ethiopia is best expressed by:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Denying the existence of cultural and linguistic diversity
options.explanation: Option A is diversity is a constitutional reality.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Working to maintain the country’s territorial integrity and shared citizenship while respecting the equality of its diverse peoples
options.explanation: Correct – This is the balanced patriotic stance.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Promoting the dominance of one group over all others
options.explanation: Option C is equality is the constitutional principle.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is fragmentation contradicts national unity.

questions.question_text: Intergenerational responsibility means that present citizens should:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Use all resources for immediate benefit without regard for the future
options.explanation: Option A is this is short-sighted and unjust.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Consider the impact of their actions on future generations when using natural resources and shaping institutions
options.explanation: Correct – This is the ethical outlook promoted.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Ignore environmental and cultural heritage issues
options.explanation: Option C is heritage and environment are shared across generations.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Leave all future problems for later generations to solve alone
options.explanation: Option D is present action can reduce future burdens.

questions.question_text: Professional integrity requires that a person:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Places personal gain above professional standards
options.explanation: Option A is this is the opposite of integrity.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Upholds honesty, competence and ethical standards in the performance of their work
options.explanation: Correct – This is the expected standard.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Follows instructions even when they clearly violate the law
options.explanation: Option C is illegal orders should not be followed.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Avoids continuous learning and skill improvement
options.explanation: Option D is competence requires ongoing development.

questions.question_text: Self-reliance and cooperation are related in the following way:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Self-reliance means complete isolation from others
options.explanation: Option A is isolation is not the goal.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Genuine self-reliance enables a person to cooperate with others from a position of strength and mutual respect
options.explanation: Correct – This is the balanced view taught.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Cooperation is always a sign of weakness and dependency
options.explanation: Option C is cooperation is valued.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Self-reliant people never need to work with anyone
options.explanation: Option D is interdependence is a social reality.

questions.question_text: Wisdom, as presented in the Civics curriculum, is most useful in civic life when it helps citizens to:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Pursue only private advantage without regard for others
options.explanation: Option A is wisdom includes concern for others.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Make judgments that balance knowledge, ethical values and concern for the common good
options.explanation: Correct – This is the civic function of wisdom emphasised in Unit 11.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is engagement with public issues is required.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Follow popular opinion without independent reflection
options.explanation: Option D is independent judgment is part of wisdom.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best defines Aggregate Demand (AD) in an economy?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The total supply of all goods and services produced within a country over a specific period.
options.explanation: Option A is this describes Aggregate Supply (AS), not Aggregate Demand.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The total demand for final goods and services in an economy at a given overall price level and in a given time period.
options.explanation: This is the standard and complete definition of Aggregate Demand.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The demand for a single good or service by consumers in a specific market.
options.explanation: Option C is this describes individual market demand, which is a microeconomic concept.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The total value of all government spending on public services and infrastructure.
options.explanation: Option D is this is a component of aggregate demand, not its full definition.

questions.question_text: Which of the following scenarios would cause the Aggregate Demand (AD) curve to shift to the left?

options.label: A
options.option_text: An increase in government spending on infrastructure projects.
options.explanation: An increase in government spending (G) is a component of AD and would shift the AD curve to the right, not the left.

options.label: B
options.option_text: A decrease in the overall price level in the economy.
options.explanation: A change in the price level causes a movement along the AD curve, not a shift of the curve itself.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A decline in consumer confidence leading to a decrease in consumption spending.
options.explanation: A fall in consumption (C) is a decrease in one of the main components of AD, causing the entire curve to shift to the left.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A rapid increase in the country's export volume due to a weaker domestic currency.
options.explanation: An increase in exports (a component of Net Exports) would increase AD, shifting the curve to the right.

questions.question_text: What does the Aggregate Supply (AS) curve represent?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The total amount of goods and services that consumers are willing to buy at a given price level.
options.explanation: Option A is this is the definition of Aggregate Demand, not Aggregate Supply.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The relationship between the price level and the total quantity of goods and services that firms are willing and able to produce.
options.explanation: This is the standard definition of Aggregate Supply.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The total expenditure by the government on goods and services.
options.explanation: This is a component of GDP and Aggregate Demand, not a definition of Aggregate Supply.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The total value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a year.
options.explanation: This is the definition of GDP, which is a measure of the total output, but the concept of Aggregate Supply describes the relationship between this output and the price level.

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors would cause the Aggregate Supply (AS) curve to shift to the right?

options.label: A
options.option_text: An increase in the cost of imported raw materials.
options.explanation: Higher input costs decrease profitability, causing the AS curve to shift to the left, not right.

options.label: B
options.option_text: A significant improvement in technology that increases productivity.
options.explanation: Technological advancement increases efficiency, reduces costs, and increases the total output the economy can produce, shifting the AS curve to the right.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A decrease in the number of available workers due to emigration.
options.explanation: A reduction in the labour force is a negative supply shock that decreases the economy's capacity to produce, shifting AS to the left.

options.label: D
options.option_text: An increase in the overall price level.
options.explanation: A change in the price level causes a movement along the existing AS curve, not a shift of the curve itself.

questions.question_text: In the classical view of the long-run Aggregate Supply (LRAS) curve, what is the primary reason it is vertical?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Because the economy is always operating at full capacity.
options.explanation: This is a related but less precise explanation. The curve is vertical because output is determined by capacity, not because the economy is always at full capacity.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Because the total output of an economy is determined by its productive capacity (factors of production and technology), not the price level.
options.explanation: This is the foundational principle of classical economics. The LRAS is vertical at the natural level of output, which is independent of the price level.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Because wages and prices are sticky in the long run.
options.explanation: Classical economists believe wages and prices are flexible, not sticky. The vertical AS is a consequence of this flexibility, but the core reason is the fixed productive capacity.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Because monetary policy is ineffective in changing the price level.
options.explanation: Classical economics argues that while monetary policy may not affect real output in the long run, it does affect the nominal price level.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of asymmetric information in a market?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A seller offering a warranty on a new car to reassure the buyer about its quality.
options.explanation: A warranty is a signal used to reduce asymmetric information, not an example of it.

options.label: B
options.option_text: A farmer knowing the health of his cattle better than the potential buyer.
options.explanation: This is a classic example where the seller has superior information compared to the buyer.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Both the buyer and seller having the same knowledge about a product's features.
options.explanation: Option C is this situation is known as symmetric information, the opposite of asymmetric information.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A government providing public information about the nutritional value of food.
options.explanation: Option D is this is a policy solution to mitigate the problems caused by asymmetric information.

questions.question_text: Which of the following transactions would be recorded as a credit entry in Ethiopia's Balance of Payments?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The Ethiopian government paying interest on a loan from the World Bank.
options.explanation: Option A is this is an outflow of foreign currency from Ethiopia, recorded as a debit entry.

options.label: B
options.option_text: An Ethiopian company importing machinery from Germany.
options.explanation: This is an outflow of foreign currency to pay for the import, recorded as a debit entry.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A foreign tourist spending money on a hotel in Addis Ababa.
options.explanation: This is an inflow of foreign currency into Ethiopia, classified as a credit entry under the services account.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Ethiopian students studying abroad sending remittances to their families back home.
options.explanation: This is an outflow of foreign currency from Ethiopia and is recorded as a debit entry.

questions.question_text: A persistent deficit in a country's current account is most likely to be offset by a surplus in its:

options.label: A
options.explanation: The merchandise trade balance is a component of the current account, so a deficit here would contribute to a current account deficit, not offset it.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Similar to merchandise trade, the services balance is part of the current account and cannot offset a deficit in the overall current account.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The BOP must balance. A current account deficit is financed by a surplus in the financial account, representing net inflows of capital.

options.label: D
options.explanation: While a country can use its official reserves to finance a deficit, it is the broader financial account that is the primary counterpart. The reserve account is itself a component of the financial account.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a key characteristic of a sole proprietorship?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Owners have limited liability for business debts.
options.explanation: Limited liability is a feature of corporations and some types of partnerships, not sole proprietorships.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The business and its owner are considered separate legal entities.
options.explanation: Option B is in a sole proprietorship, the business and the owner are legally the same entity.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The owner has unlimited liability for all business debts and obligations.
options.explanation: This is a fundamental characteristic of a sole proprietorship.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Raising capital is relatively easy through the sale of shares.
options.explanation: Option D is this is a feature of a corporation, which can issue shares to raise capital.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a core idea of the Classical School of Economics?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Government intervention is necessary to stabilize the economy.
options.explanation: Option A is this is a key principle of Keynesian economics, not the Classical School.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The economy is self-regulating and will naturally tend toward full employment.
options.explanation: This is the foundational principle of the Classical School, often referred to as the 'invisible hand' and Say's Law.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Aggregate demand is the primary driver of economic growth.
options.explanation: Option C is this is a Keynesian view, while Classical economists focus on supply-side factors (Aggregate Supply).

options.label: D
options.option_text: Prices and wages are rigid and do not adjust quickly to changes in supply and demand.
options.explanation: Classical economists assumed wages and prices were flexible, not rigid. This rigidity is a Keynesian concept.

questions.question_text: Which of the following tools is most commonly used to measure income inequality within a country?

options.label: A
options.explanation: GDP measures the total value of goods and services produced, not how it is distributed among the population.

options.label: B
options.explanation: HDI is a composite index measuring life expectancy, education, and per capita income, not specifically income inequality.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The Gini Coefficient is specifically designed to measure income or wealth inequality within a population.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is cPI is a measure of inflation, not income inequality.

questions.question_text: What does the term 'absolute poverty' refer to?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A condition where a person's income is less than the average income of the country.
options.explanation: Option A is this is a measure of relative poverty, not absolute poverty.

options.label: B
options.option_text: A condition where a person lacks the minimum income required to meet basic needs like food, water, and shelter.
options.explanation: This is the standard definition of absolute poverty.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A condition where a person cannot afford the same goods and services as others in their society.
options.explanation: Option C is this describes relative poverty, which is about social standing and inequality.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A condition where a person's income is below 50% of the median income.
options.explanation: Option D is this is a specific measure of relative poverty, not absolute poverty.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a primary cause of poverty in developing countries like Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Excessive government spending on social programs.
options.explanation: Government spending on social programs is generally seen as a tool to alleviate poverty, not cause it.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Low levels of education and limited access to healthcare.
options.explanation: Lack of education and poor health limit human capital, which is a fundamental cause of poverty.

options.label: C
options.option_text: High levels of foreign direct investment.
options.explanation: Option C is fDI generally helps reduce poverty by creating jobs and stimulating economic growth.

options.label: D
options.explanation: These are often signs of economic progress, which typically helps to reduce overall poverty levels.

questions.question_text: The law of demand states that, all other things being equal, as the price of a good increases, the quantity demanded will:

options.label: A
options.explanation: This is the opposite of the law of demand. It would describe a positive relationship, which is not typical.

options.label: B
options.explanation: This is the direct statement of the law of demand, showing an inverse relationship.

options.label: C
options.explanation: This would violate the law of demand, which predicts a change in quantity demanded when price changes.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is the law of demand provides a clear, predictable inverse relationship.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the primary purpose of consumer protection laws?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is this is the goal of private businesses, not the purpose of consumer protection regulations.

options.label: B
options.option_text: To protect consumers from unfair and deceptive business practices.
options.explanation: This is the fundamental objective of consumer protection laws.

options.label: C
options.option_text: To increase the price of goods and services.
options.explanation: Option C is this is not a goal; consumer laws often aim for fair pricing and transparency.

options.label: D
options.option_text: To reduce the variety of products available in the market.
options.explanation: This is the opposite of what consumer protection aims to do; it seeks to ensure a fair marketplace with choice.

questions.question_text: According to Keynesian economics, which of the following is the most important determinant of consumption spending?

options.label: A
options.explanation: While interest rates can affect consumption (especially for durable goods), it is not the primary determinant according to Keynes.

options.label: B
options.explanation: This is the key variable in Keynes's consumption function.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Wealth is a determinant of consumption (e.g., in the life-cycle hypothesis), but Keynes emphasized current income.

options.label: D
options.explanation: These are important but are seen as influences on the level of consumption, not the primary determinant.

questions.question_text: Economic growth is best defined as:

options.label: A
options.option_text: An increase in a country's output of goods and services over time.
options.explanation: This is the standard and precise definition of economic growth.

options.label: B
options.option_text: An improvement in the standard of living and well-being of citizens.
options.explanation: This is a broader concept known as economic development, which includes social and institutional progress.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is this is a distributional goal, often associated with economic development, not growth itself.

options.label: D
options.option_text: An increase in the price level of goods and services.
options.explanation: Option D is this describes inflation, not economic growth.

questions.question_text: The primary objective of Ethiopia's Growth and Transformation Plan (GTP) was to:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is this is not an objective; the goal is economic growth, not increasing debt.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Promote rapid and sustainable economic development through industrialization and infrastructure.
options.explanation: This accurately reflects the core objectives of the GTP.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Reduce the role of the state in the economy.
options.explanation: Option C is the GTP involved a strong, leading role for the state in driving development.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is while agriculture was a component, the GTP had a broader focus on industrialization.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a key challenge faced during the implementation of development plans in Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A surplus of highly skilled labor.
options.explanation: Option A is a shortage of skilled labor, not a surplus, is a typical challenge.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Option B is these are facilitators of development, not challenges.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Limited institutional capacity and bureaucratic inefficiency.
options.explanation: These are major obstacles to effective implementation of development plans in many contexts.

options.label: D
options.option_text: An overabundance of foreign exchange reserves.
options.explanation: Option D is most developing countries face a shortage of foreign exchange, not an overabundance.

questions.question_text: The concept of 'structural transformation' in the context of development planning refers to:

options.label: A
options.option_text: A shift of economic resources from low-productivity sectors (like agriculture) to high-productivity sectors (like industry and services).
options.explanation: This is the standard definition of structural transformation.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The process of building new roads and bridges.
options.explanation: This describes infrastructure development, which is a part of development but not structural transformation itself.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A change in the country's political system.
options.explanation: Option C is this is a political change, not an economic structural transformation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: An increase in the price of raw materials.
options.explanation: Option D is this is a terms-of-trade effect, not a structural change in the economy.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of conducting an ex-ante evaluation of a development project?

options.label: A
options.option_text: To assess the project's impact after it has been completed.
options.explanation: Option A is this describes an ex-post evaluation, which is done after the project.

options.label: B
options.option_text: To determine the project's feasibility and potential outcomes before it starts.
options.explanation: This is the definition of an ex-ante evaluation.

options.label: C
options.option_text: To calculate the project's final cost overruns.
options.explanation: Option C is this is typically done during or after project implementation, not before.

options.label: D
options.option_text: To evaluate the project's impact on the environment after implementation.
options.explanation: This is an environmental impact assessment, often a component of evaluation but not the definition of ex-ante.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best distinguishes economic development from economic growth?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Development includes improvements in living standards and well-being, while growth is just an increase in output.
options.explanation: This accurately captures the key distinction between the two concepts.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Development is about industrialization, while growth is about agriculture.
options.explanation: While structural change is part of development, this statement is an oversimplification and not the main difference.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Growth is about government spending, while development is about private investment.
options.explanation: Option C is both growth and development can be driven by both public and private sectors.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Development is short-term, while growth is long-term.
options.explanation: Option D is both are long-term concepts; development is a more comprehensive and qualitative process.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a negative externality?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A beekeeper's bees pollinating a neighbor's crops.
options.explanation: Option A is this is a positive externality, as it benefits the neighbor without payment.

options.label: B
options.option_text: A factory emitting pollution that harms the health of local residents.
options.explanation: This is a classic example of a negative externality, where production creates an external cost.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A person receiving a flu vaccine, reducing the risk of infection for others.
options.explanation: Option C is this is a positive externality (herd immunity).

options.label: D
options.option_text: A student receiving a high-quality education.
options.explanation: This is a private benefit, and while it can have positive spillovers, the benefit directly accrues to the student.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a major environmental challenge facing Ethiopia today?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is this is not a major environmental concern for Ethiopia.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Rapid urbanization leading to deforestation and soil erosion.
options.explanation: This is a critical and well-documented environmental problem in Ethiopia.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A surplus of water resources leading to widespread flooding.
options.explanation: Option C is ethiopia faces challenges with water availability and distribution, not a surplus.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Low population growth resulting in labor shortages.
options.explanation: Option D is ethiopia has a high population growth rate, which exacerbates environmental pressures.

questions.question_text: The construction of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) is primarily aimed at:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Increasing agricultural exports by creating new irrigation schemes.
options.explanation: While the dam may provide some irrigation benefits, its primary purpose is not agricultural exports but power generation.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Generating hydroelectric power to meet the country's energy needs.
options.explanation: This is the stated and primary goal of the GERD project.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Reducing the flow of the Blue Nile to Egypt.
options.explanation: The dam is designed to regulate flow for power generation, not to drastically reduce the total volume reaching downstream countries.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is this is not a primary or significant objective of the project.

questions.question_text: Under a floating exchange rate system, the exchange rate between two currencies is determined by:

options.label: A
options.explanation: This is true for a fixed or managed exchange rate system where the central bank intervenes.

options.label: B
options.option_text: An international organization like the IMF.
options.explanation: The IMF provides advice and assistance but does not determine exchange rates for floating currencies.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The supply and demand for each currency in the foreign exchange market.
options.explanation: This is the core principle of a floating exchange rate system.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A fixed parity set by law.
options.explanation: Option D is this describes a fixed exchange rate system, not a floating one.

questions.question_text: If Ethiopia experiences a higher rate of inflation than its major trading partners, what is likely to happen to the value of the Ethiopian Birr in a floating exchange rate system?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Appreciation happens when demand for a currency increases, which is the opposite of what higher inflation causes.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Higher inflation reduces the competitiveness of Ethiopian exports, decreasing demand for the Birr, leading to depreciation.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The Birr's value will remain unchanged.
options.explanation: In a floating system, the exchange rate would adjust to the change in relative prices.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The Birr's value will become fixed.
options.explanation: This would only happen if the country adopted a fixed exchange rate system, which is not the scenario.

questions.question_text: What is a positive externality?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A benefit that is enjoyed by the producer of a good.
options.explanation: Option A is this is a private benefit, not an externality, which is about third parties.

options.label: B
options.option_text: A cost that is borne by the consumer of a good.
options.explanation: Option B is this is a private cost, not an externality.

options.label: C
options.option_text: A benefit that is enjoyed by a third party not involved in a transaction.
options.explanation: This is the correct definition of a positive externality.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A cost imposed on a third party from a transaction.
options.explanation: Option D is this defines a negative externality.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a government policy designed to correct a negative externality like pollution?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Providing a subsidy to the polluting firm.
options.explanation: Option A is a subsidy would encourage more production and thus more pollution, making the problem worse.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Imposing a Pigouvian tax equal to the cost of the externality.
options.explanation: This is a classic and effective policy to internalize external costs and correct the market failure.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Offering free permits to emit pollution.
options.explanation: Option C is this would likely increase pollution unless there is a strict cap on total permits.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Deregulating the industry to allow for more competition.
options.explanation: Deregulation would generally lead to more production and potentially more pollution without addressing the externality.

questions.question_text: The term 'social cost' of production in the presence of a negative externality refers to:

options.label: A
options.option_text: The total cost incurred by the firm producing the good.
options.explanation: Option A is this describes private cost only, not the total social cost.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The total cost incurred by the consumer purchasing the good.
options.explanation: This is a private cost on the consumption side, not the social cost of production.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The private cost of the firm plus the external cost imposed on third parties.
options.explanation: This is the definition of social cost in the presence of a negative externality.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The total cost incurred by the government to regulate the industry.
options.explanation: Option D is this is a policy cost, not the social cost of production itself.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the primary function of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Providing loans to individual consumers for personal use.
options.explanation: Option A is this is a function of commercial banks, not the central bank.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Regulating the money supply and acting as a lender of last resort.
options.explanation: These are the core responsibilities of a central bank like the NBE.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Offering savings accounts to small businesses.
options.explanation: Option C is this is a function of commercial banks and microfinance institutions.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is insurance services are provided by insurance companies, not the central bank.

questions.question_text: What is the primary objective of fiscal decentralization?

options.label: A
options.option_text: To centralize all tax collection at the federal level.
options.explanation: Option A is this describes fiscal centralization, the opposite of decentralization.

options.label: B
options.option_text: To transfer fiscal responsibilities and resources from the central government to lower levels of government.
options.explanation: This is the correct definition of fiscal decentralization.

options.label: C
options.option_text: To eliminate all local government spending.
options.explanation: Option C is decentralization aims to increase local spending autonomy, not eliminate it.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is this is not a goal of fiscal decentralization.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a major challenge to effective fiscal decentralization in Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: A highly uniform tax base across all regions.
options.explanation: Tax bases are often uneven, which is a challenge, but uniformity would not be the issue.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Limited capacity of regional governments to effectively manage and utilize funds.
options.explanation: This is a well-documented challenge in fiscal decentralization.

options.label: C
options.option_text: An overabundance of skilled financial personnel at the local level.
options.explanation: Option C is a shortage, not an overabundance, of skilled personnel is a typical challenge.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Excessive local autonomy leading to no coordination.
options.explanation: While coordination is a challenge, the problem is often a lack of autonomy due to limited capacity and resources.

questions.question_text: Fiscal policy refers to the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy. Which of the following is a tool of fiscal policy?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is this is a tool of monetary policy, not fiscal policy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Option B is this is a monetary policy action.

options.label: C
options.explanation: This is a direct instrument of fiscal policy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Option D is this is a key tool of monetary policy.

questions.question_text: During a recession, the government is most likely to adopt which type of fiscal policy?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Contractionary fiscal policy, increasing taxes and decreasing spending.
options.explanation: Option A is this would worsen a recession by reducing aggregate demand.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Expansionary fiscal policy, decreasing taxes and increasing spending.
options.explanation: This is the standard response to a recession, boosting aggregate demand.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Contractionary fiscal policy, decreasing taxes and increasing spending.
options.explanation: Option C is decreasing taxes and increasing spending is expansionary, not contractionary.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Expansionary fiscal policy, increasing taxes and decreasing spending.
options.explanation: Option D is increasing taxes and decreasing spending is contractionary, not expansionary.

questions.question_text: The concept of 'crowding out' in the context of expansionary fiscal policy refers to:

options.label: A
options.option_text: Government borrowing driving up interest rates and reducing private investment.
options.explanation: This is the precise definition of the crowding-out effect.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Increased government spending leading to a decrease in taxes.
options.explanation: Option B is this is not crowding out; it's a possible combination of fiscal tools.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Private investment increasing due to government spending.
options.explanation: Option C is this is the opposite of crowding out (crowding in).

options.label: D
options.option_text: A decrease in consumer confidence due to government borrowing.
options.explanation: This could be a secondary effect, but it is not the definition of crowding out.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of a country's foreign exchange policy?

options.label: A
options.option_text: To set the price of gold.
options.explanation: This is not a function of modern foreign exchange policy, though historically it was relevant under the gold standard.

options.label: B
options.option_text: To influence the exchange rate and manage international reserves.
options.explanation: This is the core purpose of foreign exchange policy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is this is a goal of autarky, not foreign exchange policy.

options.label: D
options.option_text: To fix the price of all imports.
options.explanation: While policy can affect the price of imports via the exchange rate, it doesn't set their price directly.

questions.question_text: What is the key difference between Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and Gross National Product (GNP)?

options.label: A
options.option_text: GDP measures only goods, while GNP measures services.
options.explanation: Option A is both GDP and GNP measure both goods and services.

options.label: B
options.option_text: GDP measures production within a country's borders, while GNP measures production by a country's citizens, regardless of location.
options.explanation: This is the accurate distinction between the two concepts.

options.label: C
options.option_text: GDP is measured in nominal terms, while GNP is measured in real terms.
options.explanation: Option C is both can be measured in nominal or real terms.

options.label: D
options.option_text: GDP includes only private sector output, while GNP includes government output.
options.explanation: Option D is both GDP and GNP include output from both the private and public sectors.

questions.question_text: If an Ethiopian-owned company produces goods in Kenya, where would the value of this production be recorded?

options.label: A
options.option_text: In Ethiopia's GDP and Kenya's GNP.
options.explanation: Option A is it would be in Kenya's GDP because it's produced there, not Ethiopia's GDP.

options.label: B
options.option_text: In Kenya's GDP and Ethiopia's GNP.
options.explanation: This is the correct application of the GDP (location) and GNP (ownership) principles.

options.label: C
options.option_text: In Ethiopia's GDP and Ethiopia's GNP.
options.explanation: Option C is it is not in Ethiopia's GDP because it is not produced within Ethiopia's borders.

options.label: D
options.option_text: In Kenya's GDP and Kenya's GNP.
options.explanation: Option D is it is not in Kenya's GNP because the company is not Kenyan-owned.

questions.question_text: What does the GDP deflator measure?

options.label: A
options.option_text: The total value of all goods and services produced in the economy.
options.explanation: Option A is this is GDP, not the GDP deflator.

options.label: B
options.option_text: The average price of all goods and services included in GDP.
options.explanation: This is the definition of the GDP deflator.

options.label: C
options.option_text: The total number of people employed in the economy.
options.explanation: Option C is this is a measure of employment, unrelated to the GDP deflator.

options.label: D
options.option_text: The total amount of money in circulation.
options.explanation: Option D is this is the money supply, not the GDP deflator.

questions.question_text: If nominal GDP is 120 billion Birr and the GDP deflator is 120 (with base year = 100), what is the real GDP?

options.label: A
options.explanation: This would be the result of multiplying Nominal GDP by the Deflator (120 × 1.2), which is incorrect.

options.label: B
options.explanation: This is the nominal GDP, not the real GDP after adjusting for the price level.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The calculation: (120 / 120) × 100 = 100 billion Birr.

options.label: D
options.explanation: This would be the result of dividing nominal by the deflator (120/120 = 1), but without multiplying by 100.

questions.question_text: Which region of the world has the highest number of people living in extreme poverty?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sub-Saharan Africa has both the highest poverty rate and the largest number of extremely poor people globally.

options.label: B
options.explanation: While South Asia has a significant number of poor people, the total is lower than Sub-Saharan Africa.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Option C is latin America has lower poverty rates compared to Africa and South Asia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: This region has made significant progress in reducing poverty and now has a much smaller number of extremely poor.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the primary cause of the increase in global average temperatures?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Option A is solar radiation variations are not the main cause of the recent rapid warming.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Option B is volcanic eruptions can have a short-term cooling effect, not a long-term warming trend.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Human activities, particularly the emission of greenhouse gases.
options.explanation: This is the established primary cause of climate change.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Natural cycles of the Earth's orbit.
options.explanation: These cycles affect climate over thousands of years and cannot explain the rapid warming since the Industrial Revolution.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a major effect of climate change that disproportionately impacts developing countries like Ethiopia?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Increased frequency and severity of droughts and floods.
options.explanation: This is a major impact, especially on rain-fed agriculture, which is crucial for Ethiopia.

options.label: B
options.option_text: A decrease in the frequency of tropical storms.
options.explanation: Option B is climate change is expected to increase the intensity of storms, not decrease their frequency.

options.label: C
options.option_text: An increase in average sea levels globally.
options.explanation: Option C is while true, this is less directly impactful for a landlocked country like Ethiopia.

options.label: D
options.option_text: A uniform increase in agricultural productivity.
options.explanation: Option D is climate change is predicted to have negative effects on agricultural productivity in many regions.

questions.question_text: The concept of 'climate justice' recognizes that:

options.label: A
options.option_text: All countries are equally responsible for addressing climate change.
options.explanation: Option A is climate justice emphasizes the principle of 'common but differentiated responsibilities'.

options.label: B
options.option_text: Countries that have contributed the least to climate change are often the most vulnerable to its impacts.
options.explanation: This is the core of the climate justice argument.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Only developed countries should take action to reduce emissions.
options.explanation: While developed countries have the most responsibility, climate justice also calls for all countries to participate in mitigation.

options.label: D
options.option_text: Climate change is a purely natural phenomenon with no human responsibility.
options.explanation: Option D is this contradicts the scientific consensus and the basis of climate justice.

questions.question_text: Which international agreement is the most prominent global framework for combating climate change?

options.label: A
options.explanation: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) was a predecessor to the Paris Agreement and only applied to developed countries.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Option B is this treaty addresses the protection of the ozone layer, not climate change.

options.label: C
options.explanation: This is the current and most comprehensive global climate agreement.

options.label: D
